/News/2017/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-84th-Jan.t: Mahant Swami Maharaj 84th Janma Jayanti Mahotsav, London, UK
/News/2017/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-84th-Jan.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mahant Swami Maharaj's 84th Janma Jayanti Mahotsav (40 photos)
 The 84th birth anniversary of Mahant Swami Maharaj was joyously celebrated in his presence on Saturday 23 September 2017 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 The celebrations began in the early morning during Swamishri’s puja, when swamis sang kirtans narrating his life and virtues, especially his relationship with gurus Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 A special magazine introducing the life and work of Mahant Swami Maharaj was published in honour of his visit to the UK. This was presented to Harikrishna Maharaj and formally released during the morning festivities.
 Children had made birthday cards for Swamishri which were displayed around the assembly hall. A rangoli (traditional Indian decorative pattern) of more than 8,000 small cakes prepared by devotees was also artistically arranged.
 The evening programme centred around Swamishri’s stuti ‘Shobhe saumya mukharvind hasatu…’, exploring his serenity and divine grace, and reflected upon his humble nature and attachment to God – virtues which won the hearts of Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 The assembly began with bhajans extolling some of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s qualities. Visiting swamis then shared a montage of inspiring incidents from Swamishri’s life which encompassed his saintliness and devotion.
 Their messages were further supported by testimonies from Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, shared through historical video footage.
 Other enlightening presentations provided a deeper understanding of Swamishri and his spiritual connection with Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami offered a prayer to Mahant Swami Maharaj on behalf of all swamis and devotees. Swamis then honoured Swamishri with a decorative garland to formally welcome him to London.
 A troupe of 112 children and youths from around the UK performed a vibrant celebratory dance as part of the festivities, further infusing the assembly hall with devotional fervour.
 In his blessings, Mahant Swami Maharaj expressed his joy at seeing the congregation and encouraged everyone to see the greatness within others. He also expressed his sincere wish to bless the lives of one and all.

/News/2017/Mahila-Din-Celebration-2017-1.t: Mahila Din, Los Angeles, CA, USA
/News/2017/Mahila-Din-Celebration-2017-1.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mahila Din (34 photos)
 Women of BAPS throughout West region celebrated His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj's vicharan by participating in a community cultural events titled, Mandiram: Param Shantidam. The program was presented by a unique group of performers at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Los Angeles, CA.
 Mandiram: Param Shantidam developed as a stage play that followed the lives of three characters who are on a quest to write a book about the source of happiness and satisfaction. Their research led them to a mandir where they came across a book that takes them on a journey through colorful dances, short skits, speeches, videos, and devotional songs. Throughout this exploration, they came to understand the impact of mandir and the Ekantik Sant in their quests for peace and stability. Each character explored the ideas of responsibility, cultural preservation, and togetherness within families and among each other as tools to foster peaceful living.
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj upheld the importance of cultural preservation, personal and spiritual development, as well as family unity. Throughout blessings delivered during his vicharan, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj also emphasized the great value in building families and communities rooted in spiritual solidarity, where individuals maintain respect for each other and seek to support each other.
 The Mahila Din festivities incorporated this guidance and brought together women of all ages in devotion as a multigenerational opportunity to share art, language, and tradition. The program was made possible by hundreds of dedicated women working together to create the overall concept, design the program content, prepare volunteer participants, as well as provide audio and visual support throughout the event. Invoking the values of oneness and teamwork, the event strengthened relationships among women within the BAPS North American community and introduced BAPS’ women’s activities for individuals interested in learning more.
 Distinguished guests Califorina State Representative Judy Chu of the 27th congressional district and Dr. Nancy Gin, Medical Director for Kaiser Permanente Orange County were also in attendance. Both expressed their respect and esteem for Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.

 More than 4,500 women devotees attended the annual one-day mahila and yuvati Chaturmas parayan, which was based on the theme ‘Samp’ (Unity).
 Through discourses, bhajans, skits and dances, the program highlighted the necessity of samp, reasons why samp is broken, and the efforts of our Guru Parampara to preserve samp in Satsang. Everyone learnt the key message that by cultivating the qualities of unity and friendship with others we will be able to attain and experience the fullest benefit and joy of Satsang.

/News/2017/Mano-Mali-Chhe-Moti-Vat---Kar.t: 'Mano Mali Chhe Moti Vat' - Karyakar Shibirs, Africa
/News/2017/Mano-Mali-Chhe-Moti-Vat---Kar.text:
A total of over 825 men and women karyakars from 59 centres in 8 countries – Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda, Botswana, Zambia and Malawi countries involved in Satsang activities attended the four Karyakar Shibirs held in Kisumu, Kenya (29 April to 1 May 2017), Arusha, Tanzania (5 to 7 May), Lenasia, South Africa (12 to 14 May) and Lusaka, Zambia (19 to 21 May). The shibirs were based on the theme 'Mano Mali Chhe Moti Vat' – 'Believe You Have Attained a Great Tenet'.
 Through speeches by swamis and senior karyakars, skits, audio-video presentations, discussions and question-answer sessions, the karyakars learnt about association with the holy Sadhu, living as per God's and guru's wishes, true faith, refuge to God, pride in one's attainment, desire to earn the blessings of God and guru, devotion, glory of the manifest form of Aksharbrahman, matchless satsang fellowship, guru's affection for devotees, humble service and other topics essential for their personal spiritual progress and to assist them in their satsang duties.

Photo Gallery 
 Matru-Devo Bhava (20 photos)
 Programmes celebrating the loving bond between mothers and daughters were held at 10 mandirs and centres across the UK on Sunday 26 March 2017. This annual event brought together more than 600 children and their respective mothers.
 The events were organised and delivered by young children to honour their mothers, in keeping with the timeless Hindu values of respect and reverence prescribed in the Taittiriya Upanishad.
 Girls as young as four had prepared special cards, composed and recited poems, and performed songs, dances and sketches as a part of the inspiring programme. A series of energetic games and puzzles provided an interactive component to the day with further reflection and appreciation.
 A short mahapuja reinforced the messages of love and respect, wherein children offered prayers for their mothers and strengthened their individual relationship with them. They then offered ‘panchang pranam’ to their mothers.
 A young girl, aged 8, shared, “I love my mummy very much because she listens to me and looks after me.”
 One of the mothers who attended the event in Leicester added, “This was such a wonderful day! It was an opportunity for us to spend some quality time together, with so much love and fun and laughter.”
 Events were held in Birmingham, Leicester, London, Loughborough, Luton, Manchester, Preston, South London, South East London and Wellingborough.

/News/2017/Murti-Pratishtha-of-Guru-Para.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Felicitation Assembly (32 photos)
 Yagna (40 photos)
 Murti-Pratishtha (50 photos)
 30 JANUARY: FELICITATION ASSEMBLY
 On Monday, 30 January 2017, a special assembly was held by the BAPS in Gadhada to felicitate the leading town members of different communities and heads of organizations. The evening assembly was held in the presence of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj. After addresses by senior sadhus the leading members of Gadhada spoke glowingly of BAPS and Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Then Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the assembly. Finally, Kothari Adhyatmaswarup Swami of BAPS Mandir acknowledged the support given by all the leaders and authorities to the BAPS Mandir renovation project. Thereafter, all the leaders were honoured on stage and served mahaprasad.
 31 JANUARY: YAGNA
 On the day prior to the murti-pratishtha of the abhishek murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and marble murtis of Guru Parampara a yagna was held in Gadhada. The yagna mandap comprised of 150 yagna kunds with 1,073 yajmans (participants). The yagna commenced amidst Vedic chantings by 55 pandits in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj and senior sadhus. Mahant Swami Maharaj ignited the yagna fire, performed pujan of the murtis and finally blessed the yajmans.
 Later in the day Mahant Swami Maharaj launched the kavad yatra – where the holy waters of River Ghela was carried in kavads (traditional vessels) for the ritual bathing of the murtis in the mandir.
 In the evening, BAPS sadhus presented a wonderful kirtan aradhna before an audience of devotees and citizens of Gadhada.
 1 FEBRUARY: MAHANT SWAMI MAHARAJ AND CM VIJAYBHAI RUPANI INAUGURATE EXHIBITION
 On Vasant Panchmi, 1 February 2017, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj consecrated the abhishek murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and marble murtis of Guru Parampara at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Gadhada.
 At 9.20 a.m. the Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Vijaybhai Rupani was welcomed at the mandir. Thereafter, Mahant Swami Maharaj and Shri Vijaybhai Rupani inaugurated the grand entrance gate, Yagnapurush Dwar. Then a group photo was taken with the descendants of Dada Khachar and Jiva Khachar. Thereafter, the Chief Minister performed abhishek of the newly installed murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj and the Chief Minister inaugurated the new exhibition, ‘Gadhpur jota mane Shriji Sambhare…’ The guests were taken through the exhibition halls, which portray the life, work and message of Bhagwan Swaminarayan through audio-visual dioramas and light and sound shows.
 The highlight of the occasion was the Vasant Panchmi celebration assembly. Pujya Brahmavihari Swami, Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Pujya Dr Swami and guests addressed the assembly. Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami described the main features of the newly opened exhibition. He revealed, “For the first time ever a letter written and signed by Sahajanand Swami is displayed in the exhibition. The letter is a testament to his presence on earth.”
 Shri Bhupendrasinh Chudasama, Education Minister of Gujarat, voiced his feelings, “I congratulate the BAPS for creating an exhibition of an international standard. It is part of an effort to preserve our glorious culture. While viewing the exhibition it seemed as if Bhagwan Swaminarayan was present before us.”
 The Chief Minister opined, “This town of Gadhada was very dear to Bhagwan Swaminarayan. And the exhibition about him places Gadhada on an international level. Nowhere have I seen such an exhibition in the whole of India. I thank the BAPS for augmenting the pride of Gujarat. Through the piety of BAPS sadhus one finds them achieving great works, and their pure lives consolidate faith in the hearts of countless people.”
 In conclusion, Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the celebration assembly, “As a teenager Bhagwan Swaminarayan travelled throughout India, but he did not settle down anywhere. However, he stayed in Gadhada for three decades. The reasons being the devotion of the devotees and the merited land of Gadhada. Today, everyone is happy in Gadhada because the abhishek murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan was consecrated with Vedic rites and an exhibition on his life, work and teachings was thrown open to the public. The exhibition will inspire countless people.”
 Thereafter, all had mahaprasad.

/News/2017/Murti-Sthapan-Ceremony-11674..text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Sthapan Ceremony (20 photos)
 The murti sthapan ceremony of the newly renovated BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Leeds was held on Monday 29 May 2017 (Vaishakh Sud 4, Samvat 2073) amid Vedic chanting and devotional festivities.
 The ceremony was conducted by sadhus from London, led by Yogvivek Swami, head sadhu for BAPS in UK & Europe.
 The inauguration celebrations of the new mandir included a special mahapuja where devotees and well-wishers offered their prayers for world peace and the well-being of the community. Guests from other mandirs, communities and further afield, such as Greater Manchester, Preston, Bolton, Coventry, Doncaster, Leicester and Bradford participated in the festivities.
 Following the ceremony, the first arti was conducted followed by a special assembly marking the inauguration and also celebrating Pramukh Varni Din. Yogvivek Swami spoke about continuingly renewing and consolidating one’s faith in God and the Guru, and praised the efforts of the local volunteers and community.
 The mandir in Leeds serves as the hub of Satsang and charitable activities for BAPS in the Yorkshire area. This includes Satsang sabhas every Sunday that cater to children, teenagers and adults, and the annual charity challenge.
 One young volunteer, Tanishka Gandhi, spoke of the “vital role” the Mandir has played in her life. She said, “The Mandir is my spiritual home. It allows me to offer devotion to God and serve my fellow devotees and the local community. It allows me to grow and learn and enjoy my faith. I don’t know what I’d do without the Mandir! I and my family feel so blessed and grateful that we have a place we can call ‘our mandir’.”

/News/2017/National-Bal-Balika-Mandal-Wi.t: National Bal-Balika Mandal Winter Training Camp, UK
/News/2017/National-Bal-Balika-Mandal-Wi.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Bal-Balika Mandal Winter Training Camp (30 photos)
 The UK Bal-Balika Mandal organised a special Winter Training Camp entitled ‘Satsang Karo ne Karavo’ between Friday 16 and Sunday 18 December 2016 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. The programme conveyed useful information and volunteer training to 56 selected delegates from across the UK.
 Manoharmurti Swami explained the aims and objectives and elaborated on how to utilise the skills and knowledge to progress spiritually, including in serving others.
 Devotees who have sacrificed their time to serve others whilst achieving academic success were then recognised, providing motivation and encouragement to the young delegates. The first day also provided plenty of opportunities for the children to interact through various team-building activities. 
 On the second day, sadhus and senior karyakars delivered inspiring presentations on the fundamentals of the Akshar-Purushottam upasana. Each session provided the delegates with an insight into the core principles of BAPS by exploring the concepts of siddhant, Sanstha and Satpurush.
 The children also enjoyed a treasure hunt in the City of London. They were given several timed tasks with the emphasis of working as a team and in doing so, developed their planning, communication and leadership skills.
 The final day of the camp served as an induction for new volunteers through hands-on training that was delivered using innovative and interactive methods.
 The theoretical and practical training drew upon the tireless endeavours of the Guru Parampara as the ideal example, providing the new volunteers a solid foundation to progress in their personal lives and make a difference in the lives of others.
 As a memento, the delegates were awarded certificates to confirm they had completed the course on teamwork and voluntary services.
 One balak shared, “I feel more confident now in my understanding, and will not hesitate when someone asks me about it.”
 A balika added, “It was an enjoyable and unique experience to share with my friends, which has helped me to better understand Akshar-Purushottam upasana.”

 Shibir (35 photos)
 A total of around 165 balaks and balikas from Dar-es-Salaam, Mwanza, Arusha and Tanga attended the five-day shibir held at the White Sands Hotel and Resort in Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania in presence of swamis from Nairobi.
 Based on the theme ‘Asmita’, the shibir guided the children on spiritual and cultural values through topics such as Pride for God, Pride for Satpurush, Pride for Siddhant, Pride for Shastras and Pride for Satsang.  They also learnt about tilak-chandlo, daily personal puja, diet, arti and panchang pranam to parents. The shibir featured speeches by the swamis, group discussions, skits, question-answer sessions, workshops, team building activities, audio-visual presentations and a cultural exhibition, providing insightful and practical guidance for the children to apply in their daily life.

 More than 200 balaks and balikas from across Uganda and Eldoret, Kenya, took part in the five-day shibir themed 'Asmita-Pride For Satsang'. The shibir helped to develop a deeper understanding of satsang and Indian culture in the children.

/News/2017/National-Medico-Spiritual-Con.text:

 National Medico-Spiritual Conference (9 photos)
 The theme of this year’s conference was ‘Sadhana: Living a Meaningful Life.’ Among the approximately 650 doctors and their families present from throughout India and other countries were Dr. Navin Thakkar (President of the Asia-Pacific Paediatric Association), Konstantin Beltikov (orthopaedic surgeon, Moscow), as well as other renowned neurosurgeons, cardiologists, plastic surgeons, and other super-specialists.
 The shibir theme was effectively conveyed through speeches by senior BAPS swamis, experienced devotees, enlightening videos, workshops and panel discussions. The delegates learnt how to balance their personal, spiritual and professional lives, the role of sadhana (spiritual endeavor) in life and practical ways to apply these ideas in their daily lives.
 Topics presented included ‘What is Sadhana?’, daily worship and daily spiritual reading. The delegates were also moved by the narrations of personal experiences shared by their peers on how they have maintained the practice of satsang amidst their busy daily schedule.
 To further reinforce the theme and provide practical ideas, students from the Akshar-Purushottam Chhatralay in Vidyanagar, performed a drama entitled ‘Tannu’ based on an inspirational story about a young child who overcame difficulties in his life by practicing satsang and maintaining a positive attitude.
 In one practical session, the delegates also performed samuh puja in the morning. In addition, the doctors and their families were inspired and blessed by the special letters and video messages of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj and Pujya Doctor Swami. The conference concluded with the video blessings of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 Thereafter, the delegates travelled to the BAPS Mandir in Gadhada to view the exhibition on Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s life, which was recently inaugurated by Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj and the Chief Minister of Gujarat, Vijaybhai Rupani.
 Since 1994, more than 32,000 doctors and their families have benefitted from the medico-spiritual conferences organized in various locations by BAPS Pramukh Swami Health Services.

/News/2017/National-Shishu-Mandal-Trip-1.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Paradise Wildlife Park (25 photos)
 More than 350 young children and parents from across the UK came together for an educational and fun-filled outing at Paradise Wildlife Park in Hertfordshire on Saturday 29 April 2017.
 The day began with interactive corners for the youngsters to enjoy upon arrival. The activities, ranging from enthralling parachute games to entertaining puppet shows, captivated both children and adults alike, and conveyed the important message of unity within the family and the wider community.
 Sadhus began the day with the traditional lighting of divas and reinforced the importance of family harmony and unity in their discourses – a value which is regularly encouraged by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Sadhus also spoke of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s affection and care for all animals.
 Representatives from the Park arrived thereafter with various animals, including tortoises, lizards and snakes. Children were offered a very exciting opportunity to meet and take photographs with the animals as well as touch and interact with them.
 The sunshine and natural habitats provided the perfect opportunity for a family picnic. The eager children then explored the Park in earnest. From watching monkeys jump on their swings to face-to-face encounters with lionesses, the diverse range of creatures provided a memorable experience.
 The enthusiasm and energy visible throughout the day in both the children and their families was a testimony to the event’s success. Families were able to spend time together as well as make new friends. The outing echoed the sentiments of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who often said, “The family that plays together, stays together.”
 One parent commented, “It was a hugely enjoyable day which allowed me to spend some special time with my young children. We should do this every year!”
 A father added, “We met so many families from around the country and created lifelong memories. Thank you for organising this event.”

/News/2017/Observing-Earth-Hour-2017-111.text:
Earth Hour 2017, London
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London joined iconic landmarks as well as communities and organisations from 187 countries by switching off its non-essential lights to observe Earth Hour at 8.30pm on Saturday 25 March 2017.
 Earth Hour – the world’s largest environmental event – is a global movement involving millions of people “to shine a light on the need for climate action” and raise awareness about protecting the future of our planet.
 More than 3,100 landmarks and monuments participated around the world, including the Eiffel Tower, the Empire State Building, the Sydney Opera House and the Acropolis, as well as notable buildings in London, including Big Ben, the Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace, Tower Bridge and Piccadilly Circus.
 This year’s event marked the tenth anniversary of the Earth Hour movement, which started as a one-city event in Sydney in 2007. Today it has expanded to over 7,000 cities across seven continents.
 Earth Hour is coordinated by the World Wide Fund For Nature (WWF), one of the world’s largest and most respected independent conservation organisations.
 Sid Das, Executive Director for Earth Hour Global, explained, “Once again, the people have spoken through Earth Hour. Whether you are in the Philippines, Peru or Portugal, climate change matters and the record participation in this year’s Earth Hour is a powerful reminder that people, who are on the frontline of climate change, want to be a part of climate action.”
 Taking ‘action beyond the hour’ is a commitment that BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha continues to make for the environment. Yogen Shah, a volunteer at the Mandir, shared, “It is more than a symbolic gesture for everyone at the Mandir. Caring for the environment is one of the ideals deeply rooted in our Hindu faith and something that our spiritual leader Pramukh Swami Maharaj and now Mahant Swami Maharaj continues to inspire, and which we endeavour to foster in our various activities here.”
 Earth Hour was also observed at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi and BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs in North America.

/News/2017/Observing-International-Peace.t: Observing International Peace Day, London, UK
/News/2017/Observing-International-Peace.text:
Photo Gallery 
 International Peace Day (15 photos)
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, a member of the United Nations Economic and Social Council, observed International Peace Day in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj on Saturday 23 September at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London.
 Background
 In 1981, the United Nations General Assembly unanimously passed a resolution declaring an International Day of Peace. In 2001, the General Assembly adopted 21 September as the permanent date for this annual event.
 The Day is envisioned to provide “an opportunity for individuals, organisations and nations to create practical acts of peace on a shared date.” As the resolution states: “Peace Day should be devoted to commemorating and strengthening the ideals of peace both within and among all nations and peoples.”
 Since its inception, Peace Day has grown to include millions of people in all parts of the world, and events are organised each year over the week to commemorate and celebrate this idea.
 The theme for 2017 is “Together for Peace: Respect, Safety and Dignity for All.” It honours the spirit of TOGETHER, a global initiative that promotes respect, safety and dignity for everyone, especially those forced to flee their homes in search of a better life.
 Observance by BAPS in London
 Worshippers and visitors joined together to observe Peace Day in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj on 23 September 2017. Swamishri began the observances with the traditional lighting of lamps, while children and youths sang the shanti-paath, an ancient Vedic peace prayer.
 Sharad Patel, 15, read out a statement of prayer and reflection, stating: “Today, we, the members of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, observe the International Day of Peace by sharing the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the inspiration of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 “We pray for our fellow human brothers and sisters suffering in war-torn and conflict-stricken zones, for the bereaved and for those who have lost their lives or have been injured by acts of violence or natural disasters. We also offer our prayers for the orphaned, homeless, displaced, ailing, poor, deprived and disadvantaged and also for those who are tragically fleeing or affected by the spate of recent calamities around the world.”
 Swamishri addressed the assembly, drawing upon the work and teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in promoting the spiritual values underpinning lasting peace. He further elaborated upon the importance of peace within families, which in turn inspires peace in communities and across the world. He concluded by encouraging everyone to adopt the principles of International Peace Day beyond just a single day or week, to make a continuous commitment to instilling peace in our daily lives.

/News/2017/PSM-97th-Birthday-Mahila-Cele.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj 97th Birthday, Mahila Celebration 2017, North America

This December, Mahila devotees across North America came together to celebrate Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 97th birth anniversary and experienced an impactful program filled with skits, speeches, and dances centered around the theme, Pramukh Pratignãne Abhivandanã, meaning "We bow to the pledge taken by Pramukh Swami Maharaj." The program highlighted Pramukh Swami's solemn pledge of serving the needs of individuals and fulfilling the wishes of his gurus Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj.  Pramukh Swami Maharaj sacrificed himself in achieving this commitment through the very end of his earthly presence.  
 Through videos and reenactment of real incidences, the program reminded the audience of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's immense sacrifices in helping those in need, in building individuals with character, and in serving others.  In expressing his humble appreciation, guru Mahant Swami Maharaj has emphasized, "Roon chukvaay j nahi," meaning, "we can never repay him," noting Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s immense service for individuals and society.  
 During Mahant Swami Maharaj’s summer vicharan across North America, Mahila Mandals across North America had expressed their sincere Bhakti through performing seva in support of many programs, offering unique haars and shawls with detailed artwork, and offering donations. Through this celebration, they once again relived the divine smrutis of the summer with Mahant Swami Maharaj reaffirming that Pramukh Swami Maharaj is indeed with us.
 The celebration inspired attendees as they resolved to follow in the examples of their gurus Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2017/PSM-Birthday-Celebration-2017.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj's Birthday Celebration 2017, North America
/News/2017/PSM-Birthday-Celebration-2017.text:
This December, devotees across North America came together to celebrate Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 97th birth anniversary and experienced an impactful program filled with skits, speeches, and dances centered around the theme Pramukhji Aapnu Roon Chukvu Hu Sha Vade. Devotees participated with a renewed spirit, having experienced a summer with guru Mahant Swami Maharaj and developing a loving bond and affection with him.  
 The program brought to life divine memories of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.  Devotees in North America had been fortunate to experience Pramukh Swami Maharaj's bliss during his many trips; and this year, they experienced the same happiness as they joined Mahant Swami Maharaj’s vicharan. Through extended participation in assemblies, question and answer sessions, and spiritual discourses based on "Purshottam Boliya Prite," Mahant Swami Maharaj gave all a revitalized spirit of having Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s laabh in person.
 Throughout the trip, he reminded all of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's sacrifices, his life's dedication to serving everyone, his vision, his inspiration and his efforts as the source of all successes. In expressing his humble appreciation, Mahant Swami Maharaj emphasized, "Roon chukvaay j nahi," meaning, "we can never repay him," noting Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s immense service for individuals and society.  Mahant Swami Maharaj’s time with the devotees of North America, kept the smruti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj alive and renewed personal satsang with a feeling that Pramukh Swami Maharaj "sathej chhe," that he is indeed still with us.
 The celebration inspired attendees as they resolved to imbibe the message of their gurus; “samp” (unity within homes, families, communities, and satsang) and “das na das” (humility in our words and actions).

/News/2017/Padyatra-by-Women-Devotees-12.t: Padyatra by Women Devotees, Kheda, India
/News/2017/Padyatra-by-Women-Devotees-12.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Padyatra (10 photos)
 As part of the year-long festivities celebrating the 97th birthday of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the central office of the BAPS Women’s Wing in Ahemdabad organized a special padyatra (pilgrimage by foot) from BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Atladara to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s birthplace in Chansad. More than 3,000 women devotees from 30 centers from the Kheda Zone participated.
 The pilgrims walked the 12 km distance between 6.00 and 8.10 a.m. with great devotion. While walking, the pilgrims listened to and sang the dhun and bhajans, and some also continuously turned the rosary.
 In Chansad, the pilgrims first had the darshan at the Hanuman Gadhi Mandir, and then the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, where they also performed pradakshinas and offered prostrations. Thereafter, the pilgrims had darshan at the birthplace of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 On their return to Atladara all the pilgrims participated a short assembly, and prayed for the good health and long life of guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2017/Param-Pujya-Mahant-Swami-Maha.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Swamishri meets President (5 photos)
 Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, along with Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and sadhus, visited the State House to meet HE Uhuru Kenyatta, the President of Kenya. Atmaswarup Swami gave a brief introduction of the BAPS, Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj and shared Swamishri’s three messages of humility, respect and service towards all with the president.
 Swamishri prayed for Kenya, “May God bless the whole country with peace, progress and prosperity,” and presented the president with a decorative silver khumb, ‘Transcendence’ and other mementos.
 Many years ago, Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj had presented a rosary (mala) to the president’s father, Mr. Jomo Kenyatta (when he was the president). Remembering this, Swamishri also presented a rosary to the president by putting the rosary around his neck, and then tied a nadachhadi on his wrist.
 After the meeting, the president came all the way to the porch to bid farewell to Swamishri and the sadhus.

 HE Yoweri Museveni, the President of Uganda, sincerely thanked Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj for gracing and blessing Uganda and also took the opportunity to hold Shri Harikrishna Maharaj in his hands and take a picture.
 Since the meeting at the State House took place around 2:30 p.m., Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj very innocently and with a motherly concern asked the president, “When will you have lunch?” The president was touched by Swamishri’s affection and exclaimed emotionally, “Swamishri is worrying about me and my lunch?!”

/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Asthi-K.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Asthi Kumbh Sthapan, Wellingborough, UK
/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Asthi-K.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj Asthi Kumbh Sthapan (25 photos)
 The asthi (holy ashes) of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj were ceremoniously embedded within the Akshar Deri shrine at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Wellingborough, on Wednesday 11 October 2017. Narayanmunidas Swami and visiting swamis from India were in attendance to conduct the historic Asthi Kumbh Sthapan ceremony.
 The ceremony began with swamis singing bhajans and a visual montage of video clips and photographs reminiscing the numerous visits of Pramukh Swami Maharaj to Wellingborough.
 The asthi kumbh (urn of holy ashes) had earlier been blessed by Mahant Swami Maharaj in London on Thursday 5 October 2017, the festival of Sharad Purnima, when also a youth from Wellingborough had been ordained as a parshad.
 The kumbh was ceremoniously brought into the assembly hall on a palanquin carried by swamis. The grand procession included Harikrishna Maharaj, flag-bearing kishores and dancing yuvaks, all fronted by a traditional Indian drummer. The Vedic ceremony itself was led by Narayanmunidas Swami.
 The two-hour programme further consisted of inspiring talks from Akshartilakdas Swami and Narayanmunidas Swami explaining the history and spiritual glory of the Akshar Deri. Mahant Swami Maharaj had also sent his specially recorded blessings for the auspicious occasion.
 The memorable day concluded with devotees paying tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj by placing flowers at the feet of his murti and having darshan of the newly placed asthi.
 Just as the Akshar Deri in Gondal marks the final resting place of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami, Wellingborough’s Akshar Deri, having been consecrated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, now equally marks a similar place of pilgrimage, with his asthi enshrined within.

/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Awarded.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Awarded Certification of Distinction, Preston, UK
/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Awarded.text:
The ‘Certificate of Distinction’ was awarded to His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj by His Worshipful Mayor of Preston, Councillor Brian Rollo, during the Hindu New Year Celebrations at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Preston, on Sunday 22 October 2017. The award was received by Yogvivek Swami, Head Swami of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 The award was in recognition of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s spiritual, humanitarian and charitable contribution to Preston since 1974. Pramukh Swami Maharaj became one of only three individuals to have received this award in the history of the City. The others were Father Timothy Lipscomb for his community services to Preston and Ben Ashworth for his extensive charitable work.
 The Mayor explained that the Council was “delighted to award this certificate of recognition to His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj”. An entry confirming this award will be added into the ‘Book of Friendship, Recognition and Distinction’. This book will be kept in the Mayor’s parlour as a historical record.
 Neetal Parekh, a volunteer at the Mandir, shared her thoughts on the presentation: “Pramukh Swami Maharaj made countless positive contributions in many cities worldwide. Preston was fortunate to have received his blessings. Since his passing last year, there have been similar tributes in cities across the globe.”
 Ambrish Limbachia, also a volunteer at the Mandir added, “Preston’s history dates back prior to the 11th century, and it is remarkable to know that Pramukh Swami Maharaj is one of only three individuals to receive such an award in the long and proud heritage of the City.”

/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Dwar-In.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Dwar Inauguration, Shri Somnath Sanskrit University, Veraval, India
/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Dwar-In.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj Dwar Inauguration (17 photos)
 The grand Pramukh Swami Maharaj Dwar built in honor of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, was inaugurated as the main entrance gate to Shri Somnath Sanskrit University in Veraval.
 The 51-ft. high, 69-ft. wide and 16-ft. deep gate is decorated with the sculpted murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Ved Vyasji, Valmikiji, Saraswatiji and renowned acharyas.
 Following the Vedic mahapuja rituals, the gate was inaugurated by Pujya Swayamprakash Swami (Doctor Swami), Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Veraval MLA Shri Jashubhai Borad, Veraval-Prabhaspatan Nagarpalika President Shri Jagdishbhai Fofandi and Kulpati of Shri Somnath Sanskrit University Shri Arknath Chaudhary and other dignitaries.
 Thereafter, the inauguration assembly featured speeches by senior sadhus and guests, a drama and a dance. Finally, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj’s video blessings were shown. He blessed, “Everyone who passes through this gate will become internally pure.”
 This special occasion was attended by over 2,000 principals, scholars and students from 39 Sanskrit Mahavidyalayas located throughout Gujarat.

/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Shatabd.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Shatabdi Mahotsav: Sud Atham Kirtan Bhakti, UK & Europe
/News/2017/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Shatabd.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Sud Atham Kirtan Bhakti - January 2018 (25 photos)
 As part of the ongoing celebrations to commemorate the birth centenary of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, a series of kirtan bhakti programmes began at various mandirs and centres across the UK and Europe in December 2017.
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj was born on Magshar Sud Atham – the eighth day of the bright half of the Hindu month Magshar. Special kirtan programmes began on Tuesday 26 December 2017 (Posh Sud Atham according to the Hindu calendar). This marked the first in a series of kirtan bhakti events to be held every Sud Atham, and which continued in January 2018.
 Children, youths and senior devotees joined together to sing bhajans extolling the life and saintly virtues of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The events also brought together talented musicians who played a variety of musical instruments to accompany the devotional singing. 
 In addition to the ‘Sud Atham Kirtan Bhakti’ programmes, 100 kirtan aradhanas will take place at mandirs, centres and various other locations across the UK and in Europe until the finale of the centennial celebrations in December 2020.
 The aim of these aradhanas is to pay tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s selfless service to humanity. These aradhanas will also serve to develop devotional talent within individuals and foster unity within groups. 
 The initiative will climax with a final aradhana that will bring together singers and instrumentalists from across the UK and Europe, to provide a fitting and uplifting conclusion to this devotional initiative.

/News/2017/Pushpadolotsav-Celebration-20.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Morning Darshan (13 photos)
 Pushpadolotsav (60 photos)
 Over 70,000 devotees and well-wishers from throughout India, USA, Canada, UK, Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Bahrain, UAE, Australia, New Zealand, Indonesia and many other countries gathered in Sarangpur for the first grand Fuldol celebration in the presence of Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj after the passing away to Akshardham of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj last year.
 The beautifully decorated stage captured the attention of all. The stage background depicted the heavenly scene of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Aksharbrahman Gunatitanand Swami, seated on an adorned hindolo, together with Brahmaswarup Bhagatji Maharaj, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj and Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, blessing the village of Sarangpur from their thrones in Akshardham.
 At the center of the stage was Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj, with sadguru saints and dignitaries seated on both sides.
 The assembly, based on the theme ‘Ej Range, Ej Sange’ (‘The same color, the same association’), revealed that Bhagwan Swaminarayan remains present in the Satsang through the Gunatit Satpurush. The outer appearance of the Satpurush changes, but the divine virtues they exemplify through their inspiring lives remain pristine. The assembly highlighted some of these divine qualities of mahima, spiritual charisma and devotion evident in the lives of both Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Through their speeches, Pujya Doctor Swami, Pujya Kothari Swami, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, Pujya Viveksagar Swami and other learned swamis elaborated upon these qualities to give the inspiring message of living a more meaningful life by offering devotion to Bhagwan, acquiring spiritual knowledge, and living a moral and spiritual life.
 Interspersed between the speeches were engaging videos showing how these various virtues can be seen in the lives of both Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Among the dignitaries present was Gujarat State Education Minister Shri Bhupendrasinh Chudasama, who addressed the assembly, “Seeing this large gathering of devotees here today proves that Pramukh Swami Maharaj is still with us.”
 On this occasion, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj inaugurated several Swaminarayan Aksharpith publications: Vachanamrut app, ‘Gunatitanand Swami: Life & Work’ (English translation) and four new ebooks – ‘Prasangam 2009’, ‘Gems from Shikshapatri’, ‘Hindu Festivals’ and ‘Truth from Under a Tree’.
 Thereafter, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the assembly, emphasizing the necessity of unity and divinity for all to progress on the spiritual path.
 Then, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the pujan and arti of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and sprayed saffron-scented water on Thakorji.
 Finally, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj sat at the front of the stage to spray the devotees with the sanctified saffron-scented water. The devotees joyously departed from Sarangpur drenched by the divine shower of blessings from guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Approximately 8,000 volunteers served in 30 different departments to ensure the efficient planning, preparation and execution of the celebration.

/News/2017/Recognition-of-the-Svminrya%E.t: Recognition of the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā by the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad at Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India
/News/2017/Recognition-of-the-Svminrya%E.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Recognition of the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā by the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad (20 photos)
 Commemorating Brahmasvarūpa Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s first year of passing on 13 Aug 2017 at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, prominent committee members from the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad presented letters of declaration and endorsement for Mahāmahopādyāya Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami’s recently authored Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā – Parabrahman Svāminārāyaṇa Prabodhitam Akṣara-Puruṣottama Darśana – a vādagrantha that offers an exposition, justification, and defence of the Akṣara-Puruṣottama Darśana’s philosophical principles. 
 The Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad is a long-standing esteemed scholarly council and an authority throughout on Vedic studies. Members of the organization, including Mahāmahopādyāya Ācārya Śrī Ramyatna Shuklaji, the adhyakṣa of the Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad; Mahāmahopādyāya Ācārya Śrī Vashistha Tripathiji, the upādhyakṣa of the Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad; and Ācārya Śrī Ramnarayan Dwivediji, the mantrī of the Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad, heralded the Prasthānatrayī-Svāminārāyaṇabhāṣya and the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā as a new and unique contribution to the field of Vedānta philosophy. In addition, Ācārya Śrī Ramesh Kumar Pandeyji, the vice-chancellor of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Rashtriya Sanskrit University and Ācārya Śrī Shivshankar Mishra attended the assembly and offered their support.
 After a chanting of Vedic mantras, Sadhu Munivatsaldas first paid tribute to Brahmasvarūpa Pramukh Swami Maharaj by recalling his selfless life and meaningful works for society. Eminent scholars were thereafter traditionally welcomed with garlands and shawls by Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami, the head of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. The Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad then offered a special tribute to Brahmasvarūpa Pramukh Swami Maharaj and expressed their acclamations for the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā.
 After sharing the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad’s history and significance, Ācārya Śrī Ramesh Kumar Pandeyji asserted, “The renowned scholars of the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad have declared the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā – Parabrahman Svāminārāyaṇa Prabodhitam Akṣara-Puruṣottama Darśana - as a distinct authoritative text and have endorsed the Akṣara-Puruṣottama Siddhānta, which was revealed by Bhagavān Svāminārāyaṇa.”
 Thereafter, the vice-chancellor of Śrī Lal Bahadur Shastri Rashtriya Sanskrit University stated, “People misunderstand that the Svāminārāyaṇa tradition follows the Viśiṣṭādvaita doctrine. Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami has performed admirable work by authoring the first complete epistemological work on the Svāminārāyaṇa tradition. Adorned with Vedic references, pramāṇa mīmāṃsā, prameya mīmāṃsā and kārikās, this vādagrantha spans over 460 pages and is divided into 9 chapters. Reflecting the scholarly style of the ṣaḍdarśana texts and the literary style of Sanskrit, the vādagrantha will become the paramount of the Indian scholastic tradition.” He further emphasized, “Within the history of the Indian academic tradition: from the Vedas till the present day, it has been the first time that a single person has authored both a commentary on the entire Prasthānatrayī and also a vādagrantha of one’s own saṃpradāya. I firmly believe that this vādagrantha will achieve great admiration throughout the world.”
 After Ācārya Śrī Ramnarayan Dwivediji read the letter of endorsement aloud, scholars of the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad presented it to Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami.
 Then, Mahāmahopādyāya Ācārya Śrī Vashistha Tripathiji identified the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā as a unique contemporary work. He added, “Inspired by Brahmasvarūpa Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami framed the Akṣara-Puruṣottama siddhānta, as it was revealed by Bhagavān Svāminārāyaṇa, in the form of a commentary. By doing this, he substantiated the Svāminārāyaṇa saṃpradāya among scholarly circles. Without criticizing others, Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swamiji has expressed the doctrine in a simple yet thoughtful manner that would appeal to ardent seekers of philosophy. For these reasons, the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā is undoubtedly a distinguished vādagrantha.”
 Regarding the scholarship of the Svāminārāyaṇabhāṣya, Śrī Vashisth Tripathi offered in appraisal, “All of the portions of the text that I have read present evidence of concentrated scholarship. There is no instance of plagiarism; it is truly a newly created work. I hope that future generations may further the Svāminārāyaṇa Darśana. May numerous commentaries and discourses on the Svāminārāyaṇabhāṣya be regularly created and organized.”
 After Mahāmahopādyāya Acharya Śrī Vashistha Tripathiji read a copper-plated letter of declaration aloud, scholars of the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad presented the plaque to Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami.
 Thereafter, Mahāmahopādyāya Ācārya Śrī Ramyatna Shuklaji, while recalling the recent acclamation of the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā in Kāśī, expressed, “As the president of the Śrī Kāśī Vidvat Pariṣad, I gathered all of the committee members. Every member was given a copy of the text. After reading the text, all of the members unanimously endorsed the vādagrantha and had nothing but praises for it.”
 Heralding both the Svāminārāyaṇasiddhāntasudhā and the Svāminārāyaṇabhāṣya as exemplary of the scholarly śāstra tradition, Mahāmahopādyāya Ācārya Śrī Ramyatna Shuklaji commented, “I have carefully reviewed all of the texts written by Mahāmahopādyāya Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami. After studying these texts, it is evident that the texts are in accordance with Indian philosophy.” Then, by citing excerpts from the text, Mahāmahopādyāya Ācārya Śrī Ramyatna Shuklaji elaborated on the distinct definitions of ‘Akṣara and ‘Puruṣottama.’
 Addressing the assembly, Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami expressed his immense gratitude to the scholars of Kāśī for being present to pay a special and unique tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj and for endorsing Parabrahman Svāminārāyaṇa’s Akṣara-Puruṣottama Darśana. He then humbly credited his scholarly works to the inspiration he had received from Guru Brahmasvarūpa Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the blessings of Guru Param Pūjya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Sadhu Bhadreshdas Swami concluded the assembly by stating, “The Akṣara-Puruṣottama Darśana was revealed by Bhagavān Svāminārāyaṇa and propounded by the guru-paramaparā. I am forever indebted to have had the opportunity to serve by identifying the principles of the Akṣara-Puruṣottama Darśana within the sacred texts of the Prasthānatrayī and present them in the form of a vādagrantha. The Akṣara-Puruṣottama Darśana is not only confined to texts but is lived as a way of life by thousands of practising devotees of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.”

/News/2017/Regional-Basketball-and-Volle.t: Regional Basketball and Volleyball Yuvak Tournament - Pramukh Cup 2017, Orlando, FL, USA
/News/2017/Regional-Basketball-and-Volle.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Cup 2017 (27 photos)
 On November 11, 2017, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Orlando, FL, hosted the sixth annual Pramukh Cup, a gathering of over 150 yuvaks, 12 centers, 2 trophies, and one goal: Samp. Eighteen volleyball and twenty basketball teams pushed their physical limits to compete and bring back the trophy to their center. At the same token, each participant pushed their spiritual and mental limits to build samp through samjan. When time was called, it was truly magnificent of how opponents made new friends. Each yuvak took the journey and lived by Swami’s ruchi. By keeping samp through seeing divyabhav in their teammates and opponents alike, they realized that each haribhakta is simply divine by his association with the Satpurush.
 As the tournament came to an end, the southeast yuvaks celebrated Atlanta as the winners for volleyball tournament and Orlando as the winners of the basketball tournament. With memories made, each yuvak bid farewell as they eagerly waited for next year’s Pramukh Cup.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, current spiritual leader of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, continues to build on the vision set forth by HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj of imbibing “In the Joy of others, lies our own”. Events like this tournament create an environment for yuvaks to grow together as they cherish, encourage, and thrive in their pursuit of satsang.

/News/2017/Satsang-Activities-Karyakar-S.t: Satsang Activities Karyakar Shibirs: Smaran ane Sangath, India
/News/2017/Satsang-Activities-Karyakar-S.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shibirs (23 photos)
 Around 16,000 men and women volunteers who coordinate the youth and satsang activities in Gujarat attended the 21 Annual Karyakar Shibirs held at Sarangpur, Gondal, Bochasan, Ahmedabad, Atladara, Sankari and Tithal.
 Organized and conducted by the Satsang Activities Central Office, this year’s shibirs were based on the theme ‘Smaran ane Sangath’, in which the volunteers enjoyed the divine memories of Pramukh Swami Maharaj with the understanding that such joy is presently available in the company of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The shibir theme was presented through speeches by the sadguru sadhus and other learned swamis, video shows, workshops, involvement activities and the video blessings of guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2017/Satsang-Prasar--Management-Co.t: Satsang Prasar & Management Conference, UK & Europe
/News/2017/Satsang-Prasar--Management-Co.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Prasar & Management Conference, Leicester (30 photos)
 Satsang Prasar & Management Conference, London (30 photos)
 The 2017 Satsang Prasar & Management Conference for UK and Europe volunteers was held over the weekend of 21 and 22 January at the BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs in Leicester and London. This year’s event marked the meeting’s tenth anniversary and welcomed more than 1,000 delegates.
 The morning session began with video presentations capturing fond memories of the past decade and reminded the attendees of the key spiritual principles of seva that have been reinforced during this time.
 Swamis elaborated on the progress of Satsang activities in the UK and Europe since 2007. Satyavrat Swami continued this journey by outlining some forthcoming initiatives.
 Yogvivek Swami delivered the keynote address to the gathering thereafter, providing encouragement and guidance for all the volunteers to serve together to continue the legacy of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and earn the blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj. He especially highlighted the values of bhakti, humility, unity and spiritual integrity.
 The morning session concluded with a touching video presentation thanking Pramukh Swami Maharaj for his tireless commitment and personal care.
 After lunch, delegates broke off into separate groups to gain more specific information and guidance on how to serve better in their respective seva areas.

/News/2017/Satsang-Pravrutti-Divya-Sanni.t: Satsang Pravrutti Divya Sannidhi Parva, Sarangpur, India
/News/2017/Satsang-Pravrutti-Divya-Sanni.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Divya Sannidhi Parva (40 photos)
 Over 1,300 men and women senior Satsang and Youth Activities volunteers attended this special shibir in the presence of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Based on the theme ‘Bhagya Jagya Re…’, the shibir conveyed to the dedicated volunteers the messages that manifest God has been attained in the form of the Gunatit guru, a rare opportunity has been attained to serve the Satsang and the divine association of such pure sadhus and devotees has been attained.
 In the interactive sessions, the volunteers conducted question-answer forums, presented skits and engaged in a number of other ways with Mahant Swami Maharaj, receiving valuable guidance, inspiration and blessings from him directly. Other senior and experienced sadhus also provided inspiration to the volunteers throughout the shibir.
 During the shibir, the volunteers experienced Mahant Swami Maharaj’s genuine affection towards all.
 The shibir reinforced the resolve of the senior volunteers to continue and improve upon their satsang duties and strengthen their own personal spirituality.

/News/2017/Satsang-Shibir-11895.aspx.t: Satsang Shibir, Los Angeles, CA, USA
/News/2017/Satsang-Shibir-11895.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Sanyukta Shibir (35 photos)
 Devotees from across the region participated in Satsang Shibir in Los Angeles, CA from August 6 - August 7, 2017. The two-day family shibir took place in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.  Following the theme of Bhagya Jagya Re,  the shibir helped understand how fortunate we are for being blessed with the company of God and His pragat, or ever-present, gunatit sant.
 Senior Swamis from India explained how constantly thinking of the greatness of God and His gunatit sant helps us realize that their power and strength is enough for us to eradicate all of our base desires. They also explained how this also implies thinking of the glory of God’s devotees. This enables us to overlook people’s minor faults and develop a positive outlook on life and those around us. 
 Through his guidance and continuous vicharan, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj encourages and inspires spiritual living, nurtures faith in all individuals, promotes family values and unity, and strengthens communities small and large.
 Through events like this shibir, attendees can further develop their samjan (understanding), mahima (faith), and impact the community as a whole through seva (selfless service) and samp (unity). The value of spirituality passed down by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, and our Guru Parampara continues to impact the lives of countless individuals through devotion and prayer.

/News/2017/Satsang-Shibir-Scotland-11484.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Shibir (10 photos)
 More than 60 adults and children from various parts of Scotland gathered at the Uphall Community Education Centre in Edinburgh on Sunday 16 April 2017 for an enlightening one-day satsang shibir.
 The theme of the shibir was Hinduism and was held in the presence of Tyagprakash Swami and Amrutkirtan Swami. The topics focused on various aspects of Hinduism as a religion and way of life.
 Sadhus delivered insightful discourses, which included scriptural references detailing the importance and attributes of rituals in daily living. This was followed by a detailed discourse clarifying the concepts of karma and moksha.
 Key messages of the shibir were reinforced by various multimedia and audio-visual presentations.
 In the second half of the shibir, delegates had the opportunity to participate in fun-filled activities. This was followed by an enlightening discourse on atmanishtha, before the concluding session which covered the guru-shishya relationship and how moksha is attained by the guru’s grace.
 By the end of the shibir, delegates had gained a much deeper understanding of Hinduism, its key concepts and how to practice them in their daily lives. Participants thoroughly enjoyed the day and shared positive feedback. Jigisha, a mother of two from Aberdeen, shared, “I especially appreciated the practicality of the teachings for my family and the easy-to-understand way they were presented.”

/News/2017/Satsang-Shibir-in-the-Presenc.t: Satsang Shibir in the Presence of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, UK & Europe
/News/2017/Satsang-Shibir-in-the-Presenc.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Shibir (35 photos)
 Children's Shibir (40 photos)
 A one-day Satsang shibir was held in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj on Saturday 17 June 2017 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 Titled ‘Satpurush: The Gunatit Legacy’, the event brought together delegates from across the UK and Europe who consolidated – in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj himself – the vital spiritual understanding of God’s continual presence on earth through the Gunatit Satpurush.
 The programme began in the morning with darshan of Swamishri’s puja. He then presided over the traditional deep pragatya opening ceremony with representative karyakars.
 The key concepts of the shibir were delivered through a series of enlightening discourses and panel discussions by sadhus visiting from India, including Atmaswarup Swami and Narayanmuni Swami. They drew upon the divine characteristics of the Satpurush as well as his unique, direct relationship with God.
 Swamishri’s sevaks also shared heart-warming accounts of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s selfless love for devotees, drawing upon the personal care and attention that he extends to all. They encouraged the gathering to develop a deep spiritual bond with the Satpurush to strengthen their own relationship with Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj graced the shibir in the final session of the morning, which involved interactive games to reflect upon the messages from the earlier session. The delegates were able to express their understanding of Swamishri’s wishes by raising coloured cards in response to various questions and scenarios. A small group activity further illustrated the importance of unity and harmony.
 Swamishri addressed the audience at various intervals to offer his personal guidance. He concluded the session by sharing the universal message of ‘Ghar Sabha’ that he had personally hand-written on a whiteboard, thereby encouraging all satsangis to gather regularly in their homes to discuss satsang concepts and strengthen their family bond. He emphasised that this was the most effective tool to develop peace and harmony in the home and address life’s various challenges.
 A special shibir was also organised for children that ran concurrently throughout the day with the main shibir. The programme began with an insight into the life and spiritual importance of the Satpurush.
 Swamishri arrived at the shibir, to the delight of the young children, shortly after 11.30am. He was formally welcomed into the hall by a ‘guard of honour’ comprising young children and was presented with decorative garlands and shawl that had been prepared by the balaks and balikas for his visit.
 A memorable session with Swamishri followed where children interacted with him using a variety of toys and games which revealed underlying spiritual messages for the young delegates. A short question-answer session with Mahant Swami Maharaj provided invaluable guidance and cherished memories for everyone present. Swamishri reinforced the key principles of the Akshar-Purushottam upasana through an annotated drawing that he had prepared especially for the shibir. Before departing, he stopped to sanctify a variety of artwork and poetry that children had prepared for the shibir.

 Visits to Tribal Villages (14 photos)
 From the second 2017 batch of the Yuva Talim Kendra, 61 youths, divided into 25 groups, visited a total of 150 tribal villages in the Ukai region. They also made 385 home visits to reinforce these values and unity within families.

/News/2017/Sharad-Purnima-Celebrations-2.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Sharad Purima Celebration (32 photos)
 To commemorate Aksharbrahman Gunatitanand Swami’s 233rd birthday, three special celebrations were held in the presence of Pujya Swayamprakash Swami (Doctor Swami), Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Pujya Ghanshyamcharan Swami, and other swamis and devotees.
 At 5.45 a.m. the Amalsar Sthapan Vidhi of the new Yogi Smruti Mandir being constructed was performed to the accompaniment of Vedic verses.
 After the initial rituals, all the sadguru saints went up to the mandir spire to ritually place the amalsar in position a top the shikhar.
 Thereafter, the sadguru saints planted trees on the opposite banks of the Akshar Ghat, where the State Tourism Department will be building a riverfront.
 The second celebration, at 10.30 a.m., was the first annual ritual bath in the Akshar and Brahma Kunds, where Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj had ritually placed the sacred ashes of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj and Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj in October 2016.
 The day’s third celebration was the 233rd Birth Anniversary Celebration which began at 7.30 p.m. The program featured speeches, bhajans, skits and videos highlighting the glory of Gunatitanand Swami as the first manifest form of Aksharbrahman. The celebration assembly concluded with the inspiring video blessings of guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2017/Shilanyas-Mahotsav-for-New-BA.t: Shilanyas Mahotsav for New BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Mayfair, Johannesburg, South Africa
/News/2017/Shilanyas-Mahotsav-for-New-BA.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shilanyas Ceremony (42 photos)
 On 20 March 1960, from the banks of the Limpopo River, which divides South Africa and Zimbabwe (previously, Rhodesia), Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj blessed the devotees of South Africa that Satsang will flourish in South Africa.
 Through these blessings and the tireless efforts of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj the Satsang has indeed flourished in South Africa.
 Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed the murti-pratishtha of the first BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Johannesburg in 1991. Since then, Satsang has continued to develop, with BAPS mandirs now also in Lenasia, Durban, Pretoria, Cape Town, Tzaneen and Benoni.
 However, it was Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s vision to make a grand mandir and a haveli (a cultural complex) in South Africa. After much effort, suitable land was acquired and detailed plans were prepared with the help of architects from India and South Africa.
 The first steps in fulfilling the blessings of Pujya Yogiji Maharaj and the vision of Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj were taken in the divine presence of Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj on Saturday 25 March 2017 (Falgun vad 12, Vikram Samvat 2073) when over 3,000 devotees and well-wishers participated in the the grand Shilanyas Mahotsav (foundation stone-laying ceremony).
 The ceremony began with a Vedic mahapuja in which all participants performed the mahapuja along with guruhari Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj. Towards the end of the Vedic mahapuja, Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj sat near the shila pit and placed a beautiful kalash and five gold-painted bricks into the pit to inaugurate the grand project. Thereafter, Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj went around the whole land to bless it.
 In the assembly, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami highlighted the need for the mandir and haveli and the benefits it will bring to the society at large. Distinguished guests and dignitaries were present from around the country. They welcomed Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj and received his blessings.
 In his blessings to the assembly, Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj talked about the ultimate glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the guru parampara. He also emphasized the need to focus on doing bhajan, explaining that the main reason for building a mandir and haveli here is so that everyone can all focus on doing bhajan. He also highlighted the need for unity to accomplish such a grand project.
 After Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj’s blessings, everyone present got an opportunity to place a brick in the foundation pit before departing. More than 5,000 bricks were placed in the foundation.

/News/2017/Shishu-Karyakar-Shibir-Atmabu.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shibir (9 photos)
 With the inspiration of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the Shishu Mandal was established in India in 2004 – the 50th anniversary of BAPS’s children’s activities. Shishu mandals are special spiritual assemblies and activities designed for children between the ages of 3 and 10. Today, there are more than 1,000 shishu mandals in India alone that are led by 1600 volunteers. To further the development of these dedicated volunteers, one-day seminars were held in Rajkot and Sankri on 30 September and 2 October respectively.
 Based on the theme of Atmabuddhi, the shibir focused on fostering an environment which fosters a greater relationship with the Satpurush. P. Atmatrupt Swami and P. Dhyanjivan Swami and other learned sadhus discussed the meaning, purpose and methods of atmabuddhi with the attendees. To help better understand how children learn and relate to others, a session on Child Psychology was integral to the seminar. To help children and volunteers to make Satsang and the Satpurush a part of their daily lives, sadhus from the Children’s Activities Central Office conducted workshops on how to teach children about shishu sabha, daily puja, and panchang pranam.
 Concluding the seminar, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the shibir and said, “These are not children; they are souls from Akshardham. That they have a sense of oneness with the Sant is our seva. This seva will guarantee our liberation.”

/News/2017/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Ram Navmi Celebration 2017, North America
/News/2017/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.text:
April 5th, 2017, Chaitra Sud Nom, marks the birthday of Bhagwan Ram and the 236th birthday of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. To celebrate this joyous occasion, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandirs across North America held samaiyos centralized around the theme: "Bhaktavatsal Hari Birud Tiharo," meaning Bhagwan Swaminarayan's resolve to care for his devotees.  The emcees, drama skits, story, and dances explained how Bhagwan Ram and Maharaj had always cared for their devotees and how those devotees came to have such a firm resolve in them.
  In Vachnamrut Vadtal-19, Maharaj has said "Whenever a jiva attains a human body in Bharat-khand, God's avatars or God's sadhus will certainly also be present on earth at that time. If that jiva can recognize them, then he becomes a devotee of God... Also, whatever a devotee of God wishes for comes true." This samaiyo brought to life examples of Maharaj guiding the devotees of that time by removing their swabhavs, making their antahkarans pure and ultimately giving them moksha. Celebrating Swaminarayan Jayanti honored Maharaj's work in reforming Hinduism and instilling a strong sense of Ekantik Dharma in all of his haribhaktos. His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj cultivated these same values within devotees and today, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, is continuing to do the same and guiding devotees toward moksha.

/News/2017/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti-Mah.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti Mahila Celebration 2017, North America
/News/2017/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti-Mah.text:
Chaitra Sud Nom marks the birth of both Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Ram.  The women of BAPS North America celebrated both auspicious events by presenting a cultural program with the theme of  Vachan Vahlaji nu shir se hoon dharu.  Speeches, drama skits, emcees, and cultural dances reiterated the stories of Bhagwan Ram's and Bhagwan Swaminarayan's mission to instill Ekantik Dharma and guide people towards the path of moksha. The audience saw many examples of how devotees during Bhagwan Swaminarayan's and Bhagwan Ram's time took firm refuge in Bhagwan himself.  And Bhagwan in turn showered His compassion upon these devotees: saving them from physical harm, leading them away from the path of kusang, and ultimately giving them the bliss of liberation. 
 The event renewed the audience's understanding of Bhagwan Swaminarayan's greatness and their passion for following His aagnas. They were reminded that although Bhagwan Swaminarayan was no longer physically on this Earth, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj have been able to engender dharma amongst thousands of individuals, encouraging them to lead more virtuous lives by becoming vegetarian, by refraining from alcohol and drugs use, and by abstaining from gambling. The take home message, which resonated with many of the attendees, was to develop the same firm resolution that the devotees had during the times of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Ram.

/News/2017/South-London-Din-12071.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 South London Din (30 photos)
 A special satsang sabha was organised in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj at Beddington Conference Centre in Croydon, London, on Wednesday 27 September 2017.
 The sabha was attended by devotees from South London and nearby areas. South London is one of the largest Satsang centres in the UK, with volunteers and worshippers in the area preparing meticulously and eagerly for Swamishri's visit.
 Upon arrival, Swamishri planted a tree outside the complex before taking given a tour of the multi-storey conference centre.
 When Swamishri arrived for the evening assembly, children and youths greeted him with a garland of flowers as part of a traditional welcome. Swamishri was then joyously received with rapturous applause inside the assembly hall.
 Swamis had begun the evening programme with bhajans after which they spoke of Swamishri’s tireless efforts to bless countless people around the world, sharing inspiring accounts of his saintliness and devotion. Children and youths also presented a historical overview of the satsang activities in South London over the years.
 In his blessings, Swamishri recognised the enthusiasm of the local devotees and encouraged them to strengthen their faith in God and maintain their steadfastness in their spiritual endeavours.
 Swamishri wrote a concluding message of ‘samp, suhradbhav and ekta’ which was shared with the congregation. He also sanctified food items to be served as prasad to the devotees.

/News/2017/Students-Medico-Spiritual-Con.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Students' Medico-Spiritual Conference (13 photos)
 Over 560 university students from throughout Gujarat studying medicine, dentistry, physiotherapy and other healthcare courses attended the special medico-spiritual conference for students.
 Based on the theme ‘Abhaydaan – I Will Always Be With You’, the conference took place in the presence of Pujya Swayamprakash Swami (Doctor Swami), Pujya Viveksagar Swami and other learned swamis.
 The shibir focused on Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s blessings that the Satpurush is forever present on earth. This understanding was elaborated upon through speeches, workshops, group discussions, videos and other activities.

/News/2017/Supporting-Saree-in-a-Gadi-fo.t: Supporting ‘Saree in a Gadi’ for ‘Save Girl, Educate Girl’ Campaign, UK
/News/2017/Supporting-Saree-in-a-Gadi-fo.text:
Photo Gallery 
 'Saree in a Gadi' Rally (13 photos)
 More than 100 women dressed in red sarees embarked on a car rally from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Sunday 7 June 2017 to raise awareness of the ‘Save Girl, Educate Girl’ women empowerment and education campaign.
 The campaign was initiated by Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi to bring an end to the gender-selective abortion of female foetuses – a practise that occurs in India and many other parts of the world for assumed cultural reasons that span centuries.
 The ‘Saree in a Gadi’ rally was led by Bharulata Kamble of Navsari, India, with support from BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK. Ms Kamble recently broke a world record in becoming the first woman to drive alone through the Arctic Circle and 32,000 kilometres from England to India, propagating the vital messages of this campaign along her journey.
 The event was flagged off in traditional Hindu manner at the Mandir in the presence of local Member of Parliament, Rt. Hon. Dawn Butler MP. Before departing, the women also held a minute’s silence in prayer and remembrance of all those affected by the recent attacks in London and Manchester. 
 The rally stopped at the BAPS Swaminarayan mandir in Wellingborough to spread awareness to guests and worshippers there, before reaching BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Leicester. The participants received a grand reception from volunteers of the Mandir as well as the Lord Mayor of Leicester, Cllr Rashmikant Joshi.
 In the words of the late Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, scientist and former President of India, “When women are empowered, a society of stability is assured.” This rally was a great gesture of solidarity by women across the globe, raising awareness and empowering the less fortunate with the same basic human rights of respect, education and also the right to live.
 Speaking about her work and messages, Ms Kamble said: “It’s been perceived that Indian women are not active in adventurous activities, and I was happy to break that perception through my journey. The event aimed to mobilise non-resident Indians (NRIs) to act as brand ambassadors for the cause to support girls and their education.”
 Rena Amin, a senior BAPS volunteer, added, “We’re very proud to support the inspiring work of ‘Save Girl, Educate Girl’ and share their important values and messages. The remarkable story of Bharulata Kamble and the many women who joined the rally shows the profound impact that women can make if they are given the opportunities and their voices are heard.”
 The rally continues BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha’s continued commitment to women’s activities. Bharulata Kamble was a guest at the International Women’s Day celebrations held at London Mandir in March. London Mandir also recently welcomed Kranti (Revolution) from Mumbai to support their summer tour of women empowerment.
