 London Mandir History: A Photo Story (60 photos)
 The year-long celebrations marking the 25th anniversary of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, culminated with an eye-opening and gripping documentary-style production that explored the Mandir’s rich history, challenging creation, and profound international impact.
 The four-hour finale programme featured a compilation of audio clips, photographs and unseen video footage charting its inception from Yogiji Maharaj’s vision through to the inauguration of Europe’s first traditional stone mandir and its lasting legacy.
 The journey began with an insight into the arduous search for suitable land as well as the challenging economic climate in the early 1990s. Narrations from senior swamis, volunteers and devotees revealed Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s unshakeable faith and personal connection that inspired devotees to join a ‘labour of love’ and offer their heartwarming personal sacrifices.
 A few days before the Mandir’s opening on 20 August 1995, a magnificent procession took place through the streets of London. Iconic images of Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessing the people of London from a decorated dais at Piccadilly Circus brought back treasured memories for many who were witness to the historic occasion.
 Following its inauguration, the Mandir harnessed the efforts and collective spirit of thousands of volunteers who served individuals and families to create a better community, a better nation and a better world. This profound impact has been acknowledged by some of the country’s most prominent individuals. A selection of these, including HRH The Prince of Wales and British Prime Minister Boris Johnson, shared their messages of goodwill and gratitude through personal testimonies.
 The Mandir’s opening sparked an explosion of local, national and international media coverage, paying homage to its glorious addition to the London skyline and religious landscape of Great Britain. A selection of this coverage also featured in the programme.
 Over the last 25 years, the Mandir has provided hope for countless people in the most adverse of circumstances. Viewers learned about some of these life-changing inspirations through powerful and emotive testimonies.
 On behalf of all devotees, a young boy offered a concluding prayer inscribed on a paper swan with sentiments of gratitude to Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj for the gift of London Mandir.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj responded to the prayer by saying: “Today we celebrate 25 years of London Mandir. A day we were all meant to be together. But not a moment has passed where we have been apart. Pramukh Swami Maharaj made this mandir so that you can make yours within your hearts. Your hearts are my mandir, forever my home. We will meet again and reunite – together as a family; together as one.”
 His swan joined more than 10,000 others that were created by devotees and placed inside the assembly hall as a symbol of togetherness with him. It marked a fitting end to the overarching theme of the programme, with Mahant Swami Maharaj having written on his swan: “London Mandir is Our Home.”

/News/2020/Mahant-Swami-Maharajs-87th-Ja.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mahant Swami Maharaj's 87th Janma Jayanti Celebrations, London, UK (20 photos)
 Mahant Swami Maharaj's 87th Janma Jayanti Celebrations at Home, UK & Europe (40 photos)
 The 87th birthday anniversary of Mahant Swami Maharaj was joyously celebrated with a series of enlightening and devotional online programmes throughout the UK and Europe from 11 to 13 September 2020.
 The celebrations began on Friday 11 September – Mahant Swami Maharaj’s birthdate according to the Hindu calendar – with morning darshan of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s puja from Nenpur in India. 
 A special online evening programme explored Mahant Swami Maharaj’s ruchi (innermost wishes) for aspirants to help them progress on their spiritual path. The programme began with Mahant Swami Maharaj’s personal experiences of understanding and fulfilling Yogiji Maharaj’s ruchi.
 Video testimonies from swamis around the world as well as discourses, letters and a panel discussion explored three key ruchis of Mahant Swami Maharaj that he frequently emphasises – unity, humility, and satsang depth. The presentations elaborated upon each in the life of Swamishri himself and included examples of how he has inspired them in others through his teachings.
 The interactive programme provided opportunities for families to participate at home by decorating their ghar mandirs, creating birthday cards and baking celebratory cakes as a devotional offering. As a mark of reverence, families also offered flower petals and rice grains to the murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Mahant Swami Maharaj as well as the Satsang Diksha scripture that he recently authored.
 The celebrations continued on Saturday evening with the first of a two-part parva during the Kishore-Kishori and Yuvak-Yuvati Mandal sabha, themed “Ej Rang, Ej Sang”, which explored the similar virtues of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The morning of Sunday 13 September – Mahant Swami Maharaj’s birthday according to the Gregorian calendar – began with the darshan of Swamishri’s puja from Nenpur, India. Swamis in London, Nairobi, Houston, Atlanta and Robbinsville sang celebratory kirtans via video conference facilities to mark the auspicious occasion.
 Later in the morning, the Bal-Balika Mandal sabha celebrated Mahant Swami Maharaj’s life and showed children how they can grow spiritually closer to their guru.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj’s birth celebrations were also marked with a special three-hour ‘virtual sabha’ on Sunday afternoon, with discourses by senior and learned swamis from around the world. The presentations – available in English, Gujarati and Hindi – along with bhajans and video montages, delved into the exemplary life of Mahant Swami Maharaj. Specifically, they elaborated upon a collection of his spiritual virtues – humility, purity, compassion, faith, saintliness and a universal connection with all – that have provided peace and fulfilment in the lives of countless people.
 In his blessings, Mahant Swami Maharaj paid tribute to the life and works of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and explained how maintaining unity, remaining humble and supporting one another is a foundational part of one’s spiritual endeavours.
 Thousands around the world concluded the celebrations by performing the mantra-pushpanjali and arti at home in a collective global offering.
 The mahilas of UK & Europe also celebrated Mahant Swami Maharaj’s birthday with a special online programme on Sunday 20 September 2020.

/News/2020/Mahila-Celebrations--London-M.t: Mahila Celebrations | London Mandir 25th Anniversary, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Mahila-Celebrations--London-M.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mahila Celebrations Online Programme (40 photos)
 Mahila Celebrations at Home, UK & Europe (20 photos)
 A special online programme for mahilas was webcast on Saturday 15 August as part of the series of events celebrating the 25th anniversary of London Mandir.
 The programme, titled ‘Sarvasva Arpanam: Inspiration, Creation and Celebration’, centred on the inspirational sacrifices by women that made the Mandir possible and their continuing contributions over the last 25 years.
 The documentary-style production drew upon rare video footage, historical photographs and personal accounts from young and senior devotees.
 Women shared their experiences of the incredible sacrifices made to raise funds for the Mandir as well as their physical seva during its construction – all whilst continuing to support their families and further their own careers. They creatively presented the six-day Mandir Mahotsav festival through a series of couplets, narrations and drawings. Their vivid descriptions and treasured personal memories brought to life the divine atmosphere of the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj in 1995.
 Over the last 25 years, the Mandir has brought together multiple generations and supported countless women through every stage of their life journey. Its profound impact on the wider community was illustrated through written and recorded messages from prominent figures, led by the Secretary of State for the Home Department, Rt Hon Priti Patel. She reflected on the Mandir’s contribution to London’s “multi-culturalism” and the way in which “it has brought together people of all faiths and no faiths and all backgrounds”.
 Carolyn Downs, CEO of Brent Council, described the Mandir as “one of the most important sights in Britain”. Dame Cressida Dick, Head of London’s Metropolitan Police Service, praised the Mandir’s work “in promoting universal values of social stability, moral dignity, family unity, cultural harmony, moral integration and global responsibility”. Dawn Butler, MP for Brent Central, spoke of the experience of “peace, calmness and serenity” during her visits, and commended the Mandir’s support for the community during the Covid-19 pandemic.
 The celebrations concluded with heartfelt prayers of gratitude from all women who pledged to uphold the Mandir’s noble values of charity and service for generations to come.
 Radhika Patel, aged 20, shared her impressions of the programme: “Learning about the commitment and dedication of women to help create this magnificent mandir has provided me with even more motivation to serve like they have. I also now understand the sacrifices that my mother and grandmother and many other women made to fulfil the vision of Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj.”
 The 2.5-hour programme vividly revealed how and why women of all ages are an indispensable part of the Mandir’s past, present and future.

/News/2020/Mandir-Darshan--Abhishek--Lon.t: Mandir Darshan & Abhishek | London Mandir 25th Anniversary, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Mandir-Darshan--Abhishek--Lon.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mandir Darshan & Abhishek (40 photos)
 A special opportunity for mandir darshan and abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj was organised as part of the 25th anniversary celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 In the interest of public health and the safety of all devotees and visitors, the Mandir had closed on Friday 13 March 2020 due to the global coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. However, the Mandir still continues to meet the spiritual needs of worshippers and the community by providing a deep spiritual connection through its daily webcast services and weekly online programmes.
 Between 12 and 20 August, as permitted by local authorities, devotees were given the opportunity to visit the Mandir by registering through an online booking system. It offered devotees a chance to offer private worship while observing the government’s health protocols.
 Visitors were required to wear face coverings, while clear markings were displayed across the complex to ensure a safe social distance was maintained throughout. Sanitizing stations at key junctures allowed devotees to wash their hands regularly. Many other safety measures had also been implemented to minimise risks.
 After devotees had enjoyed darshan in the upper sanctum and abhishek in the lower chamber, swamis greeted seniors, youths and children from a safe distance in the corridor. Their interactions added to a truly memorable and uplifting experience for the devotees.
 Harish Depala shared his thoughts following his visit: “I was overjoyed that my five-year-old son could see the swamis, even if it was from a distance. Seeing them made his day and the visit was memorable for so many reasons. It has been a challenging time for so many. This visit has given a deep sense of peace and stability for my family.”
 Naiya Patel, aged 10, added, “Seeing the murtis again in person was amazing. I am so happy to have this chance to visit the Mandir.”

 Grand Nagar Yatra (Procession) Launches New Mandir Inauguration Festivities
 28 January 2020, Navsari
 A grand procession through the main streets of Navsari city marked the start of the three-day festivities to commemorate the consecration of the murtis in the new BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir.
 Stretching for 1.5 km, the procession consisted of over 60 creative attractions, including beautifully decorated chariots housing the various murtis, youths on horseback and motorcycles, children and youths performing a variety of traditional dances, BAPS sadhus and youths singing devotional bhajans, tribal youths playing drums, youths carrying lighted torches (mashals), women devotees carrying kalashes (auspicious water pots) and other presentations.
 The participation of over 300 BAPS sadhus and 4,000 devotees from Gujarat and abroad enhanced the devout atmosphere created by the procession.
 Thousands of local residents joyously and devoutly welcomed the procession along the 4 km route by showering flower petals on and offering garlands to the murtis. The murtis cast their divine gaze upon the city to bless all the residents.
 Senior BAPS sadhus and Shri Piyushbhai Desai (MLA, Navsari) performed the initial pujan rituals to flag off the procession.
 The procession set off from the Garda College Hostel grounds at 2.30 p.m. and concluded at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir at 7.00 p.m. in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Yagna For World Peace
 29 January 2020, Navsari
 The highlight of the second day of festivities to commemorate the inauguration of the new BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Navsari was the grand Yagna for World Peace.
 From 8.00 p.m. to 12 noon, around 3,750 yajmans, seated around 380 yagna altars, participated in the Vedic rituals. They were guided through the rituals by 100 learned Brahmins.
 The main yagna rituals were performed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj at the main yagna altar. He also performed the pujan and arti of the murtis to be consecrated.
 Blessing the devotees, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “A grand new mandir has been built in Navsari. May all enjoy good health and all-round prosperity. By serving God in even a small way, you will earn his infinite blessings. He will fulfil your sincere and noble prayers. All should regularly visit the mandir for darshan and to offer devotion.”
 New BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir Consecrated by Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj
 30 January 2020, Navsari
 On this auspicious day of Vasant Panchami (Maha sud 5), over 20,000 devotees and wellwishers from India and around the world gathered at the 10-acre BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir campus to celebrate the consecration ceremony of the grand new BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir performed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 At 7.00 a.m., the consecration (murti-pratishtha) rituals of the murtis began with a celebratory procession along the 900ft-long Gajendra Pith circling the mandir base. From 9.00 p.m., senior BAPS sadhus and over 900 devotees participated in the consecration mahapuja rituals under the main mandir dome, while thousands of devotees watched the live relay of the ceremonies on large LED screens in the assembly hall.
 Thereafter, at 10.30 a.m. Mahant Swami Maharaj ritually inaugurated the main gate of the mandir and released balloons from the mandir podium. Then, Swamishri and sadguru swamis performed the main consecration and pujan rituals of all the murtis in the various shrines of the marble mandir.
 At the conclusion of the Vedic consecration rituals, Mahant Swami Maharaj, sadguru swamis and everyone present performed the first arti of the consecrated murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, Shri Nilkanth Varni (abhishek murti), Shri Guru Parampara (marble murtis), Shri Radhakrishna Dev, Shri Sita-Ram and Shri Hanumanji and Shri Shiv-Parvati and Shri Ganeshji.
 Blessing the gathered devotees, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “May all the residents of Navsari and everyone be blessed with good health and prosperity and may everyone be spiritually strengthened by the mandir. May all strengthen unity and experience inner peace.”
 More than 2,500 male and female BAPS volunteers served during the 3-day festivities.
 Thereafter, all through the day till 9.30 p.m., more than 37,000 devotees and well-wishers came for darshan of the mandir.
 Mandir Features
 This mandir is built of Rajnagar marble and has the following main features:
 • 5 towering shikhars (pinnacles)
 • 2 main domes; 17 secondary domes
 • 19 golden kalashes (auspicious water pots)
 • Height= 82 ft; Length = 205 ft; Width= 188 ft
 • 222 intricately carved pillars and 150 arches
 • Over 44 statues of divinities and inspiring devotees.
 The numerous activities managed from the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Navsari include:
 • Over 150 satsang centres providing inspiring messages and practical spiritual guidance to people of all ages and backgrounds.
 • Over 100 children’s centres providing children and youngsters with character-building and academic encouragement.
 • 12 kutir mandirs in the Dang-Vasda region and around 50 regular assembly for spiritual and cultural inspiration.
 • School and hostel in Rambhas for 200 underprivileged tribal students.
 • 2 mobile ambulances providing free medical treatment and health guidance to tribal communities.
 • Deaddiction campaigns to motivate and guide people to shed addictions and other harmful habits.

/News/2020/Matru-Devo-Bhava-Celebrating-.t: Matru-Devo Bhava: Celebrating the Mother-Child Bond, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Matru-Devo-Bhava-Celebrating-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Matru-Devo Bhava, UK & Europe (40 photos)
 A special event celebrating the loving bond between mothers and children was streamed live across the UK and Europe from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Sunday 22 March 2020. This annual event, titled ‘Matru-Devo Bhava,’ was viewed by families in their respective homes due to the closure of all BAPS mandirs and centres in response to the global COVID-19 pandemic.
 The programme began with a recital of selected Sanskrit verses from the Upanishads which depict values of respect and reverence towards mothers. A short mahapuja was then performed by families to pray for all those affected by the pandemic and to strengthen family unity as they observed the Government appeal to ‘Stay At Home’.
 An insightful video was shown that highlighted the various roles that mothers perform day in day out. The poignant images helped children to understand and appreciate the tireless efforts of their respective mothers. 
 An interactive quiz and a specially designed word search further strengthened this bond by providing an informal platform to help mothers and children better understand one another and offer heartfelt pledges.
 Video blessings from Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj were also relayed in which they emphasised that ‘Matru-Devo Bhava’ is a learning that should be imbibed in one’s everyday family life.
 The programmes were brought to a close with children bowing down to their mothers – a traditional Hindu gesture of veneration. 
 The heart-warming programme left positive impressions upon all those who joined in online. A mother from Coventry who watched and participated in the programme, wrote, “I thoroughly enjoyed the webcast today. This was exactly what we needed right now! Thank you for making it a very special Mother’s Day for our family.”

/News/2020/Myanmar-President-Win-Myint-V.t: Myanmar President Win Myint Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India
/News/2020/Myanmar-President-Win-Myint-V.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Akshardham Visit (13 photos)
 Myanmar President Win Myint and First Lady Daw Cho Cho visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi as part of an official state visit to India. The 28-member Myanmar delegation also included the Union Minister for International Cooperation Mr. U Kyaw Tin, Union Minister for Religious Affairs and Culture Mr. Thura U Aung Ko, Union Minister for Transport and Communications Mr. U Thant Sin Maung, Chief Minister Rakhine State Mr. U Nyi Pu and Myanmar Ambassador to India Mr. Moe Kyaw Aung.
 President Myint was traditionally greeted by Gnanmuni Swami on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the sixth spiritual leader of BAPS.
 “I am delighted to pay a visit to the Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, home to rich art and architecture that demonstrates the rich culture and traditions of Hinduism,” President Mynit said.
 President Myint, along with the delegation offered their respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and performed abhishek to share sentiments for world peace and harmony.
 The Myanmar delegation then viewed the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth) that features 148 lifelike carved stone elephants depicting messages of social harmony, peace, and spirituality. They also experienced the Sanskruti Vihar boat ride exhibition that displays 10,000 years of India’s heritage and contributions to society.

/News/2020/National-Day-of-Prayer-and-Ac.t: National Day of Prayer and Action, UK & Europe
/News/2020/National-Day-of-Prayer-and-Ac.text:
The COVID-19 global pandemic has brought uncertainty and unrest on an unprecedented scale. At a time when world leaders and scientists are doing all they can to manage and ultimately overcome the virus, people of faith have also come together to contribute.
 In the UK, Sunday 22 March 2020 was declared as a ‘National Day of Prayer and Action’, inviting people of prayer across all faiths to unite and seek help, solace and strength from God.
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha observed the day with a special abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. 
 The ceremony began with the auspicious lighting of the divo while the Shanti Paath, an ancient Vedic peace prayer, was sung.  
 Swamis prayed for all those affected around the world by the disease, and paid tribute to the healthcare professionals and frontline personnel who are working tirelessly to help the afflicted. They also prayed for the families who have sadly lost loved ones.
 The ceremony was streamed live online with devotees around the UK and in Europe joining with the abhishek of Nilkanth Varni simultaneously in their homes. 
 During the abhishek, swamis at the mandir and thousands in their respective homes recited the 108 auspicious and liberating names of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Together, they offered their personal and heartfelt prayers.
 Although separated by physical distance, worshippers were connected digitally, side by side through technology, with a common and profound sense of devotion and prayer. 
 A mother from Watford who performed the ceremony at home with her family shared, “Thank you for organising the wonderful and divine abhishek. My husband and I are on the front line serving patients and risking our health daily. These prayers have given me the strength to confront this challenge. I have prayed to Maharaj [Bhagwan Swaminarayan] and Guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj to protect me, my family and my colleagues and for all those who have suffered through this terrible tragedy.”

/News/2020/New-Years-Day-Mahapuja-for-Fa.t: New Year's Day Mahapuja for Family Harmony and World Peace, UK & Europe
/News/2020/New-Years-Day-Mahapuja-for-Fa.text:
A special New Year’s Day family mahapuja to pray for world peace and foster family harmony was conducted at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, and broadcasted live to other BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK and in Europe on Wednesday 1 January 2020.
 The ceremonial rituals were conducted by swamis from the Mandir’s inner sanctum and relayed live inside the prayer hall of the Mandir as well as mandirs and several centres around the UK and parts of Europe.
 Sitting with their families, more than 5,800 individuals – from young children through to senior citizens – participated simultaneously across the region. During the mahapuja, swamis and participants prayed for peace to prevail in their homes, communities and across the world. 
 Mahant Swami Maharaj watched the swamis perform the mahapuja from Surat in Gujarat, India, and also gave his blessings for the New Year, for peace, harmony and righteous prosperity to prevail around the world.
 The mahapuja provided a fitting way to mark an important New Year as the Mandir in London – popularly known as the ‘Neasden Temple’ – celebrates its 25th anniversary in 2020. 
 Yogesh Patel, one of the mahapuja organisers, shared his impressions of this unique event: “It was heart-warming to see devotees from across the UK and Europe come together in their respective towns and cities to pray for peace and unity to prevail in the world and their families. Seeing the enthusiasm of young children to participate was particularly inspiring. What a fitting way to welcome 2020!”

Photo Gallery 
 Family Shibir, London, UK (40 photos)
 Family Shibir at Home, UK & Europe (60 photos)
 On 29 December 2019, Mahant Swami Maharaj wrote a letter to the UK & Europe Satsang Mandal explaining the fundamental importance of ahnik (daily personal practices of devotion) for one’s spiritual progression and as a personal contribution to the 25th anniversary celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 Making this the central theme, a special online one-day family shibir was organised on Sunday 12 July 2020 to better understand the meaning, method and benefits of these daily devotional practices and how to improve their quality.
 The shibir covered daily puja, arti, thal, mansi and cheshta as well as more generally the importance of a ghar mandir through a series of enlightening video presentations, discourses by senior and learned swamis, demonstrations, and interactive exercises throughout the day. The learning included inspiring examples from the exemplary lives of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The shibir began with samuh puja where families performed their personal puja in unison with the aid of an online tutorial. Families then enjoyed the webcast darshan of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s puja that was recorded earlier in Nenpur, India.
 The webcast sessions continued thereafter, providing detailed guidance on the various aspects of personal daily satsang and the sharing of best practises. The teachings were supported with worksheets and pre-prepared resources with opportunities for members of the family to participate in these practices at home.
 During the afternoon, families held discussions on how to improve the quality of their collective devotion at home. They also had time to enjoy fun family activities.
 Following the evening session, families also joined the live webcast of the sandhya arti and the abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj in London while joining in at their own homes. The enlightening day concluded with samuh cheshta, also webcast from London.
 The special programme provided an ideal opportunity for families to strengthen their personal devotion to God and also to make pledges of improving the quantity and quality of time together as a family. Swamis provided answers to various questions that had been submitted beforehand, providing clarity and clearing several common misconceptions.
 Samir Patel, a father of two, from Edinburgh, shared his impressions of the day: “This was one of the best shibirs I have taken part in. We learned so much! And it was really enjoyable and easy to digest. We’re really looking forward now as a family to performing arti, thal and our other ahnik and improving together in our bhakti and personal satsang.”

/News/2020/Online-Mahapuja-18656.aspx.t: Online Mahapuja connects 12,000 families for the quick resolution of the COVID-19 Pandemic, North America
/News/2020/Online-Mahapuja-18656.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mahapuja at Mandir (11 photos)
 Mahapuja at Home (47 photos)
 As individuals and organizations grapple with the financial, social, emotional and spiritual ramifications of the COVID-19 pandemic, the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha hosted a special prayer known as Mahapuja at each of its six Shikkarbaddh (traditional stone) mandirs in North America on Sunday, March 29, 2020.  The Mahapuja was held for the well-being of all people, regardless of religion, nationality, race, or beliefs, and a quick resolution to the pandemic. 
 At 9:00 am local time, the Pujya Swamis residing at the Shikkarbaddh mandirs began the rituals.  In the spirit of the Upanishadic verse ‘Vasudhaiv Kutumbakam’ (the whole world is one family), prayers were said for the well-being and betterment of all living beings and for an end to the COVID-19 pandemic. 
 Previously, BAPS closed all mandirs worldwide in accordance with governmental and scientific community guidelines creating a void in the lives of many devotees.  The online Mahapuja served to connect all BAPS devotees and well-wishers in solidarity against the pandemic. Over 12,000 families took part in the ceremonies from the safety of their homes. The virtual presence of the murtis (sacred images) of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and his spiritual lineage as well as the Pujya Swamis served to calm the minds of devotees with the chanting of Vedic mantras thousands of years old and, yet, still relevant today.

/News/2020/Online-Mahila-Sabha-18855.asp.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Online Mahila Sabha (63 photos)
 As the COVID-19 pandemic requires people to socially distance, people are finding creative ways to meaningfully connect with one another. On May 16, 2020, the BAPS North American Mahila Mandal hosted its first online sabha. The sabha was titled ‘Twameva Sarvam’ or ‘You are my everything’, honoring the importance of Bhagwan and Guru in one's life through shared personal experiences of women in the BAPS community. Thousands of women connected to this event with appreciation as they have been unable to attend their weekly assemblies at local mandirs.
 The effort and coordination of putting on such a sabha was apparent from the commencement when nine ladies from throughout North America joined together, accompanied by musical instruments, sang a melodious dhun, which was followed by the prathana, ‘Ahonish Darshan Dejo Re Murti, Chaitanya Ma Rahejo.’ Translated, it means “eternally seeking the murti of Bhagwan and His presence in one’s conscious.”
 The sabha was centered around a SMS dialogue between an aspiring medical professional whose job involves treating COVID-19 patients, and her mother. The daughter was feeling overwhelmed by the deadly impact of the virus. Through a series of text messages, her mother provided spiritually grounded guidance on how to navigate this extremely difficult situation with grace as well as understanding this to be an opportunity to strengthen her spiritual connection with Bhagwan and Guru.
 The message of the importance of Bhagwan and Guru in one’s life was exemplified by four women sharing their personal experiences of guidance, inspiration, and spiritual love given by Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj, and the impact it has had on their lives. The gratitude these women felt when conveying their stories transcended the virtual screen and left many teary-eyed.
 The personal stories provided tangible ways to strengthen one's spiritual connection by performing daily ahnik, reading the Vachanamrut, listening to katha, and offering heartfelt prarthana, as a way to feel the presence of Bhagwan and Sant by one's side at all times.

/News/2020/Online-Zonal-Yuva-Adhiveshans.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Zonal Adhiveshan (16 photos)
 During the lockdown in India, yuvaks and yuvatis from BAPS centers in Gujarat, Maharashtra and other states participated in the first-ever online Zonal Yuva Adhiveshans.
 Youths competed with others from centers in their zone. They participated in four competitions: Vachanamrut Mukhpath (Memorization), Sahajanand Namavali Mukhpath, Poster Design and Script Writing.
 On 17 and 19 May, a total of 2,155 yuvaks and 3,358 yuvatis took part online in the two mukhpath competitions. Each participant was tested by an assessor over a Whatsapp video call. While reciting their memorized material, the youths were required to keep their eyes closed to ensure fairness.
 Youths also submitted their poster design and script entries online to the Satsang Activities Central Office in Ahmedabad for assessment.
 Zonewise results were declared separately for yuvaks and yuvatis for each competition.

/News/2020/Open-House-London-2020-Specia.t: Open House London 2020: Special Film About Neasden Temple, London, UK
/News/2020/Open-House-London-2020-Specia.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Open House London Film (16 photos)
 A special film about BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, has been produced as part of the Mandir’s ongoing participation in the annual Open House London festival.
 Open House London is an annual architecture festival that celebrates the finest buildings in the British capital. The programme began in 1992 with the aim to offer free access to London’s architectural marvels and inspire the public about the benefits of great design. Open House London is organised by Open-City, with more than 46 cities across the world now embracing its concept. 
 In the absence of a physical visit to the Mandir this year because of the coronavirus pandemic, Open House London produced a short film instead. It provides an insightful glimpse into the Mandir for those who would have otherwise visited the Mandir for the first time and even those who would love to visit again. The film has become the most popular on the Open House London YouTube channel, and also features on the Open-City website homepage, which attracts 450,000 hits in the run up to the Open House festival each year.
 Jim Stephenson, an architectural photographer and filmmaker who produced the film, shared, “When we started planning which buildings to visit for the Open House film series, Neasden Temple was high on the list. I was stunned the first time I walked into the Mandir and the Haveli. I have to thank everyone involved in the making of the film for their help and their warmth on the day. I’m really pleased we can now share it.”
 Assistant Curator for Open House Nyima Murry added, “We were delighted to be able to film the Mandir to allow Open House visitors virtual access to this incredible space, and hope that through this film we are able to celebrate the craftsmanship of this building and its cultural importance to the city.”
 Kamlesh Patel, a volunteer at the Mandir, said, “We’re delighted to be able to continue supporting and contributing to Open House London even though we weren’t able to physically welcome visitors this year. When the Mandir opened in 1995, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj envisioned it as a place of peace, learning and celebration for people of all faiths and cultures, so we’re very thankful to the wonderful team at Open House London for choosing to film Neasden Temple and allowing so many to experience the architectural beauty and spiritual meaning of the Mandir.”

Underlying every traditional Hindu mandir is an ancient and exact religious discipline of architecture called Vastu Shastra that integrates the best of time and space for a harmonious relationship between dweller, dwelling and the cosmos
The Mandir is not just a beautiful building but the home of God, whose sacred images are enshrined in the upper sanctum of the Mandir

Structural features of the Mandir, such as the central cantilever dome, are profusely carved with traditional Hindu motifs of auspiciousness, peace and piety. It is where architecture becomes art and art becomes architecture, and both become devotional.

Forged in the enduring spirit of reverence, adoration and gratitude, the Mandir is a humble tribute to the inexpressible majesty and unbounded glory of the Divine. As a result, the Mandir is both a labour of love and a work of art.

The Mandir is constructed entirely from stone without reinforcing iron or steel, using more than 5,000 tonnes of Bulgarian limestone, Italian and Indian marble, and Sardinian granite

/News/2020/Param-Pujya-Mahant-Swami-Maha.t: Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj's Letter of Heartfelt Prayers: Let Us Welcome Aksharbrahma, Nenpur, India
/News/2020/Param-Pujya-Mahant-Swami-Maha.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Letter of Heartfelt Prayers (8 photos)
 Swami-Shriji
 Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj
 Let Us Welcome Aksharbrahma
 Nenpur
 29.10.’20
 Thursday
 To All Pujya Sadhus and Devotees,
 Very affectionate Jai Shree Swaminarayan from Sadhu Keshavjivandas.
 On Sharad Punam, Swami will be seated with Maharaj. With Harikrishna Maharaj we welcomed the murti of Gunatitanand Swami to Nenpur. Now, I pray daily with the murti before me. I think about [his] glory. I remember Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and pray again. I remember all the sadhus and pray again. Everyone is working very hard. I remember the village and city devotees and pray. I pray again, “O Swami! You will be installed on Sharad Punam, so now make everyone happy. Let no miseries remain. May all be physically, mentally and financially happy. May unity between all increase. May all disputes be resolved. May no one be angry. In honour or insult, joy or misery, believe Maharaj as the all-doer. If an incident arises, then [think] ‘What would Yogi Bapa or Pramukh Swami do?’ Thus, all should learn virtues in this way. Help one another. May nobody fall ill. May all who are ill recover. May the world become free from the corona[virus]. May all abundantly prosper in their businesses and jobs. May there be peace and peace. May your homes become [like] Akshardham. May all develop faith in Akshar-Purushottam and become brahmarup. Reveal to us the true form of Swaminarayan Bhagwan. Who except you can reveal Maharaj’s form to us? You are extremely compassionate. There is no limit to your compassion. Maharaj certainly listens to what you say, that is why we pray to you.” In this way, I have infused the divine energy of glory and prayer in the murti from now.
 When Gunatitanand Swami is installed, that, for us, is the New Year. The duo of Akshar and Purushottam. Everything is happening according to the line drawn by Shastriji Maharaj. We want to celebrate this festive occasion with pageantry. Not with worldly pageantry, but the inner pageantry of bhakti and prapti. You are making preparations, but prepare in this way. If you have young sons or daughters at home, then the adults should explain to them that Swaminarayan Bhagwan is Parabrahma and Gunatitanand Swami is Mul Akshar. If the adults do not know this and the children know, then they should explain it to the adults. Speak about the glory of Akshar-Purushottam. Celebrate this with true sentiments, and true joy and enthusiasm. Who is going to be installed? Aksharbrahma himself! The ideal sevak and highest disciple of Maharaj. So, such joy is natural when he is being consecrated.

/News/2020/Parenting-Webinar-for-Eleven-.t: Parenting Webinar for Eleven-Plus School Entrance Exams, UK
/News/2020/Parenting-Webinar-for-Eleven-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Parenting Webinar (8 photos)
 The Eleven-Plus (11+) is an important examination administered to some students in the UK in the final year of their primary education. It governs admission into secondary schools which rely on academic selection. This typically challenging time for many parents and children has been exacerbated this year due to the current lockdown. 
 To help ease the pressure off parents by providing helpful information and sharing guidance from teachers as well as the first-hand experiences of parents who have successfully tackled the process, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK held special webinars for parents of Year 5 children on Thursday 30 July and Wednesday 5 August 2020.
 Over 160 families attended the webinars during which teachers and experts provided a deeper insight into the competition for school places and encouraged parents to maintain a realistic perspective on their children’s potential.
 Attendees also learnt how best to prepare for the exams, with specific tips on the exam papers, including the importance of 'quality over quantity' and investing time to practise and learn from past papers.
 Experts conveyed the importance of correct preparation during the evening before and on the morning of the exam. Integral to this discussion was useful advice on maintaining a positive frame of mind when approaching and sitting the exams.
 The webinar also revealed valuable life skills that participants can harness to help them in their future academic and professional lives.
 A key concluding message drew upon Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s ethos of “Hard Work + Prayers = Success” as a universal formula to help achieve maximum potential.
 A mother from Birmingham later shared her impressions of the event: “Thank you so much for this invaluable guidance. My husband and I have been concerned for many weeks and were debating how we can prepare for these exams. The advice has eased our worries and we will now focus on the techniques to give our daughter the confidence to achieve her very best.”

/News/2020/Parenting-Webinars-Understand.t: Parenting Webinars: Understanding Mental Health, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Parenting-Webinars-Understand.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Understanding Children's Mental Health (9 photos)
 Understanding Teenage Mental Health (9 photos)
 50% of mental health difficulties begin before a child is 14 years of age, and the current pandemic has only increased the number of cases. To address and tackle this important issue, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in UK & Europe held special mental health webinars during November.
 The first webinar, ‘Understanding Children’s Mental Health’, was held on 4 November 2020. This session was tailored for parents of children in Reception to Year 6. A second webinar, ‘Understanding Teenager Mental Health’ was delivered on 6 November 2020, focussing on issues relevant to parents of teenagers in Years 7 to 13.
 More than 500 devices connected to these seminars, which were prepared and delivered by two BAPS volunteers serving in the Parenting Team, Dr Nisha Patel, a clinical psychologist, and Ms Priya Amlani, an anxiety specialist. These experts provided guidance on how to better understand the mental health of children and teenagers and techniques to resolve mental health concerns.
 Their discussions covered the impact of mental health, especially in the Indian community, and explained the importance of family conversations regarding mental health as well as ways in which parents can create an environment for children and teenagers to feel safe and open about their concerns.
 The presenters greatly emphasised the importance of an open and healthy parent-child relationship, as this in turn directly impacts the mental health of children and teenagers. They discussed strategies such as PACE (playfulness, acceptance, curiosity and empathy) in detail to help parents implement these at home.
 Another important issue relevant to certain communities is the reluctance or delay in seeking help. The importance of seeking help quickly was encouraged and supported with helpful links and contact numbers where parents can access further information and support.
 Many attendees expressed their positive feedback after the webinars. One father shared, “I learnt so much from today’s webinar. The talks were highly informative and eye-opening. They've shown me practical ways in which I can better support my child, and helped me realise how my words and behaviour, even though well-intentioned, might cause more distress if her needs are very different. Our family is truly very grateful for all that you're doing for us."

/News/2020/Patotsav-Ceremony--London-Man.t: Patotsav Ceremony | London Mandir 25th Anniversary, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Patotsav-Ceremony--London-Man.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Patotsav Ceremony Murti Darshan (20 photos)
 Patotsav Ceremony, London, UK, and Nenpur, India (40 photos)
 Patotsav Celebrations at Home, UK & Europe (40 photos)
 The 25th anniversary celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, were marked with a host of devotional festivities on Sunday 23 August 2020.
 They began with a kirtan aradhana early in the morning, performed live by swamis in London during the puja of Mahant Swami Maharaj in Nenpur, India, via video conferencing facilities.
 This was followed by the patotsav ceremony at 9.30am BST, to commemorate the anniversary of the Mandir’s murtis when they were infused with divine presence by Pramukh Swami Maharaj 25 years ago.
 Swamis performed the patotsav rituals, including the abhishek of the murtis, in a special service during the morning, which was webcast to thousands across the world. During the ceremony, they offered prayers for all those affected by the global Covid-19 pandemic as well as for peace and harmony to prevail in the world. Devotees and well-wishers joined these prayers from their respective homes.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj had expressed a wish to personally join in the patotsav ceremony. Earlier in the morning, he performed the abhishek of the murtis in London remotely from Nenpur, India, using a wireless trigger. Video highlights of this unique participation were also shown during the main ceremony.
 Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of the Mandir, delivered a discourse on the significance of mandirs, drawing upon their theological importance as revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan in the Vachanamrut. He also reflected upon the history of the Mandir’s inauguration and the tireless commitment of devotees who, inspired by the blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, offered their dedication and devotion upon which today’s 25th anniversary celebrations are founded. Video highlights of the cultural festival leading to the Mandir’s inauguration in 1995 were also shown, bringing together these messages and rekindling cherished memories.
 As part of the patotsav celebrations, a variety of sweet and savoury dishes were artistically offered to the deities in the main shrines. Swamis sang thal of this annakut under the dome in the upper sanctum, while devotees joined in at home by offering thal in their respective ghar mandirs.
 The patotsav celebrations concluded with the ceremonial arti at noon which was performed simultaneously by Mahant Swami Maharaj in Nenpur and webcast live to everyone.
 The online celebrations provided an opportunity for devotees – who could not attend this year’s event in person due to the pandemic – to still participate in this auspicious and historic occasion.
 The 25th anniversary celebrations of London Mandir culminated with an eye-opening and gripping finale programme in the afternoon, commencing at 3.30pm BST.

/News/2020/Placement-of-First-Stone-Pill.t: Placement of First Stone Pillar BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Jodhpur, India
/News/2020/Placement-of-First-Stone-Pill.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Placement of First Stone Pillar (55 photos)
 On 26 February 2020, the first stone pillar of the under-construction BAPS shikharbaddha mandir in Jodhpur was ceremonially placed into position by Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami.
 The Vedic mahapuja rituals for this auspicious occasion were performed by Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami in the presence of over 1200 devotees and invited dignitaries.
 Among the dignitaries present were: Mahant Shri Ramprasadji Maharaj, High Court Justice Shri Vinit Mathur, Collector of Jodhpur Shri Prakash Rajpurohit, Police Commissioner of Jodhpur Shri Praful Kumar, Shri Gauravbhai Pravinbhai Shah, Former Mayor Shri Rameshwarji Dadhich and Former Mayor Shri Ghanshyamji Ojha.
 As part of the week-long celebrations, on 20 February 2020, over 2,000 women devotees and well-wishes of Jodhpur participated in a devout Kalash and Pothi Yatra by carrying auspicious water-pots and cloth-wrapped copies of the Shrimad Bhagvat scripture.
 Then, in the evening assemblies from 23 to 25 February, Mahant Param Pujya Ramprasadji Maharaj of the Bada Ramdwara Math delivered discourses on the life of Shri Narsinh Mehta and his faith in God. Also, Yogiprem Swami discoursed on the Shrimad Bhagvat in the afternoon and devotional bhajans were sung by BAPS sadhus.
 Prior to these celebrations, on 17 February 2020, Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj had performed the pujan of this first stone pillar in Atladara in the presence of devotees of Jodhpur and others.

Photo Gallery 
 Prakruti Vandan (10 photos)
 In the grounds of the BAPS Mandir in Nairobi, the resident swamis and some devotees honored nature by performing the Vedic pujan of a tulsi plant, kadali and avocado trees, as well as mango trees planted by gurus Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In the presence of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, the swamis and devotees recited the Shanti Path, applied chandlos to the plants, performed the arti and prayed for the protection of the environment.

/News/2020/Prakruti-Vandan-NA-19092.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prakruti Vandan by Swamis (16 photos)
 Prakruti Vandan by Devotees (100 photos)
 On August 30, 2020 at 11:00AM local time, devotees across North America participated in a special ceremony, Prakruti Vandan, to mark the importance of taking care of nature and the environment. The spiritual head of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, requested swamis and devotees to perform a prayer for peace (Vedic Shanti Path), Pujan and Arti of a nearby tree or tulsi plant- all while adhering to coronavirus safety guidelines.
 Nature and the environment are a common thread that connects all of humanity. Hindu teachings and scriptures emphasize respect and care for nature in maintaining balance and peace for all life. Mahant Swami Maharaj emphasized in his blessings, “Pramukh Swami Maharaj frequently said that if you take care of nature, nature will take care of you. He inspired people to plant hundreds of thousands of trees and guided us on how to care for nature and the environment. Let us all resolve today to protect the environment and ensure a healthy future for all.”

/News/2020/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-99th-Ja.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj 99th Janma Jayanti Home Celebrations, UK & Europe (40 photos)
 Kishore-Kishori Mandal Pramukh Parva Bake Off, UK & Europe (24 photos)
 Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj preached that Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s birth anniversary should be celebrated with great devotional fanfare. Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 99th janma jayanti was thus joyously celebrated around the world, including in the UK and Europe, with a series of devotional offerings and enlightening online programmes throughout the day on Tuesday 22 December 2020.
 Devotees had safely marked this auspicious occasion from their respective homes with festive decorations and devotional artwork. Young and senior members of families also decorated their ghar mandirs and placed intricately crafted garlands around the murti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 As part of a devotional initiative by Kishore-Kishori Mandal, many young devotees participated in the ‘Pramukh Parva Bake Off’ in which they made and offered a variety of celebratory desserts – cakes, biscuits, puddings, etc. – to mark the occasion.
 In the lead-up to this day, the Bal-Balika Mandal, Kishore-Kishori Mandal, Yuvak-Yuvati Mandal, Sanyukta Mandal and Mahila Mandal all focused their weekly sabhas on the divine virtues of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. A total of twelve sabhas formed a part of ‘Pramukh Parva 2020’, spanning four weeks. (These sabhas are available to watch on-demand on the BAPS UK & Europe channel here.)
 During the afternoon, thousands of devotees joined the webcast from India to enjoy an absorbing three-hour programme that provided an immersive spiritual experience paying homage to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s divine, saintly life. 3D animations and special effects combined to create a virtual stage in the Himalayan mountains, the abode of the great sages of ancient India, as the setting for the celebrations. (See here for more details.)
 That evening, another online programme took viewers on a historical journey of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s birth celebrations from 1965 to 2020. The production included a montage of rare footage interspersed with commentaries and eye-witness accounts from senior swamis and devotees who shared examples of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s profound humility and selfless love for others.
 Families participated in the mantra-pushpanjali and arti at the end of the webcasts by offering flower petals and rice grains to the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the Guru Parampara as well as Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Anjali Patel, a mother from London, said, “Our daughters had so much fun baking a birthday cake and making colourful birthday cards. The evening programme was wonderful. Seeing the footage of those unforgettable celebrations over the years, many of which we saw for the first time, was truly heart-warming and inspiring.”

/News/2020/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Jivan-C.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Jivan Charitra Parayan (76 photos)
 On the occasion of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 99th birthday celebrations, one-day parayans (readings) of all four published parts of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Jivan Charitra were organized at 95 centers across Australia and New Zealand on 12 and 19 December 2020.
 The parayans were recited by local swamis and more than 3,755 young and old devotees from their homes in different locations throughout Australia and New Zealand. The parayans commenced at 6:00 a.m. with pujan and arti of the texts. Devotees participated in 20-minute sessions by reading the text from where the previous participant had stopped. At each center, the first part was read by adult men devotees, the second by adult women devotees, the third part by yuvatis and the fourth part by yuvaks. In this way, during the 24 hours of continuous reading all four parts of the jivan charitra were read 95 times.
 Following their participation in this endeavor, many have resolved to read Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Jivan Charitra on a daily basis.

 Jivan Charitra Video Parayan (14 photos)
 To celebrate Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 99th birthday, over 600 balaks, balikas, kishores and kishoris from BAPS centers in Australia and New Zealand participated in a video parayan based on the videos from parts 1 to 4 of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Jivan Charitra.
 The children and teenagers were split into 131 groups, with each being allocated a set number of videos to watch for about one hour. Each parayan viewing session began with pujan and a short speech on the life and work of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. In total, viewing of the 21 hours of video was completed six times. 
 Participating Centers:
 Adelaide, Auckland, Brisbane, Canberra, Christchurch, Darwin, Gold Coast, Hamilton, Melbourne Mandir, Melbourne South, Melbourne West, Perth, Sydney and Wellington.

/News/2020/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Smruti-.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Smruti Din | London Mandir 25th Anniversary, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Smruti-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 'Pramukh Swami Maharaj Smruti Din' Online Programme (40 photos)
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on 20 August 1995. Since that auspicious day, he visited the UK and Europe eight times, showering devotees and well-wishers with immeasurable bliss.
 Over those visits, every room, every passageway, every corner of London Mandir has been infused with unforgettable and inspiring moments of his presence.
 On Sunday 16 August 2020, a special online programme brought these historic memories alive through a montage of eye-witness accounts and unseen footage from the past 25 years.
 The video and photo montages were interspersed with narrations from swamis who shared their insights and the backstory behind these incidents. It revealed the spiritual love, sacrifice and compassion of Pramukh Swami Maharaj to please and inspire young and old.
 The programme concluded with a pledge of gratitude to Pramukh Swami Maharaj and a final collage of recollections from Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visit to the UK in 2017. It revealed how he has continued Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s legacy of unconditional love and gifted new chapters of blissful memories.
 The heart-warming programme rekindled golden memories for those present during his visits, while for others, particularly younger children, it presented an opportunity to learn, appreciate and be inspired by the selfless love that Pramukh Swami Maharaj showered upon the devotees of UK and Europe.
 Darshan Alaiya, aged 14, from Barnet, UK, said: “My dad always tells me about the special places and moments here at the Mandir with Pramukh Swami Maharaj. I now understand how precious these places are in the Mandir and I feel so lucky to have seen these. They are just as special for me now.”
 Rita Patel, a devotee added, “I am lost for words. Those wonderful memories of great festivals with Bapa [Pramukh Swami Maharaj] here in London, and witnessing so many of his daily acts of service – watching him guide, console, laugh with us and stand beside us through every stage of our lives – these moments were truly brought to life. The programme truly filled my heart with warmth and joy.”

/News/2020/Prarthana-Sabha-18847.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prarthana Sabha (48 photos)
 A special prarthana sabha (memorial assembly) was conducted by swamis at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, and webcast across the UK and Europe on Friday 8 May 2020 in memory of all those who have recently passed away. It provided much-needed closure and spiritual solace to families who had been unable to convene at local mandirs due to the COVID-19 lockdown.
 The ceremony included devotional singing by swamis and was interspersed with video blessings and messages of spiritual fortitude from Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Families of the deceased participated in the ceremonies from their respective homes, performing the various rituals simultaneously as they were conducted by swamis inside the Mandir.
 The assembly began with prayers for peace to prevail across the world and for the well-being of all. Swamis sang various bhajans with words of spiritual strength that provided comfort and solace for the many families who had sadly lost their loved ones. (Not all had passed away due to COVID-19.)
 Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of the Mandir, delivered an uplifting address, drawing upon the compassion and protection that Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit Gurus forever bestow.
 The evening service concluded with the mantrapushpanjali (a devotional offering of flowers to the murtis) and a final prayer sung by swamis and families in unison across the UK and Europe.
 During the programme, swamis, devotees and well-wishers remembered Srutidharma Das, the former president of Bhaktivedanta Manor, ISKCON UK, as well as four BAPS swamis who had passed away in India. A special remembrance tribute was also paid to healthcare and frontline workers who have passed away in their line of duty whilst serving the nation during COVID-19.
 Anup Morzaria, son of the recently deceased Purshottam Morzaria, shared his sentiments after the assembly. “Wonderful, graceful, peaceful – adjectives and words just cannot describe the profound strength that this sabha has provided to me and my family. The words from Mahant Swami Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, as well as the tributes and eloquently sung bhajans have provided peace and closure during this time of loss. My heartfelt gratitude to you all.”

/News/2020/Prasad-Pravesh-19474.aspx.t: Prasad Pravesh Ceremony of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Winnipeg, MB, Canada
/News/2020/Prasad-Pravesh-19474.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Ceremony at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto (7 photos)
 Ceremony at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Winnipeg (28 photos)
 Ceremony at Home (11 photos)
 The historic Prasad Pravesh Vidhi for a new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada was performed on Saturday, November 21, 2020. The ceremony took place at the new Mandir site in Winnipeg in accordance with  social distancing protocols. The ceremony ritual was  performed virtually by Pujya Gunsagardas Swami along with other Swamis from the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto, as well as Senior Swamis from India.
 The Prasad Pravesh ceremony is performed when a new premises or building is entered for the first time. It unites the entire community with prayers for peace and harmony and purifies the space for a new beginning with positive energy.
 By the grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the inspiration of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Swamis started doing vicharan (spiritual visits) in many parts of Canada, including Manitoba, since 2003. As a steady flow of devotees began to settle there over the years, Swamis increased their vicharan in Manitoba and established weekly Satsang Sabhas (religious services) in 2004. With steady growth of devotees in the Winnipeg area, a building was acquired for a new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir at 1488 Red River Drive in Howden, Manitoba. The new Mandir will facilitate activities and events for young and old alike, to practice and preserve Hindu traditions and spiritual values. 
 The Prasad Pravesh ceremony was performed virtually in the presence of dignitaries, community leaders and well-wishers from across Canada and around the world. The event was webcast live from the Mandir site while over 900 families participated in the ceremony from their homes. The traditional rituals involved consecration of the Mandir building, blessing the project with Vedic rituals, and prayers for peace and well-being throughout the community, province and country.
 Messages of congratulations and well wishes to the community for this historic occasion were received from dignitaries. Terry Duguid, Member of Parliament for Winnipeg South, Manitoba shared, “My warm congratulations to the BAPS community in Manitoba on the consecration of the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir. Let me also take this opportunity to say how much I value your friendship and appreciate all you do to contribute to the vibrancy of our Winnipeg and Manitoba community…This is a very proud day for Manitoba and Canada and especially for our BAPS community here in Winnipeg.”
 His Worship Chris Ewen, Mayor of the Rural Municipality of Ritchot(Winnipeg Capital Region) shared, “We’re excited to have you. On behalf of all of council and everyone from the rural municipality, thank you for taking a chance on us. We know you will love it here as much as we’re going to love having you here. I love seeing people coming together and sharing and experiencing joy, peace, happiness and opportunities and that is exactly what you have. I always love seeing growth in the municipality and that’s what you are bringing. Thank you very much and enjoy your time here.”
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj sent blessings from India for this auspicious occasion saying, “What we can see, have seen and will see here is due to the efforts of the Swamis, devotees and well-wishers. You have all put in great effort to bring us to this level.  Satsang has grown here and this has been possible with the effort of the devotees and Swamis and the grace of God… Blessings to everyone on the occasion of the Prasad Pravesh of the Mandir in Winnipeg.”

 Prayers for Humanity (6 photos)
 Today, 14 May 2020, has been declared an International Day of Prayer by the Higher Committee for Human Fraternity and has been supported by world religious leaders, national heads, the United Nations and other world organisations  It aims to unite humanity in a time of crisis which transcends faiths, traditions, borders, language and ethnicity.
 Let us join His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj who has prayed in Nenpur on the morning of 14 May, "May we together overcome the coronavirus crisis as soon as possible. And may the peace and bliss of God spread everywhere, and be experienced by every heart, in every home, in every corner of this world."
 World Religious leaders across the globe have supported this call, including:
 Pope Francis – Head of Catholic Church
 Sheikh Ahmed El Tayeb, the Grand Imam of Egypt's Al-Azhar Mosque
 Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan - Crown Prince of UAE
 Ronald S - Jewish Congress President
 António Guterres – United Nations – Secretary General
 Justin Welby - Archbishop of Canterbury
 President and Prime Ministers of many countries.
 Additionally, on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and all sadhus and devotees of BAPS, Pujya Brahmavihari Swamiji, has conveyed an inspiring and universal message of harmony through Vedic prayers and the ideals of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

 Prayers for Humanity, Abu Dhabi
 Photo Gallery 
 Prayers for Humanity 2020 (12 photos)
 Over 2,000 families and more than 5,000 participants from over 56 countries joined online to participate in the prayer assembly held by the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi. The webcast assembly was in support of the noble ‘Prayers for Humanity’ initiative of the Higher Committee for Human Fraternity (HCHF). 
 The hour-long assembly began at 7:30 p.m. with an address by Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj and continued with prayers from various Indian communities. Guest speakers included Pradeep Kumar Rath of the Odia Samaj, Mr. Ravi Kale who recited a prayer in Marathi, Mr. S. Venkatesh who shared a prayer in Tamil, and Mr. Shiv Kumar who offered prayers in Malayalam. All viewers were able to follow and understand each of these earnest prayers through the English subtitles provided.
 Devotional songs were also sung by different groups, including BAPS youths who sang in Gujarati and Hindi, and the ISKCON youth prayer group, who also thanked the UAE government and the frontline teams for helping the citizens of the UAE. This was followed by a heartfelt prayer video.
 Thereafter, Brahmavihari Swami provided the closing remarks of the prayer assembly. He extended his gratitude to the rulers of the UAE and the UAE Government for their continued efforts to bring the global community together in praying for a swift end to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 This online prayer assembly concluded with a touching gesture of lighting a lantern or candle as a symbol of hope and prayer for the world.
 Along with the assembly, more than 1,300 people from across the globe submitted personal prayers in various languages through the online portal at prayer.mandir.ae.

 Prayers for PM Narendra Modi (6 photos)
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj specially prayed for Hon. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his 70th birthday. Swamishri wrote a letter of blessings ‘with innermost prayers from the innermost part of my heart’, and guided Brahmavihari Swami to elaborate on the universal leadership and spiritual nature of the Prime Minister. 
 Swamishri prayed, “May the PM lead India for global good. Behind his amazing achievements there is a silent spirituality.” In response, the Prime Minister tweeted, “I am very proud of my association with the BAPS family, known for its impeccable service world-wide. I thank HH Mahant Swami Maharaj Ji. I also pay tributes to HH Pramukh swami Maharaj Ji.”

/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-Adhiveshan-Rac.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Adhiveshan, Phase 1, 12-13 Dec 2020 (13 photos)
 Adhiveshan, Phase 2, 27-28 Feb 2021 (13 photos)
 Adhiveshan, Phase 3, 8-9 May 2021 (16 photos)
 To commemorate the 99th birthday of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, children and teenagers of the Bal-Balika and Kishore-Kishori Mandals in Australia (Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Darwin, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Shepparton, Sydney) and New Zealand (Auckland, Christchurch,  Hamilton, Wellington) participated in the ‘Race for Rajipo’ adhiveshan. 
 Based on the 315 shloks (verses) of the Satsang Diksha, the adhiveshan consisted of memorizing shloks based on three challenge levels from which the youngsters chose to participate: the Vinu Challenge (memorize 1–50 shloks), the Keshav Challenge (1–95 shloks) and the Mahant Challenge (1–130 shloks). 
 In total, 561 balaks and balikas and 275 kishores and kishoris took part. Participants were graded based on having memorized a certain percentage of their particular challenge. For each challenge level, the Gold Award required 90% or higher, Silver required 80–89% and Bronze required 70–79%.
 Satsang Diksha Adhiveshan: Race for Rajipo, Phase 2
 27–28 February 2021
 Children and teenagers of the Bal-Balika and Kishore-Kishori Mandals in Australia (Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Darwin, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Shepparton, Sydney) and New Zealand (Auckland, Christchurch,  Hamilton, Wellington) took part in the second phase of the ‘Race for Rajipo’ adhiveshan.
 Based on the Satsang Diksha scripture, the adhiveshan was conducted online due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The adhiveshan requiured the participants to memorize shloks based on three challenge levels: the Vinu Challenge (131–180 shloks), Keshav Challenge (131–200 shloks) and Mahant Challenge (131–220 shloks).
 A total of 345 balaks and balikas and 222 kishores and kishoris took part. Participants were graded based on having memorized a certain percentage of their particular challenge. For each challenge level, the Gold Award required 90% or higher, Silver required 80–89% and Bronze required 70–79%. A total of 208 participants received an award.
 The third phase of the adhiveshan which will be held in May 2021.
 Satsang Diksha Adhiveshan: Race for Rajipo, Phase 3
 8-9 May 2021
 Bal-Balika and Kishore-Kishori Mandals across Australia (Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Darwin, Gold Coast, Melbourne, Perth, Shepparton, Sydney) and New Zealand (Auckland, Christchurch, Hamilton, Wellington) participated in the third and final part of the Race for Rajipo Adhiveshan, based on the Satsang Diksha scripture.
 The adhiveshan was conducted online due to the COVID-19 pandemic and consisted of three challenges: the Vinu Challenge (221–276 shloks), the Keshav Challenge (221–296 shloks), and the Mahant Challenge (221–315 shloks).
 In total, 325 balaks and balikas, and 167 kishores and kishoris participated, with 165 participants receiving an award for their achievement. The Gold Award required 90% or higher, Silver required 70% or higher and Bronze was 50% or higher.

/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-Granth-pujan-1.t: HH Mahant Swami Maharaj welcomed to homes in the form of the ‘Satsang Diksha’ Granth, North America
/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-Granth-pujan-1.text:
Photo Gallery 
 'Satsang Diksha’ Granth Welcome (75 photos)
 Pujan Set-up and Decoration (35 photos)
 'Satsang Diksha' Pujan at Home (150 photos)
 Pujan in the presence of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (22 photos)
 Thousands of families and individuals across North America participated in a special pujan ceremony to welcome His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to their homes in the form of the ‘Satsang Diksha Granth’.
 Based on the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the ‘Satsang Diksha’ scripture concisely describes philosophical principles and daily personal practices of devotion to be followed by all devotees. Written by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in Gujarati, the scripture contains 315 verses with translations available in Sanskrit, English, and several other languages.
 The grand welcome was organized to fulfill Mahant Swami Maharaj’s inner wish to visit all devotees’ homes personally to deliver the profound messages captured in the scripture. In a letter to devotees, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “It is my inner wish to do padhramni (personal home visit) at each and every home and explain these talks to all ‘one-to-one’, but due to many limitations, this is not possible. However, as this scripture has reached each of your homes, I feel that the padhramni has been done.”
 Volunteers across North America delivered personal copies of the scripture to the homes of devotees, while taking ample safety precautions and following social distancing protocols. Devotees celebrated the occasion with great joy and enthusiasm. After the grand welcome, devotees took part in a special pujan ceremony at their homes through a live webcast led by Pujya Swamis from various BAPS Mandirs. 
 Many children and youth, and elder devotees in North America are memorizing the 'Satsang Diksha' text as Mahant Swami Maharaj has conveyed his profound delight and blessings to all those who have undertaken the efforts.

/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-National-Compl.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Felicitation Assembly (30 photos)
 Complete Shlok Memorization Competition (19 photos)
 The yuvaks and yuvatis who had participated in the zonal competitions and memorized all 315 Sanskrit shloks of the Satsang Diksha were eligible for this national competition coordinated by the Satsang Pravrutti Central Office.
 A total of 368 yuvaks and yuvatis took part and were thoroughly tested online via video calls by 38 experienced examiners. Of the participants, 273 youths (152 yuvaks and 121 yuvatis) were assessed to have correctly memorized all 315 Sanskrit shloks. A further 28 had correctly memorized 300 shloks and 8 had memorized 285.
 For all these yuvaks and yuvatis a special online felicitation assembly was held in the presence of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The assembly began with inspiring speeches by Pujya Doctor Swami and Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami. Then, Atmaswarup Swami, narrated the effort and diligence with which Mahant Swami Maharaj had written this historic shastra.
 After arriving in the online assembly, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj were honored with pujan and garlands.
 In Swamishri’s presence, yuvaks from various centres presented recitals of the Sanskrit shloks in traditional Vedic style.
 Then, after a video depicting the zonal and national competitions, yuvaks and sadhus narrated the testing circumstances the youths overcame to memorize the shloks and the efforts they had put in.
 Swamishri then unveiled the awards that will be sent to the youths, stamped and signed a certificate, and sanctified copies of the Satsang Diksha text that each youth would receive.
 To honor and felicitate the youths Swamishri showered flower petals in their direction and also gestured to embrace them as a mark of his blessings.
 To further felicitate the participating youths and honour their outstanding achievements, all the sadhus of the Sanstha, watching this live broadcast from their respective mandirs, performed dandvats to all the youths.
 Then, on behalf of all the youths, Yagnapriya Swami, voiced a prayer to Swamishri.
 Swamishri then blessed, “There are no words to describe what you have achieved. You have attained realization of God. Now if you sincerely live by the niyams and dharma, you will all flourish.”
 Thereafter, Swamishri blessed all the winners by stroking his hand over their names on the winners’ list. Also, as a gesture of presenting the award to each personally, he placed an award on each name on the list.
 Then, Swamishri blessed all the yuvaks individually as their live streams were displayed in sequence on the large LED screen in front of Swamishri.
 This memorable and moving assembly concluded with everyone joining Swamishri to perform the arti.

/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-Online-Questio.t: Satsang Diksha Online Questionnaire Competition, India
/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-Online-Questio.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Online Competition (15 photos)
 With the wish and blessings of guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj, the Satsang and Bal Pavarutti Central Offices in Ahmedabad organized two separate nationwide online Satsang Diksha questionnaire competitions for (1) all yuvaks and yuvatis and (2) karyakars of all wings (satsang, mahila, yuvak, yuvati, bal and balika).
 The first test on 1 November was for yuvaks and yuvatis and the second on 8 November was for all the karyakars.
 Both tests involved 100 questions of two types – true/false and MCQs – to be completed in 30 minutes.
 A total 13,250 yuvaks and yuvatis, and 39,000 karyakars participated in their respective tests.
 Prior to the main tests, daily study questions and pre-tests were provided online to help all to prepare.
 By participating in this competition all the youths and karyakars received the blessings of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 સત્સંગ દીક્ષા ગ્રંથની ઓનલાઇન પ્રશ્નોત્તરી સ્પર્ધા
 સત્સંગ દીક્ષા ગ્રંથની ભેટ આપીને પરમ પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજે લાખો આબાલ-વૃદ્ધ હરિભક્તોને આધ્યાત્મિકતાનો અનેરો રંગ લગાડ્યો છે. સૌનાં હૈયે આ રંગને વધુ ઘૂંટતા પરમ પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજની અંતઃકરણની ઈચ્છા હતી કે બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાની બાળ-યુવા-મહિલા અને સંયુક્ત સત્સંગ પ્રવૃત્તિ કાર્યાલય દ્વારા રાષ્ટ્રીય ધોરણે સત્સંગ દીક્ષા ગ્રંથની એક ઓનલાઈન પ્રશ્નોત્તરીનું આયોજન થાય, જેમાં તમામ યુવક-યુવતીઓ તેમજ બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાની બાળ-બાલિકા, યુવક-યુવતી, મહિલા અને સંયુક્ત સત્સંગ પ્રવૃત્તિઓના તમામ કાર્યકરો પણ જોડાય.
 પરમ પૂજ્ય સ્વામીશ્રીના આ સંકલ્પ મુજબ, નવેમ્બરની પ્રથમ તારીખે બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાની યુવાપ્રવૃત્તિના યુવક-યુવતીઓની આ ઓનલાઈન સ્પર્ધા યોજાઈ અને આઠમી નવેમ્બરે તમામ કાર્યકરોની ઓનલાઈન સ્પર્ધા યોજાઈ. બંને સ્પર્ધામાં કુલ ૧૦૦ પ્રશ્નો પૂછવામાં આવ્યા હતા, જે 30 મિનિટમાં પરિપૂર્ણ કરવાના હતા. આ સ્પર્ધામાં કુલ ૧૩,૨૫૦ યુવક-યુવતીઓ અને ૩૯,૦૦૦ કાર્યકરોએ ભાગ લીધો હતો.
 મુખ્ય સ્પર્ધા યોજાઈ તે પૂર્વે તમામ સ્પર્ધકોને માર્ગદર્શન મળી રહે તે માટે બે પ્રિ-ટેસ્ટ પણ લેવાયા હતા. ઉપરાંત સંસ્થાના સત્સંગ પ્રવૃત્તિ મધ્યસ્થ કાર્યાલય દ્વારા રોજ ૨૦ પ્રશ્નોની ટૂંકી ટેસ્ટ પણ લેવામાં આવી હતી.
 આ સ્પર્ધામાં ભાગ લઈને તમામ યુવક-યુવતીઓ અને કાર્યકરોએ પરમ પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજની અપાર  પ્રસન્નતા મેળવી છે. સૌને હાર્દિક અભિનંદન.

/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-Sanskrit-Shlok.t: Satsang Diksha: Sanskrit Shlok Memorization Competition, India
/News/2020/Satsang-Diksha-Sanskrit-Shlok.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Diksha Competition (17 photos)
 As per the wish of guruhari Mahant Swmi Maharaj, the Satsang Pravrutti Central Office organized separate competitions for yuvaks and yuvatis to memorize the Satsang Diksha shastra.
 After a preparation period of six weeks, a total of 7,991 youths (3394 yuvaks and 4597 yuvatis) from throughout Gujarat and Mumbai participated in the zonal competitions.
 Due to the restrictions enforced by the coronavirus pandemic, the participating youths were assessed by the examiners over a WhatsApp video call. A total of 1,237 examiners assisted in this process.
 The participating yuvaks and yuvatis were graded by the number of shloks they recited correctly. Despite the short preparation time, 164 yuvaks and yuvatis memorized the entire shastra (315 shloks), 70 memorized over 250 shloks, 100 memorized over 175 and 209 memorized over 125. Many of the remaining memorized over 45 shloks.
 The enthusiasm of the youths to fulfill Mahant Swami Maharaj’s wish was evident in all. Swamishri blessed all the youths by writing a letter, appreciating and rewarding their efforts.
 Swami-Shriji
 P.P. Pramukh Swami
 Nenpur
 12.9.20
 Saturday
 Bountiful Blessings…
 As you have followed the agna and memorized:
 - Maharaj and Swami will be extremely pleased
 - Maharaj and Swami will always be with you
 - Agna and upasana will be consolidated in your life
 - The principle of Akshar-Purushottam will be established in your life
 - You will progress greatly in satsang, studies and life
 That which was in the minds of Shriji Maharaj, Gunatitanand Swami, Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj has been written.
 There is no greater status than that [attained by] ‘Satsang Diksha’. So, you have all done an outstanding job. You have attained the highest status. Do not be concerned whether others believe this or not. To you all: Bravo! Bravo! Bravo!
 Jai Swaminarayan with great affection,
 from Sadhu Keshavjivandas
