/News/2020/Satsang-Exam-Results-for-Marc.text:
To All Satsang Exam Candidates,
 Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Satsang Exam Division in Shahibaug, Ahmedabad remained under lockdown from March 25 to June 8, 2020.
 In view of the prevailing circumstances within our society, consideration for public health and the inability to access mandir facilities, it is not possible for the experienced team of 450 trained mahila teachers, 70 mahila moderators, and 25 mahila lead moderators to process and accurately grade the answer sheets received from the 33,634 examinees who sat the March 2020 Satsang Exams.
 Hence, to enable timely registration for the March 7, 2021 Satsang Examinations, Guruhari Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj has blessed that all examinees who appeared for March 2020 Exams be promoted to the next level of the Satsang Examinations. And furthermore, for those stellar examinees that have gone above and beyond in efforts to master the syllabus to receive ranking standards, P.P Mahant Swami Maharaj has given a special ashirvad and has said, "Maharaj ane Swami no rajipo, ej sauthi moto medal chhe."
 Please make a note that absentees are not promoted and are requested to sit for same Satsang Exam level. Examinees who had registered for both papers of Satsang Pragna Exam, Satsang Pravesh, Parichay and Pravin exams need to have given both papers, in order to proceed to the next level. Presence in only one paper is considered as absent.
 Also, given the lockdown situation, several countries answer paper shipments have not been delivered to Exam Division, India. We are still awaiting shipments. Therefore, these results have not been posted and will be posted upon receipt when attendance can be verified.
 Swamishri has earnestly requested that all examinees register and sincerely prepare for the next year’s Satsang exam during this challenging time.
 Please LOGIN to your SEeR account to REGISTER for the March 7, 2021 Satsang Examinations.
 We apologize for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your continued support.
 Jay Swaminarayan,
 Satsang Exam Division, India

/News/2020/Satsang-Prasar--Management-Co.t: Satsang Prasar & Management Conference, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Satsang-Prasar--Management-Co.text:
The 2020 Satsang Prasar & Management Conference for UK and Europe volunteers was held over the weekend of 25 and 26 January at the BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs in Leicester and London, respectively. The event brought together more than 1,400 delegates.
 This year’s conference focussed on the themes of ‘Satsang, Samāj, Samāgam and Sevā’, which introduced the main projects for the year – the 25th anniversary of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London (the London Mandir), the centennial birth celebrations of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and the forthcoming visit of Mahant Swami Maharaj to the UK and Europe.
 A series of videos, presentations and addresses by swamis and lead volunteers provided the spiritual context and practical aspects of each project for the year ahead.
 The Board of Trustees also shared their vision and thanked every delegate for their personal contribution throughout 2019.
 Yogvivek Swami concluded the morning plenary session by providing further words of motivation and guidance, outlining specifically how volunteers can engage in various seva initiatives and develop their personal satsang.
 After lunch, delegates separated into their respective seva areas to gain specific information and guidance on how to serve better and contribute effectively to the three significant programmes in 2020.

/News/2020/Satsang-at-Home-18584.aspx.t: Satsang at Home during Coronavirus Pandemic, North America
/News/2020/Satsang-at-Home-18584.aspx.text:
As the world is being challenged with a global pandemic of the Coronavirus, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha is providing spiritual and social solace for devotees and well-wishers through various online forums. After suspending all local spiritual and charitable activities at its 3,850 centers worldwide, including its 125 centers across North America in an effort to combat the spread of the Coronavirus (COVID-19), devotees are participating in novel online programs to continue Satsang at home. 
 The closures across the world posed a major challenge for all ages and backgrounds that participate in weekly assemblies, spiritual discourses, and community charity initiatives. In order to maintain spiritual continuity, BAPS initiated webcasts in lieu of their regular services in the United States and Canada, as well as other centers throughout the world. 
 In North America, every week there will be four separate webcasts in multiple languages based on different age groups – children under the age of 13, adolescents between the ages of 14 and 22, young adults up to the age of 35 and the fourth for those over the age of 35. Similar webcasts will also be transmitted in other parts of the world.
 These webcasts offer a unique online experience to devotees and well-wishers, supplementing other technological mediums such as social messaging, conference call goshthis, online video platforms, and the official BAPS website to help stay virtually connected amidst social distancing efforts.
 On Sunday, March 15, 2020, BAPS congregants of North America also took part in the National Day of Prayer initiative. Under the guidance of the current spiritual head of BAPS, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, a special prayer was said in homes throughout the world for the well-being of all those affected by the coronavirus pandemic.
 Presented here is a small sample of the ‘Satsang at Home’ experience of thousands of families in North America.

/News/2020/Serving-Together-In-the-Joy-o.t: "Serving Together, In the Joy of Others", UK & Europe
/News/2020/Serving-Together-In-the-Joy-o.text:
BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha has produced a new video paying tribute to the thousands of key workers serving in the UK during the COVID-19 pandemic. 
 The video, based on a poem, features over a hundred doctors, nurses, pharmacists and more, who have joined thousands of BAME (Black, Asian and minority ethnic) key workers currently serving on the frontline.
 There are an estimated million Hindus in the UK, comprising less than 2% of the population, although the proportion of British Hindus working in the healthcare sector and other key worker positions is far higher.
 The dedication to public service among British Hindus is often attributed to the ethos of selfless service prescribed in the Hindu faith. The creator of the Neasden Temple, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, taught: “In the joy of others lies our own.”
 This teaching forms the key message for the video’s poem, titled “Serving Together in the Joy of Others.” 
 Each part of the poem is delivered by British Hindus of BAPS who are currently serving on the frontline in a wide array of fields, including as medical professionals, hospital administrators, lab researchers, shopkeepers, a hospital chef, a bus driver – even a pilot.
 The video pays tribute to and thanks all key workers who are serving tirelessly and selflessly to protect the people of Great Britain and to save lives, often at the risk of their own.

/News/2020/Shri-Krishna-Janmashtami-Cele.t: Shri Krishna Janmashtami Celebrations | London Mandir 25th Anniversary , UK & Europe
/News/2020/Shri-Krishna-Janmashtami-Cele.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shri Krishna Janmashtami Celebrations, London, UK (30 photos)
 Shri Krishna Janmashtami Celebrations at Home, UK & Europe (20 photos)
 Shri Krishna Bhagwan is a popular Hindu deity for millions around the world. He manifested on earth thousands of years ago on the Hindu calendrical day of Shravan Vad 8. This year, that auspicious day fell on Wednesday 12 August. 
 His birth anniversary was celebrated at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, with a host of devotional festivities, including a ceremonial offering of food (the ‘annakut’), singing, chanting, and an arti signifying the holy birth.
 This year’s Janmashtami festival also marked the beginning of the series of events celebrating the 25th anniversary of London Mandir. This was fitting, as the Mandir’s inauguration festivities in 1995 had also begun with Shri Krishna Janmashtami.
 The festival was further celebrated through an online evening assembly which began auspiciously with images of swamis lighting traditional divas (oil lamps) under the central dome in the inner sanctum, reciprocated by devotees in their homes. 
 The teachings of Shri Krishna, specifically his message of faith and loyalty, were presented through an enlightening programme that included bhajans sung eloquently by swamis, a captivating drama, and insightful discourses.
 Yogvivekdas Swami reflected upon Krishna Bhagwan’s intense love for and protection of his devotees, drawing upon incidents from the Mahabharat and Shrimad Bhagwat Puran. Video blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj from the 2015 Janmashtami celebrations also reiterated this message, encouraging devotees to remain faithful to God. 
 The festivities culminated with the divine birth of Shri Krishna signified by the arti followed by the joyous swinging of the paranu (swing) accompanied with vibrant devotional singing.

 Photo Gallery 
 Pujan and Prayers by HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (16 photos)
 HH Mahant Swami Maharaj's Blessings (1 photos)
 It is a moment of immense joy for all Hindus that the construction of the majestic Shri Ram Mandir, an emblem of faith and spirituality, at Ayodhya, the historic birthplace of Shri Ram, will commence in the presence of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, and several great sadhus from across India. On the historic occasion of the foundation stone-laying ceremony, 50 spiritual leaders and saints have been invited as representatives of the richly diverse culture and tradition of India. Amongst these, the spiritual head of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, has also been cordially invited. Accepting this invitation and on his behalf, the sadhus of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Pujya Brahmavihari Swami and Pujya Aksharvatsal Swami, will attend the stone-laying ceremony at Ayodhya.     
 It is noteworthy to recall that 30 years ago, when the national movement for the construction of Shri Ram Janmabhumi Mandir began, HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj had sanctified the first Ramsheela of Gujarat with Vedic rituals on 16 August 1989. Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who had prayed for several years for the construction of this mandir, had sanctified this first Ramsheela on the auspicious day of Rakshabandhan. Coincidently, on the same occasion of Rakshabandhan, on 3 August 2020, his spiritual successor, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj has sanctified with vedic rituals the ‘Shri Ramyantra’ for the foundation stone-laying ceremony of the mandir and has prayed for the earliest completion of the mandir.
 On this occasion, HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, who is currently at Nenpur, stated- “As a result of many years of resolute faith, penance and sacrifice of countless devotees and various sant-mahatmas,  the construction of the majestic mandir at the birthplace of Shri Ram is going to commence. I am immensely pleased. This mandir will provide inspiration to countless generations  from Sanatan dharma, our culture, values and spirituality. Countless generations will learn the supreme values and prescripts from the divine life of Shri Ramchandraji. This mandir will remain a prestigious pinnacle of the Hindu faith.
 Our guru Param Pujya Yogiji Maharaj and Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj constantly prayed for this Ram mandir for many years and had inspired countless devotees to participate in it. They kindled faith in all, that the Shri Ram mandir will certainly be built at the birthplace of Shri Ram. The construction of this Ram mandir is commencing on the foundations of dedication, sacrifice, and prayers. I congratulate and convey my best wishes to the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India,  the Indian Judiciary and to all those engaged in the construction of this mandir.
 May the construction of this mandir be completed at the earliest, with unity, without any obstacles, and may Bhagwan Shri Ramlalla be installed with grandeur. Also, may the present crises be resolved at the earliest. I pray so from the bottom of my heart and sincerely request you all to do the same.”
 It is noteworthy that the birth of Bhagwan Swaminarayan took place at a village called Chhapiya, located near Ayodhya, on the auspicious day of Ram Navami. He spent six years of his childhood in Ayodhya. He regularly visited every mandir in Ayodhya, heard spiritual discourses and even studied the Vedic scriptures during his stay here. It was from this very town that he embarked on his journey to the various pilgrim places across India at the tender age of 11. He travelled barefoot across terrains ranging from Mansarovar and Char Dham in the North to Kanyakumari in the South. With such divine memories of Ayodhya associated with Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan, and his fifth spiritual successor, Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, pujya santos will pay homage in this stone-laying ceremony on behalf of Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 રક્ષાબંધન પર્વે મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજે કર્યું વેદોક્ત પૂજન-પ્રાર્થના
 અમદાવાદ, ૩ ઓગષ્ટ
 અયોધ્યા ખાતે કરોડો હિન્દુઓની આસ્થાના પ્રતીક સમાન શ્રી રામ જન્મભૂમિ પર ભવ્ય શ્રી રામમંદિરના નિર્માણનો વિધિવત વડાપ્રધાન શ્રી નરેન્દ્રભાઈ મોદીના હસ્તે તેમજ ભારતના મહાન સંતોના હસ્તે આરંભ થઈ રહ્યો છે, તેની ખુશાલી કરોડો હિન્દુઓમાં ફરી વળી છે. શિલાન્યાસ વિધિના આ ગૌરવવંતા ઐતિહાસિક કાર્યક્રમમાં દેશભરમાંથી વિવિધ પરંપરાનું પ્રતિનિધિત્વ કરતા ૫૦ સંતો-મહંતોને નિમંત્રિત કરવામાં આવ્યા છે. એ પૈકી બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના આધ્યાત્મિક વડા પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજને પણ સાદર નિમંત્રિત કરવામાં આવ્યા છે. આ નિમંત્રણનો સ્વીકાર કરીને તેઓશ્રી વતી બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના સંતવર્ય પૂજ્ય બ્રહ્મવિહારી સ્વામી તથા પૂજ્ય  અક્ષરવત્સલ સ્વામી આ શિલાન્યાસ વિધિમાં ભાગ લેવા માટે અયોધ્યા જશે. 
 ઉલ્લેખનીય છે કે આજથી 30 વર્ષ પહેલાં, શ્રી રામ જન્મભૂમિના આ મંદિરના નિર્માણ માટે  શ્રીરામશિલાના  પૂજનનું રાષ્ટ્રીય આંદોલન આરંભાયું ત્યારે તા. 16 ઓગષ્ટના રોજ, ગુજરાતમાં પ્રથમ રામશિલાનું વેદોક્ત વિધિપૂર્વક પૂજન કરીને પૂજ્ય પ્રમુખસ્વામી મહારાજે કર્યું હતું. દાયકાઓ સુધી શ્રી રામજન્મભૂમિ માટે આસ્થાપૂર્વક પ્રાર્થના કરી રહેલા પૂજ્ય પ્રમુખ સ્વામી મહારાજે, રામમંદિરના નિર્માણની પ્રથમ રામશિલાનું પૂજન કર્યું એ દિવસ સન ૧૯૮૯ના રક્ષાબંધનનો દિવસ હતો. યોગાનુયોગ આ જ પવિત્ર રક્ષાબંધન પર્વે, તા. ૩ ઓગષ્ટના રોજ, તેમના અનુગામી પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજે શ્રી રામ જન્મભૂમિ પર  થનાર શિલાન્યાસ વિધિ માટે શ્રીરામયંત્રનું  વૈદિક પૂજન કરીને આ મંદિર વહેલામાં વહેલી તકે સાકાર થાય તેવી શ્રદ્ધા અને પ્રાર્થના વ્યક્ત કરી છે.
 આ પ્રસંગે નેનપુર ખાતે બિરાજતા પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજ જણાવ્યું  છે કે “કરોડો ભક્તો અને સંતો-મહાત્માઓની અનેક વર્ષોની શ્રદ્ધા, તપસ્યા, બલિદાનની  ફલશ્રુતિ રૂપે ભગવાન શ્રીરામની જન્મભૂમિ પર ભવ્ય મંદિરનો આરંભ થઈ રહ્યો છે, તેનો અપાર આનંદ છે. આવનારી અનેક પેઢીઓ આ મંદિરમાંથી સનાતનધર્મ, સંસ્કૃતિ, સંસ્કારો, અધ્યાત્મ વગેરેની પવિત્ર પ્રેરણાઓ મેળવશે. અનેક પેઢીઓ ભગવાન શ્રી રામચંદ્રજીના દિવ્ય જીવનમાંથી માનવતાના સર્વોત્તમ મૂલ્યો અને આદર્શો શીખશે. આ મંદિર હિન્દુ ધર્મની અસ્મિતાનું એક ગૌરવ શિખર બની રહેશે. અમારા ગુરુ પરમ પૂજ્ય યોગીજી મહારાજ અને પરમ પૂજ્ય પ્રમુખસ્વામી મહારાજે શ્રી રામમંદિર માટે વર્ષો સુધી સતત પ્રાર્થના કરીને લાખો ભક્તોને તેમાં જોડાવાની પ્રેરણા આપી હતી અને સૌમાં વિશ્વાસ પ્રગટાવ્યો હતો કે શ્રી રામ જન્મભૂમિ પર જરૂર શ્રીરામમંદિર બનશે જ. સમર્પણ, બલિદાન અને પ્રાર્થનાની વેદી પર આ શ્રીરામમંદિરના  નિર્માણનો આરંભ થાય છે ત્યારે, તેમાં જોડાયેલા સૌ કાર્યવાહકો, માનનીય વડાપ્રધાન શ્રી નરેન્દ્રભાઈ મોદી, ભારત સરકાર અને ભારતીય ન્યાયતંત્ર સહિત સૌને અભિનંદન સાથે  હૃદયપૂર્વક શુભેચ્છાઓ પાઠવું છું.”
 વહેલાંમાં વહેલી તકે આ મંદિરનું નિર્માણ કાર્ય સૌની એકતાથી નિર્વિઘ્ને પૂર્ણ થઈ જાય અને ભગવાન શ્રી રામલલા તેમાં ધામધૂમપૂર્વક વિરાજમાન થઈ જાય, અને વર્તમાન સમયની આપત્તિઓનું પણ વહેલી તકે નિવારણ થાય, તેવી અંતઃકરણપૂર્વક પ્રાર્થના કરું છું અને આપ સૌને એવી પ્રાર્થના કરવા હાર્દિક વિનંતી કરું છું. ”
 અત્રે ઉલ્લેખનીય છે કે ભગવાન શ્રી સ્વામિનારાયણનો જન્મ અયોધ્યાની નજીક આવેલા છપૈયા ગામે  રામનવમીના પવિત્ર દિવસે થયો હતો. પોતાના બાલ્યકાળના છ વર્ષો તેઓએ અયોધ્યામાં વિતાવ્યા હતા. તીર્થનગરી અયોધ્યાના પ્રત્યેક મંદિરમાં નિત્ય  દર્શન અને  કથાનો સતત લાભ લેનાર બાળવયના તેઓએ વેદાદિક શાસ્ત્રોનો અભ્યાસ પણ અહીં જ કર્યો હતો. અહીંથી જ  ૧૧ વર્ષની ઉંમરે તેઓએ અખિલ ભારતની તીર્થ યાત્રાનો આરંભ કર્યો હતો, જેમાં તેમણે ખુલ્લા પગે માનસરોવર અને ચારધામથી લઈ દક્ષિણમાં છેક કન્યાકુમારી સુધી તીર્થોની યાત્રા કરી હતી. એવા ભગવાન શ્રી સ્વામિનારાયણ તેમજ તેમના પંચમ અનુગામી પૂજ્ય પ્રમુખ સ્વામી મહારાજની અયોધ્યા સાથે જોડાયેલી અનેક પવિત્ર સ્મૃતિઓ સાથે, પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજ વતી પ્રતિનિધિ સંતો આ શિલાન્યાસ વિધિમાં પોતાનું અર્ઘ્ય અર્પણ કરશે.

/News/2020/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti-and.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti and Shri Rama Navami Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti-and.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Darshan, London, UK (20 photos)
 Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Rama Navami Celebrations, London, UK (20 photos)
 Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti and Shri Rama Navami Celebrations, UK & Europe (80 photos)
 The birth celebrations of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Rama were devoutly observed on Thursday 2 April 2020 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. Families across the UK and Europe viewed the celebrations in their respective homes via a live web stream due to the closure of all BAPS mandirs and centres in response to the global COVID-19 pandemic.
 Swamis delivered a programme of devotional singing and discourses in Hindi during the morning, in which the exemplary life of Bhagwan Rama was described in detail, drawing particularly upon the challenges that he overcame in his life through spiritual faith and understanding. 
 These teachings imparted a timely source of strength and wisdom at a time of great uncertainty facing the world. The ceremonial arti, marking the divine birth of Bhagwan Rama, was held at noon. 
 Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s values of compassion and selfless service to society transformed the lives of millions of people. Swamis began the evening programme with a celebration of these ideals, fittingly joining in a nationwide tribute of all health workers and key personnel who are serving tirelessly and selflessly to protect others during the current pandemic. Devotees also participated in this ‘Clap for Carers’ campaign from their respective doorsteps, windows, gardens and balconies.  
 A special evening assembly thereafter unfolded in which swamis presented a musical narration of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine life and work. Their devotional singing was interspersed with enlightening video presentations and discourses, charting Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s journey of social and spiritual reform, and the spiritual legacy that he bequeathed.
 Swamis then performed the ritual bathing of Thakorji with panchamrut – a holy mixture of milk, yogurt, honey, sugar and ghee – amid the chanting of the Sahajanand Namavali, the 108 auspicious and liberating names of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Devotees simultaneously performed this ritual in their own homes and prayed for God to provide strength for everyone affected by the pandemic.
 The evening celebrations culminated with a special arti at 10.10pm, signifying the precise time Bhagwan Swaminarayan chose to be born to mother Bhaktimata in the small north Indian village of Chhapaiya. Devotees joined in this arti from their homes and gently swayed the murti of Ghanshyam in the cradles they had earlier made together as a family.
 Families had marked these celebrations throughout the day with a host of festivities, beginning their day with a samuh puja, preparing freshly made sweet dishes as a devotional offering in their ghar mandirs, and adorning their mandirs with vibrant and colourful decorations. Children also made birthday cards inscribed with their personal prayers. The uplifting and auspicious day brought a profound sense of warmth and joy to thousands of individuals in homes around the UK and European continent. Even at a time of national lockdown, it brought people together in a shared sense of spiritual purpose, through the aid of technology and the power of their devotion.

Photo Gallery 
 Mahapuja (19 photos)
 On 12 July 2020, in Nenpur, Gujarat, Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj presided, via video conference, over the sanctification of 200 sets of metallic murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj for the devotees of New Zealand to keep in their homes and offer devotion.
 Thereafter, with the coronavirus pandemic under control in New Zealand, a special mahapuja was conducted at the BAPS Mandir in Auckland. Around 300 devotees at the mandir and many more online performed pujan of the Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj murtis which had been remotely sanctified by Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 This occasion also marked the reopening of Satsang assemblies across New Zealand. Through discourses, the swamis emphasized the importance of having the murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj at home and inspired all the devotees to daily offer their heartfelt bhakti in their ghar mandirs.
 During the mahapuja rituals, the swamis also prayed for the well-being of all, and an early end to the COVID-19 pandemic.

 Over 300 kishores and kishoris from 13 BAPS centers (Sydney, Melbourne, Tarneit, Cranbourne, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Adelaide, Perth, Darwin, Canberra, Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch) in Australia and New Zealand simultaneously participated in a special online mahapuja to offer prayers for the success of the youths in their studies and especially for their upcoming final exams beginning in October.

 Over 3,000 families from BAPS centers throughout Australia and New Zealand participated in a special pujan ritual of the ‘Satsang Diksha’ shastra written by guruhari Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj. The pujan rituals were led by swamis at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Sydney, Australia, while, through a live webcast, devotees devoutly performed the pujan rituals in their homes.
 The swamis encouraged all devotees to memorize the verses of the Satsang Diksha and emphasized that Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj has expressed his profound delight and blessings to all who are memorizing the Satsang Diksha. Mahant Swami Maharaj has blessed that everyone will progress in all ways by memorizing the Satsang Diksha shastra.
 Thus, to attain Mahant Swami Maharaj's blessings, many devotees pledged to daily recite and memorize the verses.

/News/2020/Swaminarayan-Jayanti-Family-C.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Ram Navmi Family Celebrations 2020, North America
/News/2020/Swaminarayan-Jayanti-Family-C.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Ghar Mandir Decoration (31 photos)
 Family Devotion (41 photos)
 Swaminarayan Jayanti Sabha (22 photos)
 On April 2, 2020, devotees across North America watched a livestream of the celebration of Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti and Shri Ram Jayanti from the safety of their homes at 8:00 pm local time. With the COVID-19 pandemic bringing significant disruption and uncertainty to daily life, devotees took comfort in recalling the divine stories of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram.
 The beginning of the program focused on the virtues of Bhagwan Shri Ram’s life and how He was the embodiment of righteous conduct.  Particular focus was given to Bhagwan Ram’s selfless thoughts, temperament in His speech, and His steady demeanor – all being particularly relevant to current times.
 The remainder of the program was centered around the Swaminarayan Yash Gatha, a musical performance by Swamis showcasing Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s life. The program began with the divine circumstances of His birth in Chhapaiya to His parents, Dharmadev and Bhaktimata, to the establishment of a spiritual lineage of gurus years later. The performance of the Swaminarayan Yash Gatha was interwoven with animated depictions of divine incidents from Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s life as a child, Ghanshyam, and later as a traveling yogi, Nilkanth Varni. These incidents helped devotees and well-wishers understand the value Bhagwan Swaminarayan placed on devotion and remaining courageous in the face of peril.
 The culmination of the program focused on how HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj and HH Mahant Swami Maharaj have tirelessly travelled the world without regard to bodily comforts, to share the values taught and lived by Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Senior Swamis Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami, Sadguru Pujya Kothari Swami (Pujya Bhaktipriyadas Swami),  Sadguru Pujya Viveksagardas Swami, and Sadguru Pujya Doctor Swami (Pujya Swayamprakashdas Swami) imparted their knowledge and provided inspiration to devotees through their discourses.
 As a lead up to the program, devotees participated in the celebration of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram’s birth, in their homes, through a day dedicated to family and devotion. In the morning, many families performed their nitya puja (morning prayers) in unison and listened to the Shri Sahajanand Namavali.  During the day, devotees decorated their Ghar Mandirs (shrines-at-home) and made cradles to the celebrate the birth of young Ghanshyam (childhood name of Bhagwan Swaminarayan). Once the program concluded, devotees participated in the evening Arti streamed live from their nearby shikharbaddh mandir. Although devotees across North America were physically apart, they were able to experience the divine bliss of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram together through these celebrations.

/News/2020/Swamis-and-Devotees-Applaud-F.t: Swamis and Devotees Applaud Frontline Personnel During COVID-19 Pandemic, Nairobi, Kenya
/News/2020/Swamis-and-Devotees-Applaud-F.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Swamis Applaud Frontline Personnel (5 photos)
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha joined local communities, states, and countries around the world to support the fight against the current COVID-19 pandemic.  Every corner of the world has been disrupted by the pandemic as the general public is advised to take preventative measures such as social distancing and ‘sheltering in place’ in some areas. 
 For the benefit of others, many brave heroes put themselves at great risk to take care of our families and communities affected by COVID-19: doctors, nurses, paramedics, public safety officers, and other frontline workers.  These individuals risk their health every day to stem the impact of the pandemic. To honor and appreciate the selfless efforts of these men and women working tirelessly in healthcare and public safety, swamis at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Nairobi participated in applauding the frontline workers and expressed their support and solidarity during the COVID-19 pandemic. Devotees also participated by applauding from their homes.
 At a time when the most important duty of each citizen is to maintain social distancing to help contain the spread of the coronavirus, BAPS has responded to government requests for assistance to care for the needy.
 Throughout Africa, BAPS has served in various ways, as requested by local leaders.
 Under the guidance and inspiration of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha will continue to provide such assistance to help the needy during this challenging period.
 BAPS communities around the world continue to pray for the well-being of these heroes as well as for peace and positivity as we persevere through these trying times.

/News/2020/The-Voice-of-Our-Conscience--.t: The Voice of Our Conscience - Global Covid Aid, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2020/The-Voice-of-Our-Conscience--.text:
"The Voice of Our Conscience" is a creative video that portrays the challenges, the changes and the channelisation of global humanitarian efforts during the years of the Coronavirus Pandemic.
 Without showing death, disease or depression, it inspires hope and positivity through introspection.  It is an emotional,  thought-provoking journey that restores hope in humanity and faith in life.
 While it summarises the COVID AID provided by the BAPS Hindu Mandir in the UAE, it also encompasses the huge worldwide COVID support by the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.
 More than mere facts and figures, it celebrates life by focusing upon the voice within us, the voice of our conscience - the immortal holy words of HH Guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj - "The Value of saving one life is PRICELESS."

/News/2020/Threlford-Memorial-Cup-Awarde.t: Threlford Memorial Cup Awarded for Gujarati Teaching to BAPS, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Threlford-Memorial-Cup-Awarde.text:
BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK has been awarded the prestigious Threlford Memorial Cup for 2020 by the Chartered Institute of Linguists.
 The Threlford Cup, awarded annually since 1935, is presented to individuals or organisations that have evidenced a significant contribution in fostering the study of languages, and is a part of the Institute's wider initiative to "celebrate the importance of language and cultural understanding... and excellence in language learning". This award recognises the important and impactful contribution to the development of tools, resources and training to promote the learning of the Gujarati language.
 This latest accolade, in addition to others received in the past, pays tribute to the efforts of many BAPS volunteers who have transformed the learning and teaching of Gujarati into an enjoyable, accessible and innovative experience. Games and resources have been developed that have infused modern education techniques with traditional Hindu values to provide a system of ‘gammat sāthe gnān’ or ‘knowledge through enjoyment’.
 The multifarious resources include an eight-book comprehensive Gujarati syllabus to GCSE level. Many interactive board and card games, such as Gujarati Whiz, Gujarati Spinner, Gujarati Flash Cards and Gujarati Strips, as well as games and resources for pre-school children, including a wooden Gujarati alphabet board and wooden Gujarati cubes, are available through the BAPS online gift shop.
 The accessibility, scalability and simplicity of these resources have helped upskill the knowledge and performance of teachers around the world, enabling centres to replicate the methods and standards for their own schools across the UK and in Europe as well as in North America, Africa, the Asia-Pacific, the UAE, and even Gujarat. The dedication and collective endeavours of the volunteers have produced exceptional results for children taking GCSE and A-levels in Gujarati who have passed their papers with excellent scores.
 The award was accepted by Rahul Bhagvat on behalf of a team of creative and dedicated BAPS volunteers – including Alpesh Patel,  Miraj Patel, Lalji Ladwa, Shailesh Pujara, Jignasha Patel and Saryu Patel, amongst others – who spearheaded a number of projects to develop new Gujarati resources. More recently, this has involved innovative teaching aids that will harness digital technology to make learning Gujarati more enjoyable, engaging and effective. 
 Rahul explains, “Gujarati is an integral component of our services for children at BAPS. It is inspired by Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s teaching that “Bhāshā jashe to sanskār jashe” – “If language is lost, culture is lost.” We thus endeavour to ensure that our children have the highest standard of resources available to help them learn Gujarati in the most effective and enjoyable way, thereby facilitating their all-round cultural, academic and spiritual development.”
 To learn more about the award and the Chartered Institute of Linguists, please click the respective links.
 Disclaimer: BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha is not responsible for the content of external internet sites.

 The Vachanamrut is the foremost scripture of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya and contains Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s spiritual discourses compiled by four of his eminent paramhansas. The first discourse in the Vachanamrut is dated 21 November 1819. So, to commemorate the bicentenary of the commencement of the Vachanamrut, over the past 18 months, devotees of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha throughout the world have undertaken special devotional observances.
 As a grand finale to the Vachanamrut Bicentenary Celebrations, five days of festivities have been scheduled in Gadhada, the small town which served as Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s base for over 25 years.
 Among the events that will take place are:
 A vast Swaminarayan Nagar featuring:
 Four excellent exhibitions that will inspire individuals and families and to lead addiction-free, harmonious and spiritually centric lives through specially produced video films.
  Statues of inspiring acharyas, saints and devotees like Shri Vallabhacharya, Sant Tulsidas, Shri Narsinh Mehta and others.
  ‘Divya Sankalp Gatha’ (The Story of a Divine Wish) – a projection mapping show that together with live dances, skits and music narrates the history of Gadhada mandir.
 Inauguration of 25-ft murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan on his mare, Manki, Aksharbrahman Gunatitanand Swami and Bhaktaraj Shri Dada Khachar.
 Inauguration of a permanent exhibition in the renovated darbar of Bhaktaraj Shri Jiva Khachar sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 Dispersal of the sacred ashes of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj into the holy River Ghela.
 Assembly felicitating the descendents of Bhaktaraj Shri Dada Khachar, Bhaktaraj Shri Jiva Khachar and local dignitaries of Gadhada.
 Special events to honor the Vachanamrut: Colorful procession through the streets of Gadhada, worship of the Vachanamrut, continuous recital of the Vachanamrut, Vachanamrut Tula.
 Grand concluding assembly paying homage to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Vachanamrut.

/News/2020/Vedic-Hindu-Prayer-at-the-Whi.t: BAPS Participates in National Day of Prayer at the White House, Washington DC, USA
/News/2020/Vedic-Hindu-Prayer-at-the-Whi.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Vedic Shanti Path at the White House (7 photos)
 On May 7, 2020, the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha was invited to participate in the National Day of Prayer in the Rose Garden at the White House in Washington D.C.  The National Day of Prayer is an annual event formally enacted in 1952 celebrating faith and prayer in the nation’s life.  Today’s commemoration was all-the-more solemn due to the COVID-19 crisis affecting the nation.  The event allowed the country to join together to offer prayers for those affected, our brave frontline workers and healthcare workers and for the recovery of our country.  
 President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence offered their prayers followed by prayers from religious leaders representing four of the major faith traditions – Christianity, Hinduism, Judaism and Islam. 
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) was invited by the White House to participate. Harish Brahmbhatt, a pujari of BAPS was recognized at the prayer meeting and he shared a Hindu prayer of peace from the Vedas.  Speaking at the prayer meeting, he said, “In these troubled times of COVID-19, social distancing and the lockdown, it’s not unusual for people to feel anxious or not at peace.  The Shanti Path or the peace prayer, is a prayer that does not seek worldly riches, success, fame, nor is it a prayer for any desire for heaven.  It is a beautiful Hindu prayer for peace, shanti. It is a Vedic prayer derived from the Yajur Veda.”
 This prayer was specially chosen due to the overarching theme that in all circumstances we should always pray for peace above all things.
 In conjunction with prayers during these trying times, BAPS, and its non-denominational, humanitarian arm, BAPS Charities, have responded to the coronavirus pandemic with a spirit of selfless service.
 To date, in addition to other global efforts, BAPS Charities in the US has supported hospitals and frontline workers by providing over 96,000 PPE and over 35,000 food and care packages.  BAPS Charities has also provided financial support for equipment to hospitals around the country.  For more details, visit https://www.bapscharities.org/covid-19/
 BAPS continues to provide spiritual support through counseling, online religious services and ceremonies and, most importantly, regular prayer for those affected, our all healthcare workers, scientists and researchers, our leaders, and for all of humanity as we rise to face this challenge.

/News/2020/Virtual-Medico-Spiritual-Conf.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Virtual Conference (9 photos)
 Over 530 medical students from throughout Gujarat tuned in to participate in the online Medico-Spiritual Conference based on the theme ‘Faith: Winning Formula for Life’.
 The 2-day conference featured guidance from Pujya Doctor Swami, as well as inspiring speeches by learned and experienced BAPS swamis and other professionals which helped to cultivate faith in God and guru, trust in others and self-belief among the delegates. Special audio-visual presentations reinforced the conference theme.
 The highlight of the conference was the blessings from Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The virtual conference was smoothly conducted due to the diligent efforts of the technical team.

/News/2020/World-Peace-Prayers-for-COVID.t: Devotees Participate in World Peace Prayers for COVID-19 Pandemic, North America
/News/2020/World-Peace-Prayers-for-COVID.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Abhishek Vidhi at Home (101 photos)
 Abhishek Vidhi at Mandir (19 photos)
 BAPS devotees across North America participated in a Vishwashanti Abhishek Pujanvidhi (Prayer for world peace) on April 18, 2020 from their homes. Devotees were led through this prayer by Swamis in their regional Shikharbadh Mandirs, over a livestream. Instructions for the Vedic prayer were narrated by these Swamis, while each devotee performed that action from their home. Devotees embraced the ancient Hindu tradition of praying for world peace, given the far-reaching effects of the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic.
 Families dressed in traditional Indian attire and gathered in their living rooms or their Ghar Mandirs (shrine-at-home). Devotees performed abhishek, the Vedic tradition of bathing a murti (sacred image) of God, to honor God and receive His blessings for a quick and safe resolution to the COVID-19 pandemic. As a conclusion to the Pujanvidhi, Swamis also led the devotees in praying for:
 the souls who passed away due to the pandemic,
 the recovery of all those who are infected,
 the continued health and well-being of elderly and those at risk,
 the well-being of frontline workers who serve the community,
 the re-employment of those who have lost their jobs,
 financial stability for those with businesses,
 minimal disruption to students’ education,
 the well-being of teachers and academic staff who engage in ‘distance-learning’,
 the companies, researchers, and institutions trying to discover treatments and vaccines,
 and all others impacted or affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.
 In conclusion, Swamis also led devotees in praying that through working from home and spending time at home, families are able to grow together and live in unity and harmony.

/News/2020/Worldwide-Prakruti-Vandan-by-.t: Worldwide 'Prakruti Vandan' by Thousands of BAPS Swamis and Devotees, India
/News/2020/Worldwide-Prakruti-Vandan-by-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (7 photos)
 Sarangpur (11 photos)
 Ahmedabad (9 photos)
 Pune (8 photos)
 Gandhinagar (6 photos)
 Delhi (11 photos)
 BAPS Centers (96 photos)
 Since ancient times, Hindus have honored and cared for nature and the environment, since healthy surroundings are essential for human survival. Among the many challenges facing the modern-day world, the need to protect the environment is one of the most important. To raise the awareness for this, spiritual head of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, as well as thousands of BAPS swamis and devotees throughout India and the world performed ‘Prakruti Vandan’ – special worship rituals to trees and plants to honor their role in sustaining life on earth – on 30 August 2020.
 The special rituals, performed while adhering to coronavirus safety guidelines, included chanting of the Vedic Shanti Path (Universal Peace Prayer), and pujan and arti of a tree or plant.
 While performing the honor rituals in Nenpur, Gujarat, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “Pramukh Swami Maharaj frequently said that if you take care of nature, nature will take care of you. He inspired people to plant hundreds of thousands of trees and guided us on how to care for nature and the environment. Let us all resolve today to protect the environment and ensure a healthy human future.”
 As per the wish of Mahant Swami Maharaj, 1,100 BAPS sadhus and thousands of devotees in India, the UK, USA, Canada, Africa, Australia, New Zealand, the Middle East and other BAPS centers worldwide performed the special rituals at 11.00 a.m. local time.
 Of special note is that several historic and sacred trees were among those worshiped. In Sarangpur, Doctor Swami honored the Shami tree sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan; in Ahmedabad, Tyagvallabh Swami worshiped a neem tree planted at the request of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj; at Akshardham in Gandhinagar, Ishwarcharan Swami honored the generations-old banyan tree sanctified by Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj; and at Akshardham in New Delhi, Dharmavatsal Swami and other saints performed pujan of the jambu tree sanctified by Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 Such widespread participation in these worship rituals was a fitting tribute to the environmental activities inspired by Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj as we continue to celebrate his birth centenary.
 વિશ્વભરમાં ' પ્રકૃતિ વંદન' કરતા બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંપ્રદાયના હજારો સંતો અને હરિભકતો
 ભારતીય સંસ્કૃતિમાં વૈદિક સમયથી પ્રકૃતિ પ્રત્યે પ્રેમ અને  આદરનો એક અનોખો  પ્રવાહ વહેતો રહ્યો છે. વૈદિક શાંતિપાઠથી લઈને વટપૂજન કે તુલસીપૂજન જેવી અનેક પરંપરાઓ આપણને પ્રકૃતિના જતનનો સંદેશ આપતી રહી છે. વર્તમાન વિશ્વ અનેક સમસ્યાઓમાંથી પસાર થઈ રહ્યું છે ત્યારે હવે સૌને સમજાઈ રહ્યું છે કે આપણે પ્રકૃતિથી જેટલા દૂર જઈ રહ્યા છીએ  તેટલી વધુ સમસ્યાઓને નિમંત્રણ આપી રહ્યા છીએ. આથી જ પ્રકૃતિવંદના દ્વારા પ્રકૃતિના જતનનો વૈશ્વિક સંદેશ આપતાં બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના ધર્મગુરુ  પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજે તારીખ 30  ઓગસ્ટ 2020ના રોજ બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના લાખો હરિભક્તોને પ્રકૃતિવંદનાના  વૈશ્વિક કાર્યક્રમમાં જોડાવા આહવાન આપ્યું હતું. 
 તેઓશ્રીના આદેશ મુજબ  બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના  ભારત અને વિદેશના હજારો સત્સંગ કેન્દ્રોમાં તારીખ 30 ઓગસ્ટ 2020 ના રોજ સ્થાનિક સમય પ્રમાણે 11:00 વાગે લાખો હરિભક્તો પ્રકૃતિવંદનાના આ કાર્યક્રમમાં જોડાયા હતા.  કોરોના મહામારીના સમયમાં અનિવાર્ય એવા નીતિનિયમોનું બરાબર પાલન કરીને  સૌએ વૈદિક  શાંતિપાઠ સાથે વૃક્ષપૂજન અથવા તુલસીપૂજન કરીને આરતી ઉતારી હતી.
 આ જ સમયે  નેનપુર ખાતે બિરાજમાન પરમ પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજે  વૈદિક શાંતિપાઠ સાથે વૃક્ષપૂજન અને તુલસીપૂજન કરીને આરતી ઉતારી હતી. બ્રહ્મસ્વરૂપ પ્રમુખસ્વામી મહારાજે કરેલા વિરાટ વૃક્ષારોપણના  સેવાકાર્યની સ્મૃતિ સાથે પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજે જણાવ્યું હતું કે ‘પ્રમુખસ્વામી મહારાજ હંમેશા કહેતા કે તમે પ્રકૃતિનું જતન કરશો તો પ્રકૃતિ તમારું જતન કરશે.  તેમણે લાખોની સંખ્યામાં વૃક્ષારોપણ કરાવીને આપણને સૌને  વૃક્ષોનું, પ્રકૃતિનું, પર્યાવરણનું જતન કરવાનો આદેશ  અને સંદેશ આપ્યો છે. તો આપણે સૌ આજે  પ્રતિજ્ઞાબદ્ધ થઈએ અને પ્રકૃતિની સેવા કરીને, વૃક્ષોનું જતન અને સંવર્ધન કરીને માનવજાતનું ભવિષ્ય ઉજ્જવળ બનાવીએ.’
 પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજના આદેશ મુજબ બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના તમામ મંદિરોમાં ૧૧૦૦થી વધુ સંતોએ પણ વૈદિક પરંપરા મુજબ વૃક્ષપૂજન કર્યું હતું.  તેમાં સંસ્થાના વરિષ્ઠ સદગુરુવર્ય સંતોએ ઐતિહાસિક અને પ્રાસાદિક વૃક્ષનું પૂજન કર્યું હતું. પૂજ્ય ડોક્ટર સ્વામીએ સારંગપુર ખાતે ભગવાન સ્વામિનારાયણના મહાપ્રસાદિક શમીવૃક્ષનું પૂજન કર્યું હતું.  પૂજ્ય  ત્યાગવલ્લભદાસ સ્વામીએ અમદાવાદ ખાતે બ્રહ્મસ્વરૂપ શાસ્ત્રીજી મહારાજ દ્વારા રોપાયેલા  નીંબતરુના પ્રાસાદિક વૃક્ષનું પૂજન કર્યું હતું. ગાંધીનગરમાં અક્ષરધામ ખાતે પૂજ્ય ઈશ્વરચરણ સ્વામી બ્રહ્મસ્વરૂપ યોગીજી મહારાજના પ્રાસાદિક પૌરાણિક સમયના વટવૃક્ષનું પૂજન કર્યું હતું. આ ઉપરાંત દિલ્હીમાં અક્ષરધામ ખાતે બ્રહ્મસ્વરૂપ પ્રમુખસ્વામી મહારાજના પ્રાસાદિક જાંબુવૃક્ષનું પૂજન પૂજ્ય ધર્મવત્સલ સ્વામી અને સંતોએ  કર્યું હતું.
 લંડન, ન્યુયોર્ક, શિકાગો, એટલાન્ટા, લોસ એન્જેલસ, ટોરંટો, નૈરોબી, સીડની,  મેલબર્ન, દુબઈ, બાહરીન વગેરે વિશ્વના અનેક મહાનગરો સહિત  ભારતના અનેક મહાનગરો અને આદિવાસીઓના ગામડાઓ સુધી બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના લાખો ભક્તો અને સંતોએ પ્રકૃતિવંદના કરીને ભારતની આ મહાન પરંપરાના  જતનની પ્રેરણાને હૃદયમાં  દૃઢ કરી હતી. બ્રહ્મસ્વરૂપ પ્રમુખસ્વામી મહારાજના શતાબ્દી મહોત્સવના  ઉપક્રમે પ્રકૃતિવંદનાનો આ કાર્યક્રમ તેઓના ચરણે એક મહાન અંજલિરૂપ બની રહ્યો છે.

/News/2020/Yogiji-Maharaj-in-the-UK-50th.t: Yogiji Maharaj in the UK: 50th Anniversary Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2020/Yogiji-Maharaj-in-the-UK-50th.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yogiji Maharaj in the UK: A Photo Story (100 photos)
 50th Anniversary Celebrations, Nenpur, India (20 photos)
 50th Anniversary Celebrations, London, UK (20 photos)
 50th Anniversary Celebrations at Home, UK & Europe (40 photos)
 In 1970, His Holiness Yogiji Maharaj and a group of 12 swamis arrived in the UK. It was the first time that swamis of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya were visiting the country. During their one-and-half-month stay, Yogiji Maharaj inaugurated a mandir in Islington, north London – one of the very first Hindu temples in the UK and the first ever Swaminarayan mandir in the western hemisphere – setting in motion a grand legacy that lives on and thrives today.
 A grand celebration commemorating the 50th anniversary of this historic occasion was webcast to many thousands across the world on Sunday 14 June 2020. It was exactly 50 years to the day when Yogiji Maharaj performed the murti-pratishtha ceremony in Islington, on Sunday 14 June 1970. The ceremony then had concluded with the first arti of the murtis at 12.22pm, which was replicated 50 years later at precisely that time with the original murtis under the dome of the new, stone temple in Neasden that Yogiji Maharaj himself had prophesised 50 years ago. An annakut of 50 cakes, 50 dry fruit delicacies and several other items had also been offered to the murtis in the shrines.
 The day began much earlier, at 1.30am BST, when the swamis of London performed a medley of kirtans during Mahant Swami Maharaj’s puja. The live performance in London relayed to Nenpur via video conference facilities retold in brief the history and impact of Yogiji Maharaj’s visit in 1970. The performance celebrating its 50th anniversary also served as the 50th of 100 musical tributes being offered to His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj on his birth centenary. The kirtan narrative was interspersed with audio recordings of Yogiji Maharaj himself, much to the interest and delight of Mahant Swami Maharaj in India.
 The climax of the celebrations was a riveting, eye-opening three-hour documentary-style production reliving one of the most momentous periods of BAPS history. Told through rare video footage, photographs, letters and audio records as well as eyewitness accounts from senior devotees, swamis, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, it brought to life the history in a way never seen before. [Details of the visit are presented in the accompanying gallery, ‘Yogiji Maharaj in the UK: A Photo Story’.]
 In his video blessings from India, Mahant Swami Maharaj drew upon this golden history and Yogiji Maharaj’s unfathomable vision, encouraging everyone to continue his ethos of humility, devotion and sincere service with samp (unity) – values close to Yogiji Maharaj’s heart.
 The grand celebrations concluded with the evening arti and a closing prayer offered to Yogiji Maharaj paying tribute to his love, pristine saintliness and exuberant enthusiasm, with heartfelt pledges to live by his teachings and wishes.
 Families had joined in the celebrations from home throughout the day by decorating their ghar mandirs, offering celebratory food to their murtis, and participating in the special arti at the end.
 The unforgettable programme rekindled golden memories for those present in 1970, while for others, it presented an opportunity to learn, appreciate and be inspired by the priceless history upon which they stand today. Shilpa Patel, one of the thousands who watched the webcast, said, “It’s very rare to watch a historic documentary and feel as if you were really there. What a truly wonderful programme. My whole family, including my younger children, were captivated and learned so much about the history of satsang and the legacy that Yogiji Maharaj created for Hindus and the many migrant Indians from East Africa.”

St John’s Baptist Church on 77 Elmore Street in Islington, London, was for sale with an asking price of £12,000. But this was proving unaffordable for the fellowship of a few, modest devotees. Yogiji Maharaj gave them strength to persist through an inspirational letter written from Kampala on 25 March 1970

Jayantibhai (Changa) was graced with a vision of Yogiji Maharaj assuring him that the price for the building would be lowered. The faithful devotees persevered and the church authorities agreed to sell for £9,500. The innumerable memories and joy of this historic visit of 1970 made devotees fondly remember Dollis Hill as ‘Akshar Hill’

 A total of 297 yuvaks and 375 yuvatis from Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Darwin, Gold Coast, Hobart, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney in Australia; Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch and Hamilton in New Zealand; and other centers across Australia and New Zealand participated in the Satsang Diksha Adhiveshan which involved memorizing verses from the Satsang Diksha shastra.
 Starting in September 2020, this competition was conducted in four monthly phases, concluding in December 2020 on the occasion of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 99th birthday celebration. In each phase the youths were tested on what they had memorized remotely via video conferencing platforms.

/News/2020/kdc-2020-19479.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Celebration at Home (84 photos)
 Program (10 photos)
 North America for centuries has been a beacon of acceptance and integration of different religions, languages, values, cultures, and beliefs. BAPS for years has sought to preserve the essence of Hindu festivals by educating individuals, especially the youth, of their enduring spiritual significance. Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is an especially auspicious time of celebration for Hindus.  Diwali is a celebration of the historical return of Bhagwan Shri Ram from his 14-year exile from Ayodhya, accompanied by the universal values that he exemplified. During these auspicious days, families come together to celebrate these universal values of unity, respect, and loyalty while renewing efforts to live a more righteous and spiritual life.
 In order to help families pass on this understanding and values to younger generations, BAPS has annually organized Kids' Diwali Celebration at centers throughout North America. On November 7, 2020, a virtual Diwali celebration program took place for all school-aged children across North America. The theme, Choose to be Good, reminded children that righteousness is a key tenet of living a more fulfilling life. Where in past years, children would partake in carnival rides, board games, and engaging activities to learn of the significance of Diwali,  the live broadcast,  involved similar interactive activities through creative mediums this year. A unique storytelling experience engaged the children with rangoli and the lighting of divas. In the days leading up to the celebration, all children were encouraged to prepare a traditional food item to create Annakut at home across North America. Under the leadership and guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS continues to promote activities that strengthen universal values and the spiritual knowledge of children worldwide.

/News/2020/psm-99-19514.aspx.text:

 Although it was not possible to celebrate His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 99th birthday in person at BAPS mandirs across North America due to the global COVID-19 pandemic, virtual celebrations were held with equal fanfare, joy, and devotion in the homes of thousands of devotees across the world. Through five days of interactive, home-based celebrations paying tribute to the life and work of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, devotees expressed their love and bhakti with personal and family-based activities.      
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj was an ocean of virtues. His goodness spread throughout the world, with all that he directly or indirectly came into contact. Pramukh Swami Maharaj exemplified what it means to think globally and act locally.  Through his actions, Pramukh Swami Maharaj taught that to change the world, one must start with oneself.  Each of us should strive to be better parents, children, siblings, cousins, friends, and good citizens.  Each person should “lead by doing” and cultivate noble thoughts and actions within oneself to collectively create positive families, communities, and nations.  Pramukh Swami Maharaj inspired thousands through his deep spirituality, humility, and dedication to service. Through inspiring the construction of traditional Hindu mandirs and centers across India, Europe, North America, and Africa, he inspired devotees to lead values-based lives founded on the Vedic principles. Pramukh Swami's loving and gentle guidance helped devotees to balance spirituality with the pressures of school, work, and family life. This focus on personal development, in turn, helped foster stronger communities, steeped in the universal humanitarian values of love, peace, and respect for all.
 The five-day virtual programs included sadhus, devotees, and notable personalities reflecting on the positive impact Pramukh Swami Maharaj had on their lives. With a focus on samp (unity), seva (selfless service), samjan (understanding), sadhana (spiritual effort), and smruti (remembrance of divine memories of the Guru), the program highlighted Pramukh Swami Maharaj's spiritual teachings and wisdom. The interactive and introspective celebrations left families with a deeper appreciation of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's life work and a firm resolve to imbibe and carry forward their beloved Guru's legacy.

 Shilanyas Vidhi (30 photos)
 The historic foundation stone-laying ceremony (Shilanyas Vidhi) of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Calgary, Alberta took place on Sunday, August 16, 2020. The vedic ceremony took place at the new Mandir site following social distancing protocols. The rituals were performed virtually from Toronto by Pujya Gunsagar Swami, Head Swami of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto in the presence of senior Swamis of BAPS from India & North America. 
 The event was webcast live from the new Mandir site. Over 2,100 families consisting of devotees, community leaders, friends, and well-wishers from across Canada and around the world participated in the ceremony virtually from their homes. The traditional rituals involved laying the foundation stone, blessing the project with Vedic rituals and prayers for peace and well-being throughout the community, province and the country.
 By the grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and with the inspiration and guidance of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, swamis started doing vicharan from the year 2000 in Alberta. The weekly satsang assembliles started in 2005. In 2007, Pramukh Swami Maharaj instructed Calgary's devotees to search for suitable land to build a mandir. The rest, as they say, is history. In 2013, few devotees started regular satsang activities along with children and women's activities. Satsang flourished with the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and theregular visits of swamis and senior swamis.
 Messages of congratulations and well-wishes to the community on this historic occasion were received from many dignitaries including Premier Jason Kenney, Premier of Alberta and Mayor Naheed Nenshi, Mayor of the City of Calgary.
 "BAPS Swaminarayan community are model citizens who give back far more than they take, and we are so blessed as Albertans to have your community growing and thriving in our midst," said Premier Jason Kenney, Premier of Alberta.
 "As you lay this foundation stone, you're not just laying the foundation for a building. You are laying the foundation for another chapter in the lives of the community. And this temple will stand for generations," said Mayor Naheed Nenshi, Mayor of the City of Calgary. 
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj also sent blessings from India for this auspicious occasion saying, "The Shilanyas Vidhi is being completed in Calgary, a place that is extremely cold. All of the devotees are giving their all - physically, mentally and financially for this mandir. They will continue to do this seva and ensure that the Mandir is completed. The Shilanyas ceremony is happening now, but only when the mandir will be completed will everyone be satisfied. Such is the faith, devotion and love of the devotees…and everyone will experience profound happiness." 
 With the inspiration of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Calgary will facilitate activities and events for young and old alike, including children and youth activities, language classes and traditional music classes, to preserve Hindu traditions, heritage and spiritual values. As a place of harmony it will welcome people of all faiths to experience and understand Hindu traditions and spirituality. Humanitarian activities and events will also be organized to support the community.

/News/2021/15th-Patotsav-Celebration-199.text:
Photo Gallery 
 15th Patotsav Celebrations, Havant, UK (8 photos)
 On Friday 28 May 2021, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Havant celebrated 15 years since its opening in 2006.
 As a part of the anniversary celebration, a devout annakut offering was made to the murtis in the main shrine – Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Radha-Krishna, Shri Sita-Rama and Hanumanji, Shri Shiva-Parvati and Ganeshji, and the Guru Parampara.
 Due to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic, darshan was open for private prayer only between 2.00pm and 6.00pm under strict Covid-safe guidelines. 
 At 7.00pm, the sandhya arti was relayed live online, after which Prabuddhmuni Swami delivered an online discourse on the mandir’s history, meaning and spiritual signficance.

/News/2021/2020-Annual-Review-19590.aspx.text:
We began the year 2020 with regular events and activities at BAPS Mandirs throughout Canada. However, by mid-March, the pandemic led to the closure of all mandirs across the country, and all events were moved online.
 Faced with an unprecedented challenge, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha used technology to initiate new ways to give back to society, new ways to pray, strengthen our faith and to continue growing. After all, we believe that the power to build better communities lies in the hands of the very members of those communities.
 This video highlights the main events and initiatives of BAPS Canada in 2020.
 Our innermost thanks to all of the volunteers, supporters and well-wishers of BAPS who braved a very difficult year to make all of our activities undertaken in 2020 successful.

/News/2021/25th-Patotsav-Mahapuja--Groun.t: 25th Patotsav Mahapuja & Groundbreaking, Charlotte, NC, USA
/News/2021/25th-Patotsav-Mahapuja--Groun.text:
On Wednesday September 1, 2021, the BAPS Charlotte Mandir celebrated its 25 Year Anniversary in the presence of Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami. To commemorate this auspicious day, Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, along with Pujya Shantmurti Swami and the Southeast Region Pujya Swamis, performed a Mahapuja at the BAPS Mandir in Atlanta due to safety COVID safety considerations. The event was live-streamed to the devotees in Charlotte, who also participated in the Mahapuja from their homes.
 On this day in 1996, Charlotte was incredibly fortunate to have its Mandir inaugurated by Guruhari Pramukh Swami Maharaj with hundreds of devotees participating in the vedic rituals.  Since its inception, the mandir has had a profound impact on the lives of innumerable devotees providing a place to nurture spirituality, offer devotion, and experience peace. It has been instrumental in serving the community through charitable event ushering pure devotion, selfless service and community solidarity. The mandir has been instrumental in conducting youth activities to instill values, culture, and traditions in the next generation through spiritual guidance, music & language classes, sporting event, and more.  The mandir has also provided a center to plan and conduct charitable events such as walkathons, health fairs, health lectures and more benefitting the local community. In concluding the celebrations, Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami also performed the Khãt-vidhi of the new BAPS Charlotte Mandir. He also offered his deepest prayers for its earliest completion.

Photo Gallery 
 Murti Darshan, London, UK (16 photos)
 Patotsav Mahapuja, London, UK (16 photos)
 Patotsav Ceremony, London, UK (20 photos)
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – the first traditional Hindu mandir outside of India – on Sunday 20 August 1995. Over the past 26 years, the internationally renowned Mandir has served the local community and inspired millions of worshippers and visitors from across the world to experience a profound sense of peace, fulfilment and spiritual harmony.
 The 26th anniversary of the Mandir was celebrated with a host of devotional festivities. These began with darshan and the abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni for worshippers from 20 to 22 August, providing an opportunity for private worship in line with the current health protocols for the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic.
 On Saturday 21 August, families joined in an online mahapuja conducted by swamis from the Mandir in London. Families across the UK and Europe participated fully in this ceremony from their respective homes with materials and all necessary items previously provided by the Mandir. During the ceremony, the swamis offered collective prayers for family harmony and world peace, and particularly for those who continue to be impacted by the ongoing pandemic.
 The ‘patotsav’ – marking the anniversary of the Mandir’s opening – began on the morning of Sunday 22 August with a Vedic ceremony, which was streamed via a live webcast. This included prayers to seek the blessings of God for continued peace, righteousness and prosperity in the world.
 Sunday was also the auspicious day of Raksha Bandhan – a joyous Hindu festival when sisters traditionally tie a ‘rakhi’ (sacred thread) around their brothers’ wrists, affirming their sibling bond and praying for their protection. For devotees, the rakhi symbolises the spiritual bond between the Guru and disciple. A special ceremony was held to commemorate this blessed occasion, which included spiritual discourses and bhajans from swamis as well as video blessings from Pramukh Swami Maharaj that further explained the spiritual significance of the festival.
 A variety of sweet and savoury dishes were artistically arranged before the deities in the main shrines to thank God for his providence and protection. Yogvivekdas Swami paid tribute to the vision of Yogiji Maharaj and tireless endeavours of Pramukh Swami Maharaj that culminated in the inauguration of the Mandir in 1995. He also reflected on the inspiration that the Mandir has provided to millions who have walked through its doors and encouraged everyone to strengthen their spiritual bond and relationship with God.
 The festivities concluded  with the ceremonial patotsav arti. Mahant Swami Maharaj also performed the arti of the murtis of London Mandir during the sandhya arti in Sarangpur, India.
 Avani Patel, from Watford, shared, “Visiting the Mandir for darshan and abhishek was a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the Mandir’s 26th anniversary and also Raksha Bandhan. My two young daughters were overjoyed to participate in the ceremony at the Mandir and also at home, and I am so grateful to the Mandir for continuing to keep us all connected throughout Covid.”

 The resident sadhus of the Asia Pacific region conducted the Vedic mahapuja and murti consecration rituals of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. Thereafter, a grand annakut of sweet and savory vegetarian delicacies was offered to Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj.
 The auspicious ceremony was webcast live and more than 180 families throughout Perth participated in the mahapuja and abhishek rituals virtually from their homes.
 In the afternoon, devotees came in-person to perform abhishek of and offer prayers to Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj.

/News/2021/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.t: Akhand Dhun: Annual Prayers for Success, Peace & Harmony, UK & Europe
/News/2021/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Darshan & Programme, Wellingborough, UK (20 photos)
 Akhand Dhun in London, UK (20 photos)
 Akhand Dhun at Home, UK & Europe (20 photos)
 A special programme of prayers was conducted on Sunday 4 April 2021 by swamis at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, joined simultaneously online by thousands of devotees from their respective homes around the UK and in Europe.
 The ‘Akhand Dhun’ is held annually at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Wellingborough, and usually welcomes thousands of worshippers and visitors to participate in a special day of prayers for peace and prosperity to prevail in communities across the world. Throughout the day, visitors to the Mandir usually offer their respects at the ‘Akshar Deri’ – a beautiful shrine housed within the mandir.
 Due to the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic, families across the UK and Europe joined in the prayers via a live webcast from their homes and participated in a variety of ways – by chanting the Swaminarayan mahamantra, playing instruments to accompany the devotional singing, writing the Swaminarayan mahamantra, and performing pradakshinas around images of the Akshar Deri in their homes. Many children contributed by creating a 3D model of the Akshar Deri from card, paper or other creative materials.
 The programme commenced with children reciting traditional benedictory verses as well as selected verses from the Satsang Diksha scripture. Swamis performed the abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj following the hour-long dhun. Thousands of devotees joined in this sacred ceremony from their homes.
 In his blessings, Sadguru Pujya Swayamprakashdas (Doctor) Swami emphasised the statement made by Mahant Swami Maharaj that the Akshar Deri in Wellingborough is as noteworthy as the original Akshar Deri in Gondal, and there is no difference between the two shrines. He encouraged everyone to offer their sincerest prayers on this occasion with this understanding and underlined the importance of participating in daily spiritual activities together as a family at home.
 This year’s prayers were especially significant as the world continues to fight through the adversity and challenges of the coronavirus pandemic. Swamis prayed to God to offer comfort, solace and strength to all those still affected, and for the vaccination programmes to help alleviate this disease across the world.
 Janki Patel, aged 16, shared her thoughts on the special prayer programme: “To offer our devotion with all members of the family on this auspicious occasion was a very rewarding experience. We pray that everyone in the world suffering from the virus can return to good health as soon as possible.”

/News/2021/Akshar-Purushottam-Vadh%C4%81.t: Akshar-Purushottam Vadhāmanā: Shatābdi Family Mahāpujā, UK & Europe
/News/2021/Akshar-Purushottam-Vadh%C4%81.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shatabdi Family Mahapuja with Mahant Swami Maharaj, Nenpur, India (10 photos)
 Shatabdi Family Mahapuja, London, UK (40 photos)
 Shatabdi Family Mahapuja at Home (100 photos)
 Families across the UK and Europe heralded the New Year by taking part in a family mahapuja from their respective homes on Friday 1 January 2021.
 This unique global experience was enjoyed by more than 5,000 households who prayed for world peace, family harmony, and a safe and successful year ahead, particularly for those affected by the ongoing global Covid-19 pandemic.
 2021 also marks the centennial birth year of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The mahapuja therefore enabled children, adults and seniors alike to pay tribute to the inspirational life of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and also welcome the new murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, which were consecrated by Mahant Swami Maharaj on 31 October, into their homes.
 The mahapuja was conducted from the shrines of London Mandir by the resident swamis. Mahant Swami Maharaj presided over the opening of the mahapuja through a live video link from Nenpur in India. He was welcomed by a balak who, effectively, invited Swamishri into each and every home to conduct a padhramani (‘home visit’).
 The explanations of the various components and rituals were narrated in English and Gujarati, and were accompanied with on-screen guidance throughout the ceremony, helping families to understand the meaning of the Sanskrit verses and perform the mahapuja correctly.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj’s personal blessings on this auspicious occasion were shared following the conclusion of the mahapuja in which he elaborated on the spiritual significance of the new Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj murti and encouraged everyone to imbibe and share with others the exemplary virtues of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 Nimisha Patel, from Leicester, shared her thoughts after the event: “What a wonderfully uplifting way to begin the new year! Online events such as these connect communities across the world and give us tremendous strength and hope. Our children were able to fully understand the deep meaning of each step of the mahapuja and contribute together as a family. The presence and guidance of Mahant Swami Maharaj made this a truly memorable event.”

/News/2021/Atlanta-Nilkanth-Varni-Abhish.t: Shri Nilkanth Varni Abhishek Mandap Opening, Atlanta, GA, USA
/News/2021/Atlanta-Nilkanth-Varni-Abhish.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Sthapan Vidhi (85 photos)
 During His 2017 North American Vicharan, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj inaugurated the Nilkanth Varni Abhishek Mandap. On September 1, 2021, the new Nilkanth Varni Abhishek Mandap was opened with enthusiasm through Vedic rituals performed by Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Atlanta, GA. Devotees from North America and beyond joined in-person and virtually to celebrate this monumental occasion.
 In his blessings after the inauguration, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami highlighted the importance of reminiscing on the form of Nilkanth Varni, describing the value of tolerance, self-discipline, and service that can be seen throughout His pilgrimage. He emphasized that those who have the divine opportunity to conduct abhishek in this mandap, will experience the blessings and fruits of their prayers. Abhishek is the ancient Hindu practice of pouring water over the divine form of God to obtain His blessings while offering prayers. Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj has also stated during His visit in 2017, “If one prays with complete faith, by the grace of Shri Nilkanth Varni, you will experience the bliss of Akshardham right here.”
 The development of the new mandap was a significant undertaking to install over 7,000 pieces of stone and composite. The mandap itself emulates a jigsaw puzzle aggregate made of 45 domes, 34 full pillars - 20 of which are marble covered with hand-painted composite designs, and further utilizes 3 unique types of marble with 13 design variations. Under the central abhishek platform lies a 19-foot inlaid medallion made of marble surrounded by four 5-foot medallions.
 At the mere age of 11, Bhagwan Swaminarayan renounced all worldly attachments and embarked on a journey throughout India including what is now Nepal, Tibet, and Bangladesh. During this time, He came to be known as Nilkanth Varni, named after His work in liberating many spiritual aspirants. In order to memorialize Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s travels, Shri Nilkanth Varni’s murti has been ceremoniously placed for daily worship.
 The Nilkanth Varni Abhishek Mandap is the first of its kind to pay homage to the unique events of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s life and work through the intricate construction of the mandap. On the primary ceiling dome, a beautiful, hallmark depiction of Ghanshyam Maharaj regally seated on a pipal tree looking West can be observed. This dome is surrounded by ornate designs and several vibrant paintings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s childhood events as Ghanshyam. The pillars that support the mandap itself house the divine journey of Nilkanth Varni’s 7-year pilgrimage throughout India. The walls further unfold the liberating endeavours of Swaminarayan Bhagwan through His spiritual and humanitarian efforts.
 It will now remain a place of resounding devotion and reverence, as devotees and well-wishers join to express their inner sentiments through the abhishek ritual and immerse themselves in the divine events of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s unparalleled life.

/News/2021/Atmabuddhi-%E2%80%93-Jivanni-.t: ‘Atmabuddhi – Jivanni Siddhi’: Bal-Balika Shibir, Asia Pacific
/News/2021/Atmabuddhi-%E2%80%93-Jivanni-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Shibir (40 photos)
 More than 1,200 balaks and balikas from throughout Australia (Adelaide, Albury, Brisbane, Canberra, Darwin, Gold Coast, Griffith, Hobart, Melbourne, Newcastle, Perth, Shepparton and Sydney), New Zealand (Rotorua, Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch and Hamilton), Thailand (Bangkok),  Indonesia (Jakarta), Hong Kong, Singapore and Japan participated in the online Bal-Balika Shibir based on the theme ‘Atmabuddhi – Jivanni Siddhi’. The shibir elaborated upon the proper way to perform the essential daily devotional rituals of puja, arti and thal by learning Mahant Swami Maharaj’s way of doing them.
 The three shibir sessions were presented in the form of a day in the life of a child named Akshar. The children learnt about and experienced the importance of these daily devotional rituals through dramas, animated skits, presentations by swamis, activities, Zoom breakout discussions led by local karyakars, and special guidance by senior swamis and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Relevant verses from the Satsang Diksha were used as a guide for how to perform these rituals. The participants learnt about the proper ways of doing mala and mansi, the glory of the arti and the correct way of offering food to God. They were also guided on how to perform these rituals with devotion.
 The children pledged to strive to improve their regularity and quality of daily devotion by learning from Mahant Swami Maharaj’s bhakti.

/News/2021/BAPS-COVID-19-Relief-Aid-by-S.t: BAPS COVID-19 Relief Aid by Swaminarayan Akshardham, India
/News/2021/BAPS-COVID-19-Relief-Aid-by-S.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Delhi (32 photos)
 Chandigarh (2 photos)

 Uttarakhand (1 photos)
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha mobilized critical and essential COVID-19 relief aid throughout North India through its regional headquarters at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi and extensive regional network of mandirs and centres.
 An unrelenting surge in infections and deaths from the coronavirus pandemic has plagued India, with its hospitals coming under extreme pressure from shortages of oxygen and critical care beds all over North India. With large numbers of critical cases in a much shorter period of time, an overwhelmed national health service has caused shortage of medicines, hospital beds, essential oxygen supplies, oxygen cylinders, doctors and medical staff and medical equipment that has also led to a dire rise in number of deaths.
 Under the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi has been helping and supporting patients and families affected by COVID-19 in New Delhi, NCR, Chandigarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh in a number of ways.
 Sourcing & Delivering Oxygen Concentrators
 Combating the major problem facing many hospitals, COVID-19 Centres and patients with short supply of oxygen, oxygen concentrators, oxygen cylinders and essential medical support. Swaminarayan Akshardham, with the support of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi and well-wishers from Taiwan, were able to provide much-needed help. Over 220 oxygen concentrators have been distributed free by Swaminarayan Akshardham to hospitals, nursing homes, COVID-19 centres, old age homes, charitable trusts, institutions, organizations and societies.
