Spectacles Worn by Yogiji Maharaj, 1970

These are the spectacles worn by Yogiji Maharaj during his visit to the UK

Sacred Image of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, 1970

This is the sacred image (murti) of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj that Yogiji Maharaj personally worshipped for the duration of his stay at the home of Arvindbhai (‘Guru’) in Dollis Hill, London

Garments and Rosary, 14 June 1970

The gatariyu and dhotiyu displayed here were worn by Yogiji Maharaj on the day of the consecration ceremony at the Islington Mandir in 1970. The rosary displayed here was turned by Yogiji Maharaj on this historic day

Islington Invitation, 14 June 1970

This is the original invitation card for the inauguration ceremony at Islington Mandir, in the presence of Yogiji Maharaj

Sanctified Slippers, 1980

These are the slippers worn by Pramukh Swami Maharaj on his visit to the Meadow Garth warehouse, which was repurposed to house the hari mandir that opened in 1982

Written Prophecy, 6 September 1987

This is the letter written by Pramukh Swami Maharaj in Gangotri, India, where he expresses his wish for a magnificent, traditional shikharbaddha mandir to be built in London

The Search Continues, June 1988

These are the documents that were created whilst the Mandir Committee continued its search for a suitable site to construct Europe’s first traditional Hindu mandir

Preliminary Specification, August 1990

This is the planning proposal for a hari mandir to be built on the site of Neasden High School

The Site is Secured, 1 September 1990

This is the original letter detailing the purchase of the land where Arlington Motor Garage stood. It was here that the London Mandir was to be constructed, and the prophecies of Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj would come to fruition

Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Teeth Moulds, 1996

These are the moulds of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s teeth taken in London by Dr Brian Smith. Pramukh Swami Maharaj was experiencing severe toothache due to an exposed nerve

The First Gift, 19 October 1990

These kalashes were filled with prasad (sanctificed sweets) and sent to London by swamis from Ahmedabad, India, on the auspicious occasion of the Hindu New Year. Kalashes are customarily placed atop the shikhars [spires] of a mandir, as a sign of completion. Here, in the case of London Mandir, the kalashes arrived even before the foundations of the new mandir had been dug

Initial Plans, 20 January 1990

These are the initial plans for a traditional shikharbaddha mandir to be constructed on the Arlington site

Shikhars from Wooden Model, April 1992

These are the shikhars from the first wooden model created of London Mandir

India Itinerary, 4 November 1991

This is the itinerary for the London Mandir project team’s initial research trip to India, where they were advised by Pramukh Swami Maharaj to observe the architecture of the enclosed top floor of the mandir in Bochasan, the Haveli complex belonging to Mahendrabhai Amin in Vaso, and the open central dome of the mandir in Gadhada

Signature of Approval, February 1992

These are the architectural plans for the cultural complex that was to be constructed adjacent to the stone mandir. Out of the four potential building designs presented by the architects, Pramukh Swami Maharaj approved the Haveli style by signing this drawing. He remarked: “This style, found in Gujarat, is part of our Swaminarayan tradition.”

Sanctified Signature, 20 April 1994

This is an architectural drawing of the London Mandir moat and gardens, signed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj

Until the Very End, 1 February 1994

This is the letter written by Pramukh Swami Maharaj to Rajeshwar Swami in Atladara, India. Pramukh Swami Maharaj personally detailed the arrangements that were to be made for CM Patel’s funeral there

Written in Stone, 30 April 1994

This is a stone signed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj on a visit to the construction site of London Mandir

Architectural Drawings, 1 May 1994

These are full-scale drawings of the intricate wooden and marble carvings seen all around London Mandir

Written with Confidence, 20 August 1994

Pramukh Swami Maharaj personally wrote this letter confirming that the inauguration ceremony of London Mandir will take place on 20 August 1995

A Phone Call Away

These are telephones utilised by Pramukh Swami Maharaj to call various devotees and swamis during his stay in London

A Phone Call Away

This is a telephone utilised by Pramukh Swami Maharaj to call various devotees and swamis during his stay in London

Care Patrikas, 1994-1995

This is a set of five brochures that were delivered to almost 90,000 homes to promote ideals of wholesome life and one of the fundraising projects for London Mandir

Seated in Front of God

This is the chair upon which Pramukh Swami Maharaj was seated in the workshop in Gandhinagar whilst instructing Bhaktinandan Swami for the carving of the sacred images that were to be consecrated in London Mandir

Picture Perfect, 1970-1995

This is one of the many cameras used to capture footage of Pramukh Swami Maharaj while he performed his various activities during the making of London Mandir, from site visits to the final construction

Finishing Touches, 1994-1995

These are the polishing papers used over 27 years ago to polish the marble of London Mandir

A Labour of Love, 23 August 1995

This is a heart-shaped piece of marble offered to Pramukh Swami Maharaj by volunteers after the inauguration of London Mandir in 1995 and just before he departed

Invitation Card, August 1995

This is the original invitation card sent to devotees in the UK for the grand Mandir Mahotsav celebrations

Logbook, 1993-1995

This is the original logbook used to record details of volunteers who had come to perform seva on the construction site for London Mandir

Mandir Mahotsav Menu, 18 August to 24 August 1995

This is the menu served to devotees attending the Mandir Mahotsav celebrations

Celebration Banners, 18 August to 24 August 1995

These are the original banners draped around the walls of London Mandir during the Mandir Mahotsav celebrations

Sacred Image of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, 18 August 1995

This is the original sacred image of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj used in the Vastu ceremony of London Mandir. This was a traditional Hindu ceremony that blesses the new building and all those who worked on it

Nagar Yatra in Piccadilly Circus, 18 August 1995

This is the sofa chair upon which Pramukh Swami Maharaj was seated as he blessed the Nagar Yatra in Piccadilly Circus.

Nagar Yatra Leaflet, 18 August 1995

This is the leaflet that was distributed along the route with information about the Nagar Yatra in Piccadilly Circus

Sacred Image of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, 1985 to 13 August 2016

This is the sacred image of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj that Pramukh Swami Maharaj placed beside him whilst blessing the Nagar Yatra in Picadilly Circus. Since 1985, Pramukh Swami Maharaj travelled with this particular sacred image, keeping it with him everywhere

Mandir Mahotsav Upvastra, 19 August 1995

This upvastra (upper garment) was given to all participants in the Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna that was performed on 19 August 1995, as part of the Mandir Mahotsav celebrations for the inauguration of London Mandir

Drill, 19 August 1995

This drill was used at the very top of London Mandir for the kalash installation the day before the opening

Harshadbhai Rana’s Chhadi, 20 August 1995

This is the golden chhadi (ceremonial baton) used by Pramukh Swami Maharaj to perform the netravaran vidhi (eye-opening ceremony) during the consecration of the sacred images in London Mandir. This chhadi was initially kept aside and a different chhadi had been used for the original ceremony. However, in order to fulfil the wishes of his devotee, Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed the ceremony again with this chhadi

Consecration Ceremony Adornments, 20 August 1995

These are very first vaghas with which the sacred images of London Mandir were adorned on the day of the consecration ceremony

Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Handwritten Blessings, 20 August 1995

These are the blessings written by Pramukh Swami Maharaj for Pujya Satyavrat Swami on a gatariyu (cloth garment) on the evening of the inauguration ceremony of London Mandir

Mandir Mahotsav Memento, 24 August 1995

This memento was personally gifted by Pramukh Swami Maharaj to every volunteer and contractor who had selflessly served in the construction of London Mandir

Heartfelt Gratitude, 25 August 1995

This letter was written by Pramukh Swami Maharaj himself to the London Mandir project team after the completion of the Mandir, thanking them for their selfless service

Seating the Divine, 2000

This was the blue chair upon which Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat during his visit to Nottingham for the family shibir

Seating the Divine, 2000

This was the chair upon which Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat during his visit to the UK in 2000, including the iconic Guru-Bhakti Din celebrations

Record-Breaking Humility, 8 July 2000

These are the original certificates from Guinness World Records that were awarded to London Mandir and Pramukh Swami Maharaj

The People’s Guru, 2000-2017

This is the table that was used by Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj in London when conducting mulakats (personal meetings) with devotees

Eyes of the Beholder, 2006

These are the contact lenses worn by Pramukh Swami Maharaj during his visit to London in 2006

Seating the Divine, 2004 to 2017

This was the chair upon which Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat in 2004 and Mahant Swami Maharaj sat in 2017 while on the main stage of the assembly hall

Blessing the Celebrations, 2015

These are some of the items – ceremonial candle, garland, flag, baton, invitation card, pillowcases – used by Pramukh Swami Maharaj in Sarangpur to bless the 20th anniversary celebrations of London Mandir

Forever By His Side, 2000 to 13 August 2016

This is the original clock, with the sacred images of London Mandir, that was kept in Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s room, by his side, until his final day. In between meetings and activities, Pramukh Swami Maharaj would invariably do darshan of the sacred images of London Mandir

Seating the Divine, 2007 to 2017

This was the chair upon which Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat in 2007 and Mahant Swami Maharaj sat in 2017 in their room

Our Home, 23 August 2020

This is the handwritten message of Mahant Swami Maharaj blessing the finale programme of the 25th anniversary celebrations of London Mandir

Eternal Bond, 23 August 2020

This is the original origami swan made by Mahant Swami Maharaj in Nenpur, India, for the finale programme of the 25th anniversary celebrations of London Mandir

Pramukh Swami Road, 20 November 2020

The eastern section of Meadow Garth in north-west London, the home of London Mandir, has been renamed ‘Pramukh Swami Road’ in honour of the Mandir's creator. A replica of the road sign was sanctified by Mahant Swami Maharaj in Nenpur, India
The exhibition brought the historic journey to the present through ‘The First of its Kind’

Signature of Approval, 3 November 2021

This is the original poster through which Mahant Swami Maharaj inaugurated ‘The First of its Kind’ documentary series with his signature

Sanctified Episode Guide, 11 December 2021

This is the original Episode Guide that was unveiled by Mahant Swami Maharaj after his puja on the day of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s 100th birth anniversary celebrations in Chansad

A Humble Tribute

The entire ‘Museum of Memories’ was in honour of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s divine connection with London Mandir

/News/2022/10th-Anniversary-Celebration-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Dashabdi Celebration, Melbourne (18 photos)
 The Dashabdi (10th Anniversary) Mahotsav of the BAPS Mandir, Melbourne, in the presence of BAPS swamis, featured a Vedic mahapuja in which devotees offered prayers for peace and well-being to prevail everywhere. This was followed by an assembly in which included a traditional dance by children and a multimedia presentation recounting the history and activities of the mandir. Community leaders, devotees and well-wishers attended the celebration.
 Invited guests included the local member of parliament and Shadow Minister for Multicultural Affairs, Mr. Craig Ondarchie. He commended the spiritual and social activities conducted by BAPS in Melbourne over the past decade and the positive impact of the BAPS children and youth activities in the local community.

/News/2022/15th-Anniversary-Celebration-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Parsippany, 15th Anniversary (27 photos)
 With the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, devotees and well-wishers came together to celebrate the 15th anniversary of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Parsippany, NJ on July 31, 2022. Amidst the showering of flower petals and rice grains and the chanting of Vedic hymns and prayers, the celebration commenced with a traditional Mahapuja ceremony in the presence of revered swamis. 
 The cultural program featured life-changing experiences of youths who shared how the mandir helped shape their identity and maintain their cultural values. Kirtans, skits, speeches, and video presentations portrayed how the mandir helped the devotees lead a value-based life anchored in faith and community service. The central message of the celebration was to strengthen unity among families, highlight the importance of spiritual deepening and development, and empower parents and elders to instill values and morals in the lives of children through quality time and education. His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj continues to inspire the preservation of Hindu culture through events like this and the mandirs.

While 2021 featured a myriad of challenges for the world, it was also a year marked by tremendous progress - vaccines were sent to all corners of the world, thousands of athletes gathered in Tokyo to take part in the Olympics and world leaders took part in the United Nations Climate Change Conference to solve the next wave of climate challenges that face our planet.
 Similarly, communities across BAPS Canada found new ways to come together, celebrate milestones, grow spiritually and serve the community throughout the year. The Annual Review 2021 video highlights the main events and initiatives of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Canada in 2021.
 We take this opportunity to offer a heartfelt 'thank you' to all the volunteers, supporters and well-wishers who helped make 2021 such a productive and inspiring year for so many.

/News/2022/27th-Patotsav-Celebrations-21.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Patotsav Ceremony, London, UK (20 photos)
 Murti Darshan, London, UK (12 photos)
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj (1921-2016) was one of the world’s great spiritual leaders and an inspiration to millions worldwide, guiding them to lead a spiritual and noble life. One of his greatest gifts to the UK is BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – which he inaugurated on 20 August 1995. 27 years on, it continues to serve the local community and inspire millions of worshippers and visitors from across the world to experience a profound sense of peace, fulfilment, and spiritual harmony.
 The 27th anniversary of the Mandir was celebrated with various devotional activities on Sunday 21 August 2022, which began with darshan and the abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni. Vedic ceremonies for the ‘patotsav’ – marking the anniversary of the Mandir – followed thereafter.
 The programme also included devotional bhajans from swamis. A variety of sweet and savoury dishes were artistically arranged before the deities in the main shrines to thank God for his providence and protection.
 Throughout 2022, hundreds of thousands around the world are honouring and celebrating the birth centenary of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Yogvivekdas Swami paid tribute to the life of Pramukh Swami Maharaj by drawing upon the societal benefits that have been fostered from the more than 1,100 mandirs that he consecrated.
 Shruti Patel, visiting from north London, shared, “After two years of online patotsav celebrations, it was wonderful to experience the atmosphere and join worshippers for the Mandir’s anniversary. This year’s celebrations are particularly special as we celebrate Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s shatabdi (birth centenary) – and honouring his life at the Mandir he built for the community and beyond was memorable.”
 The celebrations concluded with arti in front of the maha-murti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the courtyard of the Mandir.

/News/2022/5th-Patotsav-and-Nilkanth-Var.t: 5th Patotsav and Nilkanth Varni Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav, Chigwell, UK
/News/2022/5th-Patotsav-and-Nilkanth-Var.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Nagar Yatra (40 photos)
 Nilkanth Varni Murti Pratishtha (40 photos)
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj inaugurated BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Chigwell on Sunday 8 October 2017. The 5th anniversary of the Mandir was marked with a host of devotional festivities on the weekend of 15-16 October 2022.
 The festivities began on the afternoon of 15 October with a grand procession through the streets of Chigwell. The ‘Nagar Yatra’, as the devotional parade is traditionally called, brought together hundreds of men, women and children for a colourful, joyous occasion along Chigwell High Road. The procession featured traditional Indian folk dancing, devotional music, and decorative chariots.
 This was followed by a special cultural programme of dance, devotional singing, and discourses. The keynote addresses from swamis explained the importance of mandirs and the benefits they provide to society.
 The Vedic rituals to consecrate the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj were conducted by Aksharviharidas Swami, Yogvivekdas Swami and other swamis from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. Previously, the murti-pratishtha ceremony of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj had been performed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in Sarangpur on 19 August 2021.
 This ceremony was performed alongside the ‘patotsav’ rituals – a special Vedic ceremony performed by swamis marking the anniversary of the Mandir’s opening when its murtis were first infused with the divine presence of God. Over a thousand devotees also prayed for God to bless the local community and the world with peace, prosperity and harmony by participating in the mahapuja.
 A variety of sweet and savoury dishes were offered to the deities in the main shrines to thank God for his providence. Devotees and well-wishers observed this ‘annakut’ throughout the day and had the opportunity to perform abhishek of Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. The observances culminated with a special assembly concluding the two-day festival.
 Palak Joshi, a volunteer at the Mandir, shared, “The two-day celebrations brought back wonderful memories from the inauguration ceremony by Mahant Swami Maharaj in 2017. My family were overjoyed to participate in the nagar yatra through the heart of Chigwell and the murti pratishtha celebrations. I am so grateful to the Mandir for keeping us all connected to our faith and traditions, and it was wonderful to share that with that the local community.”

/News/2022/A-Scholarly-Deliberation-with.t: A Scholarly Deliberation with Govardhan Pithadhishwar Jagadguru Shankaracharyaji, Jagannath Puri, India
/News/2022/A-Scholarly-Deliberation-with.text: A profound academic and philosophical deliberation took place between the Govardhan Pithadhishwar Shankaracharya of Jagannathpuri Nishchalanand Saraswati and Prasthantrayi Bhashyakar Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami. First, Bhadreshdas Swami offered the Prasthantrayi commentaries to Shankaracharyaji. He then concisely elucidated the doctrinal principles of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan based on Vedic authority. On hearing Bhadreshdas Swami’s scholarly explication, Shankaracharyaji expressed his contentment and gratitude for the sampradaya’s fruitful endeavors to protect, preserve and foster the eternal traditions of Sanatan Dharma. He also conveyed his noble wishes for the centenary birth celebrations of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

 Sarod Vadan at Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni (17 photos)
 World-renowned sarod player Shri Abhisek Lahiri and renowned tabla player Shri Subrata Bhattacharya visited BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Robbinsville, New Jersey, to offer their devotion on September 20, 2022. Upon their arrival, they took a tour of the Mandir complex, during which they admired the intricate architecture and beauty. After that, they offered their bhakti through a performance before the Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni.
 On the morning of September 21, 2022, Abhisekji and Sabrataji again lent their artistic talent in an offering of devotion before Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj in the mandir after Shangar Arti. Attendees had the opportunity to experience the peaceful sounds of the sarod and upbeats of the tabla.

/News/2022/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.t: Akhand Dhun: Annual Prayers for Success, Peace and Harmony, Wellingborough, UK
/News/2022/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Wellingborough, UK (40 photos)
 A special day of continuous prayers was held at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Wellingborough, on Sunday 17 April 2022. Thousands of worshippers and visitors from around the UK convened to pray for success, peace and harmony to prevail in communities across the world.
 The prayers began at 7.00am, with visitors joining throughout the day to offer their devotion at the ‘Akshar Deri’, a beautiful shrine housed within the mandir.
 Rakhee Chauhan travelled from Birmingham with her husband for the occasion. Sharing her impressions on the day, she remarked, “It was wonderful to attend this event in-person after three years. Seeing the welcome from the local community was truly inspiring. The experience of inner peace I have felt is something that I will cherish.”
 This year’s prayers were particularly poignant as the world emerges from the ongoing uncertainty and challenges caused by the coronavirus pandemic and the current humanitarian crisis unfolding in Ukraine. Mahant Swami Maharaj sent a special video message in which he shared that he is also praying for the safety, righteous prosperity and harmony of communities around the world.
 In honour of Pramukh Swami Maharaj on the occasion of his centennial birth anniversary, over seventy cyclists rode more than 100 kilometres to Wellingborough after departing from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, earlier that morning.
 The prayers continued uninterrupted through to 7.00pm, when the day’s chanting and months of preparations were brought to a conclusion.
 Rajesh Ladwa, lead volunteer at the mandir, shared, “People from across the country have united here today to offer their prayers for the well-being of the community and the world at large. We continue to pray for those who have suffered losses and hope that goodwill prevails locally, nationally and globally.”

/News/2022/Akshar-Purushottam-Adhyayan-C.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Akshar-Purushottam Adhyayan Conference 2022 (37 photos)
 The first Australia and New Zealand Akshar-Purushottam Adhyayan Conference was held in Glenaladale, Australia in the presence of Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami and resident swamis from Australia. A total of 48 yuvaks and 31 yuvatis gathered for this historic conference, organized by the recently opened BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute. For the last one-and-a-half years the delegates had participated in two separate online courses: 1) Akshar-Purushottam Adhyayan and 2) Siddhant Sadhana.  
 The Akshar-Purushottam Adhyayan course focused on learning about the history of BAPS, Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, attachment to the Satpurush, learning how to sing Sanskrit verses from the Swaminarayan Siddhant Karika and discussions about the dedication of volunteers.
 The Siddhant Sadhana course focused on understanding the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy in depth and its practical daily life applications.
 The four-day conference began with the delegates taking their final exam for their respective courses. During the conference, swamis guided and inspired the delegates to continue to learn and imbibe the teachings from their courses. Swamis also gave creative in-depth presentations on performing the different ahniks – daily devotional routines.  Also, the delegates actively engaged in group discussions on how to apply these teachings in their daily lives. At the end of the four-day conference, a convocation ceremony was held for all the delegates who had passed their final exam.
 On the last day, 15 August 2022, the delegates participated in the flag hoisting ceremony to commemorate India’s Azadi ki Amrit Mahotsav – India’s 75th Independence Day.

/News/2022/Akshar-Purushottam-Darshan-Mu.t: Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Mukhpath Mahotsav, Nenpur, India
/News/2022/Akshar-Purushottam-Darshan-Mu.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mukhpath Mahotsav (41 photos)
 As part of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Centenary Celebrations, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Sarangpur, organized an Akshar-Purushottam Siddhant Karika Mukhpath Mahotsav. Around 100 students studying in various courses at BAPS Swaminarayan Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, as well as those affiliated to the Mahavidyalaya through online courses or external studies through Shree Somnath Sanskrit University, enthusiastically participated.
 The Swaminarayan Siddhanta Karika is an extract from the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, which reveals the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The students worked hard to memorize its 565 Sanskrit verses (karikas). The Mahotsav began on the afternoon of 4 August in Nenpur, where they were assessed through written and oral examinations.
 That evening the students presented a novel Sanskrit play called ‘Pavani’, similar to the famous Sanskrit play ‘Pala’ of East India.
 On the morning of 5 August the students participated in samuh puja and chorus singing of the Karika and Satsang Diksha. Thereafter, the students received experienced guidance from Shrutiprakash Swami, Bhadresh Swami and Atmatrupt Swami.
 Overall, 11 male students successfully memorized all 565 karikas and received the title of 'Karikajayi' and 12 female students received the corresponding title of 'Karikajayini’.
 In the afternoon, a special assembly was also held at BAPS Mandir, Ahmedabad, in the presence of Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, Pujya Vivekasagar Swami and Atmaswarup Swami, in which students presented their mukhpath and received their awards.
 A separate assembly was also held for the female students to present their efforts in memorizing the karikas and receive their awards.
 The highlight of the Mukhpath Mahotsav was the assembly in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Swamishri was delighted to hear the recitations and the stories of the sincere efforts of all to prepare. Swamishri also tested the students and certified their success by saying, "All of you immersed yourself [in this mukhpath] for Rajipo... Rajipo has worked. Those who understood Rajipo were successful.
 On the morning of 6 August, students recited selected Sanskrit karikas and their Gujarati translations during Swamishri's puja.

/News/2022/Annual-Karyakar-Shibirs-Avsar.text:
A total of 976 male and 535 female karyakars from 17 African countries, including Malawi, Zambia, Congo, South Africa, Botswana, Kenya, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi, participated in the Annual Karyakar Shibirs that took place between March and May 2022 in the inspiring presence of Pujya Viveksagar Swami.
 Based on the theme ‘Avsar’(Occasion or Opportunity), the shibirs were held in Lilongwe, Malawi (11–13 March) Lusaka, Zambia (18–20 March), Lenasia, South Africa (25–27 March), Nairobi, Kenya (15–17 April), Mwanza, Tanzania (22–24 April), and Kampala, Uganda (6–8 May).
 Each two-and-a-half day shibir inspired the karyakars to celebrate the forthcoming Pramukh Swami Maharaj Centenary Celebrations with unprecedented grandeur and comprised three sessions that highlighted the Centenary Celebrations as an:
 i) ‘avsar’ (opportunity) for remembering our guru’s benevolence
 ii) ‘avsar’ (opportunity) to repay our guru’s benevolence
 iii)  ‘avsar’ (opportunity) to spread the glory of our guru throughout the world.
 During the first session, Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s innumerable altruistic contributions were recollected and presented through various mediums.
 In the second session the uniqueness of the Pramukh Swami Maharaj Shatabdi Mahotsav was explained, and that doing seva will give one a feeling of fulfilment and satisfaction of serving our gurus.
 In the third session, the benefits of our association with Satsang and the Satpurush were presented in a workshop that featured videos and discussions.
 Also, the shibirs featured theme-related activities that encouraged everyone to join in this Shatabdi seva and serve to their very best capacity.
 The shibirs were organized by the Satsang Pravrutti Madhyasth Karyalaya in Africa, and in each shibir Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj bestowed his divine blessings on the karyakars.

/News/2022/Annual-Review-2021-20878.aspx.text:
Despite another challenging year due to the Covid-19 pandemic, 2021 proved to be filled with inspiring events, heartfelt devotion and new milestones for BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK and in Europe, headquartered from Neasden Temple in London.
 We remain committed to serving our fellowship and the wider community with meaningful events and activities to make a real, lasting and positive impact in their lives.
 Please click here to view a brief interactive report of the key events and activities of 2021. (Be sure to click the underlined text to learn more about each segment.)
 2021 is also visually summarised in a short video. Click above to watch the highlights.
 All of this would not have been possible without the tireless, selfless efforts of our volunteers as well as the continuing support and goodwill of all our supporters and well-wishers. 
 We look forward to improving and growing in our service of the community, and being inspired by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and HH Mahant Swami Maharaj to do more and be better.
 Together, we can make a difference!

/News/2022/Anti-Addiction-and-Nature-Pro.t: Anti-Addiction and Nature Protection Drives, Kolkata, India
/News/2022/Anti-Addiction-and-Nature-Pro.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Anti-Addiction and Nature Protection Drives (6 photos)
 Under the auspices of the Pramukh Swami Maharaj Shatabdi Mahotsav, Bengali speaking balaks and balikas undertook anti-addiction and nature protection drives to spread the messages of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj of living an addiction-free life and caring for the environment.
 For a month, more than 50 balaks went to different public areas and motivated people to give up their addictions and more than 20 balikas visited people door to door to encourage them to adopt environment friendly habits.
 These children contacted over 3,000 people in the areas surrounding the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Bhasa and also in Kolkata city and communicated these important messages.
 In conclusion, on 31 May 2022, the balaks and balikas carried out a rally in the Aamtala area to reinforce these messages promoted by Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

/News/2022/Appeal-for-Peace-21883.aspx.t: Appeal for Peace, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2022/Appeal-for-Peace-21883.aspx.text:
We are shocked and saddened by the anti-India graffiti at the gates of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto, Canada by anti-social elements. The BAPS temple in Toronto, like all temples of BAPS worldwide, is an abode of peace, harmony, equality, selfless service, and universal Hindu values.
 At this critical time, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual leader of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, has prayed for peace and unity and has appealed to all devotees and well-wishers to maintain peace.
 We are thankful to the appropriate authorities, including the governments of India and Canada, for their continued support and sympathy.
 Let us all join in worldwide prayers, in private and at home, that God blesses and guides us all to continue to do good and think good of all.
 કેનેડાના ટોરન્ટો શહેર ખાતે બી.એ.પી.એસ. શ્રી સ્વામિનારાયણ મંદિરના પ્રવેશદ્વાર પર કેટલાંક અસામાજિક તત્ત્વોએ કરેલ  ભારત વિરોધી ગ્રાફિટી લખાણોથી અમે આઘાત અને શોક અનુભવીએ છીએ. વિશ્વભરમાં વ્યાપેલા અન્ય બી.એ.પી.એસ. મંદિરોની જેમ જ, આ બી.એ.પી.એસ. મંદિર પણ શાંતિ, સંવાદિતા, સમરસતા, સંસ્કાર, નિસ્વાર્થ જનસેવા તેમજ વૈશ્વિક હિન્દુ મૂલ્યોનું ધામ છે. આવા સંસ્કૃતિ-ધામ પર આવેલી આ વિકટ વેળાએ બી.એ.પી.એસ. સ્વામિનારાયણ સંસ્થાના આધ્યાત્મિક વડા પરમ પૂજ્ય મહંત સ્વામી મહારાજે સર્વે હરિભક્તો અને શુભેચ્છકોને શાંતિ જાળવવા હાર્દિક અપીલ કરી છે. આ વિકટ વેળાએ સહયોગ અને સહાનુભૂતિ આપવા બદલ ભારત અને કેનેડા સરકાર તેમજ તમામ સંસ્થાઓના અમે આભારી છીએ. આવો, સૌનું ભલું થાય એ ભાવના સાથે આપણે વ્યક્તિગત રીતે અને પોતપોતાના ઘરમંદિરમાં પ્રાર્થના કરીએ કે પરમાત્મા આપણને સૌને સૌનું ભલું કરવાની અને ભલું ઇચ્છવાની વધુ શક્તિ અને પ્રેરણા આપે.

/News/2022/Australian-and-Indian-Trade-D.t: Australian and Indian Trade Delegation Visit BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Rosehill, Sydney, Australia
/News/2022/Australian-and-Indian-Trade-D.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Australian and Indian Trade Delegation Visit BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir (18 photos)
 Following the signing of the Australia-India Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (AI ECTA) earlier in the week, Hon. Piyush Goyal, India’s Minister for Commerce and Trade, and the Australian Minister for Trade, Hon. Dan Tehan, visited the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Sydney. They were accompanied by a 35-member delegation which included Federal Member for Berowra Julian Leeser, High Commissioner of India Manpreet Vohra, Indian Consul General Manish Gupta, Councillor Reena Jethi and Federal Candidate for Parramatta Maria Kovacic.
 Addressing the assembly, Mr. Goyal described that his visit to the mandir was like “coming home”. He said, “My connection with the BAPS organization is truly deep. It comes from within.”
 Mr. Goyal and his family have been a part of many key moments in BAPS history, such as the inauguration of the BAPS Mandir in London in 1995 and His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 75th birthday celebrations in Mumbai, later in the same year.
 Mr. Goyal said he has been inspired and guided by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj throughout his life. Referring to a murti of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Mr. Goyal said, “Did you see the smile on his face? It was radiant. It was infectious. It just elevates your spirit and the goodness in you.
 "To me, Pramukh Swami always embodied devotion, truth, detachment and knowledge. Knowledge is important for all of us, but that knowledge has to be pure. With that knowledge, we have to serve society, and service can only happen if you are spiritual."
 Speaking about BAPS’s worldwide charitable contributions, Mr. Goyal emphasized to Mr. Tehan, "This is one set of people who are completely and selflessly devoted to giving back to society. It is in their blood. It is in their knowledge. It is in their training."
 In his address, Mr. Tehan called the AI ECTA a ‘unity’ agreement which will turbocharge the close, long-standing, and highly complementary economic relationship between the two nations.
 Both Mr. Tehan and Mr. Goyal referred to the ‘close friendship’ and ‘brotherhood’ between them, the two countries, and the two nations’ leaders, Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

/News/2022/BAPS-Campus-Diwali-Celebratio.t: BAPS Campus Fellowship Diwali Celebration 2022, North America
/News/2022/BAPS-Campus-Diwali-Celebratio.text:
Youths across North American university campuses rekindled their flame of character, integrity, and spirituality through the annual BAPS Campus Diwali Celebration hosted by the BAPS Campus Fellowship. This year, over 20 campuses across North America held the Campus Diwali Celebrations. Collegiate youths, often at remote campus locations away from childhood friends and family, balanced their academic schedules to plan, organize, and participate in this event. In addition, the student volunteers hand-prepared various vegetarian food items to offer as an annakut, upholding cornerstone elements of the Diwali tradition. Over 4,500 students, faculty, and community members participated in these celebrations. 
 The program was themed "In the Joy of Others, Lies our Own" to commemorate the Centennial Celebrations of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The celebration took place with an exhibition and live stage program on the true meaning of Pramukh Swãmi Maharaj's life motto:
 "In the Joy of Others, Lies our Own," encouraging us to celebrate small acts of kindness done consistently 
 "In the Progress of Others, Rests our Own," showing the importance of putting others ahead and mentoring the future generations 
 "In the Good of Others, Abides our Own," emphasizes putting aside negativity and ego to appreciate others' virtues and wishing well for them fully
 "Know this to be the key to peace and happiness," meaning it's worthwhile to commit to the joy, progress, and good of others because it will lead to the ultimate fulfillment of life. 
 This powerful message of Pramukh Swãmi Maharaj was illustrated via interactive exhibits and motivational speeches by swamis. Many delegates arrived wearing traditional Indian clothing and were welcomed in accordance with Hindu custom by applying a chandlo (red vermillion mark) to their forehead and tying a nadachhadi (red sacred thread) on their wrists. Guests, faculty, staff, and students were inspired to think of each other during this festive time and work for the betterment of society at large when setting personal and professional goals. This year's program showcased how to live a simple and truthful life through the lens of mental well-being and transcending today's result-driven culture.
 Students were encouraged to develop a practice of prayer and spiritual study in their daily lives, enabling them to find peace through faith, truth, and simplicity. In this manner, the program inspired today's youth to imbibe Pramukh Swami Maharaj's motto "In the Joy of Others" in their lives and experience the happiness and joy of Diwali every day of their lives. 
 Under the spiritual guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS continues to promote and organize activities that celebrate the spirit and values of Hindu festivals while simultaneously augmenting today's youth with vital life lessons. These lessons equip youths with the potential to share peace, love, harmony and provide selfless service to the community.

/News/2022/BAPS-Gainesville-Inauguration.t: Inauguration of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Gainesville, FL, USA
/News/2022/BAPS-Gainesville-Inauguration.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Sthapan Ceremony (20 photos)
 Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path Yagna (13 photos)
 HH Mahant Swami Maharaj Sanctifies Murtis in India (16 photos)
 Women's Cultural Program (7 photos)
 The opening of the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Gainesville, Florida, took place on October 29, 2022, in the presence of Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami, Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, and other swamis. In addition, devotees, community leaders, friends, and well-wishers from the southeastern United States participated in the ceremony in person and virtually.
 The inauguration culminated a host of events held over a few days. On the morning of October 22, 2022, Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path,' a special yagna ceremony was performed by BAPS Swamis and youths, on the evening of Saturday, October 22, 2022, Swamis and youths performed a Kirtan Aradhana (singing of devotional songs). In addition, a unique Women's cultural program highlighting Pramukh Swami Maharaj Centenary Celebration was organized on the evening of Saturday, October 29, 2022.
 The inauguration ceremony consisted of Hindu Vedic prayers for world peace, followed by the consecration ceremony. Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami and Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami performed the consecration ceremony at the behest of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual leader of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. The ceremony signaled the Mandir as a home of God open to one and all. The new Mandir will be home to cultural, social, and religious activities for the Hindu-American community. It will also be a hub for community service activities.

/News/2022/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Celebrates-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS Hindu Mandir Celebrates International Yoga Day (16 photos)
 The BAPS UAE Women’s Wing celebrated the 8th International Yoga Day at the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi. Over 400 female devotees and guests from across the UAE came together to celebrate this day which was centered around the theme ‘Yoga for Humanity’ to promote health and wellbeing.
 The event commenced with the chanting of Vedic mantras gracefully sung by balikas. Following an introductory speech on being ‘Calmly Active and Actively Calm’, Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s mastery of ashtang yoga during his teenage years as Nilkanth Varni was highlighted.
 Then, in an interactive yoga session, the attendees were guided on the benefits of performing regular yoga and pranayam. The event concluded with a beautiful musical presentation showcasing different yogic hand gestures – called mudras.
 Among the dignitaries present was H.E. Laila Rahhall El Atfani, Goodwill ambassador and founder/president of Business Gate.

/News/2022/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Gives-10000.t: BAPS Hindu Mandir Gives 10,000 Handmade Rakhis to Workers and Residents, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2022/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Gives-10000.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Special Prayers On The Occasion of Rakshabandhan at the BAPS Hindu Mandir (37 photos)
 BAPS Hindu Mandir held a special prayer assembly to commemorate Rakshabandhan and pay tribute to HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj on his sixth memorial anniversary. The celebration, attended by more than 4,000 workers from over 26 companies, was a joyous occasion to thank the those working earnestly to provide for their families.
 Rakshabandhan symbolizes a bond of support and protection between brothers and sisters and God and devotees. It is celebrated amongst families and friends. On this auspicious day, sisters tie a sacred thread, or rakhi, on the right-hand wrist of their brothers while praying for their well-being and prosperity. In return, brothers give their sisters a gift as a promise of protection and love. The literal translation of ‘raksha bandhan’ is ‘bond of protection.’ On this auspicious day, 10,000 rakhis, handmade by the female devotees of the BAPS in UAE, were distributed to workers, residents, families, and communities to celebrate this occasion. 
 Ram, one of the laborers, shared a sentiment echoed by many of the attendees, “I feel like I am back home with my family. We are grateful to the swamis and Mandir for inviting us to celebrate Rakshabandhan together.”
 HH Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the audience from India with prayers for harmony and fraternity – underlining that we are eternally under God’s protection and are blessed with the wisdom to help one another in the spirit of universal fellowship.
 Afterwards, the attendees participated in an auspicious brick laying ceremony called ‘Shila Sthaapan.’ Partaking in a special puja to sanctify a brick which they personally carried and placed on the five-meter-high plinth, above the foundation of the new mandir.
 Swami Brahmaviharidas, head of the BAPS Hindu Mandir, presiding over the ceremonies added, "The atmosphere is one of great love, equality, and divinity. These thousands of rakhis have been handmade with love by the female devotees of UAE, to gift to each worker, symbolizing blessings for brothers. Even this Mandir will be handmade with love! Hence, in a place of great piety we pray that may God guide and guard this beautiful nation, its leadership, and all those who call it their home."
 The resonance of respect between the Hindu Community and the workers was evident. As more than 100 volunteers helped orchestrate the flow while working conscientiously to manage logistics, prepare fresh food, and small traditional memorabilia. A successful reflection of true positivity and solidarity in this country.
 “There is a feeling of belonging which cannot be justified in words. This thread symbolizes mutual respect and togetherness. I am truly proud to serve these brothers who work tirelessly to help build marvellous projects, such as this beautiful upcoming mandir.” Ashok Kotecha, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Chairman.
 The audience also enjoyed a medley of festival hymns sung by the sadhus and youth volunteers of BAPS Hindu Mandir. Meanwhile, each member of the assembly came forward to be tied their own rakhi accompanied with a prayer for protection, fulfillment, and happiness.

Pujya Doctor Swami then showered sanctified flowers around the construction site and prayed for the successful completion of the project.

/News/2022/BAPS-Hosts-Unity-Forum-21514..t: BAPS Hosts Unity Forum, Long Island, NY, USA
/News/2022/BAPS-Hosts-Unity-Forum-21514..text:
Photo Gallery 
 Unity Forum, Long Island (22 photos)
 BAPS hosted leaders of faith based organizations at its centers across North America in ‘Unity Forums’ to discuss how to address public safety awareness and other issues affecting places of worship. The event was organized locally at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Melville, NY on June 12, 2022.
 Founded on the Hindu belief of “Vasudhaiva kutumbakam” meaning, “the entire world is one family,” the event brought together leaders from over 29 Hindu mandirs and other faith-based organizations to share ideas with each other and meet with government officials and security experts.
 The experts from local, state, and federal agencies conveyed the importance of maintaining awareness and being prepared, as well as provided best practices for security in places of worship. In some forums, District Attorneys also joined the event to explain laws and judicial processes relevant to Hindu mandirs.  Question and answer sessions were held with the respective experts, allowing community members to voice concerns and receive further guidance. 
 The other local officials present at the event included Mr. Raymond A. Tierney, Suffolk County District Attorney; Mr. Allen Bode, Chief Assistant District Attorney; Captain Michael Smith Deputy Sheriff Investigator; Mr. Jon Kaiman, Suffolk County Deputy County Executive.
 Mr. Timothy Brown Police Officer, Department of Homeland Security-Suffolk County police department; Mr. Gerard Hardy Chief of Patrol with Mr. William Scrima Inspector, Commanding Officer Second Precinct Suffolk County Police Department; Mr. Persaud for the New York City Police Department also attended this forum and gave guidance. 
 As part of the Unity Forum, renowned scholar of Hindu Philosophy and Sanskrit, Mahamahopadhyaya Pujya Bhadreshdas Swami also addressed the attendees. Drawing on his extensive dialogue with scholars and Hindu leaders throughout the world, Bhadreshdas Swami shed light on how knowledge can be applied to foster social harmony and peace.
 As a global ambassador of the Hindu faith and Indian intellectual heritage, Bhadreshdas Swami’s unique insights highlighted the need for a continuous dialogue and cooperative efforts not only for physical safety, but also for establishing a solid foundation of Hindu practices anchored in scriptural teachings and principles.

/News/2022/BAPS-Mandirs-Light-Beacons-to.t: BAPS Mandirs Light Beacons to Celebrate Queen’s Platinum Jubilee, UK
/News/2022/BAPS-Mandirs-Light-Beacons-to.text:
BAPS mandirs around the UK joined thousands of others on Thursday 2 June 2022 in lighting special beacons to mark the Platinum Jubilee of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II.
 The beacons formed part of the official national celebration marking 70 years since The Queen ascended the throne.
 More than three thousand beacons were lit by charities, communities and faith groups all over the UK. In addition, beacons were lit in all 54 Commonwealth capitals, with the Principal Beacon lit in a special ceremony at Buckingham Palace. 
 The lighting of each beacon at BAPS mandirs was part of a community celebration including prayers and a cultural programme paying tribute to Her Majesty’s seven decades of public service.

Photo Gallery 
 Maha-Annakut (23 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Secunderabad, in conjunction with NTV organized a maha-annakut during the Koti Deepotsavam festival held at NTR Stadium, Hyderabad.
 More than 1,000 sweet and savory vegetarian dishes were offered to Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and the Guru Parampara. The maha-annakut was a grand collective effort of devotion by 300 volunteers.
 As per tradition, Govardhan puja was performed. This was followed by singing of thal bhajans and the arti.
 Chief guests present included Shri G Kishan Reddy Garu (Minister of Tourism, Culture and Development of North-Eastern Region of India) and Shri Narendra Chaudhary Garu (Chairman of NTV).
 During the day, more than 30,000 devotees and well-wishers came for darshan of the annakut.

/News/2022/BAPS-Participates--Celebrates.t: BAPS Participates & Celebrates Pramukh Swami Maharaj Centennial in India Day Parade, New York, NY, USA
/News/2022/BAPS-Participates--Celebrates.text:
Photo Gallery 
 India Independence Parade (35 photos)
 On Sunday, August 21, 2022, the Federation of Indian Association (FIA) organized a parade in New York to celebrate India’s Independence Day. Over 500 BAPS devotees took part in the program along with thousands of other Indian Americans from various organizations.
 A special part of the program included a Pramukh Swami Maharaj Centennial celebration. In the parade, a float representing the Hindu sentiments of, “Vasudhaiva Kutumbhakam,” (the world is one family) carried children through the major streets of the city. At the end of the parade, there was a short program in which shlokas and kirtans were sung in unison to spread the guru’s glory. The devotees from nearby mandirs also took part in the FIA’s program of setting the Guiness World Record for the most people playing the damaru (hand-drum) and most different flags flown simultaneously - both in honor of the 75th anniversary of India’s independence.
 At the end of the celebrations, BAPS provided food to the participants from every organization. Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj’s wish to, “expand the circle of unity throughout the world,” was manifested this afternoon through the celebrations.

/News/2022/BAPS-Responds-to-Ukrainian-Hu.t: BAPS Responds to Ukrainian Humanitarian Crisis, Rzeszów, Poland
/News/2022/BAPS-Responds-to-Ukrainian-Hu.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Emergency Response in Rzeszów, Poland (20 photos)
 As a devastating humanitarian crisis unfolds in Ukraine, hundreds of thousands are fleeing the warzone seeking refuge in neighbouring countries. This has included thousands of Indian nationals, mainly students, who have been left stranded amid the conflict. 
 Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally called Brahmaviharidas Swami at midnight on Sunday 27 February, asking for assistance from BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in ensuring the safe passage of Indian nationals on the Polish, Romanian and Hungarian borders with Ukraine. 
 Brahmaviharidas Swami, with years of experience in disaster relief work, joined an emergency meeting in Delhi by video conference from Dubai. After expressing his anguish at the plight of the refugees, Brahmaviharidas Swami reassured the Prime Minister that help was already on its way. “We have already been instructed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to mobilise BAPS volunteers from all over Europe.”
 Volunteers from the UK, Ireland, France, Switzerland, Italy, Germany, Austria and Poland swiftly sprang into action to support the emergency relief effort on the ground. This has included setting up a mobile field kitchen in the south-eastern Polish city of Rzeszów, which has begun feeding around 1,000 hot vegetarian meals daily to refugees of all faiths and nationalities.  
 BAPS is also arranging accommodation facilities and coordinating medical assistance, and is working closely with the Indian government as well as local partners to further expand the humanitarian efforts as the situation escalates.
 Vijay Kumar Singh, former Army Chief of Staff and current Minister of State for Transport and Civil Aviation, observed the tireless efforts of the volunteers first-hand in Rzeszów. He commented: “BAPS has always been at the forefront of community service, being the first to arrive and the last to leave. The people of India are indebted to your swift, selfless and organised action.”
 Shailesh Bhavsar, a lead BAPS volunteer from Paris, added, “The situation in Ukraine is desperate and tragic. The priority is to support those seeking refuge by providing them with food and shelter. We are working closely with transport networks and logistical agencies to ensure the safe and timely delivery of essential services to those in need. 
 “Our volunteers are inspired by the ethos of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who personified the motto “In the joy of others lies our own”, and there has perhaps never been a more opportune moment to embody this selfless spirit of public service by providing the basic needs for those severely impacted by the conflict.”

/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.t: BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute Inauguration, Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania
/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute (26 photos)
 As part of the centenary celebrations of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute was inaugurated in the presence of Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami, BAPS swamis, Professor William Pallangyo (Senior lecturer of leadership and management at the Law School of Tanzania), Captain Ibhrahim Bendera (Advocate of the High Court of Tanzania) , Mr. Idd Mandi (Senior lecturer at University of Dar es Salaam), representatives from various Hindu communities, and BAPS devotees.
 The BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute is dedicated to advancing quality research, learning, and the expression of Hinduism, its traditons, philosophies, languages and rich body of literature. The Institute will strive to foster social harmony, interfaith dialogue, public engagement, and academic discourse through its value-based education, innovative research, and creative expression
 The ceremony began with swamis and invited dignitaries lighting the inaugural lamp (deep-pragatya), symbolizing the spreading of the light of knowledge throughout the world.
 During his keynote speech, Bhadreshdas Swami said, "India has a vast collection of knowledge and with the opening of BAPS Swaminarayan Institute, this knowledge would be shared in this part of the world as well.”
 The chief guest, Professor William Pallangyo, appreciated BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha for this initiative and pledged his full support.
 Captain Ibhrahim Bendera said in his speech that the main objective of this research institute is to promote universal harmony and is an amazing addition to our country.
 Snehalbhai Bakrania, Chairman of Shri Hindu Mandal, donated his collection of 3,400 Hindu shastras and texts to the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute.
 Mr. Idd Mandi, a senior lecturer at University of Dar es Salaam, said, “The Central vision of this institute is to bring light and togetherness at a time of great division in the world. We need more of this and we applaud your leadership. I want to recognize the wonderful work of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in Tanzania.”

/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.t: Inauguration of BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Deep Pragtya and Inauguration by HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (9 photos)
 Inauguration Assembly - Toronto (26 photos)
 Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path Yagna (29 photos)
 Recognition at the Canadian Parliament (2 photos)
 Launch Assembly - Ottawa (19 photos)
 The Canadian chapter of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute was inaugurated on June 4, 2022, at the BAPS Swaminarayan Complex in Toronto. The institute was inaugurated as a part of the centenary celebrations of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the presence of the spiritual community and government leaders. Thousands witnessed the historic ceremony in person and via live telecast across Canada and worldwide. In addition, representatives from more than 40 Hindu Mandirs and organizations were present for the occasion.
 The BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute is dedicated to advancing quality research, learning, and expression of Hinduism, its cultures, philosophies, affiliated languages, and rich collection of literature. Furthermore, the institute will strive to foster social harmony, interfaith dialogue, public engagement, and academic discourse as it generates opportunities for the highest level of value-based education, innovative research, and creative expression.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual guru of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and the visionary and inspirer of this research institute, participated in the inauguration ceremony via live webcast from India, lighting the inaugural lamp (deep-pragatya) symbolizing the spreading of the light of knowledge throughout the world. He also sent a special message saying, "In the spirit of "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam," meaning the world is one family; let's reach out to extend the circle of global harmony."
 HH Mahant Swami Maharaj had sent Mahamahopadhyay Pujya Bhadreshdas Swami from India to preside over the inauguration event. Pujya Bhadreshdas Swami is globally acclaimed for his seminal contributions to Indian philosophy and his erudite scholarship on Hindu beliefs and culture. As the author of the ground-breaking Sanskrit commentarial and philosophical texts, the Swaminarayan-Bhashyam and the Swaminarayan-Siddhanta-Sudha, he is one of the world's leading scholars of Hindu philosophy.
 Many scholars have lauded the Swaminarayan Bhashyam, written by Bhadreshdas Swami, as one of the greatest contributions to Hinduism and Indian philosophy in the past several centuries. This monumental work is a testament to the continuing tradition of spiritual inquiry that has remained vibrant over millennia within Hinduism. These volumes address the modern need for religious and social pluralism and harmony in the world, along with explaining universal ethical and spiritual values. During the inauguration ceremony, Pujya Bhadreshdas Swami gifted this scripture to Hon. Ahmed Hussen, Minister of Housing and Diversity and Inclusion, to be made available to all Canadians to appreciate for generations to come.
 During his keynote speech, Bhadreshdas Swami said, "This institute aims to promote the spirit of benevolence and harmony by spreading the message of the ancient, sacred sentiment of "Vasudev Kutumbakam" – the whole world is one family.
 The chief guest for the inauguration ceremony Hon. Ahmed Hussen, Minister of Housing and Diversity and Inclusion, shared, "Today's event marks a special milestone of the opening of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, which will serve all of humanity. The institute is dedicated to advancing education, advancing quality research, learning, reflection, and the democratization of wisdom. It is a key part of our country's future and access to Hindu culture.
 Its main objective is promoting universal harmony, and I can't think of a more amazing addition to our country as an institute about promoting universal harmony for everyone.
 We are all here to celebrate a key milestone for Hindu Canadians and all Canadians because this institute will advance knowledge, universal harmony and understanding, and an appreciation of the power of education to transform lives and change hearts. I want to thank the leadership at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir for always bringing the community together; just as for this auspicious occasion, they have brought 40 Hindu Mandirs together from across the country - which is something that I have never seen before!"
 Hon. Candice Bergen, Leader of the Official Opposition, also sent a congratulatory message saying, "It is with great joy that I offer my heartfelt congratulations to you on the launch of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute in Canada. I know that the research institute's work will strengthen the Hindu community in Canada, and I look forward to seeing the fruit of your efforts as you continue to enrich our country with the beauty of Indian culture and heritage."
 The Hon. Stephen Lecce, Minister of Education for the Province of Ontario, said, "We are proud of the work you do, your leadership, your sacrifice, and your commitment to building this country. The central vision of this institute is to bring light and togetherness at a time of great division in the world. We need more of this, and we applaud your leadership. We applaud the work of BAPS in Canada and around the world."
 Pandit Roopnauth Sharma, President of the Hindu Federation, who participated in the inauguration ceremony, said, "I am privileged to be a part of this great milestone event for Sanatan Dharma. I want to recognize the wonderful work BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha does here and worldwide to promote Sanatan Dharma. There is still hope for Hinduism when we have giants of our dharma like Bhadreshdas Swami present with us. Swamiji walks in the footsteps of Panini, Shankaracharya, and other great giants of Hindu philosophy."
 Other special guests attending the historic inauguration included:
 ●     The Hon. Kirsty Duncan, Member of Parliament for Etobicoke North
 ●     The Hon. Kinga Surma, Minister of Infrastructure for the Province of Ontario
 ●     The Hon. Stephen Lecce, Minister of Education for the Province of Ontario
 ●     Hardeep Grewal, MPP Elect for Brampton East
 ●     Deepak Anand, MPP for Mississauga—Malton
 On June 5, 2022, nearly 2,000 devotees and well-wishers participated in the 'Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path,' a unique yagna ceremony in which sanctified grains were offered in the sacrificial flame with the recital of 315 Sanskrit verses from the Satsang Diksha scripture by children and youth. Prior to that, the BAPS women's wing performed a 'Pothi Yatra,' a religious procession honouring the holy scriptures, including the Satsang Diksha, the Swaminarayan-Bhashyam and the Swaminarayan-Siddhanta-Sudha, to conclude the inauguration ceremony and offer prayers for an auspicious beginning to the new research institute.
 Subsequently, the launching of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute was held in Ottawa on June 11, 2022, where representatives from Hindu Mandirs and organizations were present for the occasion. Special guests attending the historic inauguration included:
 ●     His Excellency Anshuman Gaur, Deputy High Commissioner of India to Canada
 ●     Chandra Arya, Member of Parliament for Nepean
 ●     Glen Gower, City Councillor for Stittsville

/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.t: Inauguration of BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path Yagna & Inauguration by HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (64 photos)
 Inauguration Assembly (26 photos)
 Opening of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute (16 photos)
 Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path at Home (32 photos)
 On Saturday, June 18, 2022, the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, USA, was inaugurated in Robbinsville, New Jersey, at the site of Swaminarayan Akshardham North America.
 In the morning, hundreds of swamis and devotees gathered to participate in a ‘Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path.’ This unique yagna involved offerings in a sacred fire while selected verses from the Satsang Diksha were recited. The yagna was performed to pray for world peace along with an auspicious beginning for the research institute. Children sang Vedic peace prayers and recited Sanskrit verses. Thousands witnessed the historic ceremony in person and via live telecast across North America and worldwide. 
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj joined the ceremony virtually from Ahmedabad, India, and inaugurated the institute with the lighting of the inaugural lamp (deep-pragatya) symbolizing the spreading of the light of knowledge throughout the world. Diyas were subsequently lit by members of the assembly present in New Jersey. Mahant Swami Maharaj then blessed the attendees as well as all the people who remotely joined the live broadcast. 
 Addressing the assembly, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “Yogiji Maharaj had envisioned such an institute and was passionate about youths learning and discoursing in Sanskrit. The research institute has fulfilled this vision. May students excel in their studies and work together to serve society, expanding the circle of unity across the world. In the spirit of "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam," meaning the world is one family; let's reach out to extend the circle of global harmony.”
 The event took place in the presence of over 115 representatives from over 50 Hindu Mandirs and organizations, guests, and scholars. HH Mahant Swami Maharaj had sent Mahamahopadhyaya Pujya Bhadreshdas Swami from India to preside over the inauguration event. Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami is one of the world’s leading scholars of Hindu philosophy and Sanskrit and the author of the Sanskrit commentarial and philosophical texts, the Swaminarayan-Bhashyam and the Swaminarayan-Siddhanta-Sudha. Bhadreshdas Swami delivered the institute's inaugural lecture and reinforced His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s messages of global harmony, public service and educational excellence.  Elaborating on Mahant Swami Maharaj’s vision, he encouraged children and youth to explore their interests in the areas of arts and Hindu philosophy.
 The ‘BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute’ is the first such center of learning and research of Indian languages and Hindu scriptures in the Swaminarayan tradition to open in the United States. The impetus for the institute in Robbinsville has been a growing interest from members of the community to learn Sanskrit and gain a deeper understanding of Hindu scriptures. Through its rigorous teaching of Sanskrit, Vedic and classical literature, as well as Hindu beliefs, values and practices, the institute will strive to foster social harmony, interfaith dialogue, public engagement and academic discourse.  It will generate opportunities for value-based education, innovative research and creative expression. For more details, visit https://research.baps.org.

/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.t: ‘BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute’ inaugurated at Neasden Temple, UK & Europe
/News/2022/BAPS-Swaminarayan-Research-In.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Inauguration Assembly (40 photos)
 Inauguration Ceremony (20 photos)
 ‘BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute’ for UK & Europe was inaugurated on Sunday 29 May 2022 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – in the presence of esteemed guests from the world of academia, including Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami, from India, and Professor James Hegarty, of Cardiff University.
 The inauguration assembly commenced with a performance of devotional singing by children of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha from around the UK. It continued with Vedic peace prayers sung by a choir of 40 children and a recital of Sanskrit verses by other children, including 10-year-old Maharshi Shah of Coventry.
 The assembly, witnessed by thousands online and in-person at Neasden Temple, was inspired through the blessings and vision of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and formed a part of the celebrations marking the birth centenary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj joined the assembly via video link from India and inaugurated the Institute by lighting a lamp, symbolising the spreading of the light of knowledge throughout the world. Guests and members of the congregation in London followed by lighting their own sacred lamps. Mahant Swami Maharaj then blessed Professor Hegarty as well as representatives from various Hindu organisations who had gathered to celebrate the historic inauguration.
 Addressing the assembly, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “Yogiji Maharaj had envisioned such an institute and was passionate about youths learning and discoursing in Sanskrit. The Research Institute has fulfilled this vision. May students excel in their studies and work together to serve society, expanding the circle of unity across the world.”
 Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami, author of the ground-breaking and internationally acclaimed Swaminarayan-Bhashyam and Swaminarayan-Siddhanta-Sudha, and widely considered as one of the world’s leading scholars of Hindu philosophy today, delivered the ‘first lecture of the Institute’ by reinforcing His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s messages of global harmony, public service and academic excellence. He also urged parents to encourage their children in the arts.
 Professor Hegarty, Professor of Sanskrit and Indian Religions at Cardiff University as well as Head of History, Archaeology and Religion, also addressed the assembly. He said: “I am incredibly honoured to stand before you today. The young people [who sang and recited in Sanskrit] are extraordinary! I cannot believe what I have seen and heard. I offer my deepest respect and thanks to His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.”  
 Speaking of the benefits that the Institute will impart, Professor Hegarty added, “The new research centre will soon flourish here in the UK and Europe – and globally – under the sure and skilled guidance of the swamis assembled here today. Research and teaching based on research, if they are themselves based on true and compassionate mastery, can make a difference in the world. The new research institute we inaugurate today will show that. I have no doubt at all.” As an example of the lofty ideals of the BAPS Swaminarayan tradition, Professor Hegarty cited a Sanskrit verse from the Satsang Diksha, authored by Mahant Swami Maharaj, praying for unity, friendship, compassion, tolerance and love to flourish among all people of the world.
 The impetus for the institute in London has been a growing interest from both young and senior members of the community to learn Sanskrit and gain a deeper understanding of the scriptures of their faith.
 Through its rigorous teaching of Sanskrit, classical Vedic literature and Hindu beliefs, values and practices – all in a traditional Gurukul style – the institute will strive to foster social harmony, interfaith dialogue, public engagement and academic discourse as it generates opportunities for the highest level of value-based education, innovative research and creative expression.
 Earlier, on Friday 27 May 2022, the Indian calendrical day of Yogji Maharaj’s birth anniversary, hundreds of devotees had gathered to participate in the ‘Satsang Dikshā Homātmak Pāth’. This unique three-hour ceremony involved offerings to a sacred flame based on the recital of each verse from the Satsang Diksha scripture, in prayer for an auspicious beginning to the new research institute.

/News/2022/BAPS-Tanzania-Participates-in.t: BAPS Tanzania Participates in Interreligious Workshop, Mwanza, Tanzania
/News/2022/BAPS-Tanzania-Participates-in.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Interreligious Workshop (5 photos)
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Mwanza, was invited, together with representatives of various other religions in Mwanza, by the St. Augustine University of Tanzania (SAUT) to a workshop on interreligious dialogue. SAUT is a Catholic-owned higher academic institution managed by the Tanzania Episcopal Conference (TEC).
 The department of Philosophy and Ethics at SAUT organized this workshop on 'Interreligious dialogue to form a peaceful and harmonious society’. The workshop helped to build a respectful, loving, and cooperative society despite the religious differences.
 On behalf of BAPS, Dipeshkumar Girishchandra Dave presented how to equip the youth to serve society so that people live by the principles of love, dignity, equality and mutual respect.
 The event was attended by over 1,500 delegates, including representatives of religious institutions in the region and government officials. Vice Chancellor Prof. Costa Ricky Mahalu was the chief guest.

/News/2022/BAPS-Trustee-Receives-Queens-.t: BAPS Trustee Receives Queen’s Honour for Charitable and Voluntary Services, UK
/News/2022/BAPS-Trustee-Receives-Queens-.text:
Vinu Bhattessa, a longstanding trustee of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK, has been awarded the Order of the British Empire (OBE) by Her Majesty The Queen in the Birthday Honours List for 2022.
 The citation reads: Kishorkant Bhattessa (Vinu Bhattessa). For charitable and voluntary services, particularly during Covid-19. 
 The Most Excellent Order of the British Empire is a British order of chivalry, rewarding contributions to the arts and sciences, work with charitable and welfare organisations, and public service outside the civil service. It was established on 4 June 1917 by King George V.
 Vinubhai has been serving BAPS for over 30 years and was a key figure during the construction of Neasden Temple, one of the first traditionally built Hindu temples outside of India. 
 Further to his contributions to BAPS, Vinubhai has managed one of the largest Shakespeare Festivals in the UK, helping maintain British culture and heritage. He has also worked closely with various charities, including The Springboard Charity that helps youth find employment and, most recently, supported the emergency appeal for India’s Covid crisis by arranging ventilators as well as supplying concierge services to the local community and supplies to key London hospitals. He is also a Founders Circle member of the British Asian Trust. 
 Congratulations to Vinubhai, his family, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and the entire Hindu community for inspiring thousands of volunteers to serve society under the visionary guidance of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the current inspiration of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2022/BAPS-Volunteers-Serve-in-Pola.t: BAPS Volunteers Serve in Poland for Ukraine Humanitarian Crisis, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2022/BAPS-Volunteers-Serve-in-Pola.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Emergency Response in Rzeszów, Poland (20 photos)
 As a devastating humanitarian crisis unfolds in Ukraine, hundreds of thousands are fleeing the warzone seeking refuge in neighboring countries. This has included thousands of Indian nationals, mainly students, who have been left stranded amid the conflict. 
 Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally called BAPS to assist the government's efforts for the safe passage of Indian nationals from Ukraine. Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami reassured the Prime Minister: "We have also been instructed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to mobilise BAPS volunteers."
 Volunteers from the USA, UK, Ireland, France, Switzerland, Italy, Germany, Austria and Poland swiftly sprang into action to support the emergency relief efforts on the ground. This has included setting up a mobile field kitchen in the south-eastern Polish city of Rzeszów, which has begun feeding around 1,000 hot vegetarian meals daily to refugees of all faiths and nationalities. BAPS is also arranging accommodation facilities and coordinating medical assistance and is working closely with the Indian government and local partners.
 Volunteers travelled from Robbinsville, NJ to Rezszow, Poland and to Budomierz, Poland, on the Ukrainian border to help distribute humanitarian supplies to and facilitate the transport of international students and others fleeing Ukraine.
 Darshan Patel, an attorney by profession serving at the refugee camp said, "Seeing the need to help students and refugees leaving Ukraine, I took a flight to Poland to serve them. The least we can do is make them comfortable during this stressful time by providing them food and basic necessities."
 Shailesh Bhavsar, a lead BAPS volunteer from Paris, explained the process at the camp: "Once they arrive at the camp, we work on registering them, providing them with meals, giving them a place to stay and rest before processing them to go to the airport for a flight home."
 "Helping others through selfless service — 'seva' is a fundamental principle of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha," Dharmik Sheth, a pharmaceutical professional, said. "I am following my faith – and my family tradition. My father also volunteered during humanitarian crises when I was young." 
 "Our volunteers are inspired by the ethos of HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who personified the motto 'In the joy of others lies our own', and there has perhaps never been a more opportune moment to embody this selfless spirit of public service by providing the basic needs for those severely impacted by the conflict," said Pujya Nilkanthsevadas Swami, Head Swami at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Robbinsville, NJ. "We are working with local members of the Ukrainian community and our volunteer forces on the ground in Poland to send necessary humanitarian aid via our logistics partners. The volunteers who flew from New Jersey have been communicating information about supplies needed on the ground. We are trying our best to supply them." 
 Vijay Kumar Singh, former Army Chief of Staff and current Minister of State for Transport and Civil Aviation, observed the tireless efforts of the volunteers first-hand in Rzeszów and commented: "I would like to personally congratulate and commend BAPS volunteers. You are helping everyone with a sense of unity, without any expectations, and without worrying about yourselves. The people of India are indebted to your swift, selfless and organised action."
 Robbinsville Mayor Dave Fried immediately commended Ravi Patni and his fellow volunteers: "On behalf of Robbinsville, we are very proud of BAPS and their efforts to help the Ukrainian people. Hopefully, we can find a way to have the Township work together to help those people who are going through an unimaginably difficult time."
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj has also prayed for the welfare of those affected: "We offer our deepest gratitude to these volunteers. We also offer our prayers that peace prevails, and those who are suffering are provided support, strength and courage."
