/News/2023/Petals-and-Pinnacles-Pujan-of.t: Petals and Pinnacles: Pujan of the Seven Shikhars, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2023/Petals-and-Pinnacles-Pujan-of.text: Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami performed the pujan of the seven shikhars (spires) of the almost completed BAPS Hindu Mandir by showering petals as blessings. Volunteers, artisans, devotees and donors were filled with joy as this day marked a significant milestone for the Mandir, which stands as a beacon of global harmony, peace, and tolerance. Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami was overjoyed by the beauty, majesty and progress of this historic and iconic Mandir. He commended the selfless service and dedication of all.

/News/2023/Pramukh-Premier-League-and-Ma.t: Pramukh Premier League and Mahant Premier League Tournaments - ANZ, Neerim East, Australia
/News/2023/Pramukh-Premier-League-and-Ma.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Tournament (91 photos)
 Over 200 youths from 11 cities in Australia, New Zealand and Fiji (Perth, Adelaide, Melbourne, Hobart, Geelong, Sydney, Brisbane, Auckland, Canberra, Cranbourne, Tarneit) participated in this year’s Pacific region international cricket tournament titled, ‘Pramukh Premier League’. A total of 18 teams took part and the team from Cranbourne won the tournament.
 Also, 16 teams participated in the first international volleyball tournament titled, ‘Mahant Premier League’. After the round-robin stage, the teams competed in the playoffs. Sydney won the tournament.
 Daily, the youths performed samuh puja and the evening assemblies featured inspirational speeches by swamis, panel discussions with devotees giving their first-hand experiences of their seva, and activities to help build unity. These special daily assemblies also strengthened their faith in the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy.
 These events helped to build unity among the youths and invigorated them to progress on the spiritual path by pleasing guru Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2023/Pramukh-Swami-Apni-Prit-Kem-R.t: Pramukh Swami Apni Prit, Kem Re Bhulay, Sarangpur, India
/News/2023/Pramukh-Swami-Apni-Prit-Kem-R.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Smruti Din (19 photos)
 On 26 August 2023 (Shravan sud 10), swamis and devotees commemorated the seventh anniversary of Pramukh Swami Maharaj passing away to Akshardham by performing a short guru-pujan ceremony in the newly consecrated Pramukh Swami Maharaj Smruti Mandir. Jnaneshwar Swami, Aksharcharan Swami, and other swamis and devotees participated in the rituals. Thousands of devotees also joined from their homes through the live webcast. After the Vedic rituals, a maha-arti was performed at 6 p.m., the time when Swamishri went to Dham on 13 August 2016.
 In the assembly that followed, Atmatrupt Swami spoke about Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s eternally elevated spiritual state and Shrijikirtan Swami recollected the love and affection that Swamishri held for all the swamis and devotees. Adarshjivan Swami narrated the elevated spiritual state that was achieved by swamis and devotees through their association with Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 At the end, Jnaneshwar Swami spoke on how Swamishri is forever present through Mahant Swami Maharaj and that the truest tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj is to wholeheartedly serve Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In this way, the divine memories of Guruhari Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Pragat Guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj were recollected with bhakti and grandeur.

/News/2023/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Centenn.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Centennial Celebrations, Lisbon, Portugal
/News/2023/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Centenn.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Lisbon, Portugal (24 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Lisbon, commemorated the birth centenary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj with an inspiring two-day festival from 7 to 8 January 2023.
 Several distinguished guests attended the celebrations, including His Excellency Manish Chauhan, Ambassador of India to Portugal, who was accompanied by his wife Ranjeeta Chauhan, and Dr José Amaral Lopes, President of the Alvalade Parish Council, as well as leaders and representatives of various Hindu organisations in Portugal.
 The festival included an enlightening exhibition as well as an opportunity for visitors to
 participate in the abhishek ceremony (ancient Hindu practice of pouring water over the sacred image of God to honour him and to attain his blessings), enjoy henna painting, sample delicious vegetarian food, and select souvenirs as a memento of their visit.
 The celebratory programme comprised vibrant presentations by youths and adults revealing Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s inspiring life and uplifting messages as well as a journey through Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s previous visits to Lisbon.
 A musical tribute was also performed by devotees of the Mandir to honour Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s travels to Portugal.
 A special screening of Mystic India – a period documentary exploring India’s intricate architecture, colourful festivals, traditional rituals, fascinating diversity and stunning landscape, following the arduous journey of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as a teenage yogi – was aired on a giant LED screen to commemorate the 75th anniversary of India’s independence. The assembly further marked this historic occasion with national anthems of both India and Portugal.
 Sharing his experiences, Ambassador Chauhan said: “Thank you for inviting us to be a part of this very important celebration. This [Mystic India] was a very beautiful film. I watched it for the first time. It’s a colourful representation of India and the history of [Bhagwan] Swaminarayan, which was very useful to learn.”
 Dr Lopes added, “It’s an honour for me to be here, to celebrate Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s centennial birth anniversary. Despite practising different religions, we seek the same knowledge, harmony, peace and love. We share this concept of unity and diversity and respect to all. It’s an honour for us having you all here in the parish of Alvalade.”
 Volunteers had prepared for several weeks to plan and deliver this memorable celebration and to provide an enriching experience for the local community. More than 450 people attended the festival, departing with a deeper understanding of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life embodied by his teaching: ‘In the joy of others lies our own.’

/News/2023/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Smruti-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Guruji Nahi Bhulu Tamne (64 photos)
 On August 25, 2023, North American devotees reminisced and celebrated the cherished memories and teachings of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj in Robbinsville, NJ in a special assembly titled 'Guruji Nahi Bhulu Tamne.' The assembly was part of the Festival of Inspirations, a three-month-long celebration commemorating the inauguration of BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Jersey. The program took place in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who personally recalled memorable moments from the life of Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Pramukh Swami Maharaj's divine qualities of humility, selflessness, and unconditional love were illuminated through inspiring recollections that highlighted his virtues centered on a deep connection with God.
 Throughout the evening, swamis affectionately reminisced about their personal experiences and memories with Pramukh Swami Maharaj. They shared heartfelt incidents that touched them deeply and transformed their lives. Warmly recalling his calmness, presence of mind, and noble sentiments, the swamis demonstrated how Pramukh Swami Maharaj loved everyone with equal warmth and care, regardless of who they were. Pujya Aksharvatsaldas Swami shared the following metaphor: if one holds a flower and later sets it aside, the fragrance of the flower may still linger on the hand. Similarly, the essence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's divine qualities spread to anyone who was near him.
 Sadguru Ishwarcharandas Swami shared his personal experiences with Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Having served and worshipped in close proximity to Pramukh Swami for decades, he emphasized Pramukh Swami Maharaj's nirmaanipanu, or humility. He reflected on a specific incident during a grand festival where Pramukh Swami Maharaj credited all the success to the dedicated volunteers and devotees, even though it was due to his divine grace. Despite his many outstanding accomplishments, Pramukh Swami Maharaj attributed all his achievements entirely to God.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj candidly shared his experiences with Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who remained ever humble. He emphasized Pramukh Swami Maharaj's unwavering commitment, in every moment of his life, to the vow of service he took decades earlier. "We are all witnesses to how he lived and what he did for devotees and swamis. He was a true swami, remaining ordinary despite his extraordinary nature. Every action Pramukh Swami Maharaj took benefited future generations. Whether day or night, he overlooked his physical needs and stayed amongst his devotees."
 The program welcomed honored guests, who fondly recalled personal incidents from their time with Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the impact he had on their lives. Subhash Sam Patel, CEO of the Natson Hotel Group, spoke of a turning point when he questioned his engineering career path. Pramukh Swami Maharaj guided him to pursue business. "Our success has come from Pramukh Swami Maharaj's advice. I tell my son, if you want to learn discipline, learn it from Pramukh Swami Maharaj's life." Digvijay Gaekwad, founder of Danny Gaekwad Developments and Investments, relayed his experience as part of the American delegation accompanying former President Bill Clinton to Gandhinagar Akshardham to meet Pramukh Swami Maharaj. In a moment where both spoke in their native languages without translators, Mr. Gaekwad was awestruck. "They spoke different languages but still communicated. This can only happen if you are God or divine." Kamlesh Mehta, founder of the South Asian Times, reflected, "I always remember his affectionate touch and eyes filled with love and compassion. I sincerely believe and feel that I am a better person because of such divine impressions instilled in my thinking. Presenting Pramukh Swami Maharaj with a copy of the 2014 issue in which he was honored as the Person of the Year was a lifetime achievement for me. I am blessed that he autographed the newspaper." In a gesture of deep respect, Kamlesh Mehta presented Mahant Swami Maharaj with the newspaper bearing Pramukh Swami Maharaj's signature, along with the pen, to be displayed with other sanctified items at Akshardham.
 Also in attendance were esteemed guests Vijay Mani, Founder and CEO of Covey; Jasavant Singh and Deepak Bhardwaj, founders and owners of Apna Bazaar; and Mr. Sasha Ostashko, accompanied by his wife, Mrs. Gavshyna, respected tour operators and former Editor in Chief of a Ukrainian news agency.
 In the spirit of honoring the work and unique vision of Pramukh Swami Maharaj for BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, the program included Mahant Swami Maharaj launching the official website. This will also feature highlights from the Festival of Inspirations. True to their role model and guru, the website usa.akshardham.org was designed and developed entirely through countless hours of service from dedicated volunteers. Additionally, Mahant Swami Maharaj sanctified various miniature models of BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham, which will be available at the Aksharpith bookstore. These mementos allow visitors to have keepsakes of memories from their visit.

 Photo Gallery 
 Yagna Rituals (23 photos)
 Nagar Yatra (22 photos)

 At the sacred spot where the final rites of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj were performed on 17 August 2016, Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the murti-pratishtha of the newly built Pramukh Swami Maharaj Smruti Mandir on 26 January 2023 in the presence of thousands of swami and devotees from India and abroad.
 The location was selected by Pramukh Swami Maharaj himself – where he could constantly have the darshan of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in the main mandir and where the benevolent gaze of his guru, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, would constantly remain upon him.
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj built more than 1,100 mandirs around the world and enhanced the pride of Indian culture by creating Swaminarayan Akshardham mandirs in Gandhinagar, New Delhi and Robbinsville (USA). To pay homage to his monumental deeds, the architecture of his memorial mandir is also similar to the Akshardham mandirs and is built of white marble from Makrana, Rajasthan.
 The first stone of the Pramukh Swami Maharaj Smruti Mandir was laid by Mahant Swami Maharaj on 17 December 2018.  Built in the Naagar styled of mandir architecture, the Mandir is 140 feet long, 140 feet wide and 63 feet high. It is made of 7,839 stones and comprises 1 ghummat, 4 samarans, 16 ghummatis, and intricately carved pillars, domes and other elements. It is decorated with sculptures of contemporary saints and devotees of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Pramukh Swami Maharaj. In the mandir sanctum sanctorum, a marble murti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj is enshrined with Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj. The cremation spot is covered with a transparent case so that all can have darshan.
 In the morning, the Vedic mahapuja ceremony was performed by senior swamis. Then, at 11.45 a.m., the main murti-pratishtha rituals of the memorial mandir were performed by Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In the celebration assembly, speeches by sadguru swamis highlighted various aspects of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s inspiring life, works, virtues and teachings.
 Also, ‘Guinness World Records’ officially recognized the bubble wrap painting of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj created by 150 young men and women from London and displayed at Pramukh Swami Maharaj Nagar during the Shatabdi Mahotsav as a world record. The painting was 97.78 square meters (1,052 sq. ft.) consisting of 850,000 bubbles filled with 320 different colors.
 A new audio publication titled ‘Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj Jivangatha’ was inaugurated by Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In his blessings to the assembly, Mahant Swami Maharaj sang the glory of guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the Pramukh Smruti Mandir as a place of peace, faith and devotion, and blessed that the auspicious prayers of all who visit this mandir will be fulfilled.

/News/2023/Pramukh-Swami-Maharajs-102nd-.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 102nd Birthday Celebrations by the Women's Wing, North America
/News/2023/Pramukh-Swami-Maharajs-102nd-.text:
Devotees and well-wishers joyously gathered at BAPS Mandirs to celebrate the 102nd birth anniversary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The event titled “Pramukh Swami ni Amulya Bhet,” a cultural program cherishing the invaluable gifts given to society by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, took place at over 100 mandirs across North America.
 The program, organized by women, for women, incorporated unique mediums such as live presentations and performances, video montages with insightful reflections, and blessings from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and senior BAPS Swamis to commemorate the impact Pramukh Swami Maharaj had on individuals, families, and communities across the world. 
 Recounting one of the invaluable gifts in the form of mandirs, including the recently built BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Jersey, the program highlighted how Pramukh Swami Maharaj built mandirs which serve as beacons of culture, faith, and selfless service, and inspired individuals to become the best versions of themselves through guiding by example. 
 Hundreds paid their heartfelt tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj for a lifetime of memories, lessons, and happiness. As the program concluded, devotees reflected on the most cherished gift of all that Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave them: the opportunity to build Akshardham in not only North America but also in their hearts.

/News/2023/Pramukh-Vision-Conference-202.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Vision Conference (21 photos)
 BAPS Pramukh Academy, Atladara, organized the Pramukh Vision Conference 2023 at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Sankari. This seven-day conference, centered on the theme ‘Cultivating PRAMUKHness’ encouraged youths preparing for the competitive Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) exams to learn from Pramukh Swami Maharaj, walk in his footsteps, and embrace his visionary ideals for the betterment of the nation.
 More than 375 students from Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan participated in the conference. Motivational exhibitions and artistic displays adorned the mandir premises to highlight the saying ‘Shilam Param Bhushanam’ – ‘Character is the Supreme Ornament’ and inspired the attendees on the path of Pramukh Vision.
 Dedicated and experienced volunteers and swamis had meticulously prepared the program for this conference, which encompassed three key types of guidance: Pramukh Vision Guidance, Pramukh Strategy Guidance and Pramukh Subject Guidance.
 The Pramukh Strategy Guidance sessions guided the students on passing the UPSC Civil Services Examination, considered one of the toughest exams in the world. Experienced experts from SPIPA in Ahmedabad, Core IAS in Delhi, Ignited Minds IAS Academy in Delhi, Chahal Academy and many others conducted practical activities and workshops to impart strategic and technical guidance.
 During the Pramukh Subject Guidance sessions, renowned subject experts provided concise and clear guidance to students on the various compulsory and optional subjects they have to study. They shed light on the significance of each subject in the UPSC syllabus, its relevance in personal life, effective strategies for college preparation, what to focus on during studies, and recommended and non-recommended resources for each subject.
 At the heart of this conference were the impactful keynote sessions included in the Pramukh Vision Guidance.  Pramukh Swami Maharaj possessed a unique blend of qualities that not only served as guidance for students but also for officers. The central theme of the conference was ‘Cultivating PRAMUKHness.’ Each letter of the word ‘PRAMUKH’ highlighted a virtue embodied by Pramukh Swami Maharaj: ‘P’ for ‘Passionate yet Compassionate’, ‘R’ emphasized ‘Rational yet Spiritual’, ‘A’ highlighted ‘Abstinent yet Valiant’, ‘M’ focused on ‘Mindful yet Purposeful’, ‘U’ stressed on ‘Updated yet Cultured’, ‘K’ emphasized ‘Knowledgeable yet Adaptable’, and ‘H’ stood ‘Honorable yet Humble.’ Jnanvijay Swami provided guidance on these seven qualities.
 In addition, experienced and respected former and current officers and government officials guided the students on experiential knowledge, interviews and soft skills.
 The students were also guided in person by Yagnapriya Swami, Rajeshwar Swami, Bhagyasetu Swami, Jnanvatsal Swami, Purushottamcharan Swami and Atmatrupt Swami. Further, Anandswarup Swami, Jnaneshwar Swami and Brahmavihari Swami inspired the students via video conference on faith, association with the truth, and the need for spiritual strength along with reasoning and intellectual prowess in life. Thus, students received remarkable inspiration to become officers and contribute to society, culture and national service.
 The attendees participated in various activities, such as poster making, skit writing, debates, group discussions and a mock parliament. The students’ favorite session was the revision quiz held at the end of each day. On the final day of the conference, the talented youths who excelled in various competitions were felicitated.
 The contributing teachers, dignitaries and officials expressed that in this conference the students who are preparing for the UPSC are receiving clarity in just seven days, which otherwise would take up to two years. During this conference, more than 35 faculties, officers and experts guided the students through over 75 lectures in over 50 modules. The students also felt that the atmosphere was amazing, and that every topic had been explained with deep understanding and clarity.
 During the last session, an overview of the future planning for BAPS Pramukh Academy was presented. One of the key initiatives is the ‘Pramukh Vision’ application, designed to assist undergraduate students preparing for the UPSC exam. The application will provide a comprehensive range of resources.

/News/2023/Prapti-In-Our-Pocket--Kishori.t: Prapti In Our Pocket | Kishori Din, UK & Europe
/News/2023/Prapti-In-Our-Pocket--Kishori.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Kishori Din (20 photos)
 Kishori Din – a special programme for young girls aged between 13 and 21 – was held in the presence of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj on Tuesday 4 June 2023 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 A kishori began the day by recollecting the sacred pran-pratishtha (ceremonial invocation) of the panch-dhatu ‘chal murtis’ (mobile sacred images) of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj that was performed by Mahant Swami Maharaj in Nenpur, India, on 31 October 2020.
 A group of kishoris then performed a colourful dance to welcome Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj to the programme on an ornate palanquin and seated on a beautifully decorated swing.
 Two kishoris then presented a skit during which they reminisced on some of the highlights of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s current visit to the UK, and explained how everyone can reflect on the spiritual greatness of Bhagwan and the Satpurush in their daily lives.
 A kishori also elaborated on the history and significance of the murtis of Harikrishna Maharaj and Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj, before the programme concluded with a specially written medley of bhajans, performed by 30 kishoris.
 After the session finished, kishoris enjoyed the darshan of objects sanctified by Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and availed of the opportunity to take individual photographs with Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj before offering their personal devotion through garba (a traditional Indian folk dance) with other mahilas.

 The Prasad Pravesh rituals of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir and Community Centre, Canberra, ACT, was performed by Paramchintan Swami, devotees and other swamis.
 The Prasad Pravesh ceremony, performed on entering a new premise or building for the first time, included a Vedic mahapuja during which participants also prayed for peace, harmony, well-being, and righteous prosperity to prevail throughout the local community and worldwide.
 The new mandir will facilitate children and youth activities, language classes, and traditional music classes, as well as other activities and events for young and old alike to preserve Hindu traditions, heritage, and spiritual values. 
 As a place of harmony, the mandir welcomes people of all faiths to experience and understand Hindu traditions and spirituality.

/News/2023/Prasad-Pravesh-and-Shri-Nilka.t: Prasad Pravesh and Shri Nilkanth Varni Murti Pratishtha Ceremony at BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2023/Prasad-Pravesh-and-Shri-Nilka.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prasad Pravesh (85 photos)
 Shri Nilkanth Varni Pratishtha (43 photos)
 Women's Pujan Vidhi (25 photos)
 With great jubilation and excitement, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj engaged in the first of a series of inauguration ceremonies of the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, on September 30, 2023. These historic celebrations are 25 years in the making, fulfilling the inner wish of Pramukh Swami Maharaj to build a cultural landmark of Hindu art and architecture in New Jersey.
 Sadguru Pujya Swayamprakash Swami (Pujya Doctor Swami) began the program by speaking on the mahima, or the greatness, of the creation of BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham paralleled by the rich history of building BAPS mandirs. He echoed the sentiments of all present, that this divine creation was the inner wish of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and anything is possible with God’s power within our efforts.
 Upon the arrival of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, and senior swamis performed the Vedic rituals and prayers called the Prasad Pravesh ceremony. The Prasad Pravesh ceremony is usually performed upon entering a new premise or building for the first time. On this occasion, sacred soil and water were collected from 555 pilgrim places throughout India and other countries across the globe. With their inclusion in Akshardham, whoever comes here will experience the bliss of visiting India's holy places.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj journeyed through the 13 inner sanctums, called garbha gruhs, to honor various gods of the Hindu faith. On the ground level of Akshardham will house the sacred image of Nilkanth Varni. Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the consecration ceremony of the Nilkanth Varni Abhishek murti.
 Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami fondly recalled the numerous devotees who participated in the celebrations online. He conveyed that Mahant Swami Maharaj holds dear the commitment and service of the many devotees who have contributed in various ways over the years.
 In his blessings, Mahant Swami Maharaj explained that nirdosh buddhi is the gateway to Akshardham, essentially paving the way to live a higher spiritual life filled with faith and purity. He expressed that the unmatched dedication of the volunteers has left nothing undone for the completion of Akshardham. Mahant Swami Maharaj humbly shared that no words could accurately express Akshardham's grandeur, intricate designs, and utmost divinity.
 Throughout the nine-day inaugural ceremonies, Akshardham Mahotsav will celebrate the significant aspects of the Mahamandir and the universal values upon which it was constructed.

/News/2023/President-of-Suriname-Visits-.t: President of Suriname Visits Pramukh Swami Maharaj Centenary Celebrations, Ahmedabad, India
/News/2023/President-of-Suriname-Visits-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 President of Suriname Visits PSM100 Nagar (15 photos)
 President Chandrikapersad (Chan) Santokhi of Suriname visited the Pramukh Swami Maharaj Centenary Celebrations in Ahmedabad, Gujarat as part of his week-long visit to India. He was accompanied by First Lady Mellisa Santokhi-Seenacherry
 The president was welcomed and honored in traditional style by Anandswarup Swami and was guided around the Pramukh Swami Maharaj Nagar festival site by Brahmavihari Swami.
 The president also had a meeting with and was blessed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 President Santokhi stated, “This visit gave me a good feeling. This visit also gave me blessings. This visit gave me, as president, more encouragement to lead the country the way God wants and to bring prosperity to my people, to bring relief to my people, to bring peace in the hearts and the minds of my people. The meeting with His Holiness is more than meeting with a person. His presence is giving a lot of energy. He is very silent, but it is the energy he is providing. It’s coming from his heart. From Almighty God… through to my heart and my atma. I am very happy, and I will go back home with happiness.”
 Based on his visit to the festival, the president described Pramukh Swami Maharaj, “Peace is coming from his heart. And when you have peace in your heart, when you have peace in your atma, then you are a very peaceful man. From that position, he is spreading peace. And I think that peace is coming from the almighty God. He is not keeping that peace only for himself, but is spreading it to make everyone happy. ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ – to make the world happy and to bring peace everywhere. Now, we are the messengers, to bring his peace further in the world. I am taking that message of peace back home, to bring that peace to the hearts and minds of my people.”

/News/2023/Prime-Minister-Narendra-Modi-.t: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Meets BAPS Delegation During BRICS Summit, Mayfair, Johannesburg, South Africa
/News/2023/Prime-Minister-Narendra-Modi-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 PM Narendra Modi meets BAPS delegation during BRICS summit (7 photos)
 During his trip to South Africa for the annual BRICS Summit, Hon. Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, met the BAPS delegation led by Swami Brahmaviharidas. The delegation presented a 3D model, renditions, photographs and progress updates of the upcoming BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir and Cultural Complex in Johannesburg.
 Swami Brahmaviharidas explained to the prime minister how the mandir complex will serve the cultural and spiritual needs of the current and future generations, and that it will stand as a beacon of inspiration, service, and harmony for people of all faiths and backgrounds in the Rainbow Nation.
 The prime minister also appreciated the preservation of Indian culture and values by BAPS devotees over many generations and the mandir’s potential to further strengthen India-South Africa relations.
 Following the meeting, BAPS delegates shared the project details and the mandir's role in community-building with summit attendees, who expressed great admiration for this one of its kind project in Africa.

/News/2023/Promoting-Bal-Sanskars-23949..text:
Photo Gallery 
 Promoting Bal Sanskars (27 photos)
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj often said that children are the future of the world and should be raised to have values that enrich them and society. With this objective, over 2,500 parents and children took part in the special assemblies promoting bal sanskars held at homes in BAPS centres across Australia and New Zealand during July 2023. 
 Using material provided by the national team, devotees conducted the assemblies at their homes, inviting up to three families to participate. Through videos, group discussions, interactive activities and Mahant Swami Maharaj’s blessings, the assemblies guided children on respecting their parents and parents on their duties towards their children.
 Parents pledged to spend more quality time with their children in order to strengthen the parent-child bond. Additionally, parents were inspired to enrol their children in various BAPS bal-balika activities to further the development of their children's character and values.

/News/2023/Rajipo-Din-23824.aspx.t: Satpurush in Canada | Rajipo Din, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2023/Rajipo-Din-23824.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Rajipo Din (50 photos)
 On Sunday, July 2, 2023, Rajipo Din was celebrated in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto, in a wonderful program prepared by the children of BAPS. The program revolved around the idea of making God and the guru happy and earning their grace. The event commenced with a young child who presented a heartfelt incident in which His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj followed his guru, Yogiji Maharaj's wishes and made him happy. Following this senior swami of BAPS, Sadguru Tyagvallabhdas Swami acknowledged and honoured the award winners of the BAPS Gujarati classes and BAPS Satsang Exams, recognizing their dedicated efforts.
 Sadguru Pujya Tyagvallabhdas Swami then engaged in an interactive question-and-answer session with the children, delving deep into the topic of attaining the rajipo of Bhagwan and the guru. The insightful Q&A session provided valuable guidance to the young participants.
 Next, Pujya Krishnapremdas Swami delivered a captivating presentation, highlighting His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj's caring nature towards children. The talk shed light on His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj's profound care and concern for children, emphasizing their growth and well-being.
 The event took an enchanting turn with the commencement of a vibrant drama set in a magical botanical garden, where children portrayed the roles of flowers. The storyline revolved around the flowers eagerly awaiting the arrival of the "Maali" (gardener), symbolizing Mahant Swami Maharaj. Upon the arrival of Mahant Swami Maharaj, joy and excitement filled the hearts of both the flower characters and the audience.
 The drama unfolded as Mahant Swami Maharaj, portraying the role of the Maali, nurtured and cared for the flowers. He began by symbolically providing them with nourishing soil, representing removing negative influences from the children's lives. In this segment, Mahant Swami Maharaj played a game of 'whack-a-kusang,' swatting away negative company from the children's lives. He then proceeded to symbolically water the flowers. With that, he emphasized the importance of studies and provided a balanced approach of daily dedicating three hours to study, one hour to leisure, and one hour to devotion to Bhagwan.
 Lastly, Mahant Swami Maharaj enlightened the flowers on the significance of receiving sunlight, explaining the art of engaging in devotion with joy and enthusiasm. The event culminated with the performance of a lively dance performance by the children.
 Special guests attending the celebrations included: 
 The Hon. Pierre Poilievre, Leader of the Conservative Party of Canada and Leader of the Opposition
 Inspector Chirag Bhatt, York Regional Police
 Overall, Rajipo Din served as a memorable day of inspiration, spiritual guidance, and the manifestation of deep care from Mahant Swami Maharaj towards the children's wing of BAPS.

/News/2023/Rathyatra-Celebration-2023-23.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Rathyatra Celebration (19 photos)
 The Rathyatra celebration at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Kolkata, began with a short assembly explaining the significance of the Rathyatra festival.
 Thereafter, the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami, Shri Jagannathji Bhagwan, Subhadraji and Balramji were seated in a beautifully decorated rath (chariot). Pujan of these murtis was performed with the chanting of Vedic verses in the presence of local community leaders and other invited guests.
 Then, the sadhus, guests and devotees devoutly pulled the rath in a procession around the perimeter of the mandir. The rath was accompanied by children in traditional costumes. Over 500 devotees participated in the procession, while thousands more had darshan from various points inside the mandir campus. The celebration concluded with everyone joining in to perform the arti.

/News/2023/Re-inauguration-of-BAPS-Shri-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Kirtan Aradhana (31 photos)
 Cultural Program (36 photos)
 Murti-Pratistha (58 photos)
 Murti Darshan (8 photos)
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, through his unwavering commitment and extensive travels from 1974 to 2014, rejuvenated Hindu traditions and culture in North America, especially in the Midwestern United States. Furthermore, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and Pujya Swamis have enriched the growth of the Hindu-American community, visiting the region and amplifying its cultural, social, and religious undertakings.
 In the 1980s, Pramukh Swami Maharaj envisioned establishing a mandir in Cleveland, Ohio. This vision materialized in 1996 when he inaugurated the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Cleveland. This mandir transcended being merely a place of worship; it became a wellspring of inspiration for devotees and community members of all ages.
 In 2000, Pramukh Swami Maharaj reconsecrated the murtis. In 2011, then Sadguru Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the groundbreaking ceremony for a multipurpose gymnasium and additional youth classrooms. By 2013, Sadguru Pujya Tyagvallabhdas Swami inaugurated this gymnasium and classrooms, opening an expanded facility dedicated to youth activities.
 The Memorial Weekend of 2023 saw the mandir achieve another historic milestone with the Mandir Pratishtha Mahotsav, marking the inauguration of the expanded Mandir area and welcoming Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj and Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. The three-day Mahotsav festivities began with a Kirtan Aradhana program on Friday, May 26, 2023, helmed by Pujya Swamis known for their musical devotion. This musical homage not only celebrated the profound influence of the mandir on myriad lives but also invoked cherished memories of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 The Kirtan Aradhana was succeeded by an enthralling cultural program on Saturday, May 27, 2023. Testimonies, melodious tunes, vivid visuals, and enthralling stage acts by local youth illuminated the mandir's role in imparting enduring cultural values, fostering familial unity, and inspiring generations through the years.
 On Sunday, May 28, 2023, Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami conducted the Murti Pratishtha of the murtis of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj and Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj, blessing devotees to flourish spiritually. The unforgettable weekend culminated with devotees offering thal and arti.
 These celebrations united devotees, community leaders, friends, and supporters from nearby Midwest centers. Their unified participation showcased their collective joy and gratitude for this significant achievement.
 The mandir, symbolizing the spirit of service, devotion to God, and the spiritual odysseys of numerous volunteers who invested thousands of hours in its construction, promises to inspire and benefit future generations and the broader community.

/News/2023/Regional-Youth-Leadership-Con.t: Regional Youth Leadership Conferences 2023, North America
/News/2023/Regional-Youth-Leadership-Con.text:
In December 2023 and January 2024, over 4000 youth volunteers and Swamis across North America came together for regional leadership conferences in six regions.
 These annually recurring conferences serve to refresh and reinforce the mission and vision for BAPS North American youth activities. Through these conferences, volunteers representing local BAPS Mandirs are given a chance to meet their peers in neighboring cities, exchange ideas, share experiences, and gain inspiration from each other on improving within their seva (service). While new volunteers are oriented to their roles and responsibilities, experienced volunteers take a step back to reflect on the past year and learn best practices. The goal of the conference is to equip all attendees with the knowledge and tools they will need to successfully execute the upcoming year’s projects and initiatives.
 This year’s event commemorated 50 years of Satsang in North America since the first visit of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj in 1974. The theme of the Regional Leadership Conference was “Eni rite rit” - following in the footsteps of our gurus, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Attendees learned about the way the gurus had done seva and were inspired to imbibe those same methods and values into their lives.  
 Through various keynote speeches delivered by Swamis, three specific values from the lives of our gurus were discussed. The first was ahnik – their discipline and commitment in performing the prescribed daily Satsang rites and rituals, no matter how busy their day was. The second focus value was atmiyata – their ability to foster camaraderie and togetherness amongst all devotees, enabling all to unite towards a common goal. Finally, attendees learned about their dhanipanu – their unflinching sense of personal accountability and ownership in their seva.
 In addition to these values, senior volunteers also presented on several key pillars of BAPS North American youth activities, including discussing local and regional priorities for improving traditions and culture, presenting annual project goals, refreshing policies for youth activities, and focusing on mentoring priorities for the target audience.

/News/2023/Remember-The-Feeling--Kishore.t: Remember The Feeling | Kishore-Kishori Din, UK & Europe
/News/2023/Remember-The-Feeling--Kishore.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Swamishri's Puja (40 photos)
 Morning Session (20 photos)
 Evening Programme (80 photos)
 A memorable programme for youths aged 13 to 21 was held in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj on Saturday 27 May 2023 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 Kishore-Kishori Din was organised to address various contemporary issues with practical solutions from Mahant Swami Maharaj. Kishores began the event by singing kirtans during Swamishri’s puja, which were interspersed with recitals of prayerful poems especially written for the occasion.
 Swamishri blessed the attendees and spoke of the importance of the new Kishore Sevak Training (KST) initiative as a conduit to develop internally, and through which future volunteers and leaders will develop and serve society.
 During the mid-morning session, swamis provided an insight into Mahant Swami Maharaj’s daily routine of devotion and service to others. They also explained the connection Swamishri has with youths. These messages were brought to life through video and photo stories. Delegates also drew upon the wisdom of Sadguru Pujya Doctor Swami (Swayamprakashdas Swami), Sadguru Pujya Kothari Swami (Bhaktipriyadas Swami) and Sadguru Pujya Tyagvallabhdas Swami, who provided valuable guidance in response to searching questions.
 The sadguru swamis continued to enlighten the attendees during the opening segment of the evening session in which they shared their personal experiences with Yogiji Maharaj and their motivation and lasting fulfilment that continues from those moments. They also answered a series of questions related to various challenges that youths face and provided practical solutions.
 The programme then followed the life of a Nikhil – a kishore whose journey through defining moments of his life was presented through a captivating drama – which was integrated into a special and memorable evening live show titled ‘Saturday Night Satsang’ (SNS). This show was founded on the profound memories and feelings of joy from the Kishore-Kishori Din in the presence of Swamishri in 2017.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived to the SNS programme with a vibrant and traditional welcome. He was introduced to the over 1,000 youths who had gathered before him to avail of the important messages that were being conveyed, and said they were all muktas (liberated souls). Swamishri joined the panel to provide his perspectives as Nikhil continued to navigate through his dilemmas amid pressure from his peers that threatened to steer him away from a devout and studious life.
 Swamishri personally contacted Nikhil via a telephone call to provide him with advice and direction, during which he said he was Nikhil’s ‘best friend’. The final acts of the drama portrayed an emotional conversation between Nikhil and Swamishri, when Nikhil confessed his mistakes and prayed for forgiveness.
 Earlier in the day, kishores and kishoris had written letters to Swamishri conveying their own mistakes. These were penned on soluble paper and placed inside a tank of water by Swamishri and thus dissolved, marking his compassion and forgiveness.
 The evening provided a montage of unforgettable moments with Mahant Swami Maharaj, who offered specific guidance on the impacts of social media misuse, negative influences and pursuits, and enlightening ways to overcome the battle with one’s mind.
 He also expressed his innermost wishes of kishores and kishoris who pledged to strengthen their satsang through various observances and disciplines, and to follow Swamishri’s wishes.
 Kishores then played raas (a traditional Indian folk dance) with Swamishri before he revealed a final, reassuring and loving message: “You are mine and I am yours. Remember this feeling.”
 Prior to the evening, Swamishri had offered a special prayer for kishores and kishoris expressing his deep feelings of care and concern, urging them to reach out to him through their own prayers. This was shared via a video recording and inscribed in a souvenir that was given to attendees as they departed.

/News/2023/Remembrance-Sunday-Assembly-2.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Remembrance Sunday, London (24 photos)
 A special assembly to pay tribute to soldiers from India and the Commonwealth who sacrificed their lives for justice, peace and freedom was held at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Sunday 12 November 2023.
 Annually commemorated in the United Kingdom as ‘Remembrance Sunday’, this year, the poignant day coincided with the Hindu festival of Diwali, allowing an opportunity for an especially enlightening and moving tribute.
 The assembly was attended by several members of the British Army, Royal British Legion, Western Front Association, and various faith community representatives and civic leaders, including His Majesty The King’s representative in the London Borough of Brent, Deputy Lieutenant Mei Sim Lai OBE, and Lucy D’Orsi CVO QPM, Chief Constable of British Transport Police and Deputy Assistant Commissioner in the Metropolitan Police Service. 
 The evening began with children chanting the Shanti-Paath, an ancient Vedic peace prayer, as guests of various faiths and vocations came together to light the sacred lamps of enlightenment. Fittingly for Diwali, the ceremony symbolises the dispelling of darkness by light and the victory of good over evil. This was followed by a minute of silence, further invoking a profound sense of peace and solemnity, as attendees reflected on the significance of sacrifice and honour.
 Former Chair of the Western Front Association, Colin Wagstaff, shared a poetic homage to the fallen: “The valour of warriors, their courage and might; In memory’s embrace, forever shines bright…. On this Remembrance Sunday, we do declare, to cherish their memory, and show we care.”
 Captain Nandesh Patel of the British Army presented a poignant reading from the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, which resonated deeply with the gathering. “O seeker of truth, in life’s ever-turning wheel; Happiness and sorrow, like seasons, they reveal. Perceptions fleeting, they come and they depart; In this impermanence, find strength in your heart.”
 Daniel Kennelly, a volunteer manager at a local food bank, was also present on this occasion. He thanked Neasden Temple for its ongoing donation of fresh fruit and vegetables to help feed needy families in the neighbourhood.
 In his benedictory address, Yogvivekdas Swami paid tribute to the sacrifice of veterans while also thanking their families and the servicemen and women currently active around the world today. In praying for a peaceful resolution to unrest everywhere in the world, he called for a future of hope and harmony. He said, “Together, may we work towards a brighter future, where the world is free from the shadows of conflict and where our shared values shine brightly for all.”
 The assembly concluded with the solemn sound of the Last Post bugle call, a hallowed tradition evoking the sacrifice of civilians and the armed forces, inspiring attendees to strive towards a world of peace, love, harmony and understanding.

/News/2023/Sagpan-Tam-Sathe--Mahila-Din-.t: Sagpan Tam Sathe | Mahila Din, UK & Europe
/News/2023/Sagpan-Tam-Sathe--Mahila-Din-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Puja Darshan (12 photos)
 Mahila Programme (60 photos)
 The divine bond between female devotees and God and the Guru was explored through an enlightening programme of mono-acts, dramas, kirtans, presentations and dances on Saturday 13 May 2023 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 The Mahila Din programme began with a prayer offered on behalf of mahilas during Mahant Swami Maharaj’s morning puja, charting the spiritual connection that mahilas have with the Satpurush and how it evolves throughout the journey of their life.
 A series of devotional offerings were also presented to Swamishri, including an official invitation to Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj to preside over the day’s festivities.
 Later in the morning, women and children offered a grand welcome to Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj in the Mahila Din assembly, which centred around navdha bhakti (the nine ways to express devotion to God as detailed in Hindu scriptures). These were visually represented through cultural performances and devotional offerings to the murtis, which enhanced the spiritual experience for the attendees.
 The programme featured inspiring incidents from the lives of female devotees from the time of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and each of the Gunatit Gurus, revealing a powerful spiritual message. These teachings, brought to life through various mediums, explained the unbreakable bond between female devotees and the Guru, illustrating the spiritual benefits of cultivating the ideal understanding and living according to their wishes.
 Women shared cherished memories of Yogiji Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj through video presentations and a panel discussion, further reinforcing the spiritual bond they have maintained with their gurus.
 These personal contributions were also supported with examples of the international impact that mahilas have made – such as the world record bubble wrap painting in tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s centennial birth anniversary, the seva that mahilas from the UK offered during these centennial celebrations in Ahmedabad, India, as well as at the construction site of Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, USA, and the humanitarian relief work near the Polish border with Ukraine.
 These inspirational testimonies underlined the spiritual strength of women and the role that they play in building a better world.
 A video of Mahant Swami Maharaj touching a lamp that simultaneously illuminated a lamp inside the assembly hall provided a memorable finale to the event – delivering a symbolic message to the devotees that his connection with them is not confined by boundaries or physical distance.

/News/2023/Samarpanam-Tava-Sharanam--Bha.t: Samarpanam Tava Sharanam | Bhakti Din, UK & Europe
/News/2023/Samarpanam-Tava-Sharanam--Bha.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Bhakti Din (60 photos)
 Bhakti Din – a special day of devotion to Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj – was held on Tuesday 30 May, Monday 5 June and Tuesday 6 June at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, providing an opportunity for devotees to strengthen their spiritual bond with God and Guru.
 The day of devotional activities included the first tula of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj outside of India. The historic evening assembly began with kirtans explaining the spiritual benefits that are realised through devotion.
 This was further explored through an enlightening skit that depicted the importance of bhakti (devotion) through a dialogue between Naradji, a revered Hindu sage, and Uddhavji, a scholarly devotee of Shri Krishna Bhagwan. The colourful drama vividly highlighted that, amongst all the means to attain ultimate liberation, God is most pleased by heartfelt devotion.
 Sadguru Pujya Tyagvallabhdas Swami and Anandswarupdas Swami elaborated on the benevolence and compassion of God, and on the merits of devotion, explaining how a tula provides an ideal way to express one’s devotional gratitude. They also drew upon the lives of devotees who have excelled in their devotion and service to God and reflected upon the personal sacrifices and support of devotees across the UK and Europe over the decades.  
 This was further conveyed through video highlights of previous Bhakti Dins in the UK.
 As Swamishri arrived in the assembly, the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj were carried in a decorative palanquin and joyously welcomed inside the hall with vibrant dances by youths.
 Thereafter, Swamishri performed the pujan and arti of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj before offering his own devotion in the form of a tula.
 Swamishri then took his seat with Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj as swamis and devotees followed in performing a tula by placing packets of sākar (sugar crystals) on the scale pans, symbolising their sweet, heartfelt devotion to God and Guru. Devotees continued to file by for darshan of Mahant Swami Maharaj, as uplifting celebratory kirtans played, creating a devotionally charged atmosphere.

/News/2023/Sankari-Mandir-Suvarna-Mahots.t: Sankari Mandir Suvarna Mahotsav, Sankari, India
/News/2023/Sankari-Mandir-Suvarna-Mahots.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Suvarna Mahotsav (32 photos)
 Although Sankari is small remote village in South Gujarat, Swamishri visited it over 60 times. It has served as a major hub for BAPS satsang activities in the region.
 On 3 June 1971, Pramukh Swami Maharaj consecrated the first shikharbaddha mandir in Sankari. Then, in May 2001, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha in the new larger shikharbaddha mandir, built to replace the old, smaller one-spired mandir.
 From 12 to 19 November 2023, the Sankari Suvarna Mahotsav (50th Anniversary Celebrations) was held on a specially created Pramukh Swami Maharaj Nagar in the mandir campus.
 During the eight days of festivities, over 260,500 people visited and were inspired by the various exhibitions, thematic shows and presentations. The attractions included;
 Exhibition on Devotion to God and Ghar Sabha (Family Assembly).
 Sankari and Satpurush: an exhibition documenting Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s efforts to promote spirituality and noble living in the region.
 ‘Mandiram’ Light and Sound Show and Thematic Dance: Nightly presentations and performances depicting the history, glory and importance of mandirs over millennia.
 ‘Sant Param Hitkari’ film on the life, work and messages of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 ‘Hamara Bharat, Mera Bharat’ film conveying patriotic messages to the citizens of India.
 ‘Muktanand’ film, encouraging de-addiction by explaining the damaging effect of addictions on individuals and their families.
 ‘Buzo’ film showing the role of parents in moulding a child’s life, and how to show gratitude and respect to them.
 Bal Nagari – an area for children with educating and entertaining games and activities.
 Bhajan Kutirs, where men and women could privately offer devotion to God and listen to spiritual discourses.
 The Pramukh Swami Maharaj Nagar remained open from 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. and was operated by over 1,100 volunteers.
 On the evening of 19 November 2023, over 12,000 devotees attended the grand 50th anniversary celebration assembly in the presence of Pujya Bhaktipriya (Kothari) Swami.

/News/2023/Satpurush-in-Canada--Aabhar-D.t: Satpurush in Canada | Aabhar Din, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2023/Satpurush-in-Canada--Aabhar-D.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Aabhar Din (33 photos)
 On July 8, 2023, an unforgettable appreciation assembly was held at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto marking the final day of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj's month-long visit to Canada. 
 The mandir was brimming with devotees, all eagerly looking forward to one last glimpse of Mahant Swami Maharaj. As they waited, they viewed videos capturing the myriad of joyous celebrations and cherished moments from the past month spent in the company of Mahant Swami Maharaj. These visual memories were powerful reminders of the deep affection and joy that Mahant Swami Maharaj brought to their lives.
 Upon Mahant Swami Maharaj's arrival to the assembly, the room was filled with the resonance of joyful applause. Senior swamis took the opportunity to acknowledge the unwavering commitment and selfless efforts of all volunteers, whose contributions were instrumental in the success of the month-long festivities. They also expressed heartfelt gratitude towards Mahant Swami Maharaj for bringing his radiant presence to Canada and sharing his spiritual knowledge with everyone for the past month.
 A blend of mixed emotions permeated the air as the time drew near for Mahant Swami Maharaj's departure. In a last expression of devotion, a garland of rakhis was lovingly presented to Mahant Swami Maharaj by swamis on behalf of all the devotees, symbolizing the upcoming festival of Raksha Bandhan. Mahant Swami Mahraj blessed the rakhis and reminded everyone of the significance of nurturing relationships and fostering unity. 
 The visit of Mahant Swami Maharaj to Canada was an enriching experience for all fortunate to be part of it. The atmosphere of devotion, the enlightening interactions, and the outpouring of love and blessings left an enduring impact on the hearts and minds of the devotees. His visit will be cherished as a sacred chapter in devotees' spiritual journey, forever inspiring them to lead lives filled with love, compassion, and devotion.

/News/2023/Satpurush-in-Canada--Prapti-D.t: Satpurush in Canada | Prapti Din, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2023/Satpurush-in-Canada--Prapti-D.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prapti Din (53 photos)
 Prapti Din took place on June 24, 2023 at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The program commenced with youths eagerly sharing their personal experiences of feeling the profound prapti (attainment) of God and their gurus Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj who have influenced their lives in profound ways. The youths then came on stage and did a question and answer session, with Sadguru Tyagvallabhdas Swami who provided detailed and captivating insights about attaining God and guru and how to continuously maintain that feeling of happiness.
 The main highlight of the program was a thought-provoking and emotionally engaging drama. The narrative revolved around a youth facing various challenges in the world. Through the captivating storyline, the skit emphasized the significance of prapti, portraying it as the ultimate source of strength that can help individuals overcome even the most daunting circumstances. Mahant Swami Maharaj played a central role in guiding and supporting the youth, enabling him to navigate his journey and strive towards becoming the best version of himself.
 During the course of the skit, other participants also had the opportunity to come forward and express their own personal challenges to Mahant Swami Maharaj. His wise and insightful responses helped address their problems and offered practical guidance for experiencing prapti in their individual lives. The exchange between Mahant Swami Maharaj and the youth resonated deeply, providing valuable insights and inspiring the audience.
 Among the special guests in attendance during this celebration were: 
 ·       Doug Shipley, Member of Parliament for Barrie-Springwater-Oro-Medonte
 ·       Inspector David Doxey, Guelph Police Service
 ·       Sergeant Michael Davis, Guelph Police Service
 ·       Constable Jash Manani, Guelph Police Service
 To conclude the drama segment, youths gathered on stage and shared their personal experiences of prapti through heart-felt kirtans (devotional songs). This expression of prapti filled the atmosphere with a sense of profound connection to the divine, highlighting the power of devotional music as a means of deepening one's spiritual journey.
 As a grand finale, youths performed a dance which was dedicated to God and Mahant Swami Maharaj, showing their joy and gratitude to have attained them.

/News/2023/Satpurush-in-Canada--Rath-Yat.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Rath Yatra (45 photos)
 With great joy, the Hindu Festival of Chariots, known as Rath Yatra, resounded in vibrant celebration at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto on the auspicious day of June 20, 2023. The presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj elevated the atmosphere, filling it with deep devotion, melodious music, and the timeless tradition of gracefully pulling the sacred murtis on an exquisitely adorned chariot.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj began the celebrations in the Mandir, where he viewed a captivating presentation crafted by the youth of BAPS. With a touch of grace, he then manoeuvred a rath carrying Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Shri Gunatitanand Swami using a remote control. The resplendent rath was accentuated by intricate decorations, embodying the essence of the cherished Rath Yatra celebration. 
 Following his morning puja, Mahant Swami Maharaj reverently performed pujan of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Shri Gunatitanand Swami, offering thal with deep reverence. 
 As the anticipation mounted, the grand Rath Yatra procession commenced from the packed assembly hall. The procession continued through the Mandir campus, where children showcased their excitement through vibrant posters and traditional dance performances. Devotees, young and old, were mesmerized by the divine grandeur of the celebrations.
 Brimming with enthusiasm, Mahant Swami Maharaj joined the Swamis in playing the kartaal, adding divinity to the procession with his enchanting melodies. As the procession concluded, it left behind a trail of deep devotion in its wake, serving as a testament to the unbreakable bond between the divine and the devotees.

/News/2023/Satsang-Diksha-Janmotsav-2385.t: Satsang Diksha Janmotsav, Rosehill, Sydney, Australia
/News/2023/Satsang-Diksha-Janmotsav-2385.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Diksha 3rd Janmotsav (79 photos)
 Over 1,400 devotees participated in the auspicious 3rd anniversary celebrations of the Satsang Diksha shastra at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Sydney with devotion and excitement.
 In the morning, the local swamis performed the mahapuja of 500 specially prepared Satsang Diksha shastras in decorative wooden cases. The cases were sanctified by Mahant Swami Maharaj while he was in Toronto, Canada, on 29 June 2023. Mahant Swami Maharaj himself had written special blessings (in Gujarati) for these shastras: ‘The Satsang Diksha shastra is the form of Maharaj (Bhagwan Swaminarayan) and the Gunatit gurus. With this faith keep it in your ghar mandir, do darshan and offer puja.’ One shastra was given per family.
 In addition, Mahant Swami Maharaj also performed pujan of a hardbound book edition of the Satsang Diksha shastra, in which he wrote (in Gujarati): ‘When you come to the mandir for darshan always read three verses from the Satsang Diksha shastra.’
 In the evening, the grand celebration assembly to commemorate the Satsang Diksha’s 3rd anniversary began with a procession in honor of the Satsang Diksha written on copper plates, which Mahant Swami Maharaj had sanctified and performed pujan of on 28 December 2022 in Ahmedabad, India, during Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Centenary Celebrations. Thereafter, youths performed traditional dances to joyously welcome this Satsang Diksha shastra, which weighs 130 kg, to Australia.
 Swamis spoke about the glory of the Satsang Diksha shastra, how people live according to its teachings and how it has become an integral part of the lives of all devotees.
 Thereafter, 20 males and 52 females, aged between 5 to 70, who have memorized the 315 verses of the Satsang Diksha in Sanskrit were felicitated.

Over 4,200 devotees in 16 centers across Australia & New Zealand participated in the one-day shibirs themed ‘Sadhana’.
 The shibirs explored four topics: Rajipano Vichar (leading a life in accordance with the wishes and commands of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Gunatit gurus), Kartapanano Vichar (firmly believing God is the all-doer), Sankhya Vichar (realizing the temporary nature of all material things), and Mahimano Vichar (contemplating on the greatness of Bhagwan, his Gunatit Sadhu and his disciples).
 The attendees gained a deeper understanding about these four thought processes through powerful spiritual talks by swamis, group discussions, panel discussions, engaging skits, video presentations, Q&A sessions and narration of virtues by devotees. The shibirs provided spiritual understanding and practical tools to help manage daily challenges, and find peace and meaning in life by nurturing these essential thoughts that will enable spiritual progress.

/News/2023/Satsang-Siddhant-Mukhpath-Mah.t: Satsang Siddhant Mukhpath Mahotsav 2023, Gondal, India
/News/2023/Satsang-Siddhant-Mukhpath-Mah.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Siddhant Mukhpath Mahotsav (56 photos)
 The Satsang Siddhant Mukhpath Mahotsav marked the culmination of the 10th anniversary celebrations of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanskrit Mahavidyalay, Sarangpur.  In the presence of Pragat Guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj, 68 students from BAPS Swaminarayan Sanskrit Mahavidyalay, Sarangpur, and 89 Shri Somnath Sanskrit University External students participated.
 The participants received the blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj during the inauguration ceremony and were inspired by the speeches of Pujya Viveksagar Swami and Atmatrupt Swami.
 The Mukhpath Mahotsav was based on the detailed study and memorization of 3 texts: Satsang Diksha, Siddhant Karika and Swaminarayan Mahapuja. Participants engaged in various competitions such as mukhpath, written exam, oral exam, shlok (verse) explanation, shastrarth (debate), public speaking and essay writing.
 As a part of this Mukhpath Mahotsav, a two-day shibir was organized on the theme ‘We are Dedicated to Akshar-Purushottam’ a profound statement that was uttered by Shastriji Maharaj. Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Mahamahopadhyay Bhadresh Swami, Adarshjivan Swami, Atmatrupt Swami and other experienced and learned swamis delivered inspirational speeches that strengthened the faith, dedication, pride, and other values of the delegates.
 On the third day, a special assembly was conducted in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj, including a Q&A session that provided a deeper insight on the theme of the shibir from Mahant Swami Maharaj’ perspective.
 During the awards ceremony, winners received certificates and mementoes sanctified by Mahant Swami Maharaj. 
 This Mukhpath Mahotsav developed a deeper understanding of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan in the delegates.

/News/2023/Satsang-Vicharan-and-Diwali-C.t: Satsang Vicharan and Diwali Celebration, Brazil
/News/2023/Satsang-Vicharan-and-Diwali-C.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Curitiba (3 photos)
 Foz do Iguaçu (5 photos)
 Paraná River (4 photos)
 Campinas (7 photos)
 São Paulo (10 photos)
 With the blessing of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Pujya Priyasevadas Swami and Pujya Snehmunidas Swami undertook the fourth Satsang vicharan (spiritual journey) in Brazil from November 21st to 27th, 2023. Brazil, the largest country in South America with a population of 216 million, primarily speaks Portuguese and has a small Indian community. The purpose of this visit was to bolster the faith of devotees and the broader Hindu community.
 During their visit, the Swamis engaged with the local community by visiting homes and offices in Brazil and Paraguay, revitalizing satsang in cities like Curitiba, Foz do Iguaçu, Campinas, and São Paulo. Notably, it was the first time in over two decades that the Indian communities in Curitiba and Foz do Iguaçu had the opportunity to experience the presence of the Pujya Swamis.
 The key highlights included:
 Curitiba: In Curitiba, located 250 miles west of São Paulo a satsang sabha was held where Pujya Snehmunidas Swami introduced attendees to the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and discussed the strengthening of Hindu beliefs. Pujya Priyasevadas Swami provided in-depth insights into the principles of Satsang, referencing the Bhagwat Gita.
 Foz do Iguaçu: This city, situated at the tri-border area of Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina, 650 miles southwest from São Paulo hosted another satsang sabha. The event was a significant gathering for the local Hindu community, helping to spread the teachings and practices of Hinduism in a region with diverse cultural influences.
 Paraná River: On the auspicious occasion of Prabhodini Ekadashi, the Swamis performed the asthi visarjan (ceremonial immersion of ashes) of Pramukh Swami Maharaj at the Paraná River located on Brazil-Paraguay-Argentina border. This ceremony was coupled with prayers to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Mahant Swami Maharaj, invoking blessings for the entire South American continent.
 Paraguay: During their visit to Paraguay, a country neighboring Brazil, Pujya Swamis engaged in a meeting with Shri Govind Rupa Narsimha Das. In this interaction, Pujya Priyasevadas Swami shared insights into the Akshar Purushottam Upasana. Pujya Swamis expressed their appreciation for Shri Govind Rupa Narsimha Das' efforts in promoting vegetarianism. The meeting was further enriched with a session of devotion, highlighting shared spiritual harmony. Additionally, Pujya Swamis also did padharamanis at several businesses in Ciudad Del Este in Paraguay.
 Campinas: During their visit to Campinas, located 60 miles northwest of São Paulo, Pujya Swamis led a satsang sabha. The women's group of Campinas participated by offering Annakut, a traditional devotional food offering. In this gathering, Pujya Snehmunidas Swami delved into the concepts of Atma (soul) and Bhagwan's Avatar (divine incarnation). He further elucidated Ekantik Dharma, highlighting the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. En route from Campinas to São Paulo, Pujya Swamis visited the Templo de Shiva, a temple dedicated to Bhagwan Shiv.
 São Paulo: The culmination of their visit was marked by a Diwali celebration attended by approximately 120 people. Here, the Swamis emphasized the profound significance of Diwali, sharing the festival's deeper spiritual meanings and life lessons.
 These city-wise events significantly contributed to reinforcing Hindu faith and spirituality among the local and Hindu communities in these regions.

/News/2023/Satsang-at-Home--Family-Din-2.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Family Din | Satsang At Home (80 photos)
 A special evening programme focussed on innovative ways for families to spend time together and progress spiritually was held in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj on Saturday 13 May 2023 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 The Family Din evening programme, titled ‘Satsang at Home: A New Way. Swami’s Way’ explored effective ways to participate in satsang activities at home with family members. The underlying messages were delivered through engaging discourses, presentations, videos, and an interactive skit with Swamishri, with contributions from swamis as well as children, youths and seniors.
 Swamis began the assembly by addressing various challenges that families are facing today, particularly regarding the potentially harmful impact of various devices on family interactions and personal development, and their judicious use for positive family time together.  
 They further elaborated on an innovative way to re-energise satsang at home by exploring the wealth of tools and resources that are available for parents and children of all ages, through reading material, family games and online content in various languages. They particularly highlighted the Swaminarayan Bal Prakash – a monthly magazine that caters to the social, moral and spiritual needs and interests of children – as a vital publication to achieve this goal.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj was joyously welcomed to the assembly as the focal point of the programme transitioned into a drama, which began with Swamishri ‘arriving at the home of a family’ for a padhramani (home visit) with Sadguru Tyagvallabhdas Swami and other swamis.
 After the vibrant welcome, the interactive skit introduced Daily Satsang Time – a new, weekly structured plan for families to practise satsang at home through thematic daily activities, including the reading of various satsang texts and publications, the learning of scriptural passages, engaging in smruti (recalling and enjoying the divine incidents of God and the Guru), and conducting ghar sabha (family satsang assemblies at home).
 These daily initiatives were individually unveiled by Swamishri, who also provided practical guidance on how families can avail the maximum benefits of each activity, as the family members posed questions as a part of the skit. He also shared his personal experiences from performing these activities and explained that everyone can feel the presence of the Satpurush in their homes through such daily satsang time. In conclusion, Swamishri personally prayed for all families to immerse themselves in this valuable initiative and for their all-round happiness and welfare.
 The event provided thousands of families with a new, effective method of coming together daily and participating in satsang activities, as well as developing their family bonds. Mahant Swami Maharaj’s enthusiasm and interactions made the event a memorable one for the thousands who attended and watched online.
 Premvati Shah, a mother of two from Luton, shared, “This new package has been so carefully thought out and delivered. My children are already excited at exploring each new day and talking about what we can do throughout the week during ‘DST’ together. These different daily areas of focus will keep us all motivated and strengthen our bond with satsang and each other.”

/News/2023/Shaped-By-Your-Hands---Inspir.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shaped By Your Hands - Inspiring Morality (50 photos)
 An assembly at the Festival of Inspirations in Robbinsville, New Jersey, on the summer evening of July 22, 2023, explored one important value that lies at the heart of our existence. It is an invisible force that reminds us of the intrinsic worth of every individual and holds the power of influence over our lives: Morality. 
 Under the guiding theme, "Shaped by Your Hands, Inspiring Morality," the program used thought-provoking speeches, interactive skits, and guest speakers to bring to life how morality, under the wise direction of God and guru, has sculpted and inspired mankind. Speeches by senior swamis emphasized that although society has benefited from scientific invention, values and moral conduct have been instilled in people and communities through God's work. Bhagwan Swaminarayan met person to person, heart to heart, with the sole purpose of impressing upon individuals the importance of imbibing values in one's daily life. Culture, virtues, and faith paired with trust in God are sustained by self-discipline and moral conduct as life's center point. Behind Pramukh Swami Maharaj's vision for the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham was this exact intention: it will be a living, breathing space that inspires moral living in the masses.
 The assembly was a part of the Festival of Inspirations, a three-month-long event celebrating universal virtues that underpin the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham's teachings. Esteemed guests dedicated to serving society graced the event, their contributions to community building resonating with the festival's theme. The dignitaries included Dr. Aseem R. Shukla, Endowed Chair and Director of Minimally Invasive Surgery at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, and Mrs. Suhag Shukla, Executive Director and co-founder of HAF; Dr. Navin C. Mehta, a distinguished specialist in Ear, Nose, and Throat (ENT) medicine, and his wife, Mrs. Rashmi Mehta; acclaimed actor Dilip Joshi and Mrs. Jaymala Joshi; philanthropist Dr. Samir K. Sharma; Dr. Daniel Patrick Dunham, Chair of Medicine at Lenox Hill Hospital; and Mr. Palash Gupta and Mrs. Payal Gupta, driving forces behind business growth and diversity in the Delaware Asian American Business Association.
 Dilip Joshi, a renowned actor, captured the essence of the evening during his address to the audience. "By practicing a moral and disciplined way of living, one will never fall back in life. Pramukh Swami Maharaj's message was to create a moral society not only through words but through practice. Through the presence of BAPS, these values are alive and positively impacting the communities around them."
 Drawing a striking parallel between how stones pass through a rigorous process to become beautiful carvings, an insightful skit focused on the guru's similar role in shaping society. The skit highlighted how His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj skillfully uses his expert tools, moral values, and spiritual guidance to sculpt individuals into intricate masterpieces and builds Akshardham within countless souls.
 Ending with an interactive question and answer session, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj discussed that "the first step in living a moral lifestyle is to practice unity and not look at the faults of those around us. Rather, by being disciplined in your efforts to live within universal spiritual values and having faith in God, no matter your physical distance from God, you will certainly succeed in living prosperously."

 The two-day festivities to commemorate the grand Shikhar Sthapan Mahotsav of the BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Perth began on the morning of 15 September with the auspicious Mandir Prasad Pravesh ceremony. In the evening, devotees participated in the Vedic Mahapuja, after which Paramchintandas Swami addressed the assembly, inspiring all to regularly visit the mandir for darshan, personal prayers and other activities. In the evening, Brahmasmarandas Swami, other swamis and youths presented a wonderful kirtan aradhana.
 On 16 September traditional Vedic prayers and captivating cultural programs were held. Among the distinguished guests were Consulate General of India Mr. Amarjit Singh Takhi, Federal Senators Dean Smith and Fatima Payman, Members of Parliament of Australia Sam Lim (Federal Member of Tangney), Tracey Roberts (Federal Member for Pearce), Ayor Makur Chuot (Member for the North Metropolitan Region), Mayor of Joondalup Albert Jacob, Cr Christine Hamilton-Prime JP  (City of Joondalup), Honorary Consul of Kenya Amu Shah, Senior Policy Advisor on Citizenship and Multicultural Affairs Said Padshah, Acting Superintendent Cameron West and Acting Inspector John Lehran and representatives of WA Police. Their participation symbolized the harmony and unity the mandir fosters within the community. Local government representatives appreciated the magnificent achievement of building a mandir that truly belongs to the community. Devotees' heartwarming participation showcased unity and strength, underscoring the mandir's role as a unifying force.

/News/2023/Shri-Krishna-Janmashtami-Cele.t: Shri Krishna Janmashtami Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2023/Shri-Krishna-Janmashtami-Cele.text:
The auspicious Hindu festival of Shri Krishna Janmashtami was celebrated at BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs and centres around the UK and in Europe. The day consisted of a host of devotional festivities, including a ceremonial offering of food (the ‘annakut’), singing, chanting, and an arti signifying the auspicious birth. An englightening evening programme drew on the teachings and incidents of Shri Krishna Bhagwan from the Bhagwad Gita, Bhagwat Purana and Mahabharat, and illustrated how they can lead to a happy and harmonious life.

/News/2023/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Ram Navmi Celebrations 2023, North America
/News/2023/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.text:
On a day marked by the auspicious birth celebrations of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Ram, devotees flocked to BAPS Swaminarayan Mandirs throughout North America to honor the sacred lives and eternal values that they represent.
 This year's festivities, themed "Bhakta Thavu Bhagwan Na," showcased the path to becoming an ideal devotee of Bhagwan. As part of the celebrations, children and youth dedicated themselves to producing an enthralling stage show complete with classical devotional songs, dance performances, and spiritual discourses. These artistic expressions provided a window into the unwavering faith of devotees from the eras of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Ram, drawing meaningful connections to modern times.
 The engaging program transported attendees through history, highlighting the essence of true devotion and shining a light on the exemplary lives of Atmaram Darji, Dada Khachar, Sitaji, and Angad.
 The Swaminarayan Jayanti and Ram Navmi Celebration aimed to connect devotees with the lives of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Ram while inspiring faith in the divine and a life based on integrity, tolerance, and respect for all. These principles form the foundation of the many activities undertaken by BAPS volunteers and followers across the globe.  Today, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj carries the torch of this inspiring journey, guiding us to lead lives imbued with spirituality and a higher purpose.
