Photo Gallery 
 Yuvak Parayans (51 photos)
 Yuvati Parayans (24 photos)
 Thousands of yuvaks and yuvatis attended the separate three-day Yuva Parayans held at hundreds of BAPS centers throughout Gujarat, Maharashtra and other states in India.
 The parayans were based on three topics from the Satsang Diksha shastra: self-control, understanding and keeping good company. Each topic was presented by the yuvaks and yuvatis in their respective parayan assemblies through discourses, speeches, skits, discussions and videos. Videos of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s explanations of the three topics were also shown during each two-hour parayan assembly.
 The youths made special efforts to decorate the parayan locations to reflect the topics of the parayan.
 The parayans also re-inforced in the youths the need to daily read five verses from the Satsang Diksha shastra to remain aware of their duties.

/News/2023/Yuva-Shibir-Darshan-Yatra-Org.t: Yuva Shibir-Darshan Yatra Organized by BAPS Mandir, Bhavnagar, India
/News/2023/Yuva-Shibir-Darshan-Yatra-Org.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir-Darshan Yatra (38 photos)
 Over 630 yuvaks and yuvatis of Bhavnagar joined the one-week Yuva Shibir-Darshan Yatra organized to raise awareness of Sanatan Hindu Dharma among youths by the BAPS Mandir in Bhavnagar.
 The yatra took the youths to BAPS mandirs and Hindu mandirs in Bochasan, Mahelav, Chansad, Vartal, Navsari, Nasik, Pune, Tithal and other places. The youths learnt the rich and meaningful traditions and history of each place, which helped them to better understand the role and relevance of mandirs in daily life. They also visited other holy sites of Sanatan Hindu Dharma to offer prayers and devotion.
 In Nasik, a one-day shibir was held in the presence of Pujya Doctor Swami, based on the theme ‘Upasana, Niyam-Dharma and Vartan’. The shibir also featured speeches by experienced BAPS swamis, a question-answer session with Shri Dilipbhai Joshi, workshops, discussions, videos, skits and other activities to re-inforce the key messages of the shibir.

/News/2023/Yuva-Shibir-Darshan-Yatra-to-.t: Yuva Shibir-Darshan Yatra to Celebrate Silver Jubilee of BAPS Mandir, Rajkot, India
/News/2023/Yuva-Shibir-Darshan-Yatra-to-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir - Darshan Yatra (54 photos)
 Over 950 yuvaks and yuvatis of Rajkot joined the five-day Yuva Shibir-Darshan Yatra organized as part of the 25th anniversary celebrations of the BAPS Mandir in Rajkot.
 To become eligible for the yatra, the youths had to pass written and oral tests on the basics of the Sampradaya and also participate in the week-long seva, bhakti and upasana programs: helping to clean the sanskardhams in Rajkot, performing extra bhakti in the form of malas, dandvats and pradakshinas, and inspiring one friend to visit the mandir for darshan.
 The five-day 2,000 km yatra took the youths to BAPS mandirs and ancient Hindu mandirs in Bochasan, Bharuch, Navsari, Selvas, Nasik, Mumbai, Tithal and Chansad. The youths learnt the rich and meaningful traditions and history of each place, which helped them to better understand the role and relevance of mandirs in daily life. They also visited other holy sites and rivers of Sanatan Hindu Dharma to offer prayers and devotion.
 During the yatra, at seven locations, shibir sessions were held in which Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Adarshjivan Swami, Anirdesh Swami and other swamis explained the glory of Hindu mandirs. The sessions also featured workshops, discussions, videos, skits and other activities to re-inforce the glory of mandirs.

Photo Gallery 
 Antar Jagruti Parva (26 photos)
 As part of their six-month BAPS Yuva Talim Kendra (YTK) course, the 108 youths of the first batch of 2023 students undertook a week of vicharan. In groups of four each, the 108 youths, in 27 groups, visited 216 villages in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan to conduct the ‘Antar Jagruti Parva’ (Personal Awareness Campaign).
 During their one-day visits to these villages, the youths visited 3,232 homes, inspiring devotees to attend their local weekly assembly, perform daily personal puja, visit the local mandir regularly for darshan, daily read the Vachanamrut and Swamini Vato, conduct family assemblies, observe a fast on ekadashi and practice other basics of satsang.
 The youths conducted a total of 216 public assemblies, attended by over 14,435 people. Also, they held 151 children’s assemblies and 37 school assemblies, which were attended by over 6,575 children. In the evenings, the youths organized bhakti feris – devotional parades – through the towns and villages, in which around 2,355 devotees participated. The youths also inspired over 875 people to give up their addictions.
 These village visits energized not only the devotees, but also the youths to strive for greater spiritual growth.

/News/2023/Yuvak-Yuvati-Din-24135.aspx.t: Yuvak-Yuvati Din | Mahima, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2023/Yuvak-Yuvati-Din-24135.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuvak-Yuvati Din - Part 1 (23 photos)
 Yuvak-Yuvati Din - Part 2 (80 photos)
 On Thursday, September 21, 2023, youths gathered at the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, to explore the theme of "Mahima" as part of the Festival of Inspirations. This three-month celebration aims to perpetuate the timeless values championed by BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham for future generations. Yuvaks and yuvatis from North America presented a two-segment program that delved into understanding the glory of God, Guru, and devotees of God. The key message was that while money drives the world, in the spiritual community of satsang, "Mahima" serves as the fundamental currency. Furthermore, the more "Mahima" one possesses, the richer they are spiritually.
 The first part of the program was spearheaded by women who illustrated anecdotes in various ways in which other young women have drawn strength from their guru, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Inspirational anecdotes from real-life experiences told stories of women who have understood mahima to a deeper level. The anecdotes studied the life experiences of the women and how they've persevered challenges through faith.
 In the program's second segment, youths recounted profound interactions with Mahant Swami Maharaj, highlighting his love and humility. One spoke of feeling directionless after Pramukh Swami Maharaj's passing but found guidance seeing the same virtues in Mahant Swami Maharaj. Another shared his wife's story, an I.T. expert in the U.S. Army, who struggled with PTSD post her Afghanistan service. She wrote to Mahant Swami Maharaj about her battles and received a simple yet impactful response: "Make peace with your past." To this day, the woman lives by these protective words, remembering how they gave her love and hope when she needed it most.
 Through the recollection of the lasting impressions His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj left upon countless people, Pujya Anandswarupdas Swami shed light on his true glory. He said, "Mahant Swami Maharaj is an ideal swami. His actions, thoughts, and emotions are 100% pure. He emphasized that those who met Mahant Swami Maharaj experienced peace and divinity." He shared the words of various people who were fortunate to come into contact with Mahant Swami Maharaj, recalling the sense of peace and divinity that overcame them.
 Sadguru Ishwarcharandas Swami expressed the importance of maintaining one's religious duties and vows to maintain a strong understanding of this glory. Explaining how Yogiji Maharaj began the organization of youth assemblies within BAPS, he recalled how firmly Yogiji Maharaj enforced niyam-dharma, or core principles set by the Guru, in the youths at the time. Despite his strictness, the youths followed his wishes without hesitation due to the unconditional love he showered upon them, the way a mother loves her child and wants the best for them. Pramukh Swami Maharaj placed the same importance on niyam-dharma throughout his tireless travels throughout the world.
 Also present in the assembly,  Sadguru Pujya Viveksagardas Swami, who has traveled alongside Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj,  received a warm welcome from devotees upon his return to America to join in the celebrations for the Festival of Inspirations.
 Several distinguished guests, including Mayor of Piscataway Brian Wahler, were present in the assembly. In his speech to the audience, he said, "Given the fact of what's going on worldwide with disease, famine, wars, if we can preach a little more of peace, love, happiness, and spirituality, I think we'll all live a little better and longer." Mr. Sean Haney, Founder of Sphere Consultants LLC, remarked, "There is great power and impact in prayer. Not just prayer for ourselves, for courage and wisdom, but prayer for others. Here at this place among all of us together, the power and impact of service and prayer are quite evident." Tennessee State Senator Heidi Campbell complimented the program and said, "You did a beautiful job and it was an honor to hear you today. How wonderful, and I mean, full of wonder and a true sense of the word, to be here with you in this beautiful place and this temple proximate to this temple that is a physical testament to the power of community and volunteerism and generosity of spirits and testament to the power of love."
 The program continued into life experiences by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. In 1971, Pramukh Swami Maharaj traveled to countless villages to meet devotees. When Mahant Swami Maharaj asked how he could not be tired, Pramukh Swami Maharaj simply pointed out how much Yogiji Maharaj traveled. In this moment, Pramukh Swami Maharaj forgot about his own bodily pain and discomfort and thought only of his guru, Yogiji Maharaj.
 The youths then presented Mahant Swami Maharaj with various memorial items of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, asking him to share which one he gets the best memories from. Mahant Swami Maharaj immediately picked up the shoes, fondly recalling how much Pramukh Swami Maharaj walked and how much he traveled to meet countless devotees.
 In his evening blessing, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj shared wisdom that each soul is divine and experiences the bliss of God and spiritual guide. Although the spiritual guide may seem ordinary, believe him to be extraordinary. He also advised enhancing one's devotion through daily spiritual routines, emphasizing consistency, likening it to an athlete's regular practice.
 The assembly was graced by the presence of several esteemed guests, including Mayor Brian Wahler of Piscataway and his wife, Mrs. Paulette Wahler; Mr. Sean Haney, the founder of Sphere Consultants LLC and V.P. and Associate General Counsel at Jazz Pharmaceuticals; Mr. Carlos Medina, President of Robinson Aerial Services Inc and a member of the N.J. Transit Board of Directors; Mr. Luis O. De La Hoz, Chairman and Board of Director of NJHCC and V.P. of Valley Bank; Mr. Gaurang Bakshi, Watch Commander at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security; Mr. Ujwal Kumar Kasthala, a prominent Anchor and Reporter on T.V. 9 and Member of the Edison Cultural Arts Committee; Dr. Mukundbhai Thakar, President and Founder of the Indian Nursing Home Program; Mr. Jay Amin, Founder of Amin Standard; Mr. Piyush Patel, an entrepreneur; Diane Grillo, Vice President at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital, Hamilton; Ms. Joan Bercari, Vice President of Quality and Patient Safety at the same institution; Ms. Lisa Breza, its Interim Chief Administrative Officer; Ms. Nash Khan, CEO of Mercer Diagnostic Imaging; and Ms. Heidi Campbell, State of Tennessee Senator for District 20.

/News/2023/Yuvati-Talim-Kendra-Convocati.t: Yuvati Talim Kendra Convocation 2023, Randesan, India
/News/2023/Yuvati-Talim-Kendra-Convocati.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Convocation 2023 (31 photos)
 The convocation ceremony for the 11th batch of Yuvati Talim Kendra of 79 young women (yuvatis) from India, Africa and Australia was held in the presence of Hon’ble Ms. Justice Vaibhavi D. Nanavati, members of the BAPS Mahila Madhyastha Karyalaya, students of BAPS Swaminarayan Vidya Mandir and parents of the graduating yuvatis.
 The convocation assembly was themed ‘Vartan thi Pravartan’ (Your Actions Will Promote the Message). The key messages learnt by the sevikas during their four-month training were presented through an enlightening skit, a quiz and interviews of sevikas.
 Justice Nanavati presented the graduating sevikas their certificates. During her address to the assembly, she attributed her illustrious career to the influence of satsang in her life and advised the sevikas to uphold the cultural values acquired through this training until their last breath.
 Jignaba Jadeja and Divyaben Patel, members of the BAPS Mahila Madhyastha Karyalaya, provided guidance on the role of sevikas after training, and how they can contribute to satsang and society.
 Rohiniben Patel (Sanskrit Mahavidhyalaya Co-ordinator, Randesan) concluded the program with a vote of thanks.

/News/2023/baps-calgary-inauguration-240.t: Inauguration of the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Calgary, AB, Canada
/News/2023/baps-calgary-inauguration-240.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Nagar Yatra (23 photos)
 Vishwashanti Maha Yagna (67 photos)
 Murti Pratishtha by HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (24 photos)
 Murti Pratishtha (48 photos)
 Murti Pratishtha Assembly (22 photos)
 Murti Darshan (8 photos)
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Calgary, Alberta, Canada, was historically inaugurated on August 26-27, 2023. Situated in the scenic Rocky View County, its inauguration involved Vedic Hindu prayers for global peace, a cultural procession, and the significant murti pratishtha ceremony. This event was led by Swamis from the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto and senior Swamis from North America and India. Dignitaries, community leaders, and well-wishers from across the globe attended the ceremony.
 The thriving Satsang community in Calgary traces its growth to the guidance of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj. His vision brought BAPS Swamis to the city in 2000, fostering dedication among devotees. What began as simple spiritual activities in households has blossomed into large weekly gatherings with an increasing number of devotees.
 Inspired by the vision of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and blessed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the new Mandir in Calgary is poised to cater to the spiritual needs of a growing community. It will stand as a center for cultural and spiritual programs for all ages, preserving Hindu heritage. The mandir aims to welcome everyone, offering a range of activities from children's programs to language and music lessons, all while emphasizing the universal tenets of Hinduism. The mandir will also engage in humanitarian efforts to benefit the local community.
 Special guests attending the Mandir Mahotsav celebrations included: 
 -  Honourable Rajan Sawhney, Minister of Advanced Education for the Province of Alberta
 - Shri Manish, Consul General of India in Vancouver
 - Jasraj Singh Hallan, Member of Parliament for Calgary Forest Lawn
 - George Chahal, Member of Parliament for Calgary Skyview 
 - Mayor Jyoti Gondek, Mayor of the City of Calgary 
 - Sunny Samra, Deputy Mayor of Rocky View County 
 - Constable Mark Neufeld, Chief Constable, Calgary Police Service
 - Corporal Geordie Simpson, Diverse Communities Engagement Unit, Alberta, RCMP 
 Honourable Danielle Smith, Premier of Alberta, sent congratulations, saying, "Our province would not be what it is without the contributions of the BAPS Hindu community and its commitment to spirituality and social service. Alberta's diversity is one of our greatest strengths and a key pillar in building a brighter future for everyone in our province."
 Honourable Rajan Sawhney, Minister of Advanced Education for the Province of Alberta tweeted, "It was truly an honour to bring greetings on behalf of Alberta's government to the BAPS Murti Pratishtha this evening in Calgary. Thank you to Consul General Shri Manish and all the dignitaries for joining the celebration. So grateful to everyone in the community for their commitment to serving others and being role models to our youth." The Minister also shared a message saying, "I also want to take this opportunity to recognize the Mandir's dedication to sharing the richness of Hindu culture with Albertans of all backgrounds and for its commitment to promoting the ideals of service, pursuit of wisdom, and respect for all religions–values we all cherish as Albertans." 
 Muhammad Yaseen, Minister of Immigration and Multiculturalism, sent congratulations for the occasion, saying, "The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Calgary will be instrumental in promoting and preserving the culture and traditions of BAPS Hinduism in Alberta. This community is a valued contributor to the Albertan way of life, and its members' dedication to enriching and strengthening our society is exemplary. As a centre for cross-cultural sharing, this new mandir will help to foster greater understanding and mutual respect in our province." 
 George Chahal, Member of Parliament, Calgary Skyview, sent greetings for the event, saying, "For the past 100 years, BAPS has worked tirelessly to further the universal Hindu principles of equality, respect and compassion for all… Your organization and volunteers in Calgary are doing praiseworthy work in the community to unify us and build a brighter future."
 Mayor Jyoti Gondek, City of Calgary, tweeted, "Congratulations to the Hindu community in the Calgary Region on today's Murti Pratishtha at the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir. This was a volunteer led initiative & stewarded by Rocky View County Councillor Sunny Samra. What a wonderful new space for this faith community." 
 Reeve Crystal Kissel, Rocky View County said, "We applaud your dedication and commitment to preserving and promoting the rich culture and spiritual heritage of the Swaminarayan faith across Canada. The construction of this mandir is a testament to your unwavering support of the spiritual needs of your growing community and the residents of the County."

/News/2023/community-day-23829.aspx.t: BAPS Community Day: Celebrating Transformative Impact in Canada, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2023/community-day-23829.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Community Day (34 photos)
 On Sunday, June 25, 2023, the Community Day celebration took place in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto marking an important event for BAPS in Canada. The Hon. Omar Alghabra, Minister of Transport for Canada; Hon. Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario; Shri Sanjay Kumar Verma, High Commissioner of India to Canada; and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, kicked off the 50th Anniversary Celebrations of BAPS Community Service in Canada.
 The day recognized the growth of BAPS Canada over the past 50 years, the impact BAPS activities and volunteers have had while supporting the community, and the impact felt by well-wishers. The story of BAPS in Canada began in 1974 when His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj first visited the country. While there were only a handful of devotees at the time, their desire to serve their communities was strong. Over the years, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj visited Canada more than 20 times to foster the community's growth and its activities. Today, this humble beginning has evolved into a nationally recognized charitable organization, with thousands of volunteers serving individuals and families in over 25 centres across Canada.
 Videos and speeches given by the dedicated volunteers highlighted the growth of BAPS from a small community to a nation-wide organization dedicated to serving others. These presentations were followed by a panel discussion with senior volunteers from BAPS, who highlighted their experiences from participating in many of the BAPS activities.
 Following the panel discussion, senior BAPS swamis provided guidance on maintaining a positive community spirit and treating everyone with mutual respect. Their wisdom and teachings added depth and perspective to the event, emphasizing the importance of unity and seeing good in all.
 Throughout the celebration, various incidents were shared with the attendees, highlighting the inspiration and vision Pramukh Swami Maharaj provided directly to devotees and Mahant Swami Maharaj's immense admiration for the volunteers committed to serving others.
 The Community Day event was graced by many esteemed guests who recognized and appreciated the valuable contributions of BAPS volunteers to society. 
 The special guests included: 
 The Hon. Omar Alghabra, Minister of Transport for Canada
 Hon. Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario
 Shri Sanjay Kumar Verma, High Commissioner of India to Canada
 Sonia Sidhu, Member of Parliament for Brampton South
 Shafqat Ali, Member of Parliament for Brampton Centre
 Francesco Sorbara, Member of Parliament for Vaughan-Woodbridge
 Hon. Michael D. Ford, Minister of Citizenship and Multiculturalism for Ontario
 Hon. Stephen Lecce, Minister of Education for Ontario
 Hon. Nina Tangri, Associate Minister of Housing for Ontario
 Deepak Anand, Member of Provincial Parliament for Mississauga-Malton
 Rudy Cuzzetto, Member of Provincial Parliament for Mississauga-Lakeshore
 David Smith, Member of Provincial Parliament for Scarborough Centre
 Graham McGregor, Member of Provincial Parliament for Brampton North
 Aris Babikian, Member of Provincial Parliament for Scarborough-Agincourt
 Logan Kanapathi, Member of Provincial Parliament for Markham-Thornhill
 Amarjot Sandhu, Member of Provincial Parliament for Brampton West
 Sheref Sabawy, Member of Provincial Parliament for Mississauga-Erin Mills
 Mayor Neil Ellis, City of Belleville
 Councillor Vincent Crisanti, Councillor for Etobicoke North for the City of Toronto
 Councillor Josh Matlow, Councillor for Toronto-St. Paul for the City of Toronto  
 Minister Alghabra brought special greetings from the Prime Minister of Canada. Minister Algahbra, Premier Ford, and Shri Verma all spoke highly of the BAPS service to the community, acknowledging the tireless efforts of the volunteers and their unwavering commitment to making a positive impact on society.
 The Community Day celebration resonated powerfully, showcasing the impact BAPS has had on the community over the past half-century. Through captivating videos, insightful discourses, and panel discussions, the event effectively emphasized the power of selfless giving and the incredible service carried out by BAPS volunteers. The presence and support of notable guests further solidified the importance of the organization's service to the community. Community Day served as a reminder of the transformative impact that can be achieved through dedicated volunteers serving others with humility and respect.

 During the Festival of Inspirations in Robbinsville, NJ, at the site of the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham, devotees are participating in a Grand Vedic Mahayagna. The three-month-long Vedic Mahayagna is a first of its kind in the West, celebrating the public offering of a Hindu Mandir that symbolizes selfless service, peaceful coexistence, and timeless Hindu spirituality. The Mahayagna is done to invoke peace within one's life and family, as well as peace around the world. It promotes universal values of peace and harmony to inspire future generations. It stands as one of the cornerstone events of the festival. 
 The Vedic Maha-Yagna features ancient rituals designed to connect participants with the divine. This is among the oldest all-encompassing Hindu rituals aimed to inspire pure and virtuous thoughts and actions. His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, following in the footsteps of his guru HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj, has carried on the tradition of hosting grand yagnas for global peace and harmony. 
 On Sunday, June 25, 2023, in Toronto, Canada, in a traditional manner, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj ignited the auspicious flame of the yagna using the rays of the sun. This flame was then employed to commence the first yagna on July 19, 2023.
 Over a span of two-and-a-half months, until the beginning of October, the blissful chants and aura emanating from the daily sacred yagnas will bless the grounds of the Festival of Inspirations with a divine atmosphere. This historic yagna represents the longest-running yagna in the western hemisphere, offering a unique opportunity for thousands of well-wishers to offer prayers for peace, both personal and global. A special Bal-Yagna will provide a unique opportunity for children to participate in Hindu rituals that date back thousands of years.
 Those interested in participating in the Yagna event are invited to visit https://mahotsav.baps.org for more information and registration details.

/News/2024/10th-Anniversary-BAPS-Calhoun.text:

 For the past decade, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Calhoun, Georgia, has been much more than a place of worship. It has served as a cornerstone for spiritual growth, cultural preservation, and community service, welcoming individuals to connect with their heritage, deepen their faith, and contribute meaningfully to society. Through a wide range of programs, the Mandir has enriched lives, strengthened families, and fostered a vibrant, close-knit community.
 On September 21-22, 2024, the Mandir celebrated its 10th anniversary with a series of events that beautifully showcased the values it has upheld since its establishment. The weekend was filled with devotion, reflection, and cultural expression, paying tribute to the Mandir’s journey over the past decade.
 The celebrations began with a vibrant women’s cultural program brought the stories to life of women devotees who have been part of the Mandir's history. Women of all ages shared how the Mandir has impacted their lives, showcasing its profound influence on their personal and spiritual journeys. This program highlighted the significant role the Mandir plays in shaping future generations, particularly in nurturing spiritual growth among women. 
 Following the Women's cultural program, there was a special program to welcome Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj's new murtis into the Mandir with heartfelt prayers. As part of this event, many devotees also had the chance to welcome Akshar Purushottam Maharaj into their homes.
 A highlight of the anniversary was the Murti Abhishek, a sacred ritual in which the murtis (sacred images) were ceremonially bathed with sanctified substances. This ritual symbolizes the purification and renewal of devotion, reaffirming the spiritual bond between devotees and the divine. Over five swamis, including Pujya Shantmurtidas Swami, graced the occasion with their blessings, enriching the spiritual experience for all attendees.
 The Kirtan Aradhana, a devotional musical program, filled the Mandir with melodious bhajans that reflected the devotion over the past ten years. Pujya Swamis and devotees from across the region participated, creating an atmosphere of bhakti that resonated with all present.
 The grand finale was a nostalgic journey through the history of the Mandir, from its construction to its growth over the past decade. As devotees looked back on the Mandir's achievements and milestones, there was a deep sense of pride and anticipation for the future. The celebration was not just a commemoration of 10 years of devotion and service, but a hopeful glimpse into the many more years to come, filled with the same spirit of unity and dedication that has defined the Mandir since its inception.

Photo Gallery

 The 10th anniversary of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Scarborough, Ontario was celebrated with immense joy and devotion from August 31 to September 9, 2024. A variety of spiritual and cultural events marked the occasion, drawing devotees from across Ontario and other parts of Canada.
 The celebrations began on August 31 with the ‘Satsang Diksha Homatmak Yagna’—a sacred ceremony aimed at fostering personal and global harmony. Conducted by BAPS Swamis in the presence of devotees and well-wishers, the atmosphere was filled with reverence and harmony.
 Following the Yagna, a ‘Shobha Yatra’ (Cultural Procession) was held along Birchmount Road. Devotees of all ages enthusiastically joined in, with colourful floats and participants dressed in vibrant costumes. The streets were alive with energy and devotion as the procession moved forward.
 On September 1, a special Women’s Cultural Program was conducted. Through a series of traditional dances, speeches, video presentations, and a panel discussion, the event highlighted the vital role mandirs play in instilling and upholding morals and values for all generations.
 The next day, on September 2, the International Students Forum organized a cultural program, focusing on the theme ‘Mandir: A Home Away from Home’. Students and devotees from the Greater Toronto Area and Durham Region showcased skits, speeches, and presentations, expressing how the mandir has supported their holistic development and naturally became like family. The program culminated with a spirited traditional dance performance by the students.
 ‘Ganesh Chaturthi’ was celebrated on September 7 with the Ganesh Pujan ceremony performed by BAPS Swamis. That evening, the youth presented a cultural program with speeches, dances, and presentations, centred around the theme ‘My Mandir, My Home’. 
 On September 8, devotees from across Canada gathered for the consecration of the sacred image of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. The Vedic Mahapuja (prayer for world peace) led by BAPS Swamis filled the Mandir with Vedic chants and hymns, as devotees participated in the sacred rituals. The day's highlight was a cultural program titled ‘Mandir Gatha’, which shared the history and significance of the mandir through speeches, videos, presentations and traditional dance. The program honoured the contributions of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The day concluded with a stunning fireworks display.
 The 10th-anniversary celebrations concluded on September 9 with the ‘Patotsav Ritual’, a sacred ceremony commemorating the anniversary of the murti consecration. The ceremonies were performed by Swamis from the magnificent BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto and Senior Swamis of BAPS from North America in the presence of dignitaries, community leaders and well-wishers from across Canada. All together, the events provided an opportunity for devotees to mark the anniversary but more importantly reflect and take stock of the mandir’s vital role in shaping their lives.

 For the past decade, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, has served as more than just a place of worship. It has been a vital center for spiritual growth, cultural preservation, and community service, inviting individuals to connect with their heritage, deepen their faith, and contribute meaningfully to society. Through diverse programs, the Mandir has enriched lives, strengthened families, and nurtured a vibrant, close-knit community.  
 From September 13–15, 2024, the Mandir celebrated its 10th anniversary with events that embodied the values it has upheld for the past decade. The celebrations honored the Mandir’s journey, filled with devotion, reflection, and cultural expression.  
 The festivities began with a Parayan (discourse) by Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami on the significance of Shastras (Scriptures). The following day, a discourse focused on the importance of Mandirs. The second day also featured the Jal Jhilani and Ganeshji Visarjan festival, adding a festive spirit to the occasion. On the morning of the third day, the Kalash Yatra was a breathtaking spectacle as a procession of women, carrying ornate kalash on their heads, gracefully circumambulated the Mandir. Their captivating devotional dances and soul-stirring kirtans radiated vibrant energy.  
 The 10th anniversary was also marked by the Patotsav Vidhi and Abhishek, a traditional ceremony that brought peace and gratitude to all attendees. The spiritual depth of the event was enhanced by the presence of over five swamis and video blessings from Sadguru Pujya Swayamprakashdas Swami (Doctor Swami), Sadguru Pujya Tyagvallabhdas Swami, Sadguru Pujya Viveksagardas Swami, and Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami.  
 A highlight of the program was a moving stage drama depicting a family's journey to reunion, exemplifying Shri Ram's timeless values of unity, selflessness, respect, and obedience. This was followed by an energetic dance performance by the balaks and balikas.  
 The grand finale featured a nostalgic look back at the Mandir’s history, celebrating its growth from its opening to the present. As devotees reflected on its achievements and milestones, a sense of pride and hope for the future was palpable. The community was especially moved by video blessings from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, reinforcing the joy and spiritual significance of the occasion.  
 The 10th-anniversary celebration was not just a commemoration of a decade of devotion and service, but a hopeful glimpse into a future marked by the same unity and dedication that has defined the Mandir since its inception.

 Over the weekend of September 6-8, 2024, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Shawnee, Kansas, celebrated its 10th anniversary with a series of events that highlighted its role as a hub for youth development and community engagement. Devotees from across the Greater Kansas City Metropolitan area, including Missouri and Kansas, gathered alongside Pujya Swamis and well-wishers to commemorate the milestone with devotion and joy.
 The celebration began on Friday, September 6, with a parayan, where Pujya Swamis delivered spiritual discourses that inspired attendees and reinforced the Mandir’s core values. This set a reflective and uplifting tone for the weekend.
 On Saturday, September 7, a women’s cultural program in the afternoon provided a platform for women of all ages to come together and celebrate the Mandir’s impact on their lives. Entirely organized and performed by women, the program featured music, dance, and skits that took the audience on a journey through the history of the Kansas City women's wing. Later that day, a groundbreaking ceremony was also held for a new outdoor playground and plaza area that will serve as an outdoor community gathering place. The evening concluded with a captivating kirtan aradhana, as devotees from near and far performed melodious kirtans, filling the Mandir complex with a spiritual atmosphere.

In the evening, the grand finale celebration featured a historical documentary, live skits, and cultural performances. These thoughtfully curated presentations provided attendees with a deeper appreciation for the history of satsang in Kansas City while inspiring them to continue serving the community and nurturing future generations. The celebration beautifully showcased the Mandir’s lasting contributions to peace, community involvement, and spiritual connection, solidifying its role as a cherished space for devotees and well-wishers of all backgrounds.

Photo Gallery 
 Leeds, UK (40 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Leeds, has served as a cornerstone for spiritual growth, cultural preservation and community service for the past ten years, welcoming individuals to connect, deepen their faith, and contribute meaningfully to society. The Mandir has enriched lives, strengthened families, and fostered a vibrant, close-knit community.
 The 10th anniversary celebrations of the Mandir were joyously held at Leeds City Academy in the presence of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and over 250 devotees, members of the local community, and swamis from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 The event was attended by various guests and dignitaries, including Dr Manoj Joshi MBE – Deputy Lieutenant of West Yorkshire, Alex Sobel MP – Member of Parliament for Leeds Central and Headingly, Andy Rontree – Councillor for Kirkstall, and leading figures from various Hindu organisations.
 Dr Joshi spoke of the importance of the Mandir and its place within the community as well as the values it promotes, particularly of harmony amid diversity. He also highlighted the importance of the volunteers and their energy and enthusiasm in serving the community.
 Mr Sobel said that it was a “great pleasure to have the only two Hindu temples in Leeds in my constituency” and elaborated on his uplifting experiences of visiting the BAPS mandir in Leeds as well as Neasden Temple in London. He also shared that he was looking forward to supporting the Mandir and working closely with the volunteers in activities that will help the local community.
 Umang Brahmbhatt, a leading BAPS volunteer in Leeds, added, “It is so encouraging to see how our mandir has become such an integral part of the local community over the last decade. Our heartfelt appreciation goes to everyone for all their help and support, and we look forward to serving the community for many more years to come.”
 The 10th anniversary celebrations were not only a commemoration of a decade of devotion and service, but also a glimpse into a future marked by the same faith, harmony and dedication that has defined the Mandir since its inception.

 Satsang activities in Leeds  began in the 1980s with a small group of dedicated devotees. In 1990, His Holiness Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj graced Leeds.
 Over the years, a property was acquired, and a mandir was consecrated by Sadguru Pujya Bhaktipriya Swami (Pujya Kothari Swami) on Saturday 30 August 2014.
 The community in Leeds continued to expand steadily to better cater for worshippers.
 The tenth anniversary of the Mandir was celebrated on Sunday 1 September 2024, in the presence of swamis from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 The assembly began with a traditional Vedic mahapuja ceremony during which swamis and attendees offered prayers for peace and harmony to prevail in the local community and across the world.
 A video presentation charting the profound impact of the Mandir in the local community since its opening rekindled treasured memories.
 Swamis discoursed on the positive values that a mandir promotes in individuals as well as the wider society. They also explained how spirituality learned from mandirs guides us to grow personally, within a family, and as a community.
 Lead volunteer at the Mandir, Ashish Patel, shared, “It is so encouraging to see how our Mandir has become an integral part of the local community over the last decade and I would like to thank everyone for all their help and support. We look forward to serving the community for many more years to come.”

Over ten swamis, including Pujya Shantmurtidas Swami, graced the occasion with their blessings, enriching the spiritual experience for all attendees.
 The grand finale was a nostalgic journey through the history of the Mandir, from its construction to its growth over the past decade. As devotees looked back on the Mandir's achievements and milestones, there was a deep sense of pride and anticipation for the future. The celebration was not just a commemoration of 10 years of devotion and service, but a hopeful glimpse into the many more years to come, filled with the same spirit of unity and dedication that has defined the Mandir since its inception.

/News/2024/10th-anniversary-robbinsville.t: Celebrating 10 Years of Devotion and Service at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2024/10th-anniversary-robbinsville.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Kirtan Aradhana (30 photos)
 Parivarik Ekta Mahapuja (49 photos)
 Annakut & 10th Anniversary Assembly (68 photos)
 Patotsav (78 photos)
 Grand Finale (79 photos)
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in New Jersey, inaugurated in 2014 by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, has completed a decade of fostering unity, community, and devotion. Often referred to as New Jersey's "marble marvel," this mandir has become a prominent cultural and spiritual hub, welcoming thousands of worshippers and visitors and offering them a sanctuary of peace and fulfillment. Over the past ten years, the mandir has stood as a beacon of spirituality, faith, and harmony, hosting numerous spiritual, cultural, and community programs. To commemorate its 10th anniversary, a series of vibrant and enriching activities were organized, reflecting the mandir's ongoing mission to foster peace, universal values, and spiritual connection for generations to come.
 Kirtan Aradhana
 On July 16, 2024, devotees and visitors gathered to enjoy a live performance of kirtans in front of Tapomurti Nilkanth Varni. This day, Ashadh Sud 10 in the lunar calendar, marks the departure of Nilkanth Varni Maharaj from Ayodhya as he embarked on his spiritual journey across India to enlighten thousands of aspirants. The event also commemorated the anniversary of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj attending a special kirtan-bhakti program at the same place the previous year.
 This musical tribute highlighted the profound influence of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the gurus on the lives of countless devotees worldwide. Children and devotees from nearby centers also participated, offering their devotion during the event.
 Parivarik Ekta Mahapuja
 On July 27, 2024, the 10th anniversary celebration continued with a special Parivarik Ekta Mahapuja, themed "My Mandir, My Home." Parivarik Ekta, meaning ‘Family Unity,’ emphasizes harmony, mutual respect, and togetherness within families.
 This special mahapuja focused on strengthening family bonds and fostering collective spiritual growth. Children of BAPS conducted the entire puja, having specially learned the Vedic mantras for the rituals. Recorded blessings from Sadguru Pujya Kothari Swami, Sadguru Pujya Doctor Swami, and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj were shared with the participants.
 Volunteer Assembly
 On August 16, 2024, a special assembly for volunteers was held to celebrate the remarkable contributions of BAPS volunteers from Robbinsville, New Jersey. The event honored their dedication, devotion, and sacrifices over the years. Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami highlighted their service and reminded attendees of the importance of humility in maintaining the true purpose of service, encouraging personal growth.
 Annakut & 10th Anniversary Assembly
 As part of the 10-year celebrations, devotees and visitors enjoyed the darshan of the Annakut lovingly prepared, artistically arranged, and devoutly offered to the sacred images of God. The offering included traditional Indian delicacies and beautifully decorated cakes.
 On August 17, 2024, devotees from New Jersey, New York, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Maryland, Virginia, and West Virginia took part in a special celebration to commemorate Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s historic visit to Robbinsville in 2014. The event reflected on his immense efforts to travel to America at age 92. Devotees recalled the mandir opening rituals and devotees who gathered to experience his divine presence. Many expressed gratitude for how he fulfilled their wishes despite his age.
 Pujya Nilkanthsevadas Swami shared Swamishri’s enthusiasm for BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Robbinsville, highlighting what makes it special. In conclusion, Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami spoke about the purpose of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s visit: bringing people closer to God by nurturing his qualities within us. He urged everyone to remember Swamishri’s guidance to inspire spiritual growth.
 The evening assembly included special guests such as Ambassador Dr. Mohamed Al-Hassan, Permanent Representative of Oman to the United Nations, who praised the art and culture of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir and BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham.  Former Indian MP and journalist Mr. Tarun Vijay also spoke, sharing his reflections on Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s selfless service and experiences in Robbinsville.
 Patotsav
 On the morning of August 19, 2024 (Shravan Sud 15), the anniversary day according to the Hindu calendar, the key ritual of the patotsav (anniversary celebration) was the Murti Abhishek. In this sacred ceremony, the murtis (sacred images) were ceremonially bathed with sanctified substances, symbolizing purification and the renewal of devotion, and reaffirming the spiritual bond between devotees and the divine. The ceremony took place in the presence of  Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami, Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami and other swamis from across the region. Additionally, the first anniversary of Akshardham was celebrated with a special ritual. Following the morning patotsav rituals, a special assembly honored families in the Northeast region with members who have been initiated as swamis. Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami conveyed gratitude on behalf of Mahant Swami Maharaj and highlighted the services performed by these swamis.
 In the evening, a patotsav assembly brought together devotees from New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware to commemorate Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visits to Robbinsville in 2017 and 2023, celebrating the bliss he bestowed upon devotees and the gift of Akshardham. Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami and Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami spoke on the spiritual importance of building Akshardham within oneself. Special guests, including Assemblyman Herbert Conaway and State Senator Vin Gopal, expressed their appreciation for the mandir’s impact and presented a declaration recognizing BAPS’ support for the community.
 10th Anniversary Grand Finale
 On September 29, 2024, a palkhi yatra of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, led by women, took place in the afternoon. In the evening, the grand finale program titled “My Mandir, My Home” illustrated how different generations find a sense of belonging through their experiences at the mandir. Children and teenagers shared the values they learned, while young adults spoke about gaining discipline and balance through the mandir’s programs. Adults and seniors expressed how the mandir reinforced their faith and resilience. Volunteers appreciated the opportunities to serve and build meaningful connections within the diverse community.
 Pujya Yogananddas Swami concluded by explaining the mandir's purpose—to bring people closer to God and develop divine qualities by recognizing divinity in everyone. Community leaders and officials visited throughout the day, highlighting the mandir's role as a cornerstone of cultural and spiritual life.
 Representatives from various organizations attended the event, along with officials such as Councilman Justin Musella and Mercer County Executive Dan Benson. Benson shared his appreciation for BAPS' contributions, quoting an African proverb: "If you want to go fast, go alone. But if you want to go far, go together." He presented a proclamation to honor the mandir's ongoing efforts.

 20th Anniversary Celebrations (28 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Southend-on-Sea celebrated its 20th anniversary with a joyous three-day festival, which saw more than 600 people participate.
 Friday 31 May 2024 featured a special evening of devotional musical, which was thoroughly enjoyed by the gathering and set the scene for the weekend’s festivities.
 Saturday 1 June 2024, the main day of the celebrations, hosted a colourful cultural programme. Hundreds enjoyed the devotional singing, dramas, multimedia presentations and inspiring talks from learned swamis and members of the congregation as they recollected key moments and memories from the last 20 years of the Mandir.
 On Sunday 2 June 2024, a special prayer ceremony marked the momentous occasion of the 20th annniversary. Worshippers as well as community members of all ages and backgrounds from across Essex gathered at the Mandir to offer their prayers for peace and harmony.
 Devotees also reminisced the auspicious day in 2004 when His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, creator of the internationally acclaimed Neasden Temple, performed the consecration ceremony of the murtis for the then new mandir in Southend-on-Sea.
 Hiral Patel, one of the volunteers at the Mandir, shared, “It’s been wonderful coming together over these three days to acknowledge all the memories made over the past 20 years. It really reinforced the vital role of mandirs for our spiritual development, to preserve traditions, and to unite family, friends and communities as a whole. Here’s to many more wonderful decades ahead!”
 The Mandir is the heart of the Hindu community in the East of England and has hosted weekly gatherings since it opened in 2004. Through faith, spirituality and universal values, the Mandir has helped elevate the lives of numerous individuals and families over the years.

 Over the weekend of August 9-13, 2024, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Houston, Texas, marked its 20th anniversary with a series of vibrant celebrations that truly embodied the spirit of community and devotion. The festivities drew thousands from across Texas, the country, and even the globe, transforming the mandir into a bustling hub of cultural and spiritual activity.
 On Friday, August 9th, the celebrations began with inauguration of the new Cultural Center followed by  a kirtan aradhana—a captivating musical event where talented swamis and devotees from near and far joined forces. Their harmonious blend of classical singing and a diverse array of instruments, ranging from traditional Indian drums to modern electric guitars, filled the air with melodies that resonated deeply with the audience.
 Saturday, August 10th, began with a symbolic procession of devotees carrying kalash (ceremonial pots) atop their heads, marking the start of the weekend’s auspicious events. This was followed by a mahapuja, a Vedic ceremony conducted by swamis, further deepening the spiritual experience for all in attendance.
 The evening’s grand celebration was the highlight of the weekend, held in the newly inaugurated Cultural Center. The program focused on dharma (righteousness), gnan (knowledge), vairagya (detachment), and bhakti (devotion). Attendees were inspired by insightful discourses from senior swamis, and the night culminated in a vibrant dance performance by youth devotees, whose months of dedication and practice culminated in a show of cultural pride and unity.
 On Sunday, August 11th, under the theme "Celebrating Community," the mandir’s campus was alive with the vibrant colors of saris and traditional outfits as thousands of women from across Texas and neighboring states gathered for a morning cultural program hosted by the women’s wing. With participants ranging in age from 2 to 50, the program highlighted the unity and spirit of the community through various performances, each echoing the event's theme, "Yeh Mandir Mera." Various programs throughout the day were graced by several proclamations, including from the Governor of Texas, state representatives, Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher, Congressman Pete Sessions, Congressman Randy Weber, and Fort Bend County Judge KP George, all acknowledging the mandir’s significant role in fostering community ties and cultural preservation.
 The weekend’s festivities culminated in a sentimental gathering on Tuesday, August 13th, dedicated to expressing gratitude to His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the creator of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the current inspirer. Devotees and attendees came together to honor their enduring legacy and the spiritual guidance that continues to inspire and uplift the community.
 Throughout the weekend, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Houston, welcomed a diverse array of community leaders and officials, each representing the rich tapestry of support the mandir has woven over the past two decades. Their collective presence underscored the mandir’s role as a cornerstone of cultural and spiritual life, not just for the local Hindu community, but for all those who cherish unity, devotion, and service.
 This sentiment was highlighted when Congressman Randy Weber addressed the assembly, stating, “At times when division seems to dominate the headlines, the BAPS community reminds us of the power of unity and service. … This new cultural complex is more than just a building; it is a beacon of hope and a hub for fostering understanding and respect.”
 As the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Houston, celebrates its 20th year, it remains committed to continuing its mission of fostering peace, fulfillment, and spiritual connection for generations to come.

 On 9 May 2004, the town of Luton was blessed with a permanent spiritual home when His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir – the last BAPS mandir in UK & Europe that he personally consecrated with the murti pratishtha ceremony.
 More than two decades later, on 23 June 2024, a grand festival marking the 20th anniversary of the Mandir was celebrated. The event was graced by the presence of Gnaneshwardas Swami, a senior swami of BAPS visiting from India. 
 The celebrations began with a Vedic mahapuja, during which families offered prayers and gratitude for the Mandir. Following this, Gnaneshwardas Swami performed the sthapan vidhi of the murtis of Shri Sita-Rama Bhagwan and Shri Parvati-Shankar Bhagwan (which had been originally consecrated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj for Manchester several years ago), marking another notable chapter in the history of Luton Mandir. A grand annakut was also devoutly offered in celebration of the pratishtha and patotsav occasion.
 An insightful cultural programme, titled ‘Echoes of Devotion,’ followed the pratishtha ceremony. It highlighted the personal efforts of the Satpurush in nurturing Satsang values in Luton ever since His Holiness Yogiji Maharaj’s visit in 1970. 
 Local devotees shared moving accounts of their personal interactions with Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and how his loving care and compassion supported them through significant life challenges. Paratpardas Swami and Vibhishan Bhagat, formerly of Luton, then shared how Mahant Swami Maharaj has shaped their lives and inspired them to renounce worldly pleasures for a life dedicated to devotion and service.
 Addressing the assembly of over 600 devotees, Gnaneshwardas Swami spoke about the importance of a mandir and how the mandir has nurtured Satsang values in Luton for many families. He then read out a letter from Mahant Swami Maharaj addressed to the BAPS Satsang fellowship in Luton, in which Swamishri commended the enthusiasm of the devotees and blessed that Satsang will continue to flourish in the area.
 The High Sheriff of Bedfordshire, Bhavesh Shah, was also in attendance at the event to present the ‘Certification of Appreciation’ to BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Luton, in recognition of its valuable services to the community. 
 The climax of the programme was a vibrant cultural dance delivered by children of BAPS, with a special reference to mandirs.
 Hetvi Somani, a young volunteer who helped plan and deliver the event, explained, “I wasn’t around when the Mandir opened, but I can truly say what a positive impact it has had on my life, including my studies, over these few years that I’ve started attending, and today’s celebrations were a perfect example – it’s all about love for God, serving others selflessly, and fostering cultural values and community responsibility.”

/News/2024/20th-Anniversary-Celebrations.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Abhishek & Patotsav (19 photos)
 Women's Cultural Program (30 photos)
 Kirtan Aradhana (9 photos)
 20th Anniversary Cultural Program (16 photos)
 For two decades, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Bartlett, Illinois, has stood as a beacon of spiritual enrichment, cultural preservation, and community service. Since its establishment, the Mandir has been a sanctuary for individuals seeking to connect with their heritage, deepen their faith, and contribute to the community. Through a variety of programs and activities, the Mandir has made a lasting impact on individuals and families, fostering a strong sense of community.
 From August 8-11, 2024, the Mandir celebrated its 20th anniversary with a series of events that highlighted the values it has championed over the years. The celebrations were a heartfelt homage to the Mandir’s journey, filled with devotion, reflection, and cultural expression.
 The festivities commenced on August 8th with the Patotsav Vidhi and Abhishek, a traditional ceremony that brought peace and gratitude to all attendees. The presence of swamis, including Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, Pujya Priyasevadas Swami, and Pujya Vivekmurtidas Swami, added spiritual depth to the occasion, enriching the experience with their blessings and guidance.
 On August 10th, the women celebrated their deeply-rooted stories and experiences through a vibrant cultural program, showcasing the profound impact on their lives. Women of all ages highlighted how the Mandir has provided them with spiritual guidance, cultural identity, and community support. They shared various incidents from their lives, illustrating how the Mandir provided a sense of community and support. This program served as a powerful testament to the Mandir’s enduring influence in shaping future generations, as their experiences illuminated the significance of this spiritual community in their lives. Following this, the Kirtan Aradhana filled the Mandir with devotional songs that celebrated the glory and profound impact of such mandirs. The positive effects of music on the soul were evident, as the kirtans uplifted spirits and deepened the sense of devotion among all present.
 The grand finale on August 11th was a nostalgic journey through the history of the Mandir, from its vision to its construction, and subsequently its growth over the past two decades. As devotees reflected on the Mandir’s progress and the milestones achieved, there was a profound sense of pride and anticipation for the future. The youth, who had practiced for months, showcased their appreciation for what the Mandir has done for them through this special cultural program. This program seamlessly covered various topics, including culture and values, service and sacrifice, faith and devotion, and unity and fraternity. Each segment flowed into the next, creating a cohesive narrative that highlighted the Mandir’s impact on the community. The celebration was not just a look back at 20 years of devotion and community but a hopeful glance at the hundreds of years yet to come, filled with the same spirit of unity and service that has defined the Mandir since its inception.

/News/2024/20th-Patotsav-Celebrations-BA.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Patotsav Celebrations (71 photos)
 In January 2004, H.H Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated BAPS Shri Swaminaryan Mandir, Secunderabad.
 To mark the 20th anniversary of this momentous occasion, celebrations were held at the mandir from 1 to 13 January 2024 in the presence of Pujya Bhaktipriya Swami (Kothari Swami), and other senior swamis from throughout India. The main events organized included:
 2 January
 A felicitation assembly honoring the dignitaries who have actively render voluntary services to society.
 3 January
 A fun-filled carnival games zone for children. The evening assembly enlightened the balaks and balikas on the exemplary virtues of the children of Akshardham.
 4 January
 A melodious kirtan aradhana by swamis and youths.
 5 January
 Women’s assembly on the theme of ‘Women Empowerment Through Mandir & Satsang’ that included folk dances, skits and inspiring speeches.
 7 January
 In the morning, seated around 64 yagna kunds, 700 yajman couples participated in Vedic Mahayagna for World Peace.
 In the evening, Atmatrupt Swami addressed the assembly on the topic ‘Man ko sthir kare – Mandir’, highlighting the importance of mandirs in daily life.
 8–10 January
 Senior swamis presented enlightening discourses to strengthen faith, dedication, devotion and other values.
 12 January
 The festivities concluded with the celebration of 20th patotsav of the mandir, and consecration of the murtis of Bhagwan Ram-Sitaji and Bhagwan Shiv-Parvatiji.
 In celebration assembly, swamis shared their spiritual experiences and a video compilation of Pramukh Swami Maharaj at the Mandir was shown.

/News/2024/25th-Patotsav-Celebration-BAP.text:
Photo Gallery 
 25th Patotsav Celebration (79 photos)
 In the morning, over 1,100 devotees took part in the 25th patotsav celebration of the BAPS Mandir in Nairobi. First, the Vedic pujan and abhishek of all the consecrated murtis were performed. Thereafter, devotees participated in the celebratory mahapuja. They also performed abhishek of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj.
 Then, after speeches by Tyagvatsal Swami and Priyavrat Swami, a grand annakut was devoutly offered to the murtis. Thereafter, the 25th patotsav arti was performed.
 The evening Sunday assembly, titled ‘Nairobi - Satpurush na Sannidhyama’, took the devotees on a nostalgic journey of Satsang in Nairobi through video clips of Yogiji Maharaj, interviews of senior devotees, memorable events, speeches, a skit and an energetic dance performance by kishores.

Photo Gallery 
 Anniversary Celebrations (36 photos)
 Based on the theme ‘Jivan Dhanya Bane Che’, the 40th anniversary celebration of the BAPS Swaminarayan Chhatralay, Vadodara, marked four decades of nurturing students in education, values and personality development. The evening celebration assembly, in the esteemed presence of Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami, featured a drama, a lyrical dance, mimes, a shadow play, and insightful interviews highlighting the event theme.
 Students who had achieved academic and extracurricular excellence throughout the year were honored with trophies and certificates. Distinguished guests of honor, Dr. Vijay Srivastava, Vice Chancellor of M.S. University, and Dr. Devanshu Patel, President of Parul University, also shared their insights and emphasized the crucial roles on education, values, and personal development in shaping individuals and society.
 Along with more than 7,000 devotees and dignitaries from various institutions, hundreds of alumni attended the event with their families – a testament to the hostel’s enduring appeal.

/News/2024/91st-Janma-Jayanti-Celebratio.t: 91st Janma Jayanti Celebration of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, Mumbai, India
/News/2024/91st-Janma-Jayanti-Celebratio.text:
3:51:45
 91st Janma Jayanti Celebration of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj
 18:32
 Guruhari Darshan, 26 Sep 2024
 Photo Gallery 
 91st Janma Jayanti Celebration (101 photos)
 On 26 September 2024, the 91st birthday celebration of guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj was celebrated with profound devotion and grandeur at NESCO, Goregaon, Mumbai. The spiritual programme commenced in the afternoon at 5 p.m.
 Devotees from around the world had gathered to offer their heartfelt tributes to Mahant Swami Maharaj. More than 400 sadhus and thousands of devotees from across the globe were present to witness this divine event.
 The celebrations commenced with the devotional singing of prayers, which was followed by discourses and speeches by senior swamis.
 In his address, Jnannayan Swami highlighted the extraordinary works of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and how his divine presence continues to manifest today through his Gunatit sadhu. He stated that the birth anniversary of Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj is a sacred opportunity to experience the presence of God. 
 Narayanmuni Swami emphasized the unparalleled devotion of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, while Bhagvatsetu Swami spoke about the unwavering devotion and discipline inherent in Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Pujya Viveksagar Swami elaborated upon Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s divine love on the devotees and all of humanity. Thereafter, Adarshjivan Swami reflected on the infinite love and affection of Mahant Swami Maharaj for all.
 Brahmavihari Swami and Atmatrupt Swami highlighted the selfless services and charitable works of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj, respectively. Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami and Pujya Anandswarup Swami discoursed on the humility of both these spiritual leaders.
 In his address, Pujya Bhaktipriya Swami explained about how Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj have dedicated their entire lives for the welfare and uplift of humanity.
 Special guest, Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra, opined, "Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj is a global spiritual leader of immense stature. I consider myself extremely fortunate to be present here and receive Mahant Swamiji’s blessings. BAPS spreads our culture in a constructive and positive manner across the world. Our temple in Abu Dhabi is a clear testament of this. I am confident that BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha will play a vital role in spreading peace and happiness on the world stage."
 Dignitaries present on the stage included Shri Mangal Prabhat Lodha, Minister of Tourism, Skills, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Govt of Maharashtra, and Mr. Kishna Patel, Chief Managing Director, NESCO Ltd.
 The celebrations concluded with Mahant Swami Maharaj’s blessings, “The ultimate goal of mankind is to understand the true glory of God, engage in his devotion, and follow his divine commands.’
 The senior sadhus of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha offered flower garlands to honour Mahant Swami Maharaj, while youths and children performed a thrilling traditional dance. The assembly concluded with the performance of mass arti by 30,000 devotees. The event concluded with the mantra-pushpanjali ritual to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Thousands of devotees witnessed the enlightening celebration through a live broadcast on live.baps.org and Aastha Bhajan channel.

/News/2024/A-Bipartisan-Congressional-Re.t: A Bipartisan Congressional Resolution Marks the 50th Anniversary of BAPS, North America
/News/2024/A-Bipartisan-Congressional-Re.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS 50th Anniversary Proclamations (11 photos)
 In 2024, BAPS marks a key milestone commemorating half a century in North America. This landmark occasion is a testament to the enduring legacy of the BAPS community and its profound impact on the spiritual and cultural fabric of the continent. Since the inauguration of the first BAPS Mandir in 1974 in Flushing, New York, the organization has grown to encompass 116 Mandirs across North America.
 On July 30, 2024, Congressman Thomas Suozzi (NY-3) and Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40) introduced a bipartisan House Resolution, H.Res.1394, in the 118th Congress recognizing this achievement. The resolution highlights the democratic partnership between the United States and India as "grounded in shared principles of democracy, religious pluralism, human rights, freedom, and the rule of law." BAPS is committed to these principles and recognizes the importance of fostering these values in its initiatives and collaborations.
 To honor this significant milestone, proclamations and commendations have been received from a multitude of distinguished cities and officials across the United States. The following have declared August 4, 2024, as BAPS Day:
 Alabama: Alabama House of Representatives, Alabama Senate, City of Dothan, City of Hoover, City of Montgomery, City of Opelika
 California: California State Assembly, City of Irvine, City of San Jose
 Florida: Hillsborough County, City of Tampa
 Kentucky: State of Kentucky, Kentucky House of Representatives
 Indiana: City of Greenwood
 Maryland: State of Maryland, Prince George’s County
 Massachusetts: City of Lowell
 Mississippi: State of Mississippi, City of Jackson, City of Flowood, City of Vicksburg
 Missouri: City of St. Louis
 New Jersey: Township of Edison
 New York: Town of Colonie
 North Carolina: North Carolina House of Representatives, Wake County, Town of Cary
 Pennsylvania: Hatfield Township
 Tennessee: Tennessee Senate, Tennessee House of Representatives, Town of Collierville, City of Germantown, Town of Arlington, City of Murfreesboro, City of Clarksville, City of Columbia, City of Franklin, City of Memphis, Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County, City of Bartlett
 Texas: Dallas County, City of Austin, City of Carrollton, City of Irving, City of San Antonio, City of Sugar Land, Town of Prosper, City of Round Rock
 Virginia: County of Fairfax
 Washington: City of Bellevue  
 Other acknowledgments include:
 Alabama: City of Birmingham
 Florida: Commendation by Tampa City Council
 Illinois: Proclamation from Illinois Senate
 Kentucky: City of Bowling Green declaring July 31, 2024 as BAPS Day
 Maryland: Citation by Governor Wes Moore
 Massachusetts: Citation by Massachusetts State Senate
 Minnesota: Certificate of Recognition by Governor Tim Walz and Lt. Governor Peggy Flanagan
 Mississippi: Resolution by Governor Tate Reeves
 New York: Resolutions by New York State Senate and Assembly
 Tennessee: Congratulations Letter from Senator Marsha Blackburn, Proclamation from the City of Brentwood, Proclamation from the City of Hendersonville
 Texas: Recognition by Governor Greg Abbott, Recognition by the City of Frisco
 These accolades reflect the broad and deep appreciation for BAPS's contributions to the community, celebrating not only the architectural and cultural achievements of the organization but also its role in promoting spiritual growth and community service.
 Girish Patel reflects on this milestone, stating, “As a volunteer with BAPS for over 30 years, I've witnessed firsthand the incredible impact our community has had across the nation. The resolution introduced in Congress recognizing our 50-year journey in North America is not just an honor for our organization, but a testament to the dedication and hard work of our Gurus Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj, as well as every volunteer and well-wisher. We are grateful for this recognition that reaffirms our commitment to preserving our cultural heritage and serving society."
 The 50th anniversary speaks to the vision and tireless efforts of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who have inspired the creation of landmarks of Hindu culture across the world. For more than 50 years, they have traveled throughout North America inspiring the values of selfless service, faith, and harmony. BAPS aims to unite communities around these universal values and foster positive change, a legacy to be carried forward for generations to come.

/News/2024/Adhiveshan-2024-26622.aspx.text:
After two months of preparation, a total of 454 balaks, 499 balikas, 158 kishores and 144 kishoris from across Australia (Adelaide, Brisbane Mandir, Brisbane North, Canberra, Darwin, Geelong, Gold Coast, Griffith, Melbourne East, Melbourne Mandir, Melbourne South, Melbourne West, Perth Mandir, Perth South, Shepparton, Sunshine Coast, Sydney) and New Zealand (Auckland, Christchurch, Hamilton, Wellington) participated in the many local and national competitions as part of the ANZ Bal-Kishore Adhiveshans.
 The local competitions, conducted in-person and marked by judges from the local centre, were based on memorizing and understanding key shlokas and cultural concepts. Through the ‘questions and answers’ activities, the participants gained an insight into core Hindu beliefs. The ‘debating’ and ‘interview’ activities helped to improve their communication skills. Participation in the ‘story telling’ and ‘explaining mahima’ activities created a deeper connection with Bhagwan Swaminarayan and guru Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Around 400 youngsters participated in the national competitions. The competitions were split into two categories, written and visual. Writing activities like ‘comic strips’ or ‘poetry’ encouraged participants to improve their literary techniques. Visual activities like ‘photography’ or ‘graphic design’ enabled them to explore their creative interests and hobbies. The participants submitted their entries prior to the in-person local adhiveshans. These were then graded by judges from various centers across the pacific selected based on their expertize.
 Through the various challenges, the adhiveshans gave the children, teenagers and youths an opportunity to deepen their knowledge of culture, enhance their communication skills and express their creativity.

/News/2024/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.t: Akhand Dhun: Annual Prayers for Success, Peace and Harmony, Wellingborough, UK
/News/2024/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Akhand Dhun (80 photos)
 A special day of continuous prayers was held at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Wellingborough, on Sunday 31 March 2024. Thousands of worshippers from around the UK and even parts of Europe convened to pray for success, peace, and harmony to prevail in communities across the world.
 The prayers began at 7.00am, with visitors joining throughout the day to offer their devotion at the ‘Akshar Deri’, a beautiful shrine housed within the mandir.
 Shivani Kotecha, a first-time visitor, travelled from Leicester with her husband for the event. Sharing her impressions on the day, she remarked, “We thoroughly enjoyed this uplifting occasion where everyone joined together to think of others. We were warmly greeted by volunteers, and meeting other devotees from across the country made the day even more memorable.”
 This year marked the 40th anniversary of the Akhand Dhun, which had had modest beginnings in 1984. To celebrate the occasion, Mahant Swami Maharaj sent a special handwritten letter blessing all the attendees and reiterating the spiritual significance of the Akshar Deri shrine, calling it on par with the Akshar Deri in Gondal, India. He also conveyed his personal prayers for everyone’s well-being, and for peace and harmony to prevail in all communities at a time when unrest and humanitarian crises continue to unfold in various parts of the world.
 To promote healthy living and an active lifestyle, over fifty cyclists rode more than 100 kilometres to Wellingborough after departing from London Mandir earlier that morning, while another group of devotees walked more than 110 kilometres from Chigwell Mandir in East London.
 The prayers continued uninterrupted through to 7.00pm, when the day’s chanting, pradakshinas, darshan and seva concluded.
 Rajesh Ladwa, a lead volunteer at the Mandir, shared, “This unique annual event of devotion and collective prayer encourages the community to congregate for a common purpose. We are extremely grateful to everyone who participated, and look forward to continuing to serve the wider community throughout the year.” He added, “Following the news of their cancer diagnosis, we also extend our prayers to His Majesty King Charles III and Her Royal Highness The Princess of Wales for a swift and full recovery to good health.”
