 This year is being celebrated as the Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav, which commemorates the 50th anniversary of the establishment of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha’s satsang volunteer force. As part of this celebration, 1,700 senior volunteers from the BAPS Children’s Activities wing attended the special Divya Sannidhi Parva in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Based on the theme ‘Antar Akshardham’, the first day began with Swamishri lighting the inaugural lamp. Later, Swamishri was welcomed to the assembly hall by the volunteers, who sang kirtans in unison and offered Swamishri 1,700 garlands, each devoutly made by the volunteers. Swamishri honored each volunteer and appreciated their dedicated seva.
 Swamishri blessed the volunteers with his presence during five inspiring sessions, each filled with unforgettable memories. The 1,000 bal karyakars also got the chance to take a group photo with Swamishri, while the 700 balika karyakars had a group photo with Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj. 
 During the final session, Swamishri sat on a decorative swing, from which he celebrated the Pushpadolotsav by spraying sanctified saffron-scented water on the bal karyakars.
 Throughout the Divya Sannidhi Parva, the volunteers were guided on different aspects of nishtha, prapti, niyam-dharma, loyalty, divyabhav, rajipo and other spiritual endeavours by sadguru swamis and other experienced swamis.
 Inspired by Mahant Swami Maharaj and organized by the dedicated efforts of the swamis and volunteers of the Bal Pravrutti Central Office, the Divya Sannidhi Parva was an unforgettable experience for all the lead karyakars, enriching their personal spiritual journey.

Congratulations
 The Bal Satsang Exams have enabled many children to learn about Vedic, cultural and Satsang history and values. This year, in March 2024, a total of 3,254 out of 4,151 children from BAPS centers outside India (in India, the exams will be held in July) took the exams and 3,070 (73.96%) children passed.
 We congratulate all the participants for their efforts and pray to guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj to bless all with continued progress.
 Special recognition has been given to the boys and girls who have scored Top marks. Their names are listed below:

Photo Gallery 
 Bal Vikas Parva (56 photos)
 Over 20,000 boys and girls participated in the 3-day Bal Vikas Parvas held at BAPS centers across India during the summer of 2024. Based on a schedule prepared by the Bal Pravrutti Central Office (BPCO), local centers conducted these parvas for the all-round development of children. Titled ‘Anand Killol’, the parvas guided children on Satsang, Sanskar, Culture, Health, and Self-Development.
 During the three days, the children learned about spirituality through speeches by swamis and animation videos, and devotional activities such as collective worship, mandir darshan, and daily devotional rituals. The children also learnt about the judicious use of mobiles, regular worship, and respect for parents through an interactive workshop.
 In addition, they participated in quizzes, field games, craftwork, festive celebrations, yoga and other activities.

/News/2024/Balika-Parayan-26328.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Raleigh, Balika Parayan 2024 (42 photos)
 On July 21, 2024, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Raleigh organized a memorable Balika Parayan, where over 60 girls, aged 6 to 14, presented the traditional annual discourse celebrating the glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru. The event, themed "Unity Within," was a true reflection of the collective spirit and dedication of the community, attracting approximately 285 attendees.
 The theme "Unity Within" served as the guiding principle for the entire program, which had been in preparation for weeks. The girls took to the stage to showcase a wide array of talents, each performance deeply rooted in the values of Samp (harmony), Suhradbhav (goodwill), and Ekta (unity). The program was a vibrant blend of performances, including singing, dancing, acting, and delivering heartfelt speeches that resonated with everyone present.
 A standout moment of the event was the traditional mahapuja, conducted with great reverence and precision by the girls. This ritual was not only a demonstration of their devotion but also an affirmation of their cultural and spiritual heritage. The confidence and grace with which the girls led this significant ritual highlighted the strength of the values that have been instilled in them.
 In addition to the mahapuja, the girls showcased their commitment to spiritual education by reciting mukhpath in Sanskrit. This recitation of sacred texts, which requires both discipline and deep understanding, was performed flawlessly, underscoring the girls' dedication and hard work.
 Each performance at the Balika Parayan was more than just a display of talent; it was a powerful embodiment of the values promoted by the theme "Unity Within." Through their singing, the girls expressed harmony; through their dancing, they conveyed the joy of togetherness; and through their acting, they told stories that emphasized the importance of goodwill and unity within the community.
 The event was deeply moving for the audience, which included family members, friends, and community leaders. It provided a platform for the girls to showcase their talents while also celebrating the collective strength and unity of the community. The Balika Parayan was a remarkable success, leaving a lasting impression on everyone who attended and reinforcing the essential values of unity, harmony, and goodwill in building a strong and vibrant community.

/News/2024/Bollywood-Stars-Akshay-Kumar-.t: Bollywood Stars Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff Visit BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Bollywood-Stars-Akshay-Kumar-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff Visit Abu Dhabi Mandir (26 photos)
 Bollywood actors Akshay Kumar and Tiger Shroff, along with Vashu Bhagnani, a prominent film producer, visited the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi on 8 April 2024 for darshan, prayers, and blessings. 
 Brahmaviharidas Swami welcomed them with garlands of flowers at the Wall of Harmony. Here, iconic monuments of the world are connected with the word ‘harmony’ written in various ancient and modern languages representing the diversity of our world. 
 Thereafter, the guests climbed the Prayer Dune representing the deserts of Sharjah, where the story of the Mandir begins. On 5 April 1997, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj said a historic prayer, “May peace prevail here and everywhere. May all religions grow greater love for one another. May a mandir in Abu Dhabi bring countries, cultures, communities, and religions closer together.” Here, Akshay Kumar, Tiger Shroff, and Brahmaviharidas Swami also offered their prayers for global peace, remembering the life message of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, “In the joy of others lies our own.”
 Following the tour, they visited the origins of the three holy rivers, Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati. Brahmaviharidas Swami highlighted the significance of the Divine Eye overseeing the confluence of these rivers. 
 Proceeding towards the mandir, they visited ‘The Orchard’, a sattvic food court furnished with benches, tables, and chairs crafted from recycled wooden pallets and crates that were used in transporting the stones for the mandir.
 Ascending the steps to the mandir, the delegation marvelled at the intricate carvings – of lions, elephants, cows, camels, oryxes, parrots, peacocks, and falcons – that adorn the exterior walls. Brahmaviharidas Swami also explained the carved depictions of 14 value tales from ancient civilizations.
 The guests then entered the inner sanctum of the mandir and were greeted by the ‘Dome of Harmony’, symbolizing unity between the five elements of nature: Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Space. 
 Under the second dome, the ‘Dome of Peace’, Akshay Kumar, Tiger Shroff, and Vashu Bhagnani conducted a special puja, arti, and offered prayers to the deities.
 As the visit concluded, guests thanked Brahmaviharidas Swami and expressed their gratitude to His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, and the Ruler of Abu Dhabi His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan for creating the BAPS Hindu Mandir.
 Tiger Shroff remarked on the pure energy felt upon entering the Mandir, emphasizing its significance as a symbol of unity among religions and nations, saying, “The moment I stepped foot in the Mandir, I felt an amazing vibration and energy. I could feel the energy. It was so pure!”
 Akshay Kumar described the experience as a dream and praised the Mandir’s openness for anyone to offer prayers, highlighting its beauty and significance, adding, “This is like a dream! It is something you only imagine. I will always remember this experience. This Mandir is so open; anyone from any culture, caste or religion can come here and offer their prayers. There is no discrimination. This is truly a beautiful place.”

/News/2024/Brent-Faith-Covenant-Launch-a.t: Brent Faith Covenant Launch at the House of Commons, London, UK
/News/2024/Brent-Faith-Covenant-Launch-a.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Brent Faith Covenant Launch (10 photos)
 Representatives from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as Neasden Temple – joined faith and community leaders from across the London Borough of Brent at the House of Commons on Wednesday 13 November for a significant milestone in fostering interfaith harmony and collaboration. The event, hosted by Dawn Butler MP, Member of Parliament for Brent East, in partnership with Brent Council and the Brent Multi-Faith Forum, marked the official signing of the Brent Faith Covenant.
 The Covenant is a powerful reaffirmation of Brent’s shared commitment to interfaith harmony and collective action for the greater good of the community. By bringing together diverse faith groups and community representatives, the Covenant highlights the importance of unity, understanding, and collaboration in creating a thriving and inclusive society.
 Also present during the event was Parliamentary Secretary of the Cabinet Office Georgia Gould MP,  as well as Brent Multi-Faith Forum’s co-chairs Rabbi Dr Frank Dabba Smith and Mustafa Field, and the Leader of Brent Council Cllr Mohammed Butt.
 The occasion also featured the launch of the Brent Youth Faith Alliance, a groundbreaking initiative led by the Young Brent Foundation. The Alliance aims to empower the next generation of leaders by fostering youth engagement in interfaith dialogue and collaborative efforts.
 During the event, Rutvik Patel, a young volunteer from Neasden Temple, was invited to address the audience on behalf of Hindus in Brent. Rutvik passionately highlighted the vital role of youths in bridging divides between diverse communities and driving positive change, not only in Brent but across London, Great Britain, and the wider world. He shared: “Faith communities not only provide spiritual guidance, but also a moral framework and a sense of belonging. By connecting with our own faith and reaching out to others, we discover shared values that bind us and work towards the greater good.”
 Reflecting on the profound influence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Rutvik added, “Through his life and teachings, he has shown me the importance of integrity, compassion, humility and harmony – values that now shape my everyday actions. These teachings, which call for selfless service and seeing beyond differences, continue to inspire interfaith dialogue and respect around the world, fostering greater understanding and collaboration among communities.”
 Dawn Butler MP captured one of the evening’s core themes, echoing a sentiment expressed by several speakers: “We are not here to tolerate each other, but to celebrate each other.” Her words resonated deeply with the gathering, emphasising the collective recognition of Brent’s vibrant diversity and the importance of celebrating the differences that enrich the community.
 Zachary Williams, a manager at the Young Brent Foundation, elaborated on the Brent Youth Faith Alliance. “This new project,” he explained, “offers young people in Brent a unique platform to discuss key issues, share their insights, and tackle challenges within the context of faith. It’s a powerful opportunity for youth who often lack a voice in such discussions to bring about real, impactful change.”
 The historic gathering at the House of Commons stands as a testament to Brent’s enduring strength in fostering interfaith harmony, with Neasden Temple playing a key role in shaping a more inclusive, progressive future.

/News/2024/British-PM-Rishi-Sunak--Aksha.t: British PM Rishi Sunak & Akshata Murty Visit Neasden Temple, London, UK
/News/2024/British-PM-Rishi-Sunak--Aksha.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prime Minister Sunak & Mrs Murty Visit Neasden Temple (40 photos)
 British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, accompanied by his wife Akshata Murty, visited BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – on Saturday 29 June 2024.
 They were warmly welcomed in a traditional Hindu manner by swamis as well as senior leaders of BAPS UK & Europe.
 Mr Sunak and his wife were then guided on a brief tour of the Mandir where they paid their respects to the murtis and admired the traditional Hindu art and architecture. The couple offered their personal prayers at the central shrine and then proceeded to perform the abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni.
 They spent considerable time meeting BAPS volunteers, with whom they discussed some of the Mandir’s charity and community work that the volunteers drive. Mr Sunak and Mrs Murty were particularly impressed by the dedication of some of the young volunteers. The couple then proceeded to the prayer hall to join the evening assembly.
 Addressing the gathering, Mr Sunak paid tribute to the “contribution that the Temple and its community makes to Britain,” and to the “leadership and inspiration of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj,” the global leader of the BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu fellowship.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj had sent a video message for Mr Sunak and his family in which he said, “I pray for the people of the United Kingdom: May you all be blessed with peace and prosperity, harmony and success.” This message was also shown during the assembly.
 In his welcome address, Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of BAPS in the UK and Europe, thanked the Prime Minister for his video tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj during the centenary celebrations in India in 2022. He also recalled the Prime Minister’s visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi during the G20 Summit last year, and added, “We, as British Hindus, are always thankful for the opportunities that this great nation has given us. We want to return the goodwill by celebrating the successes of the United Kingdom as well as contributing to its progress.”
 Sharing some further impressions from his visit, Mr Sunak said: “I am completely blown away by the sheer physical beauty of this temple. The most special thing about being here is the strength of the community. Neasden Temple is a shining example of how to inspire a generation of young people to volunteer and support their community.
 “His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj is an inspiration to so many, and rightly so for the moral clarity that he brings. All of us in our lives have struggles and challenges. Being able to look up to someone like Mahant Swami Maharaj to get that strength and courage to continue is something I find particularly helpful.”
 During his visit to Neasden Temple, Mr Sunak was introduced to the plans for the new BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris. Reflecting on this project, Mr Sunak added, “The Mandir in Paris will make sure communities of different faiths can come together and understand each other. Projects like that allow us to live in societies that are tolerant, inclusive, and accepting of everybody.”
 Sanjay Kara, a trustee for BAPS in the UK, shared, “It was an honour to have the Prime Minister join the local community of British Hindus at Neasden Temple. We thank him for inspiring younger generations from all backgrounds to actively commit to public service, and we offer our prayers for the continued success of our great nation.”

/News/2024/California-State-Assembly-Hon.t: California State Assembly Honors 50th Anniversary of the First BAPS Mandir in North America, Sacramento, CA, USA
/News/2024/California-State-Assembly-Hon.text:
Photo Gallery 
 California State Assembly honors 50th anniversary of the first BAPS Mandir in North America (7 photos)
 On August 5, 2024, the California State Assembly passed a resolution commemorating the 50th anniversary of the first BAPS Mandir in North America. Introduced by Assemblymember Alex Lee of District 24 and co-sponsored by Assemblymembers Stephanie Nguyen, Ash Kalra, Liz Ortega, and Phillip Chen, the resolution marked a significant moment for the BAPS community. Volunteers from across California gathered in the State Capitol in Sacramento to celebrate the occasion in the Assembly chamber, a reflection of the community's immense pride and joy.
 Assemblymember Alex Lee praised BAPS's enduring impact: “This year marks the 50th anniversary of BAPS in North America. Since 1974, BAPS has been an organization dedicated to fostering community, spirituality, and service, and it has played a vital role in enriching the lives of countless individuals through its various initiatives, including educational programs, humanitarian efforts, and cultural activities.”
 The 50th anniversary of the first Mandir in North America celebrates the dedication of countless volunteers and devotees, guided by the vision of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. For five decades, they have promoted values of selfless service, faith, and harmony across North America. The seven Mandirs in California, including the first North American Mandir in New York, exemplify these principles, fostering community unity and driving positive change.
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha is a global Hindu organization devoted to nurturing faith, inspiring service, and promoting a better way of life. Established in 1974 by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the first BAPS Mandir in North America was constructed in New York. Since then, BAPS has expanded its North American presence to over 100 Mandirs throughout the United States and Canada, including six traditional stone Hindu Mandirs and the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey.

/News/2024/CapitolDiwali2024-27548.aspx.t: Diwali Celebration at the U.S. Capitol, Washington DC, USA
/News/2024/CapitolDiwali2024-27548.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Diwali Celebration at the U.S. Capitol (32 photos)
 On November 13, 2024, a vibrant Diwali celebration took place on Capitol Hill, hosted by BAPS Public Affairs along with multiple partner organizations, including the Hindu American Foundation (HAF), the Asian American Hotel Owners Association (AAHOA), the U.S. Indian Community Foundation, Shrimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur, Federation of Jain Associations of North America (JAINA), The Art of Living Foundation, Sikhs of America, the Asia Pacific Institute of American Jewish Committee (AJC), the Indian American Relations Council, and the National India Hub. Over 300 members of the Indian-American community from across the United States gathered at the Dirksen Senate Office Building for the celebration, joining 33 members of Congress, the Ambassador of India to the United States Vinay Mohan Kwatra, and Alia Al Suwaidi, Deputy Chief of Mission of the Embassy of the United Arab Emirates. 
 Diwali, often called the Festival of Lights, is one of the most important cultural celebrations for Hindu, Jain, Sikh, and Buddhist communities worldwide. The festival symbolizes the triumph of good over evil, light over darkness, and knowledge over ignorance.  
 Elected officials at the event underscored the value of embracing diversity and fostering unity within their communities. They spoke passionately about the role of cultural celebrations like Diwali in promoting greater understanding and building bridges between different communities.  
 In the spirit of Diwali, Rep. Haley Stevens remarked on the occasion's significance: "We know that our Indian American community is one of our success stories. It is a part of the vibrancy of our incredible economy and so many communities. And to assemble all here tonight in the Dirksen building in recognition of Diwali and Diwali's meaning is such a profound honor to be with all of you. May light continue to shine out darkness, may togetherness be our triumph, and may so many blessings and best wishes go to the young people, to the families across America." 
 Shri Vinay Mohan Kwatra, Ambassador of India to the United States, remarked on the significance of the occasion, saying, "It is wonderful to celebrate Diwali with so many Members of Congress and distinguished guests tonight. It is a reflection of their commitment to the relationship. Your presence here is a reflection of the important role that you and this festival play in the relationship. This is an Indian festival, which is embraced and celebrated the world over. And you, your presence here, the presence of so many Members of Congress, has made it all the more special." 
 Rep. Jonathan Jackson reflected on the values promoted by BAPS, stating, "BAPS has been instrumental in promoting the values of compassion, service, and spirituality, as His Holiness (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) has reminded us, 'In the joy of others, lies our own.' As we light our diyas and share in the festival, let us also strive to be instruments of enlightenment, instruments of peace, and instruments of justice. And let us be keepers of the light." 
 Reflecting on the profound impact of BAPS and its Diwali celebrations, Rep. Pete Sessions added, "I visited Robbinsville, New Jersey, to the temple (BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham) three times, and each time I have come back, it has become very apparent to me that the service is oriented not only around this great religion and these great people, but also the faith they place in themselves and the role that this festival, Diwali, plays in their lives." 
 Members of Congress who attended the celebration included Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith (Mississippi), Senator Rand Paul (Kentucky), Rep. Andrew Clyde (GA-9), Rep. Andrew Garbarino (NY-2), Rep. Andrew Ogles (TN-5), Rep. Ben Cline (VA-6), Rep. Bobby Scott (VA-3), Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1), Rep. Dan Meuser (PA-9), Rep. Darin LaHood (IL-16), Rep. Glenn Grothman (WI-6), Rep. Haley Stevens (MI-11), Rep. Jamie Raskin (MD-8), Rep. Jonathan Jackson (IL-1), Rep. Mike Ezell (MS-4), Rep. Marc Veasey (TX-33), Rep. Nick LaLota (NY-1), Rep. Norma Torres (CA-35), Rep. Pete Sessions (TX-17), Rep. Randy Weber (TX-14), Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-8), Rep. Ro Khanna (CA-17), Rep. Robert Aderholt (AL-4), Rep. Scott Perry (PA-10), Rep. Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rep. Steny Hoyer (MD-5), Rep. Tim Burchett (TN-2), Rep. Tom Suozzi (NY-3), Rep.-Elect April McClain Delaney (MD-6), Rep.-Elect Mike Haridopolos (FL-8), Rep.-Elect Rob Bresnahan (PA-8) , Rep.-Elect Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), and Rep.-Elect Sylvester Turner (TX-18). 
 The celebration offered a chance to reflect on Diwali's universal values—hope, unity, and progress—while raising awareness of the Indian American community's cultural contributions. Furthermore, attendees engaged in meaningful discussions with Members of Congress and community members, amplifying the event's overall impact.

/News/2024/Celebrating-Indian-Culture-an.t: Celebrating Indian Culture and Spirituality with the Delhi Sant Mahamandal, New Delhi, India
/News/2024/Celebrating-Indian-Culture-an.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Celebrating Indian Culture and Spirituality with the Delhi Sant Mahamandal (24 photos)
 As part of its year-long 20th Anniversary Celebrations, Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi hosted a one-day conference to mark the Silver Jubilee of the Delhi Sant Mahamandal (National Capital Region).
 The historic conference brought together over 400 sadhus, sages, and mahamandaleshwars representing various sampradayas, matths, ashrams, and mandirs across the Delhi NCR. Esteemed attendees included Shri Mahant Shraddheya Narayan Giri Ji Maharaj (International Spokesperson for Shri Panch Dashnam Juna Akhada, Varanasi, and President, Delhi Sant Mahamandal NCR), Mahamandaleshwar Naval Kishore Das Ji, Mahamandaleshwar Pujya Kanchan Giriji Maharaj, Shraddheya Swami Dhirendra Puriji Maharaj, Jainacharya Lokesh Muni Ji, Shri Mahant Pujya Swami Pramod Krishnam ji, Mahamandaleshwar Swami Sarvanand ji Maharaj, Acharya Mahamandaleshwar Swami Balakanand ji Maharaj, Mahamandaleshwar Swami Pragyanand Giri Ji Maharaj,  Pujya Devkinandan Thakur Ji , and Acharya Sudhanshu Ji Maharaj.
 The conference commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp by prominent sadhus and mahamandaleshwars, accompanied by the recitation of Vedic chants. Among the topics discussed were Indian spirituality, traditions, sadhana (spiritual practice), saintliness, unity, and mutual love. The discourses were anchored on the teachings of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, particularly his messages: ‘Dharma is that which fosters mutual love’ and ‘In the joy of others lies our own’.
 Representing the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Dharamvatsaldas Swami, Bhadreshdas Swami, and Munivtatsaldas Swami also presented the inspiring messages of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 After the conference, a new ambulance service was ceremonially inaugurated by the Delhi Sant Mahamandal. This service will support the upcoming Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj in 2025, reflecting the spirit of service and compassion advocated by the gathering.
 This momentous conference continued Swaminarayan Akshardham’s unwavering efforts to preserve Indian traditions and spirituality while promoting unity, love, and peace.

/News/2024/Celebrating-International-Wom.t: Celebrating International Women’s Day 2024, UK & Europe
/News/2024/Celebrating-International-Wom.text:
BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK and Europe observed the UN’s International Women’s Day with an inspiring programme in 30 centres around the region.
 International Women’s Day (IWD), which falls annually on 8 March, was ratified by the United Nations in 1977 to honour the significant contributions of women throughout the course of history.
 BAPS’s celebrations, titled ‘Celebrating Women: Uplifting Communities’, focussed on how everyone can be an advocate for harmony and draw inspiration from women past and present.
 The programme delved into the challenges faced by individuals and communities amid the pandemic and ongoing cost-of-living crisis. It specifically underscored the significance of cultivating a positive mindset and emphasised the transformative power of small acts of kindness in fostering unity and positively impacting society.
 These inspiring themes were thoughtfully explored through uplifting video presentations, cultural performances, panel discussions, and addresses by esteemed guests who shared their inspiring testimonies and experiences.
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha’s celebration of IWD represents its ongoing commitment to women and matters of importance to women, as inspired and guided by BAPS’s spiritual leader, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2024/Celebrating-Maternal-Bonds-BA.t: Celebrating Maternal Bonds, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Celebrating-Maternal-Bonds-BA.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Celebrating Maternal Bonds (28 photos)
 The women's wing of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi organized a special event titled ‘Matru Devo Bhava: Celebrating Motherhood’ to honor the role of mothers in society. Over 700 women of different age groups from various communities attended the event.
 The event highlighted the theme of ‘Matru Devo Bhava’, a principle in Indian culture that honors mothers as divine figures. The program, presented by youth and women from various communities, included thought-provoking talks, motivating cultural performances, interactive skits, bhajans, and other presentations emphasizing the importance of motherhood, and underscoring the selfless love and guidance mothers provide in nurturing a child's development.
 Among the distinguished guests were Dr. Tulika Shukla, who spoke on the impact of social media on modern parenting, and Dr. Geeta Ramkrishnan, who highlighted the pivotal role of mothers in shaping society, and how to balance family and professional life. A video presentation also showcased the artistic contributions of Mrs. Meera Choksi to the Abu Dhabi Mandir.
 The event concluded with a traditional group dance and a pledge by the attendees, reaffirming their commitment to embody the values of motherhood.

/News/2024/Celebrating-Shri-Ram-Janmabhu.t: Celebrating Shri Ram Janmabhumi Mandir Opening, UK & Europe
/News/2024/Celebrating-Shri-Ram-Janmabhu.text:
The opening of the new Ram Mandir in Ayodhya was a historic moment of celebration for over a billion Hindus around the world.
 With the inspiration and guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, this momentous occasion was marked at all BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu mandirs internationally, including more than 40 mandirs and centres across the UK and Europe, as well as in the homes of devotees worldwide.
 Mandirs, halls and homes were beautifully decorated to commemorate the joyous occasion, with a host of devotional festivities providing worshippers of all ages and denominations an opportunity to offer their reverence to Shri Ramchandra Bhagwan.
 The celebratory events included a vibrant and enlightening cultural programme of bhajans, dramas, and discourses from learned swamis paying homage to the exemplary life of Shri Ramchandra Bhagwan. It also included an insightful presentation on the sacred connections between Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Ayodhya, as well as the many contributions of Yogiji Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj towards the new Shri Ram Mandir.
 Leaders and representatives from various Hindu mandirs and organisations, as well as local civic leaders and distinguished guests, also joined the celebrations at BAPS mandirs and centres in another mark of solidarity and support for this historic occasion.

/News/2024/Ch%C4%81turm%C4%81s-P%C4%81r%.text:
Chāturmās is a holy period of four months in the Hindu calendar during which devotees undertake additional religious observances. During this time, pārāyans (scriptural discourses) are held at BAPS mandirs and centres around the world.
 This year, senior swamis from India – Somprakashdas Swami and Narayancharandas Swami, who served as a personal attendant to Pramukh Swami Maharaj for over 35 years – presided over more than 40 of these discourses throughout the UK and parts of Europe.
 They offered their wisdom on a variety of themes based on the Shri Harililamrut, the Vachanamrut, the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, and other scriptures.
 The discourses provided spiritual enrichment through theological insight and practical guidance to the thousands who attended.
 This year’s pārāyans also provided a unique opportunity to delve deeper into the life and virtues of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj as witnessed and experienced by both swamis. Their presentations captivated audiences with musical and visual interludes to support their narrations.

/News/2024/Chhatralay-Shibir-Sidhi-Liti-.t: Chhatralay Shibir: ‘Sidhi Liti ni Samjan’, Australia
/News/2024/Chhatralay-Shibir-Sidhi-Liti-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shibir (43 photos)
 More than 125 youths from Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Newcastle, Sydney, Perth, Wollongong, and other cities across Australia gathered at Peninsula Outdoors Camp in Victoria for the BAPS Chhatralay Shibir, Australia.
 The shibir was held in the presence of Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami, who provided crucial guidance on Indian Philosophy and the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, based on the Sanatan Vedic shastras.
 The five-day camp, themed ‘Sidhi Liti ni Samjan’ (meaning, Clear-Cut Understanding) gave the participants insights into three profound principles of Satsang:
 1. Swaminarayan Bhagwan is Parabrahma Purushottam.
 2. Gunatitanand Swami is Aksharbrahma.
 3. Pragat Satpurush (Aksharbrahma) – Mahant Swami Maharaj – is the manifest form of Swaminarayan Bhagwan on this earth and the gateway to moksha.
 In addition to the speeches by swamis, participants engaged in workshops, panel discussions, and indoor and outdoor activities. To foster their cooking skills, a special competition titled ‘My Kitchen Rule’ was held. Additionally, they received guidance on the importance of contributing to Mahant Swami Maharaj’s vision for building Akshardham in Melbourne.

/News/2024/Consecration-Ceremony--Inaugu.t: Consecration Ceremony | Inauguration of BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Consecration-Ceremony--Inaugu.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Pratishtha (100 photos)
 Murti Darshan (20 photos)
 On 5 April 1997, Pramukh Swami Maharaj prayed amid the sand dunes of the Sharjah desert that a mandir be built in Abu Dhabi that would bring together people of different faiths and forums, different cultures and countries. 
 Twenty-seven years on, that glorious divine vision of harmony was fulfilled by Mahant Swami Maharaj as he inaugurated the BAPS Hindu Mandir in the capital of the United Arab Emirates. 
 On 14 February 2024, the city of Abu Dhabi witnessed the auspicious pran-pratishtha ceremony, wherein the Mandir’s sacred images were ritually infused with divine presence amid Vedic chanting. 
 The ceremony began early in the morning at 6.00am. Hundreds had gathered in the upper sanctum of the Mandir as well as in the Abhishek Mandap while thousands more watched the live broadcast in the assembly hall and outdoor marquees. The gathering included devotees and well-wishers from all over the world, including people of diverse faiths and backgrounds, reiterating the spirit of inclusivity and harmony that the Mandir embodies.
 The historic moment culminated when Mahant Swami Maharaj conducted the final pujan in each of the seven shrines.
 The seven spires of the Mandir, themselves reflecting the union between the seven emirates of the UAE, each house a revered deity from across India: Shri Akshar-Purushottam Bhagwan, Shri Radha-Krishna Bhagwan, Shri Sita-Rama Bhagwan & Parivar, Shri Parvati-Shankar Bhagwan & Parivar, Shri Jagannath Bhagwan & Parivar, Shri Padmavati-Shrinivas Bhagwan, and Shri Ayyappa Swami. The pan-Indian representation of the diverse forms of Hindu spirituality is a further manifestation of the Mandir’s all-inclusive ethos.
 Before concluding the ceremony with the inaugural arti in all seven new shrines, Mahant Swami Maharaj addressed the gathering. He said, “Throughout the ceremony, I have been praying for the people of this country and the world. May there be peace and prosperity for everyone, and may we all progress together to serve the whole of humanity.” He went on to thank everyone who had contributed to the Mandir, including His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the President of the UAE who generously gifted the land upon which the Mandir has been built, and emphasised the Mandir as a place where people of all faiths and backgrounds are welcome to learn, experience peace, and contribute to global harmony.
 Puja Satikunvar, who had witnessed the ceremony, shared, “We had been waiting for this day for years! The moment Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived and conducted the final arti, we could all feel the divine energy. It was unforgettable, because these ceremonies transcend mere symbolism; there is precision, devotion, and reverence, making it a profoundly enriching and transformative experience. This day will be etched in my heart and the hearts of thousands like me for the rest of our lives.”
 Located in the Cultural District of Abu Dhabi, the intricately crafted BAPS Hindu Mandir is an architectural marvel imbued with sanctity, beauty, tranquillity, and spirituality. 
 The ceremonial inauguration of the Mandir marks the beginning of a new era of spiritual enlightenment and community engagement. The Mandir will continue to serve the wider region as a hub for cultural and spiritual activities, interfaith dialogue and understanding, and community service and collaboration.

/News/2024/Consuls-General-visit-BAPS-Sw.t: Consuls General visit BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2024/Consuls-General-visit-BAPS-Sw.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Consuls General visit BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham (46 photos)
 To commemorate the first anniversary of the inauguration of BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, 14 Consuls General from the Society of Foreign Consuls of New York, representing countries from all around the world visited the sacred grounds for a special event celebrating peace, harmony, and global unity. 
 The gathering was hosted by the Deputy Consul General of India, Dr. Varun Jeph, and the Consul General of Malaysia, Amir Farid Abu Hasan. 
 The event began with a warm welcome from Township of Robbinsville Council President Mike Todd, who acknowledged the significant impact BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham has had on the local and global community. Todd highlighted that Akshardham is truly a place of beauty that will instill a sense of peace and introspection. Todd also spoke about the selfless service of the volunteers who, through BAPS Charities, have been an amazing partner, “Not just in the local community, but in New Jersey and throughout the world.”  
 A moving video presentation followed, showcasing the global contributions of BAPS under the spiritual guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. From large-scale humanitarian efforts to daily acts of compassion and service, Mahant Swami Maharaj’s unique approach continues to touch lives and spread the values of unity, service, and harmony.
 The Deputy Consul General of India, Dr. Varun Jeph, shared his thoughts on the event, emphasizing the power of such gatherings in fostering global peace. Reflecting upon the fact that the Consuls General come from different geographies, religions and faiths, Jeph said, “Nothing could be better than getting them here to Akshardham to represent the coming together of humanity.”
 Similarly, Hon. Amir Farid Abu Hasan, Consul General of Malaysia, highlighted BAPS’ role in promoting universal values. “I believe that as diplomats we are here to advocate peace and interfaith and that can only be done through a greater understanding of religions from all around the world.  Based on that principle, I believe a visit to Akshardham is an example of how we could understand the different faiths there are in the world today. With that in mind, I discussed [this trip] with my colleagues and they agreed that this visit …. would be a good start for each of us to understand each other even more.”
 The highlight of the event was a special vidhi (Hindu ritual) inside BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in which the Consuls General and their teams partook, offering prayers for peace and unity in the world. This ceremony underscored the importance of intercultural and interfaith dialogue in a world increasingly divided by conflict. After the vidhi, the Consuls General toured the awe-inspiring Swaminarayan Akshardham, guided by volunteers who shared the architectural, cultural, and spiritual significance of the site. 
 As the delegation left, the Consuls General expressed their admiration for BAPS' mission and the values embedded in BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham. They left inspired, united in their commitment to promote harmony and mutual respect among all nations.
 In the words of Hon. Vladimir Božović from Serbia, “We are all human beings, and especially in these times, we need to understand and support each other, love our neighbors as ourselves, and unite to create a better world.”
 The first anniversary of BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham is a powerful reminder of the impact that seva (selfless service), compassion, and unity can have on the world stage, resonating with leaders from across continents.

/News/2024/Dashabdi-Mahotsav-Celebration.t: Dashabdi Mahotsav Celebrations, BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Hong Kong, China
/News/2024/Dashabdi-Mahotsav-Celebration.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Swagat Sabha (17 photos)
 Bhakti Sangeet (13 photos)
 Satsang Sabha (11 photos)
 Dashabdi Mahotsav (53 photos)
 Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav (7 photos)
 On 29 June 2014, with the blessings of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami performed the pran-pratishtha and inauguration of the beautiful BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Hong Kong.
 Mandir Murti-Pratishtha Mahotsav, Hong Kong, China
 From 12 to 15 July 2024, devotees and well-wishers celebrated the mandir’s Dashabdi Mahotsav, marking ten memorable years of social and spiritual contributions in the region.
 BHAKTI SANGEET
 On 12 July, the tenth anniversary celebrations commenced with Bhakti Sangeet, in which over 300 devotees were enthralled by the bhajans sung in various Indian languages by Yogipremdas Swami.
 Also, Pujya Viveksagardas Swami elaborated on how singing devotional bhajans enhances our devotion to God.
 SATSANG SABHA
 On 13 July, over 600 devotees and well-wishers attended the evening assembly, in which balaks and kishores presented a fascinating skit titled ‘Mandirma Prabhu Biraje Chhe’, highlighting the vital role mandirs play in nurturing spiritual and moral values in devotees of all ages, contributing to the greater good of society.
 Pujya Viveksagardas Swami gave practical insights into the ‘Aksharam Aham Purushottam Dasosmi’ mantra imparted by Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami explained the three pillars of Hinduism – Scriptures, Mandirs and Sant – and discussed how mandirs uphold our values and traditions. He also highlighted the significant contributions of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj in establishing over 1,500 BAPS mandirs worldwide.
 DASHABDI MAHOTSAV
 On the morning of 14 July, over 600 devotees participated in the Dashabdi Mahotsav Vedic Mahapuja along with Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami and Pujya Viveksagardas Swami.
 During the subsequent assembly, balaks and kishores performed a vibrant dance. Dharmavatsaldas Swami spoke about how mandirs inspire value-based living by sharing real-life stories. Shri Rajababu Gupta and Shri Vasantbhai Jethva, two founding members of BAPS in Hong Kong, provided a brief history of the remarkable social and spiritual activities conducted by the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir over the past decade.
 Pujya Viveksagardas Swami shared insights on how BAPS activities began in East Asia, including Hong Kong, and how Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj have nurtured these centers over the years.
 Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami further elaborated on how to sustain and nurture satsang in future generations.
 Among the guests were the Honorable Consul General of India to Hong Kong, Ms. Satwant Khanalia; Consul Mr. K. Venkata Ramana; former District Council member of Kowloon City District, Mr. Admond Yue; and other dignitaries from various communities.
 KARYAKAR SUVARNA MAHOTSAV
 On 15 July, the Karyakar Survana Mahotsav was celebrated to honor the exceptional contributions of BAPS karyakars in Hong Kong, recognizing their sincere dedication, devotion, and sacrifice over the years.
 Pujya Viveksagardas Swami spoke about the life, work, and message of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and how this message has spread across the world. He also highlighted the contributions of our gurus, swamis, and devotees in promoting the practical spirituality advocated by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami elaborated on the foundational values of karyakars – samp, suhrudbhav, and ekta – as explained by Yogiji Maharaj.
 As part of the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir Dashabdi Mahotsav in Hong Kong, members of the balika and kishori mandals created a unique exhibition showcasing inspiring messages of satsang.

/News/2024/Day-of-Civilization--Inaugura.t: Day of Civilization | Inauguration of BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Day-of-Civilization--Inaugura.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day of Civilization (40 photos)
 The Day of Civilizations evening assembly, based on the theme ‘One World, One Culture, One Story at a Time’, celebrated cultural diversity. The event highlighted the beauty and significance of each culture’s unique contribution to the shared story of humanity.
 The event brought together individuals from over 30 countries to appreciate and explore the different values depicted along the exterior walls of the BAPS Hindu Mandir through intricately carved stories in stone from diverse civilizations, including African, Arabian, Aztec, Egyptian, Eskimo, Indian, Mayan, Mesopotamian and Native American. The stories from these civilizations, permanently embedded in the mandir, help to preserve and promote the values that bind humanity together.
 Brief animated versions of some of these civilizational stories were shown to introduce the topic of the speakers. The topics included: Friendship and Love, Service, Purity, Choice, Forgiveness and positivity, and Harmony and Unity.
 The event was graced by Swami Shri Govind Dev Giri Ji Maharaj, Jagadguru Sri Dr Nirmalanandnatha Maha Swami Ji, Swami Paramatmanand Saraswati ji, Sri Chinna Jeeyar Swami Ji, His Excellency Dr Abdulrahman Abdulla Buali and American author Dr David Frawley (Pandit Vamadeva Shastri).
 David Frawley expressed his delight at the mandir, emphasizing its role in bringing civilizations together. He stated, “It’s a great experience to see this mandir. This mandir is bringing together these two civilizations and 15 ancient civilizations. This mandir is honouring the unity of all. This mandir gives us a vision of the future.”
 Chinna Jeeyar Swami also acknowledged the fulfillment of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s wish by Mahant Swami Maharaj, highlighting the significance of unity and service, “All those who have offered their service in this mandir have served not just the Swaminarayan Sampradaya, but the entire Sanatan Dharma and the country of India. We have heard of lotus flowers growing in lakes, but never before has a lotus bloomed in a desert. This is indeed remarkable and can only be done by Mahant Swami Maharaj. ‘Worship one but respect all.’ The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi is truly a living representation of this quote.”
 Jagadguru Sri Dr Nirmalanandnatha Maha Swami Ji expressed, “Albert Einstein mentioned that we have been able to split an atom before getting the wisdom of being able to unite the hearts of humans. Millions of people will benefit from this mandir. May all hearts unite. This temple is not made out of metal, stone or soil; it is made out of devotion, love and service.”
 Swami Paramatmanand Saraswati ji said, “This temple itself has created a new global civilization of love, harmony, trust and friendship.”
 Swami Shri Govind Dev Giri Ji Maharaj said, “This temple is not just a temple, this is a lighthouse of humanity, peace and love.”

/News/2024/Day-of-Devotion-Heartfelt-Off.t: Day of Devotion: Heartfelt Offerings to Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Day-of-Devotion-Heartfelt-Off.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Bhakti Tula (60 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi is a remarkable story of faith, devotion, and community collaboration. With so many contributing in so many ways to this inspiring devotional complex, it was natural that the local fellowship would wish to thank God, Guru and everyone involved.
 A special ‘Day of Devotion’ was held at the Mandir on 10 February 2024, providing an opportunity for devotees to offer their gratitude in a uniquely devotional way.
 The Bhakti Tula – a sacred devotional ceremony – united devotees and well-wishers from the Middle East and across the world to express their devotion through personal prayers and heartfelt offerings of individual rosary beads. These offerings were placed in a tula (sacred scales) to Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj to symbolize gratitude and celebrate the imminent inauguration of the Mandir.
 The assembly began with kirtans that explained the spiritual benefits that are realised through devotion. Sadguru Viveksagardas Swami delved deeper into the goodwill of countless people who have supported the construction of the new Mandir and paid tribute to their invaluable contributions.
 Upon Mahant Swami Maharaj’s arrival, the murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj were joyously welcomed into the assembly hall carried in decorative palanquins.
 Thereafter, Swamishri performed the pujan and arti of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj before offering his own devotion by placing a rosary bead in the scales.
 In his blessings, Mahant Swami Maharaj reiterated the spiritual significance of pure devotion and selfless prayer, explaining, “God is limitless and transcendental. He can never be weighed in materialistic terms. Only our selfless devotion can truly reach him and please him. By pleasing God, we are thanking everyone.”
 Swamis and devotees participated in the tula by placing their own rosary beads on the scale pans, symbolising their personal devotion and gratitude.
 Asmita Vavadiya from Sohar, Oman, shared her experiences of the evening: “The tula gave us an ideal way to express our devotional gratitude and offer our prayers. Everyone across the Gulf region – male and female, young and old – has served with dedication and enthusiasm to make this Mandir a reality. This was our opportunity to offer our gratitude and prayers to God, our guru Mahant Swami Maharaj, and to all those who have given their support.”

/News/2024/Day-of-Gratitude--Inauguratio.t: Day of Gratitude | Inauguration of BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Day-of-Gratitude--Inauguratio.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day of Gratitude (45 photos)
 to addConstruction of the BAPS Hindu Mandir and campus, comprising the Welcome Centre, Pramukh Sabhagruh, offices, residences for Swamishri and swamis, kitchen and dining areas and other areas was completed due to the diligent and dedicated efforts and support of innumerable people.
 The evening Day of Gratitude assembly was a small gesture to acknowledge the people whose selfless contributions enabled the project completion.
 Speeches by Anandswarup Swami, Uttamnilay Swami, Sanjaybhai Parikh, Sumitbhai Bheda, Ashokbhai Kotecha and Aksharatit Swami paid heartfelt appreciation to the dedication, devotion and efforts of all the BAPS men and women volunteers, the artisans and labourers, government officials and project contractors and engineers, and the swamis involved in the design, planning and onsite execution of the project. Also, Brahmavihari Swami read and elaborated upon the historic letter written by Mahant Swami Maharaj in December 2020 during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic. The biggest appreciations were expressed towards Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Uttamnilaydas Swami said, “On every stone of the mandir we can see the spirit of dedication of the devotees and volunteers. These volunteers and devotees have dedicated their entire time, beyond their jobs, beyond their daily lives. By giving their complete time to the construction work of the mandir, they have helped to successfully complete the mandir.”
 Sumeetbhai Bheda elaborated upon the significant and varied contributions of the women devotees and volunteers in completing the mandir and added, “This 108-foot-tall temple touches everyone's heart today. But at the foundation of this temple is the service of saints and devotees. Also, in such a big project, women have contributed as much men in so many ways. Once, the setting Sun was asked, ‘If you set, who will bring light to the Earth?’ No one answered, but a small lamp came forward... Today, lit by many such lamps [volunteers], this temple is shining brightly.”
 The evening Day of Gratitude assembly was a small gesture to acknowledge the people whose selfless contributions enabled the project completion.
 Narayanmunidas Swami said, “This temple is a symbol of love, peace, and dialogue. It is also a symbol of cooperation. There are many experiences in which saints and devotees, Hindus and Muslims have cooperated.”
 Ashokbhai Kotecha said, “It has been a long journey. And when we talk about the Festival of Harmony, there were so many things to do with thousands of people coming in. We depended on our friends from different parts, different sectors of the society to help us out. And they did not let us down.”
 Aksharatitdas Swami said, “In the Vachanamrut, Bhagwan Swaminarayan teaches us the spiritual necessity of gratitude. Heartfelt gratitude is a spiritual act of the humble realization that nothing is done by one’s self and that Bhagwan himself inspires countless souls to do his work. For ultimately... he is karta-harta… the all-doer.”
 Brahmaviharidas Swami, “Even if you gathered 8 billion people, and all the enlightened sadhus, who would have the heart to do a sankalp that may there be a temple in Abu Dhabi... Pramukh Swami Maharaj was a saint who saw what no humans could see and he saw a temple in Abu Dhabi. Pramukh Swami always encouraged. And he based everything on truth, transparency and trust. The most important thing was the love, encouragement, vision and sankalp of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. And when the world stopped believing in themselves, Mahant Swami Maharaj believed in the BAPS Abu Dhabi Mandir and that is the power of the guru.”

/News/2024/Day-of-Harmony--Inauguration-.t: Day of Harmony | Inauguration of BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Day-of-Harmony--Inauguration-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day of Harmony (51 photos)
 The evening assembly, titled ‘Day of Harmony’, was graced by leading representatives from the major religions of the world: His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Spiritual Leader of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and Creator of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi; Swami Avdheshanand Giri Ji Maharaj, President of the Hindu Dharma Acharya Sabha; His Excellency Dr Abdulrahman Alzaid, Deputy Secretary-General of the Muslim World League, Mecca, Saudi Arabia; Rabbi David Rosen, Special Advisor to the Abrahamic Family House, Abu Dhabi; His Eminence Bishop Paolo Martinelli, Apostolic Vicar of the Catholic Vicariate of Southern Arabia; His Holiness Sri Satguru Uday Singh Ji, Spiritual Leader of the Namdhari Sikh Community; Venerable Bhikkhu Sanghasena, Founder President & Spiritual Director of the Mahabodhi International Meditation Centre; and Brahmaviharidas Swami, Head Swami, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi. They were joined by Bawa Jain, Secretary General of the World Council of Religious Leaders.
 Compèring the proceedings was His Excellency Omar Saif Ghobash, UAE Ambassador to the Holy See, Assistant Minister of Cultural Affairs for the UAE, and Religious Advisor to His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
 Before they entered on stage, Swamishri greeted all the spiritual leaders individually in the green room and engaged in dialogues with them. Thereafter, on stage, all the leaders were honoured with garlands and shawls.
 A short video on the faith each speaker represented was shown before their speech. All the distinguished guests voiced their admiration for how His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj has inspired the BAPS Hindu Mandir, a spiritual sanctuary where people of all faiths, cultures and backgrounds are welcome to learn, benefit and contribute.
 His Excellency Dr Abdulrahman Alzaid emphasized the importance of coexistence and peaceful behaviour. He stated, “For social and spiritual harmony, we should coexist and behave peacefully with each other. We must be able to work towards coexistence; we must be able to work to that which leads to peace between humankind.”
 His Eminence Bishop Paolo Martinelli said, “This new temple is a place for my brothers and sisters to pray and strengthen harmony with God.”
 Rabbi David Rosen reminisced about his interactions with His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and his visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham in Delhi. He recalled his joy in witnessing the inauguration of the BAPS Mandir in Chicago in 2004 and expressed his delight for the wonderful Abu Dhabi Mandir.
 Venerable Bhikkhu Sanghasena said, “We are all friends, we are not strangers, we are not different, we are members of one family; the human family.”
 His Holiness Sri Satguru Uday Singh Ji said, “We are all one, but we are also wonderfully different, that is where we can enjoy the oneness of creation.”
 Swami Avdheshanand Giri Ji Maharaj said, “I have no doubt this mandir will be the spirit of communal harmony and interfaith collaboration not only in Abu Dhabi but around the world.”
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed, “If we are united with harmony, then love and peace will flourish everywhere; it will flourish in our hearts and everyone’s hearts.”

/News/2024/Day-of-Inspirations--Festival.t: Day of Inspirations | Festival of Harmony, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Day-of-Inspirations--Festival.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day of Inspirations (60 photos)
 Organized by the Women’s Wing of the BAPS Hindu Mandir, the Day of Inspirations celebrated the pivotal role of women in uplifting society and their invaluable contributions to humanity. More than 2,000 women of all ages attended the evening assembly highlighting families and inspirational individuals who have contributed to society.
 A captivating themed video titled ‘Faces of Inspiration’ highlighted the remarkable stories of individuals who have served the BAPS Hindu Mandir under extraordinary circumstances.
 The event was graced by esteemed guests, including Sadhvi Saraswati Bhagwati, a renowned spiritual leader, author and motivational speaker based in Rishikesh, India. Sadhvi Saraswati is the author of the #1 bestselling memoir, Hollywood to the Himalayas: A Journey of Healing and Transformation.
 She conveyed her joy upon visiting the mandir, highlighting its significance in fostering unity among communities and how mandirs inspire faith and peace, “This mandir is a testament to ‘Bhakti ki Shakti’ (the strength of devotion). It serves as a symbol of global harmony, akin to the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati rivers in Prayagraj. The mandir is greater than the sum of its parts and it can be seen in everyone coming together for this mandir.”
 Among the distinguished guests was Vandana Sudhir, wife of the Indian Ambassador to the UAE, who has over 30 years of experience in the field of education. She expressed, “This mandir has connected different cultures and religions, making this world a better place. What can be a better place than here to inspire unity and love in the society.”
 Poonam Bhojani, founding CEO of Innoventures Education, said, “My father used to teach me to work without expecting any results. This is the first time I have seen it in action, here at the BAPS Hindu Mandir as every individual has served without any expectations. This is true service with compassion.”
 The event splendidly celebrated community spirit, with attendees representing the Jain Samaj, Art of Living, Amey Gujarat Ladies, Indian Women of Dubai, Rising Stars Group, Maharashtra Group, South Indian community, ILA Abu Dhabi, and other communities in the UAE.
 The assembly concluded with the recorded video blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj, “You are not ordinary. You are great souls because you have obtained God. You have infinite power within you so take great pride in this.”

/News/2024/Day-of-Peace--Inauguration-of.t: Day of Peace | Inauguration of BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Day-of-Peace--Inauguration-of.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day of Peace (28 photos)
 The value of peace is at the core of the BAPS Hindu Mandir, and so, in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj, distinguished guests presided over the special Day of Peace evening assembly to share their wisdom on how to attain peace through various facets of life.
 The speakers included Swami Brahmaviharidas of BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, Honourable Justice Sharad Arvind Bobde, Former Chief Justice of India; Kailash Satyarthi, Indian social reformer and 2014 Nobel Peace Prize Winner; Padma Bhushan Dr. Tejas M. Patel, Chairman and Chief Interventional Cardiologist at Apex Heart Institute, Ahmedabad, India; Bhavish Agarwal, entrepreneur and co-founder of Ola Cabs and founder of Ola Electric; and Umang Bedi, co-founder of VerSe Innovation and Dailyhunt.
 Vivek Oberoi, a renowned Indian actor and producer, was the master of ceremonies for the assembly, introducing the eminent panel of speakers who provided enlightening perspectives on peace. He also expressed, “We are just action heroes in films, but the real action heroes are these volunteers and sadhus here in front of us. This is all due to the grace of the guru who envisioned this mandir because the guru makes impossible into ‘I am possible’.”
 The speakers gave insightful talks on attaining peace through Environment, Child Development, Justice, Wellbeing, Media and Spirituality.
 Kailash Satyarthi shared his insights about peace through child development, “Let us march together. No one should be left behind. We need to learn to walk together.”
 Bhavish Aggarwal spoke about peace through the environment, “We don’t seek peace; we are the peace by thinking of the world as one family. For me, to be here has been an inspiration, which has given me stronger vigour to work towards creating a future of peace and prosperity with the timeless values the mandir expresses.”
 Umang Bedi said, “This temple is not just a physical edifice; it is a testament to the power of the human spirit and the boundless potential of unity. It is an example for every leader about the power of unity.”
 Speaking about peace through health and wellbeing, Dr. Tejas Patel said, “To achieve peace, one must give back to humanity by volunteering and preserving mental health. Peace is a state of mind and can only exist in a conflict-free mind. What is the need of the hour? Universal peace. The BAPS Hindu Mandir is not just a place of worship, it is an immortal monument of universal peace, and it is going to direct the future.”
 Brahmaviharidas Swami said, “Very often we hear that when we close our eyes, we find peace, but peace comes to us when we open our eyes to the issues that challenge the world. When we awaken ourselves, we reinvent ourselves.”
 Justice Sharad Bobade said, “I am sure this temple has inaugurated a new era in our civilization in which justice and peace reign supreme.”
 In the end, Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the assembly.

/News/2024/Day-of-Prayers-Vedic-Yagna-fo.t: Day of Prayers: Vedic Yagna for Global Harmony, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Day-of-Prayers-Vedic-Yagna-fo.text:
Photo Gallery

 Ceremony of Yagna Offerings (48 photos)
 More than 980 people gathered for the Vishwa Samvadita Yagna (Vedic prayers for global harmony) at the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi on 11 February 2024.
 The event formed part of the ‘Festival of Harmony’ – a celebration of cultural diversity and spiritual unity – organised to commemorate the historic inauguration of the new mandir.
 Ancient Hindu scriptures describe a yagna as a powerful devotional offering that serves to seek blessings from God. The yagna – the first of its kind in the Middle East – brought together dignitaries, spiritual leaders, and members of the community to pray for peace, harmony and the well-being and success of everyone in the UAE and across the world.
 Seven expert priests had travelled from India to officiate the ancient ceremonial rituals, which connected participants through offerings and prayers that inspire pure and virtuous thoughts and actions. They were supported by more than 200 devotees who helped conduct the ceremony to provide an enriching experience for all the participants. 
 Brahmaviharidas Swami, leading the Mandir project under the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, explained, “A yagna of this significance rarely takes place outside of India. The occasion served as the perfect way to pay tribute to the Mandir’s message of global unity, a value that His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj is deeply passionate about. The peace and coexistence that was evoked throughout the morning embodied a beacon of hope for future generations that the Mandir will reinforce.” 
 The auspicious flame of the yagna symbolised the dispelling of darkness and emergence of spiritual enlightenment, which had been ignited naturally using the sun's rays by Mahant Swami Maharaj two days earlier. This was a wonderful sight to see amongst the rare backdrop of the raining skies that showed all the five elements of nature coming together. 
 Despite the inclement wet weather, the joyous spirits of the participants could hardly be dampened. Jayshri Inamdar, a 70-year-old devotee who had travelled from London to attend the event, shared, “The rains made the historic event all the more memorable and enjoyable. Never in my lifetime have I witnessed a yagna take place in the rain! It felt especially auspicious.”

/News/2024/Day-of-Values--Inauguration-o.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day of Values (23 photos)
 The Day of Values evening assembly celebrated the spiritual values on which the mandir is built and the values it will continue to promote and sustain.
 The chief stage guests were Pujya Chidanand Saraswatiji Maharaj, President and Spiritual Head of Parmarth Niketan Ashram, Rishikesh, and Padma Shri Pujya Brahmeshanand Acharya Swamiji, Founder Head, International Sadguru Foundation. In the assembly, sadguru swamis and the invited guest mahatmas gave spiritual guidance to the audience.
 Pujya Viveksagar Swami said, “In 1990 in New York, Pramukh Swami Maharaj highlighted three requirements for engaging in seva: do it with mahima, understanding and detachment from any expectations.”
 Pujya Brahmeshanand Acharya Swamiji said, “The greatest aspect of our dharma is values. These values are sanatan (eternal), hence our dharma is known as Sanatan Dharma. To establish peace everywhere these values are essential. This mandir is built on such eternal values. Everybody who comes here will feel that this is their mandir. These messages of humanity will echo around the world from here.”
 Pujya Chidanand Saraswatiji Maharaj said, “This is a pilgrimage place. Walls create barriers and boundaries, but you have created a wall of harmony here. Today, I give credit to the King and President of the UAE because you have shown the world that where there is generosity, where there is a big heart, open heart, there is a welcome for all and things can happen. This mandir is going to become another relay station for peace, love and harmony for all humanity. If you want to create harmony, please come here and see the true example. If we start giving value to values, you will see more peace, and a more sustainable world.”
 At the end, Pujya Dr. Swami said, “This mandir will help everyone to understand each other and guide all on how to lead a pious life.”

/News/2024/Dedication-Assembly--Inaugura.t: Dedication Assembly | Inauguration of BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Dedication-Assembly--Inaugura.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Dedication Assembly (179 photos)
 The iconic new BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi was inaugurated on 14 February 2024 by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj along with the Honourable Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, and the eminent Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence for the UAE, His Excellency Sheikh Nahayan Mabarak Al Nahyan.
 The new Mandir, constructed on land generously gifted by the UAE president and ruler of Abu Dhabi, His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, was guided and inspired by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual leader of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS), a global Hindu fellowship.
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi is the first traditional Hindu stone temple in the Middle East, and stands as a testament to the enduring friendship between India and the UAE, embodying the spirit of cultural inclusivity, interfaith harmony, and community collaboration. 
 After arriving at the Mandir, Prime Minister Modi was warmly welcomed by Anandswarupdas Swami on behalf of BAPS and thereafter by community members from across India and the UAE as well as religious leaders from diverse faith communities. 
 During an extensive interactive tour of the temple campus provided by Brahmaviharidas Swami, Prime Minister Modi learned about some of the inspiring features of the Mandir that promote universal compassion, respect, charity, and learning.
 Inside the Mandir, upon seeing His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the Prime Minister bowed respectfully to the global Hindu leader, before participating in a short Vedic ceremony paying homage to the seven Hindu deities enshrined under the seven spires of the Mandir, themselves reflecting the unity of the seven emirates of the UAE. 
 His Holiness and Mr Modi then conducted a grand arti (ceremony of light) of the deities, which was simultaneously performed by thousands at BAPS temples and homes across the world, with millions more watching online through the live webcast.
 After meeting volunteers, children, artisans and others from all over the world who have supported the construction of this magnificent temple, Prime Minister Modi helped carve ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ into a block of stone. The message of ‘the world is one family’ has been the foundational principle of the Mandir, guided by the life and work of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Prime Minister Modi and Sheikh Nahayan then arrived in the assembly where thousands had gathered to celebrate the opening of the Mandir.
 In his keynote address, Prime Minister Modi said: “Today, the UAE has written a golden chapter in the history of humanity through this Mandir.”
 “The BAPS Hindu Mandir is for all of humanity. So I have every faith that the Mandir will usher in a new age of faith and hope, bringing the whole world together in harmony and collaboration.”
 “The magnificent Mandir that we see today in Abu Dhabi is because it was first envisioned years ago [in 1997] by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Today, Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s heart will be glowing with joy at its fruition.”
 “We must also thank my brother Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan [the President of the UAE and Ruler of Abu Dhabi], because it is his generosity that has made possible a mandir so beautiful and magnificent. On behalf of all Indians, I thank Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed and the UAE Government.”
 The Prime Minister then called for a standing ovation from the audience as an expression of heartfelt gratitude to His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
 In his blessings, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj emphasised the importance of the new Mandir as “an abode of love, peace and harmony.” He then explained, “Harmony can be achieved when we do not expect harmony from others, but instead when we strive for harmony ourselves. For that, we must ask ourselves: ‘What can I do, what can I say, and what can I think to nourish harmony?’”
 His Holiness added, “Harmony is the power of God, and humility is the way of God. With this understanding, we can serve humanity.”
 He went on to pray for the prosperity, progress, and peace of the UAE, India, and the world.
 Sharing his sentiments on this momentous occasion, His Excellency Sheikh Nahayan Mabarak Al Nahyan first thanked Prime Minister Modi for visiting the UAE. “We are proud to welcome a great friend from a great and friendly country.” 
 The Tolerance and Coexistence Minister also welcomed His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and thanked him for building the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi. He said, “Today marks the beginning of something special. The new Mandir will serve as both a place of worship and as a community centre for all.” 
 After introducing Mahant Swami Maharaj as “a powerful advocate for human harmony” and “a renowned global leader whose teachings are a source of spirituality, inspiration, and joy,” HE Sheikh Nahayan added, “Your visit, Your Holiness, is an opportunity for us to marvel at your example in working cooperatively to resolve conflicts between different communities and to build a spirit of tolerance as a gateway to understanding, mutual respect, and peace.”
 In his address earlier in the assembly, Brahmaviharidas Swami, who has been leading the Mandir project from conception to completion under the guidance and inspiration of Mahant Swami Maharaj, also thanked the generosity of the UAE leadership and the leadership of Mr Modi, and applauded the friendship between the two that helped create the Mandir. He added, “The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi gives hope to all of humanity that the miracle of harmony is indeed possible and worth pursuing.” 
 In the morning, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj had performed the Vedic consecration ceremony that ritually infused the sacred images with the divine presence of God.
 Together, the consecration ceremony and dedication assembly formally opened the BAPS Hindu Mandir to the world as a gift to generations, to nations, and to the future.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the desert of Sharjah, on 5 April 1997, when he prayed for peace among all religions, prosperity for all countries, and a mandir in Abu Dhabi that would bring together people of all countries, cultures and religions
Brahmaviharidas Swami explained the various value tales and Indian scriptural narratives depicted in stone around the exterior of the Mandir
Prime Minister Modi observed the twelve Jyotirlingas – the most sacred places of pilgrimage for Shaivite devotees, mentioned in the Shiva Puran – sculpted in stone along the exterior of the Mandir
The twelve Jyotirlingas are sculpted along the exterior of the spire enshrining the murtis of Bhagwan Shri Shankar and Parivar
The Prime Minister admired the profusely carved exterior of the Mandir

Prime Minister Modi observed many stone friezes, including the Rath Yatra festival of Jagannath Puri in Odisha, eastern India, sculpted along the southern exterior wall of the Mandir under the spire enshrining the murtis of Bhagwan Shri Jagannath
Brahmaviharidas Swami explained to Prime Minister Modi how the divine narratives of each Hindu deity have been sculpted into the exterior of the Mandir
Bhagwan Shri Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan, as narrated in the Shrimad Bhagwat Puran, is sculpted in stone along the exterior of the spire enshrining the murtis of Shri Radha-Krishna Bhagwan
Prime Minister Modi stood in front of the exterior of the Mandir's central spire
Prime Minister Modi and Brahmaviharidas Swami looked out to the rear of the Mandir campus where the Ganga and Yamuna rivers culminate their journey in a symbolic representation of the sea
Prime Minister Modi observed the full-length exterior of the central spire, enshrining Bhagwan Swaminarayan, profusely covered with stone depictions of his divine narratives as well as devotees
One of the narratives from the life of Bhagwan Swaminarayan shows him ordaining Gunatitanand Swami, his first spiritual successor, revealing him as the personification of Aksharbrahma
Brahmaviharidas Swami pointed out some of the value tales from ancient civilizations that have been incorporated into the stone carvings

Etched hieroglyphically, the story of Osiris, the ancient Egyptian God of the Deceased, emphasises the value of purity – upon death, only a heart lighter than a feather is allowed to cross over to the Paradise of Reeds
Brahmaviharidas Swami pointed out a stone depiction of Mahant Swami Maharaj's visit to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi with HE Sheikh Nahayan Mabarak Al Nahyan in 2019
The stone depiction of Mahant Swami Maharaj's visit with the Sheikh features the Arabian desert and UAE skyline, including the Grand Mosque and BAPS Hindu Mandir in the background

Mahant Swami Maharaj visited the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi on 21 April 2019 upon the invitation of His Excellency Sheikh Nahayan Mabarak Al Nahyan, the Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence for the UAE

Prime Minister Modi offered his respects to the Guru Parampara

Prime Minister Modi met Adel Hassan Mohammed Ahmed Alali, a keen supporter of the Mandir

The plaques on the southern side of the Mandir, available in English and Arabic, provide a historical overview of the Mandir's vision, creation and inauguration
On the northern side of the Mandir, the plaques record the purpose of the Mandir as “an abode of love, peace and harmony,” as revealed by its creator, Mahant Swami Maharaj

Along the amphitheatre, Prime Minister Modi met young volunteers who had artistically crafted inspiring messages of the Mandir on waste stones as mementoes for visitors

Prime Minister Modi took time to observe and appreciate the children's artwork
Further along the Ganga Ghat, Prime Minister Modi met some of the volunteers who had convened from different parts of the world to serve in building the Mandir
At the centre of the amphitheatre, Prime Minister Modi applied a few strokes to a stone block engraved with the ancient Hindu message of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ (the whole world is one family)
The stone block will form part of a larger installation emphasising the central theme of the Mandir as a ‘spiritual oasis for global harmony’
Prime Minister Modi and Brahmaviharidas Swami stood with Vipul Sompura and Sanjay Parikh, two lead volunteers who oversaw the design and construction of the stone mandir
His Excellency Sheikh Nahayan Mabarak Al Nahyan, Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence for the UAE, arrived at the Mandir to a jubilant welcome from the Indian diasporic community

Prime Minister Modi thanked the volunteers for their invaluable service to the Mandir and contributing towards sustaining Indian culture and fostering global harmony
Prime Minister Modi was pleased to meet more children who had devoutly served in the making of the Mandir, including the ‘Tiny Treasure’ mementoes
Prime Minister Modi penned a personal message on a stone memento crafted by the children
Prime Minister Modi wrote 'Jay Jagat' ('Victory to the World') on the stone memento, echoing the Mandir's message of peace, progress and prosperity for the whole of humanity

Prime Minister Modi was accompanied by a delegation of senior government officials and diplomats, including Minister of External Affairs Dr S. Jaishankar, National Security Advisor Ajit Kumar Doval KC PPM, and Indian Ambassador to the UAE His Excellency Sunjay Sudhir
