/News/2024/Janmashtami-Celebration-2024-.text:
Devotees across North America gathered at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandirs to celebrate the auspicious birth of Bhagwan Shri Krishna, embracing the theme "Tav Gunānāmīsh Pāram Na Yāti," which reflects the boundless virtues of God.
 A key highlight of the event was the cultural performances, where children and youth presented speeches and skits that vividly brought to life Bhagwan Shri Krishna's qualities, especially ajātshatrutā—one without enemies—and his profound humility. Dance performances, inspired by Krishna’s playful raas leela, beautifully showcased his divine love and joy. Adding to the spiritual atmosphere, video blessings from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj deeply touched and uplifted the attendees, reinforcing their connection to Bhagwan Shri Krishna. The celebration ended with the joyous swinging of Shri Krishna’s cradle, a symbolic act representing renewal and Krishna's eternal presence in the hearts of his devotees.
 Many devotees also observed waterless fasts as an expression of their devotion. Throughout the celebration, devotees reflected on Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s timeless virtues, deepening their appreciation for the values that continue to guide and inspire their spiritual journeys and daily lives.

/News/2024/Janmashtami-Celebrations-at-B.t: Janmashtami Celebrations at BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Janmashtami-Celebrations-at-B.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Janmashtami Festivities (40 photos)
 Four days of celebrations marked the Janmashtami festival at the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi.
 The celebrations featured a three-day Shrimad Bhagvat Parayan from 23 to 25 August. Over 500 devotees attended the daily evening recitations and reflections from the Shrimad Bhagvat presented by BAPS swamis.
 On 26 August, the auspicious day of Janmashtami, over 5,000 devotees and well-wishers visited the mandir for darshan. Also, throughout the day, various Indian communities residing in the UAE presented kirtan bhakti programs, with visitors also participating in the devotional singing.
 The main evening Janmashtami celebration, attended by more than 1,200 devotees, commenced with Ashtami Puja. The assembly featured kirtan bhakti presentations and a speech by Brahmaviharidas Swami, in which he highlighted the significance of Janmashtami and the essence of true devotion to Bhagwan Shri Krishna. He explored the various observances of the festival and emphasized that the essence of Janmashtami lies in embodying Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s virtues and leading a life by them. In conclusion, he discussed how faith strengthens us during difficulties and recounted the journey of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi as a symbol of resilience, illustrating that with steadfast love and belief even the most formidable challenges can be overcome. This devotion, exemplified by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, inspires devotees to live with courage and perseverance.

/News/2024/Karyakar-Felicitation-Assembl.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Karyakar Felicitation Assemblies (126 photos)
 Karyakars are the active volunteers who conduct the satsang activities of the BAPS. As part of this year’s Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav, special Karyakar Felicitation Assemblies were held locally at all BAPS centers in the 278 BAPS satsang regions throughout India.
 The male and female karyakars who serve in the sanyukta, yuva, bal, mahila, yuvati and balika mandals were honoured in their local weekly assemblies.
 During the assembly, the karyakars were welcomed with showers of flower petals and rice grain by devotees. Thereafter, the notable works and dedication of the karyakars were narrated, highlighting their sacrifices and commitment to duty.
 Each male karyakar was presented mementos, which had been sanctified by Mahant Swami Maharaj, by swamis attending the assembly. Senior women devotees presented the mementos to the women karyakars. The mementos included a card containing rice hand-peeled by the swamis at all BAPS mandirs as a mark of their pure sentiments and appreciation for their seva to satsang.

/News/2024/Karyakar-Retreat-26167.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Karyakar Retreat (20 photos)
 More than 90 senior volunteers came together from 11 countries across Europe for a Karyakar Retreat in Interlaken, Switzerland, from 7 to 9 June 2024.
 The retreat aimed to appreciate the volunteers’ continuing services and strengthen the bond between them and their families while they learned from each other and improved their seva for their respective centres.
 This event was the first time some of the volunteers were meeting physically, having been connected with each other online over several years for their seva.
 Through discussions, interactive games and team-building activities, everyone learned about each other’s many virtues and abilities, while they also enjoyed outdoor walks around the picturesque villages and the inspirational discourses from swamis. The delegates also participated together in daily devotion, such as arti, thal, mansi, and cheshta.
 All the attendees found the first-ever retreat an enjoyable and inspiring experience. One volunteer from Stockholm, Sweden, shared, “It was refreshing to actually meet and learn from other volunteers who I had only interacted with online for so long.” Another volunteer, from Paris, France, added, “We really enjoyed just being with everyone! Participating in the various activities and games helped strengthen our samp (unity) with fellow karyakars across all our centres in Europe.”
 The volunteers and their families took home many memories and motivation to serve together, serve more effectively, and serve their respective fellowships with greater enthusiasm.

/News/2024/Karyakar-Suvarna-Mahotsav-Cel.t: Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav Celebration, Bangkok, Thailand
/News/2024/Karyakar-Suvarna-Mahotsav-Cel.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Celebration (18 photos)
 Over 280 devotees participated in the Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav celebration in the company of Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami and Pujya Viveksagardas Swami. The celebration was held on a cruise ship while sailing along the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok.
 The celebration honored the outstanding contributions of BAPS karyakars in Thailand, recognizing their sincere dedication, devotion, and sacrifice in serving the BAPS Satsang.
 Pujya Viveksagardas Swami began by explaining that Bhagwan Swaminarayan manifested on earth to reveal the Akshar-Purushottam Upasana and how our gurus have spread this understanding worldwide over the decades. He also highlighted the crucial role karyakars have played in this great service throughout the history of BAPS Satsang.
 Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami elaborated on the foundational qualities of great karyakars: samp, suhrudbhav, seva, samarpan, divyabhav, dasbhav, namrata, and respect for others. He emphasized that serving as karyakars is a great opportunity to earn the rajipo of our gurus and the blessings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami.

/News/2024/Karyakar-Training--Conference.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Karyakar Training & Conference (48 photos)
 More than 70 karyakars from Paris immersed themselves in a day-long workshop on 28 January 2024 graced by the presence of swamis from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. The training aimed to deepen their understanding of forthcoming responsibilities, particularly in the lead-up to the construction of Paris Mandir.
 The event commenced with an insightful speech on the history of Paris Satsang Mandal, tracing its journey to the present day. This historical perspective provided delegates with a profound appreciation of the upcoming mandir’s spiritual significance and cultural heritage.
 Updates on the Paris Mandir project, including architectural details, were presented to help participants visualise the final result. These insights into the project’s progress added a tangible dimension to the karyakars’ understanding, creating a shared vision for the future.
 Manoharmurti Swami led team-building games to reinforce unity and unleash creativity. These engaging activities served as a constructive and enjoyable way for karyakars to enhance their teamwork and problem-solving skills.
 The training day also included presentations outlining the next stages of development and how to begin preparations for Paris Mandir. This comprehensive overview equipped attendees with the knowledge and readiness required to actively contribute to the upcoming phases of this monumental project.
 A noteworthy and historical aspect of the day was the first-ever Europe-wide Satsang Pravrutti Online Conference. More than 250 karyakars from across 18 European countries gathered online to reflect on the past year’s accomplishments and gain valuable updates on new policies, structures and upcoming projects, as well as to understand the core principles and ethics of BAPS to better serve the community.
 The training day concluded with video guidance from Sadguru Tyagvallabhdas Swami and video blessings from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Their encouraging words resonated deeply, infusing the karyakars with inspiration and a profound sense of purpose and responsibility.
 Vaibhavi Parekh, a dedicated volunteer from Paris, sharing her experiences of the day, said, “This training workshop and conference proved to be really valuable for me. Even after so many years in Satsang, we need these events to refresh and strengthen our understanding of our core principles. Most importantly, it has inspired me to carry out my seva with dedication and sincerity. I’m so excited to be helping create Paris Mandir, another of Swamishri’s visionary projects.”

/News/2024/Keshav-Ramatotsav-26046.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Keshav Ramatotsav (28 photos)
 During the summer vacation, a total of 1,494 yuvaks from 42 BAPS yuvak mandals throughout Ahmedabad participated in the cricket, volleyball, badminton and chess tournaments as part of the Keshav Ramatotsav 2024.  Eligibility criteria for all yuvaks to participate in any event were that the youth daily performs puja with tilak-chandlo and attends the weekly yuvak assembly. Each yuvak could participate in a maximum of two sports.
 Representing 111 teams, each of 8 players, 888 yuvaks took part the box cricket tournament held at the Net Box Arena in Bhadaj. Each mandal was allowed to field multiple teams. A total of 118 matches were played over 27 days from 6.30 to 11 a.m. The overall winner was a team from the Nikol mandal.
 The volleyball competition was organized on the grounds of the Yogiji Maharaj Hospital, opposite the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Shahibaug, in which 324 yuvaks representing 54 teams participated. The competition winners were Paldi.
 By the wish of Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, to consolidate the understanding of mutual mahima, a special activity was performed at the end of each team game. The players of the winning team performed dandvats to the losing team players, and the losing players each lifted a player of the winning team to celebrate their victory. All the youths joyfully joined in this ritual, creating a very emotional atmosphere.
 In the badminton and chess tournaments, held at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Shahibaug, the yuvaks competed in two age groups: Nilkanth (ages 15 to 21) and Sahajanand ( between ages 21 to 27). A total of 247 yuvaks competed in the badminton competition and 92 yuvaks participated in the chess tournament.
 The Keshav Ramatotsav helped to strengthen the camaraderie between the youths and encouraged their physical and intellectual development.

/News/2024/Kids-Diwali-Celebration-BAPS-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Kids’ Diwali Celebration (60 photos)
 The inaugural Kids’ Diwali celebrations at the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi provided cultural education, fun activities, and interactive learning experiences designed to engage young minds and hearts.
 The celebrations began with over 300 children collectively participating in the sacred mahapuja ceremony, which created an atmosphere of devotion and reflection. The children prayed to bless the for happiness, wisdom, and prosperity, and learnt about the values of gratitude and devotion.
 “I loved the Mahapuja! It was so peaceful and special to pray with so many other kids,” said Jap Parikh, one of the young participants.
 One of the highlights of the event was a fun and captivating Ramayan drama, imparting valuable lessons on morality, bravery, and the victory of good over evil in a relatable way.
 “The Ramayan drama was amazing! I loved seeing the characters come to life and learning about how good always wins,” said Reeva Karia.
 In addition to the spiritual and cultural programs, a vibrant carnival provided children with an opportunity to learn through play. Featuring a variety of fun and educational games, the carnival catered to different age groups and encouraged creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.
 “It was such a wonderful experience for my child. He came home talking about the values he learned today. I am so grateful for these kinds of events that bring our children closer to our culture,” said Samiksha Padiyar, a parent who attended the event with her family.
 The joy, gratitude, meaningful experiences and sense of connection to cultural traditions felt by the children and their families truly reflected the spirit of these celebrations.

/News/2024/Kids-Diwali-Celebrations-2024.text:
Diwali, a significant Hindu festival, symbolizes Bhagwan Shri Ram's return to Ayodhya and reflects values such as love, compassion, courage, and unity. In recognition of its importance, BAPS hosted Kids' Diwali Celebrations at various mandirs across North America. This year's theme, "Illuminate the Light Within," focused on nurturing inner qualities like compassion, truth, and humility.
 Through engaging skits and diverse programs, children learned how these virtues can lead to unity, discipline, and overall well-being. A special Diwali Showcase highlighted stories from Hinduism, demonstrating how its timeless values can be applied in everyday life. The celebration also featured interactive games, moon bounces, and other fun activities, making the event both educational and enjoyable. Additionally, the Saraswati Pujan honored the Hindu goddess of knowledge, arts, and wisdom.
 These festivities helped children gain a deeper understanding of Hinduism and the true meaning of Diwali. Under the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the current spiritual leader of BAPS, these celebrations across North America continue to inspire spiritual growth and foster lasting values in young minds.

 A group of 50 kishores and 23 kishoris from the UK and Europe embarked on a spiritually enriching yatra (pilgrimage), titled ‘Asmita’, to India from 4 July to 8 August 2024. This Bharat Yatra (pilgrimage across holy sites in India) is a long-standing international initiative of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha that provides the youths with a unique opportunity to visit numerous mandirs and sacred Hindu sites, particularly those central to the Swaminarayan Sampradaya.
 The yatra began on 5 July at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, setting an inspiring tone for the journey ahead.
 Following in the footsteps of Nilkanth Varni, the group travelled through North India, visiting the ancient cities of Haridwar and Rishikesh in Uttarakhand, renowned for their revered temples and the sacred River Ganga. The pilgrims also had the privilege of visiting Ayodhya, the birthplace of Shri Ramchandra Bhagwan, and Chhapaiya, the birthplace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, in Uttar Pradesh. These sacred sites deepened their connection to their roots, faith, and heritage.
 The yatra continued westward with a flight from Ayodhya to Ahmedabad, Gujarat. On the morning of their arrival, the group journeyed to Bhadra, the birthplace of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami. Here, they received their first darshan of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj during the yatra, filling the youths with immense spiritual energy.
 A highlight of the yatra was a six-day shibir held in Sarangpur, titled ‘Brahmavidyani College’. This programme provided a focussed environment to engage in deep learning and reflection under the guidance of senior swamis. Topics such as prapti (knowledge of our spiritual attainment), nishtha (firm, resolute devotion and commitment to God), sadhana (spiritual practices), and jodan (deep personal and spiritual connection with the Satpurush) were explored through insightful discourses and practical workshops. 
 120 youths from North America joined the group from the UK and Europe, further enhancing the experience of this global yatra. The yatra was further enriched with nine memorable days in Bochasan in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj, coinciding with the celebration of Guru Purnima.
 During the Gujarat segment of the yatra, the group visited numerous mandirs consecrated by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Shastriji Maharaj, as well as sites of spiritual importance referenced in the Vachanamrut and the birthplaces of the Guru Parampara. These visits offered the kishores and kishoris a deeper understanding of the spiritual, historical, and cultural significance of these sacred places.
 Throughout the journey, the youths were blessed with interactions and guidance from sadguru swamis and learned swamis. These exchanges provided invaluable personal insights, enriching the spiritual growth of each participant.
 Amidst the focus on spiritual learning, the youths also enjoyed light-hearted moments through recreational activities, strengthening their bonds with one another and creating lasting memories.
 The Bharat Yatra proved to be a transformative journey for the young pilgrims, instilling pride in their satsang and deepening their understanding of Hinduism. The experience reinforced their spiritual values, strengthened their connection to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Mahant Swami Maharaj, and inspired them with greater faith and devotion.

/News/2024/Kishore-Kishori-Summer-Shibir.t: Kishore - Kishori Summer Shibir 2024, North America
/News/2024/Kishore-Kishori-Summer-Shibir.text:
The 2024 North American Kishore-Kishori Summer Shibirs took place from June to August 2024. Over 5,000 high school and college-aged youths from across North America participated in these three-day shibirs.
 As 2024 marks the 50-year celebration of Satsang in North America, the theme for the shibir emerged from Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s very first katha in North America in 1974. Pramukh Swami Maharaj mentioned that even here in North America, “Akshardham nu sukh malshe” - here too we can achieve the happiness of Akshardham. On October 8, 2023, after the inauguration of the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham Mahotsav in North America, Mahant Swami Maharaj revealed that we should continue to celebrate “Andar Akshardham” or “Akshardham within.” Thus, the shibir was themed “Andar Akshardham” with the overarching goal of the shibir being “How do I build the Akshardham within?”
 The messages used to explain how to build “Andar Akshardham” focused on agna, the divine guidance of God and Guru; and upasana, the philosophy imparted that one must attain a God-realized Guru to attain God. Delegates were guided on how to follow agna with the right mindset, and develop faith in God and Guru as sarva-karta-harta (all-doer) and pragat (manifest) on this earth in the form of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The first three sessions centered on understanding and feeling of “Akshardhamnu Sukh”, the happiness of Akshardham. To feel this sukh, the ‘Akshardham’ within must be skillfully built. The first step to start building “Andar Akshardham” is to understand the mahima or greatness of the guru. Thereafter, delegates learned ‘I can count on Swamishri to hold my hand and be there for me’. Delegates then discussed mutual examples of how their Gurus have been present through highs and lows, one’s community at mandir, and through Swamishri himself via the guidance of letters and prayer. While juggling their school, professional, and family expectations, they can trust their Guru to lead them in the right direction.
 Sessions four and five focused on the connectivity of trust in one’s guru. By trusting Swamishri, the motivation to follow agna amid school and family dynamics and having faith in Swamishri increases. When they face hardships in one’s life, they can conquer it because they have the tools to keep strong and have faith in Bhagwan’s kartapanu (all-doership) and the pragat (manifest) Satpurush, Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In the sixth and final common session, delegates learned from Mahant Swami Maharaj and Swamis about the messages coming converging and the practicality of Akshardhamnu Sukh. In school, they may feel that they carry a different identity than at the mandir – how do they form a singular identity? By following ahnik (daily spiritual rituals), reading inspiring incidents, and reflecting on divine memories and their connection with God and Guru, they have a routine full of opportunities to connect to Bhagwan and the Guru. With this enthusiasm, kishores and kishoris are intent on following Swamishri’s agna to strengthen their connection and keep Satsang a priority.
 Throughout the shibir, the delegates dove into the principles of agna and upasana, and the mindset and the wishes of their guru, Mahant Swami Maharaj, to truly build the pathway towards keeping Akshardham within.

 Amrut Cup 2024 (28 photos)
 In 2024, the Northeast region held the first-ever Kishori-Yuvati Amrut Cup Volleyball Tournament in Hillsborough, NJ. This two-day event saw Kishoris and Yuvatis come together enthusiastically to build relationships among players from various centers.
 Every serve, bump, spike, and cheer exemplified HH Mahant Swami Maharaj's teachings of samp (unity), suhradbhav (solidarity), and ekta (oneness). These principles were highlighted during the morning programs, reminding participants that the true purpose of the games was to strengthen bonds with each other.
 The tournament underscored the importance of communication and teamwork in achieving goals and scoring points. In moments of pressure, teams relied on their faith in one another, with every action reflecting their ability to communicate and desire to foster unity. These values, perfected on the court, emphasized the necessity of incorporating them into daily life to fulfill Mahant Swami Maharaj’s vision of becoming one team.
 The first-ever Kishori-Yuvati Amrut Cup was made a reality due to the endless support of the local and regional volunteers. Their relentless devotion in planning and supervising the tournament provided an atmosphere in which all the participants could thrive within their own satsang journey.  
 Events like the Amrut Cup promote camaraderie and sportsmanship, fostering unity and creating lifelong friendships.

/News/2024/Launch-of-BAPS-Paris-Mandir-P.t: Launch of BAPS Paris Mandir Project, UK & Europe
/News/2024/Launch-of-BAPS-Paris-Mandir-P.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Paris Mandir Project Launch Assembly (28 photos)
 On-Site Work Commencement Ceremony (28 photos)
 The forthcoming BAPS Swaminarayan mandir in Paris will be the first traditional purpose-built Hindu temple in France, making it a historic and iconic addition to one of the most beautiful cities in the world.
 After construction began on site in Paris a few days earlier, a special assembly to formally launch the new mandir project was held at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Saturday 4 May 2024 – exactly 36 years to the day when Pramukh Swami Maharaj showered flower petals from the skies over Paris to symbolise his blessings for a mandir to be consecrated in France.
 The evening programme began with prayers sung by devotees from Paris who had travelled to London for the programme, followed by a montage of video presentations chronicling the visionary journey of Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, which began more than 50 years ago at Orly Airport in Paris in 1970.
 A panel of devotees and volunteers from Paris elaborated on the tireless efforts in establishing satsang activities across France. These discussions drew upon the remarkable hardships and dedication of the congregation in Paris, and how they have overcome various formidable hurdles over the decades to practise satsang.
 Trustees then explained the opportunity for everyone to become a part of the historic project, drawing upon their experiences of leading and managing construction projects of other BAPS mandirs across the UK and in Europe.
 A replica model of the mandir in Paris was also unveiled by lead volunteers and swamis, providing an enlightening visual representation for the attendees.
 Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami had sent a video message outlining the global significance of the Paris Mandir Project. This was followed by specially recorded video blessings from Mahant Swami Maharaj in which he recalled his personal memories of visiting Paris with Yogiji Maharaj, a visit that became the inception of the profound vision culminating in the construction of the Mandir. Swamishri also called upon everyone to be a part of this historic project.
 After Yogvivekdas Swami shared some inspiring words of encouragement, Swamishri concluded the assembly, charging the atmosphere with devotional vigour by formally declaring, “Paris Mandir Mahotsavni Jay!”

 Maha-Shivaratri Celebrations (60 photos)
 On 8 March 2024, the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi was adorned with vibrant colours as devotees gathered in their thousands to celebrate Maha-Shivaratri, a revered occasion in the Hindu calendar dedicated to honouring Bhagwan Shri Shiva. This was the first Hindu festival celebrated after the Mandir’s inauguration. 
 The festivities began and concluded with prayers for the UAE. As thousands of devotees patiently lined the Mandir gates, there was a deep feeling of gratitude toward the leadership for their generosity. 
 Throughout the day, from the early hours of the morning to the late evening, pilgrims and visitors were eager to offer their reverence to their deities. The devotees found great joy, solace and spiritual connection in their prayers and traditional worship. 
 All visitors and volunteers were also made aware of the government’s emergency weather guidelines to help create enlightened citizens with greater social responsibility along with spiritual and cultural harmony.

/News/2024/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-Janma-Ja.t: Mahant Swami Maharaj Janma Jayanti Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2024/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-Janma-Ja.text:
BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK and Europe celebrated the 91st birth anniversary of Mahant Swami Maharaj with devotional festivities and inspiring cultural programmes.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj is the sixth spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the current guru of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. His remarkable humility, serene spirituality, and profound discourses continue to inspire and nurture faith and higher living in people of all ages worldwide.
 Through devotional singing, discourses, and video presentations, the celebrations illuminated some of his divine virtues, revealing him as an exemplary devotee of God. The events also explored his selfless and universal love for others, which has captivated the minds and hearts of countless people.

/News/2024/Mahila-Parayan-2024-26229.asp.text:
The BAPS Women’s Wing in Africa organized two-day Mahila Parayans at the following centers across Africa: Kenya – 1,100 attendees at Athi River, Bomet, Bungoma, Eldoret, Kericho, Kakamega, Kisumu, Mombasa, Nairobi, Nakuru, Ruiru, Thika; Malawi – 130 attendees at Blantyre and Lilongwe; Tanzania – 360 attendees at Arusha, Dar-es-Salaam, Mwanza, Tanga; Uganda – 440 attendees at Jinja, Kampala, Lira; and Southern Africa – 330 attendees at Benoni, Durban, Gabarone, Laudium,  Lenasia, Mayfair and Tzaneen.
 The parayan discourses were based on the Bhaktachintamani, Harililamrut and ‘Nari Bhakta Ratna’. The main topic of the first day was ‘Mahatmya-gnan Sahit Bhakti’ (Devotion with a True Understanding of God’s Glory) which was presented through the inspiring story of Meenbai of Kariyana and her unique devotion towards Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 The second-day topic was ‘Bhagwanna Vachan ma Vishvas’ (Faith in the Commands of God), which was portrayed through the story of Umiyabai of Mahemdavad, highlighting her faith in Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 At the end of each parayan, a pothi yatra and traditional dances were also organized. Through the Mahila Parayans, women devotees offered their special devotion at the feet of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit gurus.

/News/2024/Maru-Kartavya-Karyakar-Shibir.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Ireland & Northern Ireland Karyakar Shibir (30 photos)
 On Saturday 10 August 2024, BAPS Ireland and Northern Ireland organised an inspiring Karyakar Shibir held in Dublin, Ireland, on the theme, ‘Maru Kartavya’ (My Duty). The event brought together volunteers from across the region to deepen their understanding of their responsibilities and seva within their respective centres. The shibir was enriched with a series of insightful sessions and activities, each designed to inspire, uplift, and empower the delegates.
 The day commenced with samuh puja. This collective act of worship set a spiritually uplifting tone for the shibir, providing the participants with an opportunity to align their minds and hearts with God, reinforcing the devotional foundation of their seva and the rest of the day’s activities.
 The following session featured an inspiring presentation by Manoharmurtidas Swami in which he delved into the essence of our duty in our personal and spiritual life. The talk emphasised the importance of fulfilling one’s responsibilities with dedication and selflessness, as exemplified by our Gurus.
 A unique highlight of the day was an interview with Mangaltirthdas Swami and Manoharmurtidas Swami. This interactive session provided attendees with profound insights into the spirit of selfless service, with the swamis sharing valuable experiences, uplifting examples, and practical guidance on how to improve one’s approach to doing seva in our daily life.
 After a light meal, the participants enjoyed interactive team-building activities followed by ‘Lessons Learnt’ discussions. The games enhanced collaboration, trust, and communication, all vital for effective community service.
 The final session provided practical guidelines on how karyakars should offer services within the community, emphasising the importance of living according to the values and principles revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and lived by the Gunatit Gurus.
 One delegate from Belfast shared, “I feel so motivated now! This shibir has helped me gain valuable insights into what I need to do more of and what I need to improve upon. I really hope we can have a shibir like this every year, because it’s charged us all.” Another volunteer added, “This shibir has answered many of the queries I have been having. I feel confident and energised to improve in my seva.”

/News/2024/Maru-Kartavya-The-Legacy-Cont.t: Maru Kartavya: The Legacy Continues | Sanyukta Mandal Shibir 2024, UK & Europe
/News/2024/Maru-Kartavya-The-Legacy-Cont.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Sanyukta Mandal Shibir 2024, UK & Europe (60 photos)
 Two three-day residential shibirs for BAPS UK & Europe Sanyukta Mandal were held at Warwick Conference Park over two long weekends – from Friday 16 August to Sunday 18 August 2024 and Sunday 25 August to Tuesday 27 August 2024. 
 Titled ‘Maru Kartavya: The Legacy Continues’, the shibirs brought together over 1,700 delegates to develop their spiritual understanding and appreciation of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s work, wisdom, and virtues. Senior swamis visiting from India, including Somprakashdas Swami, Narayancharandas Swami and Gnanvatsaldas Swami graced both weekends with their presence and inspiring talks. 
 The first day of each shibir began with heartwarming insights into Mahant Swami Maharaj’s daily life, focusing on his discipline and devotion. The engaging programme continued into the evening with a lively kirtan bhakti performance accompanied by an array of instruments and interspersed with prasangs highlighting Mahant Swami Maharaj’s innate purity.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj’s manner of connecting with others through various interactions, each defined by his saintliness, love, and utmost humility, was portrayed through a montage of video clips, interviews, and speeches. Delegates also gained a deeper understanding of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s tireless work in driving satsang activities worldwide. 
 A special session was organised for mahilas with Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, where they jubilantly expressed their personal and collective devotion through garba and kirtans. 
 Somprakashdas Swami and Narayancharandas Swami shared their treasured experiences of Pramukh Swami Maharaj during candid evening sessions. Their narrations highlighted an array of extraordinary qualities of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the unconditional love that he showered upon everyone, while they also shared their experiences of that same love and compassion from Mahant Swami Maharaj today.
 The final day brought together the key messages and themes through a series of videos and presentations that extolled Mahant Swami Maharaj’s true spiritual glory and revealed the significance of one’s spiritual association with him. 
 The audience was deeply moved and departed with a clearer understanding of their duty as devotees to forge an unwavering spiritual bond with God and Guru.

/News/2024/Mission-Jod%C4%81n--Bal-Balik.t: Mission Jodān | Bal-Balika Shibir 2024, UK & Europe
/News/2024/Mission-Jod%C4%81n--Bal-Balik.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Bal-Balika Shibir 2024, UK & Europe (80 photos)
 A three-day residential shibir for around 400 children aged 8 to 13 years from across the UK and Europe was held from 25 to 27 August 2024 at Warwick Conference Park to help them develop their understanding and application of core Satsang principles.
 Conveyed through a thrilling special agent-themed theatre production interwoven with engaging spiritual talks by swamis, vibrant musicals, uplifting presentations, and interactive classroom sessions, each delegate was tasked with a ‘secret mission’ to establish jodān (a strong spiritual connection) with their guru, Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The insightful messages used to explain how to fulfil that mission focussed on three key facets:
 • Man (Mind) – Developing a deeper understanding of Mahant Swami Maharaj through his work and virtues, i.e. realising that our Guru is unique and divine. By doing constant smruti, we can reflect on his greatness and the moments of joy he has shared with us. 
 • Karma (Actions) – Following the Guru’s agnas (instructions) with pride, learning that Mahant Swami Maharaj’s guidance is meant to benefit us, moulding us into strong, responsible, spiritually aligned individuals. 
 • Vachan (Speech) – Not only speaking positively to others, but always seeing the good in everyone. And by sharing prasangs about Mahant Swami Maharaj, we not only strengthen our own faith, we also inspire others.
 Ultimately, by increasing jodān through man, karma, and vachan, we gradually imbibe the virtues of the Satpurush, experiencing his understanding and happiness as our own.  
 A vibrant kirtan bhakti programme delivered by swamis and youths provided an opportunity for the young attendees to immerse themselves in devotional music and express their feelings of devout elation by singing, clapping, and dancing, creating a spiritually charged and uplifting atmosphere.
 Group discussions and classroom sessions allowed the delegates to engage in some fun activity-based learning, delving deeper into why following our Guru’s wishes leads us to live a morally upright, happy, and successful life. They were inspired to stay courageous in times of hardship and were given practical tips on how to decide between right and wrong. 
 The children were also encouraged to describe the good qualities of fellow children to encourage seeing and speaking positively. By harbouring a positive, unified community spirit, they completed the mission and were able to establish their connection to Mahant Swami Maharaj, who gave all the ‘special agents’ unforgettable blessings.

/News/2024/Murti-Pratishtha-of-Shri-Nilk.t: Murti-Pratishtha of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj, Clifton, NJ, USA
/News/2024/Murti-Pratishtha-of-Shri-Nilk.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shri Nilkanth Varni Murti Pratishtha (30 photos)
 On June 1, 2024, the Murti Pratishtha of Shri Nilkanth Varni took place at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Clifton, NJ, in the presence of revered swamis creating an atmosphere of profound devotion and spiritual bliss.
 The eagerly awaited consecration ceremony of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj took place in the presence of Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, Pujya Nilkanthsevadas Swami, Pujya Haridarshandas Swami, and other swamis. The day began with a vibrant Nagar Yatra, a procession filled with devotion and energy. Female devotees led the way with joyous singing, creating an atmosphere of pure devotion. Following the procession, a Vedic Mahapuja took place, with the air resonating with sacred chants and prayers. 
 The spiritual ambiance set the perfect stage for the main event – the Murti-Pratishtha ceremony of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami performed the ceremony. This profound ritual signifies the transformation of the murti into a living deity infused with divine energy. Thereafter, swamis performed the first abhishek and arti of the newly consecrated murti. As the sacred water cascaded over the deity and the arti was performed, the entire gathering was enveloped in a sense of divine bliss, creating a timeless moment of spiritual elevation for all present. 
 Devotees will now be able to offer an abhishek – or arrange for one to be performed on their behalf – on days of special significance to them, such as a birthday, wedding anniversary, or in remembrance of a loved one, or sometimes to seek blessings for a personal reason.

 On August 18, 2024, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Parsippany, New Jersey, celebrated the Murti Pratishtha of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. The festivities began with a vibrant Nagar Yatra—a grand procession filled with devotional songs and traditional dances performed by youths, setting a festive and devout tone for the day.
 Following the procession, Pujya Swamis conducted a Vedic Mahapuja, attended by hundreds of devotees from across New Jersey. The Murti Pratishtha ceremony was led by Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami. Other swamis present on the occasion included Pujya Mangalswarupdas Swami, Pujya Shantyogidas Swami, Pujya Adarshnayandas Swami, and Pujya Rajendradas Swami. Thereafter, swamis performed the first abhishek and arti of the newly consecrated murti. As the sacred water cascaded over the deity and the arti was performed, the entire gathering was enveloped in a sense of divine bliss, creating a timeless moment of spiritual elevation for all present.
 Parsippany's Mayor, James R. Barberio, emphasized the significance of the event and the robust partnership between the township and the community. Devotees now have the cherished opportunity to perform or arrange for an abhishek on significant personal days, such as birthdays, wedding anniversaries, remembrances, or to seek blessings for personal matters. This practice allows them to express their devotion and seek divine grace on special occasions, deepening their personal spiritual connection and providing solace and inspiration.

 The day commenced with an energetic Nagar Yatra, filled with devotional music and traditional dance performances by participants, setting a joyful and reverent atmosphere for the proceedings that followed.

Additionally, Jaclyn Veasy, Mayor of Marlton, NJ, sent a proclamation praising the significant role BAPS and its volunteers have played in the community. Photo Gallery 
 20th Patotsav (65 photos)
 For two decades, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Portland, Oregon, has stood as a spiritual sanctuary and cultural beacon for the local community. Since its inauguration in 2004, the Mandir has welcomed individuals and families seeking connection, reflection, and spiritual growth. Rooted in timeless Hindu values, it has nurtured faith, fostered community service, and become a cherished place for devotion and celebration.
 On December 1, 2024, the 20th-anniversary celebration of the Mandir and the Murti-Pratishtha of Shri Nilkanth Varni took place in the presence of Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami and other revered swamis from across North America, creating an atmosphere of profound devotion for all in attendance.
 The morning began with a Mahapuja – a sacred Vedic ceremony – followed by the eagerly awaited consecration ceremony of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. Performed by Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami, this sacred ritual signified the installation of the murti as a living embodiment of the divine. Swamis then offered the first abhishek and arti of the newly consecrated murti, bathing it with sanctified water and invoking divine blessings. The ritual filled the Mandir with a deep sense of serenity, reverence, and spiritual upliftment. 
 In the evening, the main assembly brought the meaning of the Mandir and a Satsang-centered life to light through thoughtfully prepared skits and multimedia presentations. Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami delivered a compelling keynote address that emphasized the importance of Hindu values and the vital role of the Mandir in sustaining those values within the fabric of the local community.
 With the Murti-Pratishtha complete, devotees now have the opportunity to perform or request an abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj on special occasions—birthdays, anniversaries, or personal milestones—marking a new chapter in the spiritual life of the Mandir and its devotees.
 The 20th-anniversary celebration was not only a tribute to the Mandir’s past but also a reaffirmation of its enduring mission: to serve as a space where devotion deepens, culture thrives, and generations come together in the spirit of unity and faith.

In Warrington, Pennsylvania, they planted the seeds of Satsang and Hindu culture. After years of planning and the sincere wishes of many devotees, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Warrington opened its doors on January 2, 2012. This event marked the creation of a community that embraced people from all walks of life, united by the principles of samp, suhradbhav, and ekta. Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha ceremony, consecrating the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, and establishing the mandir as a beacon of spiritual teachings and values for all who visit.
 On the morning of August 11, 2023, Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the Murti Pratishtha of a new set of murtis to be enshrined in the mandir in Robbinsville, New Jersey.
 On July 28, 2024, the murti sthapan ceremony commenced with a Shobha Yatra of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj. This historic ceremony unfolded amidst Vedic chanting and devotional festivities, with the presence of Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami, Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, and other Swamis. Devotees participated in the Vedic Mahapuja and murti sthapan ceremony, ushering in a new era of Satsang in Warrington. The celebration concluded with an evening cultural program featuring music, dance, and heartfelt testimonies from local youth on how the mandir has profoundly impacted their lives over the past decade.

/News/2024/My-Akshardham-My-Home-Lets-Bu.text:
Over 475 high school- and university-aged youths participated in the Kishore-Kishori Shibirs held during June and July across Australia and New Zealand at six centers: Adelaide, Auckland, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney.
 The theme, ‘My Akshardham, My Home: Let’s Build It Together’ was based on Mahant Swami Maharaj’s handwritten blessings to devotees of the Asia Pacific region on his vision to build an awe-inspiring Akshardham in Melbourne, Australia. Thus, the shibirs focused on detailing how the kishores and kishoris could bring this vision to life, through the pillars of Satpurush, Samp, Samarpan and Saiyam.
 Each session was a blend of group discussions, involvement activities and enlightening elaborations by BAPS swamis on the essence of each pillar. The shibir sessions highlighted the importance and benefits of samp (teamwork), selfless service and observing niyams for success in any task.
 The shibirs provided guidance to the youths to facilitate their spiritual learning, personal growth and cultural engagement with the community.

 The Annual BAPS North American Activities Meeting (NAAM) brought together BAPS volunteers across three specialized gatherings to plan for the upcoming year and strengthen their collective efforts in seva. Each meeting offered opportunities to reflect on past achievements, gain updates on new policies and projects, and deepen the understanding of BAPS principles while fostering collaboration and unity.
 The Children and Youth Activities Meeting, held in Atlanta, GA, on September 20 and 21, brought together over 700 participants. The Satsang Activities Meeting, held in Raleigh, NC, on the same dates, welcomed 316 participants. The Services Departments Meeting, held in Atlanta, GA, on September 27 and 28, saw the participation of 355 individuals. These gatherings laid the foundation for impactful initiatives in the year ahead, empowering volunteers to better serve their communities.
 The theme, “Samp”, encouraged volunteers to integrate values like Madad (helping others selflessly), Milan (collaborating for shared goals), Mahima (appreciating the greatness of others), and Maafi (forgiveness) into their personal and collective seva. These principles were explored through thoughtful discussions, keynote speeches, and hands-on activities, empowering karyakars to overcome challenges, celebrate unity, and foster a supportive environment.
 Attendees engaged in interactive focus groups, outdoor sports, team-building exercises, which strengthened bonds among volunteers and their families. The program also highlighted collaborative problem-solving and emphasized virtues that build stronger support networks. Through daily devotions such as arti, thal, and cheshta, participants experienced a spiritually enriching environment while fostering samp. This meeting laid the groundwork for another impactful year of seva.

/News/2024/NSW-Premier-Honours-Sanskrit-.t: NSW Premier Honours Sanskrit and Cultural Unity, BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Rosehill, Sydney, Australia
/News/2024/NSW-Premier-Honours-Sanskrit-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 NSW Premier Honours Sanskrit and Cultural Unity (14 photos)
 Honorable Chris Minns, Premier of New South Wales, was traditionally welcomed to the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Sydney by Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami.
 Young boys and girls melodiously recited Sanskrit shlokas from the Satsang Diksha, filling the air with messages of world peace, prosperity, and unity. Deeply touched by the recitation, the NSW Premier remarked that younger generations learning Sanskrit will ensure that the ancient and melodic language thrives for generations to come, “To see young Australian kids recite Sanskrit is wonderful. It’s not an easy thing to do, but the BAPS community’s dedication to and understanding of these ancient rites, scripts, and languages means that 100 years from now, the great-grandchildren of the young kids here will be speaking the exact same tongue, preserving that culture and religion, and passing them on to the next generation.”
 In his address, Mr. Minns fondly recalled his first meeting with Bhadreshdas Swami in 2022, prior to being elected as the 47th Premier of NSW, when Bhadreshdas Swami tied a sacred nadachhadi for friendship and goodwill. Premier Minns emphasized the importance of cultural exchanges and their profound impact on fostering mutual respect and understanding among diverse communities.
 He added, “I take it upon myself as a personal commitment to take the scriptures from swami and the BAPS Community in Sydney, put them in the NSW Parliament, and make them available to the members of parliament and to people from other races and religions as a message of peace, tolerance, and togetherness. I can think of no finer message for a modern Australian community such as ours.”
 Mr. Minns expressed admiration and excitement for the vision behind the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir and Cultural Precinct, phase one of which is expected to open in early 2025 and shared that he has already reserved time in his schedule to attend the opening, “This religious institution in Kemps Creek will become iconic, not just for the BAPS community, but for everybody that lives in NSW.”
 The assembly concluded with a heartfelt speech by Bhadreshdas Swami, who expressed his gratitude to Mr. Minns for his continued support and encouragement. He highlighted the shared commitment to building a society grounded in mutual respect, understanding, and cooperation.

/News/2024/Neasden-Temple-Participates-i.t: Neasden Temple Participates in Open House Festival, London, UK
/News/2024/Neasden-Temple-Participates-i.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Open House Festival (40 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as Neasden Temple – welcomed more than 1,200 architecture and culture enthusiasts during the weekend of 14-15 September 2024 as part of the Mandir’s continued participation in the Open House Festival, an annual London-wide festival that opens up and celebrates the capital’s architecture, special places and neighbourhoods, with free open days and events held across all 33 London boroughs.
 The Open House programme began in 1992 to offer free access to London’s best buildings and inspire the public about the benefits of great design. It is organised by Open City, a charity dedicated to making architecture and neighbourhoods more open, accessible, and equitable. Following its inception in London, it has grown into a network of almost 60 cities worldwide, from Lagos to Hong Kong and Miami to Oslo.
 The Mandir is an active participant in the annual Open House event and welcomed visitors throughout the weekend. Volunteers provided guided walkthroughs, explaining the Mandir’s architecture, history, and religious significance as well as its contributions to the wider community.
 Guests also toured the ‘Understanding Hinduism’ exhibition, which offered insights into Hindu beliefs, values, and practices. There were also plenty of opportunities for visitors to witness one of the arti ceremonies during the day.
 Ashish Morar, a volunteer at the Mandir, explained, “Since its opening in 1995, countless people from all walks of life and from various corners of the world have walked through its gates, inspired by its spiritual beauty and captivated by its divine presence. It has become an integral part of the local community and Britain’s religious landscape. Although the Mandir is open to visitors of all faiths and backgrounds throughout the year – free of charge – the Open House programme provides an opportunity to celebrate this spirit of inclusivity that is one of this nation’s most endearing qualities.”
 Shivani Patel, who helped guide the visitors over the weekend, added, “It was an honour to welcome so many people from across London and beyond to share the cultural and spiritual significance of the Mandir and to engage with them in positive and uplifting dialogue. We also look forward to welcoming people throughout the year.”
 A selection of visitor experiences is provided below:
 “Exceeded expectations! The site itself was immaculate and looks newly built. Volunteers were enthusiastic and welcoming, and I felt like we could access everywhere and ask as many questions as we wanted.” –  A Phillips, Doctor
 “Very lovely, informative, extremely welcoming and kind. Beautifully decorated and I will definitely visit here again.” – Shakana, Aerialist
 “It was wonderful. Spiritually rewarding!” – N M Cathmhaoil, University Lecturer
 “Thank you for having us. It was such a great experience, and I will tell friends it’s definitely worth a visit.” – C Tangsgaard, Receptionist
 “I learned so much from the very enthusiastic and helpful tour guides.” – Faiza, Researcher
 “We had a wonderful day and felt so welcomed.” – M Collier, Teacher

/News/2024/Neasden-Temple-Receives-Tripa.t: Neasden Temple Receives Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award for 2024, London, UK
/News/2024/Neasden-Temple-Receives-Tripa.text:
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – has been honoured with the prestigious Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award for 2024.
 Tripadvisor is the world’s largest travel platform, featuring more than 860 million reviews of attractions and places of interest. More than 450 million travellers use Tripadvisor each month to plan their visits.
 The Travellers’ Choice Awards places the Mandir amongst the top 10% ‘things to do’ in the world from more than 8.7 million attractions, experiences, hotels, restaurants, and other places covered on its listing.
 The winners of the award are determined by the quality and quantity of travellers’ reviews and ratings over a 12-month period. As explained by Tripadvisor, the award means that the Mandir has received “consistently great reviews” and is among places that “consistently demonstrate a commitment to hospitality excellence.”
 Priya Rathod, a senior BAPS volunteer, said, “It is an honour to be recognised by such a renowned and trusted organisation. The Mandir is, of course, first and foremost a place of Hindu worship, but His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, its creator, envisioned it to be open to people of all faiths and backgrounds, so we are delighted that people from all over the world have been enjoying their visit and finding value in learning about Hinduism and experiencing first-hand the Mandir’s peace, beauty, traditional Indian architecture, and spiritual meaning.”
 Hemal Patel, another leading volunteer at the Mandir, added, “His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj teaches and energises us volunteers to welcome everyone who comes to the home of God and to serve them with selflessness, humility, and love. It is humbling to learn how the Mandir has brought such a positive impact among worshippers and visitors from around the world.”
 All the latest news and information about Neasden Temple can be found on its various social media accounts: X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and Telegram.

 Neasden Temple Summer Fair (28 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London organises various events throughout the year to bring the local community together.
 The annual Summer Fair attracts thousands to experience the vibrant culture and community spirit of an outdoor gathering, with a variety of fun activities, delicious food stalls, live performances, and much more.
 This year, the event was held on the grounds opposite the Mandir over the sunny weekend of 13-14 July, where members of the local community and visitors from further afield gathered to enjoy two days of enjoyment and learning.
 The event offered a wide range of activities, including exciting rides that brought smiles to the faces of young children, as well as a large community stage that featured live performances from a varied genre of arts, creating energy and showcasing talent from young and senior performers.
 More than 20 organisations presented their respective products and services at the fair, engaging with the public at their respective stalls.
 A Health Hub was also available, which provided guidance on healthier cooking from experts, as well as suggestions on healthy snacks. The juicing bikes proved to be particularly popular amongst attendees.
 The annual fair is incomplete without appeasing the palate. The experience of food was elevated through an array of multi-cultural cuisines that satisfied every craving.
 Shelly Jackson, a local resident, shared: “What a wonderful event! My two little girls had an amazing time and loved the henna decorations and the fabulous performances by the young children. The food was delicious, and we are already looking forward to coming along to experience this all again at Diwali later this year.”
 Pratik Patel, one of the lead volunteers who helped organise the Summer Fair, explained, “It was wonderful to welcome so many people of all backgrounds, cultures and ages to enjoy a truly exciting family day out. A special thank you to our dedicated volunteers as well as local businesses for their incredible support. We look forward to seeing everyone again next year for another unforgettable Summer Fair.”

 BAPS satsang activities in Thailand began in 1984 with a visit from Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He also visited again in 1996. Regular visits by sadguru swamis and other swamis have also significantly contributed to the growth of satsang over the years. During his visit to Bangkok in 2018, Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the devotees to find land for a mandir. Soon after, a suitable plot was found, and plans were drawn.
 The Shilanyas Ceremony was performed by the devotees during the COVID-19 period when international flights were temporarily halted.
 Construction work began after the COVID-19 restrictions were lifted. Through the guidance of Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami, the sincere efforts of Surenbhai Patel, Mayurbhai Desai and the devotees in Bangkok, and the creative designs and hard work of Brahmacharandas Swami and his team, a beautiful mandir was soon erected.
 The BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir Mahotsav, featuring four days of rituals and celebrations, marked the inauguration of the new BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Bangkok, Thailand.
 On 28 April 2024, in Sarangpur, Gujarat, Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the Vedic pran-pratishtha of the murtis for Bangkok mandir.
 Akshar Purushottam Maharaj Pujan
 On 18 July, the BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir Mahotsav began with the Vedic pujan of the small chal murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj by Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami. These murtis had been sanctified by Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj in India before arriving in Bangkok, where they received devotion from Surenbhai Patel and his family. The murtis were then ceremoniously moved to the newly constructed Mandir.
 Praasaad Pravesh & Yagna
 On 19 July, the Praasaad Pravesh ceremony, the ritual of first entry into the new premises, to sanctify the newly built BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Bangkok, Thailand, was marked with a Vedic yagna performed by Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami and Pujya Viveksagardas Swami in the presence of over 150 devotees.
 In the assembly thereafter, Pujya Viveksagardas Swami enlightened the devotees and well-wishers present on the significance and importance of such a yagna according to the Swaminarayan tradition. Then, Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami inspired them by explaining the nine forms of bhakti and how a mandir facilitates a deeper connection with God.
 Vedic Mahapuja, Shobha Yatra & Bhajan Sandhya
 On the morning of 20 July, over 350 devotees participated in the Vedic mahapuja ceremony to pray for blessings and protection from God, who will reside in this mandir. Prays were offered for the prosperity of the country and for the people of Thailand to experience lasting happiness. Additionally, they prayed that all who visit this mandir be inspired to live their lives such that they attain the happiness of God.
 After the mahapuja, Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami explained that this mandir shares the same divine significance as the Akshardham, Vaikunth, Golok and other abodes of God because it is a dwelling place for God. He added that the mandir is where one can offer devotion and seva to God, one can attain enlightenment through satsang, and children can learn about good character.
 In the evening, over 450 devotees, accompanied by traditional Thai performers, participated in the colorful Shobha Yatra. The procession traveled from the Phow Leng Association of Thailand Hall through the by-lanes of Bangkok en route to the mandir, celebrating with joy and fanfare the arrival of God to the newly built mandir.
 Thereafter, Yogipremdas Swami enthralled and captivated the audience with bhajans at the Phow Leng Association of Thailand Hall.
 Murti-Pratishtha Ceremony & Dedication Assembly
 On the morning of 21 July, which this year also marked the auspicious occasion of Guru Purnima, over 500 devotees and well-wishers from Thailand and overseas, including H.E. Shri Nagesh Singh, Ambassador of India to the Kingdom of  Thailand, gathered for the climax of the BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir Mahotsav.
 Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami and Pujya Viveksagardas Swami performed the inauguration and murti-pratishtha rituals of the BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Bangkok, Thailand, as swamis recited ceremonial Vedic verses.
 H.E. Shri Nagesh Singh commented, “I am extremely honored to be present here today on this very divine occasion as I hail from a village which is so very near to Chhapaiya, the janmabhumi of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. My work as a representative of India has taken me to many places around the word. And I have seen at first hand the commendable services conducted by BAPS. I was fortunate to have had the blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj in 2017, at Atlanta, USA. Here, too, I feel blessed that today this beautiful mandir, a cultural embassy in a way, will serve by preserving and fostering the historical and cultural bonds between India and Thailand.”
 Pujya Viveksagardas Swami explained the role and importance of a mandir for individuals, families and society at large, and how one can find peace of mind by regularly visiting the mandir. To mark the occasion of Guru Purnima, he also enlightened everyone on how pure gurus like Pramukh Swami Maharaj and today, Mahant Swami Maharaj, live not for themselves but to serve for the greater good of society.
 Then, Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami spoke about how God resides in the murtis and accepts our love, seva and bhakti. He said, “God will be waiting every day for us, his devotees, to come here and be with him. Here, arti will take place morning and evening, abhishekh of Shri Nilkanth Varni can be offered, regular satsang assemblies for everyone, including children and youths will be conducted. Also, festivals like Diwali, Annakut, Ram Navmi, Hari Jayanti, Janmashtami and more will be celebrated according to our tradition.”
 Thereafter, the dedication assembly was held at the Phow Leng Association of Thailand Hall where those who had helped with this project were honored. A special video blessings for this occasion by Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj was also shown.

/News/2024/New-BAPS-Swaminarayan-Mandir-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mandir Inauguration (45 photos)
 Two days of celebrations marked the inauguration of the new BAPS Mandir in Gurugram, the famous cyber city of Delhi-NCR, in the presence of Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami, Pujya Viveksagardas Swami, other BAPS swamis from Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, and numerous distinguished guests and devotees.
 The construction of the Gurugram mandir had begun on 29 March 2021. Over three years, local devotees, guided by guru Param Pujya Mahant Swamiji Maharaj, diligently completed this construction work through their selfless efforts.
 On the morning of 6 July 2024, the Vedic Mahapuja and World Peace Mahayagna were performed on the mandir premises. In the evening, a magnificent procession honoring the murtis took place through the streets of Sector 46. Joining the BAPS swamis in this festive parade were devotees, youths and children dressed in colorful attire. The women devotees participated in the procession by carrying kalashes on their heads as per tradition, dancing and singing kirtans, and carrying the palanquin of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj. The residents of the city also enjoyed the celebratory procession.
 On the morning of 7 July, Madhurvadan Swami recited the Vedic mantras as Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami and Pujya Viveksagar Swami performed the murti-pratishtha rituals.
 In the assembly, after a speech by Dharmavatsaldas Swami, Munivatsaldas Swami recounted the history of satsang in Gurugram. Then, Pujya Viveksagar Swami spoke, “Through BAPS, over 1,400 mandirs have been constructed worldwide. The purpose of these mandirs is to promote social and spiritual welfare for all. This mandir will be a foundation of spirituality, culture, and education.”
 Therafter, Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami defined a mandir, “Where the mind finds peace, there lies a mandir. Gurugram was the village of guru Dronacharya, thus this sacred land has been steeped in love and devotion for god and guru for ages. Today, this guru-disciple heritage has taken the form of this mandir."
 Previously, on 28 April 2024, in Sarangpur, Gujarat, Param Pujya Mahant Swamiji Maharaj had performed the Vedic murti-pratishtha rituals of the murtis.

/News/2024/New-Years-Family-Mahapuja-250.text:
Photo Gallery 
 New Year’s Family Mahapuja, London, UK (40 photos)
 New Year’s Family Mahapuja at Home, UK & Europe (20 photos)
 Hundreds of families across the UK and Europe joined in a special mahapuja on Monday 1 January 2024 to pray for world peace, family harmony, and a safe and successful year ahead.
 Many of the families, comprising worshippers and community members of all ages and backgrounds, gathered at London Mandir in two sessions, in the morning and in the afternoon. Many more joined online via a live webcast from their own homes, taking the opportunity to decorate their ghar mandirs, make sweet delicacies as a family activity, and make various devotional offerings to the murtis.
 The sacred ceremony was conducted from London Mandir by the resident swamis supported by youths. As swamis chanted powerful Vedic mantras to invoke the divine presence of God and offer various forms of reverence and adoration, they also shared explanations to allow participants to understand and enjoy the ceremony.
 The event provided an opportunity for families to herald the new year with a collective spirit of faith and hope. Seema Patel, who attended the prayers at the Mandir with her family, shared, “What a wonderful way to bring in the new year! The atmosphere inside the mandir was filled with divinity and peace, and it was just so uplifting to see people come together to pray for others. My eight-year-old daughter was focussed throughout and even offered her own personal prayer for those who are suffering.”
 Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK and Europe, explained, “The new year brings renewed faith and optimism. His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj has inspired us all to foster goodwill, unity, and positivity. It was heartwarming to see thousands of people beginning their new year by praying for others. We also pray that the blessings and positive energy from the mahapuja are fostered throughout 2024 and beyond to bring a lasting impact to our global community.”

/News/2024/New-York-State-Honors-50th-An.t: New York State Honors 50th Anniversary of First BAPS Mandir in North America, New York, NY, USA
/News/2024/New-York-State-Honors-50th-An.text:
Photo Gallery 
 New York State Honors 50th Anniversary of First BAPS Mandir in North America (4 photos)
 On June 5, 2024, the New York State Senate and Assembly passed resolutions commemorating the 50th anniversary of the opening of the first BAPS Mandir in North America in Flushing, New York. New York State Senator John Liu and Assemblymember Nily Rozic sponsored the resolutions in the Senate and Assembly, respectively. BAPS members from across New York gathered at the State Capitol in Albany to receive the resolutions and perform a traditional Hindu invocation in both the Senate and Assembly chambers to mark the occasion. It was a moment of immense pride and joy for the BAPS community to see their dedication, service, and efforts recognized with such great honor. 
 Recognizing BAPS’s contributions, Senator John Liu stated: “This year marks the 50th anniversary of the BAPS mandir in Flushing, a historic milestone for the mandir and our community. The BAPS mandir has been a cornerstone of the Hindu community, serving the spiritual, social, and community needs of so many, and we are proud to commemorate their tremendous commitments to serving the needs of others.”
 Echoing these sentiments, Assemblymember Rozic remarked: “It's an honor to recognize the BAPS Mandir on their 50th anniversary. For 50 years, the Mandir has been a center for worship, cultural heritage, and community service. Its contributions to the lives of its members and the community have been profound and far-reaching. I am grateful to celebrate their dedication to promoting unity, service, and spirituality with my fellow leaders in government.”
 The 50th anniversary of the first Mandir in North America is a testament to the hard work and devotion of countless volunteers and devotees who have contributed to its success over the years.  More so, it speaks to the vision and tireless efforts of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who inspired the creation of such Mandirs.  For more than 50 years, they have traveled throughout North America teaching the values of selfless service, faith, and harmony to all. Mandirs, like that in Flushing, unite communities around such universal values and engender positive change—a legacy that will be carried on for years to come.
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha is a global Hindu organization devoted to nurturing faith, inspiring service, and promoting a better way of life. Established in 1974 by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the first BAPS Mandir in North America was constructed on Flushing’s historic Bowne Street. Since then, BAPS has expanded its North American presence to over 100 mandirs throughout the United States and Canada, including six traditional stone Hindu mandirs and BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey.

/News/2024/Nutan-Mandir-Nirman-Vidhi-265.t: Nutan Mandir Nirman Vidhi, Jersey City, NJ, USA
/News/2024/Nutan-Mandir-Nirman-Vidhi-265.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Nutan Mandir Nirman Vidhi (47 photos)
 With the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the unwavering dedication and faith of the devotees from Jersey City culminated in a significant milestone on September 1, 2024. The Nutan Mandir Nirman ceremony marked the sacred commencement of construction for the new Mandir. Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami, along with swamis and devotees from New Jersey, led this joyous occasion.
 The Jersey City, North Bergen, and Hoboken areas have been graced by the vicharan (spiritual visits) of both Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj over the years. As the local community has grown, the current facilities have become inadequate to support the expanding cultural, social, and religious needs of the Hindu-American community. The construction of this new Mandir will address these evolving needs. 
 The Nutan Mandir Nirman ceremony featured a traditional land-blessing ritual, accompanied by Vedic chants, the Mahapuja, and prayers for peace and well-being for the entire community. Once completed, the new Mandir will serve as a vibrant center for cultural, social, and religious activities while also acting as a hub for community service, fostering unity and goodwill among all devotees.

/News/2024/Ojaswini-Celebrating-Womens-C.t: Ojaswini: Celebrating Women’s Contributions to Society, New Delhi, India
/News/2024/Ojaswini-Celebrating-Womens-C.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Celebrating Women’s Contributions to Society (37 photos)
 As part of the year-long 20th Anniversary Celebrations of Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, a special event was organized by the BAPS Women’s Wing of Delhi NCR.
 Titled ‘Ojaswini – Celebrating Women’s Contribution to Society’, this cultural program highlighted the remarkable achievements and invaluable roles of women in contemporary society. Attended by over 6,000 people from across Delhi NCR, the event reflected the ongoing commitment of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha to addressing matters vital to women and girls of all ages.
 The program commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp by distinguished guests, including Smt. Meenakshi Lekhi, Former Minister of State for External Affairs of India; Former Justice Abhilasha Kumari, Former Judicial Member of the Lokpal of India; Dr. Bulbul Sood, Senior Advisor, RMNCHA, and former Country Director at Jhpiego and CEDPA; Dr. Savita Puri, Delhi Medical Association; and Dr. Sushma Chawla, Founder President of NGO Hope – Ek Asha
 The vibrant three-hour celebration featured a compelling blend of cultural expressions, including, live stage dramas depicting themes of resilience and empowerment, thought-provoking video presentations, enthralling cultural dances, and soulful musical performances.
 The event honored the essential role of women as pillars of society and celebrated their enduring contributions. Beyond recognition, it served as a source of inspiration for the younger generation, promoting values of virtue, empowerment, and moral responsibility.
 ‘Ojaswini’ exemplified the ethos of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, reinforcing its dedication to nurturing a society rooted in equality, respect, and the empowerment of women.

/News/2024/Omsiyyat-Interfaith-Cultural-.t: Omsiyyat: Interfaith Cultural Evening at BAPS Hindu Mandir , Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Omsiyyat-Interfaith-Cultural-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Omsiyyat at BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi (48 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, a spiritual oasis for global harmony, hosted an interfaith cultural evening called ‘Omsiyyat’ on 2 April 2024. More than 200 leaders and community members from diverse faiths and backgrounds attended the pioneering event, which helped foster the spirit of faith, friendship, unity, and reflection during the holy month.
 Set against the striking backdrop of the newly inaugurated Mandir, a profound convergence of faith, culture, and dialogue took place. This momentous event was graced by the esteemed presence of several notable UAE figures, including HE Sheikh Nahayan bin Mabarak Al Nahyan, Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence, HE Dr Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of State for Foreign Trade, and HE Dr Mugheer Khamis Al Khaili, Chairman of the Department of Community Development, amongst others, whose presence added a significant layer of respect and honour to the evening.
 In addition to the local leadership, leaders of local religious communities were also in attendance: Rabbi Jeff Berger of the Abrahamic Family House, Rabbi Levi Duchmann, Father Lalji of the Church of South India Parish, and Baha’i community leaders.
 Rabbi Jeff Berger from the Abrahamic Family House shared, “Unity in diversity is not just a principle; it is a practice, vividly demonstrated here tonight. This event symbolizes our shared journey towards understanding and respect.”
 HE Sheikh Nahayan emphasized the tremendous impact of the BAPS Hindu Mandir, stating, “In these troubled times that are threatened by separatism, distrust, intolerance, and conflicts, [the BAPS Hindu Mandir] brings hope to the world… I commend the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi for organizing this interfaith meeting… You share a respect for beliefs and an admiration for each other’s good-hearted intentions. Thank you for your commitment and dedication to promoting the values of peace, harmony, fraternity, and coexistence. Your strong resolve to work together across cultural and spiritual lines for the good of all humankind is truly noble.”
 The evening was also enriched with the words of Brahmaviharidas Swami, Head of the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi. While highlighting the Mandir’s message of love, peace, and harmony from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, he expressed sincere gratitude towards HH Mohamed bin Zayed al Nahyan, the Ruler of Abu Dhabi, the UAE leadership, and the gathered well-wishers for their support and generosity. Recounting the emotions of a former space scientist, he stated, “That if ever there are aliens, and if aliens come to this earth, I would rather have the aliens judge our planet by this place of harmony than all the conflicts, wars and monuments of hate in this world. I would rather have aliens judge the world by what’s happening in Abu Dhabi. So be proud that Abu Dhabi is the new capital of harmony of the world!”
 The gathering concluded with a vegetarian suhoor, blending Indian and Arabic cuisines, prepared by temple volunteers. Guests, including HE Sheikh Nahayan, partook in the dinner and enjoyed the time spent together as a community.
 ‘Omsiyyat: An Interfaith Cultural Evening’ touched the hearts of those not only in attendance, but also the community of the UAE and the world, demonstrating that, though interfaith harmony is an ongoing mission, for a moment, it has been achieved.

/News/2024/Pad-Yatra-10th-Anniversary-Ce.text:
Photo Gallery 
 10th Anniversary Pad-Yatra (28 photos)
 More than 300 devotees of various age groups participated in a devotional pad-yatra in Lisbon, Portugal, as part of the 10th anniversary celebrations of the opening of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir.
 The pad-yatra took place amid glorious summer sunshine on Sunday 12 May, starting at Alameda D. Afonso Henriques and concluding at the Mandir on Alameda Gago Coutinho. It followed the same route as the nagar yatra during the murti-pratishtha festival in 2014.
 Throughout the journey to the Mandir, participants sang kirtans, creating a joyful, devotional atmosphere. The local authorities and BAPS volunteers also provided essential support to all the walkers.
 Upon arrival at the Mandir, the participants enjoyed darshan of the murtis in the Mandir, thereafter gathering for a communal lunch.

/News/2024/Palkhi-Yatra--Festival-of-Har.t: Palkhi Yatra | Festival of Harmony, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/Palkhi-Yatra--Festival-of-Har.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Palkhi Yatra (94 photos)
 A grand, colorful Palkhi Yatra (devotional  procession), honoring the deities consecrated in the BAPS Hindu Mandir was held on the mandir grounds.
 During the Palkhi Yatra, the murtis were first ceremoniously placed on decorated palanquins. Then, senior swamis performed pujan of all the murtis, which were then lifted by the devotees of the various communities and carried around the circumambulatory path (parikrama) of the mandir, to bestow blessings to the community.
 Over 1,100 people, representing various local communities in the UAE participated. Diasporic communities in the UAE representing Kerala, Rajasthan, Orissa, Maharashtra, and others from north, south, east, west and central India participated in the procession wearing their traditional Indian attire and performing traditional devotional music and singing.
 Each carried a palanquin with the sacred murtis of the deities widely worshiped in their respective regions of India. It was the first time that such a pan-Indian procession had taken place in the UAE.
 After the Palkhi Yatra, all the participants attended the celebratory assembly in the presence of Pujya Doctor Swami, Pujya Avichaldasji Maharaj, Head of the Sat Kaival Sampradaya, and other senior BAPS swamis.
