/News/2024/Silver-Anniversary-Celebratio.t: Silver Anniversary Celebrations of BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Mahelav, India
/News/2024/Silver-Anniversary-Celebratio.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Silver Anniversary Celebrations (33 photos)
 On 22 January 1999, Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed the Vedic murti-pratishtha of the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Mahelav – the birthplace of BAPS founder Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj.
 To commemorate its 25th anniversary (patotsav), year-long activities were organized in Mahelav and the surrounding towns and villages.
 The 10-day finale celebrations were held in Mahelav on a 12–acre plot that was transformed into the ‘Yagnapurush Nagar’.
 The Yagnapurush Nagar was ritually opened by Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami, Shri Ramanbhai Solanki (Deputy Chief Whip, Gujarat), Shri Miteshbhai Patel MP, and other dignitaries.
 The wonderful festival site featured exhibition halls: ‘Yagnapurush Jivan Darshan’ on the life and work of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, ‘Sant Param Hitkari’ on the life and work of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, ‘Ghar Sabha’ on family values, ‘Hamara Bharat, Mera Bharat’ on how to become an exemplary and responsible citizen of India, and ‘Buzo’ on respecting parents. A Bal Nagari was also set up to provide children enjoyment coupled with cultural and spiritual education.
 A total of 127,000 people viewed the exhibitions, including 15,000 students and 600 teachers from 120 schools.
 The 10-day celebrations were planned, organized and managed by over 1,450 men and women volunteers.
 On 26 January, a grand Women’s Assembly was held.
 On 31 January, Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami, Pujya Viveksagar Swami and other swamis performed the Vedic rituals to commemorate the 25th patotsav of the BAPS Mandir in Mahelav.

/News/2024/Silver-Jubilee-Celebrations-o.t: Silver Jubilee Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Augusta, GA, USA
/News/2024/Silver-Jubilee-Celebrations-o.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Akshar-Purushottam Vadhamana & Patotsav (42 photos)
 Women's Cultural Program (18 photos)
 Children's Cultural Program (22 photos)
 Grand Finale (20 photos)
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Augusta, GA, celebrated its 25th anniversary with a series of festivities from August 15th to 18th, 2024. The events were themed around Samarpan (Sacrifice), Sanskruti (Heritage), and Smruti (Reflection), with each day featuring a variety of activities, presentations, and performances that highlighted the significance of the occasion. Volunteers created a vibrant and festive atmosphere at both the mandir and Maxwell Theater at Augusta University’s Grover C. Maxwell Performing Arts Center. Revered BAPS swamis, along with government officials such as State Representatives Gary Richardson, Jodi Lott, Harold Jones II, Columbia County Chairman Doug Duncan, and Vice Chair Connie Melear, joined over 700 devotees and well-wishers from the region to commemorate this milestone.
 The celebrations began on August 15th with Akshar-Purushottam Vadhamana, where 13 revered swamis and devotees welcomed Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj with Vedic chants, pujan, and a grand procession around the mandir. The day continued with a mahapuja performed by the swamis and concluded with an inspiring spiritual talk by Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami.
 On August 16th, the Women’s Cultural Celebration took place with the theme of Samarpan (Sacrifice). The day featured performances, presentations, dramas, panel discussions, and devotional songs, with female devotees of all ages participating. The program also honored long-time residents of the region who contributed to the community’s growth and played a vital role in the development of the mandir.
 The Children’s Day Celebration on August 17th, themed Sanskruti (Heritage), was held at Maxwell Theater. The event showcased the mandir’s role in teaching and preserving cultural values. Organized and led by BAPS youths, aged 5 to 25, the program included engaging elements such as games, activities, and a puppet show with key cultural messages. The day was centered around the journey of a young boy, illustrating how the mandir contributed to his personal growth and the formation of his identity. The celebration concluded with a grand fireworks display at the mandir.
 The final day, August 18th, was dedicated to Smruti Din (Reflection), where the history of BAPS Augusta was brought to life through drama skits, panel discussions, and spiritual talks by the swamis. Under the visionary leadership of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the initial plans for a Hindu mandir in Augusta were set in motion in 1988, leading to the establishment of a traditional mandir, inaugurated in 1998. The current spiritual leader, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, blessed the mandir with his presence in 2003. The celebrations concluded with an energetic and grand dance performance by the youths of BAPS.

/News/2024/Smruti-Yatra-26140.aspx.t: Smruti Yatra: Anniversary of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s 2023 visit to Canada, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2024/Smruti-Yatra-26140.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Smruti Sabha (32 photos)
 Smruti Yatra Exhibition (72 photos)
 Exhibition Viewing (50 photos)
 Mandir Campus Smruti Yatra (13 photos)
 From June 8-16, 2024, devotees and well-wishers gathered at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto to celebrate the ‘Smruti Yatra,’ marking the first anniversary of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s 2023 visit to Canada. This auspicious occasion was a time of deep reflection and joyous remembrance for all who cherish the spiritual teachings and presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The celebrations centered around the theme that recalling the divine episodes of God, and Guru alleviates our worries and sorrows, fostering spiritual growth and inner peace. Families and individuals alike participated in various activities designed to relive the memorable moments from his visit a year ago.
 Highlights of the festivities included two special ‘Smruti Sabhas,’ spiritual assemblies where attendees revisited precious memories through video collages, heartfelt speeches by volunteers, and recounted anecdotes of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s interactions during his stay. Every aspect of his visit was cherished and celebrated, from the grand Rath Yatra and sacred arti rituals to glimpses of his morning puja and interactions with guests.
 A notable feature of the anniversary celebration was a special exhibition housed in the gymnasium. It showcased artifacts and items sanctified by Mahant Swami Maharaj himself. Attendees could also explore a recreated glimpse of his residence, offering a personal connection to his spiritual presence and teachings.
 The event featured a 'Smruti Trail' around the Mandir campus, allowing devotees and well-wishers to visit various sanctified spots associated with Mahant Swami Maharaj. Each spot included displays featuring photos of activities that occurred there, along with QR codes to view video highlights.
 There was also a volunteer appreciation assembly, a testament to the invaluable role of the volunteers in making Mahant Swami Maharaj's visit a resounding success. These dedicated individuals were acknowledged for their tireless efforts in organizing and facilitating the celebrations; their contributions serving as a beacon of inspiration for the entire community.
 A 'Smruti Board' was set up in the front lobby, where attendees could write down their favorite memories of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visit and add them to the board, creating a collective reflection of cherished moments.
 In addition to community gatherings, devotees marked the occasion at home with ‘Smruti Ghar Sabhas,’ to help children and adults come together, interact, and learn to understand each other better. They delved into Mahant Swami Maharaj’s teachings and discussed ways to incorporate his exemplary qualities into their daily lives.
 The first anniversary of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visit was a resounding success, uniting the community in gratitude and inspiration as they fondly recalled the profound impact of his spiritual presence. The ‘Smruti Mahotsav’ not only celebrated memories from the past but also reaffirmed the enduring teachings and guidance that continue to enrich lives within the Hindu community in Canada and beyond.

/News/2024/Spirituality-in-Stone-First-S.t: Spirituality in Stone: First Stone Sanctification Ceremony, Paris, France
/News/2024/Spirituality-in-Stone-First-S.text:
As the sun rose in the capital of Gujarat, India, a new milestone dawned for the capital of France.
 The first block of stone for the first traditional Hindu temple in France – BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, Paris – was ceremonially blessed by its creator, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In sanctifying the stone, he inspired each soul with the supreme purpose of the mandir – as he truly sees it – revealing the transcendental glory and compassion of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in descending upon our world.
 To learn more about the Mandir and to stay up to date about its construction, visit the website bapsmandirparis.fr and follow @BAPSParis on X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Telegram, and YouTube.

 Dr. Pujya Gnanvatsaldas Swami, renowned for his impactful teachings, has touched millions globally. With the guidance and blessings of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, he has delivered over 15,000 life-enhancement talks, promoting messages of goodness and universal harmony.
 During the seminar, Gnanvatsaldas Swami provided practical advice on managing stress in both personal and professional contexts. He emphasized the importance of balancing work and personal life and the role of quality family time in achieving this balance, offering valuable insights to help individuals manage stress more effectively.

/News/2024/Swami-Brahmaviharidas-Express.t: Swami Brahmaviharidas Expresses Gratitude to Prime Minister Modi, New Delhi, India
/News/2024/Swami-Brahmaviharidas-Express.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Meeting with Prime Minister Modi (4 photos)
 On behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the entire BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, and the community at large of the UAE, Swami Brahmaviharidas met Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at his residence at 11AM.
 Swami Brahmaviharidas expressed his heartfelt gratitude to the Prime Minister, presenting him with a garland that had been specially blessed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, accompanied by special prayers from His Holiness for the Prime Minister's health, well-being and for him to lead India for many more years to come.
 Swami Brahmaviharidas specially thanked the Prime Minister for overseeing the Abu Dhabi BAPS Hindu Mandir project from its inception to its completion and gave a brief report of the Mandir after its inauguration.
 The Mandir has been received with overwhelming warmth by the UAE community and visitors from around the world, welcoming 65,000 visitors on its first public Sunday and consistently attracting thousands daily who patiently line up in an orderly manner for peaceful darshan. It has been the venue for celebrating festivals, such as Maha Shivaratri, with plans to continue embracing such vibrant festivals, rituals, and traditions. These festivities, while attracting large gatherings have served a deeper purpose; they have generated greater cultural, social and spiritual harmony.
 While expressing gratitude to the Rulers of the UAE for their largeheartedness and support, the Prime Minister appreciated the swamis and volunteers of the BAPS Sanstha for their time, selfless service, and immense dedication put behind the creation of the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi. He stated:
 “Our culture, our country, and humanity shall remain thankful for the harmony the BAPS Hindu Mandir is spreading.”

/News/2024/Swaminarayan--Akshardham-Obse.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Earth Hour 2024 (2 photos)
 Swaminarayan  Akshardham in New Delhi participated in Earth Hour 2024, organized by the WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature), in support of protecting our planet.
 Earth Hour encourages individuals, communities and organizations to turn off their lights for one hour to symbolize a commitment to positive environment impact. BAPS Mandirs turned off its non-essential lights to observe Earth Hour from 8:30 to 9:30 pm on 23 March 2024.
 Earth Hour is the the world’s largest environmental event and a global movement which unites millions of people across the globe showing commitment to the planet.
 Inspired by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS is involved in Earth Hour and many other sustainability initiatives as part of a broader commitment to support positive environmental practices.

/News/2024/Tenth-Anniversary-Celebration.t: Tenth Anniversary Celebrations, BAPS Mandir, Jamnagar, India
/News/2024/Tenth-Anniversary-Celebration.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mahila Din (15 photos)
 Patotsav (24 photos)
 A three-day celebration marked the tenth anniversary (patotsav) of the BAPS Mandir in Jamnagar.
 On 2 March, over 1,000 women attended the special Mahila Din assembly.
 On 3 March, around 950 bal, yuva, vadil and mahila karyakars attended the Karyakar Convention.
 On the morning of 4 March, the tenth patotsav rituals were performed by Dharmacharan Swami, Rajeshwar Swami and other swamis. In the evening, devotees participated in the patotsav mahapuja ceremony and over 7,800 devotees attended the celebration assembly.

/News/2024/The-Creator-of-Creators-25044.t: The Creator of Creators, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/The-Creator-of-Creators-25044.text: This video creatively captures the final finishing of the iconic and historic BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi through the words of a team of selfless creators – the architects who have designed, the artisans who have crafted, the volunteers who have served, the directors who have guided, and the saints who have inspired… However behind these creators is the creator! The spiritual source and force of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj. With facts and figures of the final stage, everyone reaffirms their faith with innermost gratitude to their God and Guru who have spiritually shaped and created them.

/News/2024/Timeless-Inspirations-from-Hi.t: Timeless Inspirations from Hindu Festivals, Asia Pacific
/News/2024/Timeless-Inspirations-from-Hi.text:
The BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute in Australia organized a series of conferences titled ‘Timeless Inspirations from Hindu Festivals’, celebrating the spiritual and cultural essence of key Hindu festivals. The conferences were held in Melbourne, Sydney, Perth and Brisbane (Australia) and Auckland (New Zealand). Around 200 representatives from over 115 organizations from various community groups, and Hindu temples and organizations participated in the conferences, which were attended by over 5,800 people.
 Each conference featured a keynote address that explored the profound meanings behind three Hindu festivals: Janmashtami, Ram Navami and Ganesh Chaturthi. The significance of each festival was discussed in depth: Bhagwan Shri Krishna's teachings on devotion and karma; Bhagwan Shri Ram's ideals of virtue and leadership; and the wisdom and obstacle-removing powers of Shri Ganeshji.
 Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami also presented deep insights into the philosophical significance of these festivals.
 Additionally, traditional dance performances and celebrations were organized to represent these festivals as well as the Rath Yatra and Navaratri festivals.
 Also, certificates were awarded to students who had completed the ‘Introduction to Hinduism’ course conducted by the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Australia. In addition, the new ‘Memorising Sanskrit Verses from the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita’ course was launched.
 The conferences fostered unity within the global Hindu community, reinforcing the importance of devotion, harmony, and spiritual growth.

/News/2024/Tree-Planting-Campaign-26263..text:
Photo Gallery 
 Tree Plantation (14 photos)
 The launch ceremony of the Tree Planting Campaign organized by the BAPS Paryavaran Seva Kendra at the BAPS Mandir in Gadhada was held in the presence of BAPS swamis, distinguished guests and devotees. After the assembly, swamis and guests planted trees in the mandir grounds.
 Throughout the region, over 2,000 devotees from around 100 villages near Gadhada participated in the project to plant over 5,000 fruit-bearing trees.
 Of the 5,000 trees planted last year (2023), 80% (4,000) have been successfully nurtured and are thriving.

/News/2024/Tulsi-Gabbard-Visits-BAPS-Swa.t: Former Congresswoman Tulsi Gabbard Visits BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2024/Tulsi-Gabbard-Visits-BAPS-Swa.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Tulsi Gabbard Visits BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham (35 photos)
 On Sunday, December 15, 2024, BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham had the honor of hosting former Congresswoman Tulsi Gabbard, the first Hindu elected to the U.S. Congress in 2013. In addition to her distinguished political career, Gabbard serves as a lieutenant colonel in the U.S. Army Reserve, a rank she has held since 2021.
 Her visit coincided with the 103rd birth anniversary celebrations of the late Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the revered spiritual leader who profoundly impacted millions through his teachings of selfless service, humility, and devotion. The event brought together women of all ages to commemorate Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s legacy. The celebration featured inspiring speeches and heartfelt vignettes, highlighting his timeless teachings and the significance of faith and service in everyday life.
 Envisioned by the late Pramukh Swami Maharaj, BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham stands as a beacon of spirituality, tradition, and culture. Its rich heritage has drawn visitors from diverse backgrounds, making it a revered landmark. During her visit, former Congresswoman Gabbard, renowned for her advocacy and dedication to issues affecting all Americans, embarked on a campus tour where she explored the universal values expressed through Akshardham's art, architecture, and cultural exhibits.
 As a practicing Hindu for many years, Gabbard admired the spiritual atmosphere of Akshardham. She offered flowers and prayers to the sacred images enshrined in the temple.
 During her address at the cultural program, Ms. Gabbard expressed her gratitude and inspiration: "I’m grateful to be here with all of you, and my heart is warmed by this incredible welcome and celebration. To be able to hear about the many thousands of hands and hearts that went into building this iconic temple, and to walk through and see the meaning behind every single one of those sculptures—both the magnificent and the small etchings of some of the most famous stories about Krishna and Arjuna from the Bhagavad Gita—was truly inspiring. This place is special because of all of you, your hearts, and your prayers that bring us all together."
 She also reflected on the temple’s spiritual essence during an interview, saying: "Words are not sufficient to describe the incredible product of the work of so many hands that came together in a spirit of love, kindness, and unity. That welcoming spirit is something I feel here, as I know millions of others do when they visit Akshardham. This is a timeless offering that will bring peace and joy to all who come."
 Former Congresswoman Gabbard's visit served as a powerful reminder of the enduring legacy of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and his emphasis on bringing people together through shared values of faith, service, and community. Her presence at Akshardham reflected the temple’s role as a place of inspiration, uniting individuals across generations and backgrounds. It also underscored the commitment of BAPS and its current spiritual leader, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, to promote selfless service and strengthen communities across the United States.

/News/2024/UAE-National-Shibir-Lotus-in-.t: UAE National Shibir: Lotus in the Desert, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2024/UAE-National-Shibir-Lotus-in-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Lotus in the Desert (54 photos)
 Around 840 people, including 115 children and 71 teenagers, participated in the first UAE National Shibir to be held at the recently inaugurated BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi. The day-long shibir was themed ‘Lotus in the Desert’. Based on the inspiring story of the mandir’s creation, the delegates were encouraged to internalize the message: “If the mandir is our heart, let us make our heart into a mandir. Hence, the same quality, sincerity and intensity of focused efforts that went into constructing this majestic mandir should be applied to our own lives.”
 The shibir sessions featured presentations on the mandir’s construction process, skits, group discussions and interactive quizzes, all combining to provide the delegates details of the spiritual effort needed to build the inner mandir.
 Preparing the Land – Introspection: Highlighted the importance of inner preparation, deep introspection, engaging one’s mind on the Satpurush. This helps to remove negative habits and cultivate a pure heart, akin to preparing land for construction.
 Strong Foundation – Prapti: Pujya Viveksagardas Swami explained the passion of prapti and how it cements a strong foundation in satsang, comparable to the strong environmentally friendly foundations of the mandir.
 Resources – Virtues of the Satpurush: Through association with and contemplation on the Satpurush, one can acquire inner resources – the virtues of the Satpurush; these are equivalent to the resources required for building a physical mandir.
 Challenges – Addressing the Inner Issues: During a Q&A session, Brahmaviharidas Swami provided clear and concise practical guidance on how to overcome inner challenges, parallel to the series of obstacles that were overcome during the mandir’s construction.
 The toddlers, kids, teenagers and youth participated in their own separate shibirs on the same theme. Their activities were tailored to their level of understanding, including team building exercises, treasure hunts, scavenger hunts, puppet shows, and letter writing.
 The shibir inspired the participants with a personal spiritual resolve to ‘Make a Mandir in Our Hearts.’

/News/2024/Vedanta-Conferences-by-BAPS-S.t: Vedanta Conferences by BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Australia
/News/2024/Vedanta-Conferences-by-BAPS-S.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Perth (19 photos)
 Sydney (23 photos)
 The essence of Vedic inquiry, knowledge and philosophy is termed 'Vedanta'. Continuing its promotion of this ancient wisdom within the modern context, BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Australia (BSRIA) organized Vedanta Conferences in Perth and Sydney.
 The conferences were presided over by Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami and world-renowned scholar Prof. Ram Kishor Tripathi, Head, Vedanta Department, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Varanasi and Upadhyaksh of the highly respected Kashi Vidvat Parishad.
 Speakers presented lucid talks on topics such as Relevance of Vedanta in the Modern Age, Importance of Sanskrit Learning and Vedic Sanatan Dharma. Audience members also had the opportunity to interact with the scholars through Q & A sessions which provided a deeper understanding of Vedic philosophy.
 The conference concluded with certificates being awarded to students who had recently completed some of the many Vedanta and Sanskrit-based courses offered by BSRIA.
 Various social, spiritual and academic organizations presented Prof. Tripathi with letters of appreciation and expressed their gratitude to BSRIA for organizing the conferences.
 Prof. Tripathi also appreciated BSRIA's effort in promoting Indian philosophy and knowledge systems abroad, especially among the younger generation.

/News/2024/Vedic-Groundbreaking-Ceremony.t: Vedic Groundbreaking Ceremony of a New BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Charlotte, NC, USA
/News/2024/Vedic-Groundbreaking-Ceremony.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Vedic Groundbreaking Ceremony (37 photos)
 With the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the tireless dedication, unwavering faith, and relentless efforts of the devotees of Charlotte reached a momentous milestone on Sunday, June 9, 2024. This date marked the Vedic Groundbreaking Ceremony (Bhumi Pujan) for the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Charlotte, North Carolina.
 Charlotte and its surrounding areas have been blessed by the spiritual visits (vicharan) of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj over the years. As the number of devotees grew, the existing facilities became insufficient to meet the expanding needs of the Hindu-American community in terms of cultural, social, and religious activities. Consequently, the construction of the new Mandir and Satsang Activity Center became imperative to address the evolving needs.
 The Bhumi Pujan ceremony included a traditional mahapuja ritual that blessed the land amid Vedic chants and prayers for peace and well-being to prevail throughout the local community. The ceremony, attended by over 900 devotees and well-wishers from Charlotte and the surrounding areas, marked a significant milestone in the construction of the new Mandir. The event was graced by the presence of revered Swamis, including Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, Pujya Shantmurtidas Swami, Pujya Shukmunidas Swami, Pujya Munitilakdas Swami, Pujya Adarshnayandas Swami, and Pujya Agampriyadas Swami. Earlier, Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the pujan of the soil in India and blessed everyone involved. Several distinguished guests attended the ceremony, including Mr. John Higdon, Mayor of Matthews, and Ms. Mary-Ann Baldwin, Mayor of Raleigh. Also present were the project architects, engineers, and community members.
 The Bhumi Pujan ceremony signified the beginning of a new chapter in BAPS Charlotte's history, which dates back to 1996 when Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the first Mandir. The new Mandir will serve as a hub for spiritual activities, cultural programs,and community service initiatives including health fairs, walkathons, blood donation drives, and other volunteer based efforts further strengthening the bonds of unity amongst all in the community.

 In Ahmedabad, on 28 March 2024, Mahant Swami Maharaj had sanctified five stone shilas. Together with the nidhi kumbha, these shilas were ceremoniously placed by Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami in the foundation pit of the mandir.

/News/2024/Vishwashanti-Mahayagna-Swamin.t: Vishwashanti Mahayagna, Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India
/News/2024/Vishwashanti-Mahayagna-Swamin.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Vishwashanti Mahayagna (26 photos)
 On the auspicious occasion of Vijaya Dashami (Dussehra), approximately 2,000 devotees, including 900 couples, participated in the Vishwashanti Mahayagna at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, offering prayers for world peace.
 Gathered around 114 specially prepared yagna kunds, the devotees chanted sacred Vedic mantras and made traditional offerings, drawing upon the spiritual power of the yagna to honor ancient traditions. The recitation of 315 verses from the Satsang Diksha shastra further enriched the spiritual atmosphere. Special prayers were offered for peaceful co-existence in a world facing numerous challenges.
 Following the Mahayagna, Munivatsal Swami addressed the assembly, “On this day, which symbolizes the victory of good over evil, we have come together with the hope that peace prevails everywhere, in our environment, in society, in our families and within each individual. We pray for lasting happiness, good health, and harmony within families. The Vedic mantras and the Swaminarayan Mahamantra recited during this yagna should resonate within us. Let this moment be one of self-reflection, where we strive to conquer the 'Ravana' within ourselves, overcoming our inner negativity. We also pray for an end to conflicts and for peace everywhere.”

 The event featured a vibrant program, where women of all ages expressed their devotion through various cultural performances, including traditional dances, devotional songs, and insightful skits. Inspiring speeches further delved into the significance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection with the Guru, reminding everyone of the encouragement and guidance Mahant Swami Maharaj provides for their personal, professional, and spiritual journeys.
 Throughout the celebration, devotees had an opportunity to remember Mahant Swami Maharaj's presence in their lives, whether through his physical darshan or his spiritual presence. The event not only celebrated his birth but also the enduring relationship between the Guru and his devotees.

/News/2024/Womens-Celebrations-of-HH-Pra.t: Women's Celebrations of HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 103rd Birthday, North America
/News/2024/Womens-Celebrations-of-HH-Pra.text:
Women devotees gathered at BAPS Mandirs across North America to honor the divine legacy of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj through a special birthday celebration themed "Amar Vārso Gunātitno: Everlasting Legacy." The celebration highlighted the profound contributions of Pramukh Swami Maharaj in shaping the BAPS organization in North America over the past 50 years, offering an opportunity to reflect on his timeless virtues, tireless efforts, and divine impact on individuals and communities alike.
 The program highlighted three key aspects of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's life: Bhaktavatsal(love) celebrated his boundless compassion towards devotees, inspiring attendees to embody his nurturing care in their everyday interactions; Parabhakti (devotion) emphasized his unwavering dedication to Bhagwan and adherence to personal devotion despite his tremendous responsibilities, inspiring devotees to prioritize and incorporate time for their personal spiritual practices; Prabhavi Yugpurusham (influential figure of the millennium) reflected on the legacy of his personal sacrifice in caring for individuals and communities, instilling faith in God across generations, and inspiring devotees to foster unity and spirituality within their families and communities.
 Women of all ages participated in the program, expressing their bhakti through devotional songs and traditional dances as a heartfelt tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Through thought-provoking speeches, devotees explored his selfless travels, the countless individuals he inspired, and the mandirs he gifted for the benefit of all. Skits relayed his enduring presence through personal impact and transformations, which continues to flourish under the guidance of guru Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 As BAPS marks its 50th year in North America, the celebration served as a reminder of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's monumental role in growing satsang across the continent. His unwavering commitment to nurturing spirituality and inspiring future generations remains a guiding light, ensuring that his divine legacy continues to shape lives and communities for generations to come.

The tournament emphasizes the values of unity, solidarity, and oneness taught by Yogiji Maharaj. Over three enriching days, participants dive deep into the theory and application of these core principles, experiencing personal growth, teamwork, and leadership.
 Crafted under the meticulous guidance of Pujya Swamis and dedicated volunteers, the Yogi Cup Tournament also weave the fabric of satsang into every aspect of the competition—for example, all participants partake in morning and evening sessions designed to reinforce spiritual teachings and practices.
 The Yogi Cup serves as platforms for participants to have fun, deepen their spiritual journeys, and strengthen their bonds with their guru and peers. The BAPS Yogi Cup Tournament are annual sporting events where youths ages 14-30, gather to compete in their respective regions. It promotes the messages of Samp, Suhradbhav and Ekta, values instilled by Yogiji Maharaj, to bring the participants together. 
 A cornerstone of the tournament is its ability to unify geographically dispersed centers, fostering a collective spirit of togetherness. Rooted in the values of samp (unity), suhradbhav (solidarity), and ekta (oneness), the tournament is inspired by Yogiji Maharaj’s teachings. These principles are woven into every aspect of the event, offering youth the opportunity to experience and embody these timeless lessons.
 Beyond sports, the tournament serves as a platform for personal, professional, and spiritual development. Youth are encouraged to cultivate interpersonal skills such as teamwork, trust, leadership, and collaboration while being immersed in satsang values. Each day begins and ends with rituals such as arti and cheshta, accompanied by thoughtfully designed morning and evening programs. These activities reinforce the significance of satsang in daily life and deepen participants' understanding of how to apply the lessons learned at mandir and through the tournament to their life experiences.
 The event is a testament to the ongoing vision of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who carries forward the legacy of gurus Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Their vision of a united group of individuals ready to make a positive impact on the world is at the forefront of their teachings. Through initiatives like the Yogi Cup, youth are encouraged to engage actively in satsang, summer conventions, community service, and other enriching activities.
 Ultimately, the tournaments are more than just competitions—they are transformative experiences that help the youths  connect with their guru, strengthen their spirituality, and build lifelong bonds through the shared values of samp, suhradbhav, and ekta.

 The seminars emphasized to youths the profound effect the people they associate with and the media they interact with can have on them.  The youths also participated in interactive sessions via video conference with Dr Chirag Patel, Chief Medical Officer of Central Jersey Urgent Care, and Shri Mayur Patel, Equity Portfolio Manager at JP Morgan. Both guests, who are dedicated BAPS devotees living in the USA, shared insights from their inspiring career paths – particularly elaborating on how carefully choosing the influences in their lives has played a crucial role in their achievements. Youths asked questions to learn from the guests’ inspiring career journeys, and understand how they themselves could take steps to achieve success.

/News/2024/Youth-Seminars-Mandir---Unlea.t: Youth Seminars: 'Mandir - Unleash Inner Potential', Asia Pacific
/News/2024/Youth-Seminars-Mandir---Unlea.text:
Over 1,300 youths from BAPS centers across Australia and New Zealand – Adelaide, Auckland, Brisbane, Canberra, Darwin, Hamilton, Melbourne, Sydney, Perth, and Wellington – participated in the 10 one-day Youth Seminars themed ‘Mandir: Unleash Inner Potential’.
 The seminars demonstrated the multifaceted role of mandirs in enhancing individual and community well-being. By providing platforms for skill development, and fostering inner strength and spirituality, mandirs contribute significantly to the holistic growth of individuals and the community at large. 
 The seminars featured presentations from swamis, panel discussions, youth interviews and inspiring videos emphasizing the importance of mandirs in today’s day and age.
 The events provided attendees with a renewed sense of purpose and connection to their cultural and spiritual roots.

/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir--Yatra-A-Path-of-.t: Yuva Shibir & Yatra: 'A Path of Happiness', Himmatnagar, India
/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir--Yatra-A-Path-of-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (57 photos)
 Over 1,000 yuvaks and yuvatis from Himmatnagar and surrounding districts participated in the three-day Yuva Shibir and Yatra themed ‘A Path of Happiness’.
 The 1½-day shibir was held at the BAPS Mandir in Sankari, in which the youths were guided through speeches by learned and experienced swamis and volunteers. The shibir also included workshops, discussions and other activities for the youths.
 As part of the yatra, the youths had darshan at Nadiad, Bharuch, Navsari, Kanad (Surat), Chansad and other sacred sites.

/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-2024-Andar-Akshar.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (111 photos)
 In October 2023, following the inauguration of the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in North America, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “The physical Akshardham has been built. Now it is time to make Akshardham within.”
 Inspired by this vision, over 3,000 yuvaks and yuvatis from Surat participated in a five-day residential shibir at Akshar Mandir, Gondal. Themed ‘Andar Akshardham’, the shibir focused on building Akshardham within by cultivating virtues like agna and upasana that lead to ultimate happiness.
 To help participants internalize these principles, the shibir featured insightful discourses by learned BAPS swamis, engaging workshops, creative dramas, videos, dance performances, podcasts, debates, and a vibrant kirtan bhakti programme performed by swamis and youths
 Also, in the sacred Akshar Deri, delegates participated in the morning mahapuja rituals and offered pradakshina around the shrine.
 The shibir guided attendees in aligning their lives with the vision of Mahant Swami Maharaj by providing practical tools to strengthen their personal spirituality, cultivate virtues, and build a life centred on God and guru.

 Yuva Shibir (15 photos)
 Over 2,645 yuvaks and yuvatis from the rural villages near Vadodara attended the one-day Yuva Shibir held at Chansad, the birthplace of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-2024-My-Guru-My-L.t: Yuva Shibir 2024: ‘My Guru, My Life’, Sankari, India
/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-2024-My-Guru-My-L.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (33 photos)
 Around 900 yuvaks and yuvatis from BAPS centers in the South Gujarat districts of Kamrej and Vyara attended the 1½-day Yuva Shibir themed ‘My Guru, My Life’, in which the first session was held at the BAPS Mandir in Sankari. The following morning, the second session was held in Vyara and in the evening, the third session was held in Ukai.
 At each venue, the youths were guided on the shibir theme by learned swamis and also participated in discussions, workshops and other activities.

/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-2024-Nishthavan-B.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shibir (39 photos)
 More than 1,600 youths from throughout Vadodara attended this one-day Yuva Shibir, based on the theme ‘Nishthavan Bhava’, held at Chansad, the birthplace of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 After the keynote address by Rajeshwar Swami, the youths learnt about the glory of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, Parabrahma Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami, and other important aspects of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya through speeches and presentations by Shrutiprakash Swami. Also, in a question-answer session, he clarified any confusions. The shibir also featured the video blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 After the Shibir, all the youths performed Guruhari Pujan Vidhi at Narayan Sarovar.

/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-Darshan-Yatra-to-.t: Yuva Shibir-Darshan Yatra to Commemorate Silver Jubilee of BAPS Mandir, Tithal, India
/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-Darshan-Yatra-to-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (36 photos)
 To celebrate the 25th anniversary of the BAPS Mandir in Tithal, situated on the coast of the Arabian Sea in South Gujarat, over 460 yuvaks and yuvatis joined a four-day Yuva Shibir-Darshan Yatra. The youths traveled to Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gadhdha, Gondal, Limbdi, Nadiad, and Chansad, the birthplace of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The youths were delighted and inspired by darshan at all the sacred places, and also participated in the mahapuja at Akshar Deri, Gondal, and the maha-arti and mahapuja at Narayan Sarovar, Chansad.
 In Sarangpur, the youths attended a one-day shibir on the theme ‘Prapti: Andar Akshardham’ in which they were guided by discourses from Narayanmuni Swami, Atmatrupt Swami, and other swamis. They also participated in workshops other activities. In the evening the resident swamis of Sarangpur presented a melodious kirtan aradhana.

/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-Sanatanam-Back-to.t: Yuva Shibir: ‘Sanatanam: Back to Our Roots’, Abu Road, Rajasthan, India
/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-Sanatanam-Back-to.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (34 photos)
 More than 250 yuvaks and yuvatis from across Rajasthan participated in the two-day shibir ‘Sanatanam: Back to our Roots’ held at Abu Road.
 Through speeches by learned and experienced swamis, workshops, discussions, skits, videos and involvement activities, the shibir guided the youths on India’s rich heritage of mandirs, shastras and saints, cultural values, moral and ethical living and strengthened their pride as devout followers of Sanatan dharma.
 During their stay, the youths also visited places sanctified by Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj in Mt. Abu.

/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-for-Navsari-Youth.t: Yuva Shibir for Navsari Youths, Gadhada, India
/News/2024/Yuva-Shibir-for-Navsari-Youth.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (67 photos)
 More than 500 yuvaks and yuvatis of Navsari attended the 3-day Yuva Shibir held at the BAPS Mandir in Gadhada based on the theme 'His Words, Our Mission'.
 The shibir theme was presented in three sections:
 His Words, Our Life: which discussed the importance of living as per Swamishri's wish by practicing daily devotional rituals, sincerely observing niyam-dharma and using social media with proper discretion.
 His Words, Our Strength: which explained the glory of the Akshar-Purushottam upasana and the great fortune of having attained such a profound spiritual path to follow in one’s life.
 His Words, Our Mission: which discussed the role of the youths in promoting this profound spiritual path as per the wish of the Gunatit gurus.
 Each section was elaborated upon through speeches, workshops, skits, discussions, videos and other activities. Among the speakers were Narayanmuni Swami, Bhaktisagar Swami, Atmatrupt Swami, and other learned and experienced swamis.
 The youths also enjoyed a yatra, visiting the holy places in Gadhada sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Jiva Khachar’s Darbar and the exhibition ‘Gadhpur Jota Shriji Sambhare’ at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir.
 The youths also had darshan at the mandirs and other sacred places in Sarangpur; Dhari, the birthplace of Yogiji Maharaj; and Mahuva, the birthplace of Bhagatji Maharaj.
 In Mahuva, the youths were blessed with the samip darshan of guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2024/Yuvak-Antar-Jagruti-Parva-202.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Antar Jagruti Parva (37 photos)
 The 60 yuvaks of the first Yuva Talim Kendra (YTK) batch of 2024 conducted vicharan in various regions across Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.
 The 15 groups of four youths traveled to a total of 123 villages, where they visited the homes of 1,681 devotees and well-wishers, emphasizing the importance of satsang values to sustain family harmony. They inspired 1,469 families to pledge to attend weekly satsang assemblies, do daily puja, go to their local mandir for darshan, read Swamini Vato and Vachanamrut daily, fast on ekadashi, conduct ghar sabha regularly, and engage in other satsang practices.
 The youths also held 122 satsang assemblies, attended by 8,676 people. They also held 76 assemblies for children, and 49 school assemblies, in which they provided guidance to a total of 12,367 children. In the evenings, the yuvaks would host special devotional processions in the villages, in which 2,327 people participated. They also inspired 534 people to give up their addictions.
 Through these visits, the youths gained a wider perspective on how to contribute productively to and serve society.

/News/2024/Yuvak-Antar-Jagruti-Parva-202.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Antar Jagruti Parva (37 photos)
 The 197 trainees youths of the second Yuva Talim Kendra (YTK) batch of 2024 split up into 48 groups of four to travel to various regions across Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan to participate in the Antar Jagruti Parva.
 The youth traveled to 464 villages, where they contacted 6,197 households. During these visits, they spoke about the importance of satsang values and inspired 4,476 families to take different vows to help nurture their spirituality. This included attending weekly satsang assemblies, doing daily puja, going to their local mandir for darshan, reading Swamini Vato and Vachanamrut regularly, fasting on ekadashi, doing ghar sabha regularly, and other such satsang rituals and practices.
 During their visits, they held a total of 417 satsang assemblies, during which over 21,625 people enjoyed their speeches and bhajans. They also held 171 assemblies for children, and 317 school assemblies, providing guidance to over 57,165 children. In the evenings, the yuvaks held special devotional processions through the villages, in which more than 4,600 people participated. They also inspired 1,300 people to give up various addictions.
 Through this program, the YTK youths gained a wider perspective on how to improve their own lives and better serve society.

 During the holy months of Chaturmas, thousands of yuvaks and yuvatis participated in the Yuva Parayans held throughout Gujarat and other states of India.
 Using the content prepared by the Satsang Pravutti Central Office (SPCO) in Ahmedabad, the three-day parayans were conducted by over 900 yuvak and 1,200 yuvati mandals.
 This year, the parayans were conducted on selected chapters of the Shri Harililamrut shastra. Based on the stories of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine exploits and the inspiring lives of his devotees, the youths learnt about cultivating nishtha, observing niyams and dharma, and strengthening harmony and fraternity.
 The daily programs included discourses by youths, dramas and videos.

/News/2024/Yuvak-Yuvati-Summer-Shibir-20.text:
After years of dedication and tireless efforts by volunteers from across North America, BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville was inaugurated in October 2023 by His Holiness  Mahant Swami Maharaj.. As the magnificent mandir neared completion, he imparted a profound message: "Our lives should reflect this extraordinary and divine Akshardham. The physical Akshardham has been built. Now it is time to make Akshardham within. Only then is our goal complete."  That vision guided the theme of "Andar Akshardham" – an inner temple within our hearts and minds.
 In line with this vision, the 2024 Yuvak-Yuvati Summer Shibir took place across North America. This convention provided a platform for deeper understanding and practical steps to embody the concept of "Andar Akshardham." Delegates attended various sessions and breakout discussions encompassing key  messages.
 Sukh in Satsang | Prapti: Our Attainment | Prapti no Vichar 
 As yuvaks and yuvatis mature in satsang, they find lasting happiness through the teachings and lifestyle taught by the guru, emphasizing servitude and seeing divinity in others. Delegates discussed their satsang journeys, recognizing the constant pursuit of growth in careers and education while also ensuring the development of spirituality. Mahant Swami Maharaj's guidance highlighted that by focusing on the divine attainment of God and guru (Prapti) and reflecting daily, one can experience true happiness within satsang, unaffected by worldly sorrows, and appreciate the rarity of human birth and the guru's association.
 Aahnik | Vishwas | My Journey
 Ahnik, the daily practice of puja, aarti, thaal, etc., is essential for earning the blessings of Bhagwan and the Satpurush, while also ensuring personal development through discipline, goal achievement, and adaptability. Building ultimate faith and trust in one's guru, who embodies Bhagwan, leads to experiencing the bliss of Akshardham, a journey of self-awareness, humility, and divine guidance. The celebration of the opening of BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, NJ emphasized commitment to internalize its divine essence, fostering gratitude, and cultivating a lifelong spiritual journey.

/News/2024/Yuvati-Antar-Jagruti-Parva-20.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuvati Antar Jagruti Parva (23 photos)
 At the conclusion of their four-month Yuvati Talim Kendra course, the 91 yuvatis of the first batch of 2024 (Batch 13), participated in the Antar Jagruti Parva.
 A total of 22 groups, each comprising 4 or 5 yuvatis, visited 155 villages and towns in 22 districts in Saurashtra, North Gujarat, Kheda, Central Gujarat and South Gujarat.
 They visited a total of over 3,555 homes and interacted with over 4,960 women to discuss how to strengthen the practice of satsang in their daily lives. The groups conducted 147 women’s assemblies, addressing over 6,000 women, 72 balika assemblies attended by about 1,140 young girls and 142 school assemblies in which over 11,000 young girls were present.
 In the evenings, they conducted 125 sandhya feris (devotional processions) in which over 4,500 women and girls participated.
 As a result of the efforts of the yuvatis, over 3,115 women pledged to observe a variety of niyams to enhance their spirituality.
 The Antar Jagruti Parva gave an insight to the yuvatis of the devotion and dedication to satsang of the devotees.

/News/2024/spirience-inaugural-book-pres.t: Inaugural Book Presentation of "Spirience" Unites Science and Spirituality for Peace and Prosperity, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2024/spirience-inaugural-book-pres.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Spirience Book Presentation (33 photos)
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto hosted the much-anticipated launch of the groundbreaking book Spirience: Experiencing Peace and Prosperity through Science and Spirituality on September 22, 2024. Co-authored by three renowned experts, this thought-provoking work explores the intersection of science and spirituality in tackling some of today’s most pressing challenges, including mental health crises and global conflicts.
 The event drew a large gathering of community members, faith leaders, scholars, and professionals from Greater Toronto and its vicinity, underscoring the book’s relevance in today's rapidly evolving world. The book’s authors—Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami, head of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Dr. V.I. Lakshmanan, a scientist and Officer of the Order of Canada, and Mr. S. Kalyanasundaram, a prominent community leader. Together, they shared their insights on how ancient spiritual wisdom and modern scientific advancements can harmonize creation of a more peaceful and prosperous future.
 Special guests attending the event included: 
 - Kapidhwaja Pratap Singh, Deputy Consul General of India in Toronto
 - Chandra Arya, Member of Parliament - Nepean, Ontario
 - Deepak Anand, Member of Provincial Parliament for Mississauga-Malton
 - Councillor Parthi Kandavel, City of Toronto
 Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami, a distinguished spirituality scholar, emphasized the book's core message: “In today’s world, science and spirituality often seem to walk separate paths, but Spirience shows how these two pillars of human progress can unite in fostering inner well-being and global peace. Our exploration of these connections is not just theoretical; it offers practical solutions to the challenges we face every day, from managing mental health to resolving conflicts.” 
 Published by the renowned Tellwell Talent, the book results from two years of dedicated research and collaboration between the three co-authors. It uniquely combines the ancient teachings of Hindu spiritual leaders with the latest scientific developments. Its unique approach offers readers scholarly insights and practical guidance on achieving personal well-being while contributing to global harmony.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual leader of BAPS, shared a powerful message in the book, stating: “If it’s for the prosperity and ultimate peace of all, then science too, is spirituality! Spirience is a festival of life. Celebrate!” 
 The event was an enriching experience for attendees, with lively discussions about the role of spirituality and science in addressing current societal issues, particularly in light of rising mental health challenges and international tensions. The evening concluded with a collective call to action, inspiring readers to apply the principles from Spirience in their daily lives to foster peace, prosperity, and well-being for all.
 Book Overview
 In Spirience, readers embark on an enlightening journey that bridges the teachings of ancient India with the latest developments in modern science. The creative title of the book ‘Spirience', which is a blend of two words: spirituality and science, was conceived by the lead author, Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami. The book examines how Vedic texts can provide valuable insights into pressing contemporary issues such as global conflicts, ideological divides, and rising mental health challenges. As technology rapidly advances, the authors outline actionable recommendations for incorporating these insights into personal, professional, and social spheres to foster well-being and global harmony.
 Order your copy of Spirience today on Amazon: https://a.co/d/dkekWah, and begin your journey toward a life of balance, purpose, and fulfillment.

/News/2025/1000-Nakkar-Vidwan-Mahotsav-2.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Felicitation Ceremony (40 photos)
 Pushpa Vrushti (14 photos)
 Grand Celebration (98 photos)
 As part of the ‘1,000 Nakkar Vidwan Mahotsav’ organized by BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute Australia, a grand celebration was held in the divine presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to honor 1,465 individuals who had memorized the 315 Sanskrit verses of the Satsang Diksha shastra. Devotees from across Australia and New Zealand were present to pay tribute to the time, effort, and unwavering dedication of each scholar.
 The event began with the Grand Felicitation Ceremony, in which Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami and Anandswarup Swami presented each Nakkar Vidwan (scholar) with a certificate, trophy, and memento, all previously sanctified by Mahant Swami Maharaj.  Devotees honored each Nakkar Vidwan by showering them with flower petals. Thereafter, the scholars participated in a group photo session. 
 In the evening assembly, the scholars, teachers and parents narrated the transformation in their lives by engaging in this scriptural study. Also, youths presented speeches on verses from the Satsang Diksha, explaining how they have imbibed those virtues in their lives. In addition, youths presented a discussion highlighting that the values in Satsang Diksha are universal and can be useful to every person in the world. 
 Mahant Swami Maharaj participated in a special Shalaka Spardha. In the first activity, Swamishri selected a shloka and then children recited that shloka and the next three shlokas. In the second activity, he selected a number and the children would recite that shloka. At the end, Swamishri said that his favorite shloka was 108 and the entire audience recited that shloka in unison. Swamishri praised the children for their efforts and guided them on progressing in their lives. 
 For many individuals, the journey was transformative. Some cultivated the discipline to study the shastra daily, while others learned to balance their time by prioritizing spiritual study over worldly distractions. Friendships flourished through shared study, with individuals supporting each other in their spiritual journeys.
 The ‘1,000 Nakkar Vidwan Mahotsav’ reminded everyone of the importance of passing on sacred knowledge across generations and how this brings together individuals from all backgrounds to collectively experience spiritual growth.

/News/2025/10th-Anniversary-Celebrations.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Darshan (12 photos)
 Mahapuja (40 photos)
 Cultural Programme (40 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Preston marked its tenth anniversary since the opening of the new mandir, on 8 November 2025. Devotees gathered to reflect on a journey shaped by faith, perseverance, humility, and unity.
 The celebrations brought together devotees of all ages along with invited guests and senior swamis from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. Their presence added deep spiritual significance to the occasion, which celebrated not only a decade of the Mandir’s existence, but also the enduring values that continue to sustain it.
 In the lead-up to the celebrations, devotees deepened their spiritual engagement through sustained devotional efforts. Over the course of the year, they collectively completed  more than 108,000 pradakshinas and regularly participated in monthly mahapujas, reflecting a shared commitment to spiritual growth and devotion.
 During his address in the main assembly, Yogvivekdas Swami reflected on humility and shared responsibility, drawing upon the incident where Shri Krishna Bhagwan lifted Mount Govardhan to protect the local community, while the villagers stand together beneath it in support, highlighting the importance of collective effort and service rather than personal credit.
 In the same spirit, the Mandir has been built and sustained through the dedication of its volunteers, whose time, skills and generosity have helped create a place of worship, learning and community service that benefits both worshippers and the wider community.
 Over the past decade, the Mandir has grown into a vibrant spiritual and community hub in the heart of Preston. Alongside daily worship and spiritual activities, it has supported the wider community during challenging periods such as the Covid-19 pandemic and continues to contribute through ongoing community initiatives, reflecting BAPS’s enduring commitment to service and social harmony.
 The Mandir’s journey stands as a testament to the dedication, sacrifice and love of countless devotees, whose selfless service has ensured that satsang and seva continue to flourish. It remains a place where spiritual values and culture are nurtured and preserved, enabling traditions and devotional practices to be lived and enjoyed.
 Above all, the BAPS mandir in Preston is cherished as a gift from Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and it continues to thrive under the compassionate guidance and blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj, inspiring generations to come.

/News/2025/10th-Anniversary-Celebrations.t: 10th Anniversary Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Adelaide, Australia
/News/2025/10th-Anniversary-Celebrations.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Kirtan Aradhana (13 photos)
 Mahila Sabha (33 photos)
 Cultural Program & Fireworks (29 photos)
 Patotsav Mahapuja & Sabha (58 photos)
 Inaugurated on 12 April 2015 by His Holiness Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Green Fields, Adelaide, celebrated its 10th Patotsav (anniversary).
 The three-days of festivities commenced on the evening of 18 April with the devotional singing of bhajans by swamis and devotees.
 On 19 April, Mahila Din (Women’s Day) was marked with a vibrant cultural program, in which women devotees presented traditional folk dances and thematic skits as well as inspirational speeches highlighting the significance of mandirs, and the role of women in community and society. The program emphasized traditional values and the importance of spiritual engagement. The festivities concluded with a spectacular fireworks display, symbolizing the joy and unity of the community in marking this significant milestone.
 On 20 April, the 10th Patotsav was celebrated with a mahapuja and a patotsav assembly in the presence of BAPS swamis, devotees and dignitaries.
 The assembly reflected on the journey of the mandir over the last 10 years, its impact on the community, and its special significance. Swamis shared inspiring stories of the mandir’s role in spiritually uplifting lives, and reinforced the importance of unity and devotion in the community.
 Amongst the distinguished guests present on this occasion were Tony Zappia MP, Member for Makin; John Fulbrook MP, Member for Playford; Cr. Chad Buchanan, Deputy Mayor for Central Ward; Cr. Wasim Saeed, City of Port Adelaide Enfield; Cr. Surender Pal Chahal, City of West Torrens; Cr. Jagdish Lakhani, Campbelltown City Council; as well as various community leaders.

/News/2025/21st-Centurys-Greatest-Collab.t: ‘21st Century's Greatest Collaboration’, K. Annamalai Hails BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/21st-Centurys-Greatest-Collab.text:
Photo Gallery 
 K. Annamalai Hails BAPS Hindu Mandir (31 photos)
 Shri K. Annamalai, one of India’s distinguished political leaders and social workers, was warmly welcomed at the BAPS Hindu Mandir on India’s Independence Day.
 Shri Annamalai was garlanded and accorded a traditional welcome by Swami Brahmaviharidas.
 Shri Annamalai was captivated by the enormity of the award-winning audio-visual immersive show, ‘The Fairy Tale’, which spreads the message of harmony and tolerance. As he walked through the tranquil mandir grounds, Shri Annamalai was moved by the mandir’s profound architectural and spiritual features.
 Inside the main mandir, Shri Annamalai reflected deeply on the vast spiritual heritage of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, especially admiring the intricate artistry of the Pillar of Pillars. He offered heartfelt prayers at each of the seven interior shrines.
 Shri Annamalai emphasized that the mandir is not only a sacred place of devotion, but also a living example of India’s enduring values of tolerance, non-violence, and harmony in diversity.
 Emotionally moved by his visit, he added, “I strongly advise all who walk through the mandir to fully embrace the experience and the togetherness it promotes. I could feel a deep sense of connection. Not only did I see our brothers and sisters from Bharat worshiping the seven beautiful deities within, but it felt as if I was walking into the north, east, south, west, and central parts of Bharat. When anything is done with purity and the blessings of the divine, miracles happen.”
 He lauded the selfless efforts of the sadhus and volunteers, “This realization has come about through the dedication of the swamis and volunteers. It is their faith in their gurus, and sheer persistence that made this miracle possible. Seeing it in person, I am truly mesmerized and proud to be a Hindu today.”
 Praising the mandir’s architectural elegance, Shri Annamalai remarked, “This is one of the most beautiful pieces of carving I have seen in recent times. I feared we had lost the art of such intricate carvings, but this mandir revives that legacy. It is living proof of what Bharat was capable of centuries ago. To see it alive today is profoundly inspiring.”
 Reflecting on the global collaboration behind the mandir, he said, “This is truly a story for the ages, and for history. When we look back 200 years from now, this will stand as one of the greatest collaborations of the 21st century – between a BAPS guru who opened his heart and reached out, and the rulers of another faith who responded with generosity, resulting in this masterpiece.”
 Shri Annamalai concluded his visit with earnest prayers for the enduring prosperity and progress of India. He expressed profound gratitude to His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, creator of the mandir, and to His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the UAE, for his steadfast support in bringing the mandir to life – an emblem of shared values, bridging hearts and cultures across the globe.

/News/2025/24th-Anniversary-Celebration-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 24th Anniversary Celebration | BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Bahrain (21 photos)
 The 24th patotsav of BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Bahrain was joyously celebrated in the presence of BAPS swamis, devotees and invited dignitaries.
 In the morning, devotees participated in the mahapuja, and thereafter offered an annakut of over 130 vegetarian delicacies prepared by the Women’s Wing. Thereafter, in the assembly, Anantnayandas Swami emphasized the mandir’s role in uplifting lives and inspiring devotion, service, and spirituality.
 The evening assembly featured a melodius kirtan aradhana, memories of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s visits to Bahrain narrated by Shirishbhai Trivedi and Dr. Prafulbhai Vaidya, and an inspiring address by Brahmaviharidas Swami.
 Dignitaries from the Indian embassy, and business and faith communities graced the occasion.
 The year-long Mandir Silver Jubilee (Rajat Jayanti) celebrations were also launched.

/News/2025/25th-Anniversary-Celebrations.t: 25th Anniversary Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Phoenix, AZ, USA
/News/2025/25th-Anniversary-Celebrations.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Cultural Program (66 photos)
 Patotsav Mahapuja (22 photos)
 Patotsav Vidhi (26 photos)
 Women's Cultural Program (11 photos)
 Kirtan Aradhana (20 photos)
 The 25th anniversary of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Phoenix, Arizona, was celebrated with great joy and devotion on November 8 and 9, 2025, through spiritually uplifting programs that brought together devotees and well-wishers from across the Phoenix community.
 The roots of BAPS satsang in the Phoenix area date back to 2000, when devotees established the original BAPS Mandir in Mesa, Arizona. The mandir served as a spiritual gathering place for the growing satsang community, offering weekly assemblies, devotional activities, and opportunities for community service.
 As the satsang community continued to grow, the need for a larger mandir to support expanding spiritual and cultural activities became clear. This vision was fulfilled on November 1, 2014, when Sadguru Pujya Tyagvallabhdas Swami inaugurated the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Phoenix, Arizona. Inspired by the blessings and guidance of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the mandir has since served as a vibrant center for devotion, cultural learning, and community engagement, inspiring individuals and families to lead lives grounded in faith, service, and unity.
 The anniversary celebrations began on Saturday evening, November 8, with a cultural program presented by children and youths. Through speeches, devotional music, and artistic performances, the program reflected on the mandir’s journey and highlighted its role in nurturing faith, values, and unity while strengthening devotees’ connection to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru Parampara.
 On Sunday morning, November 9, devotees gathered for the sacred patotsav rituals, commemorating the consecration of the mandir’s murtis. Swamis performed the traditional ceremonies as devotees offered prayers with gratitude for the blessings of the mandir.
 The celebrations concluded on Sunday afternoon with a kirtan aradhana, during which devotees participated in devotional singing, creating an atmosphere of devotion and appreciation for the mandir, the Guru, and the many opportunities for satsang and seva it has provided.
 The 25th anniversary offered devotees an opportunity to reflect on the mandir’s journey and its continued growth as a center of satsang, seva, and spiritual learning for the Phoenix community. The occasion also inspired devotees to strengthen their commitment to faith, unity, and selfless service in the years ahead.

Photo Gallery 
 Murti Darshan (16 photos)
 Patotsav (40 photos)
 Mahapuja (24 photos)
 Sant Parayan (8 photos)
 On Sunday 20 August 1995, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj (1921–2016) – one of the world’s most revered spiritual leaders and an inspiration to millions worldwide – opened the doors of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London to the world. The inauguration represented a milestone for the British Hindu community, establishing a spiritual home and a hub of moral and cultural guidance in the United Kingdom.
 On Monday 18 August 2025, the Mandir celebrated its 30th anniversary (according to the Hindu lunar calendar), marking three decades of spiritual inspiration, community service, and devotional activities.
 Devotees from across the UK gathered to participate in a day filled with sacred rituals, cultural devotion, and opportunities for families to celebrate together.
 The anniversary was a special occasion to reflect on the Mandir’s journey and the enduring vision of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, whose legacy continues to inspire countless devotees.
 The festivities began with arti, darshan, and the patotsav ceremony, involving the maha-abhishek of all the murtis while chanting Vedic verses and praying for peace across London, the UK, and the world. This was followed by discourses, arti, and the annakut offering.
 A Vishwa Shanti Mahapuja (sacred ceremony performed to invoke global peace, harmony, and well-being) was held the day before, on Sunday 17 August, as a part of the festivities. Families from across London gathered, dressed in traditional attire, and offered prayers collectively, seeking blessings for themselves, their communities, and the whole world. The ceremony highlighted the Mandir’s role as a centre for promoting peace, harmony, and spiritual growth, emphasising the importance of personal and collective devotion.
 One of the most moving moments of the day was the maha-arti – a memorable celebration performed in front of the maha-murti of the Mandir’s visionary founder and a fitting tribute to his lifetime of spiritual guidance and service. Devotees participated with reverent enthusiasm, infusing the courtyard with a joyous atmosphere.
 The celebrations also included a four-day parayan (scriptural discourse), delivered by Atmatruptdas Swami, a senior learned swami visiting from Sarangpur, India. He explored the spiritual benefits of associating with God, Guru, and the virtuous, and living a life of righteousness. Known for his insightful teachings and ability to make scripture accessible, Atmatruptdas Swami guided devotees in reflecting on their spiritual journeys. The parayan complemented the anniversary celebrations by providing a deeper understanding of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s teachings and inspiring attendees to incorporate these values and practices into their daily lives.
 Reflecting on the celebrations, Shreya Mehta, visiting with her young children, shared, “Every time we come to the Mandir, it feels like a home filled with peace and learning. My children especially enjoyed taking part in the ceremonies and the celebrations. Today, seeing them participate in the mahapuja was heartwarming. It’s wonderful for them to grow up with these values and traditions.”

/News/2025/A-Microcosm-of-Creation-and-H.t: ‘A Microcosm of Creation and Humanity’: Dr. Shashi Tharoor Acclaims the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/A-Microcosm-of-Creation-and-H.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Dr. Shashi Tharoor Acclaims the BAPS Hindu Mandir (20 photos)
 Dr. Shashi Tharoor, Member of Parliament, author, and former UN Under-Secretary-General, visited the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, describing it as “one of the most remarkable structures I have ever seen, not only among temples but among the world’s finest architectural marvels.”
 Swami Brahmaviharidas traditionally welcomed Dr. Tharoor with a garland and personally accompanied him as he appreciated the Mandir’s intricate artistry, symbolic design, and universal message of harmony.
 An Architectural and Spiritual Masterpiece
 Reflecting on his visit, Dr. Tharoor said, “Going beyond its extraordinary spiritual content, every inch of this Mandir reflects harmony and unity. From the moment you enter through the Wall of Harmony, you sense that this is not just a place of worship, it is a statement of what humanity can be when it comes together. The attention to detail is breathtaking. You could spend weeks looking at each carving and still not see them all. The artistry is not just skill; it is devotion carved in stone.”
 Tribute to Nature, Nations, and the Spirit of Humanity
 At the Abhishek Mandapam, Dr. Tharoor reflected on the symbolism of the world’s rivers and sands gathered from the seven Emirates, “It is truly a microcosm of creation and humanity. To see sands from across the UAE and waters representing the world’s rivers — it speaks to a universal spirit that transcends boundaries.”
 Drawing from his own experience at the United Nations, he added, “I spent years at the UN talking about our common humanity. Today, I have seen the embodiment of that humanity in stone, in spirit, and in purpose.”
 Respect for the UAE’s Vision and Generosity
 Dr. Tharoor offered heartfelt gratitude to the UAE leadership for enabling such an inclusive spiritual landmark, “It is a remarkable act of vision and generosity by the UAE government to allow a temple of this scale, beauty, and authenticity to rise in the heart of the Islamic world. The late Sheikh Zayed’s legacy and the compassion of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed have made this possible. As I was told, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed said that if there is to be a temple, it must look like a temple. That openness reflects the courage and inclusiveness of this nation.”
 A Place of Interfaith Inspiration
 Accompanied by a diverse delegation, Dr. Tharoor observed, “I came with three Muslim colleagues, and they were enthralled. There were no barriers, no restrictions; only openness. That is what true spirituality is about.”
 He concluded with a vision of hope, “This Mandir is not just built of stone, it is built of faith, compassion, and imagination. It reminds us that even in times of darkness, we can light a candle that ignites many more. I will leave Abu Dhabi feeling blessed and inspired.”
 At the end, Dr. Shashi Tharoor said, “I extend my heartfelt thanks to Swami Brahmaviharidas for his gracious time and insights. This has been an experience unlike any other and I feel deeply blessed, moved, and uplifted, and I am certain that all who come here with openness will feel the same sense of peace and inspiration.”

/News/2025/A-Prayer-for-Unity-and-Peace-.t: A Prayer for Unity and Peace, Los Angeles, CA, USA
/News/2025/A-Prayer-for-Unity-and-Peace-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Unity Prayer and Call for Peace (6 photos)
 On Friday, March 7, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Chino Hills, CA, was desecrated with hateful messages. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. Similar acts of vandalism have occurred at Hindu mandirs across North America, including BAPS mandirs in Long Island, NY, and Sacramento, CA.
 In response, on Sunday, March 9, a "Unity Prayer and Call for Peace" was organized, bringing together local, state, and federal officials, clergy from various faiths, representatives from Hindu mandirs across Southern California, and community supporters. During the gathering, heartfelt prayers were offered not only for the community but also for those responsible for this crime, hoping they may be freed from hatred and recognize our shared humanity.
 Among those in attendance were Chino Hills Mayor Art Bennett, Chino Hills City Council members Cynthia Moran and Ray Marquez, and Assemblymember Leticia Castillo. Representatives from various organizations, including the Malibu Hindu Temple, Irvine Hindu Mandir, Laxmi Narayan Mandir Riverside, Jain Center of Southern California, and others, also joined in solidarity.
 Hetal Patel, a BAPS volunteer, shared a statement on behalf of BAPS:
 "We strongly denounce these actions and pray for peace among all communities. The values of peace, respect, and harmony for all people, regardless of background or faith, form the foundation of religious freedom in the United States. The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Chino Hills, like all BAPS mandirs worldwide, serves as a symbol of peace, harmony, equality, selfless service, and universal Hindu values. This mandir is home for my family."
 Chino Hills Mayor Art Bennett reaffirmed his steadfast support, stating:
 "Hate has no home here in Chino Hills. We strongly denounce this cowardly act and are working with local law enforcement to prioritize the investigation of this incident. BAPS is such a vital and beloved member of our city, and we stand firmly with them."
 The incident has also prompted an outpouring of support on social media from numerous officials, including Congresswoman Young Kim, Congresswoman Norma Torres, Congressman Derek Tran, and Congressman Ro Khanna. Members of the California State Assembly, including Assemblymembers Ash Kalra, Alex Lee and Dr. Darshana Patel, have also voiced their support. Additionally, members of the Dawoodi Bohra Al Masjid (Mosque) Al Jamali Anjuman-e-Qutbi in Ontario, CA, visited the mandir to express their solidarity with the Hindu community.
 Upon discovering the hateful vandalism, local authorities were immediately contacted, and BAPS is fully cooperating in their investigation of this hate crime. Given the large number of visitors, including children, who come to the mandir on weekends, BAPS volunteers promptly removed most of the offensive messages.
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir remains committed to its mission of promoting peace, harmony, and service to all.

/News/2025/ANZ-Youth-Seminars-A-New-Dime.t: ANZ Youth Seminars: A New Dimension to Success, Asia Pacific
/News/2025/ANZ-Youth-Seminars-A-New-Dime.text:
More than 450 kishores and kishoris participated in the seminars held at seven BAPS centers across Australia (Adelaide, Brisbane Canberra, Melbourne, Sydney and Perth) and New Zealand (Auckland) based on the theme ‘A New Dimension to Success: 3D’.
 The seminars guided the youths on discipline, determination and dedication as the key drivers of academic, spiritual and professional development at this stage of their lives.
 The seminars included panel discussions with local devotees sharing their experiences on how satsang and the mandir have helped them throughout their education and careers. Resident swamis also shared insights on the role of spirituality in achieving academic and professional success.
 Each seminar featured video conference sessions with guest speakers – Sandeep Patel, an Executive Director at Goldman Sachs in London and Kush Patel, CEO and Co-founder of Relative Dynamics in Maryland, USA. Both speakers, who are dedicated BAPS devotees, shared their journey and advice through a talk and Q&A session. They provided valuable insights and practical guidance into how spirituality, satsang and mandir provided stability, clarity, perspective and purpose throughout their careers and education.
