/News/2025/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.t: Akhand Dhun: Annual Prayers for Peace, Harmony, and Success, Wellingborough, UK
/News/2025/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Darshan (12 photos)
 Prarthana (60 photos)
 Ashirwad (12 photos)
 A spiritually uplifting day of continuous prayer was held at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Wellingborough on Sunday 20 April 2025. Devotees from across the UK gathered to offer heartfelt prayers for global peace and well-being.
 The devotional observances began early at 7.00am, with worshippers arriving throughout the day to pay their respects at the Akshar Deri, a beautiful sacred shrine within the Mandir.
 Among the many attendees was Heena Ruparelia, who travelled from Leicester with her husband and two young children. Reflecting on the day, she shared, “It was an inspiring and uplifting experience where everyone came together in a spirit of selflessness. The volunteers were incredibly welcoming, and meeting so many fellow devotees from different regions added to the day’s joy.”
 This year marked the 41st anniversary of the Akhand Dhun, a continuous prayer tradition that began humbly in 1984. To commemorate this milestone, Mahant Swami Maharaj sent a special message of blessings to all those present. In his letter, he highlighted the spiritual legacy of the Akshar Deri, a gift from Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and offered his heartfelt prayers for the health, peace, and prosperity of all – particularly during a time of widespread unrest and humanitarian challenges around the world.
 In a show of commitment to health and devotion, 16 cyclists undertook a journey of over 100 kilometres from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, to Wellingborough on the same day. Additionally, a group of devotees completed the distance on foot from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Chigwell, embodying both physical endurance and spiritual dedication.
 The day of prayer concluded at 7.00pm after hours of continuous chanting, pradakshinas (circumambulations), darshan, and seva (selfless service).
 Rajesh Ladwa, a senior volunteer at the Mandir, expressed, “This annual tradition of communal prayer brings people together with a shared purpose. We are deeply thankful to all who took part and remain committed to serving the broader community throughout the year.”

/News/2025/Akshar-Purushottam-Darshan-Fe.t: Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Featured at the 19th World Sanskrit Conference, Kathmandu, Nepal
/News/2025/Akshar-Purushottam-Darshan-Fe.text:
Photo Gallery 
 World Sanskrit Conference (90 photos)
 The World Sanskrit Conference is a prestigious international gathering dedicated to the Sanskrit language – a celebration of one of the world’s most ancient and profound languages. Held every three years in different countries, the conference brings together thousands of scholars from around the globe to present research and engage in meaningful dialogue on Sanskrit language, literature, and philosophy.
 This year, the 19th edition of the five-day conference was inaugurated by the President of Nepal. Reflecting Nepal’s sacred connection to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the organizers dedicated a special session to the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan – the unique Vedantic philosophy revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 In the late 18th century, Bhagwan Swaminarayan had journeyed across Nepal for nearly three years, sanctifying the land through his austerities, yogic practices, and divine knowledge. It was during this sacred journey that he expounded the core principles of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, which has since become a revered school of Vedantic thought.
 On June 28, the special academic session on Akshar-Purushottam Darshan involved esteemed scholars from Nepal, India, the United States, China, Japan, and various European nations.
 The session was chaired by Mahamahopadhyaya Swami Bhadreshdas, author of the Swaminarayan Bhashyas, a commentary on the Prasthanatrayi, and a globally recognized scholar of Vedanta. Many distinguished academics and institutional leaders graced the session, including:
 Shri Kashinath Nyaupane – National Coordinator of the World Sanskrit Conference and renowned scholar from Nepal
 Prof. Srinivasa Varakhedi – Vice Chancellor, Central Sanskrit University, Delhi
 Prof. Murli Manohar Pathak – Vice Chancellor, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, Delhi
 Prof. G.S. Murthy – Vice Chancellor, Central Sanskrit University, Tirupati
 Prof. Bhagyesh Jha – Renowned Sanskrit scholar and former IAS officer
 Prof. Sukanta Senapati – Vice Chancellor, Shree Somnath Sanskrit University, Gujarat
 Prof. Rani Sadashiv Murthy – Vice Chancellor, Vedic University, Tirupati
 Prof. Hareram Tripathi – Vice Chancellor, Kavikulaguru Kalidas Sanskrit University, Nagpur
 Prof. Ramsevak Dubey – Vice Chancellor, Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University
 Prof. Vijay Kumar C.G. – Vice Chancellor, Maharshi Panini Sanskrit & Vedic University, Ujjain
 Prof. Ramnarayan Dwivedi – Secretary General, Kashi Vidvat Parishad
 Dr. Sachchidanand Mishra – Member Secretary, Indian Council of Philosophical Research (ICPR)
 Representatives from several prominent Nepali organizations also attended, including Nepal Sanskrit University, Rashtriya Dharma Jagaran Abhiyan, Jayatu Sanskritam, Nepal Shikshan Parishad, Nepal Panchang Nirnayak Vikas Samiti, Nepal Pandit Mahasabha, Nepal Maharshi Vedic Foundation, and Valmiki Vidyapeeth.
 A defining feature of this session was that the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan as revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan was formally introduced in Nepal to the scholarly community for the first time. On this historic occasion, Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj conveyed his blessings and prayers for the success of the entire conference through a heartfelt video message.
 During the session, scholars presented research papers on various tenets of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan. Topics and presenters included:
 Prof. Dr. Atmatruptdas Swami: A Study on the Composition Process of the Swaminarayan Bhashyas on the Prasthanatrayi in 21st Century Sanskrit Literature
 Prof. Dr. Aksharananddas Swami: The Akshar-Purushottam Darshan’s Analysis of Dharma in the Bhagavad Gita
 Prof. Acharya Brahmananddas Swami: The Concept of Divine Manifestation in Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Revealed by Parabrahma Bhagwan Swaminarayan
 Prof. Dr. Gnanatruptdas Swami: Akshar-Purushottam Darshan in the Vachanamrut of Bhagwan Swaminarayan
 Prof. Dr. Sagar Acharya: The Unified Philosophical Structure of the Swaminarayan Bhashyas on the Prasthanatrayi from the Perspective of Aksharbrahma
 Prof. Acharya Tarun Dhola: A Study on the Brahma-Parabrahma Relationship According to Akshar-Purushottam Darshan
 Prof. Acharya Harikrishna Pedhadiya: An Analysis of Brahma-Atma Unity in the Gita Bhashya of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan
 Acharya Tejas Koria: A Comparative Study of the Concept of Akshar in Vishishtadvaita and Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Based on the Bhagavad Gita
 In his keynote remarks, Prof. Srinivasa Varakhedi praised the Akshar-Purushottam Siddhant revealed by Parabrahma Bhagwan Swaminarayan as a distinct and original contribution to the Vedic philosophical tradition. He further announced that the Central Sanskrit University has formally incorporated the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan into its curriculum from this academic year.
 In his concluding address, Mahamahopadhyaya Swami Bhadreshdas emphasized the sanctity of Nepal, Bhagwan Swaminarayan journey, and the divine truths of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan he shared with seekers. He also highlighted the unbroken flow of the Sanatan Vedic tradition, which continues to give rise to new insights and schools of thought over time.
 Today, countless aspirants across the world are striving to internalize the principles of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan. Leading scholars have recognized it as a unique and foundational contribution to Vedic Sanatan Dharma. Notably, numerous global universities are now offering courses and academic programs focused on this school of thought, furthering its reach and scholarly exploration.
 To commemorate this occasion, Shri Kashinath Nyaupane, National Coordinator of the World Sanskrit Conference, formally declared, “Today, we in Nepal joyfully welcome, honor, and establish the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan.”
 Thus, the special session on Akshar-Purushottam Darshan at the 19th World Sanskrit Conference became a memorable occasion – both from the perspective of Vedantic philosophy and the sacred bond between Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the spiritual land of Nepal.

/News/2025/Akshar-Purushottam-Darshan-Ma.t: Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Mandapam Inaugurated at the National Sanskrit University, Tirupati, India
/News/2025/Akshar-Purushottam-Darshan-Ma.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shankaracharya Mulakat (6 photos)
 Pratishtha Mahotsav (29 photos)
 Vaidik Mahayag (30 photos)
 Shobha Yatra (32 photos)
 Bhashyotsav Inaugural Session (16 photos)
 Gargi Sanman Samaroh (18 photos)
 Honorable Governor and Chief Minister at inauguration of Mandir (13 photos)
 Bhashyotsav Samapan Samaroh (8 photos)
 Samman Satra (12 photos)
 Parmatmik Yaga (7 photos)
 Tirupati is a renowned pilgrimage site in the state of Andhra Pradesh, South India. There, within the sprawling campus of the National Sanskrit University, the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Mandapam was inaugurated as part of the special ‘Bhashyotsav’.
 Under the collective decision of the university's Vice-Chancellor, Shri G.S.R. Krishna Murthy, and its administrators, the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Mandapam was inaugurated on the university campus, alongside the mandapams for other philosophical traditions.
 Organized by the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (ICPR) and the National Sanskrit University, the ‘Bhashyotsav’ celebrated the commentaries of various Vedic traditions. Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami presented and elucidated upon the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan as revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 On 2 August 2025, the sacred murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj were installed with Vedic rituals in the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Mandapam. Pujan of these murtis had been performed by Mahant Swami Maharaj on 15 July 2025 in Bochasan.
 As part of the murti installation ceremony, a Vedic yagna was performed on 3 August 2025.
 In the yagnashala, professors of the university's philosophy department were felicitated with ‘Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Prashasti’ certificates.
 Paramatmik Yagna, based on the Vaikhanasa Agama scriptures, was also performed by expert scholars as part of the installation ceremony.
 As part of the Bhashyotsav on 4 and 5 August, the organizers arranged a special procession. During the procession, the commentary texts (bhashyas) of various philosophical traditions were carried in palanquins and honored with pujan and arti.
 Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami, author of the Prasthanatrayi Bhashya, performed pujan of the acharyas of the Vedanta tradition.
 Scholars from over 10 states across India offered pujan to the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, followed by the collective worship of the commentaries (bhashyas) of various traditions.
 On 5 August 2025, the Mandapam was inaugurated by His Excellency Dr. Haribabu Kambhampati, Governor of Odisha; Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami, Chief Minister of Uttarakhand; and Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami. The Governor and the Chief Minister offered pujan to the murtis.
 On this occasion, inspired by Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Akshardham, Delhi, presented this prestigious Sanskrit university with the 'Sanskritmahalayamanih' award.
 BAPS also felicitated female professors as part of the 'Gargi Vandana' program.
 Other university professors were felicitated as part of the ‘Adhyapaka Sammanam’ program.
 On this occasion,  Mahant Swami Maharaj bestowed his blessings through a video message: "My prayers and blessings that all students studying at this university may progress in their chosen fields of knowledge and serve society; may everyone’s faith in God increase; may all receive spiritual strength; and may everyone’s life become virtuous and full of devotion."
 On this occasion, Param Pujya Vijayendra Saraswatiji Maharaj, Shankaracharya of the Kanchi Math, also sent his special blessings via a video message. He stated: " The Swaminarayan Akshardham organization is actively engaged in devotion and service. Our Guruji, Anantashri Vibhushit Shri Shri Shri Jayendra Saraswati Maharaj, had told us about this organization. It is a place of upasana, service, and even aesthetics, and as such, it embodies the principle of ‘Satyam Shivam Sundaram’ (Truth, Auspiciousness, and Beauty). There is nothing here that goes against Dharma. Work on tattvagnan is also being done through the medium of the Sanskrit language. Bhadresh Swami has composed such a profound text. His knowledge, faith, and love in this research have fostered strong relationships not just with devotees but also with scholars."
 Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami stated: "India is the land of timeless Sanatan Vedic Darshans. From time to time, various schools of thought have emerged on this land. The Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, as revealed by Parabrahma Swaminarayan, is also a Vedic Sanatan Darshan in this lineage. Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj have honorably propagated the Indian philosophical tradition throughout the world."
 Shri Harekrishna Satapathyji, Former Vice-Chancellor, National Sanskrit University, Tirupati mentioned: “The principles of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan are found in the Gita, Vedas, and Upanishads. Bhagwan Swaminarayan explained this philosophy in the Vachanamrut.”
 Prof. G.S.R. Krishnamurthy, Vice-Chancellor, National Sanskrit University, Tirupati stated: “The Akshar-Purushottam Darshan is moving with society. Now, it has become integrated with society. If we embrace it, India will prosper, and the importance of our modern Indian knowledge tradition will be enhanced. The Akshar-Purushottam Darshan embodies equality, and its very goal is to synthesize philosophy with society. It is for these reasons that we all [scholars] have been attracted to it.”
 Prof. Sukant Kumar Senapati, Vice-Chancellor, Shree Somnath Sanskrit University, Gujarat mentioned: “An assembly like this has never been held anywhere in India. This Bhashya Mahotsav is an inspiration for the next generation. It has all happened due to the inspiration of Mahant Swami Ji.”
 Prof. Murli Manohar Pathakji, Vice-Chancellor, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, Delhi stated: “In this dreadful Kaliyuga, such a blissful commentary has been composed, and for this, Swami Bhadreshdasji is worthy of our reverence. In this Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, Bhadreshdasji has considered the Vachanamrut to be a foundational text (Prasthana), along with the Gita, the Upanishads, and the Brahmasutras. It is evident that these four texts are the foundational pillars of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan.”

/News/2025/Akshardham-Academy-2025-29587.t: Empowering the Future: The Akshardham Academy, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/News/2025/Akshardham-Academy-2025-29587.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Akshardham Academy (18 photos)
 Amidst the bustle of daily life, Akshardham Academy offers college students and recent graduates a six-week journey of intellectual growth and spiritual enrichment at BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, NJ. In the summer of 2025, more than 40 Kishores, Kishoris, Yuvaks, and Yuvatis participated in the Academy’s two sessions.
 The Academy is built on four guiding pillars: strengthening Satsang, applying Satsang values in daily life, professional development, and fostering community. Together, these principles inspire participants to pursue a life of purpose and fulfillment.
 Through daily katha sessions led by Pujya Swamis, delegates immerse themselves in the wisdom of Hindu shastras while deepening their cultural and spiritual grounding. Beyond the classroom, values such as integrity, seva (selfless service), and dharma are woven into daily routines, cultivating both inner discipline and outward purpose. Community engagement is equally central—goshthi discussions, ahnik, and seva activities nurture dialogue, collaboration, and lasting bonds of fraternity and sisterhood.
 Alongside spiritual learning, participants receive specialized departmental training and professional development workshops that prepare them for today’s workforce. Hands-on projects across Akshardham’s departments enhance operational efficiency, safety, and visitor experience—ranging from commissary production oversight and logistics improvements to upgraded visitor services, volunteer training, and the creation of educational resources for K–12 students.
 Through these initiatives, both the participants and the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham campus are enriched. By nurturing Satsang, empowering professional growth, and building strong community ties, Akshardham Academy stands as a beacon of inspiration—preparing the next generation of leaders and visionaries to serve with knowledge, unity, and compassion.

/News/2025/Ambani-Family-Visit-Neasden-T.t: Ambani Family Visit Neasden Temple, London, UK
/News/2025/Ambani-Family-Visit-Neasden-T.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Ambani Family Visit Neasden Temple, London, UK (7 photos)
 On Sunday 13 July 2025, Anant and Radhika Ambani, accompanied by Mukesh Ambani, visited BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden, London, to seek blessings on the weekend of their first wedding anniversary.
 During their visit, the family took a deep interest in the Mandir’s sacred architecture and intricate carvings, marvelling at the artistry, devotion, peace and values reflected throughout the iconic place of worship.
 Mukeshbhai also affectionately recalled his memorable meeting with His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, sharing his deep appreciation for the spiritual legacy he had witnessed.
 Anant and Radhika, Mukeshbhai’s son and daughter-in-law, joined in prayers together and participated in darshan of the sacred images. They also performed abhishek – a special water-offering ceremony – to Shri Nilkanth Varni (the teenage form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan), which symbolises inner purification and the offering of reverence. The ceremony allowed them a moment of quiet reflection and connection with the divine, in keeping with the serene and spiritual atmosphere of the Mandir.
 The family also took the opportunity to learn more about the global humanitarian, cultural and spiritual initiatives of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS), including its commitment to values-led living and community service. They particularly appreciated the efforts in Paris after seeing the model of the upcoming BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, the first traditional Hindu temple in France, noting the collaborative efforts between ancient Indian traditions of religious architecture and modern French methods of cutting-edge engineering.
 Before departing, Mukesh Ambani expressed heartfelt gratitude to all the volunteers who had helped make the visit so memorable for his family and deeply appreciated the spirit of selfless service and spirituality that define BAPS and the Mandir.

/News/2025/Amrut-Cup-Tournament-2025-280.text:
The Amrut Cup Tournament is an annual sports event where high school and college girls compete in a dynamic and uplifting environment that fosters both athletic and spiritual growth. More than just a tournament, it embodies the values of samp (unity), suhradbhav (solidarity), and ekta (oneness)—principles taught by Yogiji Maharaj—creating an atmosphere where participants strengthen their bonds with one another and their guru.
 The Amrut Cup seamlessly integrates satsang into every aspect of the event. Each day begins and ends with aarti and cheshta, along with thoughtfully designed morning and evening sessions that reinforce spiritual teachings and practices. Beyond the games, the tournament serves as a powerful platform for personal, professional, and spiritual development. Participants cultivate essential skills such as teamwork, leadership, and trust, all while immersing themselves in satsang values.
 These tournaments align with the vision of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, carrying forward the legacy of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Through initiatives like the Amrut Cup, kishoris and yuvatis are encouraged to stay actively engaged in weekly sabhas, summer conventions, community service, and other enriching activities that contribute to their holistic growth.
 Ultimately, the Amrut Cup is more than just a competition—it is a transformative experience that strengthens spiritual connections, builds lifelong friendships, and inspires participants to carry the values of samp, suhradbhav, and ekta into their daily lives and communities.

/News/2025/Andhra-Pradesh-Chief-Minister.t: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, Overwhelmed by the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Andhra-Pradesh-Chief-Minister.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shri, N. Chandrababu Naidu Visits the BAPS Hindu Mandir (19 photos)
 Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, N. Chandrababu Naidu, visited the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, describing it as “one of the most extraordinary experiences of my life.”
 He was warmly welcomed by Brahmaviharidas Swami, who offered a traditional garland and then guided the Chief Minister through the Mandir’s exquisite craftsmanship, profound symbolism, and enduring messages of peace and unity.
 A Monument of Harmony and Humanity
 The visit began at the 3D-printed Wall of Harmony that embodies the Mandir’s messages of inclusivity, and that faith can unite rather than divide. The Chief Minister paused here, acknowledging the profound resonance of the word that greets every visitor.
 Tradition through a Modern Lens
 Then, at the Divine Eye sculpture, the Chief Minister saw the full expanse of the Mandir for the first time. As a broad smile lit his face, he remarked, “This is what youth need. You have to express our values in a way they understand.”
 Voices of Devotion and Belonging
 On his way to the Mandir, the Chief Minister met a devotee, originally from South India who shared his joy, “I’ve come here for over a hundred visits. This Mandir is not only a place of worship, it’s my home – a reminder that our roots and our culture live on here in the UAE.”
 The Chief Minister listened, moved by how the Mandir has become a bridge of belonging for the Indian diaspora.
 Blessings Beneath the Spires
 Beneath the Mandir’s ornate domes, the Chief Minister offered prayers before the deities. 
 At the Shrinivas-Padmavati shrine, the Chief Minister met a South Indian volunteer who had supervised the carving of the Shrinivas-Padmavati murtis in Tirupati, and commended his dedication.
 Then, standing before the murti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who first envisioned a Mandir in Abu Dhabi, the Chief Minister reflected, “This is a true miracle. The words of the truly great are always fulfilled.”
 Expressions from the Heart
 At the close of his visit, the Chief Minister shared his reflections with heartfelt sincerity, “This has been an extraordinary experience in my lifetime. I have seen many achievements, but today what I witnessed here is truly unbelievable.
 “This is the inspiration given by your guruji, and you have transformed that message into action. Nobody could have even imagined this. On this land, the words of your guruji have become reality – hats off to you.
 “I have seen many success stories, but this is a unique success story. In just five years, you have achieved something that will live in history and live as a legacy.
 “What is most remarkable is how you brought consensus among all the rulers. Every ruler appreciated your suggestion and gave their permission. I can only imagine the effort and the faith it took – truly, a miracle.
 “I also deeply appreciate our Honorable Prime Minister for his support. Both of you made this historic event happen here.
 “Only a few people create history, and I see that in your broad-minded, forward-looking approach. You have combined faith with technology, tradition with modernity, and a vision that unites humanity – beyond religion, beyond region.
 “I have seen here a truly global approach, global unity for global peace. It is an extraordinary achievement, and I sincerely appreciate you. This will go a long way.”

/News/2025/Annual-Karyakar-Shibirs-2025-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shibir (42 photos)
 Approximately 19,190 male and female karyakars who coordinate satsang, women’s, and youth activities at BAPS centers throughout Gujarat and Maharashtra participated with great enthusiasm in the Annual Karyakar Shibirs. A total of 26 shibirs were conducted at seven venues – Bochasan, Sarangpur, Gondal, Ahmedabad, Sankari, Tithal, and Nashik - based on the theme ‘Nishthavan Bhava…’ (Be Steadfast in Conviction).
 The shibirs focused on various dimensions of nishtha – conviction in doctrinal principles, loyalty to one’s supreme ishtadev, firm faith in the manifest form of God, and loyalty in devotion. Through enlightening discourses by senior and learned sadhus, workshops, inspiring skits, and the video blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj, karyakars were guided on strengthening their own nishtha (firm conviction) and on how to help strengthen it in others to help build a satsang community rooted in firm conviction and devotion.

/News/2025/Australian-House-of-Represent.t: Australian House of Representatives Speaker Milton Dick Meets His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj , Sydney, Australia
/News/2025/Australian-House-of-Represent.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Hon Milton Dick Meets His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj (13 photos)
 Speaker of the Australian House of Representatives, Milton Dick, visited the newly opened BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir and Cultural Precinct in Kemps Creek, Sydney, and met His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Mr. Dick has visited a number of BAPS mandirs in Australia and is a leader in India-Australia dialogues. Mr. Dick traveled from his home in Brisbane, Queensland, to attend the special Maha Annakut festival and meet Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Following a traditional welcome by children, Mr. Dick was given a guided tour of the new cultural precinct before arriving in the assembly hall to address the gathering,
 “I have a special relationship with BAPS; I proudly wear my nadachhadis. I’m currently wearing one from my local BAPS Mandir in Kingston, Queensland. And one I received last year when I was so graciously welcomed to the BAPS Mandir in Canberra.
 “His Holiness’s visit reminds us of the privilege we have to live freely and peacefully without conflict. To live side by side with people of different faiths, cultures and heritage. Where differences are welcomed, where cultures are shared and celebrated.
 “This new mandir will be a place that not only benefits the congregation but the broader Australian community. It will serve as a place whereby the values of peace, harmony, respect and mateship will be nurtured and inspired.”
 The Maha Annakut festival reflected the importance of community and devotion.

/News/2025/Australian-Prime-Minister-Wel.t: Australian Prime Minister Welcomes Mahant Swami Maharaj at BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir and Cultural Precinct, Sydney, Australia
/News/2025/Australian-Prime-Minister-Wel.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Australian Prime Minister Welcomes Mahant Swami Maharaj (31 photos)
 The Prime Minister of Australia, Hon. Anthony Albanese, visited the newly inaugurated BAPS Hindu Mandir and Cultural Precinct in Kemps Creek, Sydney, to welcome His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to Australia and participate in the auspicious Fuldol celebration.
 Upon arrival, Prime Minister Albanese was warmly received at the traditionally adorned gates of the BAPS Hindu Mandir and Cultural Precinct by the board of trustees of BAPS Australia and senior BAPS volunteers. He was then guided by BAPS swamis through the precinct, where he viewed the various cultural and spiritual elements, witnessing firsthand how the precinct serves as a beacon of harmony and devotion. During his visit, he also met key community leaders, acknowledging the significant contributions of the Hindu community to Australia’s multicultural landscape.
 Following these interactions, Prime Minister Albanese had a personal meeting with His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, during which, on behalf of Mahant Swami Maharaj, Anandswarupdas Swami tied a nadachhadi on the Prime Minister’s wrist in a heartfelt gesture of goodwill, friendship, and harmony. Mr. Albanese was also honoured with a garland and presented with a traditional kalash, signifying auspicious beginnings and strong connections between communities.
 Thereafter, addressing the audience assembled for the auspicious Fuldol celebration, Prime Minister Albanese remarked, "One of the great joys of being prime minister of this great country is the opportunity to come to an event like this and witness the incredible devotion of communities who have given so much to our country.
 "His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj comes to us with a message that is for all Australians: 'In the joy of others lies our own.' It is an honor for all of us that you have chosen Sydney to celebrate this occasion for only the second time in 115 years."
 Prime Minister Albanese also expressed his admiration for the BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir and Cultural Precinct, calling it "a work in majestic progress" and reflected on Mahant Swami Maharaj’s profound sentiment upon seeing the completed phase one of the complex, "I am home." Highlighting the spirit of unity, he added, "His Holiness has actively taught that unity is strength – when hearts are united, nothing is impossible."
 Before departing, Prime Minister Albanese took time to personally greet swamis and volunteers, expressing his appreciation for their dedication and selfless service.

/News/2025/BAPS-10K-Charity-Challenge-20.text:
More than 3,000 people of all ages and backgrounds came together at 20 BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu mandirs and centres around the UK in June and August 2025 to participate in the BAPS 10K Charity Challenge.
 The annual Challenge unites participants for a fun-filled 10-kilometre walk, jog, or run to raise funds for a variety of BAPS’s activities that uplift communities and serve those in need.
 The 2025 Challenge also supported BAPS’s national charity partner, Children With Cancer UK, which is the country’s leading childhood cancer charity aiming to help every child and young person survive cancer by funding life-saving research and supporting patients and their families through treatment and beyond.
 Individual mandirs and centres also supported local charities, making a tangible difference in their local communities.
 With fun activities and games for the whole family after the walk, the enjoyable, healthy day out with friends and family made a real, lasting impact by promoting active lifestyles and supporting the work of national and local charities.

/News/2025/BAPS-Baltimore-inauguration-2.t: Inauguration of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Baltimore, MD, USA
/News/2025/BAPS-Baltimore-inauguration-2.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Pratishtha by HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (8 photos)
 Nagar Yatra (10 photos)
 Mahapuja Vidhi (14 photos)
 Murti Sthapan Ceremony (22 photos)
 A vibrant and festive atmosphere filled Nottingham, Maryland, as hundreds of devotees and well-wishers gathered to celebrate the inauguration of the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Baltimore. Diyas, colorful rangolis, flower garlands, and decorative lights set the scene as families came together to witness a historic milestone for the Hindu community of Baltimore and Harford Counties. The origins of satsang in Baltimore trace back to the 1960s, when His Holiness Yogiji Maharaj encouraged devotees to visit the city and nurture their faith. His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj also visited the area on several occasions, including in 1984 and 1988, blessing devotees and inspiring the dream of a mandir. That vision was realized decades later with the establishment of this new house of worship in the White Marsh region of Baltimore County.
 The two-day celebrations commenced on Friday, August 8, 2025, with a vibrant Nagar Yatra, a traditional parade featuring grand floats carrying the sacred murtis, as children, youth, and adults joined together in the joyous procession.
 On Saturday, August 9, 2025, the inauguration day commenced with a grand Mahapuja, where devotees offered prayers for peace and well-being. Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, Pujya Viveknidhidas Swami, Pujya Nilkanthsevadas Swami and other revered swamis of BAPS then performed the Murti Sthapan Ceremony (sacred image installation ceremony), officially dedicating the new mandir. These divine images had previously been consecrated by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj on July 12, 2025, at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Bochasan, India.
 Distinguished leaders from Maryland joined the celebration, reflecting the mandir’s significance as a place of harmony and unity. Maryland State Senator Carl Jackson (8th Legislative District) presented an official Senate Citation, stating, “May this be a place of peace, sanctuary, and inclusion. A space that reflects the strength and diversity of our shared community.” Maryland State Delegate Harry Bhandari (8th District) shared, “Without peace inside, we cannot create peace outside. This mandir will create that inner peace.” Other honored guests included Senator J.B. Jennings (7th District), Delegate Nick Allen (8th District), Delegate Kim Ross (8th District), and Bel Air Chief of Police Charles Moore.
 The inauguration of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Baltimore, marks a new beginning for the Hindu community in the region. Beyond serving as a place of worship, the mandir will continue to foster family unity, spiritual growth, and charitable service, while making a positive impact in the broader community for generations to come.

/News/2025/BAPS-Campus-Fellowship-Diwali.t: BAPS Campus Fellowship Diwali Celebration 2025, North America
/News/2025/BAPS-Campus-Fellowship-Diwali.text:
The festival of Diwali is a time for celebrating the triumph of good over evil. Over 40 campuses across North America held Diwali celebrations organized by BAPS collegiate youth. Across all campuses, more than 40,000 participated in the festivities, including collegiate faculty, students, and members of the surrounding community. Putting their busy schedules aside, BAPS student volunteers meticulously planned campus celebrations that would relay the joy and importance of Diwali to their fellow peers.
 Additionally, they prepared various vegetarian dishes for the devotion-filled tradition of Annakut, an offering of food to Bhagwan.
 This year’s program was themed “Forgiveness: The Path to an Inner Symphony.” Through interactive presentations, motivational speeches by Pujya Swamis, and demonstrations of Hindu practices, attendees learned the importance of forgiveness. The interactive exhibition further explained the theme by drawing an analogy between musical instruments and the concept of forgiveness. The visuals and activities highlighted forgiveness within oneself, forgiveness of others, and forgiveness as a spiritual offering. Many arrived in traditional Indian clothing and were warmly welcomed with a chandlo (red vermilion mark) on their foreheads and a nadachhadi (red sacred thread) on their wrists. As the community came together to celebrate the auspicious festival of Diwali, they reflected on the importance of harmony, unity, and courage.
 Under the continued spiritual guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS continues to play an active role in promoting the spirit of Hinduism by organizing community events that share the importance of Hindu values and ideals. Campus Diwali celebrations are integral in equipping collegiate youth with the values and ideals that will guide them as they pursue personal and professional goals.

/News/2025/BAPS-Charities-Community-Food.t: BAPS Charities Community Food Drive 2025, UK
/News/2025/BAPS-Charities-Community-Food.text:
Devotees from BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK joined together in a nationwide drive this winter to support local families facing food insecurity through their annual Community Food Drive.
 This coordinated effort was a part of BAPS’s multifarious activities to support local communities, addressing the important issue of food insecurity.
 As the cost-of-living crisis continues to place significant strain on households around the country, food banks are experiencing record demand. In response, devotees and volunteers from various BAPS mandirs and centres, working in collaboration with their charity arm BAPS Charities, mobilised in a spirit of service, compassion, and collective action.
 Throughout November and December, volunteers coordinated with local devotees to collect hundreds of essential non-perishable food items, including cereals, pasta, lentils, tinned goods, UHT milk, and other everyday necessities. These were donated to local food banks and community charities to support their vital work of feeding the hungry.
 The nationwide collection by BAPS contributed to a combined donation of provisions equating to thousands of meals for food banks around the country, coming at a crucial time when many individuals and families continue to face financial hardships exacerbated by a difficult winter period.
 The initiative also strengthened relationships between local mandirs and their surrounding community organisations, many of whom continue to rely heavily on public support at this challenging time. Some centres partnered with longstanding local charities, while others connected with new organisations responding to rising levels of food poverty.
 As one volunteer later shared, “When we deliver these donations, we’re not just giving food – we’re sharing hope. Every tin, every box, every bag reminds someone that their community cares about them.”
 Representatives from recipient charities expressed their appreciation for the continued support of their local BAPS mandir or centre, noting the timeliness and sensitivity of the assistance during the busy winter season.
 The collective effort of devoteees and volunteers across the UK reflects the values at the heart of BAPS inspired and guided by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj – selfless service, community spirit, humility, and compassion for all. As communities continue to face unprecedented challenges, the Food Drive stands as a reminder of how meaningful change can arise through shared goodwill and sincere service.

/News/2025/BAPS-Downingtown-inauguration.t: Inauguration of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Downingtown, PA, USA
/News/2025/BAPS-Downingtown-inauguration.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Murti Pratishtha by HH Mahant Swami Maharaj (10 photos)
 Women’s Cultural Program (23 photos)
 Youth Cultural Program (23 photos)
 Murti Sthapan Ceremony (49 photos)
 Selfless Service: The Foundation of the Mandir (13 photos)
 The weekend of June 28–29, 2025, marked a joyous chapter for the Hindu-American community as the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Downingtown, Pennsylvania, hosted its grand two-day inaugural celebrations. Swamis, devotees, local leaders, and neighbors came together in a vibrant display of faith, tradition, and togetherness. 
 Saturday, June 28 – A Day of Cultural Tributes
 The weekend began with a Women’s Cultural Program on Saturday morning—a heartfelt event organized for women, by women. Featuring vibrant folk dances, thoughtful skits, and inspirational speeches, the program honored the role of women in upholding values such as faith, family, and community. The event concluded with a collective prayer, fostering spiritual connection and unity among attendees.
 That evening, the Youth Cultural Program, titled “My Mandir, My Heritage,” took center stage. The program emphasized the importance of mandirs in preserving Hindu values, traditions, and identity. The climax of the evening was a vibrant folk-dance performance that celebrated the spirit of all major Hindu festivals such as Diwali, Janmashtami, Holi, and Ganesh Jayanti. The choreography combined traditional movements with energetic music, brought to life by dedicated youth from Downingtown and Lansdale. Their enthusiasm and grace transformed the stage into a celebration of culture and devotion. Pujya Yogananddas Swami and Pujya Chaitanyamurtidas Swami offered spiritual reflections, urging the youth to lead lives rooted in seva (selfless service) and sanskar (values).
 Sunday, June 29 – Murti Sthapan Ceremony
 The celebrations culminated on Sunday with the Murti Sthapan Ceremony (Sacred Image Installation Ceremony), led by Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami. The morning began with a traditional Vedic Mahapuja, followed by the ceremonial installation of the sacred murtis. These divine images had previously been consecrated by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj on July 28, 2023, at BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey.
 Following the ceremony, devotees offered a grand Annakut, presenting a devotional array of vegetarian dishes to the newly installed murtis. The event was attended by hundreds, including community dignitaries.
 Dignitary Remarks
 Mayor Phil Dague of Downingtown shared his heartfelt appreciation for BAPS, praising its efforts in spiritual upliftment, cultural enrichment, and community service. “The new mandir,” he said, “will bring peace and make the town, the area, and the world a better place.”
 U.S. Senator Dave McCormick of Pennsylvania sent a message of goodwill, noting: “This mandir will serve as a center for values and uplift our entire community with unity, compassion, and devotion.” He praised the dedication of BAPS volunteers, adding, “You have not only created a place of worship, but also a place for future generations to learn, to grow and to give back.”
 A Community Anchor for the Future
 The newly inaugurated BAPS Mandir is poised to become a vital hub for spiritual learning, cultural celebrations, and community service. As it opens its doors to the wider public, it promises to enrich the community and contribute to the overall well-being of the region.

Photo Gallery 
 Karyakar Satsang Shibir (77 photos)
 Over 235 dedicated karyakars from BAPS centers in Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand gathered at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Bangkok for a spiritually enriching three-day Satsang Shibir themed ‘Suvarna Se Adhik’.
 The shibir focused on some of the essential pillars of BAPS Satsang: Prapti, Satsang Reading, Nitya Puja, Ghar Sabha, and Pragat Nishtha. These core topics were explored through insightful discourses by experienced and learned swamis, inspiring videos and engaging presentations.
 Separate parallel sessions for balaks-balikas and kishores-kishoris provided age-appropriate learning, deepening their understanding and practice of Satsang values.

/News/2025/BAPS-Executive-Forum-SJC-2869.t: Bay Area Tech Leaders Gain Insight into Values-Based Leadership at BAPS Executive Forum, San Jose, CA, USA
/News/2025/BAPS-Executive-Forum-SJC-2869.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS Executive Forum (13 photos)
 In a vibrant and uplifting gathering, senior technology leaders from across the San Francisco Bay Area convened at the BAPS Executive Forum, hosted at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Milpitas, CA. The event provided a unique opportunity for executives to connect with like-minded peers, reflect on purpose-driven leadership, and draw inspiration for personal and professional growth.
 Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami delivered the evening’s keynote, centering his address on the theme “Value Added Life – Leading with Values, Thriving with Purpose.” He shared powerful insights that deeply resonated with the audience, many of whom hold high-impact roles in Silicon Valley’s most influential companies.
 With clarity, warmth, and wisdom, he articulated four core principles for values-based leadership:
 Make Time, Don’t Just Find It – Be intentional with your time, especially for your loved ones and teams during moments that matter.
 Forgive and Let Go – Release the weight of others’ mistakes to move forward with peace and clarity.
 Believe in People – Win hearts, not just minds. Trust is the foundation of authentic leadership.
 Honor Your Word – Integrity begins with keeping promises. Your word shapes your legacy.
 Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami enriched these teachings with stories from his close experiences with visionary leaders such as His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, and former President of India Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, illustrating how timeless values shaped their enduring impact.
 The evening concluded with a personal interaction between each attendee and Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami. Many leaders shared that they left feeling spiritually renewed, thoughtful about their own journey, and newly inspired to lead with greater purpose.
 This unique forum highlighted the growing recognition that in a world increasingly driven by technology, it is timeless human values that remain the most enduring force behind thriving teams, organizations, and lives.

/News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Abu-Dhabi-H.t: BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi Highlighted at TEDx, Tampa, FL, USA
/News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Abu-Dhabi-H.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami at TEDx Tampa (23 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi took center stage at TEDx Tampa, as Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami addressed a sold-out audience of over 1,000 delegates. TEDx is a global platform where top leaders and changemakers share transformative ideas with millions worldwide.
 Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami elaborated on how simple, everyday conversations have the power to shape history. Beginning with the question on everyone’s mind, “Why are his clothes orange?”, he explained that saffron represents the colors of cremation and self-sacrifice, reminding us of our impermanence and urging us to strive to do as much good as we can, to as many people as we can, for as long as we can.
 He then wove together three pivotal conversations ­– one in the heart of a silent desert with no one around, one conversation in a corridor with everyone around, and one within the quiet palace of the Ruler of Abu Dhabi. Each carried a vital lesson: the power of choosing a single inner ‘yes’ over a thousand voices saying ‘no’, and the ability of generosity to unite entire cultures.
 Building on those lessons, Pujya Brahmaviharidas left the audience with a timeless message from His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, “In the joy of others lies our own.” Beautifully echoed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who often says, “You only live when you give.” Together, these words did more than inspire, they offered a philosophy to live by.
 The other remarkable speakers at TEDx Tampa were: John Couris, CEO of Tampa General Hospital; Laurel Lee, U.S. Congresswoman for Florida’s 15th District; Rhea Law, President of the University of South Florida; Bawa Jain, Secretary General of the World Council of Religious Leaders; Michael Stephens, CEO of Tampa International Airport; Dan Toomey, investigative journalist and founder of ‘Good Work’; Randall Kaplan, founder and former CEO of Akamai Technologies; Tim DeKay, acclaimed actor, director, and producer; and Wardah Inam, CEO of Overjet AI and a pioneer in dental artificial intelligence.
 Prominent media representatives from FOX, ABC, NBC, PBS, and other major outlets were in attendance, capturing the energy and power of the event. In addition, more than 25 digital content creators, including national commentators, and Tampa-based creative voices, amplified the event’s message across social media platforms, reaching tens of thousands in real time and far beyond the auditorium walls.
 Experiences
 “This has been the best experience of my life.” - John Couris, CEO of Tampa General Hospital
 “Forever changed after hearing Swami speak.” - Kara
 “The monk’s message stayed with me the most because kindness can be practiced by anyone and in everything we do. I also loved his message about the power of everyday conversations.” - Virginia

/News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Honored-wit.t: BAPS Hindu Mandir Honored with the Prestigious MONDO-DR 2025 Award, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Honored-wit.text:
Photo Gallery 
 MONDO-DR 2025 Award (14 photos)
 ‘The Fairy Tale’ immersive experience at the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi has been awarded one of the most prestigious accolades in the global audiovisual industry: the ‘2025 MONDO-DR Award’ in the ‘House of Worship’ category. Described as the ‘Oscars of the AV world’, the MONDO-DR Awards are presented by MONDO-DR, which is the leading international magazine focused on technology installations in entertainment and architectural venues.
 Held at Ole Red Orlando, Florida, on 11 June 2025, the awards celebrated the highest achievements in audiovisual integration across entertainment venues, architectural landmarks, and cultural spaces.
 This recognition cements the BAPS Hindu Mandir not only as a spiritual and architectural marvel but also as a technological benchmark for immersive AV design in sacred spaces.
 A CATEGORY FILLED WITH GLOBAL EXCELLENCE
 The House of Worship category at this year’s MONDO-DR Awards featured a record number of entries from across the world, including, renowned cathedrals, mosques, and synagogues with excellent AV designs. With dozens of high-profile submissions showcasing advanced audio and immersive lighting systems, the competition was fierce.
 Judged by a panel of international experts assembled by MONDO-DR, the awards identify exceptional projects that merge innovation with impact.
 In the world of AV, a MONDO-DR Award holds a similar prestige that an Academy Award represents in film: a mark of global excellence and peer-recognized mastery. That ‘The Fairy Tale’ immersive show at the BAPS Hindu Mandir was selected as the winner in such a saturated field is a clear testament to the unmatched integration quality, technical precision, and cultural sensitivity demonstrated throughout the BAPS Hindu Mandir project.
 FIRST IN SPIRITUAL EXPERIENCE ENGINEERING
 The first traditional Hindu stone temple in the Middle East, the BAPS Hindu Mandir stands as a symbol of peace and harmony and now, thanks to its sophisticated AV implementation, as a global showcase of innovation.
 Designed to create a deeply spiritual, yet technology-enriched atmosphere, the show integrates seamlessly into the aesthetic, acoustic, and ceremonial fabric of the temple complex. The award-winning audiovisual system was developed through a global collaboration of AV consultants, lighting designers, acoustic engineers, and AV integrators, all working under strict constraints, such as cultural sensitivity, architectural limitations, and environmental extremes.
 TRANSCENDING TECHNOLOGY
 The show itself is the culmination of creative concepts, scripting, visualizations, animations, and meticulous designing by an in-house BAPS team of swamis and volunteers, with selfless assistance from professional audio-visual experts. It has been brought to life using 20 video projectors and a cutting- edge surround sound experience.
 Adrian Goulder, Technical Director of VueAV, aptly explains why the award was unanimously awarded to the BAPS Hindu Mandir, “Every immersive show and AV experience showcases the latest available technology. What makes ‘The Fairy Tale’ Immersive Show at the BAPS Hindu Mandir stand apart, and so impactful, is its creativity, concept and global message. Most AV videos and presentations focus on user experiences to enhance a return on investment. However, here the message is solely on unity and spiritual growth. The script, its every word and whisper, written and narrated by Swami Brahmaviharidas is so powerful and penetrating that the message of harmony resonates within every heart. It is more than an immersive experience, it is transformative. Superlative. Out of this world experience!”
 THE IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCE
 The audience is transported through time and space, witnessing and experiencing all the pivotal moments: His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s first prayer in the deserts of Sharjah (1997), the generosity of the UAE President His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in the Presidential Palace (2018), and the spiritually charged inauguration performed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and Prime Minister Narendra Modi (2024).
 MESSAGE OF GLOBAL HARMONY
 Calling Abu Dhabi an ‘Epicenter of Harmony,’ the show unfolds a new dimension to the values of tolerance and harmony, significantly adding to the Mandir’s message of global inclusivity. It is committed to bridging and bringing together cultures, communities, and countries, reflecting the global appreciation for this extraordinary place of worship.
 “We're honored and humbled to receive this award,” said Swami Brahmaviharidas. “This was never about just installing a show, sound systems or lighting. This was about designing an environment where every heart regardless of background, can feel a deeper connection to universal spirituality.”
 BRIDGING HERITAGE AND FUTURE
 The award is not only a triumph for BAPS Hindu Mandir, but also for the UAE as a whole. It signifies the country’s commitment to religious tolerance, cultural inclusion, and global excellence in design and innovation.
 PREVIOUS AWARDS & RECOGNITIONS
 Inaugurated in February 2024, the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi has already received multiple prestigious awards, including: The MEED Project Awards (2024) – recognizing it the as the ‘Best Cultural Project’ in the UAE and across the MENA region; the Mechanical Engineering Plumbing MEP Award (2019) – for exceptional mechanical, electrical, and plumbing engineering; and recognition from the World Architecture Festival and other international forums, establishing it as one of the world’s most impressive and celebrated buildings.

/News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Hosts-A-Sym.t: BAPS Hindu Mandir Hosts ‘A Symphony of Harmony’ Honoring People of Determination, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Hosts-A-Sym.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS Hindu Mandir Hosts ‘A Symphony of Harmony’ (20 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi hosted an inspiring evening titled ‘A Symphony of Harmony’, celebrating People of Determination and highlighting the UAE’s values of inclusion, compassion, and shared humanity. More than 500 guests attended, including UAE leadership, community figures, and families of People of Determination.
 The highlight of the evening was a breathtaking performance by 15-year-old Emirati pianist and composer Ahmed Al Hashemi, a young star on the autism spectrum who has represented the UAE in over 200 international performances. Recipient of the UNESCO Rising Talent Honorary Certificate and the Mother Teresa Memorial Award, Ahmed performed eight pieces – including works by Beethoven and his own compositions – offering a moving reminder that courage and creativity transcend all limitations.
 Ahmed shared that he was inspired to perform at the Mandir after feeling ‘peace and love’ during a previous visit. His original piece ‘Dark to Light’, composed as a tribute to the Mandir, symbolized humanity’s journey from challenge toward harmony.
 During the interlude, Swami Brahmaviharidas reflected on the transformative power of music through a story from the life of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. He emphasized that harmony begins within each person and praised Ahmed as a beacon of determination, adding: “With courage, compassion and determination, let us overcome all inner limitations to create a world of harmony.” He also thanked the UAE leadership for empowering People of Determination nationwide.
 Swami Brahmaviharidas honoured Ahmed with a special memento, while BAPS volunteer Ms. Shaily Desai honoured Ahmed’s mother, Eiman Alaleeli, for her unwavering support. Distinguished guests, including Brigadier Hamed of Joint Taskforce Abu Dhabi; H.E. Mubarak Al Ameri and H.E. Mohamed Al Balooshi, representing H.E. Dr. Mugheer Khamis Al Khaili, Chairman of the Department of Community Development; Mr. Zubin Karkaria, CEO of VFS Global; and Dr. Vibu Bose, Executive Director of Ahalia Medical Group, were also felicitated.
 The evening concluded with heartfelt interactions between guests and People of Determination. Rabbi Jeff Berger and Asma Rubayea Al Menhali praised the Mandir as a sanctuary of harmony, coexistence, and human connection.

rows: The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi hosted a unique event, A Symphony of Harmony, honoring People of Determination.

Under the starlit sky by the Ganga ghat, 15-year-old autistic Emirati pianist Ahmed Al Hashemi, an internationally recognized artist and recipient of the UNESCO Rising Talent Honorary Certificate and the Mother Teresa Memorial Award, captivated the audience with his inspiring performance.

A Symphony of Harmony, brought together over 500 guests, including UAE leaders, UAE nationals, community leaders and People of Determination, to celebrate People of Determination, courage, and harmony.
Ahmed opened the recital with his first set, Notes of Silence and Faith, featuring his original compositions and classical pieces by Ludwig van Beethoven.
Once challenged in verbal expression, Ahmed discovered his voice through music, a universal language that bridges differences and inspires all.
Ahmed performed with the loving presence of his family in the audience, their support guiding and inspiring him.
Ahmed shared, ‘I was so moved by the temple’s peace and love that I knew I wanted to perform here. My first big solo in the UAE in such a meaningful place is a dream come true.’
As Ahmed’s first set concludes, he asks the audience to take a few minutes to prepare for his next performance.
As the audience pauses to reflect, Swami Brahmaviharidas, the visionary behind the event, is invited to share his thoughts about the evening.
Swami Brahmaviharidas opened by reflecting on the profound power of music and melody, showing how a simply melody can transform not only the world around us but also the world within.

The audience was enlightened as Swami Brahmaviharidas highlighted that every challenge is an opportunity to grow, inspiring us to face life with courage, compassion, and determination to build a harmonious world.

Swami Brahmaviharidas concluded by expressing gratitude to the UAE leadership, for their support not only for the Mandir but also in empowering People of Determination across the nation and helping each of them shine.

Moved by the evening, Ahmed shared his gratitude, saying his music carries a message of love, peace, and harmony, uniting hearts beyond language and differences. With Tolerance Day approaching, he celebrated the UAE’s spirit of inclusivity and thanked the Mandir and everyone for this special evening.
At the end of the recital, all the guests rose to give Ahmed a standing ovation, not just for his gifted performance, but for his courage, determination, and inspiring spirit.
Ahmed Al Hashemi thanked Swami Brahmaviharidas for his love, friendship, and prayers.
To honor Ahmed’s determination and the inspiration he brings to many, Swami Brahmaviharidas presented him with a special memento, a model of the Mandir surrounded by musical notes.

Swami Brahmaviharidas also honored distinguished members of the UAE leadership and community for their unwavering support: Brigadier Hamed of Joint Taskforce Abu Dhabi; H.E. Mubarak Al Ameri and H.E. Mohamed Al Balooshi, representing H.E. Dr. Mugheer Khamis Al Khaili, Chairman of the Department of Community Development; Mr. Zubin Karkaria, CEO of VFS Global; and Dr. Vibu Bose, Executive Director of Ahalia Medical Group.

 Deputy President of South Africa Paul Mashatile attended this historic occasion and met His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The deputy president praised the mandir’s contribution to multiculturalism and interfaith harmony in South Africa.
 As the largest mandir and cultural complex in the Southern Hemisphere, this spiritual landmark stands as a beacon of unity, heritage, and interfaith dialogue. /News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Welcomes-De.t: BAPS Hindu Mandir Welcomes Defence Attachés of Over 20 Nations, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Welcomes-De.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS Hindu Mandir Welcomes Defence Attachés of Over 20 Nations (25 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi ushered in the New Year by hosting Defence Attachés, dignitaries and  families  from more than 20 embassies in a unique celebration of ‘Unity, Diversity and Harmony’.
 The event brought together Defence Attachés from Belgium, Canada, Comoros Island, Czech Republic, Denmark, Egypt, France, Germany, Greece, India, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Korea, Mozambique, Tanzania, Serbia, Switzerland and other countries.
 BAPS board members and volunteers traditionally welcomed the delegates with garlands and roses. Thereafter, the delegates ascended the Prayer Dune to offer selfless prayers for world peace, watched the ‘The Fairy Tale’ immersive show, which recreates the incredible journey of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, and viewed the 6,500-year-old sub-fossil oaks from the  Czech Republic.
 Then, the dignitaries admired the Mandir’s elaborate architecture and the intricately    carved ancient civilizational value tales on the mandir’s façade, while learning about how the Mandir inspires spiritual elevation, cultural preservation, and  social service.
 Then, in a brief address to the guests in ‘The Orchard’ Brahmaviharidas Swami, said, “The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi reflects our deep love for God and humanity, our commitment to global harmony, and our belief that, at their core, even those engaged in conflict seek peace. The vast diversity of flowers, faces and races strengthen our belief that God and nature that created us all believe in harmony.”
 In his vote of thanks, Captain Harpreet Singh Luthra congratulated the Mandir on welcoming two million visitors within the first year. Highlighting its role as a symbol of India-UAE friendship, he emphasized the Mandir’s significance as a cultural bridge between the two nations.
 The evening concluded with the delegates sharing and discussing ideas of peace and harmony while enjoying a dinner of exquisite Indian vegetarian dishes home cooked by volunteers.
 Guest Experiences
 Kale Glaicar, Canada: “This mandir is a very beautiful and it is so nice to be welcomed into a place of worship that is open to everyone regardless of religion. It will help people understand different religions and different cultures. One of the messages is tolerance of different people, different cultures, and different viewpoints. And this just emulates that.”
 Nicolai Abildgaard, Denmark: “I have thoroughly enjoyed my visit and the key inspiration that I will take away from this visit is that tolerance must be nurtured. I have never been in a place where so much positive vibe and ambient tolerance are portrayed. It is truly magnificent.”
 Nico Hoornaert, Denmark: “The temple’s impressive design and surroundings reflect India’s rich culture and spiritual essence. Its creation, the result of over a thousand people working together, shows that ‘Alone you go far, but together you go further.’”
 Tae ik Yeo, Korea: “I am honored to be here where different religions can be harmonized in this holy place. I feel today I had a ‘spiritual flight’ in the Hindu Mandir.”
 Takayuki Kubo, Japan: “Our experience was truly amazing. We were enveloped in the warm hospitality of the organizers, and felt the powerful sense of unity among the gathering of the delegates, all resonating with the true spirit of the Mandir.”
 Ms. Andrea Russo, Italy: “The Harmony Wall is symbolic in uniting everyone. The interior of the temple is from Italian marble which makes me proud as these were just stones, but such wonderful carvings gave them life.”
 Susanne Steiner, Switzerland: “It is a gorgeous, magnificent structure, I love how every detail speaks of harmony.”
 Rita Rmeily, Switzerland: “May my child come into the world safely and may I be able to become a good mother to her and make her a Harmony ambassador too. I would regularly want to come here to sit and meditate and clear my mind under the Peace Dome.”

 TALKPODS Lecture (5 photos)
 Over 500 distinguished guests, representing many age groups, attended the fourth TalkPods lecture, which was hosted by BAPS Mumbai, in the presence of Pujya Doctor Swami.
 Renowned industrialist, Shri Chandubhai Virani, MD of the Balaji Group, shared his inspiring journey from humble beginnings to business success, emphasizing empathy, people-first leadership, and the importance of spiritual grounding in today’s fast-changing business world. He fondly recalled seeking the blessings of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj before commencing each factory and shared how Doctor Swami constantly inspired him to aim higher in his entrepreneurial journey. As a senior industry leader, he further highlighted the delicate wisdom required in mentoring today’s youths with understanding rather than authority.
 Pujya Doctor Swami also addressed the gathering, sharing heart-touching and motivating stories of youths he has met who have defied the odds to achieve spiritual and societal success.
 The event concluded with an engaging Q&A session that left attendees spiritually enriched and inspired.

/News/2025/BAPS-Karyakar-Shibir-Praptini.t: BAPS Karyakar Shibir: Praptini Pratiti, Africa
/News/2025/BAPS-Karyakar-Shibir-Praptini.text:
More than 1,300 male karyakars and 1,100 female karyakars participated in the BAPS Karyakar Shibirs held at 16 centers across 7 African countries: Uganda (Kampala, Lira, Jinja), Kenya (Mombasa, Nairobi, Kisumu, Eldoret, Nakuru), Tanzania (Dar es Salaam, Arusha, Mwanza), Malawi (Mzuzu, Blantyre), Zambia (Lusaka), Botswana (Gaborone), and South Africa (Johannesburg). The theme of the two-day shibirs was ‘Praptini Pratiti – Conviction of Attainment’.
 The attendees were dedicated volunteers serving in various mandir departments and in satsang activities. The shibirs featured informative and inspiring speeches – in person by resident swamis and via video conference by swamis from India – as well as workshops, discussions, Q&A sessions, engaging activities, and special videos that highlighted Mahant Swami Maharaj’s love for and appreciation of the karyakars.
 The shibirs guided the delegates to develop a deeper understanding of their own responsibility and commitment to Satsang duties; strengthened their thoughts on prapti; elaborated on awareness, faith, and spiritual contentment to help transform attainment into conviction; and highlighted the importance of personal outreach.
 The shibirs also provided insights on present day challenges, including cyber crime and social media awareness.
 The shibirs deepened the understanding of seva (selfless service) and sadhana (spiritual practices) among the karyakars, and recharged their devotion and dedication. They pledged to reflect daily for 15 minutes on our spiritual attainment (prapti).

/News/2025/BAPS-Participates-in-Bharatee.t: BAPS Participates in Bharateeya Santa Mahaa Parishhad, Bengaluru, India
/News/2025/BAPS-Participates-in-Bharatee.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Bharateeya Santa Mahaa Parishhad (31 photos)
 To strengthen and facilitate coordination between the various denominations of Sanatan Dharma, over 1000 spiritual heads, saints, acharyas, and mahatmas from India and across the globe attended the inauguration ceremony of Bharateeya Santa Mahaa Parishhad (BSMP) on 16 June 2025, in Bengaluru, South India.
 This historic gathering took place in the esteemed presence of:
 ● Jagadguru Shri Shankar Vi Jayendra Saraswati Swami Gal
   (Head, Jagadguru Kanchi Kamakoti Peeth)
 ● Jagadguru Ramanandacharya & Swami Rambhadracharya
 ● Jagadguru Sri Sri Varatri Deshi Kendra Mahaswamiji
   (Jagadguru Sri Veerasimhasan Mahasansthan Math, Sutturu Srikshetra)
 ● Acharya Shri Govinddev Giri Maharaj
   (Treasurer, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust)
 ● Sri Sri Swayam Prakash Sachchidanand Saraswati Mahaswamiji
   (Sri Adi Shankaracharya Sarada Lakshminarayan Singh Peetham)
 ● Sri Sri Sri Dr. Nirmalanandanath Mahaswamiji
   (Sri Adi Chunchanagiri Mahasansthan Math)
 ● Sri Vishwesha Tirtha Shri Ramnath Swamiji
   (Pejawar Math)
 ● HH Sadguru Bodhinatha Veylanaswamy Swamiji
   (Kauai Hindu Monastery, Hawaii, USA)
 ● Sri Masilamani Desi Gyan Sambandh Swamigal
   (Dharmapuram Adheenam, Mayiladuthurai, Tamil Nadu)
 ● Jain Acharya Shri Lokesh Muni Ji
   (Founder, Ahimsa Vishwa Bharati & World Peace Center, New Delhi)
 ● Sri Sri Sri Jayendra Puri Mahaswamiji
   (Padsevak Peethadhipati, Shri Kailash Ashram Mahasansthan, Bengaluru)
 On behalf of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami attended the BSMP. During his address at the inaugural ceremony, Bhadreshdas Swami highlighted the invaluable contributions of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj to society and Sanatan Dharma. He emphasized the three key pillars of Indian culture as taught by Pramukh Swami Maharaj: Mandir, Shastra, and Sant. He also conveyed Mahant Swami Maharaj’s heartfelt prayers for the preservation, nourishment, and flourishing of Vedic Sanatan Dharma and the great long-term success of the Bharateeya Sant Mahaa Parishad.
 Prior to the Parishad, on the evening of 15 June, Bhadreshdas Swami met Pujya Jayendrapuri Mahaswamiji of Rajarajeshwari Temple, Bengaluru, who appreciated BAPS's global efforts toward the propagation of Sanatan Dharma.
 Then, on 16 June, during the main inauguration, Bhadreshdas Swami met Jagadguru Shri Shankaracharya, who fondly recalled the divine lives and contributions of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, and also lauded the work of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Sanstha.

/News/2025/BAPS-Participates-in-Queens-I.t: BAPS Participates in Queens Interfaith Unity Walk, New York, NY, USA
/News/2025/BAPS-Participates-in-Queens-I.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Queens Interfaith Unity Walk (5 photos)
 On Sunday, March 23, 2025, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Flushing, New York, proudly served as the concluding stop of the 17th Annual Queens Interfaith Unity Walk. Organized by the Flushing Interfaith Council, the event brought together individuals of diverse backgrounds to promote dialogue, understanding, and peace across faith communities.
 BAPS devotees joined fellow participants on the walk, visiting various houses of worship and fostering connections along the way. As the final destination, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Flushing, New York welcomed over 100 attendees into a warm, inclusive atmosphere.
 Guests were offered light refreshments and invited to attend a thoughtful presentation on Hinduism, with a special emphasis on the Swaminarayan tradition and the teachings of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The presentation underscored BAPS’s dedication to universal harmony, seva (selfless service), and interfaith collaboration.
 Visitors also toured the mandir and engaged in meaningful conversations with devotees, gaining a deeper appreciation for Hindu traditions and the spiritual values that guide the BAPS community.
 The event beautifully reflected the timeless message of Pramukh Swami Maharaj: “In the joy of others lies our own.” It reinforced the powerful role faith communities play in building bridges of mutual respect and shared humanity.

/News/2025/BAPS-Participates-in-the-Afri.t: BAPS Participates in the Afri-Asia Drug Prevention and Treatment Summit 2025, Nairobi, Kenya
/News/2025/BAPS-Participates-in-the-Afri.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Afri-Asia Drug Prevention and Treatment Summit (15 photos)
 The Afri-Asia Drug Prevention and Treatment Summit 2025 was held in Nairobi, Kenya, under the theme “Drug Prevention Without Borders – Leave No One Behind”. The Summit brought together over 200 delegates from 24 countries across Africa, Asia, and beyond, fostering collaboration among leaders, policymakers, researchers, and organizations dedicated to addressing drug-related harms through prevention, education, and community engagement.
 The Summit was convened by Slumchild Foundation, SCAD Kenya, 4th Wave Foundation, Ministry of Health Kenya, NACADA, Bluecross Kenya, Graceful Youth and Recovery Centre, ISSUP Kenya, Childspace Organization, and Apar Foundation, uniting diverse partners in a shared commitment to advancing prevention and wellbeing across regions.
 Official Opening and Keynote Addresses
 Hon. Dr. Isaac Mwaura, Government Spokesman of Kenya, inaugurated The Afri-Asia Drug Summit 2025. In his address, Dr. Mwaura highlighted the importance of international cooperation in protecting public health and reaffirmed Kenya’s leadership in advancing evidence-based prevention.
 In the session’s keynote address, Paramtattva Swami spoke on effective addiction prevention, emphasizing the transformative power of moral values, spirituality, and community-based action in nurturing healthy, drug-free lifestyles. He illustrated how faith-based organizations like BAPS play a pivotal role in prevention by cultivating discipline, compassion, and social responsibility, reminding delegates that lasting change begins with character, family, and faith.
 Other keynote speakers included Dr. Anthony Omerikwa, CEO of NACADA Kenya, who affirmed that “Prevention is not an event, it’s a total commitment,” and Dr. Kevin Sabet, President of Smart Approaches to Marijuana (SAM), who urged global leaders to prioritize prevention-first approaches over drug legalization to protect communities and future generations.
 Launch of the Nairobi Declaration
 A defining moment of the Summit was the launch of the Nairobi Declaration on Drug Demand Reduction – a bold, action-oriented framework advocating prevention, education, youth empowerment, gender equality, and inter-continental collaboration.
 The Declaration marks a renewed commitment from the Global South to shared responsibility and collective action in addressing drug demand, rooted in compassion, cultural values, and evidence-based strategies.
 Volunteer Support and Mandir Visit
 BAPS volunteers supported the Summit by contributing to the logistics, protocol, and hospitality.
 Delegates also visited the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Nairobi, where they experienced the mandir’s tranquil spirituality, intricate architecture, and welcoming community atmosphere.

/News/2025/BAPS-Receives-Award-for-Servi.t: BAPS Receives Award for Services to Community Well-Being, London, UK
/News/2025/BAPS-Receives-Award-for-Servi.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Dangoor Awards 2025 (12 photos)
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha received the ‘Health & Well-Being’ award at the London Dangoor Awards 2025, for its outstanding service to Greater London’s communities through the BAPS wellNESS project.
 The initiative addresses the significant health inequalities faced by British South Asians – who experience higher rates of diabetes, heart disease, and mental health challenges – by promoting practical, sustainable habits that integrate physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.
 The London Dangoor Awards (formerly known as the London Faith & Belief Community Awards) celebrate the unsung heroes of London’s faith communities, highlighting projects that uplift society through service, compassion, and collaboration. The awards work closely with the Greater London Lieutenancy’s Council on Faith to strengthen connectedness and bring wider recognition to London’s interfaith landscape.
 The award was presented at the Royal Society of Medicine by Dr David Dangoor CBE, founder of the Dangoor Education foundation, alongside Bushra Nasir CBE DL, Chair of His Majesty’s Lord Lieutenant of Greater London’s Council on Faith.
 Inspired by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the BAPS wellNESS project is built upon four core pillars of health: Nutrition, Exercise, Stress Management, and Sleep. The programme empowers individuals of all ages to develop sustainable habits in each of these areas, while highlighting how these practices are further strengthened through spirituality. By integrating evidence-based guidance with spiritual wisdom, BAPS wellNESS encourages participants towards healthier, more balanced lives.
 More than 30 volunteers contributed to the project, delivering expert-led talks, interactive workshops, personalised well-being support, and practical resources, including journals, habit trackers, and healthy cookbooks. The initiative has engaged thousands of community members through in-person activities and digital resources. The accompanying webinars have encouraged thousands of participants to cultivate healthier habits and embed positive lifestyle changes.
 Speaking after receiving the award on behalf of BAPS, lead volunteer Dr Tanvi Raghvani shared, “This recognition belongs entirely to the volunteers who give their time and expertise to help others. BAPS wellNESS is about empowering our community to take small, meaningful steps towards better health so that each person can lead a more purposeful, joy-filled life.”
 BAPS in London has been consistently recognised for its valuable contributions to community health, elderly welfare, supporting women, children and youth development, etc. Some of the recent awards include the following:
     ● 2024: Elderly Welfare Centre – Services to the Elderly
     ● 2023: International Women’s Day – Supporting Women
     ● 2022: ‘Island of Heroes’ – Inspiring Youth
     ● 2020: Connect & Care – Covid-19 Response
     ● 2019: Health Screenings – Community Project of the Year
     ● 2018: Care Home Visits – Services to the Elderly
