/News/2025/Janmashtami-Celebrations-2025.text:
BAPS Mandirs across North America recently celebrated Janmashtami, honoring the divine incarnation of Bhagwan Shri Krishna on earth—a day filled with profound spiritual significance. The day came alive with devotion as attendees immersed themselves in bhajans, kirtans, austerities, and inspiring discourses by swamis. This year’s celebration centered on the theme Mamekam Sharanam Vraja, meaning devotees should be committed to seeking refuge in Bhagwan, highlighting the timeless principle from Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s teachings in the Bhagavad Gita.
 The program explored the concept of ashro, or refuge, through four key aspects: wisely choosing whom we place our faith in; developing unflinching ashro; surrendering with faith; and the benefits of ashro. Each segment drew from the life and divine actions of Bhagwan Shri Krishna, emphasizing his guidance to Arjun on the battlefield of Kurukshetra and its relevance for navigating life’s challenges today.
 Devotees of all ages participated in the celebration through musical performances, insightful skits and speeches, and traditional Indian dances, which brought these teachings to life. The program illustrated that ashro is not just a concept, but a personal journey and a transformative experience. Stories from Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s life, such as his unwavering protection of his devotees, were paired with lessons from the Bhagavad Gita to reinforce trust along that journey.
 The celebration concluded with devotional singing and heartfelt prayers. The program reinforced that true refuge lies in surrendering fully to Bhagwan and the Guru with utmost faith, love, and steadfast devotion, enabling stability even amid life’s uncertainties.

/News/2025/Janmashtami-Celebrations-BAPS.t: Janmashtami Celebrations, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Janmashtami-Celebrations-BAPS.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Janmashtami Celebrations (33 photos)
 More than 15,000 devotees celebrated Janmashtami over a two-day period at the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi.
 As part of the two-day celebrations, members of the ISKCON community sang soulful bhajans in the Abhishek Mandap. Dedicated teams of children and youths led the devotional singing with sincerity and grace.
 In the evening, children beautifully recited Bhagavad Gita shlokas before the shrine Bhagwan Krishna and Radhaji. Their clear and fluent Sanskrit pronunciations filled the atmosphere with divine vibrations.
 In the Janmashtami celebration assembly, more than 500 devotees assembled for Ashtami Puja and thereafter the Krishna Janmotsav with joy and reverence.
 The celebrations featured a magnificent annakut, the janmotsav arti and jhula darshan, with the murti of Bhagwan Shri Krishna gracefully seated in a beautifully adorned cradle.
 The UAE Bal-Kishore Mandal presented a thought-provoking drama titled ‘Gita Gyan – Yugo Se Yugo Tak’. Based on verses from the Bhagavad Gita, the presentation highlighted how these teachings which guided Arjun on the battlefield, also address modern-day challenges faced by children, youths, and families.
 In his address to the assembly, Swami Brahmaviharidas elaborated upon the timeless wisdom from Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s life, “When surrounded by societal darkness, when suffocation weighs upon us, do not despair­ ­– for that is precisely the moment when God enters our lives. Bhagwan teaches us that the darker the night, the more powerful even a single candle becomes. Never tire, never fear.
 “The Mandir stands today, not merely as a temple of stone, but as a living beacon of harmony and devotion ­– proclaiming to the world that even in the heart of the desert, faith can blossom into an oasis of peace and unity.”

/News/2025/Jena-Guru-Akshar-Hoy--Bal-Bal.t: Jena Guru Akshar Hoy | Bal-Balika Winter Shibir, UK
/News/2025/Jena-Guru-Akshar-Hoy--Bal-Bal.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Leicester, UK (60 photos)
 London, UK (60 photos)
 A one-day winter shibir for balaks and balikas aged 7 to 13 years was held on 14 December 2025 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, and on 25 January 2026 at BAPS Shri Swaminaryan Mandir, Leicester. More than 800 children from across the UK attended the shibir to strengthen their understanding of Akshar-Purushottam Upasana. Themed ‘Jena Guru Akshar Hoy’, the shibir brought this spiritual concept to life through a nautical journey in which the audience set sail on a symbolic voyage towards Akshardham, guided by Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Through a captivating theatre production, the programme followed three friends – Aarav, Vinay, and Rudra – on their journey across the ‘Ocean of Maya’. The boats represented Akshar Purushottam Upasana, which steered them through turbulent waters and past tempting islands that lured them from their course.
 The parts of the boat symbolised key principles: the rudder, being the guiding direction, represented Sarvoparipanu; the hull, which offers protection, represented Karta-Harta; the cannons, which provide strength, represented Sakar; and the sails, which provide power and force, represented Pragat.
 The delegates left with the following key lessons:
 ▪ Akshardham is our Goal – Life’s true destination is Akshardham; worldly pleasures are fleeting.
 ▪ Upasana is the Boat – Just as a vessel carries one safely across the sea, understanding Akshar-Purushottam keeps one afloat amid distractions.
 ▪ Jena Guru Akshar Hoy – Only when guided by the Akshar-Guru can one reach Purushottam swiftly and without error.
 ▪ Faith in the Living Sant – The Satpurush is divine, through whom Bhagwan works, loves, and remains present.
 Through interactive dramas, sant presentations, and immersive storytelling, balaks and balikas grasped how faith in Sarvopari Bhagwan gives courage through life’s storms, how the understanding of Karta-Harta brings stability, and how belief in the Pragat Satpurush accelerates spiritual progress. When the young voyagers pressed their “Emergency Button” of prarthana, they discovered that God and Swami were with them all along, listening and guiding them.
 Throughout the day, summary activity sessions deepened the insight and understanding of the four pillars of Akshar Purushottam Upasana.
 To conclude, a vibrant kirtan-bhakti session anchored everyone’s connection with the Pragat Guru, emphasising that Akshardham is not distant, but something to experience here and now on earth.
 All the participants left inspired to keep their boat strong, sail steadily, and remain lovingly connected to their Guru – the true way to Akshardham.

/News/2025/Jivan-Utkarsh-Mahotsav-Celebr.t: Jivan Utkarsh Mahotsav: Celebrating the Life and Values of Mahant Swami Maharaj, Jabalpur, India
/News/2025/Jivan-Utkarsh-Mahotsav-Celebr.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Jivan-Utkarsh-Mahotsav (37 photos)
 Thousands of devotees, dignitaries, and swamis from India and abroad participated with great devotion in the five-day Jivan Utkarsh Mahotsav (Festival for the Upliftment of Life) to celebrate Mahant Swami Maharaj’s divine life, teachings, and services to humanity at his birthplace in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh.
 Each morning, devotees drew inspiration from the saintly life of Mahant Swami Maharaj from the Mahant Charitam parayan delivered by Adarshjivandas Swami.
 In the evenings, Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami, Anandswarupdas Swami, Jnaneshwardas Swami, Brahmaviharidas Swami, Jnanvatsal Swami, Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami and other BAPS swamis delivered inspiring discourses on culture, selfless service, the role of saints in the uplift of society, and other topics. Their talks highlighted Mahant Swami Maharaj’s tireless dedication to spreading faith, unity, and compassion across the world.
 The inaugural evening session was graced by Dr. Mohan Bhagwat, Sarsanghchalak (Chief) of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), who emphasized the importance of spirituality in national development and encouraged all to draw inspiration from the selfless life of Mahant Swami Maharaj. In his address, he highlighted how the values of devotion, service, and humility embodied by Mahant Swami Maharaj can serve as guiding lights for a vibrant and value-based nation.
 The Hon. Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Shri Mohan Yadav, also graced the festival and inaugurated two transformative value-based initiatives for youth and students – ‘Chalo Bane Adarsh’ and the ‘Integrated Personality Development Course (IPDC)’. Both programs aim to foster moral education and holistic development in alignment with the National Education Policy (NEP 2020). The chief minister commended the efforts of BAPS in nurturing values and contributing to national uplift through education and spirituality.
 Supported by the Jabalpur Municipal Corporation, Mayor Shri Jagat Bahadur Singh announced that Jabalpur’s main road from Dayanand Chowk to Maharshi Valmiki Chowk would now be renamed as ‘Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj Marg’.
 Among the many other distinguished mahatmas and dignitaries who attended were Shri Rakesh Singh, Minister, PWD, Madhya Pradesh; Prof. Rajesh Kumar Verma, Vice-Chancellor, Rani Durgavati University; Prof. K.R.S. Sambashiva Rao, Vice-Chancellor, Mangalayatan University; Pujya Badriprapannacharyaji Maharaj; and Pujya Dandi Swami Shri Kalikanandji Maharaj, Kalidham. All expressed admiration for the life, work, and spiritual leadership of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 A special evening celebration also highlighted the contributions of women to social and spiritual life, featuring inspiring performances and reflections by members of the BAPS Women’s Wing, who showcased how Mahant Swami Maharaj’s teachings continue to inspire women to live with faith, strength, and devotion.
 The event was a sacred celebration of the timeless values, compassion, and divine vision of Mahant Swami Maharaj, whose life continues to inspire countless people toward service, spirituality, and harmony.

 More than 2,000 volunteers gathered for an inspiring Karyakar Shibir hosted in multiple locations across the UK and Europe – in London (UK), Leicester (UK), Manchester (UK), Paris (France), Heidenrod (Germany), and Lisbon (Portugal) – over the weekend of 22-23 March 2025.
 Themed ‘Upasak Karyakar’, the event aimed to deepen the understanding of what it means to be a devoted volunteer who firmly upholds and practises Akshar-Purushottam upasana as revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
 Participants reflected on Shastriji Maharaj’s immense hardships in propagating the eternal truth at the foundation of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, strengthening their conviction and commitment to seva.
 The programmes began by exploring the rich history of BAPS, helping karyakars understand its journey and progression. The focus then shifted to the four key principles of Shastriji Maharaj, explained by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, namely: faith in upasana; versatility and perseverance in one’s seva; humility and empathy whilst performing one’s seva; and remaining dedicated and loyal.
 The shibir featured a diverse range of engaging sessions, including panel discussions that explored the practical application of upasana in one’s daily life, inspiring presentations on seva and spiritual resilience, discourses by swamis reinforcing the importance of humility, dedication and steadfastness, and impactful videos bringing to life the legacy of Shastriji Maharaj and his spiritual principles.
 These powerful sessions instilled inspiration amongst the delegates who departed with a renewed feeling of empowerment to perform their respective seva with conviction, humility, and unwavering faith. The shibir reinforced the importance of remaining rooted in upasana while excelling in seva, ensuring that the spiritual legacy of Shastriji Maharaj continues to thrive.
 Pooja Parmar from Munich, Germany, who attended the event in Heidenrod, shared, “The compassionate and selfless service of Shastriji Maharaj and his spiritual successors is so relevant today – their principles serve as a guiding light and were beautifully presented. It was also very inspiring to hear personal testimonies from fellow karyakars who perform their seva with such diligence and dedication whilst remaining steadfast in their own spiritual endeavours as well as devoted to their families and successful in their careers.”

/News/2025/Kids-Diwali-Celebrations--BAP.t: Kids’ Diwali Celebrations BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Kids-Diwali-Celebrations--BAP.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Kids’ Diwali Celebrations (25 photos)
 Over 300 children gathered for the special Kids’ Diwali Celebration titled ‘The Ultimate Win’. The event began with the children participating in the mahapuja, creating an atmosphere of devotion and peace, and enabling them to connect with the deeper meaning of Diwali as a time for introspection and renewal. The children prayed for good health, academic success, and a year filled with happiness for themselves, their families, and the world. 
 Next, they attended a play on stories from the Ramayan. Through creative storytelling, the children learned that no service is too small for God and that unflinching faith results in the ultimate win.
  The celebrations concluded with a Diwali Carnival, featuring bouncy castles, face painting, carnival-themed games, and a lively magic show.
 The Kids’ Diwali Celebration blended devotion, learning, and fun, and providing participants with lasting memories and a deeper appreciation of the timeless values of Diwali. The entire event – from the initial concept to the final farewell – was planned, organized, and managed by youth volunteers.
 Children’s Experiences
 “The mahapuja was so special, I felt peaceful, and I enjoyed praying with everyone together,” said Prapti.
  “The Ramayan play was amazing! I loved watching all the characters come to life and learning how good always wins,” shared Bhavya.
  “The games and activities were so much fun. I especially enjoyed playing on the bouncy castle! I got to play with my friends, and I also got my face painted,” said Smruti.

/News/2025/Kids-Diwali-Celebrations-2025.text:
The Hindu festival Diwali celebrates the return of Bhagwan Shri Ram to his home kingdom of Ayodhya. It symbolizes the victory of good over evil and is commonly associated with lit diyas (lamps), symbolizing the triumph of good. The Kids’ Diwali Celebration held annually at mandirs across North America aims to share the spiritual significance of Diwali with children in a joyful and memorable way.
 This year’s celebration was centered around the theme ‘Sanghe Shaktihi: Strength in Unity.’ The festive event featured engaging exhibitions that explored the themes behind Diwali by teaching children important values from stories of Hinduism. The children participated in the celebration with their families and left with a better understanding of the meaning behind Diwali and how to imbibe courage, unity, and righteousness (dharma) into their own lives. The celebration also featured interactive games, moon bounces, and other fun activities, making the event both educational and enjoyable. Additionally, the Saraswati Pujan honored the Hindu goddess of knowledge, arts, and wisdom.
 The annual Kids’ Diwali Celebration is one of many activities carried out under the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj that help to foster spirituality in youth and instill cultural values in a fun and engaging manner.

/News/2025/Kishore-Kishori-Adhiveshan--S.t: Kishore-Kishori Adhiveshan & Summer Shibir 2025, North America
/News/2025/Kishore-Kishori-Adhiveshan--S.text:
This summer, kishores and kishoris from high school and college across North America gathered for a transformative 4-day experience through the Adhiveshan and Summer Shibir, themed “Satsang: The Journey to Rajipo.” The Adhiveshan focused on memorizing selected verses (mukhpath) from sacred texts. Designed to go beyond memorization, the Adhiveshan emphasized cultivating a deeper understanding of mukhpath while deepening their connection with Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Satpurush.
 The purpose of the Adhiveshan was deeply rooted in earning the rajipo (blessings) of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. It aimed to help participants grasp introductory mukhpath—covering daily rituals, sabha-related items, and personal ahnik practices—while highlighting the importance of comprehension alongside memorization. It also emphasized the real-life value of mukhpath, demonstrating how these teachings could serve as guiding principles and offer grounding in the values of satsang.
 The Adhiveshan featured three categories: Prathmik Mukhpath, Purna Mukhpath with Satsang Diksha Challenge, and skills competitions. Completion of the Prathmik Mukhpath was a prerequisite to participate in the other categories. The Purna Mukhpath included various modules built around key satsang themes, drawing from Swamini Vato, Vachanamrut quotations, shlokas and sakhis, Satsang Diksha shlokas, kirtans, and prasangs.
 Following these sessions, participants channeled their creativity through a wide range of skills competitions. These skills competitions allowed participants to learn and develop new talents by combining their talents with the mukhpath they memorized. Skills included individual competitions such as art expressions (painting/drawing and 3D art), digital expressions (digital posters and photography), written expressions (article writing), technology expressions (app and website development), cultural expressions (classical dance), solo musical expressions (solo singing, solo wind instrumental, solo string instrumental, solo percussion instrumental), and verbal expressions (Vachanamrut, Swamini Vat, and Satsang Diksha nirupan, visual presentation, and prachar short speech). Group competitions including group musical expressions (group singing and group instrumental). 
 The event concluded with a message inspiring kishores and kishoris to continue expanding their satsang knowledge and embrace the path of shravan, manan, and nidhidhyas—a journey that leads toward sakshatkar and lifelong spiritual growth.

/News/2025/Kishore-Kishori-Shibirs-2025-.t: Kishore-Kishori Shibirs 2025: Apne Yad Karva, Asia Pacific
/News/2025/Kishore-Kishori-Shibirs-2025-.text:
Following the historic 2025 ‘Aksharbrahma in the Pacific’ vicharan of Mahant Swami Maharaj in the Asia Pacific region, over 500 kishores and kishoris from Australia and New Zealand participated in the special shibirs held in Adelaide, Auckland, Brisbane, Canberra, Christchurch, Darwin, Perth, Sydney, Wellington, and Melbourne.
 Titled ‘Apne Yad Karva’, the shibirs helped the youths to unlock the power of their memories from Swamishri’s visit, enhance their spiritual understanding of satsang, and strenghten their bond with the Satpurush. The shibirs focused on techniques to transform these sacred memories into lasting spiritual growth for the youths ­– turning ‘Aksharbrahma in the Pacific’ into ‘Aksharbrahma in my Heart’.
 Structured around four key themes of smruti (memories), samp (unity), bhajan (devotion), and niyam (observance of spiritual codes of conduct), the shibirs featured interactive activities and presentations, panel discussions, and focus sessions on three key smrutis from Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visit.
 This thoughtful approach guided the kishores and kishoris to transform their precious memories of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s historic Asia Pacific vicharan into practical tools for ongoing spiritual development.

/News/2025/Leader-of-the-Opposition-Hon-.t: Leader of the Opposition, Hon. Pierre Poilievre Visits BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2025/Leader-of-the-Opposition-Hon-.text:
The Honourable Pierre Poilievre, Leader of the Official Opposition of Canada, visited the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto on April 18, 2025, to pay his respects to Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan.
 Upon his arrival, the Hon. Poilievre was warmly welcomed by the Board of Directors of BAPS Canada and greeted in a traditional Hindu manner in the Abhishek Mandapam. Pujya Satyavratdas Swami honored him with a rose garland, and Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami tied a nada-chhadi (sacred thread) on his wrist.
 Pujya Gunsagardas Swami, Head Swami of BAPS activities in Canada, then performed the auspicious abhishek ritual of Nilkanth Varni Maharaj alongside the Hon. Poilievre. Together, they offered heartfelt prayers for peace and well-being across Canada and around the world.
 The Hon. Poilievre was then presented with Spirience: Experiencing Peace and Prosperity through Science and Spirituality, a thought-provoking book that explores the harmony between ancient spiritual wisdom and modern scientific understanding. The book offers a path toward personal well-being and global peace through the integration of science and spirituality. It was presented by Dr. V.I. Lakshmanan, who co-authored it alongside Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami (Head of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute) and Mr. S. Kalyanasundaram.
 During his visit, the Hon. Poilievre interacted with volunteers of all ages—from young children to seniors—as well as representatives from Hindu community organizations and local leaders, acknowledging their service and contributions to society.

/News/2025/Leader-of-the-Opposition-Kemi.t: Leader of the Opposition Kemi Badenoch Celebrates Diwali and Hindu New Year at Neasden Temple, London, UK
/News/2025/Leader-of-the-Opposition-Kemi.text:
Photo Gallery 
 London, UK (12 photos)
 The Rt Hon Kemi Badenoch MP, Leader of the Conservative Party, visited BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Wednesday 22 October 2025 to join the Diwali and Hindu New Year celebrations in Britain.
 Mrs Badenoch was warmly welcomed by senior volunteers before embarking on a brief tour of the Mandir. She spent several moments appreciating its spiritual atmosphere and intricate architecture, and observed the devotional annakut – literally, ‘mountain of food’ – beautifully arranged before the sacred deities as an offering of gratitude to mark the first meal of the new year.
 During her visit, volunteers presented artistic displays depicting the River Seine, its bridges, and iconic Parisian landmarks. The exhibition was organised to celebrate the forthcoming BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris – the first traditional Hindu temple in France – set to be inaugurated next year. Through these displays, Mrs Badenoch learned of the universal values of peace, harmony, and cross-cultural friendship that the new Mandir will embody.
 Addressing the congregation, Mrs Badenoch said, “It is a personal honour to join you at this joyous celebration, in this magnificent Neasden Temple, a testament to British diversity and a celebration of faith. The Hindu community in Britian continues to enrich our country through enterprise, education, charity, and seva, strengthening the fabric of modern Britain. Your values of faith, family, and service mirror the best of our national spirit – hard work, compassion, and the belief that we are stronger together.”
 Before departing the Mandir, Mrs Badenoch paused to interact with members of the community and was presented with a special gift as a memento of her visit.
 Sanjay Kara, a BAPS trustee in the UK, said: “We were honoured to welcome Kemi Badenoch to Neasden Temple for our Diwali and Hindu New Year celebrations. Diwali is a special time for reflection, renewal, and community, and we appreciate her taking the time to join us on this important occasion.”

/News/2025/Life-Enhancing-Seminars-by-Dr.t: Life-Enhancing Seminars by Dr Gnanvatsaldas Swami, Europe
/News/2025/Life-Enhancing-Seminars-by-Dr.text:
Dr Gnanvatsaldas Swami, a learned swami of BAPS and a highly sought-after motivational speaker, delivered a series of insightful seminars during his visit to Europe in May and June 2025.
 Delivering 20 presentations at BAPS mandirs and other venues across 12 European countries – Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, and Switzerland – Gnanvatsaldas Swami spoke on topics such as ‘Think Different, Be Different, Succeed Different’, ‘Stress Management’, ‘The Attitude Factor’, ‘To Serve is Life’, and ‘My Family, Happy Family’.
 The topics allowed attendees to receive practical guidance on how to tackle contemporary challenges currently being faced by individuals and families in both their personal lives as well as their professional careers.
 Drawing from the life, work and wisdom of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Gnanvatsaldas Swami spoke emphatically, helping inspire people towards personal integrity, family values, ethical leadership, community service, and global harmony.
 One delegate, working in finance, shared her experience after attending one of the seminars in Paris. She said, “What a refreshing and relatable talk! It was wonderful to gain an insight into the inspiring leadership of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj. These are values that are important for any organisation and its people, and I look forward to using their lives as inspiration for my own organisation for the future.”
 Gnanvatsaldas Swami also launched his new book, Inspired: Daily Wisdom for Holistic Living, at the seminars. The book, published by Penguin Random House India, is available from Amazon here.

/News/2025/Mahamahopadhyaya-Swami-Bhadre.t: Mahamahopadhyaya Swami Bhadreshdasji Honored with the Prestigious National Saraswati Award for Literature, Ahmedabad, India
/News/2025/Mahamahopadhyaya-Swami-Bhadre.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Award Presentation Ceremony (67 photos)
 The Saraswati Puraskar for the year 2024 has been conferred upon Mahamahopadhyaya Swami Bhadreshdasji for his unparalleled Sanskrit treatise, ‘Swaminarayan Siddhanta Sudha.’
 The Saraswati Puraskar (Saraswati Award) is one of India’s most prestigious literary awards, established by the K.K. Birla Foundation in 1991. It is presented annually for an outstanding literary work published within the previous 10 years by an Indian citizen in one of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 This esteemed award has been given to a work in the Sanskrit language after a gap of 22 years. Published in 2022, the ‘Swaminarayan Siddhanta Sudha’ presents the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, expounded by Parabrahma Bhagwan Swaminarayan, as a distinct philosophical tenet. The work has been praised for its classical scholarship, profundity of meaning, simplicity, and unique literary contribution, further strengthening India’s eternal Vedic tradition.
 The Honorable Governor of Gujarat and Maharashtra Shri Acharya Devvratji graced the presentation ceremony. Also present on this occasion were Justice Shri A.K. Sikriji, former Supreme Court Judge and Chairman of the Saraswati Award Selection Committee and Dr. Suresh Rituparnaji, Trustee of the K.K. Birla Foundation.
 The ceremony commenced with the lighting of the sacred lamp. Thereafter, Dr. Suresh Rituparnaji highlighted the prestige of the nation’s eminent literary honor, the Saraswati Award, and elaborated on its rigorous and impartial selection process. He noted that, from among the finest works in 22 Indian languages, the awardee is chosen through a meticulous three-phase evaluation. After careful deliberation by around 90 distinguished scholars and consultation with a former Supreme Court judge, ‘Swaminarayan Siddhant Sudha’ was adjudged as the year’s foremost literary masterpiece.
 Expressing his sentiments, former Supreme Court Justice A.K. Sikri observed, “It is a matter of great pride that, for the first time in 34 years, a saint has been honored with this distinguished literary award. In bestowing this recognition upon Swamiji, the award itself has been ennobled.”
 Following these remarks, the Honorable Governor of Gujarat presented the award to Swami Bhadreshdasji.
 With characteristic humility, Swami Bhadreshdas addressed the gathering, “This honor is the result of the love, tireless efforts, and selfless dedication of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj. For me, it is not merely an honor, but a profound responsibility.”
 The Head of the world-renowned BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami, was also present at the ceremony. Expressing his delight in his address, he said, “I have personally witnessed Pujya Bhadresh Swami’s  inspiring academic journey of sacrifice and dedication. He has achieved this success through the inspiration and blessings of Param Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.”
 On this occasion, Pujya Anandswarupdas Swami reflected, “Pramukh Swami Maharaj was a seer of exalted foresight. Through his guidance and blessings, a once-restless child has become the great Sanskrit scholar known as Bhadresh Swami.”
 Presiding as Chief Guest and Chair of the ceremony, His Excellency Governor Acharya Devvrat remarked, “India’s ancient Vedic tradition, upheld by generations of ascetic sages, has been carried to the wider world through this monumental work by Swami Bhadreshdas. The profound contemplations of the Vedas, Upanishads, the Gita, and the Ramayan reside within this text, which forms a foundation for all human life and holds the promise of global welfare.”
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha is honored by the conferment of this prestigious award to Mahamahopadhyaya Swami Bhadreshdasji, who has dedicated this historic honor to Parabrahma Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2025/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-92nd-Jan.t: Mahant Swami Maharaj 92nd Janma Jayanti Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2025/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-92nd-Jan.text:
The 92nd birth anniversary of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj was devoutly celebrated at BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs and centres around the UK and across Europe. 
 The programme, titled ‘An Ocean of Virtues’, offered a luminous tribute to Mahant Swami Maharaj’s divine life. Through an ocean-themed presentation of devotion and reflection, devotees were inspired to contemplate upon his profound spiritual qualities.
 The celebration featured skits, conversations, sketches, bhajans, impressions from sadguru swamis, discourses from swamis, and a montage of video presentations. Together, these elements highlighted six virtues embodied by Mahant Swami Maharaj. 
 Ocean of Presence – which revealed how Mahant Swami Maharaj’s presence reaches beyond his physical proximity, blessing endless people across the world with guidance, compassion, and reassurance that they are never alone.
 Ocean of Selflessness – which reflected upon his tireless travels, personal correspondence and countless hidden sacrifices to serve others before himself.
 Ocean of Embracement – which included a medley of bhajans that depicted how Mahant Swami Maharaj embraces all unconditionally, nurturing their spiritual growth.
 Ocean of Humility – which underlined how he perceives all as divine, concealing his own greatness while embodying the highest humility.
 Ocean of Spirituality – which brought to life his ceaseless guidance that continually centres individuals upon God, inspiring a deep and abiding faith.
 Ocean of Love – which reminded thousands that his unconditional love flows through constant prayers and boundless care, and that his heart is universally open to all. 
 Mahant Swami Maharaj also shared a personal message, in which he explained how to experience an Ocean of Bliss: “God always walks beside you, and the Satpurush always carries you. This bond is forever.” His words and the day’s celebrations inspired all to deepen their spiritual connection and to imbibe his divine virtues in their daily lives.
 The celebrations across UK & Europe served as a precursor to the main janma jayanti mahotsav taking place in India in February 2026.

/News/2025/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-92nd-Jan.t: Mahant Swami Maharaj 92nd Janma Jayanti Mahila Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2025/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-92nd-Jan.text:
Mahilas of all ages across the UK and Europe joyously celebrated the birth anniversary of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj with the inspiring theme ‘You Know Him, You Love Him.’ Drawn from Mahant Swami Maharaj’s own words, the programme encouraged devotees to deepen their devotional bond with the guru, recognising that true spiritual love flourishes from profound understanding.
 Through devotional singing, inspiring speeches, and creative presentations, the celebrations highlighted four of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s divine virtues – his selfless service, humility, devotion to God and Guru, and dedication to his devotees. Each portrayal offered moments of reflection and inspiration, nurturing a stronger spiritual connection with the guru.
 The celebrations concluded with collective prayers and expressions of gratitude for Mahant Swami Maharaj, inspiring all to imbibe his teachings in their own lives. 
 For everyone who took part, it was an event of deep appreciation, filled with joyous devotion and an abiding sense of spiritual closeness – a true celebration of love for the guru.

/News/2025/Mahila-Parayans-During-Shrava.t: Mahila Parayans During Shravan Month 2025, Africa
/News/2025/Mahila-Parayans-During-Shrava.text:
More than 2,000 women devotees at BAPS centers throughout Africa attended the two-day Mahila Parayans organized during the holy month of Shravan by the BAPS Women’s Wing in Africa. The parayans were held in Kenya – Kisumu, Eldoret, Mombasa, Thika, Kakamega, Bungoma, Kericho, Ruiru, Kajiado, Athi River; Tanzania – Dar es Salaam, Mwanza, Arusha, Tanga; Uganda – Kampala, Jinja, Lira/Soroti, Mbale; Southern Africa – Johannesburg, Lenasia, Mayfair, Benoni, Laudium, Central Africa – Lusaka, Lilongwe, Limbe and Rwanda – Kigali.
 The parayans focused on Mahant Swami Maharaj’s message that the form of God we have attained is the greatest blessing of life, and this attainment must be transformed into personal experience. The  discourses revolved around two themes. First day: Mune pragat malya Purushottam aj…  and second day: Bhagya Jagya re aj…
 Through kirtans, multimedia presentations, and inspiring talks, the women devotees at each center reflected on the greatness of this divine gift. The lives of great women devotees were also highlighted: Monghiba of Gondal and Jhamkuba of Mewar,  showcasing their steadfast devotion and faith in Bhagwan Swaminarayan, and serving as a powerful reminder to cultivate the same conviction and love in daily life. In some centers, these stories were presented as plays.
 A pothiyatra (procession of shastras) was also organized at all centers.

/News/2025/Matru-Devo-Bhava--A-Timeless-.t: Matru-Devo Bhava | A ‘Timeless Hindu Wisdom’ Seminar, Northampton, UK
/News/2025/Matru-Devo-Bhava--A-Timeless-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Matru-Devo Bhava, Northampton (36 photos)
 Following the successful ‘Timeless Hindu Wisdom’ seminar in October 2024 – ‘From Ayodhya to Abu Dhabi: A Journey of Global Harmony’ – more than 350 guests enjoyed another inspirational evening at the Mercure Hotel in Northampton on Sunday 30 March 2025. Coinciding with Mother’s Day, the title of the seminar was ‘Matru-Devo Bhava: Reverence and Responsibility for Mothers in Hinduism’.
 Guests were warmly welcomed with heartfelt greetings and refreshments before they proceeded into the banquet hall. The seminar formally commenced with Vedic prayers and the ceremonial lighting of the sacred lamp, symbolising the call for wisdom and spiritual illumination.
 The keynote address was delivered by Paramtattvadas Swami, a learned swami of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who expanded upon the deep spiritual and cultural roots of this ancient Vedic blessing, ‘Matru-Devo Bhava’ – ‘May your mother be a god unto you’ – and how it shapes values and traditions within Hindu society. 
 The seminar delved into the teachings that honour mothers as revered figures, highlighting their pivotal role in nurturing, guiding, and sustaining families and communities – and what we can all learn from them. 
 Attendees had the opportunity to celebrate mothers and the timeless Hindu wisdom behind motherhood, maternal love, and the sacred bond between mother and child.
 A parallel interactive session led by Saumyavadandas Swami was organised for children aged 5 to 13, titled ‘Lessons from the Ramayan’. With the help of games and engaging activities, the children learned about family values, respect, and harmony at home in a fun, meaningful way.
 The event concluded with an authentic Indian vegetarian meal.
 Jaynita Patel, one of the delegates at the seminar, shared, “What a wonderful, heartfelt tribute to mothers everywhere! The presentation was captivating and thought-provoking, and really made us reflect on how we need to celebrate mothers and their sacrifices, their selfless love, their care and nourishment, and also our responsibility to the world as ‘influencers’ and first teachers to our children.”
 Dhaval Gosaliya, a leading member of the Hindu community in Northampton, added, “Thank you to BAPS for organising this deeply meaningful and relevant event. We need more of these topics and seminars that help us understand our Sanatan Hindu culture better. As was eloquently explained, we all need to learn from ideal mothers to become better citizens of the world.”

 Medical Spiritual Symposium (29 photos)
 Doctors from some of Mumbai’s renowned and leading super-specialty hospitals attended the Medico-Spiritual Symposium on the theme ‘Healing the Healers’ at the BAPS Mandir in Dadar, Mumbai.
 The program commenced with darshan, abhishek, Vedic prayers, and an introductory video on Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In the panel discussion, India’s renowned cardiologist Padma Bhushan Dr. Ashwin Mehta, eminent heart surgeon Dr. Sudhanshu Bhattacharya and distinguished ENT surgeon Dr. Kanti Patel shared their experiences and offered thoughtful insights on the importance of mental health among doctors and how it can be preserved.
 Following this, Gnanvatsal Swami provided experiential guidance on how doctors can maintain mental stability and positivity while fulfilling their personal, social, and family responsibilities.
 On this occasion, officials from the State Blood Transfusion Council (SBTC), on behalf of the Maharashtra State Health Department and the Honorable Health Minister, presented a letter of appreciation to BAPS for collecting more than 12 lakh cc of blood during the blood donation camp held on the occasion of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s 92nd birth anniversary in September.

/News/2025/Message-of-Condolences-and-Pr.t: Message of Condolences and Prayers from HH Mahant Swami Maharaj on the Passing of HH Pope Francis, Surat, India
/News/2025/Message-of-Condolences-and-Pr.text:
Photo Gallery 
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj has sent a letter of condolences and prayers to the Catholic community following the passing of His Holiness Pope Francis today. It reads:
 Dear Members of the Roman Catholic Church,
 On behalf of the worldwide BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu fellowship, we extend our deepest condolences on the passing of His Holiness Pope Francis. His departure is a profound loss to the Catholic community and Christians around the world.
 Pope Francis will be remembered as a beacon of hope, compassion, and unity. His efforts to promote social justice, environmental stewardship, and peace-building have left an indelible mark. His commitment to the marginalized and his call for global solidarity resonated deeply with the values we hold dear in our own tradition.
 We commend his endeavours to build bridges between different faiths, including his promotion of respect for the Hindu community and other religious traditions.
 In this time of mourning, we stand in solidarity with you. We share in your sorrow and pray to God and all the divine energies that you find comfort in the legacy of simplicity and compassion that Pope Francis strove to promote.
 May his vision of a more just and harmonious world continue to inspire us all.
 With heartfelt prayers,
 Sadhu Keshavjivandas
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj
 Spiritual Leader, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha

/News/2025/Message-of-Condolences-and-Pr.t: Message of Condolences and Prayers on the Passing of President Russell M Nelson from HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, Jodhpur, India
/News/2025/Message-of-Condolences-and-Pr.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Message of Condolences and Prayers (1 photos)
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj has sent a letter of condolences and prayers to the Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints following the passing of President Russell M Nelson. It reads:
 Dear Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints,
 On behalf of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and our worldwide fellowship, we offer our deepest condolences on the passing of President Russell M. Nelson at the age of 101. His departure is a profound loss to your faith, community and to all who were touched by his remarkable life of service. I offer prayers of peace and comfort to his beloved family and to the global membership of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
 President Nelson will be remembered as a devoted spiritual leader, a compassionate healer, and a steadfast guide to millions. His lifelong commitment to faith, moral living, and service to humanity resonates deeply. His example as both a distinguished surgeon and a spiritual shepherd stands as a powerful testament to humility, wisdom, and dedication to God.
 Over the years, BAPS and the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints have cherished a warm relationship, built upon mutual respect, shared values, and a common commitment to faith, family, and service. This bond of friendship between our communities continues to inspire harmony and understanding in a world that deeply needs both.
 At this difficult time of mourning, we stand in solidarity with you all. May the blessings of God sustain you and may the memory of President Nelson be a guiding light to future generations.
 With heartfelt prayers and respect,
 Jai Swaminarayan from Sadhu Keshavjivandas
 (His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Spiritual Head, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha)

 Two days of vibrant and spiritually enriching celebrations marked the grand inauguration of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Sunshine Coast, Queensland.
 The festivities commenced on the afternoon of 26 January with a traditional nagar yatra (grand procession) in which devotees and local residents honored the sacred murtis to be enshrined in the new mandir. Among the dignitaries present were Councillor Joe Natoli (Division 4, Sunshine Coast) and esteemed officers from the Queensland Police Service (QPS), including Chief Inspector Jason Overland and PLO Vernon Corporal.
 In the evening, youths and devotees sang melodious bhajans during a captivating kirtan aradhana.
 On the morning of 27 January, the Vedic murti-pratishtha rituals were performed by BAPS swamis to consecrate the deities within the mandir. 
 Present on this historic occasion were Hon. Fiona Simpson (State Multicultural Minister), Mr. Andrew Wallace (Federal MP for Fisher), Ms. Kendall Morton (State MP for Caloundra), Mayor Rosanna Natoli (Sunshine Coast) and other dignitaries.

 A glorious chapter was added to the religious and cultural history of Jodhpur as the grand new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir was inaugurated with divine splendor and devotion by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 At 6:45 a.m., Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami, Pujya Viveksagar Swami and Pujya Ghanshyamcharan Swami performed the preliminary murti-pratishtha mahapuja rituals in the presence of a large congregation of devotees, and also offered prayers for peace, harmony, and prosperity for Rajasthan, India and the entire world.
 Thereafter, Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the main Vedic murti-pratishtha rituals in the central shrine.
 The murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami (central shrine); Bhagwan Krishna and Shri Radhaji (left shrine); Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj (right shrine); Bhagwan Shankar, Shri Parvatiji and Shri Ganapatiji; Bhagwan Ram, Shri Sitaji and Shri Hanumanji; and Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj and the Guru Parampara (ground floor) were ritually consecrated in the newly constructed mandir. Mahant Swami Maharaj then performed pujan and the first arti of the deities, filling the atmosphere with divine energy and overwhelming devotion.
 In his blessings following the consecration rituals, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, “This mandir is now open to all devotees and well-wishers. Come, have darshan of Bhagwan, chant his holy name, perform pradakshina, and offer prostrations. Bhagwan manifests here in his divine form. May every citizen of Jodhpur and the entire world be blessed with peace, happiness, and prosperity.”
 The mandir opening drew a large gathering of devotees eager for the first darshan of the deities.

/News/2025/Murti-Pratishtha-Mahotsav-of-.t: Murti-Pratishtha Mahotsav of BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir & Cultural Precinct, Sydney, Australia
/News/2025/Murti-Pratishtha-Mahotsav-of-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shri Swaminarayan Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna (69 photos)
 Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Murti-Pratishtha (105 photos)
 Nagar Yatra (98 photos)
 Women's Day Cultural Program (42 photos)
 Murti Abhishek (14 photos)
 Murti-Pratishtha (120 photos)
 Murtis (10 photos)
 Eleven days of celebrations marked the inauguration of the new 25-acre BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir and Cultural Precinct in Sydney, in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 On the morning on 5 March, a Vedic Shri Swaminarayan Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna was organized for world peace and the well-being of society. Mahant Swami Maharaj commenced the yagna by lighting the auspicious ritual flame. Sanctified grains were offered in the ritual flame while over 330 children from Australia and New Zealand recited the 315 Sanskrit verses of the Satsang Diksha shastra. New South Wales Legislative Assembly Member for Leppington Mr. Nathan Hagarty was present for the ceremony.
 On 6 March, senior swamis performed the Vedic murti-pratishtha mahapuja for Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni. Thereafter, the murti-consecration ceremony was performed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.  Hon. Chris Bowen, Minister for Climate Change and Energy; Hon. Michelle Rowland, Minister for Communications; and Ms. Karen McKeown, NSW Member for Penrith were present for the ceremony.
 On 7 March, a colorful nagar yatra (grand procession) took place around the cultural precinct campus. The sacred murtis to be installed in the mandir were honored on beautifully decorated floats. Mark Speakman, Leader of the NSW Opposition; Mark Coure, NSW Shadow Minister for Multiculturalism; and Jordan Lane, Shadow Assistant Minister for Multiculturalism were present to take part in this joyous procession.
 On 9 March, a special Women’s Day Cultural Program themed ‘Yeh Mandir Mera’ highlighted the inspirational sacrifices by women that made the mandir possible. It featured cultural performances and inspiring speeches by young and senior women.
 On 15 March, prior to their placement in the shrine of the mandir, Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the pujan of the murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and then offered abhishek to the murtis with sanctified water from the River Ghela in Gadhada.
 On 16 March, Pujya Viveksagar Swami performed the Vedic murti-pratishtha mahapuja. Thereafter, Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the murti-pratishtha rituals in the presence of devotees from across the Pacific region and other countries. Dr. Andrew Charlton, Member for Parramatta, and Dr. S. Janakiraman, Consul General of India in Sydney, were present during this auspicious occasion and expressed their gratitude for this precinct in this part of the nation.

/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Named-Communit.t: Neasden Temple Named Community Partner in British Museum Exhibition on Ancient Indian Sacred Art, London, UK
/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Named-Communit.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Ancient India: living traditions (15 photos)
 The British Museum has opened a major new exhibition, titled Ancient India: living traditions, exploring the origins and evolution of Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist sacred art dating back over 2,000 years. 
 As one of the world’s most prestigious cultural institutions, the British Museum houses one of the largest permanent collections of artworks and artefacts globally, with more than eight million objects. In 2024, it was officially recognised as the most-visited attraction in the UK for the second consecutive year, welcoming over 6.4 million visitors through its doors.
 In curating this exhibition, the British Museum collaborated closely with an advisory panel comprising practising Hindus, Jains, and Buddhists, as well as cultural experts, academics, and a diverse group of community partners. Among these consultants was BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as Neasden Temple. Neasden Temple and the British Museum share a longstanding relationship, having previously collaborated on the Museum’s Celebrating Diwali event in 2022 and an interfaith music festival in 2018. 
 As part of the development of Ancient India: living traditions, curators, designers, and planners from the British Museum visited Neasden Temple on several occasions. These visits fostered meaningful dialogue on devotional practice, sacred iconography, and the respectful display of living religious traditions. The insights shared during these discussions helped inspire various elements of the exhibition and its design. 
 The exhibition was officially inaugurated on Sunday 19 May with a community event hosted in the Museum’s iconic Great Court, bringing together senior leaders, interfaith representatives, academics, trustees, journalists, and cultural partners from across the UK. Reflecting the living spirit of the exhibition, the evening opened with sacred chants offered by representatives of Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions. Kirtan Patel from BAPS chanted Sanskrit verses from Hindu scriptures such as the Upanishads and offered prayers composed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, invoking peace, harmony, and universal well-being. The evening was presided over by the Chair of the British Museum’s Trustees, Rt Hon George Osborne CH, who emphasised the exhibition’s significance and the collaborative spirit in which it was created.
 Featuring more than 180 objects, including sculptures, paintings, and devotional artefacts, the exhibition offers a compelling, multi-sensory journey through the sacred art of ancient India. It highlights not only the enduring aesthetic legacy of Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism, but also their continuing relevance in Britain’s diverse religious and cultural landscape.
 Sushma Jansari, the exhibition’s curator, reflected on the unique continuity and influence of these living traditions: “We have been fortunate to work with a number of different community partners, one of them is of course Neasden Temple, and we were so lucky to have been welcomed to this beautiful space. We came with our designers, the lighting designer, the graphic designer, at the very start of this project, thinking about what a sacred space looks like and feels like. How does it impact how you venerate and how you feel inside a sacred space? And when you come to the exhibition, you see vibrant colours, beautiful lighting, lots of textures as well, and it really enhances how you experience the exhibition and look at the devotional sculptures on display. I think what’s really very special is that these are living traditions and when you go to places like Neasden Temple, and you go into the mandir, you will see these incredible figures of God being venerated and you’ll see them being dressed, you’ll see them being garlanded with fresh flowers – and if you think about the ancient past, that’s pretty much exactly what people would have done to the incredible ancient sculptures on display in the exhibition.”
 Kamlesh Patel, a volunteer from Neasden Temple who contributed to the consultation process, shared, “It was a privilege to support the British Museum in shaping this important exhibition. To see Hindu, Jain and Buddhist sacred art presented not as relics of the past but as part of living, breathing traditions is deeply meaningful. We are delighted to have contributed to a project that celebrates the continuing relevance of these traditions in the UK and around the world, and to be a part of this landmark exhibition, which brings the sacred art of India into dialogue with contemporary expressions of faith and devotion.”
 To learn more about the Ancient India: living traditions exhibition at the British Museum, please click here.

/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Participates-i.t: Neasden Temple Participates in Open House Festival, London, UK
/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Participates-i.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Open House London (40 photos)
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as Neasden Temple – once again participated in the Open House Festival, marking its 30th consecutive annual involvement, over the weekend of 20-21 September 2025.
 The annual festival, organised by Open City, celebrates London’s rich architectural heritage by offering free access to hundreds of landmark buildings across the capital. This year, the Open House Festival ran from 13 to 21 September across all 33 London boroughs, reaffirming the unique role that architecture and community spaces play in shaping the cultural and social life of the capital.
 Open City is London’s leading architecture education organisation and the founder of the global Open House Worldwide network, which now spans over 50 cities around the world, from New York to Lagos and Buenos Aires to Taipei. Its mission is to make architecture and urban design accessible to all, fostering greater understanding of the built environment and the communities it serves.
 Visitors to the Mandir were able to experience its intricate architecture and spiritual ambience through guided tours, exhibitions, and moments of quiet reflection. This year, young children of the congregation also participated by sharing simple explanations of the Mandir’s traditions and practices. Their enthusiasm and sincerity made a lasting impression on many guests, who remarked how much they valued hearing directly from the younger generation and how it brought their visit to life.
 Guests appreciated not only the craftsmanship and artistry of the Mandir, but also the opportunity to learn more about Hindu beliefs and values in an open and welcoming environment, including a tour of the ‘Understanding Hinduism’ exhibition. There were also plenty of opportunities for visitors to witness one of the arti ceremonies during the day.
 Many spoke warmly of the peace and serenity they experienced inside the sanctum as well as the personal warmth of the volunteer guides who accompanied them.
 Amish Raghwani, a volunteer at the Mandir, shared, “The Open House weekend is always special because it allows us to share the Mandir’s beauty and meaning with so many people. It was wonderful to see families, neighbours and people from all walks of life come together here. That sense of openness and harmony is exactly what Mahant Swami Maharaj inspires us to cultivate.”
 Raksha Jethwa, a young guide, added, “I really enjoyed explaining what the Mandir means to us and answering people’s questions about Hinduism. It felt nice to see how interested they were and how much they appreciated hearing from us directly. I learned a lot, too. It made me feel proud to be part of the Mandir and a British Hindu.”
 A selection of visitor experiences is provided below:
 “Incredibly beautiful building and wonderfully helpful guides – one of the best Open House destinations of all! Simply amazing!” – BR, Software Engineer
 “Such an amazing spiritual experience. I loved finding out more about the Hindu faith. I was also so impressed with the knowledge and presentation of the young volunteers. Thank you.” – CB, Communications Executive
 “Very beautiful architecture and craftmanship. Very kind guides. Guides very knowledgeable including young children.” – FS, Doctor
 “Fantastic talking to so many young people – it felt very welcoming, and the temple is inspiring.  Thank you.” – SE, Consultant
 “Really enjoyed our visit and would highly recommend.” – MM, IT Engineer
 The Open House weekend was a great success, providing visitors with a unique opportunity to gain insights into the Mandir’s architecture, spiritual traditions, and community life. Many guests left with a deeper appreciation of its role as a centre of faith, learning, and service.
 The Mandir remains open to visitors free of charge throughout the year, welcoming people of all ages and backgrounds to experience its peace, beauty, and spiritual atmosphere.

/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Receives-Tripa.t: Neasden Temple Receives Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award for 2025, London, UK
/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Receives-Tripa.text:
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – has once again been honoured with the prestigious Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award.
 Tripadvisor, the world’s largest travel guidance platform, hosts more than 1 billion reviews and opinions covering millions of attractions, restaurants, and places of interest. Each month, more than 450 million travellers turn to Tripadvisor to help plan their journeys.
 The Travellers’ Choice Award for 2025 places the Mandir amongst the top 10% ‘things to do’ in the world from more than 8.7 million attractions, experiences, hotels, restaurants, and other places covered on its listing.
 The winners of the award are determined by the quality and consistency of reviews and ratings shared by visitors over the past 12 months. As explained by Tripadvisor, the award means that the Mandir has received “consistently great reviews” and is among places that “consistently demonstrate a commitment to hospitality excellence.”
 Shivani Patel, a leading BAPS volunteer, said, “We feel humbled that so many people have taken the time to share their experiences of the Mandir. For us as volunteers, the joy comes from seeing families and visitors of all backgrounds appreciating not just the beauty of the building, but also the values it represents – peace, devotion, service, and community. It is heartening to know that what His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj envisioned when creating the Mandir continues to resonate with people from around the world.”
 Niraj Rao, another leading volunteer at the Mandir, added, “His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj always reminds us that true spirituality is expressed through service. Every visitor who walks through these doors is welcomed with that spirit of humility and warmth. This award is really a reflection of their experiences – moments of peace, inspiration, and connection – which they’ve kindly chosen to share.”
 All the latest news and information about Neasden Temple can be found on its various social media accounts: X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and Telegram

/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Summer-Fair-28.t: Neasden Temple Summer Fair, London, UK
/News/2025/Neasden-Temple-Summer-Fair-28.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Neasden Temple Summer Fair (40 photos)
 Neasden Temple’s annual summer fair welcomed thousands of visitors over the long weekend of 11 to 13 July 2025, bringing together individuals and families from across the community for three vibrant days of culture, cuisine, and celebration. 
 The joyous community event was a part of the 30th anniversary celebrations of the iconic Hindu mandir, since its inauguration in 1995 by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 The festivities commenced on the evening of Friday 11 July with an uplifting programme of devotional singing by swamis and youths that provided a peaceful, spiritual tone for the weekend ahead.
 The fair was officially inaugurated on Saturday 12 July by Captain Simon Cheadle, Director of Flight Operations at British Airways. He was warmly welcomed by volunteers and guests and commended the Mandir’s efforts in hosting such an inclusive and joyful event that celebrates diversity and community spirit.
 Throughout the day, visitors explored more than 30 different market stalls representing local businesses and community organisations. Offerings ranged from artisan crafts and home décor to clothing, financial services, and travel – all reflecting the creativity and enterprise of the wider community.
 The much-anticipated food court remained a highlight of the event, captivating visitors with a vibrant and varied culinary experience. A fusion of traditional delights and contemporary flavours created an irresistible atmosphere, where familiar tastes met creative new offerings. With something to satisfy every palate – whether savoury, sweet, or refreshing – the food court brought people together through its rich variety and warm, welcoming aromas.
 Live performances on the cultural stage continued throughout both days, offering an engaging programme of music, dance and wellness activities. From energetic drumming and classical dance to soulful bhajans, yoga, and more, the stage entertained and inspired guests of all ages. Saturday concluded with an evening of music, rhythm, and soul as the acclaimed Alap Desai captivated hearts with a fusion of classical melodies and contemporary compositions.
 Families and children also enjoyed a lively funfair with rides, including bumper cars, rollercoasters, trampolines, and carousels. Face painting, henna art, and traditional games added to the festive atmosphere, while the Health Hub promoted well-being with smoothie-making bikes and nutritious snacks. A second-hand clothes stall proved especially popular, selling out completely and reflecting the community’s strong commitment to sustainable living.
 A particular highlight for many young visitors was the British Airways A350 flight simulator, which offered an immersive and educational experience into aviation. Aspiring pilots and enthusiasts had the opportunity to step into the cockpit and learn more about careers in the skies.
 The Paris Mandir Gift Shop also attracted many visitors, with new merchandise and unique souvenirs allowing guests to take home special mementoes from the weekend.
 Reflecting on the event, lead volunteer Randhir Patel shared, “The Summer Fair is always a highlight of our calendar, and this year was no exception. The spirit of togetherness, the dedication of our volunteers, and the generosity of all our supporters made it another memorable day for the whole community. Our heartfelt thanks goes to everyone – all the volunteers, stall-holders, performers, guests, and supporters – whose selfless contributions and wholehearted participation helped make the Summer Fair 2025 another remarkable success.”

/News/2025/New-Years-Family-Mahapuja-UK-.t: New Year’s Family Mahapuja, UK & Europe, London, UK
/News/2025/New-Years-Family-Mahapuja-UK-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 New Year’s Family Mahapuja, London, UK (48 photos)
 Hundreds of families from across the UK and Europe participated in a special mahapuja on Monday 1 January 2025 – joining together to pray for global peace, family unity, and a prosperous year ahead.
 Families, including worshippers and community members gathered at London Mandir for two sessions, one in the morning and another in the afternoon. Many others participated online through a live webcast from their homes, taking the opportunity to adorn their ghar mandirs, prepare sweet treats as a family, and make various devotional offerings to the murtis.
 The sacred ceremony was led by resident swamis of London Mandir, with support from youths, in the presence of Pujya Gnaneshwardas Swami, a senior BAPS swami visiting from India. As the swamis chanted Vedic mantras to invoke the divine presence of God, they shared insights to help enhance the participants’ understanding and enjoyment of the deeply meaningful ceremony.
 This event allowed families to welcome the new year with a collective spirit of faith and optimism. Meera Patel, who attended the prayers with her family, expressed, “What a meaningful way to step into the new year! The atmosphere in the Mandir was truly serene and uplifting. It was heartwarming to see everyone united in prayer for those in need. My two young girls were fully engrossed and even took a moment to offer their own prayers for those who are struggling.”
 Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK and Europe, shared, “The arrival of the new year instils a fresh sense of faith and optimism. His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj encourages us to foster kindness, unity, and positivity. It was uplifting to witness so many individuals starting the year with prayers for others. We also hope that the blessings and spiritual energy from this mahapuja will continue to echo throughout 2025 and beyond, leaving a lasting impression on our global community.”

/News/2025/New-Zealand-Prime-Minister-Ce.t: New Zealand Prime Minister Celebrates Diwali and Hindu New Year at BAPS Mandir, Wellington, New Zealand
/News/2025/New-Zealand-Prime-Minister-Ce.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Annakut Celebrations (21 photos)
 Hundreds of devotees and community members gathered at the newly opened BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Lower Hutt to celebrate Diwali and the Hindu New Year in the presence of the Prime Minister of New Zealand, The Right Honourable Christopher Luxon.
 Mr. Luxon personally added the final preparatory touches to a bowl of shiro, before placing it in the colorful annakut display of over 900 vegetarian food delicacies offered to the deities. Thereafter, he performed the arti.
 During his time at the mandir, the prime minister spoke with community members, young and old, listening to their stories and sharing in their joy on this auspicious day.
 Addressing the assembly, he said, "Today, we are celebrating the central idea of Diwali which is that light will always triumph over darkness, knowledge over ignorance, and hope over hopelessness.
 “You have enriched our country tremendously – economically, socially and culturally. We wouldn’t be the New Zealand that we are today without your strong, vibrant contributions.
 “Thank you for caring about your community and continuing to impart the teachings to the next generation of young people coming through.”
 The prime minister reflected on his previous engagements with BAPS, including meeting Kiwi volunteers during his March 2025 visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, and his 2023 visit to the BAPS Mandir in Auckland.
 In a special gesture, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj wrote a personal letter to the prime minister, offering prayers for peace, prosperity, and unity amongst all New Zealanders. The letter was presented during the celebration.
 Accompanying the prime minister were Ministers Hon. Chris Bishop and Hon. Louise Upston, along with MPs Nancy Lu, Carlos Cheung, Rima Nakhle, and Tim Costley, and other parliamentary colleagues.

/News/2025/New-Zealand-Prime-Minister-Ch.t: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, Strengthening India-NZ Cultural Ties, New Delhi, India
/News/2025/New-Zealand-Prime-Minister-Ch.text:
Photo Gallery 
 PM of New Zealand, Visits Akshardham (39 photos)
 The Rt Hon Christopher Luxon, Prime Minister of New Zealand, visited BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, with a 110-member delegation, including senior government officials, ministers, business leaders, and community representatives from New Zealand.
 Prime Minister Luxon and his delegation received a traditional welcome before exploring the intricately carved mandir, which embodies India’s rich heritage, devotion, and values. As a mark of respect, Prime Minister Luxon offered flower petals at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and participated in the abhishek ceremony.
 View this post on Instagram
 A post shared by Christopher Luxon (@christopherluxon)
 Accompanying the Prime Minister were Minister for Trade Todd McClay, Minister for Ethnic Communities Mark Mitchell, and Minister for Tourism Louise Upston. Also present were Members of Parliament Andy Foster, Carlos Cheung, Dr. Parmjeet Parmar, and Priyanca Radhakrishnan, along with New Zealand High Commissioner H.E. Patrick Rata. The business delegation included top executives from leading New Zealand firms, further strengthening economic and trade relations between the two nations.
 In a special moment, the Prime Minister was presented an inaugural Maori language copy of the Satsang Diksha, a sacred Hindu scripture written by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, currently in Sydney, Australia, conveyed a heartfelt message to Prime Minister Luxon in a personal letter:
 "Your presence at Akshardham and the time you devoted to this visit reflect your respect for cultural and spiritual values. Akshardham stands as a symbol of faith, unity, and service to society, and your visit has further strengthened the message of harmony and goodwill."
 Swamishri also expressed gratitude for the prime minister’s support to the Indian community in New Zealand, acknowledging his efforts to foster an inclusive and peaceful society that continues to strengthen the bonds of friendship between New Zealand and India.
 Furthermore, special prayers were offered for Prime Minister Luxon’s leadership, the well-being of his family, and the peace and prosperity of New Zealand.
 Shared Experiences
 Reflecting on his experience, Prime Minister Luxon shared:
 "It's incredibly special to be here at Akshardham. To see this magnificent temple and the amazing work that has been done is truly inspiring. It has been a great honour to bring our business and community delegation from New Zealand to witness what has been achieved here. I just want to say a big shout out to all the BAPS community back home in New Zealand. I remember visiting Auckland in 2023, and it's been fantastic to see the continued growth of the faith in New Zealand and actually see the opening of a new temple in Wellington. It's really, really special."
 He was particularly moved by the serene atmosphere and spiritual depth of Swaminarayan Akshardham. He expressed his sentiments in the guest book: "It was a great privilege to pay my respects at the beautiful and inspiring Akshardham Temple and to be hosted so warmly by the temple authorities. Thank you for a wonderful place of peace and learning."
 On social media, he further acknowledged the temple’s significance for the Indian community in New Zealand:
 "The Hindu community in New Zealand has made a large contribution to our country. Today in Delhi, I paid my respects at a place sacred to many Kiwi-Indians – the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple."
 pic.twitter.com/SW1UcxfLDi
 — Christopher Luxon (@chrisluxonmp) March 18, 2025
 Acknowledging the Indian Community's Contribution in New Zealand
 Prime Minister Luxon also took a moment to acknowledge the contributions of the Indian community in New Zealand, saying, "We admire you so much. The contributions you have made to New Zealand are incredibly rich on so many different levels—culturally, socially, and economically. You have made New Zealand a better and richer place."
 BAPS in New Zealand
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha has served the Hindu community in New Zealand for decades, fostering faith, culture, and service through centres in Auckland, Hamilton, Rotorua, Christchurch, and the soon-to-open Wellington.
 Alongside spiritual and youth programs, BAPS Charities supports local communities through food drives, environmental efforts, health campaigns, and disaster relief. Committed to unity and service, BAPS continues to strengthen cultural ties and social well-being across New Zealand.

/News/2025/Niranjan-Peethadheeshwar-Swam.t: Niranjan Peethadheeshwar Swami Kailashanand Giri Ji Maharaj Visits BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Niranjan-Peethadheeshwar-Swam.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Niranjan Peethadheeshwar Swami Kailashanand Giri Ji Maharaj Visits BAPS Hindu Mandir (27 photos)
 Swami Kailashanand Giri ji Maharaj, Neeranjan Peethadheeshwar Shree Shree 1008 Acharya Mahamandaleshwar, visited the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi. He was welcomed with traditional honor by Swami Brahmviharidas and sadhus at the mandir.
 During his visit, Swamiji toured the mandir complex and observed its divine architecture, intricate carvings, and peaceful spiritual atmosphere. He was deeply moved by the devotion, discipline, and dedication with which the mandir had been created. Swamiji offered his respects at the sanctum sanctorum and appreciated the mandir as a vibrant symbol of Sanatan Dharma outside India.
 Swamiji reflected on the mandir's role in sharing Indian culture, values, and spirituality with the world. He praised the vision and blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj. He appreciated the continued immense support and active contribution of the UAE leadership to the mandir.
 He called upon people from all faiths and countries, whether they believe in Sanatan Dharma or not, to visit this mandir to witness what strong conviction backed by divinity can build.
 Swamiji also participated in the abhishek ritual and joined devotees and visitors in the Ganga Arti.
 Sharing his joy, Swamiji expressed that the mandir stands as a testament to faith and unity. Beyond being a source of pride for Sanatan Dharma, the mandir also reflects the spirit of global peace and harmony, a message that will inspire countless hearts across the world and serve as a symbol of respect and pride for the leadership and people of the UAE.

/News/2025/PM-Mark-Carney-Visits-BAPS-To.t: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney Visits BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2025/PM-Mark-Carney-Visits-BAPS-To.text:
The Right Honourable Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada, visited the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto on April 5, 2025, on the auspicious occasion of the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram.
 Upon his arrival, Prime Minister Carney was warmly received by the Board of Directors of BAPS Canada and welcomed in a traditional Hindu manner in the Abhishek Mandapam. Pujya Gunsagardas Swami, the Head Swami of BAPS activities in Canada, honoured the Prime Minister with a rose garland. Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami, a senior BAPS swami, tied the nada-chhadi (sacred thread symbolising goodwill) on his wrist.
 Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, the Head Swami of BAPS activities in North America, then performed the auspicious abhishek ritual of Nilkanth Varni Maharaj alongside the Prime Minister, offering prayers for peace and well-being across Canada and around the world.
 The Prime Minister then proceeded to the Mandir, where he admired the architecture and intricate carvings, taking a deep interest in the spiritual and cultural significance of this sacred place. He joined the swamis in performing the arti and offered flowers and a basket of fruits to the murtis in the central shrine.
 Prime Minister Carney was then presented with a special edition of the Satsang Diksha, a spiritual scripture authored by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. This unique edition was written in Sanskrit, Gujarati, English, and French.
 A special letter of blessings for the Prime Minister, sent from India by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, was then read aloud in his presence. The Prime Minister was touched by the heartfelt message. Mahant Swami Maharaj wrote: “It is a pleasure and joy to welcome you today to the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto, Canada. Your visit is deeply appreciated, and prayers have been offered to Bhagwan Swaminarayan for your continued strength and clarity as you lead the nation of Canada with wisdom, strength, and integrity… Prayers have also been offered for Canada’s continued success and for the well-being of its citizens.”
 Before his departure, the Prime Minister took a few moments to write a message in the guest book: “With the deepest appreciation for your prayers and hospitality, and with all my conviction to work without fail to promote peace, unity, harmony, and prosperity for Canada, India, and all nations.”
 He also spent time interacting with community members and Hindu leaders, marking a warm and meaningful conclusion to his visit.

/News/2025/Parasmani-Discover-Believe-Ex.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day 1: Arrival & Registration (10 photos)
 Day 2: Discover (20 photos)
 Day 3: Believe (20 photos)
 Day 4: Experience (20 photos)
 Yuvati Mandal Session (10 photos)
 Shibir Experience Exhibition (20 photos)
 From Thursday 14 August to Sunday 17 August 2025, around 850 yuvaks and yuvatis from around the UK and parts of Europe gathered at Warwick Conference Park for their annual satsang shibir, themed “Parasmani: Discover, Believe, Experience.” 
 The shibir took place in the presence of visiting swamis from North America and India – Gnanpriyadas Swami, Pujya Atmatruptdas Swami and Dharmasetudas Swami – as well as resident swamis of UK & Europe.
 Inspired by Mahant Swami Maharaj’s Diwali ashirwad, the shibir guided participants to move from understanding prapti (what we have attained) to cultivating pratiti (unshakeable conviction). 
 The title ‘Parasmani’, the philosopher’s stone that turns iron into gold, symbolised that just as iron must touch it to become gold, we, too, must engage with our prapti to experience bliss.
 The four-day shibir began with games on Thursday night, building friendships and strengthening samp. From Friday, the shibir unfolded through the three themes.
 Day 2: Discover – Realising Our Prapti
 Participants explored the extraordinary prapti of Sarvopari Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the Aksharbrahma Guru, and the divine Satsang through presentations, podcasts, and insightful discussions. The day closed with a unique 20-sant panel, sharing light-hearted and heartfelt prasangs of the Satpurush.
 Day 3: Believe – Cultivating Conviction
 The day explored how to turn understanding into conviction. Sessions addressed barriers to faith, with topics such as ‘Terms and Conditions Apply: My Satsang Mentality’ and ‘Comfortably Lost: Beyond Checking Boxes.’ An interactive game, The Prapti Files, reinforced teamwork, with the day ending through an uplifting kirtan aradhana by Jaydeepbhai Swadia. 
 Day 4: Experience – Living Our Prapti, Becoming Gold
 The final day turned belief into transformation through the fulfilment (krutarthpanu) of living with pratiti, highlighting three outcomes: understanding the virtues of the Satpurush, becoming Akshardham within, and experiencing inner peace.
 Through sankirtans and real-life stories, participants were inspired to embody their prapti daily. 
 The shibir concluded with Mahant Swami Maharaj’s ashirwad, “The Satpurush is your Parasmani.” Participants left with a renewed purpose to not only know prapti, but live, believe, and experience its bliss daily.
 The Experience Exhibition
 A creative exhibition distilled the theme through features such as the Prapti Tree, reflective scales showing ‘Prapti>Problems,’ and interactive boards and props. Attendees praised it as “brilliantly creative.”
 Transformative Impact
 Classroom-style sessions by Atmatruptdas Swami and Dharmasetudas Swami “simplified complex concepts into easy-to-understand frameworks,” noted one participant.
 The shibir was described as life-changing: “This shibir has changed the way I think, talk, and act. I now understand Satsang far, far better.” Others praised it as “flawless,” “the best shibir I’ve ever been to,” and simply “an experience of a lifetime!”
