/News/2025/Parasmani-Realising-Our-Supre.t: Parasmani: Realising Our Supreme Attainment | Sanyukta Mandal Shibir 2025, UK & Europe
/News/2025/Parasmani-Realising-Our-Supre.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Day 1: Our Glorious Prapti (20 photos)
 Day 2: The Manifest Parasmani (20 photos)
 Day 3: The Essence of the Satpurush (20 photos)
 Satsang Diksha Playgroup (20 photos)
 Over 22-24 August and 24-26 August 2025, more than 2,300 participants from Sanyukta Mandal across the UK and parts of Europe gathered at Warwick Conference Park for an inspiring and transformative shibir titled “Parasmani: Praptini Pratiti” – Conviction in Our Supreme Attainment.
 The shibir, graced by the presence of senior and learned swamis from India and the UK, was a deep dive into realising the unparalleled spiritual blessing of having attained Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit Satpurush.
 The central theme, ‘Parasmani,’ used the ancient metaphor of a divine touchstone that turns iron into gold. Atmatruptdas Swami, in his enlightening discourses and interactive presentations, explained that our prapti – Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the manifest Satpurush – is this very parasmani, which has the power to transform the ‘iron’ jiva into the ‘golden’ brahmarup state.
 The entire shibir was structured to guide participants on a journey from vichār (understanding) to vishwās (faith), and priti (love), culminating in pratiti (unwavering conviction).
 Dharmasetudas Swami and other learned swamis elaborated on the nature of the jiva, the obscuring influence of māyā, and the ingrained swabhāvs that act as ‘rust’ on the soul.
 Through innovative sessions deploying the use of a smartboard to help participants structure their thoughts and grasp complex topics, as well as compelling panel discussions and podcast-style conversations, the swamis presented many profound spiritual concepts in a uniquely engaging and relatable manner. The sessions emphasised that while our intellect and senses have limitations, unwavering faith in the Satpurush is the key that unlocks his transformative grace.
 The shibir was not just a spiritual retreat for the adults. In parallel, a vibrant and meticulously organised set-up facilitated the spiritual nurturing of the next generation. Over 300 children participated in dedicated Satsang Diksha playgroup camps, learning core Satsang principles through interactive stories, games, and activities. Furthermore, professionally managed crèche facilities ensured that even the youngest children were lovingly cared for, allowing parents to immerse themselves fully in the shibir sessions. This comprehensive arrangement truly made it a family event, reinforcing the legacy of Satsang for all ages.
 Each shibir culminated with a powerful call to action from Atmatruptdas Swami, inspiring all attendees to commit to a daily 15-minute practice of ‘praptino vichār’ – contemplating upon the greatness of our spiritual attainment.
 Participants departed with a renewed sense of purpose, a deeper understanding of their invaluable prapti, and a clear roadmap for achieving spiritual transformation and ultimate liberation through the grace of their Guru, Mahant Swami Maharaj.

 Peter Dutton Visits His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj (38 photos)
 Australia’s Leader of the Opposition, Hon. Peter Dutton, was warmly welcomed to the Maha Annakut festival at the recently opened BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir and Cultural Precinct in southwest Sydney.
 More than 1,000 pure vegetarian dishes were lovingly prepared, decoratively displayed, and offered to God by community members. The Annakut festival was held to celebrate the opening of phase one of the cultural precinct.
 During his visit, Mr Dutton interacted with various volunteers, from young children to senior adults, and also many members of Hindu community organizations and local leaders.
 A key moment of Mr Dutton’s visit was his personal meeting with His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who tied a sacred nadachhadi on his wrist, offering prayers for his and his family’s well-being.
 In his address, Mr Dutton expressed his admiration for the community’s devotion, saying, “Meditation is a big part of my life and religion is a part of my life. When I look out this morning and see those young boys and girls so proudly wearing their costumes and their religious beliefs on display, as a country we should express that more clearly and be proud of it.”
 The Maha Annakut festival reflected the importance of community and devotion.

Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Premier League (56 photos)
 Mahant Premier League (18 photos)
 The Pramukh Premier League (PPL) cricket tournament and the Mahant Premier League (MPL) volleyball tournament, both held in Melbourne, featured 15 teams and over 172 participants.
 In an atmosphere filled with enthusiasm, friendship, and positive competition, both tournaments were firmly rooted in the core BAPS values of Samp (Harmony), Suhradbhav (Fraternity), and Ekta (Unity). Participants travelled from major cities across Australia and New Zealand to take part. Healthy competition with discipline, humility, and mutual encouragement, reinforced the message that sport is a medium to build character, strengthen relationships, and cultivate respect for one another.
 This event enabled participants to learn spiritual and other values, such as teamwork, perseverance, humility in success, and grace in defeat to apply in their daily lives.

/News/2025/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Birthda.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Birthday Celebrations 2025, North America
/News/2025/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Birthda.text:
Devotees across North America came together to honor the birthday of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj through a special celebration themed “Satpurush: The Gateway to Moksha.” The program reflected on how Pramukh Swami Maharaj embodied the four pillars of ekantik dharma—dharma, gnan, vairagya, and bhakti—and how his legacy continues to guide and elevate seekers on the path toward moksha.
 Through musical performances, traditional dances, skits, and inspiring speeches, devotees of all ages offered heartfelt tributes highlighting Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s divine virtues. Each segment focused on one of the four pillars, illustrating how Pramukh Swami Maharaj not only mastered these principles but lived them effortlessly. Stories shared by devotees emphasized how his unwavering commitment to dharma upheld truth and righteousness, how his profound gnan provided clarity and spiritual strength, how his natural vairagya demonstrated detachment from worldly desires, and how his pure bhakti expressed complete devotion to God and Guru.
 These narratives reflected on Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life as a practical, living blueprint for spiritual growth. Children, youth, and adults alike found inspiration in the simplicity and depth of his daily actions—from his compassion and humility to his discipline and devotion. Performances beautifully portrayed how these virtues shaped his interactions, decisions, and teachings, leaving a lasting impact on all who crossed his path.
 Today, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj continues to carry forward this legacy, guiding devotees with the same principles of dharma, gnan, vairagya, and bhakti. Under his spiritual guidance, the values embodied by Pramukh Swami Maharaj continue to inspire and uplift generations, strengthening the journey toward moksha with every step.

/News/2025/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Jayanti.text:
The 104th birth anniversary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj was celebrated at mandirs and centres across the UK and Europe with an inspirational programme that delved deeper into his profound humility.
 Despite guiding a global spiritual fellowship, Pramukh Swami Maharaj consistently embodied the deep conviction that God alone is the doer. His life of selfless service, simplicity, equanimity, and unwavering faith stood as a living expression of these virtues, and was conveyed through enlightening cultural performances, insightful discourses, and impactful presentations.

/News/2025/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Jayanti.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Jayanti Mahila Celebrations 2025, UK & Europe
/News/2025/Pramukh-Swami-Maharaj-Jayanti.text:
Mahilas from across the UK and Europe gathered at BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs and centres to joyously celebrate the birth anniversary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj through a vibrant and devotional programme themed ‘Sarvopari Bhagwanna Sarvopari Sant’.
 Inspired by the blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj during his 2017 visit to London, the assembly reflected upon Pramukh Swami Maharaj as Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s Param Ekantik Sant (the perfectly faithful and spiritually complete guru), setting a tone of reverence, reflection, and spiritual joy.
 The programme unfolded through a thoughtful blend of presentations that explored three facets of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s unparalleled greatness. An interactive discourse provided a scriptural perspective on how his life exemplified the characteristics of a supreme sant as described in the Hindu scriptures. Complementing this were graceful cultural performances, insightful skits, and multimedia features that highlighted his lifelong dedication to nurturing mandirs, strengthening communities, and fostering values of faith, harmony, and righteous living.
 The celebration concluded with a heartfelt address that reflected on the profound and lasting impact Pramukh Swami Maharaj has had on innumerable lives. The assembly was reminded of his compassionate guidance, his spiritual leadership, and his ability to elevate individuals towards the highest ideals of spirituality. Filled with devotion, unity, and gratitude, the event honoured not only his birth anniversary but also the timeless legacy he continues to inspire in individuals, families, and communities worldwide through the blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2025/Pramukh-Swami-Maharajs-104th-.t: Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 104th Birthday Celebrations by the Women's Wing, North America
/News/2025/Pramukh-Swami-Maharajs-104th-.text:
Women devotees across North America gathered at BAPS Mandirs with devotion and unity to celebrate the birth anniversary of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, reflecting on his life through the lens of the qualities of Aksharbrahma described by Bhagwan Swaminarayan in the Vachanamrut. This year’s program, themed “Vande Pramukh Swaminam,” offered a heartfelt exploration of how these divine virtues manifested in Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life, as experienced and cherished by women devotees across generations.
 The first segment focused on Samdarshi Sant, highlighting how Pramukh Swami Maharaj truly embodied equanimity in every interaction and every moment of his life. His ability to see all with equal vision, beyond differences or distinctions, left a lasting impression on countless women who felt deeply understood, valued, and uplifted in his presence. The program also explored Samarth Thaka Jharna, reflecting on Swamishri’s extraordinary tolerance and humility. Despite being the guru, he consistently lived with profound modesty, accepting challenges with grace and teaching by example how true strength lies in humility.
 The celebration continued with reflections on Sarvottam Bhakta, emphasizing how devotion defined Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s every breath. His unwavering bhakti served as a guiding light for women devotees, inspiring them to cultivate devotion within their families, communities, and personal spiritual journeys.
 The final theme, Mokshapradata Sant, emphasized Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s role as a sant who grants liberation. Women shared how simply being in his association strengthened their faith, deepened their spiritual understanding, and illuminated the path toward moksha. Through devotional songs, traditional dances, thought-provoking skits, and inspiring speeches, women of all ages offered their heartfelt bhakti in honor of his divine legacy. The celebration encapsulated how Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s virtues continue to guide, protect, and inspire devotees, reaffirming the timeless truth that the Satpurush remains the gateway to spiritual liberation.

/News/2025/Pramukh-Varni-Amrut-Mahotsav-.t: Pramukh Varni Amrut Mahotsav, Ahmedabad, India
/News/2025/Pramukh-Varni-Amrut-Mahotsav-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Pramukh Varni Amrut Mahotsav (188 photos)
 The culmination of the much-anticipated Pramukh Varni Amrut Mahotsav, which had resonated throughout the past year, unfolded today in grand splendour at the Riverfront Event Center by the River Sabarmati in Ahmedabad. The event was celebrated from 5.30 to 8 p.m, portraying the selfless services of Pramukh Swami Maharaj through a series of breathtaking presentations.
 Celebration of an Extraordinary Life of Selfless Service
 The magnificent celebration honoured 75 years since Shastriji Maharaj, founder of BAPS, appointed Pramukh Swami Maharaj as President of BAPS at Ambli Vali Pol, Ahmedabad. The very day he was appointed as President in 1950, Pramukh Swami Maharaj washed utensils. This guiding ideal of seva remained the hallmark of his 95-year life.
 The celebration stage exquisitely reflected this historic journey. On one side, stood a beautifully crafted representation of Ambli Vali Pol — the sacred place where Pramukh Swami Maharaj was appointed President — and on the other side rose the iconic form of Akshardham in New Delhi, symbolizing the global spiritual footprint that blossomed through his vision and efforts. This artistic and spiritual setting framed the entire celebration, highlighting how a humble beginning in a small pol in Ahmedabad mushroomed into a worldwide spiritual organization. The impressive main stage also included the murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Guru Parampara.
 The assembly commenced with the singing of dhun followed by a kirtan, ‘Amrut Mahotsav aaje re Ambli Vali Pol ma…’ by youths.
 Senior BAPS swamis greeted the Home Minister of India Shri Amitbhai Shah, Hon. Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, and Hon. Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harshbhai Sanghavi on their arrival. Thereafter, the guests joined Mahant Swami Maharaj and Pujya Kothari Bhaktipriya Swami, Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami and Pujya Viveksagar Swami on the main stage.
 An exhilarating traditional dance, extolling the glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit gurus, ‘Divyam Sukhadam Parabrahma Swaminarayan, Gunātit Gurum Aksharam...’, was performed by children and youths. Another presentation portrayed an analogy between Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life and a flowing river – ‘Pramukhjini Sant Sarita Mahant Rupe Vaheti…’  – ‘What does a river do? The saintly river of Pramukhji now flows in the form of Mahant Swami.’
 The entire programme was weaved through a dialogue between a father, who lived in the time of Shastriji Maharaj, and his son speaking from the backdrop of Akshardham.
 Speeches on Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s Virtues
 Seva – Selfless Service
 A series of evocative videos highlighted touching incidents of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s lifelong dedication and service to humanity. A lyrical presentation and a video showcased BAPS’s global humanitarian services.
 Sadhu Aksharvatsaldas spoke, “A true Sant is like a flowing river, always giving. Pramukh Swami Maharaj served selflessly to millions of people. Service was a synonym for his life; a constant rhythm of his life. He served with profound humility.
 “The depth of his compassion was seen when, after reading the postal stamp on a postcard, he sent people to a remote village to ensure a hand pump was installed for an Adivasi person named Reshma Parghi. Mahant Swami Maharaj is the embodiment of this seva today.”
 Aham-Shunyata – Egolessness
 Through creative visual storytelling, the virtue of egolessness was illustrated with episodes of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life. Sadhu Brahmaviharidas shared reflections on how Pramukh Swami Maharaj remained free from ego despite receiving global admiration. He shared, “The vibrations of the milestone incident at Ambli Vali Pol (where he was appointed President) are still resonating throughout the world. Egolessness (Aham Shunyata) was the identity of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 “When a World Wide Studios interviewer asked him, during the inauguration of the London Mandir in 1995, ‘What role are you playing as the guru of millions?’ Pramukh Swami Maharaj replied, ‘God is the guru of millions. I serve according to his command.’
 “When asked to list his achievements, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, ‘Yogiji Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj perform this work, so how can I make a list?’ Pramukh Swami Maharaj attributed all his accomplishments to his gurus.
 “Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam once revealed to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, ‘You have removed ‘I’ and ‘mine’ from me.’“
 Shraddha – Faith
 A compelling video presentation depicted Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s unshakeable faith while steering the organization. In his discourse, Sadhu Anandswarupdas highlighted inspiring examples of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s unwavering trust in Bhagwan Swaminarayan and his gurus. He said, “Pramukh Swami Maharaj demonstrated an unwavering faith in his guru’s word by obeying his instruction to become a sant at the age of 18.
 “He fulfilled the sankalp of Yogiji Maharaj, who had resolved in 1968 to build a mandir in Delhi on the banks of River Yamuna. Despite the immense hurdles, he fulfilled the vow of his guru by completing the mandir in 2003 and the Akshardham complex in 2005.
 “In 1998, a renowned journalist Ron Patel asked him about his first thought when he regained consciousness after his heart bypass surgery. Pramukh Swami Maharaj replied, ‘God is constantly with me. I firmly believe everything happens according to God’s will.’ His greatest gift to the organization is Mahant Swami Maharaj, his spiritual successor.”
 Addresses by Dignitaries
 The Hon. Home Minister Shri Amitbhai Shah offered his heartfelt tributes to Pramukh Swami Maharaj and acknowledged his spiritual and social services to society. He elaborated, “It is impossible for me to fully describe the entire life, work, divine memories, and infinite virtues of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. I see today that the ‘Pramukh Varni Amrut Mahotsav’, organized by BAPS, is being held on the banks of River Sabarmati in an extremely serene environment, and it is a truly delightful experience.
 “By linking devotion and service, Pujya Pramukh Swami Maharaj revived our ancient tradition of compassion for every living being. As the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, I want to state with full confidence that Sanatan Dharma has faced many crises in its journey through the millennia. However, the greatest crisis after India’s independence was the decline in reverence for sants and sannyasis. The credit for restoring that reverence goes to Pramukh Swami Maharaj and the BAPS organization. He paved a beautiful and universally acceptable path that has now become an ideal for all sanyasis and sects of Sanatan Dharma.
 “The work he carried out from 1950 to 2016 has today become an inspiration for all sects across the country. While listening to the swamis, Ambli Vali Pol and Shahpur were repeatedly brought up. I am fully confident that after today’s program, Ambli Vali Pol will no longer remain limited to Gujarat or India, but will become an unforgettable pilgrimage site for the entire world.”
 A festive dance by BAPS youths followed, which culminated in a symbolic presentation of the Guruhari Jyot – torches carried by youths, beginning from Jabalpur, to commemorate Mahant Swami Maharaj’s birthday on 2 February in Vadodara.
 Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami revealed in his address the meaning and purpose of Pramukh Varni Amrut Mahotsav. He said, “Today, we have gathered here to celebrate Pramukh Varni Amrut Mahotsav. Shastriji Maharaj had envisioned that the philosophy of Akshar Purushottam should flourish for thousands of years. We had witnessed the extraordinary, unprecedented, and divine tasks of Pramukh Swami Maharaj to fulfil this vision. Despite his colossal accomplishments he never uttered or even thought, ‘I did all this’.
 “During and after the inauguration of Delhi Akshardham in 2005, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was profusely showered with praises for his accomplishment. When Dr Kalam praised, Swamishri replied, ‘I have done nothing.’ Dr Kalam responded, ‘Neelkanth (Bhagwan Swaminarayan), who resides in your heart, has done this.’
 “We offer our utmost reverences to Pramukh Swami Maharaj for bestowing us with the gift of Mahant Swami Maharaj. Now, we have only one task to do; to please Mahant Swami Maharaj by obeying his commands.”
 Shri Jagdish Vishwakarma, President of BJP, Gujarat State, offered his heartfelt tributes to Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s egoless personality and inspiring, divine life.
 The Honourable Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel expressed, “Pramukh Swami Maharaj remained tirelessly active through all the nine decades of his life, dedicating himself completely to God and society. Our culture stands on three fundamental pillars – sant, shastra, and mandirs. Pramukh Swami Maharaj strengthened all three through his extraordinary efforts and works. The land of Gujarat has been blessed with the divine presence and guidance of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Mahant Swami Maharaj, and many great sadhus. The Pramukh Varni Amrut Mahotsav is truly a celebration for all people.”
 Publications Launched
 The program featured the launch of three Gujarati print publications at the holy hands of Mahant Swami Maharaj:
 ‘Pramukh Swami Jivan Charitra, Vol. 11’, authored by Adarshjivandas Swami. The volume meticulously documents the life and work of Pramukh Swami Maharaj between 2007 and 2010. Complementing the print edition, an audiobook was also launched.
 A book dedicated to the virtues of ‘Mahant Swami Maharaj, Sadgunna Sindhu’, written by Aksharvatsaldas Swami.
 A Gujarati translation, ‘Snehmay Sahaj Sannidhya’, of ‘In Love, At Ease’ by Yogi Trivedi.
 HH Mahant Swami Maharaj’s Blessings
 Mahant Swami Maharaj inspired all to imbibe the virtues of seva, humility, and faith exemplified by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He said, “Pramukh Swami Maharaj dedicated his entire life for seva. He lived as a ‘servant of servants’ (das na das). Today, we heard the praises of Swami Bapa’s virtues. He truly lived only for us. He had love for everyone. When I was a youth, I once visited Ambli Vali Pol with him. At that time, Babubhai, who managed the small mandir in Ambli Vali Pol, was very restrictive in providing food rations to cook meals. Pramukh Swami Maharaj made rotlis for lunch and gave his portion to me, of which I was completely unware. He knew I enjoyed eating rotlis. Such was his selfless seva and sacrifice.
 “The vow he took upon his appointment as Pramukh or President, he fulfilled and lived it throughout his entire life. The virtues of Pramukh Swami Maharaj are visible here in the River Sabarmati through seventy-five decorative floats. If we truly internalize these virtues, then the ‘Pramukh Varni Mahotsav’ will be celebrated in its truest sense.”
 Finally, the highlight of the grand finale celebration was a spectacular fireworks display from the banks of River Sabarmati.
 Through Mahant Swami Maharaj’s inspiration, it took over three months for 7,000 volunteers in 21 different departments to plan and prepare for the celebration. Fifty thousand devotees and dignitaries from India and abroad attended the program.
 The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) provided generous support in making the celebration possible and successful in all ways.
 The celebration was viewed live by countless devotees and well-wishers in India and abroad through live streaming on live.baps.org and Aastha Bhajan channel.

/News/2025/Prayer-for-Peace-28932.aspx.t: Prayer for Peace and Solidarity, Indianapolis, IN, USA
/News/2025/Prayer-for-Peace-28932.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prayer for Peace (10 photos)
 On August 10, 2025, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Greenwood, IN—a sacred Hindu place of peace and worship—was desecrated with messages of hate and intolerance. This act caused profound pain, not only to our mandir community but to all who believe in mutual respect, understanding, and coexistence.
 Upon discovering the hateful vandalism, local authorities were immediately contacted, and BAPS has been fully cooperating in their investigation of this hate crime. Sadly, this is not an isolated incident. Similar acts of vandalism have occurred at Hindu mandirs across North America, including BAPS mandirs in Toronto, ON; Long Island, NY; Sacramento, CA; and Los Angeles, CA.
 In times of challenge, it is unity, compassion, and shared values that carry us forward. Guided by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s ideals for harmony, peace, and respect, a prayer assembly was organized on August 12, 2025. Voices from across our city, state, and faith communities came together in solidarity, compassion, and shared purpose.
 Congressman Frank J. Mrvan, via video message, shared, “As a country, we have to go beyond division and focus on love.”
 Representative Mike Andrade stated, “We must come together—no matter our backgrounds, faiths, or cultures—to reject hate and build bridges of understanding.”
 Mayor of Greenwood, Mark Myers, expressed, “The city of Greenwood supports BAPS here in our community. We do not tolerate any form of hate towards any person or any religion in our community, and your religion especially shows peace and harmony. We are here to support you and protect you.”
 Chief of Police James Ison emphasized, “Any time an individual or group within our community is attacked, that is an attack on the entire community, and as peacekeepers, we take this seriously.”
 Consul General of India, Mr. Somnath Ghosh, expressed over the phone, "I want to show my support for the BAPS community and reaffirm our shared commitment to peace, harmony, and progress."
 Mr. Yaniv Shmukler of the Indianapolis Jewish Community Relations Council stated, “I want to express my deepest solidarity with BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir and the Hindu community. May our presence here remind us that in times of darkness, we can choose to show up for one another to protect what is sacred, to lift each other up, and to keep building a community with trust and care.”
 Dr. Erin Hougland, Executive Director of the Center for Interfaith Cooperation (CIC), said, “We will not let this single act of hate snuff out the more powerful light of love and compassion that we all carry within us, no matter what tradition we come from.”
 JR Sandadi, Board Chair of CIC and HSS USA, reflected, “By standing together today, people of different faiths, backgrounds, and walks of life show that love and unity are far stronger than hate. As Hindus, we believe in Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam—the whole world is one big family. In times like these, let us stand together and let peace prevail.”
 Rabbi Hal Schevitz of Congregation Beth-El Zedeck offered scripture, saying, “The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree. Those that are planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of our God.” – Psalm 92.
 Amarsinghji, Former Minister of Religion and Sikh Priest, shared, “As long as you remain engaged to serve the community, nothing will touch you.”
 Raju Chinthala, Founder and President of the Indiana-India Business Council, noted, “Our response to hate will always be love, our response to anger will always be compassion, and our way forward will always be together.”
 Representatives from the Hindu Mandir of Central Indiana and other community organizations were also present to show their support.
 BAPS extends its heartfelt gratitude to the local and state authorities and to the broader community for their ongoing support. BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha remains committed to its mission of promoting peace, harmony, and service to all.

/News/2025/Prayers-for-Pahalgam-28358.as.text:
BAPS condemns the brutal terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu & Kashmir, India.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and BAPS worldwide continue to pray for the innocent victims and their families, and for the recovery of the injured.
 We also pray that in this hour of deep grief and shock, may the whole world unite to take conscious and collective action to uproot terrorism everywhere and anywhere in the world.

/News/2025/President-of-Mongolia-Visits-.t: President of Mongolia Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India
/News/2025/President-of-Mongolia-Visits-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 President of Mongolia Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India (17 photos)
 His Excellency Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh, President of Mongolia, visited BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi during his state visit to India. He was accompanied by Minister of Foreign Affairs Battsetseg Batmunkh, Ambassador Ganbold Dambajav, and members of the Mongolian delegation.
 His Excellency was accorded a traditional welcome by senior swamis on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The president paid his respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and performed abhishek of Shri Neelkanth Varni, offering prayers for peace, harmony, and the well-being of the people of both nations.
 His Excellency received a personal letter of blessings and prayers from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who expressed appreciation for the president’s visit and commended his leadership in nurturing peace, compassion, and unity among the people of Mongolia. Mahant Swami Maharaj also prayed for His Excellency’s continued good health and success, and for the enduring friendship between India and Mongolia to grow in mutual respect and shared spiritual values.
 As a gesture of friendship and respect, President Khürelsükh presented a specially crafted print of the Akshardham Mandir on fine Mongolian cashmere cloth.
 Reflecting on the enduring ties between the two nations and his visit, President Khürelsükh remarked, “The bond between the people of India, serene and peaceful like the flow of the River Ganges, and the people of Mongolia, whose hearts are as vast as the Mongolian steppes, traces its origins back to the time of the Hunnu Empire.
 “Today, I am very delighted to visit this wonderful temple that reflects the spirituality, religion, way of life, traditions, history, and culture of the Indian people. It is truly a temple that is a symbol and expression of the Indian people’s deep spirituality.”
 His Excellency expressed heartfelt gratitude for the warm welcome and peaceful experience at Akshardham. He also conveyed deep appreciation to His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj for his kind letter of blessings and prayers.

/News/2025/Pujya-Brahmavihari-Swami-Hono.t: Pujya Brahmavihari Swami Honored at Lokmat Maharashtrian of the Year Awards 2025, Mumbai, India
/News/2025/Pujya-Brahmavihari-Swami-Hono.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Lokmat Maharashtrian of the Year Awards 2025 (9 photos)
 On behalf of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Pujya Brahmavihari Swami was honored at the Lokmat Maharashtrian of the Year Awards 2025 by Lokmat, a prestigious media group that recognizes individuals who have made outstanding contributions to society, driving progress and excellence in their respective fields.
 The event, held at Raj Bhavan, Mumbai, was graced by esteemed dignitaries from politics, business, and culture, including chief guest Honorable Governor of Maharashtra Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan, as well as Honorable Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Honorable Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde, and Honorable Speaker of the Maharashtra Assembly Shri Rahul Narwekar.
 Brahmavihari Swami was honored by the Governor of Maharashtra for his remarkable contributions to international relations, humanitarian service, and interfaith harmony through BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. His leadership has been instrumental in fostering global unity, overseeing humanitarian projects, and strengthening cultural ties across nations. He played a key role in leading the construction of the historic BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, the first traditional Hindu mandir in the Middle East. Additionally, during the peak of the Russia-Ukraine war, he led the BAPS relief efforts at the Poland-Ukraine border, assisting Indian nationals and global citizens in their safe evacuation.
 The event also recognized Shri Devendra Fadnavis with a Special Award for his impactful leadership and services to Maharashtra. Other distinguished awardees included Shri Sanjiv Bajaj (Chairman & MD, Bajaj Finserv), Shri Kartik Aaryan (Indian Actor), and Shri Deven Bharti (Special Commissioner, Mumbai Police).
 The awards ceremony, backed by a prestigious jury comprising eminent leaders, industrialists, and experts, celebrated the remarkable achievements of individuals who have made a lasting impact in their respective fields, furthering Maharashtra’s legacy of excellence and service.

/News/2025/Rakshabandhan-Celebration-293.t: Rakshabandhan Celebration in the presence of Sadguru Pujya Bhaktipriya Swami, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2025/Rakshabandhan-Celebration-293.text:
Devotees from across Canada gathered at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto on weekend of August 9 and 10, 2025, to welcome Sadguru Pujya Bhaktipriya Swami (Kothari Swami) upon his arrival in North America.
 The assembly began with a vibrant cultural dance performed by youths, expressing devotion and joy while setting a celebratory tone for the occasion. The gathering also coincided with the celebration of Rakshabandhan, during which devotees reflected on the spiritual significance of protection, unity, and the bond between a guru and a disciple.
 Two upcoming historic occasions: the Mandir Mahotsav (Inauguration) of the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Belleville, Ontario, and the Shilanyas Mahotsav (Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony) for the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Ottawa, Canada’s capital city were also formally launched in the presence of Pujya Kothari Swami. These new mandirs will serve not only as places of spiritual enrichment and devotion, but also as centres for community service, cultural preservation, and youth development. Through regular assemblies, children and youth activities, and community initiatives, they will provide a welcoming space for individuals and families while contributing to the betterment of the wider Canadian society.
 As the program came to a close, the atmosphere was filled with devotion and gratitude. The tying of rakhis symbolized the sacred bond of faith and unity, while the blessings imparted by Pujya Kothari Swami inspired all to strengthen their spiritual resolve. Devotees departed with renewed enthusiasm, cherishing the opportunity to celebrate Rakshabandhan in his presence.

/News/2025/Rakshabandhan-Weaving-a-Tapes.t: Rakshabandhan: Weaving a Tapestry of Love, Care, and Protection, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Rakshabandhan-Weaving-a-Tapes.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Rakshabandhan (20 photos)
 Over 20,000 devotees and community members from across the seven emirates of the UAE came to the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi to celebrate the auspicious festival of Rakshabandhan with faith and devotion.
 The celebrations unfolded in three phases in three places. A special assembly of several thousand workers where ‘rakhis’ were tied by BAPS swamis; special spots in the Mandir foreground were created where hundreds of sisters tied ‘rakhis’ to their brothers; and BAPS swamis visited dozens of factories and companies to pray for protection and tie ‘rakhis’ to each and every worker. 
 The celebrations at the BAPS Hindu Mandir featured two captivating programs, morning and evening. Brimming with traditional devotional songs presented by talented volunteers and community members, they filled the Mandir with an atmosphere of joy and reverence. Following these inspiring performances, Brahmaviharidas Swami addressed the gatherings, “Rakshabandhan celebrates one of the noblest human emotions of lifelong protection. More than 5,000 ‘rakhis’ were handmade with love by BAPS women devotees to gift to each recipient, symbolizing protection. Even this Mandir is handmade with love! Hence, in a place of great love and harmony, we pray that may God guide and guard this beautiful nation, its leadership, and all those who call it their home.”
 One humble worker summarized the voice of thousands with these words, “Even though I am many miles away from my home, I feel honored that the swamis tied a rakhi on my wrist. It is as if I am transported back to my village in Gujarat with my sister around me.”
 The Rakshabandhan celebrations at the BAPS Hindu Mandir were a living example of how traditions can foster harmony, gratitude, and shared humanity across the UAE.

/News/2025/Ramkatha-Inspires-Devotees-Ac.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Ramkatha (22 photos)
 Daily, over 450 devotees and well-wishers from diverse communities across Bahrain attended the five days of inspiring discourses on the Ramayan delivered by Tyagvatsal Swami. Families, youths, and elders enthusiastically participated, reflecting the universal appeal of Bhagwan Shri Ram’s life and teachings.
 The engaging daily discourses featured soulful narrations that offered practical guidance for strengthening family bonds and leading a value-based life amidst modern challenges. The profound and timeless messages on values such as truth, compassion, duty, sacrifice, respect for elders, and unity within families left a lasting impression on all participants.

/News/2025/Regional-Training-Camps-for-B.t: Regional Training Camps for BAPS Bal-Balika Activities Volunteers, India
/News/2025/Regional-Training-Camps-for-B.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Bal Karyakars (40 photos)
 Balika Karyakars (26 photos)
 Across India, more than 150,000 boys and girls take part in over 8,500 bal and balika mandals. Around 17,000 karyakars help run these activities for children.
 Annual Regional Training Camps help these karyakars to strengthen their satsang and learn new ways to serve the children better.
 During July and August 2025, 25 Regional Training Camps were held at BAPS mandirs across India on the theme ‘Be A Perfect Karyakar’ to help the volunteers improve their skills and seva.
 Volunteers learned how to tell stories in a simple and enjoyable way for children as a powerful way to teach them values and culture. Volunteers were also guided on how to create and conduct fun games that keep children excited and engaged.
 Other sessions demonstrated how videos and other media can be used to make bal sabhas more informative, interesting, and impactful.
 In addition, the camps included activities, video shows, and discussions that gave valuable insights to the karyakars.

/News/2025/Sangam-30361.aspx.t: Sangam: An Interfaith and Multicultural Diwali Celebration at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Los Angeles, CA, USA
/News/2025/Sangam-30361.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Welcome & Tour (11 photos)
 Diwali Gala (37 photos)
 In a radiant display of unity and cultural harmony, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Los Angeles hosted Sangam, an interfaith and multicultural Diwali celebration that brought together a remarkable confluence of communities, leaders, and cultures.
 From diplomats and interfaith representatives to scholars, athletes, business executives, and cultural organizations, Sangam served as a living embodiment of Diwali’s message — the triumph of light over darkness and unity over division. The evening fostered understanding among diverse communities, strengthened ties with India and the Indian diaspora, and deepened mutual respect for the Mandir’s mission of faith in action.
 A Welcoming Beginning
 The celebration began with a warm reception in the Haveli, where youth volunteers greeted guests with traditional hospitality. Attendees were then guided through the intricately carved Mandir, where they learned about Hindu architecture, craftsmanship, and the deeper spiritual significance of the Mandir as a place of peace and devotion.
 As twilight descended, guests gathered outdoors for a gala dinner under the glow of festive lights and the Mandir’s majestic silhouette — an unforgettable backdrop for an evening dedicated to unity and reflection.
 Messages of Partnership and Light
 The formal program opened with remarks from Dr. K. J. Srinivasa, the inaugural Consul General of India in Los Angeles. He reflected on the enduring U.S.–India partnership and the importance of shared celebrations like Sangam in building bridges across communities and faiths.
 Following tradition, attendees participated in a ceremonial lighting of diyas — small oil lamps symbolizing the victory of light and knowledge. During the program, a letter from California Governor Gavin Newsom was read aloud, extending warm Diwali wishes to all and recognizing the event’s contribution to unity and service.
 Interfaith Reflections and Shared Prayers
 The interfaith segment opened with a land acknowledgment and indigenous prayer from members of the Gabrieleno/Tongva San Gabriel Band of Mission Indians, honoring the original stewards of Southern California’s land.
 Faith leaders from across the region then shared reflections aligned with Diwali’s universal themes of light, renewal, and hope. Participants represented:
 Gabrieleno/Tongva San Gabriel Band of Mission Indians
 Namdhari Sikh Sangat of Los Angeles
 Zoroastrian Association of California
 Jain Center of Southern California
 St. Paul the Apostle Catholic Church
 The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
 Masjid Al Jamali – Dawoodi Bohra Community of OC/IE
 Fo Guang Shan Hsi Lai Temple
 Malibu Hindu Temple
 BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Los Angeles
 Each prayer highlighted a shared aspiration: that compassion, humility, and service may light the way forward for all communities.
 A Message of Hope and Harmony
 The evening culminated with an inspiring video address from Pujya Paramtattvadas Swami of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London (Neasden Temple). His reflections on light, positivity, and unity resonated deeply with the audience.
 Drawing from BAPS’ participation in the London 2012 and Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games, he looked ahead to the FIFA World Cup 2026 and the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, encouraging collaboration, faith-based service, and collective goodwill. “When faith communities come together,” he reminded the audience, “we illuminate the world far beyond our own walls.”
 A Gathering of Global and Local Voices
 Among the distinguished attendees were representatives from the following diplomatic missions, organizations, and institutions:
 Consulates: India, Armenia, El Salvador, Switzerland, Cambodia, Dominican Republic, South Africa, Lithuania, and Myanmar.
 Academic and Civic Organizations: University of California – Riverside, University of Southern California, California State University – Fullerton, Interfaith Youth Alliance, and LA28 Cultural Olympiad Committee.
 Community and Business Leaders: LMNTRIX Cybersecurity, Asian American Hotel Owners Association, MS International, ALAPIO (Association of Los Angeles Physicians of Indian Origin), Smart Village Movement, KPC Group, and the LA Knightriders Major League Cricket Team.
 Illuminating the Path Forward
 As guests departed, many expressed admiration for the Mandir’s role in uniting communities through faith, culture, and service. Sangam was more than a Diwali celebration — it was a shared commitment to building bridges across traditions and reaffirming that in unity, there is light.

/News/2025/Sant-Parayan-Shri-Swaminaraya.t: Sant Parayan: Shri Swaminarayan Charitam, UK & Europe
/News/2025/Sant-Parayan-Shri-Swaminaraya.text:
A spiritually uplifting series of parayans (scriptural discourses) on ‘Swaminarayan Charitam’ was delivered across the UK and mainland Europe by Gnanpriyadas Swami, a learned and senior swami of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, visiting from North America.
 The 44 parayans hosted at BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK and in 12 European countries explored the divine incidents of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and his profound interactions with swamis and devotees. Through vivid prasangs, interspersed kirtans, and scriptural references, Gnanpriyadas Swami offered deep spiritual insights that inspired reflection, strengthened faith, and fostered devotion among thousands of attendees.
 Devotees gathered in large numbers at each mandir and centre to listen attentively to the enlightening discourses. The sessions highlighted Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s compassion, his role as the eternal guide, and the timeless relevance of his teachings today through the Aksharbrahma Guru. The atmosphere in every assembly was infused with devotion, reverence, and spiritual enrichment.
 In addition to these discourses, a series of parayans were also delivered by mahilas (women devotees) of all ages, and children. Their heartfelt presentations, rooted in devotion and scriptural study, further enriched the community with inspiring reflections on Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine life, work, and teachings.
 This inspiring series not only nurtured individual faith but also reinforced community unity, as devotees across the UK and Europe connected with the life and message of Bhagwan Swaminarayan through these gatherings.

/News/2025/Santvibhuti-Pramukh-Swami-Mah.t: ‘Santvibhuti Pramukh Swami Maharaj’ Book Launch at BAPS Mandir, Ahmedabad, India
/News/2025/Santvibhuti-Pramukh-Swami-Mah.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Book Lauch Ceremony (43 photos)
 In a momentous literary and spiritual celebration, the Sahitya Akademi – India's National Academy of Letters under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India – in collaboration with BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, Delhi, launched the book ‘Santvibhuti Pramukh Swami Maharaj’ at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Ahmedabad in the presence of the Honorable Union Minister of Culture, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.
 The event was attended by notable dignitaries, including, Dr. K. Sreenivasa Rao, Secretary, National Sahitya Akademi; Dr. N. Suresh Babu, Deputy Secretary, Publication, Sahitya Akademi; Padma Shri Gautambhai Patel, a renowned Sanskrit scholar from Gujarat; Madhav Ramanuj, a celebrated Gujarati poet, writer, and critic; Tarun Vijay, former editor of Panchjanya and retired MP; Srinivas Varkhedi, Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University, Delhi; Harekrishna Satpathi, a distinguished Sanskrit scholar; Murli Manohar Pathak, Vice-Chancellor of Lal Bahadur Shastri University; G.S.R. Krishnamurti, Vice-Chancellor of Tirupati Sanskrit University; Sukant Senapati, Vice-Chancellor, Shree Somnath Sanskrit University; and Shri Virendrakumar Tiwari, Former Director of IIT Kharagpur; and Shri Bhagyesh Jha, President of Gujarat Sahitya Akademi and former IAS officer.
 Authored by Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami, the book presents an insightful portrayal of the profound life, works, and global services of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and his contributions to the elevation of Indian culture. It reflects upon his spiritual influence and service-driven leadership that brought global recognition to India's timeless heritage of Sanatan Dharma.
 During this grand event, the distinguished dignitaries lit the ceremonial lamp and offered floral tributes at Pramukh Swami Maharaj's feet. During the launch assembly, the eminent guests shared their wisdom.
 Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Minister of Culture, Government of India: “It is impossible to capture Pramukh Swami Maharaj's vast life journey in a single book. The moment I had darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj was the most fortunate and blessed moment of my life.
 “Pramukh Swami Maharaj was a rare soul. He was a saint who dedicated every moment of his life to public welfare. He was a saint who lived every moment in infinite bliss, seeing the entire world as a manifestation of God.
 “He was the embodiment of infinite peace, yet simultaneously simple, straightforward, and humble. By dedicating every moment of life to public welfare, he made an immense contribution to preserving Sanatan Dharma. Amidst numerous invasions, the reason Indian culture remains uninterrupted and eternal is because of such saints who have donned saffron robes and made sacrifices.
 “He kept Indian culture perpetually renewed. At a time when Indian culture needed preservation and the saint tradition needed strengthening, Pramukh Swami Maharaj initiated saints, built mandirs, and promoted scriptural traditions.
 “He was full of affection and capable of delivering eternal wisdom in just a few words. People felt that every message he gave was for their welfare, and his words would resonate deeply in their hearts. The changing global role of India today has a special contribution from Pramukh Swami Maharaj. By publishing this book about his life, I feel that my ministry and I have been blessed.”
 Dr. Bhagyesh Jha, President, Gujarat Literature Academy, Gandhinagar: “Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed many devotees like myself. I met him 29 times. In 2000, I spent 24 hours with him in Sarangpur. At that time, I realized that the globally venerable Pramukh Swami Maharaj never used a single moment for himself, but used every moment for society, religion, and cultural protection. Being in the proximity of such a person was a blessed moment of my life. His blessings were a greater honor for me than even the Padma Bhushan.
 “This book is not just a book, it is a guru's saga, a poem, the essence of our shastras, and the purpose of human life. Despite managing a vast empire-like organization, Swami Bapa always smiled like a child. Today, the subtle presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj is here.”
 Dr. K. Srinivas Rao, Secretary, National Literature Academy, Delhi: “Pramukh Swami Maharaj was one of the greatest spiritual personalities of the 20th century. He was a spiritual guide and supreme friend to everyone. He showered selfless love towards all. Due to Pramukh Swami Maharaj's tireless efforts, BAPS has served in numerous spiritual and social activities.
 “The Literature Academy is extremely pleased to publish this book about his life, written by Bhadreshdasji Swami. This book is a brilliant document of a divine life and philosophy.”
 Shri Tarun Vijayji, Former Member of Parliament, Scholar, and Author: “When I became a member of parliament, Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed me at Akshardham in Delhi to spend my life serving India along with serving the poor and helpless people of society. Only India’s sages, ascetics, and saints can give such blessings. Pramukh Swami Maharaj dedicated his entire life to serving humanity. Through him, Vedantic knowledge is being spread to everyone, and through him, brave saints are propagating and expanding the radiance of India's eternal religion across the entire globe. This is Pramukh Swami Maharaj's greatest gift to the world. He was a century-defining personality.”
 Prof. Srinivas Varkhedi, Vice Chancellor, Central Sanskrit University, Delhi: “Today, through this book, we are having darshan of a great personality and guiding light, Pramukh Swami Maharaj. This book is not a literary work or a biography, but a manifestation of a saint. In every word of this book, one experiences the presence of the Akshar-Purushottam philosophy and Pramukh Swami Maharaj himself.
 “My guru Swami Vishveshtirthji Maharaj used to say that just as King Bhagirath brought the divine Ganga to this land to liberate his ancestors, Pramukh Swami Maharaj has propagated the Indian cultural Ganga worldwide for the liberation of future generations. He was a modern-day Bhagirath-like saint.”
 Prof. Murali Manohar Pathak, Vice Chancellor, Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University: “I have watched Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s videos many times. His facial expressions reveal the essence of the Indian spiritual aura. Reading this book, I felt that this is the language of conduct, civilization, good character, and culture.
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj lived for the welfare of the public and dedicated his entire life for social good. He has done so much for the society, nation, and world that we cannot even imagine. Mahant Swami Maharaj is another form of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Just by having his darshan, worldly sorrows disappear, and all difficulties are resolved.”
 Prof. G.S.R. Krishnamurthy, Vice Chancellor, National Sanskrit University, Tirupati: “Just by remembering Pramukh Swami Maharaj, our heart's desires are fulfilled. Under his inspiration, Bhadreshdas Swami wrote the commentary on the Prasthantrayi. Pramukh Swami Maharaj was the embodiment of service. His special quality was that he paved the way of selfless action.”
 Prof. Harekrishna Satpathi, Former Vice Chancellor, National Sanskrit University, Tirupati: “Like a sacred confluence, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was himself a confluence. He was an ocean of knowledge, an ocean of action, an ocean of devotion. In Swamiji, the Ganga of action, the Yamuna of devotion, and the Saraswati of knowledge flowed. These three rivers merged into one great ocean.
 “The same merit one gets by bathing at a holy pilgrimage site will be obtained by remembering the name and life of the saintly personality Pramukh Swami Maharaj.”
 Mahamahopadhyaya Padmashri Gautambhai Patel, Eminent Scholar: “India has produced great personalities like Swami Vivekanand and Pramukh Swami Maharaj who have guided the world. Pramukh Swamiji was the embodiment of equality. If a four-year-old child invited him, he would go to their hut, and on the other hand, he would give an inspiring speech at the UN addressing the entire world. The composition of this book is marvelous. I request that everyone study this book.”
 Prof. Virendrakumar Tiwari, Former Director, IIT Kharagpur: “BAPS volunteers provide service worldwide through Pramukh Swami Maharaj's grace. People from every walk of life are involved. Today, the world needs dialogue and peace, which can only come through the words of a saint like Pramukh Swami Maharaj and by reading such books.”
 Shri Madhav Ramanuj, Renowned Poet: “I had the benefit of having Pramukh Swami Maharaj's darshan on many occasions. He has saved many people’s lives. Many great works have been done by him. Much more can be written about him. By seeing, knowing, and reading all this, we will continue to get constant inspiration.”
 Prof. Sukantakumar Senapati, Vice Chancellor, Somnath Sanskrit University: “Pramukh Swami Maharaj was a great human being. The objective of Indian wisdom is to become human. Pramukh Swami Maharaj was its best example. His vow was public welfare. He remained dedicated to public service throughout his life.”
 Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami, author of the book: “Pramukh Swami Maharaj's life was not lived in a single time period; it was an immortal historical event. Pramukh Swami Maharaj was a noble saint. A supreme devotee of God, a pure heart, pure thoughts, and pure actions were his identity. Such a saint is called Brahmaswarup in spiritual philosophy. Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s extraordinary life infused energy into us. In the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, Lord Shri Krishna says, ‘Esha Brahmi-sthiti’ –This is the Brahmic state. Another name for the Brahmic state is Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He was the living embodiment of the ‘sthitaprajna’ described in the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita. His existence is eternal. Presently, Mahant Swami Maharaj is the representative of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. This book is a unique offering at the feet of Pramukh Swami Maharaj on behalf of the Government of India, for his divine life and selfless service works.”
 The event concluded with a grand unveiling of the book by Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture, and the stage dignitaries, to the excited applause of the packed auditorium.

/News/2025/Sarang-2025-30324.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Detroit, Sarang 2025 (52 photos)
 Sarang is a weekend-long event in which balikas, kishoris, and yuvatis have the opportunity to offer their bhakti through garba. Inspired by the kirtan “Āp vachan nā megh malhāre, sārang thai nāchu”, the first Sarang was launched in July 2017 during HH Mahant Swami Maharaj’s vicharan in Chicago, IL. A few months later, the first Sarang in Indianapolis, IN, was held.
 Eight years later, balikas, kishoris, and yuvatis joined in celebrating the 5th Sarang in Detroit, MI, from November 7-9, 2025. During the event, delegates participated in an outing to the University of Michigan, enjoyed an evening program centered around the importance of bhakti, and concluded the weekend by performing their heartfelt bhakti through garba. 
 This year, delegates had the unique opportunity to participate in a live garba format in which kishoris from Chicago, Indianapolis, and Milwaukee sang kirtans live- allowing delegates to offer bhakti through both singing and dancing. Delegates left the weekend feeling reenergized with one goal in mind: to make every action a form of bhakti to earn the rajipo of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2025/Satsang-Adhiveshan---Rajipo-D.t: Satsang Adhiveshan - Rajipo Din Satsang Shibir, North America
/News/2025/Satsang-Adhiveshan---Rajipo-D.text:
In 2025, devotees across North America participated in the Satsang Adhiveshan themed “Satsang: The Journey to Rajipo.” The eight-month-long Adhiveshan provided participants with an opportunity to strengthen their understanding of satsang through study, reflection, and creative expression, culminating in the Rajipo Din Satsang Shibir.
 The Adhiveshan featured a wide range of competitions that encouraged both scriptural knowledge and personal development. Participants took part in Mukhpath competitions by memorizing selected verses from sacred scriptures, and in Prasang competitions that involved reading incidents from satsang and completing related exams. Other categories highlighted various soft skills, including public speaking, emceeing, skit performance, speech writing, skit writing, article writing, and multimedia content creation.
 After months of preparation and participation, the grand finale, Rajipo Din Satsang Shibir, brought participants together to reflect on the essence of rajipo (divine pleasure) of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The shibir included insightful discourses by swamis who emphasized the importance of rajipo and prapti (realizing one’s spiritual fortune).
 Through engaging dialogues, Q&A sessions, and group discussions, participants deepened their understanding of the shibir’s central message. Video guidance from senior swamis enriched the sessions, and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed all attendees through a special video message, expressing his rajipo upon their sincere efforts.
 On the same day, children participants took part in the Mukhpath competition, followed by an award ceremony recognizing their dedication and achievement.
 The event concluded with an inspiring award ceremony and reflections on praptino vichar—the invaluable spiritual attainment of being under the guidance of the Satpurush.

/News/2025/Satsang-Adhiveshan-2025-The-J.t: Satsang Adhiveshan 2025: The Journey to Rajipo, North America
/News/2025/Satsang-Adhiveshan-2025-The-J.text:
In 2025, devotees, young and old, across North America participated in the Satsang Adhiveshan themed “Satsang: The Journey to Rajipo.” Over eight months, participants from every age group deepened their understanding of satsang through study, reflection, and creative expression.
 The Adhiveshan inspired devotees to please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and their guru, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, through sincere effort, discipline, and devotion. Competitions across all wings integrated scriptural learning, inspiring devotees to live the values of satsang every day.
 Throughout the journey, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj continuously guided and motivated devotees and youths. Through special assemblies, Q&A sessions, and inspiring video messages, Swamishri encouraged everyone to participate in the adhiveshan, thereby deepening their understanding of satsang and strengthening their connection with Bhagwan.
 Sanyukt-Premvati Adhiveshan (Adults)
 The Sanyukt-Premvati Adhiveshan provided adults across North America with an opportunity to strengthen their scriptural knowledge and leadership skills. Over 21,130 participants took part in the Adhiveshan, which included Mukhpath competitions, Satsang Prasang exams, and Skills Competitions.
 In the Satsang Mukhpath category, participants memorized verses from twelve sacred texts, including the Vachanamrut, Swamini Vato, Satsang Diksha, Purushottam Bolya Prite, and Yogi Gita. Together, they memorized an astounding 3,378,525 verses.
 In the Satsang Prasang competition, participants read, reflected on, and completed an exam based on 100 inspiring incidents from the lives of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru Parampara. These lessons helped devotees cultivate steadiness, faith, and perspective in daily life.
 The Skills Competition engaged over 5,000 participants in categories such as public speaking, emceeing, skit performance, speech and skit writing, article writing, and multimedia content creation. Structured online training helped participants refine their communication and presentation abilities. The Adhiveshan encouraged lifelong learning and deepened the collective spirit of devotion across local mandirs.
 Bal-Balika, Kishore-Kishori, and Yuvak-Yuvati Adhiveshan (Youth)
 Between June and August 2025, 12,295 youth participants joined the Adhiveshan and Summer Shibir series held across North America. The programs centered on Mukhpath memorization, with participants collectively memorizing 1,609,663 verses from Hindu shastras, including 868,981 Satsang Diksha shlokas.
 Youth also showcased their creativity and talent through Skills Competitions, where 7,907 participants explored diverse categories such as art, design, writing, music, dance, technology, and public speaking. Individual events included painting and 3D art, graphic design, photography, digital illustration, story writing, poetry, music production, videography, and short speeches. Group events included drama, singing, and instrumental performances.
 These experiences helped participants internalize the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Satpurush while building confidence, creativity, and teamwork. Each youth Adhiveshan concluded with reflections on shravan, manan, and nidhidhyas—hearing, contemplating, and realizing spiritual truths. Together, these experiences inspired participants to continue their lifelong journey toward rajipo and spiritual growth.
 Across every age group and activity, the 2025 Satsang Adhiveshan reflected the unity, enthusiasm, and spiritual progress of the North American satsang community.
 Strengthened by the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, devotees continue to walk the path of rajipo—living with faith, understanding, and unwavering devotion.

/News/2025/Satsang-Diksha-Felicitation-C.t: Satsang Diksha Felicitation Ceremony, Nagpur, India
/News/2025/Satsang-Diksha-Felicitation-C.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Felicitation Ceremony (12 photos)
 Worldwide, under the auspices of the Mission Rajipo project initiated by Mahant Swami Maharaj, 15,666 children aged 3 to 14 memorized the entire Satsang Diksha scripture.
 Of these, 55 boys and girls are from the Nagpur region. A special felicitation ceremony was organized to honor the achievements of these young Vidwans (scholars).
 On this occasion, the glory of the Satsang Diksha scripture and the benefits of its memorization were presented through dialogues, dances, quizzes, speeches, and other presentations.
 Dr. Pankaj Chande, founder and former Vice-Chancellor of Kavi Kulguru Kalidas University in Nagpur, graced the occasion and in his address explained the importance of the Sanskrit language and the Satsang Diksha scripture.
 All the boys and girls who had memorized the Satsang Diksha scripture were seated in artistically decorated palkhis and felicitated with a shower of flowers. They were also honored with trophies, certificates, gifts, and garlands.

/News/2025/Satsang-Diksha-Homatmak-Path-.t: Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path Yagna, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2025/Satsang-Diksha-Homatmak-Path-.text:
On Sunday, August 17, 2025, devotees and well-wishers gathered at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto for a memorable occasion. The 326th Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path Yagna was held in the divine presence of Sadguru Pujya Bhaktipriyadas Swami (Kothari Swami).
 The day began with the yagna ceremony, led by Pujya Bhaktipriyadas Swami. With devotion and unity, families and devotees offered prayers and oblations, seeking peace, harmony, and spiritual upliftment for themselves, their loved ones, and and society at large.
 This initiative was blessed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in October 2024, encouraging families across Canada to perform homatmak yagnas in their homes. Rooted in ancient Vedic tradition, the yagna is more than a ritual. It sanctifies the home, strengthens family unity, and deepens one’s personal connection to the Guru and the satsang fellowship.
 In the afternoon, a celebration assembly filled the mandir with joy and inspiration. A highlight of the program was honouring children from across Canada who had memorized the entire Satsang Diksha scripture in Sanskrit. Among them was the youngest child, only three years old, who memorized all 315 verses. In total, 88 girls and 67 boys reached this milestone and received the blessings of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The assembly also recognized Canadian devotees who had completed all 20 chapters in the North America Adhiveshan, a demanding but deeply rewarding journey of scriptural study and memorization. Their dedication served as an inspiration to the entire satsang community in Canada.
 Later, a pujan of the Satsang Diksha scripture was performed with great reverence. This reminded everyone of the timeless wisdom and daily guidance the scripture provides. Plans were also shared to enshrine Satsang Diksha in every BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir across Canada so its teachings may continue to guide and inspire generations.
 The evening concluded with the launch of the BAPS Prakash app, which brings the spiritual wisdom of Swaminarayan Prakash magazine and BAPS News directly to devotees worldwide. This new platform provides an accessible way to stay connected with inspiring messages and reflections.
 The day was filled with devotion, joy, and unity. Devotees left with cherished memories and renewed motivation to live by the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and guidance of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2025/Satsang-Diksha-Homatmak-Yagna.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Diksha Homatmak Yagna (13 photos)
 A special two-year initiative was launched on the premises of the under construction BAPS mandir in Amreli in the build-up to the murti-pratishtha. On the day of Vasant Panchami, 551 yajmans, seated around 51 yagna kunds, participated in a Vedic mahapuja ceremony and then offered over 100,000 ahutis into the yagna pits while the 315 verses of the Satsang Diksha shastra were recited.
 Following this launch, every day, a devotee family in Amreli will perform the Satsang Diksha Homatmak Yagna at their home with the help of specially trained youths to pray for universal peace and harmony and the successful completion of the mandir.

/News/2025/Satsang-Diksha-Symposium-at-U.t: Satsang Diksha Symposium at University of Cambridge, UK
/News/2025/Satsang-Diksha-Symposium-at-U.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Diksha Symposium (32 photos)
 A full-day symposium on the Satsang Diksha was held at the University of Cambridge on Friday 17 January 2025.
 Distinguished scholars as well as advanced students were invited to present their research and engage in academic dialogue on various aspects of this vital scripture of the BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu tradition.
 Invited scholars joined from around the UK as well as from Finland, Germany, India, the Netherlands, and the USA.
 The event was supported by Cambridge’s Faculty of Divinity, the St Andrews Encyclopaedia of Theology, the Sanskrit Department at Heidelberg University, the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute in London, and the Cambridge Interfaith Programme.
 The symposium sought to facilitate research and dialogue in a number of disciplinary areas directly related to this primary revelatory scripture, authored by the guru of BAPS, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. With the text serving as an important foundation of the Swaminarayan tradition’s distinctive school of Vedanta, namely, Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, and its adherents’ spiritual, devotional, and moral way of life, the symposium provided a forum for exploring the vitality and relevance of a contemporary Sanskrit scripture along with an opportunity to engaging with some key articulations of lived Hinduism.
 The papers covered a number of contemporary subjects, such as civil law, domestic life, ethical finance, and religious pluralism, as well as some classical topics of theology, philosophy, philology, pedagogy, material culture, textual studies, and others.
 James Hegarty, Professor of the Religions of South Asia at Cardiff University and one of the convenors of the symposium, explained, “For a text so recent, the extensive range of global public engagement – from the thousands of people, young and old, who have been memorising its 315 Sanskrit verses, to the thousands joining weekly for an in-depth online course – makes the Satsang Diksha especially worthy of academic study.”
 Professor Alice Collet, Academic Editor of the Hinduism and Buddhism sections of the St Andrews Encyclopaedia of Theology, reflected, “It was a pleasure to attend the symposium, which was a good balance of academic rigour and a positive collegiate environment.”
 Dr Ankur Barua, Senior Lecturer in Hindu Studies at the University of Cambridge, appreciated the symposium’s collaborative focus: “The symposium brought together doctoral students, established academics, and scholar-practitioners in a series of discussions on how a recently composed scriptural text distils the essence of various Hindu religious themes and presents it in a manner that would be accessible to devotees at the grassroots.”
 In his keynote address, delivered online, Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami demonstrated the universal scope of the Satsang Diksha and explained how it is, at once, a Darshan Shastra, Dharma Shastra, Bhakti Shastra, and much more.
 Overall, the symposium provided a multidisciplinary exploration of the Satsang Diksha, critically engaging with its theological, ethical, linguistic, and material dimensions while situating it within the broader contexts of Hindu studies and global religious thought.
 For further details about the symposium, please see the report on Cambridge University’s Faculty of Divinity website here.
 Disclaimer: BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha is not responsible for the content of external internet sites.

/News/2025/Satsang-Sabha-with-BAPS-Swami.t: Satsang Sabha with BAPS Swamis, Oslo, Norway
/News/2025/Satsang-Sabha-with-BAPS-Swami.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Oslo, Norway (12 photos)
 On 22 May 1988, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj concluded his historic Europe Vicharan in Oslo, Norway. During lunch that day, sevak swamis lovingly requested Swamishri to have one more rotli, saying: “This is the last rotli and the last day in Europe. The next meal will be in London later today.” 
 Swamishri replied with profound foresight: “This might be the last vicharan for me, but sadhus and devotees will come here often to spread satsang. It is Guru Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj’s resolve that Satsang spreads across Europe. To fulfil their resolve, you all will have to come here many times.”
 These words became reality when, in 2012, Shrutiprakashdas Swami and other swamis from London visited Oslo. Later, Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of BAPS UK & Europe, and accompanying swamis continued to nurture the spiritual needs of devotees in Norway.
 Carrying forward this divine vision, Tyagprakashdas Swami and Aksharsankalpdas Swami from London visited Oslo on Thursday 16 October 2025, and participated in a special Satsang Sabha organised by local devotees.
 During the assembly, Tyagprakashdas Swami delivered an inspiring discourse on the core principles of Sanatan Hindu Dharma: Satya (Truth), Daya (Compassion), Ahimsa Non-violence), Brahmacharya (Self-restraint), and Asteya (Non-stealing). 
 He emphasised the importance of spirituality and faith in today’s rapidly changing world. His words resonated deeply with the devotees, who expressed heartfelt gratitude for the swamis’ visit and the spiritual guidance they received.
 This sabha reaffirmed the enduring commitment to fulfil the vision of the Satpurush and strengthen Satsang in Europe.

/News/2025/Satsang-Shibirs-2025-29689.as.text:
The 2025 residential satsang shibirs for UK & Europe were held during the month of August at Warwick Conference Park, bringing together more than 4,000 delegates of all ages to help develop their understanding and application of core satsang principles. 
 The shibirs were separated into four age groups, allowing young and old to learn according to their interests, capacity, and needs.
 The Bal-Balika Sevak Training Summer Camp (for 8- to 13-year-olds) was held from 14 to 20 August, with over 110 selected children, supported by 40 volunteers. Themed on the four mahavakyas of Shastriji Maharaj, the shibir helped to develop a stronger identity, firm conviction in Akshar-Purushottam upasana, and a deeper jodaan (spiritual connection) with Mahant Swami Maharaj for all the delegates.
 The Kishore-Kishori Shibir (for 14- to 22-year-olds) was held from 16 to 18 August. It attracted more than 630 enthusiastic youths for a four-day youth convention that immersed them in the life and legacy of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, whose sacrifices secured the eternal siddhant of Akshar-Purushottam for generations to come.
 The Yuvak-Yuvati Shibir (for 23- to 35-year-olds) was held from 14 to 17 August, in which around 850 yuvaks and yuvatis participated. Inspired by Mahant Swami Maharaj’s Diwali ashirwad, the shibir guided participants to move from understanding prapti (what we have attained) to cultivating pratiti (unshakeable conviction). 
 The Sanyukta Shibir (for over-35s) was held twice – from 22 to 24 August and 24 to 26 August – to accommodate the more than 2,300 delegates. During the shibir, they were carried on a spiritual journey from vichār (understanding) to vishwās (faith), and priti (love), culminating in pratiti (unwavering conviction) of having attained Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit Satpurush. In addition, over 300 children participated in the Satsang Diksha playgroups.
 Parasmani: Realising Our Supreme Attainment | Sanyukta Mandal Shibir 2025, UK & Europe 
 22 Aug 2025
 Over 22-24 August and 24-26 August 2025, more than 2,300 participants from Sanyukta Mandal across the UK and parts of Europe gathered at Warwick Conference Centre for an inspiring and transformative shibir titled “Parasmani: Praptini Pratiti” – Conviction in Our Supreme Attainment. 
 Parasmani: Discover, Believe, Experience | Yuvak-Yuvati Shibir 2025, UK & Europe 
 14 Aug 2025
 From Thursday 14 August to Sunday 17 August 2025, around 850 yuvaks and yuvatis from around the UK and parts of Europe gathered at Warwick Conference Park for their annual satsang shibir, themed “Parasmani: Discover, Believe, Experience.” 
 For the Sake of Akshar-Purushottam | Kishore-Kishori Shibir 2025, UK & Europe 
 23 Aug 2025
 Over 630 kishores and kishoris from across the UK and Europe gathered at Warwick University for a four-day journey of faith, learning, and inspiration. Themed “For the Sake of Akshar-Purushottam,” this year’s shibir immersed delegates into the life and legacy of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, whose sacrifices secured the eternal siddhant of Akshar-Purushottam for generations to come.
 Satsangnā Pāyā | Bal-Balika Sevak Training Summer Camp 2025, UK & Europe 
 14 Aug 2025
 Rooted in the guiding theme of ‘Satsangnā Pāyā,’ the Bal-Balika Sevak Training (BST) Summer Camp for 2025 was held from Thursday 14 August to Wednesday 20 August at Warwick Conference Park and BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.

During his stay, in addition to the daily morning and evening satsang discourses on a wide range of topics, many other inspiring and enlightening programs were held.
 On 14 January, the Makar Sankranti (Uttarayan) and Jholi Utsav celebration was held in his presence.

In the early evening, senior representatives of many Gujarati, Marwadi and Telugu associations in Hyderabad came to meet Pujya Viveksagar Swami.
