/News/2025/Satsang-Vicharan-in-South-Cen.t: Satsang Vicharan in South Central America, Guyana
/News/2025/Satsang-Vicharan-in-South-Cen.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Trinidad & Tobago (4 photos)
 Guyana (10 photos)
 Chile (5 photos)
 Panama (4 photos)
 With the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Pujya Priyasevadas Swami and Pujya Bhaktiswarupdas Swami embarked on their Satsang vicharan (spiritual tour) across South America from November 25 - December 4, 2025. This vicharan was specially organized to bring the values of Hinduism to devotees living far away, offering them renewed spiritual strength, cultural pride, and a deeper connection to Sanatan Dharma.
 During this vicharan, the BAPS Swamis visited four countries including Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana, Chile, and Panama. In each place, they conducted Satsang sabhas (spiritual assemblies) that encouraged spiritual growth, and moral living. Each assembly began with kirtan-bhakti (devotional singing), filling the atmosphere with heartfelt bhajans which created a deeply devotional and uplifting spiritual mood. Drawing from the timeless teachings of the Bhagavad Gita, Pujya Priyasevadas Swami shared thoughtful discourses that helped us empathize with Arjun to see how his struggles are like our own. He explained how we can rise above similar challenges through endurance, a steady mind and a strong connection with God. He also shared practical examples to show how to stay spiritually grounded amid the pressures of modern life.
 Highlights:
 Trinidad & Tobago:
 In Port of Spain, Pujya Swamis graced a satsang assembly of over 75 devotees, where heartfelt kirtans and uplifting discourses deepened everyone’s faith and connection to satsang. Devotees were especially touched to see how practical the Bhagavad Gita is and how its teachings speak directly to their daily lives.
 Guyana:
 Pujya Swamis’ visit to Georgetown was marked by a Satsang sabha with over 125 attendees. During the sabha, the swamis warmly welcomed Amit Telang, the High Commissioner of India to Guyana, along with Dr. Ashani Singh, the Finance Minister of Guyana. Deeply moved by the spiritual discourses, Dr. Singh shared that the messages inspired him to do his very best in his financial role, seeing this as a way to truly fulfill his dharma (duty) to the country. He also echoed the event’s core message that people should always put God first and recognize divine grace in every success, rather than getting lost in the chaos of purely material pursuits.
 Chile:
 Pujya Swamis’ third visit to Santiago was met with great joy as they conducted a Satsang sabha with over 80 devotees. During the assembly, Francisco, a local resident, was deeply moved by the devotion he witnessed and offered his heartfelt bhakti by accompanying the singing of bhajans on the tabla. Pujya Swamis also blessed the homes and businesses of devotees in the area.
 Panama:
 In Panama, Pujya Swamis began their vicharan with a focused spiritual assembly, inspiring them to strengthen values of seva(service), unity, and steadfast Satsang in their daily lives. Panama also served as the final stop of this vicharan, where the swamis graced a grand sabha of over 200 devotees. Pujya Priyasevadas Swami delivered discourses based on Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami’s Swamini Vato, offering powerful guidance for living a steady, value-centered life, while Pujya Bhaktiswarupdas Swami spoke especially to the youth on how to preserve their Hindu identity and maintain unity amongst one another.

/News/2025/Satsangn%C4%81-P%C4%81y%C4%81.t: Satsangnā Pāyā | Bal-Balika Sevak Training Summer Camp 2025, UK & Europe
/News/2025/Satsangn%C4%81-P%C4%81y%C4%81.text:
Rooted in the guiding theme of ‘Satsangnā Pāyā’, the Bal-Balika Sevak Training (BST) Summer Camp for 2025 was held from Thursday 14 August to Wednesday 20 August at Warwick Conference Park and BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.
 More than 110 balaks and balikas, supported by 40 dedicated karyakars, gathered for seven days of learning, bonding, and spiritual enrichment.
 The camp centred on the four mahavakyas of Shastriji Maharaj, with each day delving into the core takeaways explained by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Through interactive sessions, activities, and group discussions, the children learned how to develop unflinching faith in Akshar-Purushottam upasana and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Each day blended structured learning with fun and creativity. A lively treasure hunt, sports session, and a video project on Shastriji Maharaj’s mandirs encouraged teamwork while consolidating a deeper understanding of his legacy.
 Delegates also had the rare opportunity of engaging in interactive Q&A sessions with Atmatruptdas Swami and Dharmasetudas Swami, who shared personal guidance that inspired the bal-balika sevaks.
 The outings brought the camp’s lessons to life. The balaks journeyed to Ashridge Estate, where they completed a scavenger hunt in which they followed Shastriji Maharaj in a journey to propagate Akshar-Purushottam upasana. Joined by Atmatruptdas Swami, they reflected on Shastriji Maharaj’s courage and conviction. Meanwhile, the balikas explored Central London through a scavenger hunt of their own, visiting historical places that have been sanctified by our gurus. They completed fun yet meaningful challenges that encouraged teamwork, strengthened friendships, and deepened their appreciation for samp, suhradbhav, and ekta.
 The evenings were filled with preparatory sessions for the much-anticipated “BST’s Got Talent” showcase. The children exhibited their abilities, from music and dance to skits and storytelling.
 The camp concluded at London Mandir with a finale programme that recapped the year, highlighted the most memorable moments of the camp, and shared final blessings and insights from the senior swamis. It was a fitting close to a week of inspiration, fun, and growth.
 Through seven transformative days, the children left with a stronger identity, firm conviction in Akshar-Purushottam upasana, and a deeper jodaan (spiritual connection) with their guru, Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/News/2025/Shila-Pujan-Ceremony-of-BAPS-.t: Shila Pujan Ceremony of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Boston, MA, USA
/News/2025/Shila-Pujan-Ceremony-of-BAPS-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shila Pujan Ceremony (44 photos)
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Tyngsborough, Massachusetts, marked a historic milestone with the celebration of the Shila Pujan -  the sacred foundation-laying ceremony for the new mandir serving the Boston area. Satsang in the region began in early 1990 with weekly assemblies held in devotees’ homes and local venues. Later that same year, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated a mandir, nurturing a growing spiritual community. Over the decades, this steady growth has inspired the development of a larger mandir to meet the needs of the expanding Hindu community in the Boston area.
 On October 11, 2025, more than 1,000 devotees and well-wishers gathered for the Shila Pujan, which was graced by Pujya Nilkanthsevadas Swami and other revered swamis. Traditional Vedic rituals included devotees placing sanctified bricks and rice into the foundation, symbolizing unity, devotion, and the spiritual grounding of the new mandir.
 The Shila Pujan vidhi, the ritual sanctifying the foundation stones, was initiated by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj on August 23, 2025, in Himmatnagar, Gujarat. On September 7, 2025, Pujya Bhaktipriyadas Swami also sanctified the Shila in Robbinsville, New Jersey.
 The celebration also featured a vibrant Annakut offering, with hundreds of vegetarian delicacies lovingly presented to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Gunatitanand Swami. Volunteers from across New England joined with devotion to make the occasion memorable and inspiring.
 BAPS Mandirs stand as a beacon of faith and service—nurturing values, strengthening character, and uplifting communities. Grounded in timeless spirituality, they inspire individuals to live with purpose, harmony, and compassion. In addition to its spiritual offerings, daily darshan, arti, discourses, and weekly satsang assemblies, the mandir fosters holistic growth through youth activities, sports, and classes in language, music, and dance, all designed to promote leadership, culture, and service. Through BAPS Charities, the mandir also serves the broader community with initiatives such as annual walkathons benefiting local organizations, including the police and fire departments, as well as a local food pantry, along with food and blood donation drives, health fairs, and other humanitarian efforts.
 Together, the Shila Pujan Mahotsav and Annakut Utsav reflected the enduring values of faith, community, and service, marking a meaningful step forward in the journey of the new mandir.

/News/2025/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti-%E2.text:
To celebrate the auspicious birth anniversaries of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram, devotees gathered with great devotion and enthusiasm. This year’s celebration was themed "Maano Chaitanya Rup Tamaaru", highlighting the divine tools that Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram have bestowed upon humanity to conquer the ongoing inner battle against negative swabhavs (intrinsic tendencies).
 Ram Bhagwan’s victory over Ravan in the Ramayan serves as a profound metaphor for the internal struggle individuals face against their own swabhavs, such as arrogance, envy, and greed. Just as Ravan’s downfall stemmed from his unchecked negative tendencies, individuals must also overcome these inner obstacles to progress on the path of spiritual growth. The program emphasized that the battle between Ram and Ravan is not merely a historical event, but a timeless lesson encouraging self-improvement and righteousness.
 Bhagwan Swaminarayan introduced bhakti as a powerful medium to align one’s thoughts, words, and actions with God and Guru. Through the establishment of the Ekantik Satpurush lineage, mandirs, and the preservation of sacred scriptures and teachings, He laid a strong foundation for sustained spiritual progress. The program, through heartfelt testimonials, reinforced that by adhering to the teachings and commands of the Guru, individuals can overcome inner weaknesses, experience personal spiritual transformation, and foster harmony within their families and communities.Women of all ages actively participated in the celebrations, expressing their devotion through classical musical performances, traditional dances, engaging skits, and insightful discourses. The program served as a powerful reminder that the path to moksha, or liberation, is made possible through a deep connection with our Guru, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who continues to inspire and guide us with a practical approach to spiritual growth.

/News/2025/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Ram Navmi Celebrations 2025, North America
/News/2025/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.text:
Devotees across North America recently gathered at BAPS Mandirs to joyously celebrate the auspicious birth anniversaries of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram with the theme, “Unity Begins Within.” The celebration focused on the profound teachings of unity exemplified by both Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Ram through the four pillars of mahima (glory), milan (togetherness), madad (support), and maafi (forgiveness). Through these divine principles, attendees learned the importance of fostering unity within their families, communities, and spiritual lives.
 The program shared inspiring episodes from the Ramayan and Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s time that illustrated these pillars. The story of Bhagwan Ram and Shabri highlighted the power of mahima, as she saw divinity in Ram Bhagwan beyond societal norms. The bond between Sugriva and Bhagwan Ram demonstrated madad, showcasing how unity in purpose leads to victory. Mata Kaikeyi’s redemption was a testament to maafi, underscoring the transformative power of forgiveness. Similarly, Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s interactions with Dada Khachar, Jivan Koli, and Jhinabhai Thakor illustrated these virtues in action, guiding devotees on how to embody them in their own lives.
 Devotees of all ages participated in the program, which featured engaging elements including devotional musical performances, insightful skits, and videos that conveyed the essence of unity. Pujya Swamis delivered impactful discourses, elaborating on the four pillars and their relevance in strengthening unity. Through these teachings, devotees gained a deeper understanding of cultivating harmony in their relationships and overcoming challenges through spiritual wisdom.
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj exemplified these values, and today, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj continues to reinforce these teachings—reminding individuals that unity does not begin externally, but within each individual, through milan, madad, mahima, and maafi.

 Themed ‘Purushottam Pragati Re’, the programme provided an opportunity for thousands of devotees and guests to understand how Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Ramachandra were replete with all virtues, free from all faults, and the source of supreme bliss – drawing upon the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in Vachanamrut Gadhada III 10.
 Many of the mandirs and centres had children and youths present the vibrant programme through a colourful array of enlightening skits, vibrant dances, eloquent bhajans, and uplifting presentations that recreated defining moments from history. The performances were delivered across various thematic segments, each focusing on different aspects of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s and Bhagwan Rama’s life and teachings.
 Many mandirs and centres also offered an opportunity for darshan, pujan, and family photos with large images of Bal Prabhu Ghanshyam Maharaj and Shri Rama Lalla.
 The festivities concluded with the janmotsav arti for Bhagwan Shri Ramachandra and Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan.

/News/2025/Shri-Vikram-Misri-Indias-Fore.t: Shri Vikram Misri, India's Foreign Secretary overwhelmed by BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Shri-Vikram-Misri-Indias-Fore.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shri Vikram Misri Visits BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi (10 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi had the privilege of welcoming the Foreign Secretary of India, Shri Vikram Misri. His visit underscored the shared values of peace and partnership that define India’s engagement with the world, especially in the context of India-UAE relations.
 Shri Misri, accompanied by Aseem Raja Mahajan, Joint Secretary for Gulf Affairs, Ambassador Sanjay Sudhir and the members of his delegation, was welcomed with a sanctified garland at the Harmony Wall by Pujya Brahmavihari Swami, Head of BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi. 
 Shri Misri was spellbound by The Fairy Tale, an immersive experience that creatively conveys universal values of harmony, mutual respect, and cultural understanding through vibrant storytelling and historical reflections. Recounting Dr S. Jaishankar’s words, he mentioned the tale of the mandir is indeed a fairy tale.
 As he walked through the tranquil premises, he observed the symbolic Tolerance Trees, representing unity in diversity, and explored the key architectural and spiritual elements of the mandir.
 Swami Brahmaviharidas unfolded the profound symbolism woven into the Harmony Dome, illuminating its spiritual essence and universal message of harmony between the Divine and Humankind. Shri Misri revealed that each aspect of the mandir evoked deep reflections in him, unravelling layers of thoughtful symbolism with its ornate craftsmanship. Within the sanctum of the mandir, he offered reverent prayers at the seven inner shrines and paused in contemplative homage to the visionary guidance and spiritual legacy of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, whose divine foresight gave rise to this monumental beacon of faith and harmony.
 Expressing his feelings, he said, “I have had a thousand blessings today. This is not just a building; it is an expression of faith, beliefs, and ideas that are transcendental. The Mandir unites not just different streams of faith but the entire humanity. It is miraculous...my mind and heart are overflowing...it is a mandir deserving of the greatest accolades...and will be spoken about for generations. People may think it is for religion, but it is something for the world, for humanity, for our universal existence....It is a Mandir every Indian must visit.”
 Shri Misri commended its engineering, architectural brilliance and the values the mandir embodies, describing the mandir as “a global symbol of interfaith harmony and cultural dialogue.” He remarked that such places of devotion, built through international collaboration and inspired leadership, can play a powerful role in uniting people across boundaries.
 Shri Misri offered earnest prayers for the enduring prosperity, visionary leadership and friendship of both India's Prime Minister, Narendra Modi and His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the UAE. He expressed profound gratitude for His Highness’s steadfast support in bringing the mandir to life—an emblem of shared values, bridging hearts and cultures across the globe.

 Photo Gallery 
 Nakkar Vidwan Shibir (45 photos)
 Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Chhavani (20 photos)
 Children who have memorized all 315 verses of Satsang Diksha and all 565 verses of the Siddhant Karika, totaling 880 verses, can enroll in the special Siddhant Sarvasvam course, conducted by the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute.
 On June 2 and 3, 71 boys and 103 girls who have memorized the Siddhant Karika, participated in the Siddhant Sarvasvam Shibir at the BAPS Mandir in Sankari. Based on Mahant Swami Maharaj’s inspirational letter to the children, the central theme of the shibir was 'Nakkar Vidwan'.
 The shibir focused on four key points: understanding the meanings of the shlokas, comprehending the Akshar-Purushottam Siddhant, explaining the Akshar-Purushottam Siddhant to others, and strengthening personal practice of niyam-dharma and satsang samjan.
 These topics were covered through enlightening talks by swamis, interactive activities, engaging workshops, and creative presentations. The children also participated in discussions and Q&A sessions with senior swamis, gaining inspiration for academic and spiritual progress.
 On 4 June, the children had Swamishri’s puja darshan in Kanad, Surat, during which they recited memorized shlokas. Throughout the day, the children participated in an Akshar-Purushottam Chhavani in which they presented on various topics related to the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan.
 In the evening assembly, Swamishri blessed the children through a fascinating Q&A session. Also, the Karikajayi boys and Karikajayini girls were honored. Additionally, those who achieved top ranks in the Siddhant Sarvasvam course were recognized.
 Through this shibir and assembly, the children got great academic strength and spiritual inspiration.

/News/2025/Silver-Jubilee-30769.aspx.t: Silver Jubilee Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, San Antonio, TX, USA
/News/2025/Silver-Jubilee-30769.aspx.text:
The Silver Jubilee of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in San Antonio, Texas, was a heartfelt celebration marking 25 years of devotion, unity, and community. From humble beginnings—when weekly services were held in devotees’ homes—the Satsang in San Antonio has blossomed into a vibrant mandir where generations have found peace, purpose, and connection through the blessings of HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj and HH Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj consecrated the murtis on September 1–2, 2000, at the original mandir location, formally establishing the Satsang in San Antonio. A decade later, on October 9, 2010, Sadgur Pujya Doctor Swami performed the Murti Pratishta Vidhi for the current mandir, once again blessing the community and inspiring its continued spiritual growth.
 The Silver Jubilee celebrations began on August 16, 2025, with Mahila Din, themed “Sacho Maliyo Che Satsang.” Women of all ages came together through soulful performances and heartfelt reflections, expressing gratitude for the gift of God and guru. Their devotion and unity reflected the strength and grace that have long helped shape the heart of the mandir.
 On October 4, 2025, the community gathered for a Mahapuja—the centerpiece of the Silver Jubilee celebrations. Devotees filled the mandir with prayers, devotion, and memories of the 25-year journey, celebrating not only a milestone but also the shared spirit that continues to guide the community forward. As Pujya Krishnaprem Swami beautifully expressed: “God hungers for devotion. One is measured not by wealth, but by the sincerity of one’s heart; through your heartfelt devotion, God has become pleased.” He further shared, “All that we have belongs to God, and it is only to Him that we offer it; through this Rajat Jayanti, our devotion itself has become our offering.”
 The Silver Jubilee was a reminder that while the mandir stands as a place of worship, its true foundation lies in the hearts of devotees who have built it with love, seva, and unwavering faith. The mandir also continues to serve as a pillar of community service—bringing people together to give back through annual walkathons supporting local charities, health fairs, food and blood donation drives, and countless acts of seva that uplift the wider community. This celebration not only honored the past 25 years, but also set the stage for the mandir’s continued role in inspiring faith and service for decades to come.

 History (36 photos)
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Levittown, PA, celebrated its Silver Jubilee with a series of events centered on the theme “My Mandir, My Home.” The events reflected the Mandir’s enduring role as a spiritual and cultural home, highlighting its impact on the community and the inspiration that has guided its growth since its inauguration by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj on August 20, 2000.
 The festivities began on June 28, 2025, with the Women’s Cultural Celebration, “Yeh Mandir Mera.” More than 225 participants from toddlers to elders, shared heartfelt reflections, skits, and performances that emphasized how the Mandir has shaped spiritual journeys while empowering women in academics, careers, and family life.
 The celebration continued with a Parivarik Ekta Mahapuja on July 12–13, where families from across the region gathered to offer prayers together. This collective worship reinforced unity, devotion, and a shared commitment to fostering peace throughout the world.
 On September 19, swamis and youths filled the Mandir with uplifting devotional melodies during a Kirtan Aradhana. The following morning, September 20, began with a vibrant Nagar Yatra. Women devotees led the colorful procession through the streets, carrying sacred murtis and singing kirtans, spreading joy and devotion throughout the community. That evening, the concluding Cultural Program, “My Mandir, My Home,” brought the jubilee celebrations to life through dramas, dances, multimedia presentations, and personal testimonies that highlighted how the Mandir has guided and enriched multiple generations over the past 25 years.
 Special guests in attendance included U.S. Representative Brian Fitzpatrick, State Representatives Jim Prokopiak and Tina Davis, Senators Frank Farry and Steve Santarsiero, Bucks County District Attorney Jennifer Schron, Commissioners Robert Harvie and Gene DiGirolamo, Sheriff Fred Harran, Middletown Township Manager Eden Ratliff, Police Chief Joe Bartorilla, Bensalem Mayor Joseph DiGirolamo, Magisterial Judge Michael Gallagher, and local candidates Chelsey Jackman and Joe Pizzo. Their presence underscored the Mandir’s significance as a pillar of faith, culture, and service in the region.
 The Silver Jubilee of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Philadelphia, honored 25 years of devotion, community service, and spiritual growth. It celebrated the Mandir’s lasting influence on individuals and families while renewing its vision to guide and uplift future generations.

 History (30 photos)
 On August 19, 2000, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Beltsville, MD. Over the past 25 years, the Mandir has flourished as a spiritual home for devotees across the DC, Maryland, and Virginia region—serving as a center of devotion, cultural identity, and community service.
 To commemorate this milestone, the Mandir celebrated its Silver Jubilee from September 12 to 14, 2025, with a series of devotional and cultural programs.
 The celebrations began on the evening of Friday, September 12, with an uplifting Kirtan Aradhana that inspired reflection, devotion, and gratitude for the Mandir and Guru. On Saturday morning, September 13, families from across the region gathered for a collective Parivarik Ekta Mahapuja, strengthening unity and reaffirming shared spiritual values. That evening, youths and children presented a vibrant cultural program themed “Mandir: A Gift That Keeps Giving.” Through drama, dance, speeches, and music, they conveyed the Mandir’s enduring role as a home for all and a source of timeless values for future generations.
 On Sunday morning, September 14, devotees assembled for the sacred ‘Patotsav Ritual’, a sacred ceremony commemorating the anniversary of the murti consecration. Swamis performed the ceremonies in the presence of dignitaries, community leaders, and well-wishers.
 The three-day celebration concluded that afternoon with a heartfelt Women’s Celebration themed “Mandir: The Untold Stories,” honoring the devotion, sacrifice, and contributions of women in nurturing families and sustaining satsang through the generations.
 The Silver Jubilee was both a commemoration and a reflection—a time to look back on the Mandir’s remarkable journey from its humble beginnings in 2000 to its place today as a vibrant hub of satsang, seva, and unity. It also set the stage for the Mandir’s continued role in inspiring faith and service for decades to come.

 Following extensive renovations of the mandir premises, two days of celebrations marked the 25th anniversary and reconsecration ceremony of the BAPS Mandir in Raipur.
 On the morning of 29 November, more than 400 yajmans participated in the grand Vishwashanti Mahapuja with deep reverence.

 On the morning of 30 November, in the presence of over 500 devotees, the murtis were reconsecrated in the refurbished mandir.

/News/2025/Spiritual-Family-Retreat-2883.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Spiritual Family Retreat (48 photos)
 More than 90 devotees from Austria, Italy, Malta and Switzerland, as well as parts of southern France and Luxembourg, gathered at Sportcamp Melchtal in Switzerland from 11 to 13 July 2025 to participate in a spiritual family retreat.
 Sportcamp is a youth sports and family centre nestled in the picturesque Swiss hamlet of Melchtal amid the Melch valley of central Switzerland.
 The shibir, titled ‘Strengthening Families, Securing Futures’, was blessed by the presence of Gnanpriyadas Swami – a senior and learned swami visiting from the US – as well as four swamis from the UK.
 Themed around strengthening satsang within families, the spiritual retreat focused on deepening the understanding and application of core satsang practices. Across six sessions, attendees learned about daily puja, arti, thal, ghar sabha, and satsang reading. Each session was designed to provide practical guidance on how families can incorporate these devotional practices together in their homes and ghar mandirs.
 Various interactive mediums were used throughout the shibir, including discourses, videos, quizzes, panel discussions, group activities, and workshops. A samuh puja session encouraged many to grow stronger in their personal devotion and spiritual bond with God and the Guru.
 The shibir further included sessions emphasising the importance of daily listening to scriptural discourses (katha), attending weekly assemblies (sabha), and strengthening family harmony through collective devotion and shared activities.
 In addition to the spiritual sessions, participants enjoyed a picnic by Lake Melch, which included singing and offering thal, as well as outdoor activities such as walks, sports and games, creating a joyful and memorable experience for all the delegates.
 Reflecting on the shibir, Smit Thacker, a mother from Vienna, Austria, shared, “This retreat has really helped us understand the value of performing satsang activities as a family. It has brought us closer and inspired us to practise together regularly at home.”
 Atit Patel from Zurich, Switzerland, one of the lead volunteers for the event, added, “It was wonderful to see families from different countries come together and experience the joy of satsang. The teamwork and collective spirit throughout the retreat were truly inspiring, embodying Mahant Swami Maharaj’s profound wish of unity amongst us all and growing together spiritually.”
 The family retreat provided an invaluable opportunity for devotees to strengthen their spiritual bonds, learn practical ways to enhance their satsang, and create cherished memories together.

/News/2025/Swami-Padharya-Mare-Anganie-P.t: ‘Swami Padharya Mare Anganie’ Padhramani Project, Africa
/News/2025/Swami-Padharya-Mare-Anganie-P.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Swami Padharya Mare Anganie (76 photos)
 Under the guidance of the Satsang Pravrutti Central Office in Africa, over a period of 32 days, 88 BAPS swamis from India conducted over 11,110 padhramanis (home visits) to the homes of devotees and well-wishers. These visits were spread across 203 centers in 13 countries throughout Africa, under the auspices of the ‘Swami Padharya Mare Anganie’ project.
 The swamis conveyed Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s and Mahant Swami Maharaj’s message of ghar sabha as a means to strengthen family harmony by resolving family discord, enhancing communication, and reducing emotional disconnects. Each family was presented a one-year outline on what to do in their ghar sabha.
 The swamis contacted over 26,000 people and inspired many to quit addictions, take spiritual pledges, strengthen their Hindu faith, and participate in performing social services. Also, over 7,710 families pledged to conduct a ghar sabha regularly.
 In each center the swamis visited, they also conducted satsang assemblies and discussion sessions with karyakars.
 The devotees also enthusiastically welcomed the swamis to their homes and agreed to sincerely fulfil their pledges.

 The Telugu New Year, Ugadi, was celebrated with great devotion at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Secunderabad.
 Telugu devotees were warmly welcomed with the traditional drink, ‘pachadi’.
 Prayers for a happy and prosperous New Year for all were offered through abhishek of Shri Nilkanth Varni and recitation of Sahajanand Namavali. Also, an Annakut of South Indian vegetarian delicacies was offered before the murtis at Secunderabad Mandir.

 During the afternoon Sunday Satsang assembly, swamis gave inspiring discourses and a motivational video was presented in Telugu.

/News/2025/TennesseeHonor-28772.aspx.t: Tennessee State Honors BAPS and Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami for Global Spiritual Leadership and Humanitarian Impact, Atlanta, GA, USA
/News/2025/TennesseeHonor-28772.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Tennessee State Honors BAPS and Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami (9 photos)
 The State of Tennessee formally recognized the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami through Senate Joint Resolution No. 442. The resolution honored BAPS’s global spiritual leadership and humanitarian impact, and recognized Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami for spearheading the creation of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi—one of the most pivotal landmarks for establishing global peace in modern history. He was also acknowledged for coordinating vast volunteer relief during the 2001 Bhuj earthquake, leading humanitarian support throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, and establishing relief camps that served war refugees during the Ukraine-Russia conflict—all carried out under the guidance and blessings of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, whose lifelong messages of devotion, service, and harmony continue to guide Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami’s efforts.
 Reflecting the deep respect held for him across the state, Governor Bill Lee extended a warm welcome through his Senior Advisor, John DeBerry, and House Representative Mark Sparks, who traveled to Atlanta to personally honor Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami during a large spiritual assembly of over 2,000 people titled “In Conversation”, which also included government dignitaries from across the state of Georgia.
 This recognition highlights the strong alignment between Tennessee's core values and BAPS’s guiding principles of selfless service, unity, and uplifting all individuals. This esteemed acknowledgment not only strengthens the relationship between BAPS and the State of Tennessee but also underscores their mutual commitment to building a better world through shared respect and collaborative spirit.

/News/2025/The-Global-Justice-Love-and-P.t: The Global Justice, Love, and Peace Summit 2025, Dubai, UAE
/News/2025/The-Global-Justice-Love-and-P.text:
Photo Gallery 
 The Global Justice, Love, and Peace Summit (21 photos)
 Around 1,200 delegates from the world over attended ‘The Global Justice, Love, and Peace Summit’, a unique peace summit organized by the ‘I am Peacekeeper Movement’ at the EXPO 2020 venue in Dubai. The delegates included a galaxy of Nobel laureates, celebrities, leaders, thinkers, and speakers.
 Among the Nobel laureates present were human rights activist Abdessattar Ben Moussa, educationist Houcine Abbasi, Jose Ramos Horta, President of East Timor, Indian social activist Kailash Satyarthi, Lech Walesa, former President of Poland, Leymah Gbowee from Liberia, Mohamed Fadhel Mahfoudh, President of the Tunisian Order of Lawyers, and others.
 In his address, HE Sheikh Nahayan Mabarak Al Nahyan, Minister of Tolerance and Co- existence, said, “It will be our wisdom that will strengthen peace among nations and will promote and ensure respect and human rights for everyone. It will be our wisdom that will allow us to resolve conflicts through peaceful means.”
 Speaking at the summit, Head of BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, Swami Brahmaviharidas said, "The role of faith leaders in promoting peace and harmony is critical. My spiritual master, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj prayed for and envisioned a mandir in Abu Dhabi that bridges countries, cultures, and religions. Today, the BAPS Hindu Mandir has become a spiritual oasis for global harmony. With over 70,000 people stepping forward to lay a brick during the construction of the mandir, the journey itself was one of harmony. In the past year, over 2.5 million people from all over the world, of all religions, races, and cultures have visited. Since its completion, the mandir has developed into a place of spiritual refuge for world peace, where people come to pray and leave with greater joy and love for themselves and others. The mandir itself is the proof that religions can coexist, that countries can help one another, that culture is no longer a point of conflict, but the creation of cohesion. Let us professionally and passionately breathe more harmony in our families, in our society, and in our daily lives.”
 Dr. Huzaifa Khorakiwala, Chairman of the ‘I am Peacekeeper Movement’, reinforced the call for a peaceful and just world through a Peace Charter – 'A Love Letter to Humanity' – which will be presented to the United Nations. The joint Peace Charter preamble stated: “Peace is not merely the absence of conflict but the presence of justice, love, and peace, committed to upholding the principles that foster harmony, progress, and human equality for all.”
 The two-day conference created positive energy across all sections of society.

/News/2025/The-Great-British-Spring-Clea.t: The Great British Spring Clean, UK
/News/2025/The-Great-British-Spring-Clea.text:
Volunteers from 18 BAPS mandirs and centres around the UK took to the streets to help clean up and rejuvenate their local neighbourhoods.
 The volunteers filled more than 150 bags containing various forms of litter, significantly improving the surrounding environment.
 The initiative was part of The Great British Spring Clean, the nation’s largest mass-action environmental campaign in which thousands of individuals, groups and schools come together around the country to participate.
 The annual event is organised by Keep Britain Tidy, a leading independent environmental charity that works to inspire, educate and enable everyone in the country to value the environment on their doorstep. 
 In many places, BAPS volunteers were joined by local councillors, well-wishers and residents, who were grateful to BAPS for helping improve the local neighbourhood.
 One local resident in Leicester commented, “Keep up the great work! It's great to see your volunteers at work in the community.”
 The community outreach initiative was inspired by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who has taught to respect and care for the environment and to serve local communities as part of a wider social responsibility.

/News/2025/The-Holistic-12-Week-BAPS-wel.t: The Holistic 12-Week BAPS wellNESS Programme, UK
/News/2025/The-Holistic-12-Week-BAPS-wel.text:
BAPS Charities UK recently completed its inaugural 12-week wellNESS programme, a community-based initiative aimed at addressing health disparities among British South Asians, who face elevated risks of diabetes, heart disease, and mental health challenges.
 Rooted in lifestyle medicine and inspired by the spiritual guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the programme was held at Neasden Temple, London, integrating science, culture, and spirituality in a trusted environment.
 A Holistic Model: N.E.S.S.
 The programme focused on four key lifestyle pillars:
 Nutrition: Participants learned about macro- and micronutrients through cooking demonstrations and meal-planning aligned with a sattvic vegetarian diet.
 Exercise: Weekly sessions included group workouts, yoga, and strategies for managing pain and incorporating movement into daily routines.
 Sleep: Emphasis was placed on mindful bedtime routines and enhancing focus, including the role of cheshta.
 Stress: Emotional well-being was supported through mindfulness, satsang practices, and peer support.
 Delivered by a dedicated team of volunteer healthcare professionals – including GPs, psychiatrists, psychologists, physiotherapists, and nutritionists – the programme welcomed 41 participants aged 34 to 61, offering interactive, in-person education tailored to cultural and spiritual values.
 Faith as a Foundation
 Spirituality played a central role in promoting health. Participants explored how faith and Satsang can support well-being, for example, by reciting shlokas before eating to encourage mindful eating, following spiritual disciplines (niyam dharma), and making small, consistent habit changes inspired by the guidance of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Measured Impact
 Pre- and post-programme assessments revealed significant improvements:
 Physical health: Reductions in cholesterol, HbA1C (blood glucose), weight, waist circumference, body fat, blood pressure, and resting heart rate
 Mental well-being: Increased openness around emotional health and reduced symptoms of depression
 Lifestyle habits: Healthier eating, improved hydration, and increased physical activity with better strength, flexibility, and balance
 Community connection: Stronger social bonds and peer support
 Some of these findings were also presented between 18 to 20 September 2025 at the British Society of Lifestyle Medicine Conference in Brighton.   
 Participant Reflections
 Feedback from the participants highlighted the programme’s cultural relevance and transformative impact. Nimisha Patel shared, “When I’ve done other health programmes, it’s been quite difficult to follow and to stay consistent because the suggestions they give don’t really align with our values and our diet. But from the BAPS wellNESS programme, I’ve found a community that I didn’t know I was missing. I feel like I have gained not only spiritual health from coming to the Mandir, but it has helped me focus on my physical and my mental health as well.”
 Others added: “I have chronic neuropathy in both legs. From Day 1, I was encouraged to exercise. Now, just 10–15 minutes of daily yoga has helped me regain my balance. I have tried many other things over the years, but nothing really worked. I wish we had started wellNESS 10-15 years ago; I would be in much better health today.”
 “This programme changed my well-being. Start this with children early – it’ll prevent future health issues.”
 “The content was digestible and motivating, which has helped me stay committed to my fitness goals.”
 “After months of depression, I followed advice from the sessions and felt better – enough to book a hair appointment after six months!”
 “The team have done a fantastic job with this programme, and so much effort and thinking have gone into this. I would recommend it to everyone.”
 Looking Ahead
 The success of this pilot demonstrates the power of a community-driven, culturally sensitive approach to long-term health. By combining evidence-based education with the strength of Satsang, BAPS Charities plans to expand the wellNESS programme to other mandirs and communities, inspiring healthier, more balanced lives.

/News/2025/Their-Majesties-King-Charles-.t: Their Majesties King Charles and Queen Camilla Visit Neasden Temple, London, UK
/News/2025/Their-Majesties-King-Charles-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Visit (60 photos)
 Interactions (30 photos)
 History (20 photos)
 Their Majesties King Charles III and Queen Camilla visited BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – to mark the Mandir’s 30th anniversary, coinciding with Diwali and the Hindu New Year celebrations.
 Their Majesties were welcomed by Jitu Patel, Chair of the Board of Trustees. This was His Majesty’s first visit to the Mandir as monarch, following previous visits as the Prince of Wales, and Her Majesty’s third visit, reflecting the Royal Family’s longstanding and warm relationship with the Mandir and the BAPS Hindu community.
 Since its opening in 1995, Neasden Temple has become an internationally acclaimed spiritual and cultural landmark, welcoming millions of visitors and worshippers from around the world and contributing to British society through initiatives in child and youth development, elderly welfare, health, and humanitarian relief.
 Their Majesties were welcomed with flower garlands before proceeding to the Mandir’s upper sanctum, later pausing beneath the carved domes to appreciate the tranquillity and craftsmanship. After this brief reflection, His Majesty was introduced to the resident swamis, who greeted him warmly with folded hands in the traditional Hindu manner.
 During their visit, Their Majesties met volunteers and community members and learned about the Temple’s charitable work, including its longstanding partnership with The Felix Project – a London-based charity that redistributes surplus food to alleviate hunger for the vulnerable – which also forms a part of His Majesty’s Coronation Food Project.
 Along their tour, Their Majesties also learned about the upcoming BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris – the first traditional Hindu temple in France – opening next September, while meeting key members of the project team.
 Several distinguished guests, including peers, Members of Parliament, councillors, mayors, industry leaders as well as various faith representatives and Hindu community leaders and members had joined the assembly to welcome Their Majesties and celebrate the joyous occasion.
 Addressing the congregation, Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of the Temple, remarked, “It was an honour for the community to welcome Their Majesties to Neasden Temple on this historic occasion. We are deeply grateful for their friendship and their continuing interest in our services for the community.”
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj conveyed his prayers and blessings through a letter as well as a video message sent from India. He said, “Though I cannot be present, my heart and prayers are with you and the Royal Family. Pramukh Swami Maharaj would be delighted to see you here on this occasion. It is a personal delight to welcome you, as for many years in my teachings I have drawn upon your words from a speech you delivered in 1991, in which you said: ‘The most urgent need for Western man is to rediscover that divine element in his being, without which there can never be any possible hope or meaning to our existence in this earthly realm.’ That insight has stayed with me.”
 As Their Majesties departed, they expressed their appreciation for the devotion and selfless service of the volunteers whose efforts sustain the Mandir’s spiritual and community life throughout the year.

/News/2025/UNESCOs-Recognition-of-Deepav.t: UNESCO’s Recognition of Deepavali at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Houston, TX, USA
/News/2025/UNESCOs-Recognition-of-Deepav.text:
Photo Gallery 
 UNESCO’s Recognition of Deepavali (19 photos)
 In a radiant display of culture and community pride, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Houston hosted a special gathering to mark a historic milestone: the inclusion of Deepavali in UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on December 10, 2025. Hosted alongside the Consul General of India, Houston, the evening brought together civic leaders, members of the judiciary, and community representatives to celebrate this global recognition of the Festival of Lights.
 Much like the lights of Deepavali themselves, the event served as a beacon of unity, highlighting how this ancient tradition continues to illuminate the path of knowledge, righteousness, and spiritual awakening for millions around the world.
 The celebration was graced by a distinguished group of attendees who joined in honoring this cultural triumph. Among the notable guests were the Mayor of Missouri City, Robin Elackatt, and the Mayor of Stafford, Ken Matthews, reflecting the strong local support for the Mandir’s cultural initiatives.
 The judiciary was also well-represented, with Judge Juli Matthew and Judge Surendran Pattel in attendance, underscoring the deep integration of the Indian diaspora into the fabric of American civic life. They were joined by numerous other community leaders, all gathered to witness this moment of shared heritage.
 A key highlight of the evening was the commemoration of Deepavali’s new status as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. The Consul General of India, Houston, addressed the gathering and reflected on the significance of this designation. It is not merely a recognition of a festival, but a global acknowledgement of the values Deepavali represents — the victory of light over darkness and good over evil.
 Guests were welcomed into the serene atmosphere of the Mandir, a testament to traditional Hindu architecture and devotion. The backdrop of the Mandir offered a meaningful setting to reflect on the preservation of these traditions, and the light and sound show added to the commemoration of the evening.
 The gathering concluded with a shared sense of pride and purpose. More than a celebration, it was a reaffirmation of the enduring power of culture to bridge communities. As Deepavali now takes its place on the global stage through UNESCO, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Houston remains committed to preserving these traditions and fostering a spirit of unity and service in the wider community.

/News/2025/US-Vice-President-JD-Vance-Vi.t: US Vice President JD Vance Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India
/News/2025/US-Vice-President-JD-Vance-Vi.text:
Photo Gallery 
 US Vice President JD Vance Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham (12 photos)
 The Vice President of the United States, Mr. JD Vance, began his maiden official visit to India with a spiritually enriching visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. He was joined by his wife, Second Lady Usha Vance, and their three children – Ewan, Vivek, and Mirabel.
 Upon arrival, the Vance family received a traditional Indian welcome with flower garlands and friendship threads, symbolizing goodwill and unity. On behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, spiritual leader of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, senior swamis Dharmavatsaldas Swami, Brahmaviharidas Swami, and Gnanmunidas Swami warmly greeted the Vice President.
 The family was guided through the Akshardham complex, gaining insights into India’s ancient cultural and spiritual heritage of faith, peace, selfless service, and family unity, which the complex embodies through its architecture and exhibitions.
 Vice President Vance was presented a personal letter of blessings and prayers from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The letter expressed heartfelt gratitude for the visit and special prayers for the well-being of the Vice President and his family, as well as for the continued unity and progress of the United States of America.
 As a gesture of friendship, the Vance family was presented with several commemorative gifts, including a model of the Swaminarayan Akshardham mandir, intricately carved wooden elephants, literature about the Swaminarayan Akshardham campuses in New Delhi and Robbinsville (USA), and value-based illustrated storybooks for their children. A framed family photograph taken in front of the mandir was also presented as a special memento.
 Reflecting on the experience, Vice President JD Vance wrote in the guest book:
 “Thank you all so much for your hospitality and kindness in welcoming me and my family to this beautiful place. It is a great credit to India that you built a beautiful temple with precision and care. Our kids, in particular, loved it. God bless.”
 The special visit reflected the deep-rooted friendship and shared ideals between India and the United States. It also underscored the vital role of spiritual and cultural institutions in fostering and promoting dialogue, respect, and harmony between nations and traditions.

/News/2025/Union-Minister-Dharmendra-Pra.t: Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan Praises BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Union-Minister-Dharmendra-Pra.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan Praises BAPS Hindu Mandir (15 photos)
 Shri Dharmendra Pradhan, India’s Union Cabinet Minister of Education, visited the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, where he was traditionally welcomed with a garland.
 Reflecting on his visit, he shared: “Today, it is my good fortune that I have come to the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Abu Dhabi — an iconic creation that embodies India’s culture, spirituality, and consciousness. My bond with this Mandir runs deep. For many years I have walked alongside the Swaminarayan fellowship, bound by its spirit of seva, community, strength, and dedication.”
 The minister recalled how the idea of a Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi was not merely a thought but a vision foreseen by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and was brought to life by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj with the wholehearted support of  Prime Minister Narendrabhai Modi and remarkable generosity of the UAE’s rulers.
 The minister remarked that while mandirs grace many corners of the globe, this mandir “is more than stone and artistry; it is a message of harmony to humanity. Standing before its grandeur, I feel as if civilization itself has been restored — tradition anchored in the past, yet infused with every modern facility and detail that speaks to the present.”
 Calling the Mandir both an impossible miracle and a civilizational achievement, he expressed his deepest respects for the selfless seva of the swamis of BAPS. Sharing his sentiments, he said, “I am deeply fortunate to have had darshan at this Mandir and of all the deities within. My heart overflows with gratitude. India has not only proclaimed ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ — the world is one family — it has lived it.”
 He concluded by describing the Mandir as more than a place of worship: “It is a spiritual anchor and a civilizational landmark — a radiant creation of India’s timeless heritage that will inspire humanity for thousands of years to come. I once again offer my heartfelt gratitude to the BAPS community for gifting this masterpiece of harmony, faith, and civilization to the world.”

/News/2025/Unity-Forum-2025-BAPS-Shri-Sw.t: Unity Forum 2025, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania
/News/2025/Unity-Forum-2025-BAPS-Shri-Sw.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Unity Forum - 2025 (16 photos)
 Representatives from 33 Dharmik Indian communities attended the Unity Forum 2025 organized by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Tanzania, to celebrate cultural and spiritual harmony. Uniting under the theme ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – The World Is One Family’, the event was a powerful reminder of the shared heritage and values that bind together these communities living abroad, and emphasized the importance of unity in preserving and celebrating Indic traditions globally.
 The evening commenced with a spiritually uplifting performance by young children reciting prayers. Thereafter, revered swamis and respected community members, Kumarbhai Pujara, Malharbhai Dave, and Hirenbhai Chandarana, lit the ceremonial lamp.
 Then, Tyagvatsal Swami spoke eloquently on the joy and responsibility of living one’s culture even when far from its geographical roots. He stressed that unity is the foundation of collective success and inner peace, highlighting the timeless wisdom of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
 In his address, P. Priyavrat Swami reflected on the visible unity of the Hindu community in Tanzania. He noted with joy how nearly all Hindu temples in Dar es Salaam are situated in close proximity and how devotees of various communities come together to celebrate each other’s festivals with enthusiasm and mutual support. He emphasized that such unity is not only a source of strength today, but also a precious value that must be passed on to future generations for the continued growth and harmony of the community.
 Malharbhai Dave, President of the Hindu Council of Tanzania, addressed the gathering with gratitude, expressing appreciation for the initiative taken by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha to bring together so many communities to strengthen spiritual and cultural bonds across all Indic traditions. Kumarbhai Pujara, Chairman of BAPS, Dar es Salaam, delivered a heartfelt Vote of Thanks to all the communities for their wholehearted support during the Dar es Salaam Mandir Mahotsav held in December 2024.

/News/2025/Welcoming-and-Recognizing-the.t: Welcoming and Recognizing the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, Kathmandu, Nepal
/News/2025/Welcoming-and-Recognizing-the.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Welcoming and Recognizing the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan (32 photos)
 In a historic gathering near the sacred Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu, Nepal, scholars from across the country convened to formally recognize and honor the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, as revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The event was jointly organized by the Nepal Shikshan Parishad and the Nepal Pandit Mahasabha as part of a traditional scriptural assembly.
 During the assembly, the attending scholars enthusiastically welcomed and established the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan in Nepal’s intellectual and spiritual landscape. They also conferred the distinguished title ‘Vidya-Mahamanishi’ (Great Seeker of Knowledge) upon Mahamahopadhyaya Swami Bhadreshdas in recognition of his outstanding scholarship.
 The gathering was graced by some of Nepal’s foremost scholars and dignitaries, including:
 Dr. Ramkrishna Timalsina, President, Nepal Shikshan Parishad
 Shri Kashinath Nyaupane, renowned scholar and National Coordinator, World Sanskrit Conference
 Prof. Gullapalli Sriramakrishnamurti, Vice-Chancellor, Central Sanskrit University, Tirupati
 Prof. Sukanta Senapati, Vice-Chancellor, Shree Somnath Sanskrit University, Gujarat
 Prof. Dhaneshwar Nepal, Vice-Chancellor, Nepal Sanskrit University
 Dr. Vasudevkrishna Shastri, General Secretary, Nepal Shikshan Parishad and Member, Panchang Nirnayak Samiti
 Acharya Navaraj Kandel, Secretary, Jayatu Sanskritam
 At the start of the assembly, Prof. Kashinath Nyaupane declared, “Today, we wholeheartedly welcome, honor, and formally establish the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.”
 All scholars present affirmed this proclamation and individually offered their respects to the Swaminarayan commentaries (bhashyas) on the foundational texts of Vedant.
 In his keynote address, Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami delivered a precise, scripture-based exposition of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, drawing on the three foundational texts of Vedant – the Brahmasutras, Upanishads, and Bhagavad Gita.
 Both Dr. Ramkrishna Timalsina and Prof. Dhaneshwar Nepal emphasized that universities in Nepal should include the study of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan in their academic curricula.
 On this historic occasion, Bhadreshdas Swami and Atmatruptdas Swami personally honored and performed pujan of the attending scholars.

/News/2025/Where-Light-Meets-Devotion-Di.t: Where Light Meets Devotion: Diwali at BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2025/Where-Light-Meets-Devotion-Di.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Where Light Meets Devotion: Diwali at the BAPS Hindu Mandir (192 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi marked its second Diwali and Maha Annakut with several days of heartfelt celebrations, bringing together more than 60,000 devotees and visitors from the UAE and around the world in a spirit of community, devotion, and togetherness. Many experienced Diwali for the first time, appreciating a celebration that was new yet deeply welcoming.
 On 20 October, Diwali began with prayers and expressions of gratitude. Throughout the day, devotees arrived with family and friends to mark the auspicious occasion.
 That evening, during Sharda Pujan, hundreds of account books were sanctified with flower petals and rice grains amid the chanting of Vedic hymns and prayers for prosperity. 
 Swami Brahmaviharidas addressed the Sharda Pujan participants, “Let us begin every effort with prayer, pursue prosperity with integrity, and offer our work as seva. May knowledge guide our decisions, harmony shape our relationships, and divinity dwell in our daily duties.”
 He added, “We humbly acknowledge the vision and generosity of the Rulers of the UAE, especially His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose historic decision to grant the land for this Mandir made this spiritual and cultural landmark a reality. Their support continues to inspire a shared commitment to coexistence, harmony, and mutual respect.”
 On 22 October, marking the Hindu New Year, devotees arrived early to participate in the first arti of the year. An annakut of hundreds of vegetarian dishes was lovingly prepared and offered to the deities. 
 Over the weekend of 25 and 26 October, thousands visited the Mandir for darshan of the Maha Annakut. Before each of the Mandir’s seven shrines, hundreds of handmade, home-cooked food offerings were arranged in the form of sacred trees from across India:
 Neem – The Tree of Enlightenment before Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, represented the divine discourses of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in Gadhada
 Kadamba – The Tree of Divine Love before Shri Radha-Krishna, evoking Shri Krishna’s childhood lila
 Kalpavruksha – The Wish-Fulfilling Tree before Shri Jagannathji, symbolizing perfection
 Bilva – The Trinity Tree before Shri Shiv Parivar, representing purity and grace
 Ber – The Tree of Devotion before Shri Ram Parivar, invoking Shabri’s faith and patience; Banana – The Pious Plant before Shri Ayyappaji, reflecting simplicity
 Tulsi – The Sacred Plant before Shri Padmavati Srinivasji, signifying purity and bhakti
 The cultural programmes in the Abhishek Mandap and at the Ganga Ghat featuring devotional singing, chanting, and classical dance, added to the spirit of celebration and unity.

/News/2025/Womens-Celebration-of-HH-Maha.t: Women's Celebration of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj's 92nd Birthday, North America
/News/2025/Womens-Celebration-of-HH-Maha.text:
Women across North America joined together to celebrate the 92nd birthday of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The celebration was themed “Sadhutānā Himalay Mahant Swami Maharaj,” highlighting how the definition of sadhuta, or ideal saintliness, lives and breathes today through His Holiness. The program emphasized that Mahant Swami Maharaj embodies the qualities of a true sadhu and that this is the extraordinary prapti (spiritual attainment) that devotees have attained.
 The program reflected on how gurus Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj themselves recognized and expressed the greatness of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s saintliness, guiding devotees to follow in his footsteps. Through various presentations, women highlighted his gentle humility, profound purity, flowing compassion, universal equality, and unshakeable faith in Bhagwan. Each of these virtues revealed the depth of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s character and offered devotees insights into his divinity.
 Women of all ages participated in the celebration through cultural and devotional performances, including traditional dances, devotional singing, skits, and speeches. Each performance reflected heartfelt devotion and conveyed gratitude for the opportunity to celebrate such a divine figure.
 The celebration was a reminder that the presence of a true sadhu like Mahant Swami Maharaj provides constant guidance, compassion, and strength, illuminating the path of faith and spiritual growth for generations to come.

/News/2025/Womens-Day-Celebration-Yeh-Ma.t: Women's Day Celebration: ‘Yeh Mandir Mera’, Melbourne South, Melbourne, Australia
/News/2025/Womens-Day-Celebration-Yeh-Ma.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Women's Day (30 photos)
 Over 1,300 women of all ages attended the Women's Day celebration based on the theme ‘Yeh Mandir Mera’ – ‘This Is My Mandir’. This uplifting event honored the devotion and unwavering faith of women, and their contributions to building a mandir. The thoughtfully curated program highlighted self-control (saiyam), understanding (samjan), and dedication (samarpan) as the core principles that not only go into the construction of a mandir, but also as the qualities needed in every woman’s spiritual and everyday life.
 These values were vividly brought to life through a variety of engaging, insightful and inspiring videos, cultural performances and interviews. The presentations involved over 300 participants from five BAPS centres, demonstrating their unity, harmony, and friendship.
 A particularly impactful presentation involved a series of skits based on real-life scenarios that illustrated the practical application of Satsang Diksha shloka 152 – that Bhagwan is the all-doer ¬– in the everyday life of devotees.
 Another highlight was the fluent recitation of verses from the Satsang Diksha over 100 balikas.
 One of the most heartfelt presentations was by Riddhi Khatri, who shared the heartbreaking loss of her 5-year-old daughter. Despite their immense grief, Riddhi and her husband, rather than mourning on the day of the funeral, encouraged all to wear festive traditional clothing and celebrate the day. This powerful display of strength and faith reflected their deep trust in God and guru, reminding us that true spiritual understanding brings inner peace and joy.
 Among the distinguished guests present were Honorable Cassandra Fernando, Honorable Lily D’Ambrosio, Ms Pauline Richards MP, Ms Lauren Kathage MP, Ms Vivienne Nguyen, Dr. Karthika Hinduja, Senior Sergeant Katie Johnson, Sergeant Kim Gammon and Ms Manali Brahmbhatt. In their speeches, the esteemed guests highlighted the power of unity, faith, and perseverance, and the strength women bring to society.
 The occasion was a powerful reflection of women’s spiritual strength, their devotion, and their ability to build, nurture, and preserve not only mandirs, but also communities, families, and cultures.

/News/2025/Womens-Program-Making-a-Chait.t: Women's Program: Making a Chaitanya Mandir Within, Nairobi, Kenya
/News/2025/Womens-Program-Making-a-Chait.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Woman's program (63 photos)
 Over 1,700 women devotees from across Kenya gathered to celebrate the 25th Anniversary of the BAPS Mandir in Nairobi.
 Themed ‘Making a Mandir Within – Chaitanya Mandir’, the vibrant celebration focused on inner development. Presented by 325 participants from 9 BAPS centers (Athi River, Eldoret, Kericho, Kisumu, Mombasa, Nakuru, Nairobi, Ruiru and Thika), the program featured a compelling blend of cultural expressions, live stage dramas depicting resilience and empowerment, thought-provoking video presentations and enthralling cultural dances showcasing India’s rich culture. The event encouraged women to focus on spiritual growth, strengthen values and contribute positively to families and society.
 Among the chief guests were Mrs Kalpa Padia, Managing Director of Raka Cheese; Sujata Kotamraju, Hindu Council of Kenya Chairlady; Miss Nisha Hirani, Managing Director of ‘The Asian Weekly’; and Mrs Mona Wadhwana, wife of Deputy Indian High Commissioner to Kenya.
 Women from all walks of life shared heartfelt stories about how the spirit of selfless service, the preservation of traditional arts and culture, and the joy of divine bliss have enriched their lives. The event concluded with a lively finale dance celebrating the essence of the mandir in all its forms.

/News/2025/Yogi-Cup-Tournament-2025-2026.text:
The BAPS Yogi Cup Tournament, an annual sports event, united youths ages 14–30 from centers across North America. More than a competition, the tournament was rooted in the values of samp, suhradbhav, and ekta, inspired by Yogiji Maharaj. These principles shaped the atmosphere of the event, bringing together geographically dispersed kishores and yuvaks in a spirit of teamwork, friendship, and oneness.
 Throughout the tournament, participants experienced both athletic and spiritual growth. Daily practices such as arti, cheshta, and thoughtfully planned morning and evening sessions helped youths connect sportsmanship with satsang values. The structure of the event encouraged leadership, discipline, collaboration, and personal reflection, ensuring that the lessons learned on the court carried into their lives, studies, careers, and seva.
 Guided by the ongoing vision of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the Yogi Cup continued to build on the legacy of Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The 2025–2026 tournament served as a platform for youths to deepen their spirituality, strengthen their connection with their guru, and build meaningful bonds, while experiencing the joy of competition and the unity that defined Yogi Cup.

/News/2025/Yuva-Gnansatras-2025-28665.as.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Gnansatras (98 photos)
 During their summer vacations, a total of 850 yuvaks and 860 yuvatis participated in the 7-day Yuva Gnansatras conducted at 19 BAPS shikharbaddha mandirs across Gujarat and Maharashtra. The youths attending the Gnansatras stayed at the mandir for seven days and engaged in various programs as per the schedule designed by the Satsang Pravrutti Central Office in Ahmedabad.
 The program included guidance and training on Vachanamrut study, spiritual discourse preparations, memorization (mukhpath), story narration, public speaking and other practical topics.
 Enlightening discourses, workshops and discussions by sadhus and volunteers on the Akshar-Purushottam upasana, inspiring stories of devotees and a variety of spiritual topics imparted invaluable lessons. Furthermore, interviews with dedicated volunteers and senior devotees guided and inspired the youths towards incorporating devotion and service in their daily lives.
 Also, through videos and Q&A sessions, the youths experienced the divine presence and guidance of guruhari Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In addition to the daily knowledge-based sessions, the youths engaged in seva activities and sports.
 After six days of in-depth learning at the mandirs, the seventh day involved a one-day rural satsang outreach in which all the youths visited nearby villages, building rapport with local devotees. The youths also conducted de-addiction camps, inspiring many to give up their addictions.
 Thus, the 7-day Yuva Gnansatras provided the youths valuable practical guidance to apply in their daily lives.

/News/2025/Yuva-Shibir-2025-Dhanya-Dhany.t: Yuva Shibir 2025: 'Dhanya Dhanya Mama Jivan’, Atladara (Vadodara), India
/News/2025/Yuva-Shibir-2025-Dhanya-Dhany.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (86 photos)
 More than 1,150 youths from Vadodara participated in the four-day Yuva Shibir based on the theme 'Dhanya Dhanya Mama Jivan'.
 On 15 May, in Sankari, speeches by learned and experienced swamis guided the youths on prapti (spiritual attainments), niyams and dharma, restraint and discretion in using social media, understanding the all-doership of Bhagwan, and other topics.  The shibir theme was further elaborated on through workshops, skits, videos, quizzes, and other activities.
 The highlight of the shibir was the kirtan bhakti and Q&A with Mahant Swami Maharaj during puja darshan at Surat Akshardham on 16 May. Afterwards, the youths learnt in detail about the under-construction Surat Akshardham.
 During the Darshan Yatra on 16 and 17 May, the youths visited Navsari, Silvassa and Tithal mandirs, where they learnt about the history of each mandir.
 As a result of this shibir, the youths pledged to observe social media discretion and restraint, maintain a pure vegetarian diet, attend their weekly local youth assembly, daily read satsang literature and other niyams.

/News/2025/Yuva-Shibir-2025-My-Guru-My-L.t: Yuva Shibir 2025: 'My Guru, My Life', Navsari, India
/News/2025/Yuva-Shibir-2025-My-Guru-My-L.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (42 photos)
 More than 350 youths from Navsari participated in a four-day Yuva Shibir in Nashik based on the theme ‘Mara Guru, Maru Jivan’ (My Guru, My Life). The shibir emphasized placing the guru at the heart of one’s existence and making his teachings the guiding compass for all of life’s decisions.
 On 31 May, learned swamis delivered discourses on prapti (attainment), observing niyams and dharma, using social media with restraint and discretion, understanding Bhagwan’s all-doership and other key spiritual topics. Interactive workshops, skits, videos, quizzes, and activities deepened the youths’ understanding of aligning their thoughts and actions with their guru’s principles.
 In the evening, the youths engaged in an inspiring dialogue with acclaimed actor Shri Dilip Joshi, who shared his experiences of navigating the materialistic world while staying anchored in spiritual values. He explained how steadfast adherence to niyams brings him peace and strength, attributing this bliss to walking the path illuminated by gurus Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 On 1 June, the shibir continued with sessions until noon. Afterwards, the youths embarked on darshan of the holy shrines in Nashik, culminating in the divine experience of the evening arti on the banks of the Godavari River in Panchavati. 
 The final day, 2 June, was dedicated to strengthening friendships and unity with a fun trip to Imagica Amusement Park.

/News/2025/Yuva-Shibirs-2025-Brahmanand-.t: Yuva Shibirs 2025: 'Brahmanand – The Eternal Happiness', India
/News/2025/Yuva-Shibirs-2025-Brahmanand-.text:
Over 20,700 yuvaks and yuvatis participated in the one-day Yuva Shibirs organized at 22 BAPS centers throughout Gujarat and Maharashtra. The central theme of the shibirs was 'Brahmanand – The Eternal Happiness'.
 First, the shibirs introduced to the youths the Brahmanand that we have attained in the form of Satsang and the Satpurush. This was followed by a detailed examination of the obstacles in the path of retaining that Brahmanand, such as indiscriminate use of social media and the violation of male-female boundaries. The youths were guided on measures that enable the daily experience of Brahmanand day and night: daily reflection to appreciate the glory of our attainment, daily personal puja, satsang reading, studies and other practices.
 The participants were guided through scholarly speeches by learned swamis, workshops, discussions, audio-visual presentations, and video blessings from Guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 At the end, the youths pledged to retain Brahmanand in their daily lives.

/News/2025/Yuva-Yuvati-Talim-Kendra-Grad.t: Yuva-Yuvati Talim Kendra Graduates Reunion, Sarangpur, India
/News/2025/Yuva-Yuvati-Talim-Kendra-Grad.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Graduates Reunion (68 photos)
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the ‘Yuva Talim Kendra’ at Sarangpur in 2007 and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj initiated the ‘Yuvati Talim Kendra’ at Randesan in 2017.
 Since then, hundreds of young men and women have received guidance to help them nurture values, latent talents, social skills, and other abilities.
 More than 2,400 graduates of the Yuva Talim Kendra and Yuvati Talim Kendra enthusiastically gathered for this reunion in the presence of Pujya Dr. Swami.
 In 2014, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj wrote a letter revealing his vision of an ideal sevak. In alignment with that letter, this reunion was themed ‘Sevaks of Swami’s Sankalp’.
 During this three-day reunion, workshops, presentations, and podcasts were conducted on devotion, spiritual disciplines, daily rituals, seva and other topics.
 Senior and learned swamis guided the youths on how to apply the lessons learned during training in their daily lives by addressing practical questions and real-life situations. Pujya Dr. Swami also delivered highly inspiring blessings on how to integrate the training into one’s personal life.
 The most cherished moment of the reunion was when His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj joined online from Mehsana, blessing all the youths and sanctifying the gathering with his divine presence.

/News/2025/Yuvak-Antar-Jagruti-Parva-202.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Antar Jagruti Parva (37 photos)
 The 91 youths of the first Yuva Talim Kendra batch of 2025 participated in the Antar Jagruti Parva. The yuvaks, split into 22 groups, visited 232 villages in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.
 The youths contacted 8,928 households to convey the importance of satsang values in daily lives. They inspired 1,651 families to take various vows to help foster personal spirituality and family harmony. These included attending weekly satsang assemblies, doing daily puja, going to their local mandir for darshan, reading Swamini Vato and Vachanamrut regularly, fasting on ekadashi, doing ghar sabha regularly, and other such devotional satsang rituals and practices.
 During their travels, the youths conducted 186 satsang assemblies, which were attended by around 11,400 people. They also held about 80 assemblies especially for children, and 105 school assemblies, where they provided guidance to over 18,800 children. In the evenings, the yuvaks organized special devotional processions in the villages, in which about 2,000 people participated. They also inspired 400 people to give up various addictions.
 This opportunity gave the yuvaks practical experience and enabled them to also draw inspiration from devotees who sincerely practice satsang in their daily lives.

/News/2025/Yuvak-Yuvati-Adhiveshan--Summ.t: Yuvak-Yuvati Adhiveshan & Summer Shibir 2025, North America
/News/2025/Yuvak-Yuvati-Adhiveshan--Summ.text:
Across North America, Yuvaks and Yuvatis found the 2025 Adhiveshan and Summer Shibir to be a meaningful opportunity for personal spiritual growth. Held over four days between June and August, the experience centered around the theme “Satsang: The Journey to Rajipo,” encouraging participants to engage in memorizing selected verses from sacred texts (mukhpath) as a way to build conviction, gain clarity, and lead a purposeful life.
 The purpose of the Adhiveshan was deeply rooted in earning the rajipo (blessings) of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The Adhiveshan encouraged participants to move beyond recitation and internalize the teachings they were learning. By understanding the content of mukhpath and applying it to real-life decisions and challenges, participants discovered how this wisdom could strengthen their relationship with Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Satpurush and help them navigate modern life with spiritual insight.
 Structured into three components—Prathmik Mukhpath, Purna Mukhpath, and skills competitions—the Adhiveshan required all participants to begin with the Prathmik Mukhpath, which introduced elements commonly used in daily rituals and sabhas. The Purna Mukhpath explored modules rooted in satsang principles and included texts from the Swamini Vato, Vachanamrut, Purushottam Bolya Prite, Satsang Diksha, Yogi Gita, Yogi Vani, Harililamrut, Bhaktachintamani, as well as kirtans, sakhis, and prasangs.
 Participants then had the opportunity to showcase their abilities through skills competitions. Individual categories included music production, article writing, hand-drawn art, digital illustration, graphic design, photography, videography, video reels, granth nirupan, short speeches, elevator talks, and solo singing. Group categories included group drama and group singing, emphasizing collaboration and creativity grounded in spiritual knowledge.
 The Adhiveshan and Summer Shibir concluded with an inspiring call to deepen spiritual understanding, emphasizing shravan, manan, and nidhidhyas as essential steps toward realizing sakshatkar and earning the rajipo of the Satpurush.

/News/2025/Yuvak-Yuvati-Shibir-and-Yatra.t: Yuvak-Yuvati Shibir and Yatra: Connection with the Manifest Satpurush, Bhavnagar, India
/News/2025/Yuvak-Yuvati-Shibir-and-Yatra.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuvak-Yuvati Shibir (64 photos)
 Pilgrimage (Yatra) (99 photos)
 Over 350 yuvaks and yuvatis from BAPS Mandir in Bhavnagar participated in its annual Yuva Shibir and Yatra. Themed ‘Connection with the Manifest Satpurush’, the five-day event began in Gondal on 23 October, where they received Mahant Swami Maharaj’s blessings.
 Pilgrimage (Yatra)
 The pilgrimage, on 24 and 25 October, included visits to Bharuch, Sankari, Dhule (Maharashtra) and Varkhede Village – where they visited spots sanctified by Shastriji Maharaj and participated in a bullock cart procession.
 Shibir at Nagpur
 The shibir was held in Nagpur on 26 and 27 October.
 During the shibir, learned swamis presented speeches and workshops on the glory of the Gunatit parampara, the manifest Satpurush – Mahant Swami Maharaj, increasing love for and faith in the Satpurush, the key to becoming brahmarup, and other topics.
 The presentations also emphasized the importance of obeying agna, observing brahmacharya, and discretion in using mobile phones, the internet and social media.
 In an evening session, the youths participated in an entertaining and enlightening online spiritual quiz titled ‘Kon Banega Jnanpati?’
 A special separate session for the yuvatis was also organized.
 The shibir strengthened the faith of the youths and they pledged to sincerely observe satsang principles in their daily lives to please guru Mahant swami Maharaj.
 The return journey included visits to Jabalpur (Mahant Swami Maharaj’s birthplace), Pachmarhi, Ujjain Mahakaleshwar and Omkareshwar.
