They contacted 3,379 households, reaching out to 5,258 women. The yuvatis conducted a total of 156 women's assemblies, which were attended by over 4,900 women.
 Additionally, they conducted 69 balika sabhas, guiding over 1,100 young girls, and 99 school sabhas, reaching out to over 7,650 girl students. The yuvatis also organized evening processions in 110 locations, in which over 3,500 women participated.
 Through the efforts of the yuvatis, 8,595 women pledged to observe vows to enhance their daily spirituality.

 Convocation Ceremony (15 photos)
 The convocation ceremony for the 89 yuvatis of the first Yuvati Talim Kenra batch of 2025 who completed their four-month training in Randesan was held in the presence of 550 attendees, including Vidyaben Manubhai Single from Vadodara, Nilaben Chandrakantbhai Patel, other dignitaries, as well as parents and other guests.
 Based on the theme ‘Mano Mali Chhe Moti Vat’, the yuvatis presented a series of skits and traditional dance performances that captured the essence of their learning experience.
 In her convocation address, Shrimati Vidyaben emphasized the value of the training, noting that it imparted crucial life skills and helped cultivate the inner stability necessary for personal and social challenges. Then, Shrimati Neelaben praised the holistic nature of the training, which provides a comprehensive framework for well-rounded personal development.
 During the convocation ceremony, certificates were presented to yuvatis.

/News/2025/nsc-25-28973.aspx.t: Bal-Balika & Kishore-Kishori North American Summer Camp 2025, San Jose, CA, USA
/News/2025/nsc-25-28973.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Arrival (18 photos)
 Daily Activities (31 photos)
 Outings (13 photos)
 Sessions (21 photos)
 Dradh Priti—deep, unwavering love for Bhagwan and the Satpurush—was the guiding force of the 2025 BAPS North American Summer Camp, held from July 1 to 9 in San Jose, California. Around 400 youth delegates from across North America gathered for nine days of focused learning, reflection, and spiritual growth. Each day centered on one of the four pillars of Dradh Priti: Shastras, Siddhant, Sanstha, and Satpurush. Through engaging classroom sessions, workshops, and goshthis, delegates explored how to develop consistent spiritual habits and navigate real-life challenges with Satsang values.
 In the afternoons, delegates joined clubs that nurtured both creativity and connection. From Architecture and Business to Cooking, Music, and Coding, each club offered a space to build new skills while anchoring them in spiritual purpose. Whether preparing a skit, filming a story, or designing models, these sessions encouraged teamwork and self-expression, all with the goal of offering something meaningful to Swamishri.
 Several outings brought the lessons of Dradh Priti to life through shared experiences. Delegates hiked through Muir Woods, reflected during goshthi on the beach, and kayaked across the open waters of Lake Tahoe. A day in San Francisco included a walk across the Golden Gate Bridge, a visit to Ghirardelli Square, and sports at Crissy Field—all moments that combined fun, friendship, and Satsang. For kishores and kishoris, a campus walk and discussion at Stanford offered a glimpse into how Satsang can remain strong during college life.
 The camp concluded with a gala dinner and heartfelt reflections from swamis and delegates. Through nine transformative days, each youth left with a stronger identity, a deeper connection to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, and a clearer sense of purpose. As they return to their communities, they carry the lessons of NSC 2025 with them—rooted in love, guided by agna, and ready to live with strength and conviction.

 25th Patosav Celebration (30 photos)
 The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Clifton, New Jersey marked its 25th anniversary with devotion and gratitude. The occasion, also known as the Mandir’s Pãtotsav, is a sacred observance that commemorates the anniversary of murti consecration (pran pratishtha) in mandirs. The morning celebrations honored the historic day twenty-five years ago when HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed the pran pratishtha of the Mandir’s murtis, establishing the Mandir as a divine place of worship.
 The milestone was graced by the presence of Pujya Swamis, whose visit brought immense spiritual inspiration to the assembly. Devotees gathered in large numbers to participate in the mahapuja and sacred abhishek, offering prayers for peace, prosperity, and spiritual growth.
 As the community reflected on 25 years of faith, seva, and unity, the celebration reaffirmed the Mandir’s enduring role as a center for devotion, cultural values, and community service for generations to come.

/News/2026/-His-Holiness-Mahant-Swami-Ma.t: His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in London 2026, UK & Europe
/News/2026/-His-Holiness-Mahant-Swami-Ma.text:
After inaugurating France’s first traditional Hindu mandir in Paris, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj will arrive in London on Wednesday 16 September 2026 for a four-week spiritual tour blessing the people of the UK.
 Various devotional and inspiring programmes have been organised in his presence, focussing on strengthening faith, mobilising community service, and fostering harmony among people of all ages and backgrounds.
 For detailed information about Mahant Swami Maharaj’s stay at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London (popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’), please visit msm.neasdentemple.org. The website includes helpful visitor info, a ‘What’s On’ calendar of events, further information about Mahant Swami Maharaj, and ways to stay connected.
 Devotees and well-wishers from outside the UK wishing to enjoy Mahant Swami Maharaj’s spiritual presence in London should register here.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj’s morning puja and evening programmes will also be streamed live on certain days. Check the ‘Live Webcast’ page for the schedule. 
 The latest news and updates about Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visit will be available from the ‘Neasden Temple’ Telegram channel and its various other social media accounts – X, Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn – as well as the ‘BAPS UK & Europe’ YouTube channel.

/News/2026/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.t: Akhand Dhun: Annual Prayers for Success, Peace and Harmony, Wellingborough, UK
/News/2026/Akhand-Dhun-Annual-Prayers-fo.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Darshan (12 photos)
 Prarthana (48 photos)
 Ashirwad (8 photos)
 Devotees from across the UK gathered at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Wellingborough, on Sunday 5 April 2026 for the annual Akhand Dhun – a spiritually uplifting day of continuous prayer offered for success, peace, and harmony throughout the world.
 The devotional observances commenced in the early hours of the morning, with kishores performing a mahapuja at 5.00am. Inspired by the spiritual legacy of Yogiji Maharaj, this sacred ritual created a serene and devotional foundation for the day.
 From 7.00am onwards, devotees arrived steadily to participate in the dhun. The Mandir resonated with the rhythmic chanting of the Swaminarayan Mahamantra as devotees offered prayers and performed pradakshinas at the Akshar Deri, the sacred shrine at the heart of the Mandir. Each act of devotion was offered with heartfelt prayers for the well-being of families, communities, and society at large.
 Among those in attendance was Dr Mitbhai Dattani, who travelled from Birmingham with his family. Reflecting on the occasion, he shared, “Coming here every year is something we deeply look forward to. There is a unique peace you feel the moment you walk in; being surrounded by so many people united in prayer and devotion is truly humbling. We left feeling spiritually renewed and grateful.”
 This year’s Akhand Dhun carried additional significance as devotees prepare to welcome His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to the UK later this year. The theme for the year, ‘Satsangnu Vatavaran Vadharvu’ – to nurture the spiritual environment around us – offered a timely reminder of the importance of unity, collective devotion, and mutual appreciation within the satsang fellowship.
 Krushali Kataria, who travelled from London, reflected, “The theme this year really struck a chord with me. It is easy to focus on our own spiritual progress, but Mahant Swami Maharaj is reminding us that satsang grows when we genuinely appreciate and uplift one another. That is a message I will be taking home and reflecting upon.”
 Throughout the day, the Mandir remained immersed in devotion, with a continuous flow of chanting, prayer, pradakshinas, and seva, as devotees collectively offered their prayers for success, peace, and harmony for all.
 Adding to the spirit of the day, a group of 15 cyclists rode more than 100 kilometres from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Chigwell, whilst 10 devotees undertook a pad-yatra – a pilgrimage on foot – covering the same distance, with both groups arriving in Wellingborough by the evening.
 Parth Mistry, a lead volunteer in Wellingborough, shared, “Seeing so many devotees come through the Mandir with one purpose in their hearts is something that never loses its meaning. It was a privilege to welcome so many families from near and far, and our team of volunteers is honoured to serve in whatever way we can.”

/News/2026/Americas250-31522.aspx.t: Honoring America's 250th Anniversary Through Unity, Service, and Community, USA
/News/2026/Americas250-31522.aspx.text:
As the United States celebrates the 250th anniversary of its independence, devotees at BAPS Hindu mandirs across North America joined local communities to commemorate this historic milestone through service, reflection, and civic engagement. As an official America250 supporting partner, BAPS is honored to participate in this nationwide commemoration, helping foster unity, service, and civic engagement across communities. For many Hindu American families, the celebration was deeply personal, providing an opportunity to express gratitude for the freedom to practice their faith openly while contributing to the diverse fabric of American society.
 Inspired by the Hindu teachings of selfless service, unity, and harmony, BAPS devotees participated in America 250 through open houses, interfaith events, local parades, patriotic cultural displays, and community outreach initiatives led through BAPS Charities, like the annual Walk-Run. For over two decades, the 1,200 Walk-Runs organized across North America have supported hundreds of local organizations through initiatives focused on health, education, disaster relief, sustainability, hunger relief, and community outreach. Across towns and cities nationwide, mandirs welcomed neighbors, elected officials, and faith leaders to foster understanding and strengthen relationships built over decades of shared service and friendship.
 Many celebrations highlighted the values that unite communities across backgrounds and beliefs. Through interfaith discussions on religious liberty and pluralism, as well as volunteer efforts supporting local causes, devotees reflected on how America's ideals have allowed generations to preserve their traditions while giving back to the communities they call home. Mandirs also featured patriotic displays such as red, white, and blue rangoli (traditional Indian floor art), as well as family-centered activities to commemorate the anniversary.
 For more than 50 years in North America, BAPS has worked to serve society through humanitarian relief efforts, health awareness initiatives, educational programs, environmental campaigns, and community service activities. As the United States marked 250 years, BAPS devotees were honored to celebrate not only the nation's history, but also the opportunity to continue building stronger, more compassionate communities together.

High school and college girls from across North America came together for this year’s Amrut Cup Volleyball Tournament. Teams competed in fast-paced matches while exemplifying the values of samp (unity), suhradbhav (solidarity), and ekta (oneness) — timeless principles taught by Yogiji Maharaj. More than just a sporting event, the tournament created a vibrant environment where participants strengthened their bonds with one another while striving together toward a common goal.
 Throughout the tournament, satsang was woven into every aspect of the experience. Each day began and concluded with aarti and cheshta, complemented by thoughtfully planned morning and evening sessions that encouraged reflection, gratitude, and spiritual growth. These moments grounded the athletes in purpose, reminding them that competition and cooperation go hand in hand when guided by shared values.
 The Amrut Cup also reflects the vision of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, continuing the legacy of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj to nurture well-rounded, values-driven youth. Through initiatives like this, kishoris and yuvatis are inspired to stay engaged in weekly sabhas, summer conventions, and community service, developing leadership, teamwork, and character alongside their spiritual growth.
 By the tournament’s end, the victories extended far beyond the scoreboard. Participants returned home with renewed friendships, deeper connections to their Guru, and a lasting commitment to carry the ideals of unity, solidarity, and oneness into their schools, families, and communities, making the Amrut Cup a truly transformative experience.

/News/2026/BAPS-Children-Break-Guinness-.t: BAPS Children Break Guinness World Record with Historic Recitations, Atladara (Vadodara), India
/News/2026/BAPS-Children-Break-Guinness-.text:
1:11:51
 One Guru, 15,000 Children & the Power of Pure Love

 PART II | Bhagwanni Shakti: Real. Impossible. Stories.
 1:12:22
 भगवान की शक्ति, भाग - २, Real. Impossible. Stories.
 Photo Gallery 
 Guinness World Record (60 photos)
 Guinness World Record Certificate (7 photos)
 On the auspicious occasion of the 92nd birth celebrations of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, 12,723 child scholars (bal and balika vidvans) gathered in Vadodara to collectively recite Sanskrit verses from the ‘Satsang Diksha’ shastra written by Mahant Swami Maharaj, creating a new Guinness World Record for ‘The Largest Simultaneous Hindu Text Recital’.
 On 25 October 2024, Mahant Swami Maharaj expressed: “By next Diwali [2025], 10,000 children shall memorize this scripture [Satsang Diksha] in the Sanskrit language.”
 To fulfill this resolve, the ‘Mission Rajipo’ campaign was launched, in which 103 swamis and more than 17,000 volunteers worked with unwavering dedication to make Swamishri’s resolve a reality.
 Within just one year, a total of 15,666 children, aged 3 to 13 years, memorized all 315 Sanskrit verses of the Satsang Diksha text as a devotional tribute to guru Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 The Satsang Diksha shastra serves as a complete guidebook for all aspects of human life. It expounds the eternal principles of agna and upasana as propounded by Parabrahma Bhagwan Swaminarayan, along with clear guidance on daily conduct applicable to all. This shastra instills noble values in individuals of all ages, thereby nurturing an ethical, spiritual, and value-based society.
 The world record recital attempt took place on 2 February 2026, between 1:30 and 2:00 p.m. in the presence of Guinness World Records adjudicator Mr. Swapnil Dangarikar and approximately 360 official stewards. Following a meticulous process of verification, counting, and the examination of the young scholars, Mr. Swapnil Dangarikar honored this unprecedented feat by presenting the official world record certificate to His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The citation reads: “The largest simultaneous Hindu text recital was achieved by the International Children's Forum of Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) in Atladara, Gujarat, India, on 2 February 2026.”
 Among the participants were child scholars from India, England, USA, UAE, Australia, Canada, and other countries, making this mass recital a truly global celebration of Sanskrit and Sanatan culture.
 This memorization campaign and mass recital of Sanskrit verses will have long-term societal impact:
 Cultural Revival:
 Awareness and appreciation of Sanskrit and Sanatan Hindu Dharma values have been powerfully awakened in the young generation through this unique initiative.
 Educational Achievement:
 The discipline of Sanskrit memorization has resulted in a significant enhancement of memory, concentration, and comprehension among children. Parents, teachers, and students alike have witnessed notable academic progress.
 Character Building:
 Beyond memorization, 15,666 children have imbibed virtues such as honesty, non-violence, mutual respect, stability, and patience. Parents have joyfully observed this positive transformation in their children.
 Guru-Shishya Tradition:
 This historic occasion offered a sublime and living glimpse of the guru-shishya tradition, demonstrating what disciples can achieve to preserve Sanatan Dharma, and please God and guru.

/News/2026/BAPS-Delegation-Participates-.t: BAPS Delegation Participates in Vatican Interfaith Conference and Meets Pope Leo XIV, Rome, Italy
/News/2026/BAPS-Delegation-Participates-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Interfaith Conference in Rome (32 photos)
 Religious leaders, scholars, academics, and representatives of Europe’s dharmic faith communities gathered in Rome to explore how interreligious dialogue can strengthen fraternity and inspire practical collaboration, culminating in an audience with His Holiness Pope Leo XIV.
 A delegation from BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, participated in the international interfaith conference, titled “Buddhists, Christians, Hindus, Jains and Sikhs in Europe: Building Fraternity through Dialogue and Collaboration,” held on 23 & 24 June 2026 at the Angelicum – Pontifical University of St. Thomas Aquinas – in Rome. 
 Convened by the Catholic Church’s Dicastery for Interreligious Dialogue, the conference was organised in partnership with a wide coalition of institutions, including the Council of European Bishops’ Conferences, the Focolare Movement, the Angelicum’s Institute for Interreligious Relations, the Hindu Forum of Europe, the European Buddhist Union, the Institute of Jainology, and the Sikhi Sewa Society of Italy. It brought together more than 150 religious leaders, scholars, academics, and faith representatives from across Europe, together with senior officials of the Holy See.
 The programme featured keynote addresses, panel discussions, and interreligious dialogue sessions, creating an exchange between academics, who examined the opportunities and challenges of religious pluralism in contemporary Europe, and faith leaders, who shared practical experience of fostering dialogue, mutual understanding, and collaboration within their communities.
 Opening the conference, Cardinal George Jacob Koovakad, Prefect of the Dicastery for Interreligious Dialogue, acknowledged that fraternity is often dismissed as a distant ideal amid the wars, divisions, and hatred of the present age – yet insisted it remains a concrete and lived reality, capable of enduring even in a fractured world. 
 Throughout the conference, participants reaffirmed that dialogue and collaboration are essential to building more peaceful and cohesive societies. While remaining firmly rooted in their own faith traditions, they emphasised the importance of engaging openly and respectfully with others and translating fraternity into practical action that promotes peace, harmony, and the common good.
 BAPS was represented by a delegation of eight members, including two swamis, who joined fellow participants in this shared commitment to fostering mutual understanding, respect, and collaboration.
 During the opening session of the conference, Paramtattvadas Swami was invited to felicitate Cardinal George Jacob Koovakad by presenting him with a traditional shawl.
 On 24 June, the conference concluded as the full body of participants joined His Holiness Pope Leo XIV’s traditional Wednesday General Audience in St Peter’s Square. Within this setting, BAPS representatives were received for a special audience with His Holiness.
 During the audience, BAPS representatives recalled the historic meeting between His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Pope John Paul II, held at the Vatican on 7 April 1984. A photograph commemorating that landmark occasion was presented to Pope Leo XIV, highlighting more than four decades of earnest dialogue and mutual respect between BAPS and the Catholic Church.
 The representatives also presented a recent photograph of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, together with two gifts and a message of love, peace, harmony, and respect.
 The first gift, a mala (Hindu rosary), represented the belief that although people of different faiths pray in different ways, they are united by one Divine thread. Echoing Pope Leo XIV’s episcopal motto, ‘In illo Uno unum’ (‘In the One, we are one’), the representatives reflected on humanity’s shared search for God, peace, and the common good.
 The second gift, a traditional diya (sacred lamp), reflected the Hindu belief that the light of love, peace and harmony always triumphs over the darkness of hatred, violence and discord. Presented on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the gifts expressed BAPS’s continued commitment to prayer, friendship, and interfaith dialogue.
 Reflecting on the conference and the audience, Paramtattvadas Swami said, “These two days have reminded us that dialogue is not simply about listening to one another; it is about walking together in friendship and serving society together. We were deeply honoured to convey the blessings and heartfelt message of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to His Holiness Pope Leo XIV. The exchange of these gifts expressed our shared aspiration that faith should always be a source of peace, compassion, and harmony.”
 Participation in the conference and the audience with Pope Leo XIV reaffirmed BAPS’s longstanding commitment to working alongside people of all faiths in promoting peace, harmony, and selfless service.

/News/2026/BAPS-Engages-in-Interfaith-Di.t: BAPS Engages in Interfaith Dialogue at Muslim World League’s Faith, Leadership, and Global Coexistence Capitol Hill Gathering, Washington DC, USA
/News/2026/BAPS-Engages-in-Interfaith-Di.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS Joins Interfaith Leaders on Capitol Hill (4 photos)
 On February 4, 2026, BAPS participated in a interfaith gathering on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., aimed at strengthening dialogue and cooperation among diverse religious and civic leaders. The event, hosted by the Muslim World League, brought together policymakers, diplomats, faith leaders, and community representatives to affirm the shared commitment to peaceful coexistence and mutual understanding.
 Akshar Patel, MD, representing BAPS, expressed deep appreciation for the leadership of His Excellency Sheikh Dr. Mohammad bin Abdulkarim Al-Issa, Secretary General of the Muslim World League, whose global efforts have strengthened interreligious cooperation. He noted that in the nation’s capital, where dialogue and debate shape public life, advancing understanding across faiths is especially significant.
 BAPS’ longstanding commitment to interfaith engagement was highlighted, including the historic 2022 interfaith conference in Riyadh and the 2024 International Conference of Religious Leaders in Malaysia, where faith leaders reaffirmed the responsibility of sustained dialogue and partnership.
 Reflecting the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual head of BAPS, Dr. Patel emphasized that interfaith dialogue rooted in humility, mutual respect, and service to society is essential to foster harmony in an increasingly interconnected world.
 He also recalled H.E. Sheikh Dr. Al-Issa’s 2023 visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, as well as the presence of Mr. Muath Alamri, representing His Excellency, at the opening of Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, as meaningful symbols of mutual respect and interfaith friendship.
 Referring to the Hindu concept of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the belief that humanity is one family, Dr. Patel remarked that such interfaith moments of unity “affirm that when religious institutions work together, they can strengthen social cohesion, counter hatred, and contribute positively to the moral fabric of our societies.”
 As the gathering concluded, H.E. Sheikh Dr. Al-Issa was greeted by BAPS Swamis,  Pujya Viratswarupdas Swami and Pujya Mangalnidhidas Swami, expressing gratitude for the opportunity to participate in this dialogue.

/News/2026/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Wins-Presti.t: BAPS Hindu Mandir Wins Prestigious ‘TOLERANCE AWARD 2026’, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2026/BAPS-Hindu-Mandir-Wins-Presti.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Tolerance Award 2026 (29 photos)
 The BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi was honored with the prestigious ‘Tolerance Award’ at the 3rd International Dialogue of Civilizations and Tolerance Conference (IDCT 2026). The Tolerance Award recognizes individuals and organizations whose work promotes global tolerance, mutual respect, and peaceful coexistence. Recipients are selected by the conference’s scientific committee based on their measurable international impact.
 The Conference was organized and conducted by The Emirates Scholar Center for Research & Studies (ESCRS) and the Abrahamic Family House, in partnership with Emirates Journalists Association, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, and Abu Dhabi Convention & Exhibition Bureau.
 Held in Abu Dhabi as part of the UAE’s celebration of 2026 as the Year of the Family, IDCT 2026 was a landmark global event bringing together governments, academic institutions, international organizations, faith communities, and civil society leaders to strengthen intercultural dialogue, advance the science of coexistence, and address the profound transformations that artificial intelligence and new media are imposing upon families and communities worldwide.
 The award is a profound recognition of the BAPS Hindu Mandir's contribution to fostering harmony, dialogue, and social cohesion in the UAE and beyond. Through initiatives such as the Festival of Harmony, Omsiyyat, and Care in Crisis during the Covid pandemic and the current conflict, the Mandir continues to serve selflessly, personally and universally. The award reflects the collective efforts of thousands of volunteers and countless visitors, and a shared commitment to creating a space where people of every background, culture, and faith feel welcomed and valued.
 Accepting the award from the hands of HE Dr. Abdulla Belhaif Al Nuaimi, Chancellor of Emirates Scholar Center for Research and Studies, and HE Dr. Khalifa Al Dhaheri, Chancellor of Mohamed Bin Zayed University for Humanities, Brahmavihari Swami, Head of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, delivered a thought-provoking keynote address on the future of family, faith, and technology.
 While much of the world is focused on what artificial intelligence can do, he invited delegates to reflect on a deeper question: what kind of humanity are we becoming because of it?
 Drawing on wisdom from civilizations across the world, he highlighted a timeless truth: strong societies are built upon strong families. Whether expressed through civilizational lessons that unity creates strength, or the Hindu ideals of Matrudevo Bhava (respect your mother as God), Pitrudevo Bhava (respect your father as God) and Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (the world is one family), the message across cultures remains remarkably consistent.
 He particularly emphasized the simple but transformative practice of Ghar Sabha encouraged by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, in which families spend twenty minutes together each day in prayer, conversation, reflection, and listening. In a world increasingly connected by technology, yet often disconnected from one another, he reminded the audience that meaningful relationships are built not through constant communication, but through genuine presence.
 He stated that ‘What we need are AI-Empowered Families, not just AI-Powered Families’. As technology advances, humanity must advance with it. Innovation requires values. Progress requires purpose. And the future will depend not only on smarter machines, but on stronger families and more compassionate communities.
 Brahmavihari Swami concluded by expressing gratitude to the conference organizers for this honour, and to the UAE's leadership for continually championing the values of coexistence, dialogue, and human fraternity.

/News/2026/BAPS-Hosts-Fresno-Pacific-Rel.t: BAPS Hosts Fresno Pacific Religious Studies Students, Fresno, CA, USA

Photo Gallery 
 Fresno Pacific University Students Visit (3 photos)
 Religious Studies students from Fresno Pacific University, accompanied by Professor Darren Duerksen, visited the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Fresno, California, on Wednesday, March 18, 2026, to gain a deeper understanding of Hinduism through an immersive, first-hand experience.
 During the visit, foundational aspects of Hinduism were thoughtfully presented and discussed. Students learned about Hinduism as a monotheistic tradition expressed through diverse forms, its ancient origins, and its key scriptures. The significance of rituals in fostering discipline and spirituality was explained, along with the role of murtis as sacred representations that help devotees focus their devotion.
 The presentation also introduced the BAPS way of life, highlighting values such as faith, service, humility, and moral living. In addition, students were informed about the humanitarian initiatives of BAPS Charities, including efforts in community service, health awareness, and disaster relief.
 Students actively engaged in the session, asking insightful questions and participating in meaningful dialogue. They appreciated the opportunity to experience the mandir environment firsthand, with many describing the visit as enriching—gaining not only knowledge but also a deeper appreciation for the depth, diversity, and lived practices of Hinduism.

 On May 10, 2026, the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Huntsville, Alabama, joyfully marked a historic milestone with the celebration of its grand opening and the sacred Murti Sthapan Vidhi a traditional consecration ceremony for the installation of the divine images. The sacred murtis had been originally consecrated on August 20, 2023, by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in Robbinsville, NJ.
 The occasion drew over 1,200 devotees and well-wishers, with Pujya Gyanpriya Swami presiding over the Murti Sthapan Vidhi, accompanied by the chanting of Vedic Shlokas. True to the spirit of BAPS, the ceremony welcomed all attendees, reflecting the Mandir's founding vision as a spiritual home open to everyone.
 The grand opening was the culmination of three days of joyous celebrations that began on the evening of May 8, 2026, with a Kirtan Aradhana, a devotional music program. Festivities continued on May 9, 2026 with a Vedic Yagna in the morning, a Women's Cultural Celebration in the afternoon, and a vibrant Nagar Yatra procession in the evening.
 The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Huntsville is poised to serve as a cherished center for cultural, spiritual, and social life within the local Hindu-American community, while also supporting a wide range of community service initiatives.

/News/2026/BAPS-Participates-in-East-Afr.t: BAPS Participates in East Africa Youth Forum on Drugs, Arusha, Tanzania
/News/2026/BAPS-Participates-in-East-Afr.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS Participates in East Africa Youth Forum on Drugs (7 photos)
 BAPS representatives participated in the East Africa Youth Forum on Drugs 2026, which brought together 205 delegates from eight countries – Tanzania, Zanzibar, Kenya, Uganda, Malawi, South Africa, Turkey, and Seychelles – to discuss the growing challenges of substance abuse and explore collaborative solutions for prevention and youth empowerment.
 Organized by the Drug Control and Enforcement Authority (DCEA) Tanzania, Care for All, Slumchild Foundation, and Apar Foundation, the three-day forum provided a platform for youth leaders, government representatives, civil society organizations, health professionals, faith-based organizations, and community stakeholders to exchange ideas and strengthen partnerships aimed at creating drug-free communities.
 Throughout the forum, participants engaged in discussions on drug prevention, mental health, youth leadership, rehabilitation, and community-based approaches to addressing substance use challenges. The sessions highlighted the importance of empowering young people with knowledge, positive values, and supportive environments that enable them to make healthy life choices.
 BAPS contributed to the discussions by sharing its commitment to character development, value-based education, and youth empowerment. Through its various spiritual, educational, and community service initiatives, BAPS continues to inspire young people to lead disciplined, purposeful, and addiction-free lives. The forum provided an opportunity to showcase the important role that faith-based organizations can play in strengthening resilience and promoting positive social change among youth.
 The forum concluded with a closing ceremony officiated by the Commissioner General of the Drug Control and Enforcement Authority (DCEA), Mr Aretas Lyimo who commended the participants for their dedication and encouraged young people to remain drug-free and become ambassadors of prevention within their communities. He emphasized the collective responsibility of families, educators, faith-based organizations, governments, and communities in safeguarding future generations from the dangers of substance abuse.

/News/2026/BAPS-Strengthens-Community-Bo.t: BAPS Strengthens Community Bonds at Texas Hindu Campsite through Service and Unity Forum, Houston, TX, USA
/News/2026/BAPS-Strengthens-Community-Bo.text:
Reflecting a shared vision of unity, service, and cultural continuity, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Houston participated in a day of collaboration and dialogue at the newly inaugurated Texas Hindu Campsite along with Hindus of Greater Houston, an umbrella organization representing more than 40 Hindu mandirs and organizations across the Houston area. The gathering served as both a service initiative and a Unity Forum, reaffirming collective efforts to strengthen Hindu values and community bonds.
 Service as a Foundation for Unity
 As part of its continued commitment to selfless service, BAPS Houston donated several youth trailers to the Texas Hindu Campsite, the first and only Hindu campsite in the United States, established with the mission of supporting, preserving, and sustaining Hindu values for future generations. These trailers will enhance the campsite’s ability to host educational, cultural, and spiritual programs for Hindu youth, providing a nurturing environment where young participants can connect with their heritage.
 This act of service reflects BAPS’s longstanding ethos of supporting fellow organizations and investing in shared infrastructure that benefits the broader Hindu community. The campsite’s founders and primary donors, Shri Subhash Gupta and Shri Sarojini Gupta, organized a Day of Gratitude, inviting over 60 donors along with BAPS senior leaders and volunteers to celebrate and acknowledge this collective effort.
 The 2026 Unity Forum: Collaboration Across Organizations
 The event also featured the 2026 Unity Forum, an ongoing initiative by BAPS aimed at fostering harmony and cooperation among Hindu organizations. Over 200 leaders and representatives from more than 49 mandirs and Hindu social organizations gathered to exchange ideas, discuss common challenges, and explore opportunities for collaboration—ranging from humanitarian service projects to youth education and leadership development.
 The forum highlighted the growing spirit of Suhradbhav (fraternity) among Hindu organizations, reinforcing the belief that collective progress is achieved through shared purpose and mutual respect.
 Spiritual Guidance and Vision for the Future
 Addressing the assembly, Pujya Shwetmunidas Swami, Lead Swami of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Houston, emphasized the spiritual necessity of working together for the greater good. He highlighted that unity rooted in values enables communities to serve society more effectively and sustainably.
 Complementing this message, Pujya Bhaktivardhandas Swami delivered a message on the importance of preserving, sharing, and carrying forward Hindu culture, values, and spirituality for generations to come. He reflected on how selfless love for humanity, a principle exemplified by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, serves as a powerful unifying force—transcending organizational boundaries and inspiring leaders to think beyond the present generation.
 Building a Shared Legacy
 The presence of many Hindu organizations at the Texas Hindu Campsite stood as a testament to the community’s collective commitment to unity, service, and cultural continuity. Through initiatives like the Unity Forum and shared acts of service, BAPS Houston and its partners are laying a strong foundation for future generations—ensuring that Hindu values, culture, and spirituality continue to thrive in an atmosphere of harmony and cooperation.

/News/2026/BAPS-Volunteers-Participate-i.t: BAPS Volunteers Participate in United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (70th Session), New York, NY, USA
/News/2026/BAPS-Volunteers-Participate-i.text:
Photo Gallery 
 United Nations Commission on the Status of Women 2026 (13 photos)
 Last month, BAPS volunteers proudly participated in the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (70th Session), held in New York City from March 9 to 19, 2026. CSW is an annual platform for discussing and advancing women’s rights and gender equality across the globe. The active participation of non-governmental organizations, such as BAPS, which holds General Consultative Status with the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations, is critical to the success of the event. This year, the session’s theme focused on ensuring and strengthening access to justice for all women and girls. 
 In his opening remarks, UN Secretary General António Guterres emphasized that access to justice “cuts to the heart of the struggle for equality”, as “around the globe, women hold only 64 percent of the legal rights enjoyed by men.” He also impressed that “justice for women and girls must be a cornerstone of the world we seek to build” because “justice is the engine for sustainable development”, “the foundation for peace and security”, “the guardian of human rights and human dignity”, “essential to a safe and inclusive digital future”, and “essential for climate action.” 
 The Commission on the Status of Women consisted of a wide range of meetings, panel discussions, interactive dialogues, round tables, and intergovernmental negotiations, wherein participants from diverse backgrounds advocated, learned, and shared experiences about women’s challenges to accessing justice and how to effect enduring solutions. Sixteen BAPS volunteers attended various events and shared insights on how faith can be a key driver of women’s empowerment. One volunteer, Kajal Patel, recounted, “It was so meaningful to come together with other NGOs in the same space, learn from their experience, and collectively brainstorm ways to improve and expand our respective work in driving better outcomes for women and girls around the globe. One thing I really took away is that there isn’t a one-size-fits-all approach to gender equality. A lot of the discussions showed that context, which includes culture, upbringing, and values, plays a huge role in how these topics are understood.” 
 As part of CSW this year, our volunteers also participated in a workshop hosted by the Gender Working Group of the United Nations Multi-Faith Advisory Council and members of the United Nations Inter-Agency Task Force on Religion and Sustainable Development. The workshop focused on a draft compendium of positive faith-based approaches to advancing gender equality, grounded in sacred scriptures. Puja Patel of BAPS facilitated the Hinduism track, engaging 20 Hindu women from around the world in discussion and reflection. She shared, “It was inspiring to be part of a space bringing together so many different faith perspectives. In the Hinduism track, we shared personal experiences and reflected on how our faith and upbringings shape our approach to gender equality.” 
 For more information on CSW and the United Nations’ commitment to women’s rights and empowerment, please visit: https://www.unwomen.org/en/how-we-work/commission-on-the-status-of-women.

/News/2026/BAPS-wellNESS-Health-Conventi.text:
Photo Gallery 
 BAPS wellNESS Health Convention (50 photos)
 Over 500 people came together from across the UK to participate in the BAPS wellNESS Health Convention at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Sunday 11 January 2026.
 The convention – a full-day event dedicated to promoting healthier living – brought together NHS professionals, charities, public health leaders, and faith representatives to address key health challenges affecting the South Asian community, such as heart disease, diabetes, mental health, and many others.
 Building on the success of conventions in Manchester and Leicester in 2025, the London convention focused on the four pillars of the BAPS wellNESS initiative: Nutrition, Exercise, Sleep, and Stress Management. Attendees participated in expert-led talks, interactive workshops, and practical demonstrations in the trusted setting of a mandir for accessible, culturally relevant health education. The aim is to support long-term well-being and healthy habit formation in individuals and families.
 The day began with a video message of inspiration from Mahant Swami Maharaj and an address from Yogvivekdas Swami. Leading medical and healthcare professionals delivered engaging talks on heart health, diabetes, nutrition, cancer, and mental health. Speakers included Dr Niket Patel (Consultant Interventional Cardiologist), Dr Nirav Amin (General Practitioner), Sujata Din (Health Coach, Cancer Coach and Meditation Teacher), Dr Alexandra Pender (Consultant Medical Oncologist), and Dr Chandni Pujara (Consultant Psychiatrist).
 Participants also joined interactive workshops on men’s and women’s health, meditation, exercise, breathwork, stress management, and live cooking demonstrations. The resuscitation training proved especially popular, with enthusiastic engagement from participants of all ages.
 A highlight of the convention was the ‘Health Marketplace,’ supported and attended by 25 NHS, academic and charity partners as well as local services providing personalised guidance and practical support. These included Alzheimer’s Society, Bowel Cancer UK, Breast Cancer Now, Brent Talking Therapies, British Heart Foundation, BHF Clinical Research Team in Electrophysiology and AI, Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust Health Inequalities Team and Recovery & Wellbeing College, Harrow Carers Support Group, Hillingdon Stroke Support, Hope2Sleep Charity, Imperial National Heart and Lung Institute, Imperial Patient Experience Research Centre, Jain and Hindu Organ Donation Alliance, Kidney Care UK, London North West Healthcare Charity, Marie Curie, NHS North Thames Genomic Medicine Service, Rare Dementia Support, Royal Osteoporosis Society, Prostate Cancer UK, Stroke Association, and The Menopause Charity.
 Joining the convention through a video address, The Rt Hon Wes Streeting MP, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, said, “I know firsthand from having spent time with the brilliant team of volunteers, many of them expert clinicians in their own right, the difference that you are making for your community, but also the wider community as well.” He went on to speak about the BAPS wellNESS project, adding, “This initiative is so important and the work that you’re doing is pioneering and leading, and I’m determined to share your experience right across the country because there’s so much that we can learn.”
 Dr Niket Patel, Consultant Interventional Cardiologist, who spoke on heart health during the day, said, “Events like this play a vital role in empowering people with accurate and practical knowledge to make positive changes to their lifestyle.”
 One attendee shared her feedback on the convention: “Today’s convention was fantastic, especially the workshops! I will definitely start practising the breathing exercises that I have learnt today, make healthier cooking swaps, and talk to my family about mental health. Thank you so much for organising this convention!”
 Professor Sejal Saglani, Head of BAPS Healthcare activities in the UK, shared, “The large attendance shows community-led health initiatives are important and effective, and highlights the key role that faith settings play in helping people understand more about a healthy lifestyle and disease prevention by enabling education in a trusted and culturally sensitive environment.”
 The BAPS wellNESS Health Convention forms part of an ongoing commitment by BAPS to support healthier communities through education, collaboration, and practical action. Recently, the BAPS wellNESS project received the ‘Health & Well-Being’ award at the London Dangoor Awards 2025 at the Royal Society of Medicine, for outstanding service to Greater London’s communities.

/News/2026/BSRI-Australia-Conferences-20.t: BSRI Australia Conferences 2026: Timeless Teachings from Hindu Gurus, Asia Pacific
/News/2026/BSRI-Australia-Conferences-20.text:
BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute Australia, through its centres across the Pacific region, organised the 2026 BSRIA Conference titled “Timeless Teachings from Hindu Gurus.” Held across BAPS centres in Australia and New Zealand, the conference was attended by more than 6,500 people, including devotees, youths, families, community leaders, invited guests and representatives from various organisations.
 The conference explored the timeless role of the Guru in Hindu tradition and highlighted how the Guru guides individuals towards moral, intellectual and spiritual growth. Centred on the sacred verse “Gurur Brahma, Gurur Vishnu, Gurur Devo Maheshwara, Guru Sakshat Parabrahma,” the program reflected on how the Guru creates noble values within a person, nurtures their spiritual journey, removes inner weaknesses and ultimately leads them towards God-realisation.
 A significant feature of the conference was the strong participation from the wider community. Representatives from 191 organisations attended across the Pacific region, along with nearly 600 community guests, reflecting a shared appreciation for Hindu values, culture, learning and spirituality. Their presence added depth to the conference and highlighted BSRIA’s ongoing role in bringing together diverse community groups through dialogue, education and cultural understanding.
 Through inspiring speeches, devotional presentations, panel discussions, videos and cultural performances, the conference presented the Guru not only as a teacher, but as a divine guide who shapes character, strengthens faith and transforms lives. The teachings of Hindu gurus were shared in a way that connected ancient wisdom with the challenges of modern life, making the message relevant for all generations, especially children and youths growing up in today’s fast-changing world.
 The conference also showcased the ongoing educational initiatives of BSRIA, including online courses introducing young learners to Hinduism and the Bhagavad Gita. These initiatives aim to help the next generation better understand Sanatan Hindu Dharma, its values, scriptures, traditions and relevance in daily life. Inspired by the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BSRIA continues to support learning, research and cultural understanding across the Pacific region.

/News/2026/Bal-Vikas-Parva-2026-Rajipo-3.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Art and Craft Session (27 photos)
 Sampark Abhiyan (27 photos)
 Talim Sabha (28 photos)
 Every year, during the summer vacation for children, the Bal Pravrutti Central Office organizes the Bal Vikas Parva. The initiative is designed to help children productively use their vacation time. It provides them an opportunity to develop their confidence, leadership and communication skills, teamwork, and creativity.
 This year, the 11-day Bal Vikas Parva was conducted at over 8519 bal and balika mandals throughout India, in which over 13377 balaks and 13443 balikas participated.
 As part of the program, the children underwent two days of training in public speaking, communication, arts and crafts, poster-making. Also, value-based presentations developed their sense of responsibility and guided them on practicing positive family values.
 They then participated in a nine-day outreach campaign titled ‘Adarsh Parivar Abhiyan’ (Ideal Family Campaign). Working in 4,829 teams, 26,820 children visited more than 128,000 families in their local communities and shared five simple yet powerful values for building happier and stronger families:
 Family prayer and spiritual reflection
 Eating at least one meal together
 Respecting and serving elders
 Speaking with kindness and understanding
 Conducting a daily family assembly (Ghar Sabha)
 Through this campaign, the families actively engaged in meaningful conversations about family harmony and communication, mutual respect, and shared values.
 The Bal Vikas Parva serves as a powerful platform for child development and empowers them to become confident ambassadors of positive values within their communities.

/News/2026/Beginning-the-Academic-Year-w.t: Beginning the Academic Year with Prayers and Values, Hong Kong, China
/News/2026/Beginning-the-Academic-Year-w.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Back-to-School Mahapuja (27 photos)
 On Sunday, 13 September 2026, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Hong Kong (China), held a special Back-to-School Mahapuja for students as they prepared to embark on a new academic year. The students gathered to offer prayers to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and seek the blessings of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj for wisdom, concentration, perseverance and success in their studies.
 The occasion was especially auspicious as it coincided with the celebration of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj’s Janma Jayanti. Inspired by his teachings, the students resolved to put his guidance into practice in their daily lives by maintaining samp (unity and harmony), refraining from abhav-avgun (seeing faults in others), and approaching their studies with sincerity, discipline and determination.
 During the Mahapuja, each balak and balika offered heartfelt prayers for the year ahead. Beyond academic achievement, they prayed for strength to develop good character, respect their parents and teachers, make wise choices, and remain firmly connected to satsang while fulfilling their school commitments.
 The programme reinforced an important message: success is nurtured through both sincere effort and faith
 Hard work + Prayers = Success
 With the blessings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, the students departed with renewed enthusiasm to study diligently, uphold their values, maintain unity and put their spiritual teachings into practice at school and in everyday life.

/News/2026/Brahmavihari-Swami-Receives-P.t: Brahmavihari Swami Receives Prestigious ‘Asmita Mahasanman Award’, Ahmedabad, India
/News/2026/Brahmavihari-Swami-Receives-P.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prestigious ‘Asmita Mahasanman Award’ (15 photos)
 On behalf of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Brahmavihari Swami was honored with the Asmita Mahasanman Award 2026, one of Gujarat’s most prestigious recognitions celebrating individuals whose contributions have enriched society and elevated the cultural and social identity of the state.
 The award was presented by the Honorable Chief Minister of Gujarat, Shri Bhupendra Patel, at a distinguished ceremony that brought together eminent personalities from diverse fields, recognizing their exceptional achievements and lasting contributions to society.
 Brahmavihari Swami was honored for his outstanding contributions to spirituality, humanitarian service, interfaith harmony, and the global promotion of Indian values and culture through BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. Over the years, he has represented BAPS and Hindu values at international forums, fostered dialogue among communities and faith traditions, and guided numerous humanitarian, educational, and social initiatives benefiting people across the world. His leadership has also been instrumental in landmark projects such as the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi and various international relief and community service efforts.
 The ceremony also honored other distinguished personalities, including entrepreneur Halkubhai Patel, renowned folk singer Farida Mir, acclaimed playback singer Aishwarya Majmudar, literary figure Dr. Devdanbhai Patel, educationist Rangjibhai Thakor, environmental conservationist Mohanbhai Thummar, industrialist Mukesh Patel, and other eminent contributors from the fields of arts, culture, education, industry, and public service.
 Accepting the honor, Brahmavihari Swami dedicated the award to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, and the countless volunteers and devotees of BAPS who selflessly serve society. Reflecting on the significance of the occasion, he shared that every talent, ability, and opportunity is a gift from God, and that when society honors individuals who use those gifts for the welfare of others, it is ultimately honoring God, the source of all such gifts.
 The awards ceremony celebrated individuals whose dedication, excellence, and commitment to society have created a lasting impact in their respective fields, inspiring future generations to contribute positively to their communities and the nation.

/News/2026/Care-in-Crisis---Comfort-in-K.t: Care in Crisis - Comfort in Kuwait, Middle East
/News/2026/Care-in-Crisis---Comfort-in-K.text:
This video documentary is a journey from the chaos in a war zone to the comfort of a home zone.
 Amid the uncertainty of war, a routine journey turned into a test of courage and faith. 'Comfort in Kuwait' is a true story of families stranded in Kuwait far from home, facing fear, confusion, and the unknown. Yet in those darkest moments, compassion prevailed. Through the selfless support of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi and its volunteers - who provided food, shelter, guidance, and emotional strength - the stranded travelers found hope, safety, and a path back home. This powerful story is a reminder that even in times of crisis, humanity, faith, and service can overcome fear, bring people together like family and light the path of our future.

/News/2026/Care-in-Crisis-BAPS-Hindu-Man.t: Care in Crisis: BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2026/Care-in-Crisis-BAPS-Hindu-Man.text:
Supporting the UAE Leadership's incredible efforts  in protecting and serving one and all during these difficult days of war,  the swamis at the BAPS Hindu Mandir Abu Dhabi remain engaged in prayer, service and care for the affected and needy.
 Prayer
 The swamis daily offer heartfelt prayers for peace, stability, safety and harmony for all.
 Food
 Alongside prayers, the swamis prepare food packets for the needy, serving with compassion and ensuring support reaches those in need.
 Counseling
 The swamis also connect to families across the region through phone calls and virtual gatherings, offering reassurance, courage and spiritual guidance.
 Inspiration
 Through regular interactions, volunteers are inspired to remain calm, united and steadfast in service.
 Coordination
 Under the leadership of Swami Brahmaviharidas, meetings with fellow swamis and key volunteers ensure that care, support and supplies reach those in need.
 Blessings
 HH Mahant Swami Maharaj has been calling the swamis in Abu Dhabi twice daily, providing blessings, guidance and  strength to continue serving.
 Region-wide
 Through committed BAPS volunteers, hundreds of individuals and families across the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman have received timely comfort, support and care.
 In times of conflict, prayer strengthens hearts, faith overcomes fear, service unites communities, and harmony inspires hope for peace and wellbeing for all.

/News/2026/Celebrating-International-Wom.t: Celebrating International Women’s Day 2026, UK & Europe
/News/2026/Celebrating-International-Wom.text:
BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK and across Europe observed the UN’s International Women’s Day with inspiring programmes in more than 30 centres around the region.
 International Women’s Day (IWD), which falls annually on 8 March, was ratified by the United Nations in 1977 to honour the significant contributions of women throughout the course of history.
 This year’s celebrations, titled “Celebrating Women: Give to Gain”, encouraged participants to reflect on how selfless actions can positively impact families, communities, and society.
 Inspired by the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to understand and appreciate the goodness in one another, the programmes highlighted the importance of patience, inclusivity, and kindness in everyday interactions.
 Through a blend of engaging presentations, reflective moments, and real-life experiences shared by women from the community, attendees explored how small yet meaningful acts of giving can lead to personal growth and collective harmony.
 Many programmes featured creative segments such as portrayals of mentor–mentee relationships, illustrating how both individuals grow through generosity, guidance, and mutual respect, as well as reflections on the wider impact of positive actions in helping others feel valued and included.
 Participants were also encouraged to consider simple commitments they could adopt in their daily lives – from offering a smile or kind word to someone new, to listening more attentively and supporting others with empathy and understanding.
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha’s celebration of IWD represents its ongoing commitment to women and matters of importance to women, as inspired and guided by BAPS’s spiritual leader, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.

 Confluence 2026 (101 photos)
 Around 117 delegates from throughout Australia and New Zealand attended the four-day ‘Pacific Rangvu Chhe Confluence 2026’ gathering organized by the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute Australia (BSRIA) in the presence of BAPS swamis.
 The event featured a panel session in which delegates from various fields of arts and music shared their insights and experiences, enlightening speeches by swamis, and in-depth discussions with professional artists and musicians that deepened the understanding of service and utilization of unique talents. 
 The event motivated participants to contribute to music and arts while embodying the principles of excellence and spirituality.

/News/2026/Croatian-Prime-Minister-Visit.t: Croatian Prime Minister Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India
/News/2026/Croatian-Prime-Minister-Visit.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Croatia’s Prime Minister H.E. Andrej Plenković Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham (13 photos)
 His Excellency Andrej Plenković, Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham with members of the official Croatian delegation attending the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi.
 The prime minister’s delegation included Damir Habijan, Minister of Justice, Public Administration and Digital Transformation; Zvonimir Frka-Petešić, Head of the Prime Minister’s Office (Chief of Staff); and other senior representatives of the Government of Croatia.
 The prime minister was traditionally welcomed by Divyamurtidas Swami and Gnanmunidas Swami. He offered respects in the Akshardham mahamandir and performed abhishek while praying for global peace, harmony, and the well-being of all communities.
 During the visit, a personal letter from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj was presented to Prime Minister Plenković, expressing appreciation for his visit and that it reflected respect for cultural and spiritual values. Mahant Swami Maharaj described Swaminarayan Akshardham as a symbol of faith and unity, offered prayers for the peace and prosperity of Croatia, and prayed for the prime minister’s health, wisdom, and continued leadership in service to his people.
 Appreciating the warm hospitality and the opportunity to experience India’s spiritual and cultural heritage, Prime Minister Plenković wrote in the visitor’s guest book: “It was a great honour for me and the Croatian delegation to visit the Swaminarayan Akshardham temple in New Delhi. I would like to extend my gratitude for the enchanting hospitality and the opportunity to visit this unique temple. This is an important part of Indian identity, which I greatly respect.”
 The visit reflected the spirit of dialogue, cultural understanding, and the growing partnership between Croatia and India, particularly in areas of innovation, governance, and international cooperation.

/News/2026/Estonias-President-Visits-Swa.t: Estonia’s President Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi, India
/News/2026/Estonias-President-Visits-Swa.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Estonia President's Visit (12 photos)
 His Excellency Alar Karis, President of the Republic of Estonia, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, accompanied by a distinguished delegation from Tallinn, Estonia.
 President Karis was joined by H.E. Ms. Marje Luup, Ambassador of the Republic of Estonia to India, senior officials from the Office of the President, members of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and representatives from Estonia’s digital and AI sector, including leadership from AI-Leap.
 On arrival, the president and his delegation were traditionally welcomed by Divyamrutidas  Swami, Gnanmunidas Swami and senior staff. They then paid their respects at the mandir, and performed abhishek, offering prayers for global peace, harmony, and the well-being of all communities. The delegation also experienced the cultural boat ride, gaining insights into India’s rich heritage, philosophy, and contributions to human progress.
 The visit reflected Estonia and India’s shared commitment to dialogue, innovation, and intercultural understanding, particularly in digital advancement and ethical development. The presence of senior officials from Estonia’s Digital and Cyber Diplomacy Department and AI-Leap underscored the importance of responsible technology and global cooperation.
 In a personal letter to President Karis, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj conveyed his gratitude to the president for his visit and offered prayers for the peace and prosperity of Estonia and its citizens, as well as for the president’s health and success. He also expressed hope that the friendly ties between Estonia and India continue to strengthen through mutual understanding and cooperation.
 Expressing his appreciation for the warm hospitality and the opportunity to experience India’s spiritual and cultural traditions in such an inspiring setting, President Karis wrote, “Thank you for the visit to the temple, and I do hope to come back. It has been very impressive. Let us hope for peace and very good relations between India and Estonia.”

/News/2026/Festival-of-Culture--Launch-o.t: Festival of Culture | Launch of Mandir Mahotsav, Paris, France
/News/2026/Festival-of-Culture--Launch-o.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Festival of Culture, Paris, France (8 photos)
 The ‘Festival of Culture’, a 13-day celebration in September marking the opening of BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, Paris – the first traditional Hindu temple in France – was launched globally in satsang assemblies around the world during the months of March and April.
 The historic global event, to be blessed by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, will take place from Wednesday 2 September to Monday 14 September 2026, in the Parisian district of Bussy-Saint-Georges.
 The launch announcement incorporated various video presentations, including a personal message from Yogvivekdas Swami, head swami for BAPS in the UK and across Europe, as well as a creative insight into the historical significance of the new mandir, and highlights of what to expect in the upcoming festival. Devotees and well-wishers from around the world have thus been warmly invited to convene in Paris, one of the world’s most beautiful cities, for a deeply spiritual and culturally uplifting experience.
 The ‘Festival of Culture’, celebrating the opening of the new mandir, will comprise a series of inspiring, joyous, and vibrant cultural events, including a Jal Yatra (boat procession along the River Seine), Nagar Yatra through Paris, Palkhi Yatra through Bussy-Saint-Georges, daily Vedic Mahayagna, murti-pratishtha ceremony and dedication assembly, women’s convention, musical tribute (kirtan aradhana), Mahant Swami Maharaj’s janma jayanti celebrations (by date), and various other programmes.
 Registration for the Festival is mandatory to help ensure a smooth experience for all participants.
 Further information about the ‘Festival of Culture’ programme, how to plan your visit, and how to register can be found at bapsmandirparis.fr. 
 To stay up to date with all the latest news and information about BAPS Paris Mandir and the Festival of Culture, be sure to follow the various social media accounts on X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Telegram.

Between 2 September and 14 September 2026, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj presided over the ‘Festival of Culture’ in Paris, a 13-day celebration marking the inauguration of the first traditional Hindu mandir in France.
 The occasion brought to fruition a vision fifty-six years in the making, first blessed by Yogiji Maharaj in 1970 during a stopover at Orly Airport, carried forward by Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the coming decades, and then guided to completion under Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Various inspiring programmes and family events were organised in his presence, focussing on nourishing faith, celebrating culture, and fostering harmony among people of diverse backgrounds.

/News/2026/Foundation-Stone-Laying-Cerem.t: Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony of the New BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Charlotte, NC, USA
/News/2026/Foundation-Stone-Laying-Cerem.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shila Pujan Ceremony (50 photos)
 Shilanyas, the foundation stone laying ceremony for the new BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Matthews, North Carolina, was celebrated with great reverence on May 31, 2026. The ceremony featured traditional Vedic rituals, sacred shlokas, and prayers conducted in the presence of BAPS swamis to consecrate the earth and mark the beginning of a new spiritual home for the greater Charlotte region.
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed the Charlotte community on two historic occasions. In 1996, he personally inaugurated the current BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Matthews, and in 2000, he again visited and offered prayers for the peace and progress of the entire region. The community, which first took root in the late 1970s, has since grown far beyond the capacity of its current space. Today, under the inspiring guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the current spiritual leader of BAPS, that long-cherished vision for a new, expanded Mandir has taken its first tangible form.
 The new Mandir will be a 72,000-square-foot, single-story facility featuring traditional shikars and ghumtis crafted in India. Designed to serve future generations, the campus will include a main assembly hall with seating for approximately 1,000 people, along with flexible space connected to the dining hall and gymnasium to accommodate larger events. The campus will provide 415 dedicated parking spaces, 16 classrooms for youth education, cultural learning, and community activities, as well as dedicated areas for daily darshan, arti, meditation, and spiritual assemblies. Site preparation began in July 2024, with vertical construction to follow. The Mandir is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2027 and will be open to all, welcoming people from every background.
 The Shila Pujan Ceremony was honored by the presence of several distinguished civic leaders from across the Charlotte-Matthews region, including Mayor of Matthews John Higdon, State Senator Woodson Bradley and Mr. William Bradley, Mayor Pro Tem of Matthews Susan Chambers, and Charlotte City Council Member At-Large Dimple Ajmera. In their addresses, the guests commended the BAPS community's longstanding contributions to the spiritual, cultural, and civic life of Matthews and Charlotte. They noted that the new Mandir will stand as a symbol of peace, service, and unity for the entire region.
 Guided by Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s principle, “In the joy of others, lies our own,” BAPS volunteers in Matthews and Charlotte have served the broader community for decades. Their efforts have included annual walkathons supporting local and national organizations such as Susan G. Komen and The Nature Conservancy, while also benefiting local groups including the Levine Senior Center, Rotary Club of Matthews, Matthews Free Clinic, and Kiwanis Club of Matthews. Volunteers have also organized regular blood drives, wellness screenings staffed by medical professionals, health awareness lectures, food bank partnerships, and hunger relief initiatives serving neighbors of all faiths and backgrounds. In addition, youth programs have focused on leadership development, health and wellness, character building, and community service.
 The Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony marks the first step toward realizing a vision that has been held in the hearts of the Matthews and greater Charlotte BAPS community for many years. The new Mandir will serve as a place of peace, devotion, and service, standing as a beacon of spirituality and harmony for generations to come.

/News/2026/Four-Million-Hearts-One-Messa.t: Four Million Hearts, One Message of Harmony: BAPS Hindu Mandir Celebrates 2nd Anniversary, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2026/Four-Million-Hearts-One-Messa.text:
Photo Gallery 
 2nd Anniversary Celebration (126 photos)
 More than 8,000 devotees and over 1,500 participants visited the special ‘Mandir Talks at 2’ assembly to celebrate the 2nd anniversary of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, marking two years of spiritual service, community connection and cultural harmony. The strong turnout reflected the community’s deep connection to the mandir and its growing role as a center for cultural and spiritual enrichment.
 This year’s theme, ‘Mandir: Our Family, Our Future’, brought together community leaders, diplomats, families and children to reflect on the Mandir’s enduring role as a home of peace, values and harmony in the UAE.
 The evening opened with kirtan bhakti by BAPS volunteers and community members. Then, welcoming everyone on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Swami Brahmaviharidas compared the evolution of the Mandir to that of a newborn child. He explained that a baby begins to walk at one and but only begins to speak at two, “To the four million visitors it has welcomed in just two years – devotees, dignitaries, tourists, ambassadors and diplomats – from more than one hundred countries, its message has consistently been one of harmony. The former Ambassador of Egypt remarked on seeing a carving depicting Egyptian civilization on the Mandir wall, ‘The pyramids are great because they speak of the past. The Mandir is equally great because it speaks to the future. Without harmony, we will have no future.’ By the third year, at the age of three, the Mandir will set you free.”
 Swami Brahmviharidas went on to share how families express deep gratitude for the Mandir and the country that made it possible, “Before, people had to travel to India; now India has come here. Families express deep gratitude to the UAE’s rulers and to the Mandir itself, saying that while the UAE once felt like a home away from home, it has now truly become home within our home.”
 Then, H.E. Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan was honored for his longstanding commitment to cultural coexistence and social unity in the UAE. In his address, he noted, “This splendid temple stands not only as a place of worship, but as a powerful symbol of shared human values. This remarkable temple is also a powerful symbol of the deep and enduring friendship between India and the United Arab Emirates. It stands as a bridge between us, strengthening mutual understanding and deepening goodwill between our two nations.”
 Praising the ruler of the UAE, H.E. Sheikh Nahyan said, “We are immensely proud of His Highness’s leadership, which calls on all people of every faith, culture, and background to look beyond our differences and recognize the fundamental unity of humankind. May this Mandir continue to be a source of spiritual strength, moral guidance, and community uplift for many generations to come.”
 The ‘Mandir Talks’ programme featured segments exploring the Mandir’s impact across the world, within families, across communities, and into the future.
 In ‘Mandir Talks to the World’, international voices reflected on the Mandir’s universal message.
 H.E. Dr. Deepak Mittal, Ambassador of India to the UAE, described the Mandir as a place of gratitude for the Indian community, linking heritage with the future and strengthening ties between India and the UAE for generations to come. He noted that the Mandir is shaped not only by stone, but by friendship and culture, with its intricate details reflecting a shared commitment to coexistence.
 H.E. Patricio Broughton, Ambassador of Chile to the UAE, described the Mandir as a reflection of universal values, where respect and responsibility across faiths strengthen social cohesion and human fraternity.
 Mr Udaya Indrarathna, former Ambassador of Sri Lanka to the UAE, spoke of the Mandir as a cultural bridge, shaped as much by friendship as by architecture.
 In ‘Mandir Talks to the Families’, a beautifully curated interactive audiovisual conversation captured and showcased how the Mandir has become a space that feels like another home, bringing families closer together.
 Parents spoke of children moving freely, elders pausing without hurry, and visitors staying longer because the space felt welcoming. Families shared that before the Mandir, celebrations were often kept within the home, while today they feel comfortable celebrating more openly, with a deeper sense of connection. Acts of service such as Annakut seva were highlighted as meaningful bonding moments, particularly during preparation, when families work side by side and enjoy the shared effort.
 In ‘Mandir Talks to the Communities’, community leaders reflected on the Mandir’s role as a welcoming home for traditions, rituals and cultural identity.
 The discussions highlighted how the Mandir has become a unifying hub where diverse communities gather, celebrate festivals together, and preserve heritage while strengthening social bonds. Speakers noted that the Mandir fosters inclusion, simplifies community life, and provides a shared space where values, service and belonging naturally come together.
 ‘Mandir Talks to the Future’ brought forward the voices of children, whose reflections on goodness, respect and responsibility illustrated how the Mandir continues shaping young hearts with purpose, understanding and positivity.
 The evening concluded with children leading the audience in four collective pledges for Self-Positivity, Family Values, National Harmony and Environmental Responsibility, symbolizing the Mandir’s mission to inspire individuals, strengthen families, unite communities, and cultivate a better world for future generations.
 The second anniversary of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi reaffirmed its growing role as a global symbol of harmony, peacefully housed within the UAE. Through reflections on family, community and the future, the evening highlighted how the Mandir continues to serve not only as a place of worship, but as a living space where traditions are preserved, relationships are strengthened and generations are inspired. As the Mandir enters its third year, it stands as a powerful reminder of the UAE’s commitment to coexistence and of the enduring belief that faith, service and harmony can help build a more united and hopeful world.
