/News/2026/From-Vision-to-Fruition--The-.t: From Vision to Fruition | The Remarkable Creation Story of BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, Paris, France
/News/2026/From-Vision-to-Fruition--The-.text:
From the earth of Bharat to the skyline of Paris – this is the story of how stone became a mandir, and a fifty-six-year prayer became reality.
 On 6 September 2026, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj consecrated BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, Paris – France’s first traditionally designed Hindu temple – in a sacred ceremony at Bussy-Saint-Georges. This short film tells the journey that made that moment possible.
 It begins with the birth of the stone itself, hand-carved in India by generations of artisans who shape it ‘like a prayer’ – chisel by chisel, breath by breath. It follows that stone across seas and borders to France, where it meets a new lineage of craftsmen – including masons who once worked on the restoration of Notre-Dame de Paris – who measure it, align it, and carry the work forward with their own knowledge and history. And it arrives, finally, at the moment two crafts and two cultures become one creation: Made in India, Built in France.
 Told through narration and an original score woven through English, French, Hindi and Gujarati – voiced in part by two children, one of Bharat and one of France, discovering the story together – this is more than the record of a building rising; it is the story of a sankalp first blessed by Yogiji Maharaj in 1970, carried forward by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and brought to fruition under Mahant Swami Maharaj: a new lamp, lit in the City of Light, for the world.
 Subtitles available in English, Français, हिन्दी and ગુજરાતી.

/News/2026/Guinness-World-Records-Recogn.t: Guinness World Records Recognises World’s Longest Biography by a Single Author, London, UK
/News/2026/Guinness-World-Records-Recogn.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Guinness World Record (8 photos)
 A monumental 13-volume biography spanning 8,848 pages and comprising 2,146,447 words on His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj has been officially recognised by Guinness World Records as the longest biography by a single author.
 Authored by Sanskrit scholar Sadhu Adarshjivandas, PhD, Brahmaswarup Shri Pramukh Swami Maharaj: Vistrut Jivan ane Karya chronicles the extraordinary 95-year life and legacy of Pramukh Swami Maharaj (1921–2016), the late spiritual leader of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.
 The biography traces Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life from his birth in 1921 through to his passing in 2016, documenting his spiritual leadership, profound humility, selfless service, and devotion, as well as his extensive work serving and inspiring individuals and communities around the world. The work was researched and written over an intensive 38-month period between July 2017 and August 2020.
 The Guinness World Records certificate was presented to His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj at OVO Arena Wembley on Sunday 4 October 2026, during celebrations marking his 93rd birth anniversary. More than 10,500 people at the arena witnessed the historic presentation, with tens of thousands more watching via a live webcast around the world.
 Carl Saville, Senior Adjudicator who presented the certificate, said, “Today’s presentation for the ‘Longest Biography by a Single Author’ has been a true pleasure, privilege, and honour to deliver on behalf of Guinness World Records.
 “Guinness World Records’ main objective, as a brand, is to document the incredible from around the world, to share unique and special achievements which, ultimately, no one else on earth has managed to achieve to date, so what a powerful relevance to this specific title which has been documented over a whole lifetime.”
 Reflecting on the achievement, Sadhu Adarshjivandas added, “The subject of this biography is infinitely more important than the author. His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj lived a life defined by deep spirituality, profound humility, and an unwavering commitment to global harmony, compassion, and empathy. It was an honour and a privilege to chronicle his divine life and enduring legacy.”
 More than a record of extraordinary literary scale, the biography represents an extensive historical archive of a life dedicated to spirituality, service, and the well-being of others, preserving Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life and work for present and future generations. More than 310,000 copies of the volumes have already been sold.
 Click here to view an insightful documentary exploring the history, making, and significance of Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s biography as one of the most important scriptures of our generation.

/News/2026/His-Holiness-Mahant-Swami-Mah.t: His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in Paris 2026, Paris, France
/News/2026/His-Holiness-Mahant-Swami-Mah.text:
His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj has arrived in Paris, France. He will be presiding over the Festival of Culture, a 13-day celebration marking the inauguration of the first traditional Hindu mandir in France, commencing on Wednesday 2 September 2026.
 The occasion brings to fruition a vision fifty-six years in the making, first blessed by Yogiji Maharaj in 1970 during a stopover at Orly Airport, carried forward by Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the coming decades, and now guided to completion under Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Various inspiring programmes and family events have been organised in his presence, focussing on nourishing faith, celebrating culture, and fostering harmony among people of diverse backgrounds.
 These events include a Jal Yatra (a boat procession along the River Seine), a Nagar Yatra through central Paris, a Palkhi Yatra through Bussy-Saint-Georges, a daily Vedic Mahayagna, the murti-pratishtha ceremony and dedication assembly, a women’s convention, a kirtan aradhana, and celebrations for Mahant Swami Maharaj’s janma jayanti (by date).
 For detailed information about Mahant Swami Maharaj’s presence in Paris and the Festival of Culture, please visit bapsmandirparis.fr. In particular, the What’s On calendar provides a schedule of all events, including public puja darshan, ceremonies, yatras, and evening programmes. 
 Mahant Swami Maharaj’s morning puja and evening assemblies will be streamed live on certain days. These will be available for viewing at live.baps.org. 
 The latest news and updates about the Mandir and the Festival of Culture will also be available from BAPS Paris’s Telegram channel and other social media accounts: X, Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn.
 Stay connected through these various platforms to be a part of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s historic vicharan in Paris, France.
 As a devotional tribute to his guru in fulfilling that vision from 1970, Mahant Swami Maharaj has called this vicharan “Yogi Anjali Yatra”.

/News/2026/Historic-Pratham-Shila-Pujan-.t: Historic Pratham Shila Pujan Held for Tapomurti Nilkanth Varni Maharaj, London, UK
/News/2026/Historic-Pratham-Shila-Pujan-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Tapomurti Nilkanth Varni Pratham Shila Pujan, London, UK (90 photos)
 Hundreds of devotees gathered at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Monday 6 April 2026 to participate in the Pratham Shila Pujan (first ceremonial offering of the foundation stones) for Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj, marking the commencement of a historic project that will inspire generations to come.
 The ceremony followed the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who, on 15 March 2026 in Sarangpur, India, sanctified the foundation stones for the Tapomurti project and blessed the bricks that would form its foundation.
 In the weeks leading up to the ceremony, devotees had the opportunity to write personal prayers on their individual bricks before placing them in their respective ghar mandirs. During the Pratham Shila Pujan, families reverently offered these sanctified bricks, symbolically embedding their prayers, faith and devotion into the foundation of this sacred project and becoming part of a lasting spiritual legacy.
 Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj will depict the youthful, ascetic form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan during his remarkable pilgrimage across India. Standing 42 feet tall, the murti will serve as an enduring symbol of unwavering faith, spiritual discipline, loving compassion, and selfless service. His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj will perform the murti’s pratishtha (consecration ceremony) on Sunday 20 September 2026, marking another historic milestone in the spiritual journey of BAPS in the United Kingdom.
 As the first bricks were reverently placed into the foundation, the ceremony marked not only the beginning of construction but also the collective offering of countless individuals united in devotion and prayer. The occasion provided a unique opportunity for families across generations to personally participate in a sacred milestone that will remain embedded within the very foundations of the Tapomurti.
 Reflecting on the occasion, Arpan Patel, one of the volunteers who is leading the construction project, shared, “Through the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, devotees were able to offer not just a brick, but their heartfelt prayers and devotion into the foundation of Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj. It was deeply moving to see entire families come together to participate in this historic moment, knowing that the Tapomurti will inspire countless people for generations to come with the timeless ideals of faith, devotion, courage, and selfless service that he emobodied.”

/News/2026/Inauguration-of-Akshar-Purush.t: Inauguration of Akshar-Purushottam Sanskrit Pathshala, London, UK
/News/2026/Inauguration-of-Akshar-Purush.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Inauguration of Sanskrit Pathshala in London (16 photos)
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj inaugurated the Akshar-Purushottam Sanskrit Pathshala at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – on Sunday 11 October 2026, fulfilling a vision inspired by his guru, Yogiji Maharaj, to encourage the study and use of Sanskrit among children and young people.
 Earlier, Mahant Swami Maharaj had expressed his wish in a specially written letter for a Sanskrit pathshala (traditional school) to be established at the Mandir during his visit to London. The inauguration marked the fulfilment of that resolve and, as Dr Ankur Barua, Senior Lecturer in Hindu Studies at the University of Cambridge, observed, “an important milestone in the preservation and promotion of Sanskrit within the UK.”
 Addressing the assembly, Mahamahopadhyay Bhadreshdas Swami reflected on the longstanding tradition of Sanskrit learning and scholarship within the Swaminarayan Sampradaya. From the composition of scriptures during the lifetime of Bhagwan Swaminarayan to the encouragement of Sanskrit studies by Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, he highlighted the spiritual and scholarly legacy upon which the new pathshala would build.
 Bhadreshdas Swami also shared Mahant Swami Maharaj’s aspiration for children, teenagers and young adults, both boys and girls, in the UK to learn and converse in Sanskrit. He revealed that Mahant Swami Maharaj had personally named the new institution ‘Akshar-Purushottam Sanskrit Pathshala’, drawing an enthusiastic response from the assembly.
 The occasion was particularly significant, with around 400 young students already engaged in Sanskrit learning ready to enrol in the pathshala, reflecting strong enthusiasm and a solid foundation for the initiative.
 In his blessings, Mahant Swami Maharaj spoke in Sanskrit, expressing his appreciation for the sacred language and encouraging its study. He explained how Sanskrit learning would help spread a deeper understanding of Sanatan Hindu values and strengthen the spiritual foundations of future generations.
 Scholars, teachers, and community leaders in the UK have warmly welcomed news of the pathshala, also sharing hope, enthusiasm, and support for the future.
 The inauguration of Akshar-Purushottam Sanskrit Pathshala marks a meaningful new chapter in Sanskrit education at Neasden Temple, nurturing linguistic scholarship, spiritual understanding, and the enduring vision of Mahant Swami Maharaj for generations to come.

/News/2026/Jal-Yatra--Festival-of-Cultur.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Jal Yatra | Festival of Culture, Paris (95 photos)
 More than 5,500 participants from around the world joined a historic ‘Jal Yatra’ – cultural boat procession – on the River Seine in Paris, France, on 3 September 2026.
 It formed one of the most memorable celebrations of the 13-day Festival of Culture (Paris Mandir Mahotsav), marking the inauguration of BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, Paris – France’s first traditional Hindu stone temple.
 A magnificent flotilla of 11 beautifully decorated boats, adorned with Indian cultural décor, flowers, and Indian and French flags, stretched for almost one kilometre through the heart of Paris, carrying a timeless message of fraternity, peace, and harmony. The procession became the largest coordinated flotilla to sail the River Seine since the Opening Ceremony of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.
 Brahmaviharidas Swami, head sadhu of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, said during the opening ceremony, “The River Seine carries the history, inspiration and aspirations of France. The Jal Yatra brings to it the sacred prayers and traditions of the Hindu faith. Together, they express a shared hope for peace and for the friendship between France and India.”
 Accompanied by devotional music and joyful celebrations, the procession passed some of Paris’s most iconic landmarks, including the Eiffel Tower, Musée d’Orsay, Notre-Dame Cathedral, and Louvre Museum. Residents, visitors and tourists lined the riverbanks and bridges to watch, photograph and enjoy the vibrant procession, as the spirit of the Festival extended into the heart of the French capital. For the passengers aboard the boats, volunteers provided a brief history of the landmarks and inspirational connections with the BAPS tradition.
 Inspired by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s historic journey along the River Seine in 1997, the Jal Yatra rekindled a treasured chapter in the history of BAPS in France. Nearly three decades after Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s memorable journey, devotees retraced that voyage with the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, creating new memories while honouring the vision, prayers and values that have inspired generations and culminated in the new mandir.
 Vipul Buddhdev, whose family had travelled from San Jose, USA, to participate in this celebration, reflected, “The atmosphere throughout the journey was incredible Everywhere you looked, people were smiling, waving,… just enjoying the experience together. It was a wonderful living example of fraternity and harmony – values so embedded in French and Hindu culture – here in the very heart of this beautiful city of Paris.”

The Leadership Summit was held at over 50 centers throughout North America, bringing together students, parents, and professionals for a shared learning experience centered on the theme “Be the Best.”
 Inspired by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj's guidance and the message “Do your best and leave the rest,” the event encouraged attendees to give their full effort to education and career pursuits while remaining grounded, humble, and purpose-driven. The theme emphasized striving for excellence across all areas of life, recognizing that growth comes through effort, persistence, and faith.
 The program included a keynote that introduced the theme and encouraged students and parents to stay curious, become lifelong learners, and build the confidence to ask thoughtful, meaningful questions in an ever-changing academic and professional landscape. It also featured a career panel where professionals and students shared real journeys, pivots, and lessons learned, highlighting the wide range of pathways ahead.
 Professionals who volunteered to represent their fields participated in a breakout session focused on authentic networking and the importance of building strong connections to support the next generation. Parents also had a dedicated panel discussion this year, hearing a broad range of experiences and practical advice on supporting their children through education decisions, finances, and major life transitions.
 Students also had the opportunity to take part in a networking session where they could ask questions and connect with professionals in a real-world setting designed to spark curiosity and jump-start their network. Across North America, the Leadership Summit inspired students and parents alike to pursue excellence, seek guidance, and approach the journey ahead with confidence and purpose.

/News/2026/Launch-of-the-Become-Adarsh-P.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Launch of the ‘Become Adarsh’ Program (25 photos)
 The BAPS Children’s Activities Central Office officially launched the ‘Become Adarsh’ program for school students in the Jabalpur district during a convention attended by over 3,500 principals and teachers from across the region.
 The Become Adarsh project aims to instill strong moral values and provide value-based education to school students through: Digital Learning – in which schools receive monthly inspirational videos and resources via the Become Adarsh mobile application, and Holistic Development – since the curriculum focuses on the all-round personality and character development of students.
 The convention included an address by Jnannayandas Swami emphasizing that the true essence of education lies in building character and culture.
 Teachers were provided with a roadmap on how to effectively implement this BAPS initiative to build a strong moral foundation for their students. The event concluded with the national anthem and a collective pledge to build a bright and ethical future for India.
 Among the dignitaries present were Shri Raghavendra Singh (District Collector), Shri Ghanshyam Soni (District Education Officer), Shri Yogesh Sharma (D.P.C.), Shri Ashok Rohani (MLA, Jabalpur), and Shri Ratnesh Sonkar (City BJP President).
 Guest Experiences
 Shri Raghavendra Singh (Collector, Jabalpur): "This project is designed to transform an ideal student into an ideal citizen."
 Shri Ashok Rohani (MLA, Jabalpur): "This project is a necessity for society and should be started in every school. It will definitely provide the right guidance to the next generation."
 Shri Ghanshyam Soni (DEO, Jabalpur): "This project will be very helpful in implementing the National Education Policy (NEP-2020)."

/News/2026/London-to-Paris-Charity-Cycle.t: London to Paris Charity Cycle Ride Supports Historic Paris Mandir Opening, UK & Europe
/News/2026/London-to-Paris-Charity-Cycle.text:
Photo Gallery 
 London to Paris Charity Cycle Ride (48 photos)
 Demonstrating endurance, determination, and a shared sense of purpose, 15 cyclists successfully completed a 315-kilometre charity cycle ride from London to Paris in support of the forthcoming inauguration of BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in the suburbs of Paris later this year.
 The four-day journey began with prayers and blessings in London before the riders set off from South London. Cycling through the English countryside to Newhaven, the group crossed the English Channel by ferry before continuing their journey through northern France.
 Over the following three days, the cyclists travelled through picturesque towns and rural landscapes, covering a further 239 kilometres en route to Paris. The ride brought together participants from across generations, with riders ranging in age from 18 to 75, united by a common goal of supporting the Paris Mandir project while promoting healthy living, teamwork, and community spirit.
 The event was designed not as a competition, but as an opportunity to encourage participation, personal achievement, and friendship. Throughout the journey, riders supported one another through every challenge, creating lasting memories and strengthening bonds across the wider BAPS community.
 As the cyclists approached Paris, they were joined by 11 local riders for the final stage from the Eiffel Tower to BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Bussy-Saint-Georges. Upon arrival, they received a warm welcome from swamis and hundreds of devotees who had gathered to celebrate the completion of the challenge.
 One participant shared, “This whole journey was exceptionally well organised, with every detail carefully planned. Completing the challenge was only possible because of the commitment, encouragement, and teamwork of everyone involved.”
 The cycle ride forms part of the wider preparations for the historic opening of BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris in September 2026. Inspired by the vision of His Holiness Yogiji Maharaj and guided through the continued efforts of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the Mandir stands as a testament to decades of devotion, service, and community endeavour across Europe.

/News/2026/M%C4%81r%C4%81-S%C4%81ch%C4%8.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Kishori Din (48 photos)
 Young women from across the UK gathered at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Sunday 20 September 2026 for a special Kishori Din organised as part of the programmes accompanying His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visit to the UK.
 Themed ‘Mārā Sāchā Chho Sanehi: My Forever Companion’, the programme explored the enduring bond that young devotees share with Mahant Swami Maharaj – recognising him as a constant source of love, guidance and strength who inspires them towards Bhagwan Swaminarayan and a deeper spiritual life.
 Through a series of interactive presentations, discussions, videos and devotional activities, the day explored three expressions of this relationship. Letters from Mahant Swami Maharaj demonstrated how his words can offer personal guidance, reassurance and strength, while smruti (cherished memories) explored how recalling moments with him can sustain a sense of connection even when physically apart.
 The final theme reflected on the many spiritual gifts and blessings received through faith, particularly the privilege of worshipping Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj.
 The programme culminated with each kishori having an opportunity for a personal moment of devotion before Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, allowing them to reflect on their faith and their relationship with God.
 Together, the three experiences expressed a simple but deeply personal message: through his letters, he spoke to me; through smruti, he never left me; and through his gifts, he remembered me – inspiring each kishori to recognise Mahant Swami Maharaj as her sāchā sanehi: her true, loving, forever companion.

/News/2026/Maha-Shivaratri-Celebrations-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Maha-Shivaratri Celebrations, UK & Europe (100 photos)
 BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha celebrated the Hindu festival of Maha-Shivaratri with various devotional activities on Sunday 15 February 2026.
 Maha-Shivaratri is the sacred day in the Hindu calendar that marks the divine manifestation of Shankar Bhagwan in his Shivaling form, his celestial wedding with Mata Parvatiji, and his divine Tandava dance.
 Devotees, well-wishers, and members of local Hindu communities gathered in large numbers at BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK and parts of Europe to celebrate the sacred occasion.
 The festival was observed with fasting, prayers, chanting of the ‘Aum Namah Shivaya’ mantra, and annakut offerings. Swamis and devotees also bathed the Shivaling with panchamrut (a holy mixture of milk, yoghurt, honey, sugar and ghee) and offered bilva-patra (bael leaves) during which they prayed for the well-being, protection, and success of people across the world.
 An ice Shivaling, symbolising the manifestation of Shiva Bhagwan, was also presented at various mandirs, providing a reminder of the sacred pilgrimage town of Amarnath in India where a natural ice Shivaling exists.

/News/2026/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-Joyously.t: Mahant Swami Maharaj Joyously Welcomed in London, UK
/News/2026/Mahant-Swami-Maharaj-Joyously.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Arrival in London (40 photos)
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived in London on Wednesday 16 September 2026, beginning a month-long spiritual visit eagerly anticipated by thousands of devotees across the UK.
 His arrival came just days after he inaugurated BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, Paris – France’s first traditional Hindu stone mandir – following a landmark 13-day ‘Festival of Culture’ that brought together people from across France, Europe and around the world through faith, culture, service and friendship.
 Travelling from Paris, Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden shortly before 6.30pm.
 Thousands of devotees had gathered at the Mandir to welcome him back to London after more than three years. Flags filled the courtyard as drums sounded and children and youths performed celebratory dances, creating a vibrant welcome for his arrival.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj first proceeded to the Mandir for darshan, then made his way to the assembly hall. His entrance was met with cheers of joy and jubilation as devotees, young and old, warmly welcomed their guru back to London. Children greeted him by holding colourful signs of welcome. In a touching moment, Mahant Swami Maharaj held one of the signs and sanctified it, to the delight of the children and those watching.
 Reflecting the affection and longstanding connection he shares with devotees in the UK, Mahant Swami Maharaj expressed simply that he had “arrived home”.
 The words carried particular meaning after a three-year wait. Mahant Swami Maharaj last visited London in 2023, and his return – at the age of 93 – marked the beginning of several cherished weeks in his presence, with a series of devotional, spiritual and cultural programmes bringing together devotees of all generations from across the UK and beyond.
 All the latest news and updates about Mahant Swami Maharaj’s stay at Neasden Temple (London Mandir), including live webcasts, will be available from msm.neasdentemple.org and the Neasden Temple Telegram channel.

/News/2026/Mahant-Swami-Maharajs-92nd-Bi.t: Mahant Swami Maharaj's 92nd Birthday Celebration, Atladara (Vadodara), India
/News/2026/Mahant-Swami-Maharajs-92nd-Bi.text:
12:00
 92nd Birthday Celebration Assembly (Highlights)
 3:26:37
 92nd Birthday Celebration Assembly (Live)
 Photo Gallery 
 Arrival of Bal Vidvans (37 photos)
 Guinness World Record (60 photos)
 92nd Birthday Celebration Assembly (142 photos)
 Bal-Balika Vidvans Samip Darshan (25 photos)
 From 5.00 pm to 8. 15 pm, a vast open ground near APMC Market on National Highway 48, Vadodara, became the venue of a spectacular celebration for the 92nd birthday of Mahant Swami Maharaj. It was celebrated with profound spiritual splendour. Nearly 200,000 devotees, well-wishers and around 800 BAPS swamis from India and abroad assembled to offer heartfelt tributes to Swamishri’s exemplary saintliness and selfless community services.
 The colourful stage backdrop comprised giant decorated suns with photos of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru Parampara, symbolizing the timeless source of divine light, compassion, and guidance for humanity.
 The programme commenced with dhun and kirtan by BAPS swamis and youths, followed by a graceful thematic welcome dance for Swamishri.
 The celebration was themed ‘Vande Guruparamparam, Vande Mahant Swaminam’, which portrayed the unbroken flow of divine wisdom from Bhagwan Swaminarayan to the present guru Mahant Swami Maharaj. After each drama performance, related to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru Parampara, senior BAPS swamis delivered inspiring thematic discourses that highlighted the divine life, virtues, and contributions of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Bhagwan Swaminarayan: Transformative Divine Presence
 The opening segment unfolded with a drama about the transformative impact of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The Gujarati literary stalwart Kavi Shri Dalpatram narrated his experience of the divine radiance of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The presentation also briefly portrayed how Shriji Maharaj’s divinity transformed the dacoit Joban Pagi.
 Aksharvatsaldas Swami then elaborated in his speech about Mahant’s Swami Maharaj’s divine impact on individuals and transformatory works in society.
 Gunatitanand Swami: Power of His Speech
 The next chapter highlighted the spiritual power of Gunatitanand Swami’s speech through a drama. Maharaja of Gondal Bhagvatsinhji narrated his profound experience about Swami’s discourses.
 Atmatruptdas Swami related this legacy to the present, sharing incidents about how Mahant Swami Maharaj’s gentle yet spiritually powerful words impact the lives of countless aspirants.
 Bhagatji Maharaj: His Brahmisthiti
 The brahmisthiti (God-realized state) of Bhagatji Maharaj was portrayed through a drama about the renowned Sanskrit scholar Rangacharya’s testament.
 Anandswarupdas Swami elaborated upon the presentation through incidents about Mahant Swami Maharaj’s God-realized state.
 Shastriji Maharaj: Loyalty to Upasana
 A powerful mime presentation by youths, based on Brahmanand Swami’s bhajan ‘Tek na mele re…’, portrayed Shastriji Maharaj’s unwavering resolve to uphold the Akshar-Purushottam siddhant in the face of stiff opposition. A drama presentation portrayed Shri Gulzarilal Nanda, former Prime Minister of India and Bharat Ratna awardee, sharing his personal account of Shastriji Maharaj’s indomitable spirit, moral courage, uncompromising adherence to truth, and as a living embodiment of Satyameva Jayate.
 A video presentation reflected Shastriji Maharaj’s spiritual conviction today through Mahant Swami Maharaj, who remains firmly rooted in principles while guiding the BAPS Sanstha with quiet strength and humility.
 Yogiji Maharaj: His Touching Humility
 The monumental humility of Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj was portrayed through a reflection by Padma Shri Dula Bhaya Kag, the celebrated Gujarati poet. A rendition of his bhajan ‘Jogi joyā jovā nu kāi na rahyu re…’ with an animated raas dance set the tempo of the story.
 Building on this, Bhagwatsetudas Swami highlighted how Mahant Swami Maharaj continues Yogiji Maharaj’s vision today by nurturing children with values, spirituality, and character. He underscored how Mahant Swami Maharaj inspired over 15,000 children to memorize the Satsang Diksha shastra.
 Children Living the Satsang Diksha: Values in Action
 A deeply touching programme, anchored by Shri Dilipbhai Joshi, showcased how children, inspired by Mahant Swami Maharaj to memorize 315 slokas of the Satsang Diksha, imbibed the values of honesty, respect for parents, and hard work. Through video narratives and live presentations, children and families shared how these teachings transformed their lives and inspired others to pursue a value-based and spiritual life.
 Each virtue was supported by children reciting appropriate Sanskrit shlokas from the Satsang Diksha, illustrating how scriptural wisdom is being lived under the inspiration of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Pramukh Swami Maharaj: His Purity and Transformative Power
 A short, riveting drama unfolded on the stage with a youth playing the role of Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. Mr Kalam shared his experiences of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and claimed him to be his ultimate teacher and praised his profound humility.
 Brahmaviharidas Swami narrated how the same humility shines through Mahant Swami Maharaj, who attributes all success to Bhagwan and the Guru Parampara and identifies himself simply as “das na das.”
 Guinness World Records Recognition
 A historic highlight of the evening celebration was the formal recognition by Guinness World Records for the ‘Largest Simultaneous Hindu Text Recitation’. Inspired by Mahant Swami Maharaj, over 15,000 children memorized all 315 Sanskrit shlokas of the Satsang Diksha within one year. Of these, 12,723 children present were acknowledged by officials of the Guinness World Records.
 The honour was presented to Mahant Swami Maharaj by the adjudicator Mr Swapnil Dangarikar.
 Addresses by Chief Guests
 A message from the Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah was read during the assembly.
 The Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Shri Mohan Yadav praised the Guru Parampara as an elixir and highlighted Mahant Swami Maharaj’s role in connecting the world with Sanatan values through satsang and service.
 The Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Patel shared that satsang offered practical solutions to life’s challenges and described Mahant Swami Maharaj’s leadership as one that builds hearts and strengthens the three pillars of Sanatan Dharma, namely, saints, scriptures, and mandirs.
 Pujya Doctor Swami shared, “May we live in accordance with the teachings prescribed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru Parampara. If we uphold unity and harmony, success and peace will surely follow.”

 Release of ‘Hetna Hastakshar’ calendar on baps.store.
 Dedication of a mobile school for the education of tribal children in Sabarkantha district, Gujarat.
 Blessings of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj
 The celebration climaxed with Mahant Swami Maharaj’s blessings. He humbly offered all honour and recognition at the feet of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Guru Parampara. Swamishri said, “All this has happened by Bhagwan’s grace and compassion. He alone is the doer; we do nothing. Shastriji Maharaj established this Sanstha through Herculean efforts. Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj carried it forward.
 “Whatever honour bestowed here today I offer at the feet of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and all the Gunatit gurus. This recognition belongs to the children, swamis, volunteers, and parents. They have all worked tirelessly and with devotion.”
 The Mahotsav concluded with the rituals of mantra-pushpanjali and arti. The devotees departed, inspired to live with humility, faith, unity, and selfless service as exemplified by Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Collective Effort
 Preparations for the celebration spanned over three months, involving hundreds of BAPS swamis and 14,000 volunteers in 34 departments. The Vadodara Municipal Corporation provided generous support for security, safety, and civic services.
 Devotees worldwide joined the celebration through live broadcasts on live.baps.org and Aastha Bhajan channel.

/News/2026/Mahant-Swami-Maharajs-93rd-Ja.t: Mahant Swami Maharaj’s 93rd Janma Jayanti Mahotsav, London, UK
/News/2026/Mahant-Swami-Maharajs-93rd-Ja.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Arrival & Opening (30 photos)
 Chapter 1: In Our Eyes (60 photos)
 Chapter 2: In His Eyes (30 photos)
 Chapter 3: In God’s Eyes (30 photos)
 Guinness World Record (10 photos)
 Conclusion & Finale (30 photos)
 More than 10,500 devotees and well-wishers from across the UK and around the world gathered at the OVO Arena Wembley on Sunday 4 October to celebrate the 93rd birth anniversary of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Tens of thousands more joined via a worldwide live webcast.
 Titled ‘Pratyaksh: Before Our Eyes’, the celebration explored Mahant Swami Maharaj’s life, character and spiritual identity through personal testimonies, historic footage and handwritten letters as well as music, dance, and immersive visual presentations.
 The first part, ‘In Our Eyes’, traced his journey from his childhood as Vinubhai through his years as Vinu Bhagat and Sadhu Keshavjivandas to his present role as the guru of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. A video dialogue with his friend Herald offered affectionate insights into his younger years, while senior swamis shared first-hand memories from different periods of his life.
 Ishwarcharandas Swami recalled the qualities he had observed in Vinu Bhagat, while Viveksagardas Swami reflected on his years as a swami, recalling his wholehearted dedication to seva and personal affection. The programme then turned to Mahant Swami Maharaj’s first ten years as guru, looking beyond the remarkable scale of his travels and responsibilities to the dedication, compassion and spirituality that lie behind each and every one of his works.
 After a vibrant ceremonial welcome, Mahant Swami Maharaj entered the arena to an outpouring of devotion and celebration. The occasion was especially historic, marking the first time in 56 years that devotees in London had been able to celebrate the birthday of the BAPS guru in his physical presence on the actual day.
 Personal experiences from individuals across generations then illustrated his enduring presence through every stage of life – from childhood and adolescence to young adulthood and senior years. Their accounts reflected moments of aspiration and achievement as well as profound difficulty and loss.
 Among them was Captain Minesh Patel, whose relationship with Mahant Swami Maharaj stretches back more than five decades. Letters from Mahant Swami Maharaj accompanied Minesh through his formative years and encouraged his ambition to become a pilot. He went on to fulfil that childhood dream as a British Airways captain and later had the privilege of flying Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 ‘In His Eyes’ then explored the way Mahant Swami Maharaj sees himself and those around him. Through his own words and personal incidents, the section revealed his dasbhav – a spirit of profound humility and service – alongside his attentive love for people of all ages.
 In one of the evening’s most personal moments, Mahant Swami Maharaj responded to heartfelt birthday messages from devotees with a handwritten letter, which he read to the assembly. Expressing his prayers and affection for devotees, he concluded simply: “We love you all.”
 The section also reflected on his unwavering devotion to his gurus, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and the sacrifices through which he has sought to fulfil their wishes.
 A landmark announcement followed as Guinness World Records officially recognised the 13-volume biography of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, authored by Sadhu Adarshjivandas, as the ‘Longest Biography by a Single Author’. Official adjudicator Carl Saville announced that the work comprises 2,146,447 words across 8,848 pages, representing “years of scholarship, research, documentation, and dedication” to preserving Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life and legacy. (Learn more here.)
 The final perspective, ‘In God’s Eyes’, explored Mahant Swami Maharaj’s spiritual identity through the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in the Vachanamrut, Bhaktachintamani, Purushottam Prakash and Haricharitramrutsagar (excerpted as Purushottam Bolya Prite). Scriptural passages, devotional compositions and reflections from senior swamis described the enlightened guru as one who remains wholly devoted to Bhagwan, who sees goodness in others, and who guides seekers towards spiritual liberation.
 The finale brought together prayer, devotional music and dance before Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the assembly. Reflecting on the Guinness World Records recognition, he shared his joy at the honour bestowed upon Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s biography, explaining that reading it creates the feeling that “Pramukh Swami Maharaj is right here with us.” He encouraged everyone to read it regularly and described the recognition as “a fitting tribute to Pramukh Swami Maharaj.”

 Over 180 dedicated karyakars from 29 BAPS centers across Australia and New Zealand attended the Mandir Sevak Leadership Conference 2026 (MSLC 2026) based on the theme ‘Apni Ekta – Our Unity’.

/News/2026/Mandire-Shubh-Sw%C4%81gatam-A.t: Mandire Shubh Swāgatam: A Musical Welcome, Paris, France
/News/2026/Mandire-Shubh-Sw%C4%81gatam-A.text:
Experience a breathtaking musical journey across the heart of Paris, uniting classical Indian instrumentation with the timeless spirit of the French capital.
 Filmed on location at some of the world’s most iconic landmarks, this special tribute is created by BAPS musicians to honour our rich Indian heritage and celebrate the opening of the new BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris.
 Join the journey as we travel from landmark to landmark:
 – Eiffel Tower: Shehnai
 – Petit Palais: Veena
 – River Seine: Sarangi
 – Sacré-Cœur: Bansuri
 – The Louvre: Santoor
 – River Seine Boat Tour: Sitar
 – Notre-Dame: Violin
 – Gare du Nord: Piano
 – Luxembourg Gardens: Bandoneon
 – Place de la Concorde: Tabla
 – Arc de Triomphe: Dhol
 From these historic cityscapes, our journey flows from the vibrant streets of Paris to the sacred doors of our BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, culminating in a powerful finale featuring a live choir.
 This tribute is a celebration of harmony, mutual respect, and the beautiful confluence of two great traditions.
 We welcome everyone to experience our new sacred home.

/News/2026/Mindfulness-Amid-Mayhem--A-Ti.t: Mindfulness Amid Mayhem | A ‘Timeless Hindu Wisdom’ Seminar, Wellingborough, UK
/News/2026/Mindfulness-Amid-Mayhem--A-Ti.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mindfulness Amid Mayhem | A ‘Timeless Hindu Wisdom’ Seminar (20 photos)
 Following the successful ‘Timeless Hindu Wisdom’ seminars held in October 2024 – ‘From Ayodhya to Abu Dhabi: A Journey of Global Harmony’ – and March 2025 – ‘Matru-Devo Bhava: Reverence and Responsibility for Mothers in Hinduism’ – more than 350 guests enjoyed an inspiring evening at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Wellingborough on Saturday 21 February 2026. The third seminar in the series was titled ‘Mindfulness Amid Mayhem’, and explored how the timeless teachings of the Shrimad Bhagawatam and Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s Vachanamrut can help navigate the challenges of today’s fast-paced world with clarity, purpose, and resilience.
 As guests arrived, they were invited to participate in activities that encouraged each individual to reflect on what they wished to cultivate in their lives – a fitting prelude to an evening centred on inner awareness and mindfulness.
 The seminar formally commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the sacred lamp, accompanied by the Shanti Path – the universal Vedic peace prayer invoking peace in the world, in communities, in families, and within the individual.
 Where the previous seminars had journeyed through sacred geographies – from Ayodhya to Abu Dhabi, and through the rich tradition of honouring mothers – this third edition turned inward. The keynote address was delivered by Paramtattvadas Swami, a learned swami of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 In his presentation, Paramtattvadas Swami drew upon sacred narratives from the Shrimad Bhagawat Puran and various teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj to provide a clear, succinct framework for finding balance and poise amid the chaos and relentless pace of modern life. He guided the audience towards antar-drashti (insight – of the soul), ant-drashti (foresight – of the world), and anant-drashti (surroundsight – of God).
 The proceedings concluded with the arti followed by an authentic Indian vegetarian meal.
 Milan Pancholi, a devoted volunteer currently studying medicine in Prague, reflected, “As a medical student, I am constantly learning how stress and mental well-being affect our physical health, but tonight reminded me that ancient Hindu wisdom had already mapped this connection thousands of years ago. Paramtattvadas Swami’s insights from the Vachanamrut were both deeply grounding and practically relevant. I came away with a renewed sense of purpose and a clearer sense of how to manage the pressures of life abroad.”
 Ved Bankley, a young apprentice at a leading financial consultancy, added, “Working in tech, the pace never really lets up – and it is easy to lose sight of what truly matters. This seminar gave me a completely fresh perspective. The idea that we can train our minds rather than be controlled by them is so simple, yet so powerful. I will be carrying that teaching with me into the working week.”

/News/2026/National-Medico-Spiritual-Con.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Medico-Spiritual Conference (22 photos)
 More than 700 doctors and professionals from allied medical disciplines gathered for the three-day National Medico-Spiritual Conference, themed ‘Prapti in Practice’.
 Pujya Viveksagar Swami and Jnaneshwar Swami, as well as other learned swamis delivered discourses offering spiritual guidance on topics such as Alaukik Prapti (Divine Attainment), Rising Above Stress, Purity in Practice, Balancing Professional and Family Life, Puja and Arti as Daily Spiritual Anchors, and Boundaries for Protection, Peace, and Progress.
 The conference also featured interactive question-and-answer sessions with senior swamis, enabling participants to explore the practical application of spirituality in clinical practice and everyday life.

/News/2026/National-Yuvak-Yuvati-Karyaka.t: National Yuvak-Yuvati Karyakar Skills Workshop & Get-Together, UK
/News/2026/National-Yuvak-Yuvati-Karyaka.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Karyakar Skills Workshop & Get-Together, UK (40 photos)
 More than 200 yuvak and yuvati karyakars from across the United Kingdom gathered at Pendley Manor Hotel, Tring, on Sunday 21 June 2026 for the National UK Yuvak-Yuvati Mandal Karyakar Skills Workshop and Get-Together, themed ‘Seva ej Sadhana’ (Service is Spiritual Practice).
 The one-day workshop provided karyakars with an opportunity to strengthen friendships, develop practical skills, and deepen their understanding of seva (selfless service) within the Yuvak-Yuvati Mandal. Bringing together volunteers from mandals and centres across the country, the event encouraged participants to learn from one another while reflecting on how to serve more effectively in their local satsang communities.
 Throughout the day, participants engaged in a series of interactive workshops and practical training sessions focusing on key aspects of satsang development, personal growth, and effective seva. Through discussion, reflection, and collaborative activities, karyakars explored ways to strengthen both their own spiritual development and the support they provide to others through their various seva responsibilities.
 Breakout sessions provided opportunities for participants to exchange ideas, share experiences, and discuss best practices with fellow karyakars from across the UK. These conversations fostered a spirit of openness and collaboration while reinforcing the importance of performing seva with understanding (samjan), humility, and the aspiration to earn the rajipo (inner happiness) of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Alongside the learning sessions, the programme included outdoor team-building activities, providing an enjoyable environment for karyakars to build new friendships and strengthen existing bonds. A shared lunch further contributed to the atmosphere of unity, appreciation, and fellowship that characterised the day.
 Many participants reflected that one of the highlights of the event was the opportunity to meet fellow karyakars from other centres, exchange practical ideas, and gain fresh perspectives that they could take back to their local mandals. The workshop inspired attendees to continue developing their skills, fulfilling their responsibilities with greater confidence and contributing to the continued growth of satsang across the United Kingdom.
 The National UK Yuvak-Yuvati Mandal Karyakar Skills Workshop and Get-Together concluded with a renewed sense of purpose and commitment. Inspired by the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, participants returned to their local mandals with a shared resolve to offer their seva with samp (unity), suhradbhav (togetherness), and ekta (oneness), recognising that sincere service performed with devotion is itself a path to spiritual growth.

/News/2026/Neasden-Temple-Receives-Tripa.t: Neasden Temple Receives Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award for 2026, London, UK
/News/2026/Neasden-Temple-Receives-Tripa.text:
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London – popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’ – has once again been honoured with the prestigious Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award. 
 Tripadvisor, the world’s largest travel guidance platform, hosts more than 1 billion reviews and opinions covering millions of attractions, restaurants, and places of interest. Each month, more than 450 million travellers turn to Tripadvisor to help plan their journeys.
 The Travellers’ Choice Award for 2026 places the Mandir amongst the top 10% ‘things to do’ in the world from more than 8.7 million attractions, experiences, hotels, restaurants, and other places covered on its listing. 
 The winners of the award are determined by the quality and consistency of reviews and ratings shared by visitors over the past 12 months. As explained by Tripadvisor, the award means that the Mandir has received “consistently great reviews” and is among places that “consistently demonstrate a commitment to hospitality excellence.”
 This latest accolade is, in fact, the ninth award from Tripadvisor in recent years, again reflecting the consistent quality of service provided to visitors by the volunteers.
 Sonal Patel, a volunteer guide at the Mandir, shared, “We are deeply humbled to know that visitors from around the world have enjoyed their time at the Mandir and taken the time to share their positive experiences with others. We’re always striving to improve our services, so we will continue to see how more and more people can enjoy and learn about the spiritual significance behind the architectural beauty of the Mandir. It’s really an extension of what we all feel every time we come to Mandir, too – the devotion, selfless service, and divine energy that are alive here evoke the sense of peace and tranquillity that so many visitors cite in their reviews.”
 Amish Raghwani, another volunteer who regularly greets and guides visitors at the Mandir, added, “On behalf of all the tireless volunteers who give their time to look after the Mandir and our guests, this award is a reflection of the values Mahant Swami Maharaj has inspired in us all – to welcome guests of all faiths and backgrounds with respect, humility, and genuine care. We hope that everyone who visits leaves with a greater appreciation of our shared values of peace, harmony, and service.”
 All the latest news and information about Neasden Temple can be found on its various social media accounts: X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Telegram

/News/2026/Neighbourhood-Open-Day-31898..text:
Photo Gallery 
 Neighbourhood Open Day (27 photos)
 Around 200 local residents were welcomed to the newly inaugurated BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Bussy-Saint-Georges on Saturday 12 September for a special open day that gave neighbours an opportunity to discover the Mandir, meet its volunteers, and get to know one another better.
 The afternoon included guided tours of France’s first traditional Hindu stone temple, enabling visitors to discover its intricate architecture and craftsmanship while gaining an insight into the Hindu beliefs, traditions and values that shaped its creation.
 Guests also explored an interactive exhibition introducing the values that inspire BAPS and its humanitarian work around the world, alongside cultural displays offering a glimpse into Hindu traditions and heritage. A special photo booth, set against the backdrop of the Mandir, gave visitors the opportunity to capture a personal memento of the occasion. They also enjoyed snacks and refreshments during their visit, creating a relaxed setting for informal conversation with volunteers.
 The gathering built upon a programme of neighbourhood engagement undertaken in the months leading up to the Mandir’s inauguration and the Festival of Culture (Paris Mandir Mahotsav). BAPS volunteers had visited local residents and businesses to share information about the celebrations, answer questions and, importantly, listen to their views and concerns.
 These conversations formed part of a wider effort to establish meaningful relationships with the Mandir’s neighbours from the outset. Saturday’s gathering brought that approach to life in a more personal way, allowing residents to experience the Mandir for themselves while giving volunteers an opportunity to spend time with the people who share its surroundings.
 During their visit, guests shared their impressions of the new Mandir, reflecting on its architecture and craftsmanship, the sense of peace they experienced, and its wider significance as a place of culture, friendship and understanding.
 Thierry Deslos from Ormesson-sur-Marne said, “I have been to India many times, so to see this magnificent Mandir here, with its traditional Hindu craftsmanship, is really quite remarkable. You feel a great sense of spirituality, and I think it is a great success – a wonderful representation of Hinduism in France.”
 Frédérique from Bussy-Saint-Georges reflected on the Mandir’s wider significance: “It is also a sign of friendship between peoples. I am not of this religion, but I believe that knowing others is fundamental to peace, relationships and exchange. I know that BAPS here is about exchange, and we have already had the opportunity to share many events together. It is a real pleasure.”
 Christophe Nguyen from Bussy-Saint-Georges, who had watched the Mandir take shape, shared, “I watched the Mandir being built for a long time and followed its progress, so it is an honour and a pleasure to finally be able to visit inside. When I enter, I feel my soul at peace. There are people here from many different backgrounds, and as visitors we are welcomed so warmly. There is politeness and peace between people. You really feel that sense of peace inside the Mandir.”
 Manan Bhavsar, a local volunteer, added, “Building the Mandir has also meant becoming part of a neighbourhood. Over recent months, we have had the pleasure of meeting many of the people who live around us, listening to them and answering their questions. Today gave us an opportunity to continue those conversations, to get to know one another better and to strengthen the warm and respectful relationships that we hope will endure for many years.”
 The open day reflected the Mandir’s longer-term commitment to remaining connected with and serving its neighbours beyond the opening celebrations and to being a welcoming and considerate presence within Bussy-Saint-Georges.

/News/2026/New-Mandir-Bhumi-Pujan-31423..t: New Mandir Bhumi Pujan, Austin, TX, USA
/News/2026/New-Mandir-Bhumi-Pujan-31423..text:
Photo Gallery 
 Bhumi Punjan (73 photos)
 More than 1,000 devotees and well-wishers gathered on Sunday, April 19, 2026, to mark a significant milestone in the development of the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Austin: the Bhumi Pujan, or sacred ground-breaking ceremony.
 The occasion followed an earlier sanctification ritual conducted on March 17 in Sarangpur, India, where His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj consecrated the sand and bricks destined for the Austin site. His blessings set the spiritual foundation for what devotees described as a long-awaited project shaped by years of devotion and voluntary service.
 The Bhumi Pujan ceremony blended religious tradition with civic recognition. Among those visiting the site ahead of the formal proceedings were Congressman Pete Sessions and Mr. Manjunath Chenneerappa, India’s Consul General in Houston, both of whom addressed attendees and offered their support.
 At the heart of the event was a traditional mahapuja, performed amid Vedic chants invoking peace, harmony, and well-being for the wider Austin community. The ceremony was led by senior BAPS swamis. 
 Local civic leadership was also represented, including Councilmember Mike Siegel, alongside representatives from Hindu organizations and the broader Indian-American community.
 For many in attendance, the Bhumi Pujan symbolized more than the beginning of construction. It marked the start of a new chapter for BAPS in Central Texas. The planned mandir is expected to serve not only as a place of worship, but also as a center for cultural education, spiritual growth, and community service.
 As the first ceremonial steps give way to physical construction, organizers said the project stands as a testament to collective effort and shared vision,  rooted in faith and dedicated to serving the broader Austin community.

/News/2026/New-Years-Day-Family-Mahapuja.t: New Year's Day Family Mahapuja, UK & Europe
/News/2026/New-Years-Day-Family-Mahapuja.text:
Photo Gallery 
 New Year’s Family Mahapuja (40 photos)
 Hundreds of families from across the UK and Europe came together on Thursday 1 January 2026 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, to take part in a special mahapuja, offering prayers for global peace, family unity, and a positive year ahead.
 Thousands of devotees participated both in person at the Mandir and online via a live webcast, transforming their homes into spaces of devotion by decorating their ghar mandirs, preparing sweet offerings, and joining in the prayers as one global community. Two assemblies were held during the day, in the morning and afternoon, allowing families to take part in this auspicious start to the year.
 The ceremony was conducted by the resident swamis, supported by youths. Through the chanting of Vedic mantras, the swamis invoked the divine presence of God while also sharing reflections to deepen participants’ appreciation of the spiritual significance of the mahapuja.
 The occasion offered a meaningful start to the year, bringing families together in a spirit of faith and positivity. Priya Patel, who attended with her family, shared, “It was such a special way to begin the year. The Mandir felt calm and uplifting, and it was touching to see so many people praying for others. My daughters were completely absorbed in the experience and even took time to offer their own prayers for those facing challenges.”
 Yogvivekdas Swami, Head Swami of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in the UK and Europe, said, “The start of a new year offers an opportunity to reflect, renew, and refocus our lives. Guided by the teachings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, we are encouraged to nurture unity, compassion, and positivity. It was inspiring to see so many people begin 2026 with prayers for the wider community. We hope the blessings of this mahapuja continue to inspire and uplift individuals and families throughout the year ahead.”

/News/2026/Palkhi-Yatra-31857.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Palkhi Yatra | Festival of Culture, Paris (60 photos)
 The streets of Bussy-Saint-Georges came alive with colour, music and celebration on 2 September 2026 as more than 2,500 participants gathered for the Palkhi Yatra, an inspiring highlight of the ‘Festival of Culture’ (Paris Mandir Mahotsav).
 Led by women and girls of all ages, the joyful procession celebrated faith, culture and community while marking the ceremonial opening of the Festival, welcoming families, local residents, and visitors from around the world.
 Beautifully decorated palkhis (ceremonial palanquins), accompanied by traditional music and devotional singing and dance, made their way through the town in a vibrant expression of community spirit.
 The procession presented the rich cultural diversity of India through colourful performances, traditional attire, and creative displays inspired by the different regions of the country. It also celebrated the vital role women play in nurturing and transmitting culture, values and traditions across generations.
 Along the route, spectators paused to watch, photograph and enjoy the festivities, adding to the warm atmosphere that has become a hallmark of the Festival.
 Featuring nine ceremonial palkhis, a traditional rath (chariot), and around 250 performers, the Yatra reflected timeless values of devotion, gratitude, and harmony. It culminated in a vibrant cultural performance before continuing to the new Hindu Mandir on the Esplanade des Religions et des Cultures, celebrating the shared spirit that unites people of different backgrounds across France.
 Valérie Pécresse, President of the Île-de-France region, had joined for the opening ceremony and initial part of the procession. In her welcome address, she shared, “It is a great pleasure to be with you today in Bussy-Saint-Georges for this historic moment: the opening of France’s first traditional Hindu temple built of stone.”
 Madame Pécresse went on to explain: “This mandir is not merely a building; it is the culmination of more than fifty years of vision, patience, and commitment. It is the result of an exceptional meeting of outstanding expertise – that of the Indian master artisans and designers, custodians of a thousand-year-old tradition, and that of French stonemasons and companies, some of whom also worked on the restoration of Notre-Dame [Cathedral]. As a result, a monument was born – a monument that honours both India and France.”
 Also present for the opening ceremony was Ms Eenam Gambhir, Deputy Chief of Mission from the Embassy of India in France. She said, “This temple is indeed an extraordinary work of architecture and craftsmanship, but, more importantly, its real significance is not only in the form of the stone, but the values that those stones seek to embody, and the generations of people who will come here seeking faith, reflection, community, and peace.”
 Ms Gambhir added: “France has given the world a powerful language of liberty, equality, and fraternity. India’s own civilisational vocabulary speaks of the world as one family. A temple that opens its doors to people of every background can contribute to that answer – not by erasing differences, but by creating opportunities to understand and respect each other.”
 Ruchi Mehta from Berlin, Germany, who participated in the procession, also shared, “What touched me the most was seeing so many women and girls from different generations and countries celebrating side by side. There was such a genuine feeling of encouragement, joy and belonging, and it was wonderful to share this moment with families and visitors from the wider neighbourhood. Days like this create memories that stay with people for a lifetime.”
 The Palkhi Yatra formed one of the many highlights of the 13-day ‘Festival of Culture’, which continues with devotional ceremonies, cultural celebrations, and family activities centred on faith, heritage, service, and fraternity.

/News/2026/Prasad-Pravesh-BAPS-Bellevill.t: Prasad Pravesh Ceremony of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Belleville, ON, Canada
/News/2026/Prasad-Pravesh-BAPS-Bellevill.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Prasad Pravesh Ceremony (70 photos)
 A new chapter of spiritual growth and community service began in Belleville, Ontario, with the Prasad Pravesh Vidhi of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir solemnly performed on Sunday, April 5, 2026. By the grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the divine inspiration of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the ceremony marked the first ceremonial entry into the mandir’s new premises and the beginning of a meaningful milestone for the region’s growing Hindu community.
 Belleville is a vibrant and welcoming city located in Eastern Ontario, along the scenic Bay of Quinte. It is known for its natural beauty, strong sense of community, and steadily growing diverse population.
 His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj visited the City of Belleville in 1988. This historic visit inspired the growth of the community and laid the foundation for decades of spiritual, cultural, and community development.
 The Prasad Pravesh ceremony is traditionally performed upon entering a new premise for the first time. It brings together community members in collective prayer to sanctify the space and invoke peace, harmony, and spiritual positivity. It symbolizes a sacred new beginning. The ceremony included traditional rituals for the purification of the mandir, as well as prayers for peace and well-being across the local community, the province, and the nation.
 The ceremony was attended by community members and distinguished guests, including Mayor Neil Ellis, who joined the gathering to commemorate this significant occasion and acknowledged the positive contributions of the BAPS organization to the region.
 Guided by the vision of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS volunteers are inspired to actively serve the Belleville community through a wide range of initiatives, including regular spiritual assemblies and youth and children’s development programmes.
 The new mandir will serve as a centre for spiritual, cultural, and community activities for individuals of all ages. Planned initiatives include children’s and youth programmes, language classes, and traditional music education, all aimed at preserving Hindu traditions, heritage, and values. As a place of harmony and inclusivity, the mandir will welcome people of all backgrounds and offer opportunities to experience and learn about Hindu culture and spirituality. It will also serve as a hub for charitable activities and community support.

 By the grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the divine inspiration of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the Prasad Pravesh Vidhi of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Thunder Bay, Ontario, was solemnly performed on Friday, January 23, 2026, on the auspicious occasion of Vasant Panchami.
 Thunder Bay is a picturesque city located in Northwestern Ontario, along the shores of Lake Superior, surrounded by forests, hills, and remarkable natural beauty. The city has a population of over 100,000 residents.
 The Prasad Pravesh ceremony is traditionally performed upon entering a new premises for the first time. It unites the community in collective prayer for peace and harmony and sanctifies the space, marking a new beginning infused with spiritual positivity. The ceremony included traditional rituals for the purification of the mandir building, along with prayers for peace and well-being across the local community, the province, and the nation.
 The religious proceedings featured a Vedic Mahapuja, during which participants prayed for peace, harmony, well-being, and righteous prosperity to prevail locally and globally.
 The new mandir will serve as a centre for spiritual, cultural, and community activities for individuals of all ages. Planned initiatives include children’s and youth programs, language instruction, and traditional music classes, all aimed at preserving Hindu traditions, heritage, and spiritual values. As a place of harmony and inclusivity, the mandir will welcome people of all faiths to experience and learn about Hindu traditions and spirituality. It will also function as a venue for charitable initiatives and community-support activities.

/News/2026/Pushpadolotsav-Celebration-20.text:
20:20
 Pushpadolotsav

 Pushpadolotsav 2026 with Mahant Swami Maharaj (Live)
 Photo Gallery 
 Pushpadolotsav 2026 (109 photos)
 On Sunday, 8 March 2026, from 4.45 to 8.00 p.m., over 60,000 devotees and well-wishers from throughout India and many other countries assembled in Sarangpur to celebrate the grand Pushpadolotsav (Festival of Colours) in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj. Countless devotees around the world also witnessed the celebration through a live webcast on baps.org.
 The large festival venue was located behind the BAPS Vidyamandir. A magnificent stage and backdrop constructed for the occasion beautifully depicted scenes of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit Guru Parampara, along with vibrant motifs symbolizing the spirit of the Rangotsav. Devotees received food packs as prasad upon entering the assembly.
 The festival assembly commenced at 4.45 p.m. with the singing of dhun and devotional kirtans by swamis. Thereafter sadguru and senior swamis addressed the assembly.
 At the outset, Pujya Viveksagar Swami explained the spiritual essence of the festival. He said that on this sacred occasion, devotees should become imbued with the divine colours of devotion to Bhagwan. Quoting Bhagatji Maharaj, he added that the true aspiration of a devotee should be to become a sincere satsangi.
 The programme then continued through three thematic segments highlighting the glory of the Satpurush: The Satpurush Sanctifies, The Satpurush Connects Aspirants with God and The Satpurush Bestows One with God-realization.
 The Satpurush Sanctifies
 Atmatrupt Swami explained that the sins accumulated over many births are destroyed through even a single darshan of the Satpurush. Through Swamishri’s natural association deep-rooted material impressions are removed, because his heart is supremely pure.
 Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami added that the association of the Satpurush sanctifies devotees, helping them overcome their faults and spiritual weaknesses. When one becomes coloured with the divine hue of the Satpurush, worldly colours no longer influence the mind.
 The Satpurush Connects Aspirants with God
 Bhadresh Swami explained that Mahant Swami Maharaj connects devotees with Bhagwan and strengthens within them the true conviction of spiritual realization.
 Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami further explained that Bhagwan Swaminarayan manifested in this world for the liberation of countless souls and that his divine presence continues today through the Gunatit Guru. Having attained the association of Mahant Swami Maharaj, devotees have received the greatest refuge, which strengthens their faith in Bhagwan through mandirs, scriptures, and spiritual discourses.
 The Satpurush Bestows One with God-Realization
 Anandswarup Swami explained that the final moments of life are like a vast ocean, and one requires the divine boat of Bhagwan to cross it. Mahant Swami Maharaj is such a Satpurush who can dissolve the worldly desires in devotees in this very birth, make them brahmarup, and deliver them to Akshardham.
 Pujya Kothari Swami (Bhaktipriydas Swami) further emphasized that the param ekantik sant is constantly associated with Bhagwan and ultimately blesses the devotees with the supreme spiritual state.
 Aksharpith Publications Launched
 Mahant Swami Maharaj inaugurated the following publications and media releases published by Swaminarayan Aksharpith:
 Video Animation Publication: Shri Swaminarayan Charitra, Part 8 – Neelkanth and the Dawn of Divine Destiny
 Print Publication in Marathi: Sant Vibhuti Pramukh Swami Maharaj
 Print Publication in Bengali: Bhagwan Swaminarayan: Life and Work
 Audio Publication: Brahmarasna Bhogi
 Thereafter, Pujya Doctor Swami addressed the assembly. Quoting Brahmanand Swami, he said that devotees should worship Bhagwan with one-pointed focus. True devotion also requires harmony and unity among devotees. Just as sugar dissolves completely in milk, devotees should blend with one another in unity and harmony. Such unity itself is the true celebration of a spiritual festival.

In December 2025 and January 2026, volunteers and swamis gathered for the Regional Karyakar Convention across North America. Centered on the theme Aadarsh for the Children and Youth Wing, and Samjan for Satsang Pravrutti, the conferences offered spiritual guidance while equipping volunteers with practical tools for upcoming seva initiatives. Volunteers connected with peers from nearby cities, exchanged ideas, and shared experiences - building inspiration and collaboration. New volunteers received role guidance, while experienced volunteers reflected on the past year and adopted best practices.

/News/2026/Regional-Satsang-Gnan-Spardha.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Gnan Spardha (68 photos)
 To help satsangi youths deepen their understanding of the Sampradaya during their summer vacation, the Satsang Pravrutti Central Office organized the Regional Satsang Gnan Spardha.
 As part of this competition, all participants were assessed through three competitions conducted at the regional level:
 1. Prathmik Mukhpath Recitation
 Participants were required to recite from memory the arti and ashtak verses.
 2. Written Examination: Satsang Gnanamrut
 A written examination based on:
 the philosophical principles of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, and
 the 61 shlokas selected by Mahant Swami Maharaj from the Satsang Diksha.
 3. Oral Examination: Vachanamrut
 Based on 18 selected passages from the Vachanamrut, participants were required to explain which Vachanamrut teachings could be applied to resolve particular personal or practical life situations and challenges.
 This Satsang Gnan Spardha was conducted at 83 centres across India, with approximately 16,000 yuvaks and yuvatis participating.

/News/2026/Sadhuta-Vartan-Vatu-Karshe--Y.t: Sadhuta: Vartan Vatu Karshe | Yuvak-Yuvati Winter Shibir 2026, UK & Europe
/News/2026/Sadhuta-Vartan-Vatu-Karshe--Y.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Leicester, UK (30 photos)
 London, UK (30 photos)
 On Saturday 7 February 2026 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Leicester, and on Sunday 8 February 2026 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, more than 750 yuvaks and yuvatis gathered for a one-day winter shibir titled ‘Sadhuta: Vartan Vatu Karshe’.
 The uplifting programme focused on cultivating saintliness in everyday life, guided by the inspiring words of Mahant Swami Maharaj, who lovingly wrote: “Always fill one’s work with the fragrance of sadhuta.”
 Rooted in these teachings and the living example of Mahant Swami Maharaj, the shibir inspired yuvaks and yuvatis to place character before skills and allow the fragrance of saintly virtues to infuse their every action.
 Session 1: Humility & Tolerance
 Through visual presentations, skits and inspiring discourses, participants explored the first pillar of sadhuta – humility and tolerance. Speakers shared that true greatness lies not in recognition but in quiet saintliness. Live acts and the spoken word connected these virtues to everyday life, encouraging reflection on tone of speech, unseen seva, and genuine respect, followed by guided introspection.
 Session 2: Adherence to Agna and Niyam-Dharma
 The second session focused on building strength and stability through the observance of niyams. Presentations highlighted how inner peace grows when life is rooted in niyam-dharma. Drawing on Mahant Swami Maharaj’s guidance to “be fearless, courageous and stable,” speakers illustrated how these qualities help us navigate modern challenges with strength drawn from niyam-dharma. Interactive elements, sant panels, and devotional kirtans brought these teachings to life.
 Session 3: Truthfulness, Purity and Faith
 The final session centred on the living embodiment of sadhuta, Mahant Swami Maharaj. Through heartfelt talks and discussions, yuvaks and yuvatis reflected on his humility, selfless love, and purity of heart. The virtues of niswarth prem and shuddhabhav were conveyed powerfully, culminating in the message that firm faith in the Satpurush is the master key to developing all aspects of sadhuta.
 A Lasting Fragrance of Sadhuta
 Marking the day’s message in a deeply meaningful way, each participant received a memorable gift – pendas prepared using kesar (saffron) lovingly sanctified by Mahant Swami Maharaj himself. As the living embodiment of sadhuta, his touch transformed the pendas into a powerful symbol, showing that as the sanctified saffron becomes part of us, may sadhuta take root and flourish within each heart. Carrying the sweetness of the moment and Swamishri’s blessings, participants departed inspired to fragrance every aspect of their life with his divine virtues.

/News/2026/Satsang-Shibir-2026-31534.asp.text:
This summer, devotees from across North America gathered at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandirs for a Satsang Shibir themed "Antarma Akshar Purushottam." Centered on the foundational principles of Akshar Purushottam Darshan, the shibir encouraged devotees to deepen their understanding of God, guru, and the path to spiritual liberation. Through scriptural reflections, historical accounts, and practical guidance, attendees explored how firm nishtha (conviction) in these principles can inspire lasting inner transformation.
 During the shibir, senior swamis and recorded sessions highlighted the life, teachings, and contributions of Shastriji Maharaj, whose unwavering conviction in the Akshar Purushottam Upasana laid the foundation for BAPS. Sessions explored Bhagwan Swaminarayan's identity as Parabrahma through his own teachings, the accounts of the paramhansas, and the understanding shared by Gunatitanand Swami. Devotees also examined scriptural and historical evidence affirming Gunatitanand Swami as Aksharbrahma, drawing on the Vachanamrut and numerous incidents from his lifetime.
 The shibir also highlighted Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s continued manifest presence (pragat) through the Ekantik Sant and how a devotee’s conviction is strengthened through a living connection with the Satpurush. Recorded blessings and question-and-answer sessions featuring His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, along with presentations by senior swamis, emphasized that Gunatitanand Swami serves as the medium through which devotees connect with Bhagwan Swaminarayan and that, today, the Satpurush is the manifest form through whom devotees experience Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Sessions also highlighted how niyam-dharma (personal vows and religious duties), daily spiritual practices, and sincere efforts to live by these principles help devotees cultivate a stronger relationship with God and guru.
 Throughout the shibir, devotees participated in live kathas (spiritual discourses), skits, kirtans (devotional songs), and interactive sessions that brought these teachings to life. Drawing on inspiring examples from Satsang history, attendees reflected on the transformative fruits of firm conviction, including fearlessness, unity, stability, and the courage to uphold spiritual disciplines that bring peace and happiness in this very life. The shibir reinforced that conviction in these three foundational principles can guide devotees in their daily lives, inspire positive inner transformation, and strengthen their spiritual journey.

/News/2026/Second-Patotsav-Celebrated-wi.t: Second Patotsav Celebrated with Sacred Yagna for Family Harmony, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2026/Second-Patotsav-Celebrated-wi.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Second Patotsav Celebration (104 photos)
 Hundreds of families participated in the sacred Yagna for Family Harmony on the auspicious occasion of the second patotsav of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi. Devotees arrived from 4 a.m., taking their seats in the mandir courtyard.
 The yagna commenced with a mahapuja led by Swami Brahmaviharidas. The recitation of Vedic mantras resonated through the air, offering prayers for peace, unity, gratitude, and harmony within families and society.
 At 5 a.m., before dawn, swamis performed the patotsav abhishek and traditional rituals at each shrine in the mandir with deep devotion, culminating in the patotsav arti, reverently performed by Pujya Doctor Swami. As part of the celebrations, an annakut was lovingly offered to the deities.
 As dawn broke, the yagna hom commenced in the courtyard. The rhythmic mantras reverberating across the mandir, the glow of the sacred yagna fires, and the fragrant smoke ascending heavenward carrying prayers created a profound atmosphere of spiritual peace and uplift.
 The yagna concluded in the presence of Pujya Doctor Swami, who offered the final oblations and blessed the assembled devotees. In his address, he praised the Abu Dhabi Mandir as Number One – the finest Mandir he has seen in his 90 years of life. He expressed heartfelt gratitude to the Rulers of the United Arab Emirates and various government authorities for their unwavering support in nurturing this spiritual landmark.
 This sacred celebration marked a deeply meaningful beginning to 2026, aligning with the UAE’s ‘Year of Family’ proclaimed by His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, reinforcing the timeless values of faith, unity, gratitude, and the central role of family in building a harmonious society, as advocated by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
