 On his maiden visit to Gujarat as the National President of Bharatiya Janta Party, Shri Nitin Nabin met His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj at Swaminarayan Akshardham in Gandhinagar. He was accompanied by Shri Jagdish Vishwakarma, BJP Gujarat President; Shri B.L. Santhosh, BJP National General Secretary; and Shri Ratnakarji, BJP Gujarat Organisation Secretary.

/News/2026/Shri-Piyush-Goyal-Visits-BAPS.t: India’s Union Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Visits BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto, ON, Canada
/News/2026/Shri-Piyush-Goyal-Visits-BAPS.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Shri Piyush Goyal visits BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto (13 photos)
 Shri Piyush Goyal, Union Minister of India, visited BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto, Canada on May 26, 2026. He currently serves as India’s Minister of Commerce and Industry. He was accompanied by Shri Dinesh Patnaik, High Commissioner of India to Canada, Shri Mahaveer Singhvi, Consul General of India in Toronto, and other delegates.
 Shri Piyush Goyal was traditionally welcomed by Pujya Gunsagardas Swami, Head Swami of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Toronto, while the accompanying guests were warmly received by BAPS volunteers and community leaders. The delegation was then guided on a tour of the Mandir, where they experienced its intricate craftsmanship, traditional Hindu architecture, and serene spiritual ambiance.
 During the visit, the delegation participated in the sacred Abhishek ritual, offering prayers before the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni, and visited the various sanctums within the Mandir. Shri Piyush Goyal also interacted with community leaders, volunteers, and devotees, appreciating their spirit of service, dedication, and commitment toward preserving cultural and spiritual values.
 Reflecting on his visit, Shri Piyush Goyal remarked, “The Mandir stands as a symbol of spirituality, harmony, service, and shared values and reflects the deep cultural and people-to-people ties that continue to strengthen the India-Canada relationship.” He also appreciated the Mandir’s role in bringing together the Indo-Canadian community and preserving Indian culture and heritage in Canada.

/News/2026/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Ram Navami – Women’s Celebrations, North America
/News/2026/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Ra.text:
The auspicious birth anniversaries of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram were celebrated by women devotees at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandirs across North America through a devotional program centered on the theme, “Preme Pragatya Re,” celebrating Bhagwan’s boundless love for His devotees.
 The program presented how Bhagwan incarnates on earth out of compassion, with the ultimate purpose of granting moksha, or liberation, while also guiding devotees, through His own life and actions, to live pure, noble, and virtuous lives.
 The life of Bhagwan Shri Ram was presented through the many relationships in which His love was expressed. As an ideal son, He honored and respected His parents with complete sincerity, offering a lasting example for both youth and families today. As an ideal husband, the sacred and enduring bond between Bhagwan Shri Ram and Sitaji, as well as Laxmanji and Urmilaji, reflected values of loyalty, sacrifice, and mutual respect. Across every role He fulfilled, Bhagwan Shri Ram demonstrated how to live an ideal life while guiding others with compassion and care.
 Similarly, the life of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan highlighted His profound love for devotees through the gift of true gnan, or knowledge, and a spiritual connection that transcends the material world. Through His interactions, teachings, and genuine care for each individual, Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan established a relationship rooted in eternal well-being. This same spiritual connection continues today through the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, through whom devotees continue to experience Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan’s presence and love.
 Women of all ages offered their devotion through a vibrant cultural program featuring devotional songs, traditional dances, thoughtful skits, and inspiring speeches. The performances brought forward the message of the theme in thoughtful and engaging ways, adding to the devotional atmosphere of the celebration and highlighting the spirit of divine love.

/News/2026/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Sh.text:
Devotees across North America recently gathered at BAPS Mandirs to joyously celebrate the auspicious birth anniversaries of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram under the theme, “Divine Lives, Enduring Family Values.” The program presented their lives not only as divine, but also as deeply relatable, highlighting how, through moments of loss, criticism, sacrifice, and hardship, they exemplified values that remain profoundly relevant today.
 A central focus of the celebration was how both responded to challenges with an unshakable positive attitude, unconditional support without criticism, and unwavering forgiveness. Through thoughtfully curated presentations and discourses by Pujya Swamis, these timeless values were shared as a practical framework for nurturing stronger families and relationships.
 His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj continues to reinforce these teachings, encouraging all to cultivate a positive attitude, offer unconditional support without criticism, and practice unwavering forgiveness in their daily lives.
 The celebrations concluded with the traditional rocking of the cradle, marking the joyous occasion.

/News/2026/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Sh.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Shri Rama Navmi Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2026/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Sh.text:
The divine manifestations of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ramachandra were joyously celebrated with a host of devotional festivities and vibrant cultural programmes at BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK and in Europe.
 This year’s celebrations provided an opportunity for thousands of devotees and guests to reflect on the transformative power of God’s grace, exploring how Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Rama have uplifted and transformed countless lives. Through inspiring narratives and spiritual insights, the programmes highlighted how faith and devotion can bring profound inner change, purpose, and lasting joy.
 Many mandirs and centres featured a colourful cultural programme delivered by children and youths themed ‘Naam Ratan’. The programme was organised into three core elements – Shakti, Bhakti, and Mukti – each reflecting a different aspect of engaging in the divine name of Bhagwan. It explored the transformative power of God’s name to protect and fulfil a devotee’s life, how God’s name becomes a constant refuge in every situation, and how God’s name ultimately guides one to his divine abode, while also enabling one to experience Akshardham here and now through his manifest form. Together, these themes provided a clear and accessible reflection on the importance of chanting God’s name in daily spiritual practice and its lasting impact on both personal and collective devotion.
 Many mandirs and centres also offered opportunities for darshan, pujan, and family photos with images of Bal Prabhu Ghanshyam Maharaj and Shri Rama Lalla, allowing visitors to engage in devotion in a personal and memorable way.
 Devotees also celebrated the janmotsav artis of Bhagwan Shri Ramachandra and Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan, marking their divine births with devotion and joy.

/News/2026/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Sh.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Shri Rama Navmi Mahila Celebrations, UK & Europe
/News/2026/Shri-Swaminarayan-Jayanti--Sh.text:
Mahila devotees from BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK and Europe joyfully celebrated Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti and Shri Rama Navmi with an inspiring cultural programme.Titled ‘Sahajanand Mare Man Vasiyo,’ the celebration conveyed the joy of attaining Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ramachandra, bringing together women and girls of all ages in a spirit of devotion and unity.
 The programme highlighted how devotees can remain immersed in the bliss of God through steadfast faith (vishwas) and deep understanding (samjan), drawing on the inspiring lives of Shabari from the time of Bhagwan Shri Rama, and Jivuba and Jatanba from the era of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Featuring devotional songs, dances, dramas, and speeches, participants illustrated how such faith and understanding nurture a constant inner connection with God.
 These heartfelt presentations inspired devotees to strengthen their faith, deepen their spiritual understanding, and lead lives rooted in devotion, experiencing lasting peace and fulfilment through their connection with Bhagwan.

/News/2026/Siddhant-Sarvasvam-Shibir-202.t: Siddhant Sarvasvam Shibir 2026: 'Akshar-Purushottamne Kaaj: Living the Mahavakyas', Sarangpur, India
/News/2026/Siddhant-Sarvasvam-Shibir-202.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Siddhant Sarvasvam Shibir (83 photos)
 Titled ‘Akshar-Purushottamne Kaaj: Living the Mahavakyas’ the four-day Siddhant Sarvasvam Shibir for young scholars brought together 185 children and youths (103 boys and 82 girls) from India, the USA, UAE, and Tanzania enrolled in the Satsang Diksha Visharad and Siddhant Sarvasvam courses.
 The shibir, in the divine presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, was designed to deepen understanding of the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan and inspire the youngsters to imbibe and live the teachings embodied in the four mahavakyas of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj:
 ‘Apne to Akshar-Purushottamna baladiya chhiye.’ – We are the oxen (devoted servants) of Akshar-Purushottam.
 ‘Akshar-Purushottamni vat koi mara matha par besine kare to pan ochhu chhe.’ – Even if someone were to sit on my head while speaking about Akshar-Purushottam, it would still not be too much for me to bear.
 ‘Akshar-Purushottam mate to vechai jaiye to pan ochhu chhe.’ – Even if we were to sell ourselves completely for the sake of Akshar-Purushottam, it would still be too little.
 ‘A mundavyu chhe te Akshar-Purushottam mate mundavyu chhe.’ – This head has been shaved for the sake of Akshar-Purushottam.
 Through spiritual discourses, workshops, discussions, presentations, and interactive activities, participants explored the historical context, profound meaning, and practical application of these mahavakyas in their daily lives. The sessions developed a deeper conviction in the Akshar-Purushottam Siddhant in the young scholars and strengthened their commitment to seva, satsang, and guru-bhakti.
 The scholars received guidance from Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Jnaneshwar Swami, Bhadresh Swami, Atmatrupt Swami, and other learned swamis. Various sessions emphasized scriptural understanding, spiritual conviction, and the importance of dedicating one’s efforts towards the service of Akshar and Purushottam.
 A notable feature of the shibir was the scholarly presentations delivered by students of the Siddhant Sarvasvam course. Drawing from the Swaminarayan Bhashya, the Vachanamrut, Upanishads, and other scriptural sources, participants confidently presented key philosophical concepts and demonstrated their growing proficiency in Sanskrit and scriptural studies.
 Throughout the shibir, the participants were blessed with the darshan and guidance of Mahant Swami Maharaj. Following Swamishri’s daily puja, the children received his blessings and were inspired by his affectionate encouragement. These memorable moments reinforced the values of devotion, discipline, and dedication that form the foundation of their spiritual and academic journey.
 During one assembly with Swamishri, three-year-old Parambhai Vaghela, the youngest participant, recited the Siddhant Karika from memory, while students from various courses shared their learning through presentations. Appreciating their remarkable achievements, Swamishri remarked, “If they are shattering all records right now, what won’t they achieve in the future!”
 Parents of the participants attended a special gathering on the concluding day, where they witnessed the academic and spiritual growth of the young scholars. The children also organized presentations on the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan, drawing upon the Vedas, Upanishads, Vachanamrut, and other sacred texts. Their ability to articulate profound philosophical concepts with clarity and conviction left the audience deeply impressed.
 The shibir culminated in a vibrant and spiritually uplifting assembly themed “Amraphalo Ame Mahantjina” (We Are the Mangoes of Mahant Swami Maharaj). Through inspiring presentations, devotional performances, and engaging activities, the young scholars reflected on their transformative journey of spiritual learning and growth. The assembly beautifully portrayed how, under the guidance and blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj, these children have blossomed into disciplined, virtuous, and devoted individuals rooted in the Akshar-Purushottam tradition.
 The highlight of the event was Mahant Swami Maharaj’s personal participation in the celebrations, which filled the children with immense joy and enthusiasm. Showering his blessings upon them, Swamishri encouraged the young scholars to continue their scriptural studies with sincerity, humility, and a deep understanding of the glory of Bhagwan and guru.
 The event concluded at the sacred Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir, where all participants resolved to imbibe the lessons learned during the shibir and apply them in their daily lives.

/News/2026/Silver-Jubilee-Celebration-of.t: Silver Jubilee Celebration of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Bahrain
/News/2026/Silver-Jubilee-Celebration-of.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Silver Jubilee Celebration (21 photos)
 Consecrated in 2001 by Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Bahrain marked its 25 years dedicated to spiritual service and community harmony. Since its inception, the mandir has stood as a vibrant centre for devotion, worship, and fostering unity among diverse communities.
 The mandir completed 25 years on 13 April 2026, and the Silver Jubilee celebrations were held on 17 April 2026 with great devotion and enthusiasm.
 The day commenced with an auspicious mahapuja performed by devotees and the offering of annakut to Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and the Guru Parampara.
 The main assembly took place in the evening and was attended by dignitaries, representatives of various communities, and devotees from across Bahrain. The assembly featured heartfelt recollections highlighting the spiritual journey and impact of the mandir over the past 25 years.
 During is online address from the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi, Brahmavihari Swami recalled cherished memories of the Bahrain Mandir and expressed deep gratitude towards His Highness Sheikh Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa, who had personally met His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and warmly invited him to make Bahrain his home. He also acknowledged the continued generosity of the ruler His Majesty King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and His Royal Highness Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, the Crown Prince and Prime Minister. He offered prayers for the upcoming mandir in Bahrain, for which land has been generously gifted by the nation’s leadership.
 The celebration took place in a spirit of unity, joy, and shared devotion.

/News/2026/Swagat-Din-31923.aspx.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Swagat Din (60 photos)
 Thousands of devotees gathered at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Saturday 19 September 2026 for a special swagat sabha (welcome assembly), formally welcoming His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to the UK.
 The assembly marked the first major programme in Mahant Swami Maharaj’s presence since his arrival in London on Wednesday. As devotees celebrated his return after three years, the evening also reflected on the preparations they had undertaken in anticipation of his visit.
 In guidance shared beforehand, Mahant Swami Maharaj had encouraged devotees to focus particularly on two areas: ‘Satsangnu Vatavaran Vadharvu’ (strengthening a spiritual environment) and ‘Ek Bijano Mahima Samajvo’ (appreciating the spiritual goodness of one another).
 The first part of the evening explored these two teachings through devotional bhajans, videos and discourses by Narayanmunidas Swami and Anandswarupdas Swami, reflecting on how they could help devotees prepare not only for Mahant Swami Maharaj’s visit, but also deepen their personal faith and strengthen their relationships with one another.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj was then joyously welcomed into the assembly to the vibrant beating of dhols, before a special dance by children and youths celebrated his return. Devotees joined him in the arti before the focus turned to the many personal endeavours they had undertaken ahead of his arrival.
 A series of presentations highlighted the disciplines and acts of devotion that individuals had embraced, representing a collective effort to make the months leading up to his visit spiritually formative.
 The assembly also celebrated the importance of recognising the goodness of others. A special initiative had encouraged devotees to identify and note down the positive qualities of those around them, culminating in a presentation of hundreds of such journals to Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Together, these experiences revealed how preparations for his visit had extended far beyond organising events or preparing the Mandir. For many, his impending arrival had provided an opportunity to look inward – to deepen their faith, strengthen personal devotion, grow in humility, and put his teachings into practice.
 The celebrations were interwoven with devotional music and dance, including the presentation ‘Guruna Vachanthi Gurune Vadhaviye’ – expressing the devotees’ joy in receiving their guru by striving to live according to his teachings.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the assembly, emphasising that recognising and sharing the virtues of others, together with strengthening one’s personal satsang, earns the grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Drawing upon examples of prominent figures from history, he explained that true fulfilment cannot be found in material possessions or social status, but through a life grounded in faith and devotion.
 Various guests also joined the assembly, including Cllr Muhammed Butt, Leader of Brent Council, who personally welcomed Mahant Swami Maharaj to the UK and spoke warmly of his experiences of BAPS and the “contribution it [Neasden Temple] makes to Brent, London, and the UK”.
 The swagat sabha captured the significance of Mahant Swami Maharaj’s return after three years: not simply the joy of having him back in London, but the inspiration his presence had already generated long before he arrived.

/News/2026/The-Great-British-Spring-Clea.t: The Great British Spring Clean, UK
/News/2026/The-Great-British-Spring-Clea.text:
Volunteers from 18 BAPS mandirs and centres across the UK once again stepped forward in 2026 to help tidy and revitalise their local neighbourhoods.
 Working together in towns and cities nationwide, the volunteers collected over 140 bags of litter, removing a wide range of waste and helping to enhance the cleanliness and appearance of the surrounding environment.
 The activities formed part of The Great British Spring Clean – the country’s largest mass-action environmental campaign, which brings together thousands of individuals, community groups and schools to take part in litter-picking and environmental action.
 The annual campaign is organised by Keep Britain Tidy, a leading independent environmental charity dedicated to inspiring, educating and enabling people across the country to care for and protect the environment in their communities.
 In several locations, BAPS volunteers were joined by local councillors, residents and supporters who welcomed the initiative and appreciated the efforts to improve their neighbourhoods.
 A resident in Birmingham shared their appreciation, commenting, “It's wonderful to see the temple volunteers giving their time to care for the local environment. Their efforts make a real difference to the community and the local area here is unrecognisable.”
 The community outreach efforts were inspired by the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who encourages respect for the environment and service to society as part of a broader commitment to social responsibility.

/News/2026/The-Swaminarayan-Tradition-Re.t: The Swaminarayan Tradition Represented at Historic 'The Dharmic Renaissance and The Athens Declaration' Summit, Athens, Greece
/News/2026/The-Swaminarayan-Tradition-Re.text:
Photo Gallery 
 'The Dharmic Renaissance and The Athens Declaration' Summit (27 photos)
 The Vedic and Greek civilizations are two of the world's most ancient and rich cultural traditions. In a historic confluence of these two great heritages, 'The Dharmic Renaissance and The Athens Declaration' summit was held at the Athens Conservatoire. This landmark gathering brought together acharyas, spiritual leaders, and saints from ten living traditions of India with the primary objective of fostering a global dialogue on dharma, ethics, and sustainable living by presenting the timeless wisdom of India's spiritual traditions to the world.
 The summit featured esteemed representatives from major Indian religious traditions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism.
 Representing the Swaminarayan tradition, Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami delivered a profound and impactful address on the theme of 'Vedantic Dialogues'. In his discourse, he presented the messages on global dialogue from His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. He further elucidated that the dialogues of the Upanishads form the very introduction to Indian civilization, having given birth to eternal Vedantic philosophies such as Advaita, Dvaita, Vishishtadvaita, and the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan.
 The audience was deeply impressed and informed by Bhadreshdas Swami's exposition. Organizers expressed that his insights would prove to be a milestone in strengthening the spiritual bonds between the Indian and Greek traditions.
 Distinct philosophies like the Akshar-Purushottam Darshan and other Indian Vedantic traditions were accorded a place of honor on this prestigious international platform.
 Organizers described the program as a 'historic mandate' to revive ancient ethical values in the context of the 21st century. Through the collective efforts of spiritual luminaries, scholars, and cultural leaders, there is a shared hope that the Vedic vision based on the principle of 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family) and universal welfare will form the foundation for international policymaking.

/News/2026/UNESCO-Indo-French-Cultural-O.t: UNESCO Indo-French Cultural Open Day, Paris, France
/News/2026/UNESCO-Indo-French-Cultural-O.text:
Photo Gallery 
 UNESCO Open Day (48 photos)
 UNESCO ambassadors and diplomats representing 50 countries – from Albania to Zambia – gathered at the newly inaugurated BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Bussy-Saint-Georges on Thursday 10 September 2026 for a special Indo-French Cultural Open Day. The event celebrated cultural dialogue, shared values, and the enduring friendship between India and France.
 Hosted by the Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO, the Open Day brought together ambassadors, permanent delegates and other senior diplomatic representatives from across Europe, Africa, Asia, the Arab States, the Americas and the Caribbean, alongside UNESCO officials. The breadth of representation gave the occasion a distinctly international character, with guests from diverse cultures and traditions coming together to discover Indian heritage in contemporary France.
 Delegates travelled from UNESCO headquarters in Paris to Bussy-Saint-Georges. After arriving at the ‘Festival of Culture’ village, guests were invited to share a traditional Indian meal before gathering for a programme introducing the story of the Mandir and the values of service, cultural understanding and dialogue that underpin its place in modern-day France.
 H.E. Vishal Sharma, Ambassador and Permanent Representative of India to UNESCO, addressed the assembly, describing the Mandir as “a remarkable celebration of India’s civilisation [and] heritage and Indo-French collaborative masonry.” Reflecting on its significance for UNESCO, he said, “There is also a larger reason why this temple resonates so strongly with all of us associated with UNESCO – culture and heritage are at the heart of UNESCO.”
 He added: “Here, Indian cultural heritage has travelled across continents, not as a museum artefact, but as a living tradition.” Summing up the international spirit of the occasion, he described the Mandir as “Made in India, built in France, celebrated by the world.”
 A special film introduced the new Mandir and the remarkable collaboration behind its creation, bringing centuries-old Indian craftsmanship and sacred architectural traditions together with cutting-edge French engineering and expertise.
 Bhavisha Patel, a lead BAPS volunteer, reflected on her own experience of selfless service, describing how volunteering had given her purpose, confidence, friendships and opportunities while allowing her to help others. She spoke of thousands of volunteers who give their time alongside work and family responsibilities, often without recognition or reward, guided by the simple question, “How can I help?” Inspired by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, she explained how this shared spirit brought countless individuals together to help create the Paris Mandir and achieve something far greater than any one person could accomplish alone.
 Jyoti Hosagrahar, Deputy Director of the UNESCO World Heritage Centre, reflected on how the Mandir embodies the living heritage and cultural dialogue that UNESCO seeks to promote. “UNESCO attaches great importance to initiatives such as this, which celebrate cultural diversity, strengthen bonds between communities, promote intercultural dialogue and mutual understanding,” she said. “This temple illustrates that heritage is a living process and stands as a testament to the richness of cultural diversity and to the capacity of heritage and craftsmanship to foster dialogue, mutual respect, and social cohesion among people of all backgrounds.”
 Following a guided tour of the Mandir, ambassadors and delegates gathered over refreshments to share their reflections on the Open Day and their experience of the Mandir.
 Sanjay Kara, project lead of the Mandir, said, “It was a privilege to welcome so many ambassadors and diplomats from around the world and to share the beauty and values of the Mandir with them. His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj has inspired this Mandir to be a place that brings people together in a spirit of peace, respect and understanding. To see representatives of 50 nations gathered here today was a beautiful expression of that vision.”

/News/2026/US-Congressman-Pete-Sessions-.t: U.S. Congressman Pete Sessions Welcomed at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Ahmedabad, India
/News/2026/US-Congressman-Pete-Sessions-.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Mandir Visit (37 photos)
 U.S. Congressman Pete Sessions, elected representative of Texas’s 17th Congressional District, commenced his seven‑day visit to India with an official tour of the BAPS Yogiji Maharaj Hospital in Shahibaug, where he was traditionally welcomed by Brahmavihari Swami. During the visit, the Congressman commended the hospital’s advanced healthcare infrastructure, noting its integration of modern medical practices with traditional systems such as Naturopathy and Ayurveda. He also expressed appreciation for the hospital’s rehabilitation and physiotherapy facilities.
 Following the hospital visit, the Congressman proceeded to the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Shahibaug, where he had darshan of the deities and performed abhishek of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. He also held a special meeting with Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, International Convenor of BAPS. In this dialogue, Congressman Sessions acknowledged the extensive humanitarian initiatives undertaken by BAPS globally, with particular emphasis on its activities in the United States. He highlighted the dedication of BAPS volunteers and attributed the distinguished stature of the BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, to their commitment and devotion.
 The Congressman was then formally welcomed at a grand event held at the mandir, attended by Shri Jagdishbhai Vishwakarma (President, Gujarat BJP), Shri Prerakbhai Shah (President, Ahmedabad BJP), other social and political dignitaries, and thousands of devotees. Addressing the gathering, Congressman Sessions expressed deep admiration for India’s cultural heritage, values, and global influence. He praised the contributions of BAPS volunteers worldwide, reaffirming the organization’s positive impact on communities in the United States. Reflecting on his visits to other BAPS locations in the US, the Congressman highlighted the importance of the BAPS community, its volunteers and temples within each society. Emphasizing the importance of the India-US relationship, the Congressman voiced optimism for enhanced strategic cooperation between the two nations. He also acknowledged India’s progress under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 On this occasion, Congressman Sessions presented an American flag to Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami as a gesture of goodwill and appreciation. Speaking at the event, Shri Jagdishbhai Vishwakarma highlighted the inspirational leadership of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in propagating Indian culture and values internationally, and commended the Congressman’s deep respect for Indian traditions and the BAPS community.

/News/2026/Unveiling-of-Namaste-Sculptur.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Unveiling of Namaste Sculpture (25 photos)
 A new sculpture was unveiled in the Greater Parisian suburb of Bussy-Saint-Georges on Tuesday 1 September by the local Mayor, Yann Dubosc, the Consular Minister of India K. G. Praveen Kumar, and, on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Anandswarupdas Swami and senior swamis of the nearby BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir.
 Installed at the roundabout on Avenue du Général-de-Gaulle, the folded hands in the traditional and widely recognised Indian gesture of ‘namaste’ represent welcome, respect, and humility. Positioned on a key approach into Bussy-Saint-Georges, the sculpture is intended to offer a warm, inclusive welcome to everyone entering the town, while reflecting the cultural diversity and spirit of inclusivity of the local community.
 The sculpture continues a distinctive tradition of cultural landmarks across Bussy-Saint-Georges, representing the diverse histories, cultures and traditions present across the town. Existing landmarks include the three-headed elephant at the Rond-Point du Laos, created with a message of peace and tolerance; the sandstone Bayon sculpture at the Rond-Point Phnom Penh, reflecting Cambodian heritage and values of compassion and kindness; and Le Rêve de la Mère at the Rond-Point Saïgon, commemorating the experiences of Vietnamese refugees.
 The unveiling came on the eve of the ‘Festival of Culture’, a 13-day celebration in Bussy-Saint-Georges marking the inauguration of BAPS Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir, the first traditionally designed stone Hindu temple in France.
 At the unveiling ceremony, Mayor Dubosc began by applauding “the story of French-Indian friendship embodied in Bussy-Saint-Georges,” before adding: “Joined hands symbolise both peace and compassion towards others, but they also symbolise the junction of our two cultures, our two traditions, our two civilisations; different in their existence, but complementary in their search for sharing, brotherhood, and the building of a united humanity. Because that is what Bussy-Saint-Georges is: a unique space where cultures and traditions of all communities mingle.”
 The Mayor concluded by saying, “I congratulate each and every one of you, and I very officially welcome you all to Bussy-Saint-Georges. Thank you all. Namaste!”
 Véronique Lacroix, Head of Public Spaces for Bussy-Saint-Georges, also participated in the ceremony and was warmly appreciated for her efforts in helping set up the roundabout with the sculpture.
 Also joining from the Mayor’s office were Deputy Mayor Marc Nougayrol and Chief of Staff Cédric Tartaud-Gineste.
 The Indian Consul Minister Mr Kumar shared, “[The Namaste sculpture] is a testimony to India’s civilizational heritage. It is a testimony to the enduring French ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity. It is a testimony to the ideals of secularism as practised in France. Above all, it is a testimony to the beautiful manner in which the Indian community has integrated into France, while retaining their own heritage.”
 Anandswarupdas Swami further elaborated upon the value of humility as embodied by the folded hands. He explained: “Humility teaches us three beautiful qualities: to learn from others, to respect others, and to serve others; when our ego becomes smaller, our desire to serve others becomes greater.” He added: “All these qualities are deeply cherished in Indian culture, and they create a beautiful bond with France’s appreciation for courtesy, consideration for others, dignity, respect, and human fellowship.”

/News/2026/Upkar-Forever-Grateful--North.t: Upkar: Forever Grateful | North UK Din, UK
/News/2026/Upkar-Forever-Grateful--North.text:
Photo Gallery 
 North UK Din (60 photos)
 Thousands of devotees from across the BAPS North UK region – some travelling from as far as Scotland – gathered at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, on Sunday 20 September 2026 for a special North UK Din in the presence of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, celebrating a cherished legacy of faith, devotion and the enduring love of the BAPS gurus.
 The programme, titled ‘Upkar: Forever Grateful’, began with youths and senior devotees singing a medley of devotional kirtans extolling the virtues and selfless service of Yogiji Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj. Through videos, personal reflections and presentations, the programme then revisited treasured memories of the gurus’ visits to towns and cities across the region and their longstanding connection with devotees there.
 Sadguru Pujya Viveksagardas Swami and Adarshjivandas Swami shared memories that brought to life these visits and the personal care and guidance of the gurus over several decades.
 The evening also reflected on the formative years of satsang across the region, recalling the considerable challenges earlier generations faced and the dedication with which they established and nurtured local centres. Their experiences highlighted enduring virtues such as samp (unity and mutual support), niyamitta (consistency in personal devotion and service) and khap (dedicated perseverance), which continue to inspire devotees today.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj was then joyously welcomed into the assembly by Akshar Marching Band from Leicester, before five palkhis (decorative palanquins) were brought before him in a colourful procession. Each carried the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj from one of five BAPS mandirs – Preston, Manchester, Birmingham, Wellingborough and Leicester – symbolically bringing together communities from across the region in Mahant Swami Maharaj’s presence.
 The procession carried poignant significance; after decades of BAPS gurus travelling throughout the region to visit devotees in their towns and homes, devotees had now journeyed to London with the sacred murtis from their mandirs to welcome Mahant Swami Maharaj.
 Mahant Swami Maharaj offered flowers to the sacred murtis before joining devotees in the arti.
 The programme then reflected on recognising and appreciating the virtues of others, before expressions of gratitude through devotional music and dance celebrated the profound impact of the BAPS gurus upon generations of families and the flourishing of satsang across the BAPS North UK region.
 The evening culminated in collective prayer, as Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the gathering, praising the tremendous enthusiasm of devotees from the region who had gathered for this special programme, and encouraging everyone to reflect on their spiritual attainment and strengthen their personal devotion.

 On behalf of Swamishri, Pujya Anandswarupdas Swami warmly welcomed the vice president on his arrival. The vice president first performed the puja and arti of Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj with deep reverence.
 Thereafter, he had darshan of Swamishri, who blessed him by offering a garland and tying a nadachhadi, symbolizing prayers for his well-being and continued service to the nation.
 Following this, Shri Radhakrishnan had darshan of Thakorji in the mandir and offered heartfelt prayers for the peace, prosperity, and progress of the country and its people.
 During his visit, he also paid his respects on the auspicious occasion of the 245th birth anniversary of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, honoring his timeless teachings and spiritual legacy.

/News/2026/Visit-of-Rt-Hon-Wes-Streeting.t: Visit of Rt Hon Wes Streeting MP, Secretary of State for Health & Social Care, Chigwell, UK
/News/2026/Visit-of-Rt-Hon-Wes-Streeting.text:
Photo Gallery 
 British Health Secretary Visits BAPS Chigwell Mandir (32 photos)
 Rt Hon Wes Streeting MP, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care and Member of Parliament for Ilford North visited BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Chigwell, on Sunday 26 April 2026.
 Mr Streeting was warmly welcomed with a customary garland of fresh flowers by the Head Swami of Neasden Temple, Yogvivekdas Swami, as well as trustees of the local Mandir.
 During his visit, Mr Streeting was given a tour of the Mandir where he offered his personal respects to the deities inside the inner sanctum. 
 Mr Streeting also took the opportunity to meet with various volunteers from the Temple’s core volunteer team. He also met with many of the children and teenagers, discussing with them about what values they learn at the Mandir, and what future careers they were interested in.
 In his speech to the main assembly, Mr Streeting said: “I hope that together we can rebuild politics as a force of good… and that we can unite around the common good.
 The Hindu community has always been one that has always contributed and given in Britain’s past, Britain’s present and Britain’s future. It’s a community that’s always stood strong… a community I’m very proud of representing in Parliament.”
 Devotees at the Mandir appreciated the visit from Mr Streeting noting his desire for an integrated and harmonious society to which everyone can contribute.

/News/2026/Youth-Career-Fair-Empowers-Yo.t: Youth Career Fair Empowers Young Minds, BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, UAE
/News/2026/Youth-Career-Fair-Empowers-Yo.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Youth Career Fair (30 photos)
 More than 150 youths, parents, and professionals from across the UAE attended the Youth Career Fair, which provided the youths invaluable career guidance, one-on-one counselling, and inspiration to align their professional aspirations with spiritual values.
 In his keynote address, Brahmavihari Swami emphasized the immense potential and responsibility of today’s youths. He stressed that true success lies in the power to persist in one’s choice with discipline, consistency, and resilience, even in the face of challenges and setbacks. He added that professional ambition guided by spiritual values leads not only to career success but also to inner fulfilment and lasting character.
 Following the keynote, attendees took part in personal counselling sessions with professionals from engineering, finance, IT, interior design, and many other fields. Experts offered insights into higher education options and career pathways both in the UAE and abroad.
 A special session for parents focused on how they can support their children in making informed educational and career choices while maintaining a strong connection to satsang and seva.
 Participants appreciated the opportunity to connect with experienced professionals and gain practical guidance.
 One student shared, “The counselling session really helped me to gain clarity and confidence about my future path. I feel more prepared and focused than ever before.”
 A parent added, “It was wonderful to see such guidance offered within the Mandir environment. The balance between professional advice and spiritual grounding was truly unique and reassuring.”

/News/2026/Yuva-Shibirs-2026-Samadhan-31.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Yuva Shibir (32 photos)
 More than 26,000 yuvaks and yuvatis benefited from these one-day shibirs organized by the BAPS Satsang Activities Central Office and conducted at 30 BAPS centres across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Punjab, and other states. Based on the theme ‘Samadhan – For All Our Problems’, they provide practical solutions for today’s challenges, giving the youths renewed direction and confidence to pursue their personal, academic, and spiritual goals.
 The shibirs focused on six major challenges commonly faced by today’s youth: Difficulty maintaining concentration in studies, fear of failure, problems arising from inappropriate relationships and attractions, mobile phone addiction strained relationships between parents, and weakness in observing spiritual values and disciplines.
 Each topic was introduced through a short dramatic presentation portraying a realistic life situation. Learned sadhus then offered practical solutions through inspiring talks, workshops, presentations, and interactive question-and-answer sessions. These programmes enabled participants to understand the root causes of these problems and discover constructive, value-based approaches to overcoming them.
 The youths were inspired to cultivate strong moral values, positive thinking, spiritual living, academic excellence, and successful careers through the guidance of satsang.
 A special highlight of each shibir was a video message from Mahant Swami Maharaj, in which he encouraged the youths to face life’s challenges with courage, faith, and determination.

/News/2026/satsang-vicharan-panama-30969.t: Satsang Vicharan by BAPS Swamis, Panama
/News/2026/satsang-vicharan-panama-30969.text:
Photo Gallery 
 Satsang Vicharan in Panama (6 photos)
 By the grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the divine inspiration of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, Pujya Shwetmunidas Swami and Pujya Brahmatilakdas Swami recently completed a satsang vicharan across the Republic of Panama, where they have been visiting regularly since 2009. This visit once again provided devotees and well-wishers with an opportunity to strengthen their spiritual connection and discover practical guidance for navigating modern-day challenges through the lens of Hindu values.
 Panama, widely recognized for its historic canal and thriving international commerce, is also home to a devoted Hindu community. Throughout the visit, the swamis reached families across Panama City, La Chorrera, and Chitre through padhramanis, personal guidance, and daily satsang assemblies. Each evening sabha began with kirtan-bhakti, creating a serene and devotional atmosphere that brought together hundreds of devotees.
 During his discourses, Pujya Shwetmunidas Swami emphasized the importance of family unity and spiritual resilience, drawing from the Vachanamrut and the Satsang Diksha. He explained how regular Ghar Sabha and daily spiritual practices can serve as a strong foundation for families living far from mandirs, helping them remain spiritually connected to the Guru through discipline, devotion, and a life rooted in values. Pujya Brahmatilakdas Swami focused on engaging with the youth, addressing the unique challenges faced by second- and third-generation Hindus in Central America. Through interactive sessions, he highlighted how timeless spiritual wisdom can be applied in academic and professional life while nurturing pride in one’s cultural and spiritual heritage.
 Over the six-day vicharan, more than 850 devotees participated in the assemblies, reflecting growing enthusiasm and spiritual engagement within the community. In Panama City, over 20 youths took part in a Satsang Diksha Adhiveshan, gaining a deeper understanding of the text and strengthening their connection with Mahant Swami Maharaj. The swamis also visited over 120 homes and businesses, performing pujas and offering blessings for peace and prosperity, further deepening personal bonds with the local community.
 This vicharan reflects BAPS’s ongoing commitment to nurturing satsang in every corner of the world. As shared during the concluding assembly, while geography may differ, the message of Ekantik Dharma remains constant, and the true aim is to experience the joy of Bhagwan and the Guru in daily life. During the visit, devotees offered prayers for Mahant Swami Maharaj’s well-being and expressed gratitude for the spiritual guidance received. The vicharan left the community inspired to strengthen their faith, remain united in devotion, and live the principles of Ekantik Dharma in their everyday lives.

/robbinsville/news/shri-anant-ambani-vis.t: Shri Anant Ambani Visits BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham
/robbinsville/news/shri-anant-ambani-vis.text:
Shri Anant Ambani, an Indian business leader and Executive Director of Reliance Industries Limited, visited BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, on November 2, 2026. His visit included interactions with the Swamis and volunteers, a tour of the campus and Akshardham Mahamandir, and a preview of the upcoming Akshardham Museum.
Experiencing the Architecture
During his tour, Shri Anant Ambani experienced Akshardham's architecture and intricate craftsmanship. The visit offered an opportunity to learn about the devotion, traditions, and spirit of service behind its creation, as well as its connection to India’s spiritual and cultural heritage.
Interaction with Volunteers
He also met with volunteers whose dedication and collective efforts support Akshardham. Reflecting on the scale of its creation, he described it as a seemingly impossible feat made possible through the commitment and service of volunteers. He expressed that witnessing what they had accomplished together left him inspired.
Meeting with the Swamis
During his meeting with the Swamis, the conversation highlighted a shared compassion for animals. The Swamis spoke about Shri Anant Ambani’s love and care for animals, drawing a connection to the deep affection and concern His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj also holds for them. During the visit, the Swamis also conveyed His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj’s blessings to Shri Anant Ambani, adding a personal and heartfelt touch to the occasion.
A Sense of Home
Reflecting further on his experience in an interview, Shri Anant Ambani shared that being at Akshardham gave him a sense of being back home in India. His remarks conveyed both a connection to the campus’s spiritual and cultural atmosphere and admiration for the volunteers who helped bring its vision to life.
The visit also included a brief preview tour of the upcoming Akshardham Museum (scheduled to open in early 2027) offering him an early look at the next addition to the campus.
Through his conversations with the Swamis and volunteers, his experience of Akshardham, and a glimpse of the forthcoming museum, the visit brought together themes of spirituality, service, compassion, and cultural connection.

/nairobi/news/celebrating-national-heroe.text:
In Kenya, the prestigious National Hero Award is presented by the President of the country on Mashujaa Day, celebrated annually on 20 October, to individuals who have made exceptional contributions to the nation and society.
Each year, approximately 250 individuals selected by the National Heroes Council are honoured with this award for their outstanding contributions in various fields, including religion and spirituality, education and healthcare, charity and philanthropy, national, service, arts, sports, research, and industry.
In 2026, two dedicated, devoted, and senior devotees of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha were honoured with the prestigious National Hero Award: Shri Harshadbhai Rana for his exceptional contributions in the field of charity and philanthropy, and Shri Hitenbhai Majewadia for his remarkable contributions in the field of industry.
On 1 November 2026, during the Satsang Sabha held in Nairobi, Kothari Pujya Priyavratdas Swami honoured both devotees on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The felicitation ceremony took place in the esteemed presence of Mr. Charles Wambia, CEO of the National Heroes Council.
His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj expressed immense joy upon learning of this distinguished recognition bestowed upon both devotees. He conveyed his heartfelt congratulations and blessings through personal letters of appreciation.
Heartfelt congratulations to both devotees for receiving this prestigious national honour and bringing immense pride and glory to BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

/abudhabi/news/swami-balkanand-giriji-ma.t: Swami Balkanand Giriji Maharaj Graces BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi
/abudhabi/news/swami-balkanand-giriji-ma.text:
Divine Work of God, A Beacon of Universal Harmony and Sanatan Dharma
The revered spiritual leader, Swami Balkanand Giriji Maharaj, Acharya and Mahamandaleshwar of Anand Akhara, was received by offering a garland and applying the traditional chandlo by Swami Brahmaviharidas, Head of the BAPS Hindu Mandir.
During a personal tour of the complex led by Swami Brahmaviharidas, Swami Balkanandji expressed profound admiration for the temple’s magnificent architecture, intricate hand-carved stone, and serene spiritual ambience. Offering his respects at the sanctum sanctorum, he acknowledged the Mandir as a monumental center of Sanatan Dharma flourishing beyond the borders of India.
Reflecting on the visit, Swami Balkanandji highlighted the spiritual foundation and universal message of the Mandir: "This is perhaps the only Mandir where I feel the complete presence of all the four Vedas. The eternal values and principles of Sanatan Dharma …. of peace, unity, compassion, and harmony among people of all faiths. Here, Hinduism, Islam, Sikhism, and Christianity are deeply respected, conveying an enduring message of mutual respect and peaceful coexistence."
Paying tribute to the extraordinary vision and blessings of H H Pramukh Swami Maharaj and H H Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, whose inspiration made the sacred vision a reality, he thanked Swami Brahmaviharidas, “A Hindu Mandir in this region at this hour is the divine work of an Avatar. It is unthinkable. Unimaginable. God specially sends people on earth for such work to transform history and humanity.” He also expressed sincere gratitude for the continuous support, friendship, and encouragement extended by the Ruler of Abu Dhabi and the leadership of the United Arab Emirates.
The occasion served as a memorable meeting of two great Swamijis, sharing a quiet moment of deep reflection, mutual appreciation, and heartfelt gratitude celebrating their common dedication to selfless service, spiritual fellowship, and global harmony.

/uganda/news/baps-luweero-mandir-murti-p.t: BAPS Luweero Mandir Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav
/uganda/news/baps-luweero-mandir-murti-p.text:
Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav, Luweero, Uganda
The Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav of the newly constructed BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Luweero, Uganda, was celebrated with great devotion and spiritual enthusiasm on 17 and 18 October 2026, in the presence of senior BAPS swamis, distinguished guests, and more than 500 devotees from Uganda and Kenya.
A Town Blessed by the Guru Parampara
Located in central Uganda, Luweero holds special spiritual significance, having been sanctified by the visits of Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj, Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj.
Luweero also has a special connection with Pujya Govinddas Swami, a dedicated sadhu of BAPS, who lived here before embracing the sadhu-fold. Inspired by satsang during his time in Luweero, he subsequently received sadhu diksha and rendered dedicated service for many years at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Navsari, India.
A Noble Vision Inspired by Devotion
The inspiration for the new mandir arose from the faith and devotion of a group of BAPS satsangis associated with Victoria Sugar Limited, an industrial enterprise established in Luweero.
The principal devotees involved in this initiative were Shri Alpeshbhai Manubhai Jiyani, Shri Nandlal Mavaljibhai Thummar, Shri Dilipbhai Kanubhai Jiyani, Shri Kanubhai Madhabhai Trapaliya, Shri Maheshbhai Gordhanbhai Patel, Shri Dipakkumar Parvatbhai Kachadiya, Shri Harishkumar Dhirajlal Rangani, and Shri Dilipkumar Dhirajlal Rangani.
With the noble aspiration of establishing a beautiful mandir as a spiritual centre for the town, devotees came together with a shared vision to create a sacred place dedicated to worship, devotion, and satsang. This collective endeavour led to the establishment of a permanent spiritual centre, serving as a source of peace, inspiration, and spiritual upliftment for the entire community.
Construction of the New Mandir
The foundation-laying ceremony was performed in December 2024 in the auspicious presence of 130 BAPS swamis who had travelled from India to Africa.
Under the guidance of Kothari Pujya Priyavratdas Swami, and through the tireless efforts of Pujya Vishwakirtidas Swami and Pujya Yogimanandas Swami, who oversee local satsang activities, the beautiful mandir was completed in less than two years.
The mandir stands as a testament to the devotees' faith, unity, dedication, and spirit of selfless service.
Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav: 17–18 October 2026
With the divine blessings and inspiration of Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj, the two-day Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav was celebrated in the presence of senior BAPS swamis Pujya Dharmacharandas Swami and Pujya Nandkishordas Swami, along with more than 13 swamis serving across Africa.
17 October – Prasad Pravesh and Special Assembly
The celebrations commenced with the auspicious Prasad Pravesh-Pujan ceremony, marking the ceremonial entry into the newly constructed mandir. A special evening satsang assembly featured inspiring presentations highlighting the spiritual significance of mandirs and their role in preserving cultural values and strengthening faith. Devotees who had contributed towards the mandir's construction were also specially introduced and honoured.
18 October – Shobha Yatra and Murti Pratishtha
The celebrations began at 7:30 a.m. with a beautiful Shobha Yatra, during which the sacred murtis were carried in an artistically decorated chariot. Devotional kirtans, traditional drums, and enthusiastic participation by devotees and Victoria Sugar Limited employees created a spiritually uplifting atmosphere.
The Murti Pratishtha ceremony was conducted by Pujya Dharmacharanadas Swami, Pujya Nandkishordas Swami, and Pujya Priyavratdas Swami. Amid sacred Vedic chanting, the murtis of Parabrahman Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahman Gunatitanand Swami, Bhagwan Radha-Krishna, and the Gunatit Guru Parampara were ceremoniously consecrated in the new mandir.
Distinguished Guests Grace the Celebrations
Hon. Sam Engola, Minister for Disaster Preparedness and Refugees, and Hon. Alice Kaboyo, Minister of State for the Luweero Triangle and Rwenzori Region, attended the celebrations as chief guests.
Both dignitaries expressed their admiration for the mandir and appreciated BAPS's contribution to spiritual values and community harmony. They described the mandir as a symbol of peace, unity, and service, highlighting its positive contribution to society.
A New Spiritual Landmark in Luweero
More than 500 devotees from Uganda and Kenya participated in this historic celebration. The newly consecrated BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir marks a significant milestone in the growth of BAPS satsang in Uganda. Inspired by the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit Guru Parampara, it will serve as a lasting centre of worship, satsang, cultural preservation, and community harmony.

/lusaka/news/baps-lusaka-mandir-dashabdi.text:
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Lusaka, proudly celebrated its 10th anniversary, marking a decade of devotion, unity, spirituality and community service. The three-day celebration took place from 23rd October to 25th October 2026, commemorating ten memorable years since the mandir was established in 2016.
The celebrations began on 23rd October with a beautiful Kirtan Aradhana, a devotional evening filled with melodious kirtans and prayers.
On 24th October, the mandir hosted a vibrant Raas Garba evening, bringing the community together through traditional Gujarati dance, music and festive celebrations. Devotees and members of the community participated enthusiastically, creating an atmosphere of joy, culture and togetherness.
The three-day celebration concluded on 25th October with a sacred Mahapuja, followed by an evening sabha. The programme provided an opportunity for devotees to offer prayers, reflect on the mandir's ten-year journey and express gratitude for the blessings and spiritual guidance received over the years.
The 10th anniversary celebration was not only a milestone in the mandir's history but also a tribute to the dedication of devotees, volunteers and the wider community who have contributed to its growth. The three days beautifully reflected the mandir's continued commitment to faith, unity, culture and service, while looking forward to many more years of inspiration and spiritual progress.

/newdelhi/news/ndtv-world-summit-2026-as.t: NDTV World Summit 2026: As the Global Order Shifts, Brahmavihari Swami Says the Bigger Test Is Human Wisdom
/newdelhi/news/ndtv-world-summit-2026-as.text:
NDTV World Summit 2026
What happens when the established global order is shifting but the shape of the next one is unclear? That was the question at the center of the NDTV World Summit 2026, held in New Delhi under the theme A World Between Orders. Political leaders, diplomats, economists, entrepreneurs, military strategists and spiritual leaders put geopolitics, economic transformation, artificial intelligence and national security into one conversation.
The speakers included Prime Minister Narendra Modi, His Highness Sheikh Theyab Bin Mohamed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan (Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, UAE) , H.E. Abdulla Bin Touq Al Marri (Minister of Economy and Tourism, United Arab Emirates), H.E. Mr. Abdullah M.A. Abushawesh (Ambassador of the State of Palestine to India), General David Petraeus (Retired US Army General and former Director of the CIA), Jean-Eric Paquet (Ambassador of the European Union to India), Dr S. Jaishankar (Minister of External Affairs) Ashwini Vaishnaw (Union Minister for Railways, Information and Broadcasting, and Electronics and Information Technology), Andrew Ng (AI researcher and entrepreneur; founder of DeepLearning.AI, managing partner of AI Aspire, managing general partner of AI Fund, and co-founder of Coursera), Nikhil Kamath (Investor and entrepreneur; co-founder of Zerodha), Zubin Karkaria (Founder and CEO of VFS Global), Gautam Singhania (Chairman and Managing Director of Raymond Group), Sanjay Malhotra (RBI Governor), Dr Shashi Tharoor (Member of Parliament, India; former international diplomat and author), Dr. Swarnim Wagle (Finance minister of Nepal), Swami Sarvapriyananda (Resident Minister of the Vedanta Society of New York), Puneet Chandok (President of Microsoft India and South Asia) and also Tilly Norwood (AI-generated actor representing the intersection of artificial intelligence and creative industries)
‘Beyond Intelligence: AI, Faith and the Meaning of Being Human’
A session in this Summit featured Brahmavihari Swami, representing BAPS on the topic of ‘Beyond Intelligence: AI, Faith and the Meaning of Being Human’.
The session addressed how the way people think may change by using AI, whom they trust and even how they understand themselves. Brahmavihari Swami emphasized the need for people to weigh intelligence without wisdom and convenience without reflection.
“AI is the biggest breakthrough humanity has seen,” he told NDTV’s Aditya Raj Kaul, ranking it alongside fire, the wheel and the light bulb. But those transformed the world outside us. “AI is the only invention that is going to change things within us.”
On the rise and autonomy of AI agents, he offered a deliberately provocative analogy, “Washing machines do not reproduce smaller washing machines. AI is reproducing on its own, it has agents.” Humanity, he warned, may be approaching the creation of something like a new species. This was a philosophical warning, not a technical prediction. The question it poses is that when a tool becomes an autonomous participant in the world, how should we respond?
His sharpest observation concerned people rather than machines, “I am not worried about machines thinking and behaving like humans, but humans will start thinking like machines.” He illustrated it with a familiar scene: someone trusting Google Maps over a spouse sitting beside them. The example was light, the concern serious. Convenience can erode independent judgement, and the line between receiving assistance and surrendering agency is easy to blur.
“The problem begins when it becomes your adviser, when you listen to AI more than human beings.” Persuasive answers are not wisdom, and a simulated empathetic reply is not the understanding that grows between people through shared experience and responsibility.
His most distinctive point was about faith and the potential of an ‘AI Divine’. Religious traditions rarely treat prayer as a system in which every question gets an instant answer; spiritual life involves waiting and reflection. An AI that responds instantly, confidently and personally could pass for an all-knowing presence, and could produce what he called ‘phantom Gods’ and ‘phantom ghosts’: artificial spiritual experiences mistaken for real ones. The worry was less about misinformation than the exploitation of the human need for meaning.
“Fear should not set the response,” he said. “I think the world has to face it with faith,” while insisting on safeguards and controls. Faith here is an alternative to panic, not to regulation. The aim, he suggested, is not faster, more autonomous systems but technology that serves human flourishing.
Regarding ethics or guardrails in AI, Brahmavihari Swami said that putting ethics in AI and a machine is going to be the biggest challenge, considering that we are unable to infuse ethics in our own children or even consistently practice our own value systems in our own life.
When asked how the AI vs Humans conflict would evolve, he raised a very novel take on the matter that the real divide may not be humans against machines, but between people who use AI to augment themselves and those who become subordinate to it, a conflict of “super humans and sub-humans”. Access alone is not enough; people need the judgement and agency to use it well, which makes education and ethics as important as infrastructure. It echoes Ng’s warning about learning, while widening the frame to relationships, consciousness and meaning.
In a summit about shifting orders, Brahmavihari Swami’s contribution was a reminder that the transition concerns not only which nations and companies lead, but what kind of society humanity wants to build.
Some notable insights from other key speakers were as follows:
Hon. PM Shri Narendra Modi: Indias rise and a changing order
PM Modi’s keynote on October 22 presented India’s development as a project with global stakes. A shifting order, he argued, needs stronger international institutions, greater representation for the Global South and cooperation that holds up in a crisis. “Viksit Bharat is not just for us. It is also a guarantee for a better world,” he said. Also, he warned, “Trade, technology and sea routes are being weaponized today.” His message was that India must build its own capabilities while helping to make the wider system more resilient.
The UAE delegation: A partnership that deepens as power shifts
The UAE delegation was led by His Highness Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the UAE Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs. It also included Economy and Tourism Minister Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri, Minister of State Saeed bin Mubarak Al Hajeri and Ambassador Abdulla Saif Al Nuaimi. The relationship shows how two countries can deepen cooperation on investment, energy, connectivity and security even as the balance of power moves.
S. Jaishankar: A world of chokepoints
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar argued that the international system is growing more volatile because states are increasingly willing to use dependencies as instruments of pressure. “Today, it’s a world of chokepoints,” he said, adding that countries now use their leverage with fewer restraints and less regard for the consequences. For India, that means diversifying energy supplies, trade relationships and strategic partnerships, since reliance on a single supplier or route becomes a liability under stress.
On terrorism he was blunt, “Of course, I want good relations with all our neighbors. But will I overlook terrorism for good relations? Absolutely not.” His remarks captured the summit’s central tension. Countries want the benefits of integration, yet must plan for the possibility that links, technology and resources can be turned into weapons.
David Petraeus: AI on the battlefield
General David Petraeus, a retired US Army general and former CIA Director, described AI shifting from a tool that assists commanders to a network of capable agents that can act on their own. Of large language models, he said, “They’re Nobel Laureates in terms of brainpower.” He envisaged systems working around the clock and taking on duties now handled by staff officers.
AI could speed up intelligence analysis, surveillance and planning, and compress the time available for decisions. That raises hard questions about human oversight and accountability, and gave the summit a practical counterpoint to its more philosophical AI debates.
Nikhil Kamath: Inheritance, inequality and wages
Entrepreneur and investor Nikhil Kamath turned to wealth policy. He had reservations about taxing wealth as it passes between generations, but conceded that a well-designed levy, one that does not force founders to sell equity just to pay it, could work. “It’s probably not the worst idea in the world,” he said.
He also argued that inequality will be hard to reduce while wages lag asset-price inflation, and suggested governments may need to intervene. His question: how can societies encourage wealth creation without concentrating prosperity among those who already own assets?
Andrew Ng: Learning, not just answers
Andrew Ng, founder of DeepLearning.AI and co-founder of Coursera, challenged the idea that AI help makes students learn more. Citing research discussed in his session, he warned that students can do better on homework yet understand less when later tested unaided. “AI chatbots are terrible for learning,” he said, urging tools designed to build understanding rather than hand over finished work.
He was equally firm about the workplace, “Today, I will not hire a software engineer who doesn’t know how to use an AI coding agent.” The two positions are consistent. People must learn to use AI well without outsourcing their own knowledge and judgement.
Swarnim Wagle: Joined at the hip
Nepal’s Finance Minister, Dr Swarnim Wagle, offered a neighbour’s view. “There may be occasional hiccups, but we are joined at the hip,” he said, pointing to ties of geography and culture. He recalled India’s role as first responder in Nepal’s 2015 earthquake and after recent flash floods, and noted Modi’s pledge of further assistance. Looking ahead, Wagle argued that Nepal could gain from India’s expansion through closer regional integration, with freer movement of goods, people, ideas and capital on the model of the European common market. Such gains, he cautioned, require deliberate policy choices.
Ashwini Vaishnaw: Moving up the chip value chain
Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw spoke about India’s push into semiconductor manufacturing. According to NDTV’s coverage, he said India’s first domestically manufactured chip is expected in 2028. He called it the culmination of efforts across successive governments and stressed how complex the industry is. The strategic logic is clear. Chips underpin smartphones, vehicles, communications and AI, and domestic capacity could ease supply-chain vulnerabilities. It also supports Modi’s argument that India aims to build the infrastructure behind future industries, not just consume technology or supply services.
Sanjay Malhotra: Orderly markets, not a target rate
Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra addressed rupee management amid global volatility. “We do not target any price or level for the rupee,” he said. The RBI’s goal is orderly foreign-exchange conditions, and it may act against speculation or excessive volatility.
The distinction matters. Smoothing disorderly moves is not the same as defending a particular rate, and for an economy so exposed to trade and capital flows, policy must absorb external shocks while keeping domestic conditions stable.
Judgement in a time of transition
The summit’s voices approached uncertainty from different angles. PM Modi made the case for India’s rise and stronger cooperation, and the UAE’s presence underscored a deepening partnership. Jaishankar warned of weaponized dependencies, Wagle argued for regional integration, Vaishnaw for technological self-reliance and Malhotra for financial stability. Petraeus examined AI in war, Kamath inequality and Ng education.
Brahmavihari Swami tied these threads together with a question beneath them all: can humanity navigate extraordinary technological and geopolitical change while keeping what gives human life meaning? The next order will be shaped not only by the capabilities that states and institutions acquire, but by the judgement with which they use them.
