/india/news/equilibrium-baps-it-professi.text:
‘Equilibrium: Outer Success to Inner Fulfilment’
The third edition of the BAPS IT Professionals’ Convention (ITPC) was held at Sankari, Gujarat, on 17 - 18 October 2026, with more than 350 professionals from across the BAPS community. Inspired by the blessings of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, the convention explored the theme ‘Equilibrium: Outer Success to Inner Fulfilment’, focusing on balancing professional growth with physical well-being, mental stability and spiritual development.
The convention aimed to guide IT professionals through personal and professional challenges using the values of Satsang, encourage interaction and mutual learning.
Divyacharan Swami introduced the theme of Equilibrium, highlighting the importance of balancing external achievements with inner fulfilment.
The Burdens of the Body
Punyadarshan Swami spoke about the body as a means of purposeful action and its role in achieving a balanced life. Dr Kiritbhai Sisodiya addressed common health challenges faced by IT professionals, including sedentary lifestyles, stress and physical discomfort. He shared practical guidance on nutrition, exercise and maintaining good health amid demanding work schedules.
The Measures of the Mind
Drawing on a shloka from the Kathopanishad, Gnannayan Swami discussed the challenges of overthinking and mental stress. The session explored ways to strengthen the mind and develop inner stability through spiritual understanding. It also highlighted God as the ultimate doer and the importance of Aksharbrahma, emphasising that true balance requires clarity of thought alongside professional competence.
The Awe of the Aatma
Anirdesh Swami and Gnannayan Swami spoke on Atma-vichar (reflection on the self) and Paramatma-vichar (reflection on God). The sessions explained the principles of becoming Brahmarup and offering devotion to God. They highlighted how understanding the self, developing a deeper connection with God and living according to spiritual values lead towards lasting fulfilment.
The first day concluded with Kirtan Bhakti, featuring devotional singing by Gurudarshan Swami and Harivandan Swami.
Samuh Puja
Following Mangala Aarti, participants gathered for an early-morning Samuh Puja. The collective worship emphasised devotion, discipline and keeping God at the centre of daily life. It also reinforced the spiritual principle of becoming one with Akshar and offering devotion to Purushottam.
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Mr. Nikhil Malhotra, CEO of Makers Lab at Tech Mahindra, led a session on artificial intelligence, explaining its fundamentals, functioning and practical applications. The session addressed participants’ questions and helped them understand the technology and its growing relevance.
Participants also discussed five key AI use cases, sharing examples of how the technology can improve efficiency and productivity in their professional and personal lives.
Group Discussions
Participants were divided into groups of 10 - 15 according to their professional profiles. Two rounds of group discussions encouraged the exchange of ideas on emerging technologies, innovative approaches and the integration of AI into different professional domains. The discussions promoted collaborative learning and strengthened connections among IT professionals in the Satsang community.
The convention concluded with the address of Pujya Gnaneshwar Swami and the blessings of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj.
ITPC 2026 brought together technology, professional development, health and spirituality under the theme ‘Equilibrium: Outer Success to Inner Fulfilment’. The convention encouraged participants to pursue professional excellence while maintaining physical and mental well-being, deepening their spiritual understanding.

/toronto/news/tapomurti-shri-nilkanth-va.t: Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Murti-Pratishtha Mahotsav, Toronto
/toronto/news/tapomurti-shri-nilkanth-va.text:
Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Murti-Pratishtha Mahotsav
The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Toronto, Canada celebrated the Murti Pratishtha and dedication of a 49-foot Tapomurti of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj in October 2026. The Tapomurti of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj depicts the youthful, ascetic form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan during his remarkable seven-year pilgrimage across India. A journey that was guided by one purpose: to uplift others. It is a profound expression of devotion to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, revered by millions as the manifestation of the Supreme God and to whom the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir is dedicated.
Shri Nilkanth Varni Graces Homes Across Canada
In the lead-up to the celebrations, 17 small murtis of Shri Nilkanth Varni, which had been sanctified by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, visited the homes of more than 7,000 devotees and well-wishers through padhramnis (home visits) across Canada, spanning seven provinces and 137 cities.
A total of 1,247 volunteers participated in this nationwide initiative organized by the Women’s wing of BAPS, bringing families together in devotion and strengthening the values of dharma, gnan, vairagya and bhakti. The visits offered families a meaningful opportunity to welcome Nilkanth Varni into their homes and create cherished memories that would last a lifetime. HH Mahant Swami Maharaj also received reports of the padhramnis, reflecting his blessings and connection with devotees across Canada.
The three-day celebrations from October 16-18, 2026 offered devotees and well-wishers an opportunity to learn about Hindu spiritual heritage and explore the life, teachings, and enduring values of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni
On October 16, 2026, senior BAPS Swamis, Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami and Sadguru Pujya Anandswarupdas Swami led the traditional Vedic Pratishtha (consecration) ceremony in the presence of more than 50 BAPS Swamis from around the world.
The ceremony featured sacred prayers and rituals rooted in centuries of Hindu tradition, using items that had been sanctified by HH Mahant Swami Maharaj during his stay in London, UK.
HH Mahant Swami Maharaj Joins Celebrations Live from India
HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, who had taken a keen interest from the beginning in the plan for this murti in Canada, joined the celebrations live from India. HH Mahant Swami Maharaj also sent special blessings in Gujarati saying: ‘Here in Canada, a very beautiful and divine murti of Nilkanth Varni has been consecrated and installed for darshan. Whoever performs darshan, mala and pradakshina here, God will fulfill all their noble resolutions. Whoever performs darshan with heart-felt devotion, will have their desires fulfilled.’
Maha Abhishek
Pratishtha Assembly
As a part of the afternoon program, children presented a skit and recited verses in Sanskrit from the ‘Satsang Diksha’ and other scriptures, showcasing their appreciation for the divine language and its rich heritage. The assembly was graced by Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami, Sadguru Pujya Anandswarupdas Swami and Pujya Brahmviharidas Swami, head of the BAPS Hindu Mandir in Abu Dhabi.
Dedication Ceremony
The Pratishtha ceremony was followed on October 17, 2026 by a dedication ceremony in the presence of eminent BAPS speaker Dr. Gnanvatsaldas Swami, which brought together devotees, dignitaries, community leaders and leaders of Hindu Mandirs from across Ontario, to reflect on the abiding ideals of Nilkanth Varni.
Women’s Cultural Program
A Women’s Cultural Program on October 18, 2026 explored the timeless values embodied by Nilkanth Varni Maharaj and their enduring relevance in strengthening families, communities and society. Through cultural performances, skits and presentations, the program highlighted how these values can inspire positive change in everyday life.
Distinguished guests present during the celebrations included:
Hon. John Zerucelli, Canada's Secretary of State (Labour) and MP for Etobicoke North
Hon. Michael A. Tibollo, Ontario's Associate Attorney General and MPP for Vaughan-Woodbridge
Shri Mahaveer Singhvi, Consul General of India in Toronto
Mayor Olivia Chow, City of Toronto
Councillor Vincent Crisanti, City of Toronto
Councillor Brad Bradford, City of Toronto

/atlanta/news/executives-gain-insights-o.t: Inaugural Executive Forum on “Value Added Life” Held at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Atlanta, GA
/atlanta/news/executives-gain-insights-o.text:
On the evening of Wednesday, October 14, 2026, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Atlanta, Georgia, hosted its inaugural Executive Forum, featuring an insightful address on “Value Added Life” by Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami.
The forum brought together nearly 100 distinguished executives, presidents, board members, and senior leaders from leading companies for an evening of reflection, meaningful dialogue, and inspiration. The discussion explored how timeless values, purpose, humility, and forgiveness can enrich leadership, strengthen organizations, and create a lasting positive impact on society.
The inaugural gathering marked an important step in fostering connections between business leadership and timeless human values, inspiring leaders to pursue not only professional success but also a truly value-added life.

/washingtondc/news/bhumi-pujan-of-baps-s.t: Bhumi Pujan of BAPS Spiritual Complex, Washington, D.C.
/washingtondc/news/bhumi-pujan-of-baps-s.text:
With the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the Bhumi Pujan celebrations for the BAPS Spiritual Complex in Beltsville, Maryland, commenced on Sunday, October 11, 2026.
This occasion marked the beginning of a new chapter for BAPS in the Washington, D.C., region, dating back to 2000, when His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the first mandir. Over the past 25 years, the steady growth of the congregation has created the need for a larger, encompassing spiritual complex to continue serving, educating, and sustaining the community.
A Bhumi Pujan is a traditional Hindu land sanctification ceremony performed before the construction of a new faith complex. Swamis, devotees, and guests participated in this sacred ceremony through a Vedic mahapuja, offering prayers for community harmony, well-being, and the project’s success.
The celebrations commenced on Sunday afternoon with a Women’s Cultural Program filled with Vedic prayers, devotional singing, traditional dances, and speeches. Maryland Lieutenant Governor Aruna Miller joined the gathering and reflected on the lasting purpose of the sacred grounds, sharing, “More than a place of worship, it will be a home for future generations to celebrate their heritage, strengthen their faith, and serve their community.”
Congresswoman April McClain Delaney (MD-6) highlighted how the congregation’s ethos extends into daily life, stating, “BAPS’s commitment to service, peace, and harmony has meaning far beyond any one gathering. It lives in the time volunteers give, the care neighbors show one another, and the lessons passed from one generation to the next.”
Speaker of the Maryland House of Delegates Joseline Peña-Melnyk echoed this sentiment, emphasizing the deeper intention behind the groundbreaking: “You are building so much more than a physical structure. You are creating a place where families will gather, where children will learn the traditions and values passed down through generations, where people will come in prayer and leave strengthened in spirit, and where a commitment to seva - selfless service - will continue to reach far beyond these grounds and into the surrounding community.”
The Bhumi Pujan ceremonies were presided over by Sadguru Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami, Pujya Anandswarupdas Swami, and over 100 BAPS Swamis from across North America and around the world. To accommodate the large number of devotees and well-wishers across the region, the ceremony was held in two parts on October 11 and October 12.
The first Bhumi Pujan ceremony took place October 11, 2026 on Sunday evening, as devotees and guests from across Washington, D.C., Maryland, Virginia, and West Virginia gathered in joyful devotion despite the afternoon rain.
Congressman Glenn Ivey (MD-4) offered an insightful reflection that turned the rain into a symbol of hope. Drawing on his North Carolina roots, where farmers welcomed rain as the promise of a bountiful harvest, Ivey told the gathering, “I think it’s a great sign for us overall that we’re all going to be planted. The seeds will grow, and we’ll all grow together.” His words framed the future mandir not merely as a building, but as a seed planted in the soil of the community - one that depends on shared care to flourish.
Prince George’s County Councilmember Tom Dernoga, a friend of the BAPS community for over 20 years, commended the congregation’s perseverance in bringing the project to fruition, saying, “You had faith, and you prayed, and the clouds cleared, and the light returned.” Reflecting the clearing skies after the heavy rainfall, his imagery offered a promise that the same steadfast faith would carry the project forward.
On Monday, October 12, the second ceremony commenced with devotees and guests attending from across the wider mid-Atlantic region. The culmination of the Bhumi Pujan was blessed through a live video telecast of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who emphasized the central message of Samp (unity) as the guiding force behind the project.
That evening, a special program titled Mandir: A Dream Takes Shape highlighted the vision and hope offered by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj for how the mandir will uplift and serve the community.
The three-day celebration concluded on Tuesday, October 13, when BAPS youth presented a cultural program themed Samarpan: Now It’s Our Turn. They honored the sacrifices of previous generations and emphasized that everyone, regardless of age, can carry this legacy forward through acts of service and dedication - both big and small - for the mandir, one another, and the wider community.
Once completed, the new BAPS Spiritual Complex will serve as a spiritual sanctuary and a vibrant center for preserving Hindu culture and heritage. It will also anchor community service initiatives - including walkathons, blood drives, and other volunteer-led efforts - further strengthening the bonds of unity and service among devotees and the broader community.

/apac/news/akshar-purushottam-siddhant-c.text:
From 7 to 11 October 2026, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha held the Akshar-Purushottam Siddhant Conference in Bega, Australia. It brought together yuvaks and yuvatis who had completed the Yuva Sevak Talim and Akshar-Purushottam Adhyayan courses, which are run across Australia and the wider Pacific region.
More than 270 yuvaks and yuvatis from centers across Australia and New Zealand took part. The five-day program focused on the life and work of Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, who founded BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha and dedicated his life to establishing the Akshar-Purushottam Upasana. Drawing on his life, delegates explored and strengthened five core values: Ahnik, Seva, Samp, Samarpan and Upasana Pravartan.
An exhibition ran for the duration of the conference, with new presentations displayed each day. A replica of Shastriji Maharaj’s Smruti Mandir was also built to commemorate his life and work.
Presentations, panel discussions and performances each drew on incidents from Shastriji Maharaj’s life, showing how his daily devotion, selfless service, unity among devotees, complete dedication and tireless efforts to spread the Upasana remain relevant today.
Special sessions were held on a letter written by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj in Paris, in which Swamishri wrote, “Chālo have satsang nu vātāvaran jamāviye” (Come, let us now foster an atmosphere of satsang). Through discourses and discussions, delegates reflected on the letter’s message and how they could put it into practice in their own lives and centers.
Throughout the conference, swamis delivered discourses and encouraged delegates to apply these values in their daily lives at home, in their studies and workplaces, and in the community.

/cleveland/news/30th-anniversary-celebra.t: 30th Anniversary Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir Cleveland, OH
/cleveland/news/30th-anniversary-celebra.text:
30th Anniversary Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Cleveland, OH
On the weekend of September 26 and 27, 2026, the devotees of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Cleveland, OH gathered to celebrate a grand milestone - the 30th anniversary celebrations of the mandir. A celebration commemorating decades of spiritual growth, volunteerism, and unity, this was a moment to reflect on the past and pay homage to the sacrifices of those that came before us, while also look ahead to the future. This grand celebration was the final piece of a months-long celebration.
A story that began with a few devotees and a vision has grown over decades into a thriving spiritual home for generations of families across Northeast Ohio. The story of this mandir began long before its inauguration in 1996. Thirty years after its inauguration, the Anniversary Celebrations brought everyone together not only to celebrate where the community has come from, but also the legacy it continues to carry forward.
Satsang Diksha Homatmak Yagna
The celebrations began on the afternoon of Saturday, September 26, 2026, with a special Satsang Diksha Homatmak Yagna, conducted exclusively by and for the women’s wing of BAPS Cleveland. Bringing together women and girls from multiple generations, the auspicious ceremony provided a meaningful opportunity to offer bhakti, express gratitude, and reflect upon the countless blessings that have shaped the journey of the mandir and the Satsang community over the past three decades.
Surrounded by family, fellowship, and devotion, the yagna became more than the opening event of the celebratory weekend—it became a sacred offering of gratitude. As devotees gathered around the holy fire, they remembered the dedication, sacrifices, prayers, and seva of those who helped nurture Satsang in Cleveland and pass it from one generation to the next.
Patotsav Mahapuja
Sunday, September 27, 2026, began with the Patotsav Mahapuja, a traditional ceremony commemorating the anniversary of a mandir’s murti consecration (pran pratishtha). The ceremony marked the sacred occasion 30 years earlier when the Mandir’s murtis were consecrated by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
Swamis from across the region led the elaborate rituals, including the sacred abhishek of the murtis, and offered collective prayers for peace and harmony throughout the world. The ceremonial Patotsav arti was performed by the Swamis together with more than 400 devotees. A magnificent annakut featuring an expansive array of sweet and savory offerings was presented to the murtis as the congregation sang devotional thals. The morning concluded with heartfelt stories and cherished memories from the Mandir’s 30-year journey.
Grand Finale
In the evening, the finale program took the audience on a journey through the remarkable story of Satsang in Cleveland—from its humble beginnings to the mandir that stands today. The story began in 1974, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj planted the seeds of Satsang in Cleveland at City Hall. It continued through the shores of Lake Erie in 1977 and the celebration of Guru Purnima at Cleveland State University in 1988—moments that deepened the community’s devotion, unity, and bond with their guru. These chapters culminated in 1996, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the Cleveland Mandir, transforming decades of faith, sacrifice, and seva into a permanent spiritual home.
Through skits, archival footage, personal reflections, monologues, and devotional performances, the program brought these memories together as one continuous story. It then celebrated 30 years of the mandir and the generations who have grown within its walls, carrying forward faith, values, culture, and seva. Pujya Veddarshan Swami reminded the assembly that the mandirs built by HH Pramukh Swami Maharaj and HH Mahant Swami Maharaj serve as guardians of our culture and heritage—and that it is now our responsibility to carry this legacy into the future.
The celebration concluded with a powerful reminder: the pioneers who planted the seeds of Satsang could not have known what those seeds would become. Each generation has nurtured them, built upon them, and passed them forward. Now, a new generation stands ready to write the next chapter.

/mountgambier/news/inauguration-of-baps-.t: Inauguration of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
/mountgambier/news/inauguration-of-baps-.text:
Two days of spiritual and cultural celebrations marked the opening of Mount Gambier's first Hindu mandir, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, in the presence of P. Paramchintan Swami and BAPS Sadhus.
On Saturday, October 3, 2026, a Nagar Yatra (cultural parade) proceeded through Mount Gambier with festive traditional music, festive dance and decorated murtis, bringing together devotees, local residents, families and well-wishers.
On Sunday, October 4, 2026, all attendees witnessed the Murti-Pratishtha rituals. Through this traditional Vedic ceremony the murtis were ceremonially consecrated within the mandir, formally marking its opening as a place of worship.
A celebration assembly followed, at which the significance of the occasion was highlighted. Rooted in the Hindu faith, the mandir welcomes visitors of all faiths and backgrounds to learn about Hindu traditions and culture.
Several distinguished attendees also joined the festivities across the two days, including the State Member for Playford, Mr John Fulbrook MP, Deputy Mayor Cr Josh Lynagh (City of Mount Gambier), Cr Sonya Mezinec (City of Mount Gambier), Cr Surender Pal (City of West Torrens) and Cr Jagdish Lakhani (Campbelltown City Council).
The mandir has been established with the blessings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj and will serve as a centre for spiritual, cultural and community activities in South Australia's Limestone Coast.

/india/news/medico-spiritual-students-co.text:
‘Jivishu Swamina Vachane’ (Living by Swami’s Words)
Approximately 550 male and female students from across Gujarat, pursuing studies in medicine, dentistry, physiotherapy, Ayurveda, homoeopathy, and other medical disciplines participated in the Medico-Spiritual Students Conference in the presence of Sadguru Pujya Doctor Swami.
The central theme of the conference was ‘Jivishu Swamina Vachane’ (Living by Swami’s Words). Mahant Swami Maharaj had expressed his wish that students in the various medical fields should study diligently, lead pure lives, serve others and cultivate a spirit of complete dedication.
Focusing on these four principles, Pujya Doctor Swami, Narayanmuni Swami, Atmatrupt Swami and other learned and experienced swamis delivered inspiring guidance.
In addition to discourses, the conference featured workshops, videos, panel discussions and interviews. Through these activities, the young men and women gained valuable insights and inspiration on how to integrate their academic studies with the values of satsang in their daily lives.

/india/news/launch-of-the-become-adarsh-.t: Launch of the ‘Become Adarsh’ Program in Jabalpur
/india/news/launch-of-the-become-adarsh-.text:
‘Become Adarsh’ Program
Around 1,500 principals and teachers from schools in the Jabalpur district attended the Phase 2 launch of the ‘Become Adarsh’ program for school students.
Organized by the BAPS Children’s Activities Central Office, the event took place at the Geeta Bhawan, Netaji Subhash Chandra Auditorium, Jabalpur. The program commenced with a traditional lamp-lighting ceremony and was conducted in two sessions.
The Phase 2 launch extended the ‘Become Adarsh’ project to schools in the remaining talukas of Jabalpur district, enabling more students to benefit from the value-based education and character development provided through inspirational videos and educational resources designed to encourage good values, positive habits and the holistic development of students.
Tilakbhai Modi, National Project Coordinator, guided the participating principals and teachers on how to effectively use the ‘Become Adarsh’ mobile application to implement the initiative in their schools.
Addressing the educators, Jnannayandas Swami emphasized that for the all-round development of students, it is necessary to educate and guide them on sanskars, character and moral values.
The program concluded with the national anthem and a collective commitment by the educators to promote value-based education and contribute towards building a brighter and ethical future for India.
Among the dignitaries present were Shri Jagat Bahadur Ji (Annu), Mayor, Jabalpur; Shri Ghanshyam Soni, Joint Director, Public Education, Jabalpur Division; Shri Sandeep Jain, Chairman, Jabalpur Development Authority; Shri Prashant Pol, Author and Thinker; and Shri Gautam Barve, District Education Officer, Jabalpur.
Guest Experiences
“This project will certainly contribute to building an ideal India. At a time when there is a need to nurture ideal values in children, the work being undertaken by BAPS will act as a catalyst in cultivating these values.”
- Shri Jagat Bahadur Ji (Annu), Mayor, Jabalpur
“This project will nurture moral values in every child and bring meaningful change. Its impact will extend to their families and the nation. The project is also very important for the effective implementation of the National Education Policy.”
- Shri Ghanshyam Soni, Joint Director, Public Education, Jabalpur Division
“This project will prove highly beneficial in making the coming generation more values-oriented. I sincerely hope that more and more schools take advantage of this initiative.”
- Shri Gautam Barve, District Education Officer, Jabalpur
Press & Media Highlights

/chicago/news/connected-communities-brea.text:
Over twenty county, township, and village leaders from across Chicagoland area gathered at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Bartlett (IL) for our first Connected Communities breakfast.
The morning commenced with a guided tour of the mandir, followed by breakfast and meaningful dialogue. Volunteers and officials sat side by side, discussing the towns they serve and exploring opportunities for collaborating in our communities.
Guests learned about the organization's activities across community service, youth and family development, cultural preservation, and civic engagement, and heard how BAPS continues to give back to and stay connected with the Chicagoland area.
This gathering represents a vital first step in understanding the needs of our neighbors and discovering how the mandir and local towns can mutually support one another.

/sydney/news/rakshabandhan-celebration-a.t: Rakshabandhan Celebration at the Parliament of New South Wales
/sydney/news/rakshabandhan-celebration-a.text:
BAPS Sydney pays tribute to Members of NSW Parliament
Among those in attendance were the Premier of New South Wales, Hon. Chris Minns MP; Hon. Steve Kamper MP, Minister for Multiculturalism; Mr Mark Coure MP, Shadow Minister for Multiculturalism, representing the Leader of the Opposition; Mr Gurmesh Singh MP, Leader of the Nationals; Hon. Mark Speakman SC MP, Shadow Minister for Education; Hon. Scott Farlow MLC, Shadow Treasurer; and Hon. Sarah Mitchell MLC, Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council.
In the Jubilee Room, youth volunteers presented an interactive exhibition on the history, traditions and significance of Rakshabandhan. It showed how the festival's message of protection and responsibility extends beyond the bond between siblings to public service and the commitment to safeguard and serve the community.
Rakhis were tied on the wrists of the attending parliamentarians, councillors and community leaders, and guests made personal pledges reflecting the values of the festival. Female youth volunteers recited shloks from the Satsang Diksha on unity, protection and mutual respect.
Among those in attendance were the Premier of New South Wales, Hon. Chris Minns MP; Hon. Steve Kamper MP, Minister for Multiculturalism; Mr Mark Coure MP, Shadow Minister for Multiculturalism, representing the Leader of the Opposition; Mr Gurmesh Singh MP, Leader of the Nationals; Hon. Mark Speakman SC MP, Shadow Minister for Education; Hon. Scott Farlow MLC, Shadow Treasurer; and Hon. Sarah Mitchell MLC, Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council.
Welcoming the guests on behalf of BAPS, trustee Yogi Savani said, "While Rakshabandhan traditionally celebrates the sacred bond between brothers and sisters, its deeper meaning extends far beyond family relationships. It reminds us that strong families build strong communities, and strong communities build a strong nation." He added that these values are central to the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and continue to inspire the work of BAPS under the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
Premier Chris Minns spoke of his association with BAPS, including his recent visit to BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. Displaying the rakhi on his wrist, he said, "It will be here as long as it lasts!" He described the BAPS mandir under construction at Kemps Creek as a place that will become a significant part of Western Sydney, and thanked the youth volunteers for bringing the celebration and exhibition to Parliament.
Donna Davis thanked the guests and spoke of the positive contribution of BAPS communities worldwide. Mark Coure described Rakshabandhan as symbolising a thread of togetherness and congratulated BAPS on presenting the exhibition at the NSW Parliament for the first time.

/americas/news/kdc2026.text:
Kids’ Diwali Celebrations 2026, North America
Diwali is the festival of lights, celebrating light's victory over darkness and goodness over negativity. As we light diyas in our homes and mandirs, we are reminded of another light: the goodness within each of us.
The Light Within, this year’s Kids’ Diwali Celebration theme, encourages Balaks and Balikas to recognize the qualities Bhagwan has already placed in them. Honesty, compassion, patience, and forgiveness are just a few ways that light can shine through everyday choices. A kind word, a truthful response, or a moment of patience can brighten someone else’s day.
With the guidance of the Guru and the example of HHMahant Swami Maharaj, children learn to bring out those qualities at home, at school, and in their communities. This Diwali, every good choice is an opportunity to let the light within shine.

/americas/news/diwali-at-state-capitols-.t: Diwali at State Capitols 2026: Honoring Heritage, Inspiring Unity, North America
/americas/news/diwali-at-state-capitols-.text:
Diwali at State Capitols 2026: Honoring Heritage, Inspiring Unity, North America
Celebrating the triumph of light over darkness, Diwali brings timeless Hindu values of hope, service, and unity to communities across America. In 2026, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha continued its Diwali celebrations at state capitols across America, bringing together elected officials, their staff, community leaders, and members of the Hindu community.
The celebrations highlighted the values of light, service, compassion, gratitude, and unity, connecting these ideals with shared civic principles. As the nation commemorated its 250th anniversary, the gatherings recognized the contributions of Hindu Americans and their institutions to the American story through faith, service, and community engagement.
Across state capitols, Diwali celebrations honored cultural heritage, highlighted the contributions of Indian Americans, and strengthened civic connections, reflecting how diverse communities continue to enrich the nation.

/americas/news/baps-campus-fellowship-di.t: BAPS Campus Fellowship Diwali Celebrations 2026, North America
/americas/news/baps-campus-fellowship-di.text:
BAPS Campus Fellowship Diwali Celebrations 2026, North America
Youths across university campuses in North America rekindled their flame of character, integrity, and spirituality through the annual BAPS Campus Diwali Celebration, hosted by the BAPS Campus Fellowship. This year, over 50 campuses across North America held Campus Diwali Celebrations. Collegiate youths, often located far from their childhood friends and family, balanced their academic schedules to plan, organize, and participate in this event. In addition, student volunteers hand-prepared various vegetarian food items to offer as an annakut, upholding cornerstone elements of the Diwali tradition. Over 20,000 students, faculty, and community members participated in these celebrations nationwide.
Under the spiritual guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS continues to promote activities that celebrate Hindu festivals while enriching today’s youth with important life lessons. Through “The Journey to Humility,” participants were reminded that some of the greatest impact comes not from seeking recognition, but from thinking of ourselves less and finding ways to serve others..

/abudhabi/news/ganesh-utsav-2026.text:
14–20 September 2026
A week of devotion and celebration concluded today at the #AbuDhabiMandir with a grand Ganesh Yatra, Visarjan and Jal Jhilani.
The week-long Ganesh Utsav began with the puja and sthapan of Shri Ganeshji, with devotees and visitors offering darshan and prayers throughout the week.
Today, over 5000 young and old, dressed in colourful traditional attire, joined the grand yatra around the Mandir as the vibrant sounds of dhol and tasha, devotional singing and chants filled the Mandir campus. The procession concluded with arti and the traditional Visarjan of Shri Ganeshji.
In the presence of Swami Brahmaviharidas, the celebrations also included Jal Jhilani, with Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj ceremonially seated in a decorated boat and taken on the water amid arti and devotional bhajans.
Swami Brahmaviharidas reflected on Shri Ganeshji as ‘Vighnaharta’ – the remover of obstacles, and prayed that all who had darshan during the week-long Ganesh Utsav be freed from the obstacles they face in life.
A beautiful conclusion to a week of bhakti, prayer and celebration at the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi.

/americas/news/diwali-annakut-celebratio.text:
Diwali & Annakut Celebrations 2026, North America
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandirs across North America celebrated Diwali and the Hindu New Year, welcoming families, friends and community members for one of the most cherished festivals. Celebrations featured traditional Annakut offerings, colorful rangoli, illuminated diyas and festive decorations.
This year’s theme, “Light Beyond Lamps: Journey Through Hindu Sanskruti,” explored Hinduism as a vibrant, living way of life, connecting its beliefs, traditions and practices to enduring values such as family, gratitude, service and community.
A centerpiece was the Annakut, an offering of hundreds of vegetarian dishes lovingly prepared by devotees and offered to God in gratitude. Supported by volunteers through seva, or selfless service, the celebrations reflected how the light of Diwali extends beyond diyas through devotion, gratitude, family, and service.

/americas/news/womens-celebration-of-hh-.t: Women's Celebration of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj's 93rd Birthday
/americas/news/womens-celebration-of-hh-.text:
Women's Celebration of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj's 93rd Birthday, North America
Women across North America joined together to celebrate the 93rd birthday of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The celebration, themed “Marag Pan Ap, Mari Manzil Pan Ap,” invited participants to align their daily lives with Mahant Swami Maharaj’s example.
Structured around the twenty-four hours of a day, the program explored how sincere prayer, reflection on spiritual attainment, focused puja, health, disciplined eating, satsang reading, and wise use of time can transform everyday life. Through skits, devotional singing, dances, presentations, and interactive reflections, women of all ages learned practical ways to follow in his footsteps.
The celebration reminded participants that Mahant Swami Maharaj is both their path and destination, inspiring them to make every moment an opportunity for devotion and spiritual growth..

/americas/news/hh-mahant-swami-maharaj-s.t: HH Mahant Swami Maharaj's 93rd Birthday Celebrations, North America
/americas/news/hh-mahant-swami-maharaj-s.text:
HH Mahant Swami Maharaj's 93rd Birthday Celebrations, North America
BAPS devotees across North America came together to celebrate the 93rd birthday of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Centered on the theme “Sadgunnā Sindhu Mahant Swami Maharaj” (Mahant Swami Maharaj: An Ocean of Virtues), the celebrations highlighted his exemplary life of integrity, divine love, and devotion to Bhagwan.
Through devotional singing, speeches, panel discussions, dramas, and traditional dances, devotees of all ages reflected on Mahant Swami Maharaj’s virtues. The program highlighted the harmony of his thoughts, words, and actions, his unconditional love for all, and his complete devotion and surrender to Bhagwan and his gurus.
The celebrations created an atmosphere of devotion, joy, and gratitude, inspiring devotees to cultivate his virtues in their own lives and strengthen their faith, humility, harmony, compassion, and service to others.

/newcastle-de/news/20th-anniversary-cele.t: 20th Anniversary Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, New Castle, DE
/newcastle-de/news/20th-anniversary-cele.text:
For 20 years, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in New Castle, Delaware, has been more than just a place of worship; it has been a cornerstone of the community, fostering spiritual growth, cultural preservation, and community service. Since its inception, the Mandir has welcomed countless individuals, offering them a space to connect with their heritage, deepen their faith, and engage in meaningful service to others. Through various programs, the Mandir has enriched lives, strengthened families, and helped build a strong and vibrant community.
The Mandir marked its 20th anniversary on September 12–13, 2026, with a series of events that beautifully reflected the values it has upheld over the past two decades. The celebrations were a joyful tribute to the Mandir’s journey, filled with moments of devotion, reflection, and cultural expression.
Women’s Cultural Program
The festivities began with women devotees sharing their deeply rooted connections to the Mandir and its history through a vibrant cultural program. Women of all ages highlighted how the Mandir has shaped their lives, underscoring its profound impact on their personal and spiritual journeys.
Kirtan Aradhana
The celebrations also included a Kirtan Aradhana, filling the Mandir with bhajans that reflected the devotion cultivated over the past 20 years. Devotees from across Delaware came together for this musical offering, creating an atmosphere of bhakti and devotion that will be remembered for years to come.
Patotsav Mahapuja
At the heart of the 20th anniversary celebrations was the Patotsav Mahapuja and Abhishek, the central spiritual observance of the milestone occasion. Devotees came together in prayer and gratitude, offering their devotion to Bhagwan and giving thanks for the Mandir’s 20-year journey. The sacred ceremonies provided an opportunity to reflect on the blessings of the past two decades and pray for the continued spiritual growth of the Mandir and its community. The presence of Pujya Viveknidhidas Swami and Pujya Ghanshyamsevadas Swami, further enriched the occasion through their blessings and spiritual guidance.
Dedication Assembly
The celebrations concluded with the 20th Anniversary Dedication Assembly, which took devotees on a nostalgic journey through the Mandir’s history, from its construction to its growth over the past two decades. As devotees reflected on the Mandir’s progress and the milestones achieved, there was a profound sense of gratitude and anticipation for the future.
The celebration was not only a reflection on 20 years of devotion and community but also a hopeful look toward the years ahead, guided by the same spirit of unity, faith, and service that has defined the Mandir since its inception.

/ahmedabad/news/baps-youth-yatra-2026-ex.t: BAPS Youth Yatra 2026: 'Exploring the Path of Truth'
/ahmedabad/news/baps-youth-yatra-2026-ex.text:
BAPS Youth Yatra - 2026
The Yuvak-Yuvati Mandal of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir Amdavad, embarked on a spiritually enriching three-day Youth Yatra, covering several sacred Satsang destinations across Gujarat and Maharashtra. The journey began in Amdavad and continued through Nashik, Saputara, Surat Akshardham, Chansad, and Atladara.
The youth experienced divine bliss through the darshan of the magnificent BAPS Mandir in Nashik and visits to sacred places. The inspiring words and blessings of Pujya Swamis added spiritual depth to the visit, motivating everyone to strengthen their faith and devotion.
Amidst the refreshing weather and scenic beauty of Saputara and Igatpuri, the youth enjoyed visiting sacred places and memorable moments of togetherness. The gathering strengthened bonds of friendship, unity, and fellowship among all participants.
At Sankari, the youth enjoyed an atmosphere filled with devotion and enthusiasm through joyful garba and an inspiring spiritual sabha. The enlightening pravachan of Swamis offered valuable guidance and strengthened the spirit of satsang, unity, and devotion among all participants.
At Surat Akshardham, the youth received the divine blessings of Pujya Ghanshyamcharan Swami. During the pravachan labh, they gained valuable insights into the ongoing construction of this magnificent spiritual complex. Witnessing the remarkable architectural work was truly an inspiring and memorable experience.
The visit to Chansad, the birthplace of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, offered a deeply inspiring spiritual experience. The youth also enjoyed divine darshan at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Atladara, cherishing moments of devotion, gratitude, and spiritual inspiration.

/newzealand/news/new-zealand-prime-minis.t: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon Visits BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Auckland
/newzealand/news/new-zealand-prime-minis.text:
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Auckland, New Zealand
The Prime Minister was received by BAPS volunteers, Members of Parliament and community leaders, and welcomed in the traditional Hindu manner with a garland as children waved flags.
On Sunday 6 September 2026, over 1,200 devotees and community members gathered at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Auckland, to celebrate Janmashtami, the birth of Bhagwan Shri Krishna, in the presence of the Prime Minister of New Zealand, the Rt Hon Christopher Luxon.
He was then guided through My New Zealand, My Home, My Duty, an exhibition prepared and presented by the children and youth of the mandir. Arranged in four stages, Belong, Live, Grow and Serve, it traced how a young person raised at the mandir comes to understand who they are and turns those values outward in service to their country. The Prime Minister spoke with the presenters at every stand, and was particularly taken by the youngest children, who explained through stories the values they are learning.
The final section introduced BAPS Charities, which has served communities across New Zealand for nineteen years through food and blood drives, tree planting, hot meals, winter care and disaster relief. Volunteers described the response to the recent Wairoa floods, when hygiene and wellbeing kits were assembled and delivered within a day alongside local partners. Anna Rennie of Kindness Collective and Kay Thomas, Chairperson of the Whau Local Board, also spoke of working with BAPS volunteers.
The Prime Minister had darshan, rocked the murti of Bhagwan Shri Krishna in the hindolo, the decorated cradle, and performed the abhishek of Nilkanth Varni before offering flowers to the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj during the mantra pushpanjali.
In the assembly, a nadachhadi, the sacred thread symbolising goodwill, was tied on his wrist, and he was honoured with a garland and a memento. Responding to questions from young members of the assembly, the Prime Minister said, "It's a tremendous privilege to spend time with the BAPS community. I get very inspired when I come in and spend time with you all, because you inspire me to go back to work and to try and make this a better country. You are a great role model for so many other New Zealanders to follow."
A personal letter from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, written from Paris, was presented to the Prime Minister. In it Mahant Swami Maharaj wrote that the Prime Minister had truly become part of the BAPS family, adding in his own handwriting, "I pray for peace, prosperity, and progress for all the people of New Zealand."
Accompanying the Prime Minister were Hon Simon Watts, Minister for Auckland, and Members of Parliament Melissa Lee, Carlos Cheung and Nancy Lu. Also present were Shri Madan Mohan Sethi, Consul General of India in Auckland, along with guests from the Indian diaspora and community and faith leaders from across Auckland.

/edmonton/news/shri-nilkanth-varni-mahar.t: Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav, Edmonton, AB
/edmonton/news/shri-nilkanth-varni-mahar.text:
Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav
Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav was celebrated at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Edmonton, Alberta, through a series of sacred ceremonies and devotional programs held from September 5 to 7, 2026. The historic celebrations culminated on September 7 with the Murti Pratishtha and Pratishtha Sabha, during which Hindu Vedic rituals were performed to consecrate the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj in the presence of senior BAPS swamis, dignitaries, community leaders, devotees, and well-wishers from across the region.
The growth of the BAPS community in Edmonton has been guided by the vision and blessings of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Over the years, regular spiritual assemblies, cultural programs, and volunteer-driven initiatives have fostered a vibrant and growing community dedicated to preserving Hindu traditions, values, and heritage while strengthening family and community bonds.
Kirtan Aradhana
The celebrations commenced on September 5 with a Kirtan Aradhana. Through devotional kirtans and prayers, devotees expressed their faith while reflecting on the spiritual significance of the occasion. The evening brought the community together in an atmosphere of devotion and unity, marking an auspicious beginning to the Mahotsav.
Vedic Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna
The festivities continued on September 6 with the Vedic Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna, during which devotees and families gathered to offer prayers for global peace, harmony, and the well-being of society. Amid the chanting of Vedic mantras and traditional rituals, participants took part in an ancient Hindu tradition that emphasized the values of faith, unity, and selfless service.
Nagar Yatra
Later that evening, devotees of all ages participated in a vibrant Nagar Yatra around the mandir. Featuring beautifully decorated raths and devotional kirtans, the procession filled the atmosphere with joy and spirituality while celebrating the richness of Hindu faith, culture, and traditions.
Murti Pratishtha
The celebrations culminated on September 7 with the Murti Pratishtha ceremony. Amid Vedic chanting and sacred rituals, Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami, along with senior swamis of BAPS North America, consecrated the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj, enabling devotees to perform the traditional abhishek ritual.
Following the ceremony, devotees gathered for a special Pratishtha Sabha commemorating this historic milestone for the Edmonton community. The assembly reflected on the spiritual significance of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj and highlighted the important role of the mandir in nurturing faith, values, and devotion for generations to come.
Special guests attending the celebrations included:
Hon. Tim Uppal, MP for Edmonton Gateway and Deputy Leader of the Official Opposition
Jagsharan Singh Mahal, MP for Edmonton Southeast
Hon. Christina Gray, MLA for Edmonton-Mill Woods and Official Opposition House Leader
Jasvir Deol, MLA for Edmonton-Meadows and Shadow Minister for Infrastructure
Gurtej Singh Brar, MLA for Edmonton-Ellerslie
Councillor Keren Tang, City of Edmonton
Councillor Jon Morgan, City of Edmonton
The guests congratulated the BAPS community on this significant milestone and recognized the mandir’s ongoing role in preserving Hindu faith, culture, and values while fostering community service, harmony, and understanding. They also acknowledged the contributions of BAPS volunteers and the positive impact of the organization’s spiritual, cultural, and humanitarian initiatives within the broader community.
The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Edmonton continues to serve as a centre for spiritual, cultural, and community activities for people of all ages. Through weekly assemblies, educational programs, cultural initiatives, and community service activities, the mandir helps preserve Hindu traditions and values while encouraging service, inclusivity, and positive contributions to society.
The Mahotsav was made possible through the dedicated efforts of numerous volunteers, supporters, and well-wishers whose commitment and selfless service contributed to the success of the celebrations. Their collective seva has helped create a lasting spiritual legacy and an enduring milestone for the BAPS community in Edmonton for generations to come.

/apac/news/janmashtami-2026.text:
Shri Krishna Janmashtami Celebrations 2026
The auspicious Hindu festival of Shri Krishna Janmashtami was joyously celebrated at all BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs and centres across the Australia and New Zealand.
The day was filled with a multitude of devotional activities, including the soulful singing and chanting, and an arti commemorating Shri Krishna Bhagwan’s divine birth.

/abudhabi/news/janmashtami-2026.text:
13,000 Celebrate Janmashtami
More than 13,000 devotees and visitors gathered at the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, from 4 to 6 September 2026 for three days of Janmashtami celebrations marking the birth of Bhagwan Shri Krishna.
The celebrations began on Friday with special darshan and kirtan bhakti across the Mandir. In the evening, more than 500 devotees participated in the Ashtami Puja, joining in the singing of Krishna stutis, recitation of shloks and prayers dedicated to Bhagwan Shri Krishna. The evening culminated with Krishna Janmotsav, as devotees gathered in the Main Mandir to joyously celebrate the birth of Bhagwan Shri Krishna.
On Saturday and Sunday, the celebrations placed a special focus on children and families. Hundreds of children participated in nearly 20 cultural performances, presenting the life, teachings and values of Bhagwan Shri Krishna through devotional music, dance, shlok recitations and creative presentations.
Throughout the weekend, families and visitors also participated in hourly Janmashtami arti in the Main Mandir. Each evening, Ganga Arti created a beautiful devotional atmosphere at the Swaminarayan Ghat, with floating lotus lights illuminating the river and hundreds of artis glowing in the hands of devotees and visitors as they joined together in prayer.
Across the three days, the celebrations brought together children, youth, families and visitors of all ages, sharing the spiritual and cultural significance of Janmashtami through devotion, joy and family, and bringing the timeless life and teachings of Bhagwan Shri Krishna closer to all.

/perth/news/rakshabandhan-visits-to-wann.t: Rakshabandhan Visits to Wanneroo Police Station and Wangara Fire Station
/perth/news/rakshabandhan-visits-to-wann.text:
To mark Rakshabandhan, members of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Perth, visited Wanneroo Police Station on Wednesday 2 September 2026 and Wangara Fire Station on Saturday 5 September 2026 to express their gratitude to those who serve and protect the local community.
At both visits, youth volunteers introduced the mandir, its values, traditions and activities, and its commitment to community service. The youth volunteers then explained the significance of Rakshabandhan as a celebration of protection, gratitude and service to others. In recognition of the service provided by police officers and firefighters, rakhis were tied on their wrists as a gesture of respect and protection. A conversation followed on the work of BAPS locally and around the world, and on the role emergency services play in the community.
At Wangara Fire Station, firefighters spoke warmly of the mandir's contributions to the local community, including the hot meals provided by volunteers during bushfires. Inspired by the words of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "In the joy of others lies our own," they asked for the quotation to be written on the station's notice board. The volunteers were then given a tour of the station and its fire trucks, and the firefighters welcomed future visits.
At Wanneroo Police Station, officers expressed their thanks and appreciated the effort to connect with and recognise them.
The visits reflected the relationship of trust and respect that has developed between the mandir and local emergency services through a shared commitment to selflessly serving the community.

/rajkot/news/youth-conclave-2026.text:
YOUTH CONCLAVE - 2026
Organised by Rajkot Yuva Pravruti, a grand three-day Youth Conclave was held from 1 to 3 September, centred around the inspiring theme:
SATPURUSH – Love, Life & Legacy
The Conclave brought together 900 carefully selected young men and women from across Rajkot. The first day was held at ADB Hotel, the second at Heaven Water Park, while on the third day, the beautiful auditorium and expansive lawns of Marwadi University came alive with a variety of engaging sessions and activities.
Throughout the Conclave, participants received profound inspiration through enlightening discourses by sadhus, career guidance from renowned speakers, and engaging presentations by the youth. These included quizzes, debates, skits, dance performances, Q&A sessions and kirtan aradhana. Together, these diverse experiences filled the three days with joy, enthusiasm and meaningful inspiration.
Young men and women from diverse academic, professional and business backgrounds participated in specially designed breakout sessions held across various seminar halls. Through these sessions, they received invaluable guidance from sadhus and subject-matter experts on achieving professional excellence while leading a meaningful and purposeful life.
Keshav Premier League
The expansive grounds of Marwadi University hosted the spectacular KPL – Keshav Premier League, a thrilling cricket tournament exclusively for the young men. Alongside the cricket tournament, participants enthusiastically took part in football, volleyball, table tennis, carrom, tug-of-war, badminton and numerous group activities. These activities provided valuable lessons in teamwork, camaraderie and collective living.
The Conclave offered much more than activities and entertainment. With special gifts, a variety of snacks each day, interesting prasad, personality and skill-development activities, and valuable guidance for life and career, participants experienced a wholesome and enriching journey. They were also blessed with a personal letter of blessings from Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, making the experience even more memorable and spiritually significant.
Organised under the leadership of Apurvamuni Swami, the Rajkot Youth Conclave inspired more than 900 well-educated and virtuous young men and women. Through the love, guidance and companionship of the sadhus, they were inspired and committed to making the Love, Life and Legacy of the manifest Satpurush, Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, a meaningful part of their own lives.

/abudhabi/news/rakshabandhan-2026.text:
Rakshabandhan Celebrated with Faith, Love and a Spirit of Protection
On Sunday, 30 August 2026, over 7,000 devotees, families and community members from across the UAE visited the BAPS Hindu Mandir, Abu Dhabi, to celebrate Rakshabandhan with faith and devotion. Across two days of celebrations at the Mandir and visits to workplaces across the UAE, more than 3,300 handmade rakhis were tied, each carrying a heartfelt prayer for God’s protection and blessings
Among them, over 1,800 workers and community members from across all seven emirates attended a special Rakshabandhan assembly at the Mandir. For many workers living far from their families, the occasion offered a particularly meaningful experience of faith, warmth and belonging.
As guests arrived, children warmly welcomed them with the traditional tilak. A joyful Kirtan Bhakti filled the gathering with devotional music, followed by an insightful presentation exploring the unique features of the BAPS Hindu Mandir. BAPS swamis then shared an inspiring message on the deeper significance of Rakshabandhan and its timeless ideals of love, care and protection.
A particularly touching moment followed as BAPS swamis personally tied 1,800 handmade rakhis to those attending the assembly. Lovingly prepared by BAPS women devotees, each carried a heartfelt expression of prayer and protection. The gathering concluded with a meal served to everyone in a spirit of fellowship and famil
Throughout the day, specially created Rakhi spots in the foreground of the Mandir also welcomed brothers, sisters and families. Against the beautiful backdrop of the Mandir, sisters tied rakhis to their brothers as families celebrated their cherished bonds and created lasting memories together.
On Monday, 31 August 2026, the celebrations continued beyond the Mandir as BAPS swamis visited 23 factories and worker facilities across the UAE, travelling as far as Umm Al Quwain. During these visits, a further 1,500 handmade rakhis were personally tied to workers who had been unable to attend the celebration at the Mandir, sharing with them the prayers, warmth and spirit of Rakshabandhan.
From the BAPS Hindu Mandir to communities across the UAE, Rakshabandhan brought together thousands in a celebration of faith, family and belonging, with a heartfelt prayer for God’s protection and blessings upon all.
/abudhabi/news/rakshabandhan-2026.place: Love and a Spirit of Protection

/belleville/news/inauguration-of-baps-sh.t: Inauguration of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Belleville, ON
/belleville/news/inauguration-of-baps-sh.text:
Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav
The inauguration of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Belleville, Ontario, was celebrated through a series of sacred ceremonies held on August 29 and 30, 2026. The historic celebrations culminated in the Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav on August 30, during which traditional Hindu Vedic rituals were performed to consecrate the sacred murtis. The ceremonies were attended by BAPS swamis from across North America, elected officials, community leaders, devotees, and well-wishers from throughout the region.
The growth of the BAPS community in Belleville has been guided by the vision and blessings of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. A significant milestone in this journey was the visit of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj to Belleville in 1988. His visit inspired the growth of the local community and laid the foundation for decades of spiritual, cultural, and community development. Since then, regular spiritual assemblies, cultural programs, and volunteer-driven initiatives have fostered a vibrant and growing community dedicated to preserving Hindu values, traditions, and heritage.
Vishwashanti Mahayagna
The inauguration festivities commenced on August 29 with the Vishwashanti Mahayagna, during which devotees gathered to offer Vedic prayers for global peace, harmony, and the well-being of all.
Nagar Yatra
Later that day, the community hosted a vibrant Nagar Yatra. As part of this traditional procession, the sacred murtis were carried through the heart of downtown Belleville on beautifully decorated floats, offering blessings to residents and visitors before their installation in the mandir. The colorful parade showcased Hindu culture and traditions while bringing together people from diverse backgrounds in a spirit of unity and celebration.
Murti Pratishtha
The celebrations culminated on August 30 with the Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav. Amid the chanting of Vedic mantras and the performance of sacred rituals, the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami, Radha-Krishna Bhagwan, Sita-Ramchandra Bhagwan, Hanumanji, Uma-Pati-Shankar Bhagwan, Ganapatiji, and the Guru Parampara were ceremonially consecrated in their respective shrines. The ceremonies were conducted by Pujya Yagnavallabhdas Swami, Senior Swami of BAPS North America.
Among the distinguished guests was Mayor Neil Ellis of the City of Belleville. Reflecting on the significance of the occasion, he remarked: "Canada is at its best when people of different faiths, cultures, and traditions come together with mutual respect and understanding. We believe this temple will help foster that spirit of harmony, strengthen our community, and build bridges between people throughout the region." He further added: "We are honoured to have the BAPS Temple in Belleville, and we look forward to the many ways it will enrich our community for generations to come." In recognition of the occasion and the contributions of BAPS to the community, Mayor Ellis also proclaimed August 30, 2026, as BAPS Day in the City of Belleville.
The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Belleville will serve as a center for spiritual, cultural, educational, and humanitarian activities for people of all ages. Through weekly assemblies, youth and children's programs, cultural initiatives, educational workshops, and community service projects, the mandir will help preserve Hindu traditions and values while fostering inclusivity, understanding, and service to society.
The creation of this mandir represents the culmination of decades of devotion, dedication, and selfless service by volunteers, supporters, and well-wishers. Their collective efforts have established a lasting centre of faith, culture, and community that will inspire and benefit future generations for years to come.

/dallas/news/baps-connect-stronger-toget.text:
BAPS volunteers welcomed City of Frisco and Texas state officials, elected leaders, and business and community members to the BAPS Connect event in Frisco, Texas, an evening dedicated to introducing BAPS and its ongoing work in the region. Guests learned about the organization's activities across community service, youth and family development, cultural preservation, and civic engagement, and heard how BAPS continues to give back to and stay connected with the Frisco community. The gathering offered attendees a firsthand look at the values of service and character-building that guide the organization, while opening the door to deeper collaboration between BAPS and local leaders in the years ahead.
Anchored by the theme "Stronger Together," the evening centered on three guiding ideas — community, service, and unity — that define BAPS's presence in the Dallas metroplex. Speakers reflected on how strong communities are built through everyday acts of service, and how unity across faiths, cultures, and civic life makes the whole community more resilient. Reflecting the guiding words of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the current spiritual leader of BAPS, that "samp (unity) is about understanding each other's greatness," speakers emphasized that true unity begins with recognizing and honoring the strengths in one another. The message resonated throughout the program: that lasting impact comes not from any one group working alone, but from neighbors, leaders, and organizations coming together toward a shared purpose. It was a reminder that when a community stands together, its capacity to serve and uplift others grows stronger.

/nepal/news/bhote-koshi-flood-disaster-b.t: Bhote Koshi Flood Disaster: BAPS Emergency Relief Work
/nepal/news/bhote-koshi-flood-disaster-b.text:
BAPS Emergency Relief Work
Following the devastating floods in the Bhote Koshi region of Nepal, volunteers of BAPS Nepal immediately responded to the situation and initiated relief and humanitarian services for the affected communities.
Under the guidance, inspiration and blessings of Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS Nepal volunteers have been engaged continuously in this seva, working with a sense of urgency, compassion and responsibility, in collaboration with the concerned authorities.
Immediately following the disaster, BAPS volunteers began arranging essential relief materials for the affected communities. The primary focus of the initial response was to provide basic food and essential supplies that could offer immediate support to families facing difficulties due to the floods.
BAPS Nepal has dispatched relief materials to the affected areas, including rice, lentils, cooking oil, clothes for children and woman, blankets, medicines, and other essential food and relief supplies in coordination with the District Administration Office in Kathmandu.
Mahant Swami Maharaj and all swamis and devotees of BAPS worldwide continue to offer prayers for everyone affected by this tragic natural calamity.

/ahmedabad/news/hh-mahant-swami-maharaj-.t: HH Mahant Swami Maharaj Offers Prayers For the Victims of Nepal Flood
/ahmedabad/news/hh-mahant-swami-maharaj-.text:
Victims of Nepal Flood
During his morning puja today, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj prayed with swamis for the people of Nepal after the devastating floods that struck the Himalayan region of Nepal.
He prayed for the peace of those who lost their lives, for courage and consolation for families waiting for news, and for the safety of all who remain missing or have been left without shelter.
He has also humbly urged all devotees to offer special prayers during the morning assemblies on Friday, 28 August. Furthermore, on Sunday, 30 August, BAPS centers across the world will offer special prayers during their weekly assemblies.
May these prayers bring comfort to every home touched by this tragedy.

/americas/news/janmashtami-celebration-2.text:
Janmashtami Celebrations 2026, North America
BAPS mandirs across North America celebrated Janmashtami, commemorating the divine incarnation of Bhagwan Shri Krishna. This year’s celebration centered on the theme Mamekam Sharanam Vraja, highlighting Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s timeless teaching from the Bhagavad Gita to seek complete refuge in Bhagwan.
Through bhajans, kirtans, skits, speeches, traditional dances, and spiritual discourses, devotees explored the meaning of ashro, or refuge, and the importance of developing unwavering faith and surrender. Teachings and inspiring incidents from Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s life illustrated how reliance on Bhagwan and the Guru provides strength and stability through life’s challenges.
The celebrations brought together devotees of all ages in an atmosphere of devotion and reinforced the enduring message of living with faith, love, and steadfast refuge in Bhagwan and the Guru..

/australia/news/historic-rakshabandhan-c.t: Historic Rakshabandhan Celebrations Mark a First at the Parliament of Victoria
/australia/news/historic-rakshabandhan-c.text:
The Parliament of Victoria, Melbourne, Australia
On Wednesday 26 August 2026, two days ahead of the festival, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha celebrated Rakshabandhan at Parliament House, Melbourne, marking the first occasion on which the festival has been formally observed at the Victorian Parliament.
The Treasurer of Victoria, the Hon. Colin Brooks MP, welcomed those gathered with "Jai Swaminarayan" and spoke of the teachings of Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, and of the values they have fostered within the community.
Rakhis were then tied on the wrists of 32 Members of Parliament, each offered as a prayer for the recipient's wellbeing and as a token of mutual respect and protection. Among those who received a rakhi were the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, the Hon. Maree Edwards MP, and the Leader of the Opposition, Ms Jess Wilson MP.
Alongside the ceremony, an exhibition traced the origins of Rakshabandhan and the manner in which it is observed in Hindu homes and at BAPS mandirs. Around 30 representatives of 12 community organisations from across Melbourne joined the occasion, and several Members remarked upon the BAPS activities taking place within their own electorates.
The celebration coincided with a sitting day. As the division bells rang, Members stepped away to vote and returned to resume their conversations, some doing so more than once.
The exhibition came to life through the dedication of volunteers from multiple BAPS centres across Melbourne, who continue to serve their communities selflessly, generation after generation.

/canberra/news/tree-plantation-drive-202.text:
Tree Plantation Drive
BAPS Canberra held its first Tree Plantation Drive, organised in collaboration with the ACT Government’s Environment, Heritage and Parks branch, City and Environment Directorate, and the High Commission of India in Australia.
Ninety-eight community members from 38 families, ranging in age from 5 to 75, took part, planting a total of 50 trees. Each participating family nominated a name for their tree, creating a lasting connection between the families and the trees they planted.
Pujya Priyachintan Swami and Pujya Nirvedmuni Swami planted three trees named for the value of unity in three languages: ‘Unity’ in English, ‘Samp’ in Gujarati and ‘Galumbany’ in the Ngunnawal language. The trees were planted on Ngunnawal Country, and the three names reflect a shared commitment to unity, respect and care for Country and the environment.
The Hon. Suzanne Orr MLA, Member for Yerrabi, Minister for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Affairs and Minister for Climate Change, Environment, Energy and Water, and Mr Rajeev Goswami, First Secretary (Consular) at the High Commission of India in Canberra, joined the volunteers in planting.
The drive was undertaken in the spirit of selfless service through which BAPS volunteers support their communities across Australia.

/robbinsville/news/gujarat-chief-ministe.t: Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendrabhai Patel Visits BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham, Robbinsville, NJ, USA
/robbinsville/news/gujarat-chief-ministe.text:
The Honorable Bhupendrabhai Patel, Chief Minister of Gujarat, India, visited BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, New Jersey, on Saturday, August 22, 2026. During his visit, he expressed deep appreciation for Akshardham’s inspiring presentation of India’s spiritual and cultural heritage, its commitment to community service, and the extraordinary dedication of its volunteers.
Welcome & Akshardham Tour
Upon his arrival, Chief Minister Patel was warmly welcomed and garlanded by Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami and Pujya Nilkanthsevadas Swami. He was accompanied by a delegation of senior Gujarat government officials, including the Additional Chief Secretary of the Finance Department; Dr. Sanjeev Kumar, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister; and Vikrant Pandey, Secretary to the Chief Minister.Already familiar with BAPS and its deep roots in Gujarat, the Chief Minister reflected on how Akshardham carries India’s timeless values of service, spirituality, and excellence to communities around the world. He emphasized the importance of preserving cultural values among the Indian diaspora and expressed his appreciation for the way Akshardham nurtures and celebrates India’s cultural heritage in the United States.
Interaction With Volunteers
A highlight of the visit was Chief Minister Patel’s interaction with the volunteers who serve throughout Akshardham. He commended their discipline, humility, hospitality, and spirit of seva (selfless service), recognizing how their collective contributions help create a welcoming and meaningful experience for visitors from around the world.
Tour of the Akshardham Museum
Chief Minister Patel also received a special tour of the Akshardham Museum, currently under construction, and will be one of the first Hindu American museums dedicated to showcasing India’s rich heritage and culture. The museum will feature 12 architectural replicas, 40 multimedia shows, 85 immersive dioramas, and 200 lifelike statues. He described the museum as a landmark in itself, offering visitors of every age and background an opportunity to connect with universal ideals of faith, harmony, compassion, family values, and selfless service. He noted that these enduring principles continue to guide Gujarat’s progress and strengthen India’s cultural identity while remaining relevant to people and cultures worldwide.
Assembly
“It was a privilege to have Gujarat’s Honorable Chief Minister, Bhupendrabhai Patel, visit BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville today,” said Pujya Brahmaviharidas Swami, a senior swami of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. “Not only was he overwhelmed and fascinated by the beautiful carvings and the sheer size and scale of the Mandir, but he was deeply touched by its serene and spiritual environment. While touring the museum, the Chief Minister remarked, ‘You brought India’s ancient culture back to life.”
“From my heart, I thank all the BAPS volunteers for their contributions to the construction of Akshardham, which will inspire many generations to come,” Chief Minister Patel said. “Everyone who comes here from across the world will find peace, wherever he or she is from.”
Chief Minister Patel is visiting the United States in connection with the Vibrant Gujarat initiative, marking the first visit by a Chief Minister of Gujarat to the United States in nearly 30 years. Reflecting on his experience at Akshardham, he noted that while his visit focused on Vibrant Gujarat, he remarked that India's culture is vibrant at BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham. More than a place of worship, he observed, Akshardham is a celebration of culture, art, spirituality, and enduring values.
Delegates and community leaders from across the United States gathered to welcome the Chief Minister and mark the occasion. The visit further highlighted the important role BAPS has played in preserving and sharing India’s rich spiritual and cultural heritage around the world. Through mandirs, educational programs, humanitarian relief initiatives, healthcare services, environmental awareness, youth development, and cultural activities, BAPS has contributed significantly to the well-being of communities in Gujarat, throughout India, and across the globe.

/india/news/baps-flood-relief-work-in-as.t: BAPS Flood Relief Work in Assam
/india/news/baps-flood-relief-work-in-as.text:
Assam
Incessant rainfall caused devastating floods across Assam, inundating hundreds of villages and severely disrupting daily life.
After learning about the situation, Mahant Swami Maharaj immediately sent BAPS swamis from Kolkata to visit the flood-affected communities and assess their needs. The swamis travelled through affected villages, prepared a list of essential items urgently required by residents and reported their findings to Swamishri.
Mahant Swami Maharaj expressed his concern for both the people and livestock affected by the floods and offered prayers for everyone. He also instructed the swamis to provide essential help to the affected families.
From 16 August, volunteers began relief operations across Sivasagar, Demow, Mangaldoi and Darrang, including Dolakasharia, Ligiribari Garhbhanga, Phulpani Chinga, Nora Kunwar Bailung, Nimai Zones 1, 2 and 5, Khatpathar Shyamnagar, Gadkosh Kaivarta, Mangaldoi Nagar, Bengabara, Mathanga, Ahaka and other villages and towns.
Under the guidance of government officials and local villagers, swamis and volunteers personally distributed thousands of mattresses, blankets, buckets, tubs, mosquito nets, pillows, bedsheets and other essential items to those affected.
Also, special animal-relief kits were prepared. Over 25,000 kg of nutritious animal feed was distributed, together with medicines for 1,000 sick animals.
Appreciating the relief work by BAPS, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma remarked, “Mahant Swami Maharaj is so compassionate. He has sent all of you here from Gujarat to serve.”
Media & Coverage

/india/news/bal-parayans-2026-shrimad-bh.text:
Shrimad Bhagavad Gita
Each year, during the holy month of Shravan, the Bal Pravrutti Central Offices organize inspiring 3-day Bal Parayans, in which boys under 14 gather separately at their local centers to hear their peers recite shastras and explore their deeper messages.
This year’s Bal Parayans were based on the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, one of Sanatan Hindu Dharma’s most revered shastras.
Over three days, the children explored Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s timeless teachings, including the importance of self-confidence, self-control, and faith in God.
Each parayan began with a palkhi yatra, a ceremonial procession carrying the sacred shastra into the venue, which the children themselves decorated with colorful displays. The children then sang dhun and prarthana, performed pujan while singing Sanskrit verses, and presented lively theme songs and skits.
Young speakers then took their places at the vyas peeth (speaker’s platform). They shared the scripture’s teachings through shlokas, couplets, devotional verses, stories, real-life incidents, and videos. These engaging presentations brought the teachings to life and made them easy for children in the audience to understand and relate to.
Across India, a total of 1,221 Bal Parayans took place, in which more than 67,600 boys participated.
The Bal Parayans inspired the children to practice Bhagwan Shri Krishna’s teachings in their daily lives and earn the heartfelt blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj.
