/newdelhi/news/sadhguru-visits-swaminara.text:
Sadhguru
Despite heavy rainfall, Indian spiritual leader Jaggi Vasudev (Sadhguru), founder of the Isha Foundation, visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi on 11 August 2026.
On behalf of HH Mahant Swami Maharaj, he was warmly welcomed at the main steps in a traditional way by Divyamurti Swami.
Expressing admiration for the mandir’s breathtaking architecture and profound spiritual atmosphere, Sadhguru offered a garland at the sacred feet of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as a mark of respect.

/newdelhi/news/central-sanskrit-universi.t: Central Sanskrit University Confers ‘Vedanta Vidya Vishvaguru’ Honor to Bhadreshdas Swami
/newdelhi/news/central-sanskrit-universi.text:
‘Vedanta Vidya Vishvaguru’ Honor to Bhadreshdas Swami
The Central Sanskrit University, widely recognized as among the premier Sanskrit institutions globally, organized a function at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, to confer the distinguished ‘Vedanta Vidya Vishvaguru’ title on Mahamahopadhyaya Bhadreshdas Swami in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to the study, research, and global promotion of Vedanta, Sanskrit literature, and the Indian knowledge tradition.
This occasion was graced by Param Pujya Shri Shri Vishwaprasanna Theertha Swamiji of the Pejavara Adhokshaja Matha in Udupi; Prof. Srinivasa Varkhedi, Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University; Prof. Sukanta Kumar Senapati, Vice-Chancellor of Shree Somnath Sanskrit University; Prof. V. Narayanan; Prof. Omnath Bimli; Prof. Muralikrishna; Prof. Ganesh T. Pandit; and other distinguished scholars.
On this occasion, Param Pujya Shri Shri Vishwaprasanna Theertha Swami Maharaj, a revered swami of the Madhvacharya tradition, praised Bhadreshdas Swami’s philosophical brilliance and highlighted the true significance of the award.
Prof. Srinivasa Varkhedi stated that this honor was being conferred on Bhadreshdas Swami for his remarkable contributions in firmly establishing the classical framework of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan within the Sanskrit Prasthanatrayi tradition.
Prof. Sukanta Kumar Senapati shared that Bhadreshdas Swami has become a globally renowned scholar today owing to the grace and blessings of his gurus, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.
Prof. V. Narayanan read out the official citation, and all present warmly welcomed this distinguished honor with enthusiastic applause.
In his acceptance address, Bhadreshdas Swami dedicated the honor at the feet of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and gurus Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj.

/india/news/become-adarsh-project-launch.t: ‘Become Adarsh’ Project Launched in Darrang, Assam
/india/news/become-adarsh-project-launch.text:
Become Adarsh
At the District Library Auditorium in Mangaldai, the BAPS Children’s Activities Central Office launched the ‘Become Adarsh’ project for school students in the Darrang district of Assam. More than 1,500 principals and teachers from schools across the district attended the program.
The morning session began with the traditional lighting of the lamp and took place in the presence of Smt. Nilima Devi, Cabinet Minister, Government of Assam; Shri Anupam Deka, Industrialist; Shri Devajit Barua, Development Commissioner, Darrang district; Shri Jayanta Thakuria, District Education Officer; Smt. Nirmali Devi, Municipal Chairperson; Shri Pratap Bordoloi, Chairman, Urban Development Authority, and other dignitaries.
The afternoon session was attended by Shri Gurujyoti Das, Chairman, Assam Fisheries Development Corporation; Shri Paresh Kumar Sharma, retired teacher of Mangaldai College, and other prominent personalities.
The Become Adarsh project focuses on developing good values, character, healthy habits, interest in education, Indian culture and a sense of responsibility among students. Through the Become Adarsh mobile application, schools will receive inspirational and educational videos that will help in the overall development of students.
On this occasion, Jnannayandas Swami delivered an inspiring talk explaining that true education is not only about academic knowledge, but should also help a person develop good values, character and moral thinking that will guide them to make the right choices in life.
The program highlighted the important role of teachers in shaping not only the academic future of students but also their values, character and sense of responsibility towards society and the nation.
The program concluded with the National Anthem. All the participating teachers took a pledge to promote value-based and character-building education and to contribute towards building a brighter future for India.
Words of Appreciation
“The Become Adarsh project of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha will help bring positive change in society. Such an initiative is important for the interest of the nation.”
- Hon. Smt. Nilima Devi, Cabinet Minister, Government of Assam
“BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha has started this initiative to develop valuable qualities such as good values, morality and devotion among students. This is a very good initiative, and students across Assam will benefit greatly from the Become Adarsh project.”
- Shri Jayanta Thakuria, District Education Officer, Darrang
“The Become Adarsh project will give a new direction to the students of Assam. It will also help teachers in developing good values among their students.”
- Shri Anupam Deka, Industrialist

/vancouver/news/murti-pratishtha-mahotsa.text:
The Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Vancouver, British Columbia, was celebrated through a series of sacred ceremonies held from July 19 to August 2, 2026. The historic celebrations culminated in the Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav on August 2, during which Hindu Vedic rituals were performed to consecrate the sacred murtis in the presence of BAPS swamis from North America, dignitaries, community leaders, devotees, and well-wishers from across the region.
The growth of the BAPS community in Vancouver has been guided by the vision and blessings of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj and His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. Over the years, regular spiritual assemblies, cultural activities, and volunteer-driven initiatives have fostered a vibrant and growing community dedicated to preserving Hindu traditions, values, and heritage.
Women’s Cultural Program.
The celebrations commenced on July 19 with a Women’s Cultural Program. Through traditional dances, speeches, and video presentations, the program highlighted the vital role mandirs play in nurturing faith, culture, and values across generations. The event also celebrated the contributions of women in strengthening families, communities, and cultural traditions.
Jal Yatra
The inauguration festivities continued on July 29 with a Jal Yatra, a sacred procession held on the waters of Burrard Inlet. Hundreds of devotees participated in this unique event, offering prayers and devotion as the sanctified murtis were ceremonially welcomed.
Vedic Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna
The Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna was held on August 1, during which devotees gathered to offer Vedic prayers for global peace, harmony, and the well-being of society.
Reflecting on the significance of the Vishwa Shanti Mahayagna, MP Tamara Jansen shared, “In a world that can often feel divided, gatherings like this remind us that peace begins with each of us, in our homes, our communities, and in how we care for one another.”
Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav
The festivities culminated on August 2 with the Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav. Amid Vedic chanting and sacred rituals, the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami, Ghanshyam Maharaj, Bhagwan Shri Krishna and Shri Radhaji, Bhagwan Shri Ram and Shri Sitaji, Shri Hanumanji, Bhagwan Shri Shankar and Shri Parvatiji, Shri Ganapatiji, and the Guru Parampara were consecrated in their respective shrines. A murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj was also installed, enabling devotees to perform the traditional abhishek ritual. The ceremonies were performed by Pujya Yagnavallabh Swami, Senior Swami of BAPS North America.
Special guest attendees
Tamara Jansen, Member of Parliament for Cloverdale-Langley City
Brent Chapman, Member of the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia for Surrey South
Mayor Brenda Locke, City of Surrey
Councillor Dylan Kruger, City of Delta
Councillor Linda Annis, City of Surrey
Councillor Mike Bose, City of Surrey
Shri Ravinder Mangla, Acting Consul General of India in Vancouver
Ashwant K. Dwivedi, Honorary Consul General of the Solomon Islands to Canada
MLA Brent Chapman remarked, “May this mandir serve as a place where culture is preserved and where people of different faiths can come together in understanding.”
Mayor Brenda Locke congratulated the community on the opening of the new mandir and noted that it marked the beginning of a new chapter for the many families who will gather there for years to come.
Councillor Dylan Kruger congratulated the BAPS community on this historic milestone and praised the organization's longstanding contributions to Canada through community service, charitable initiatives, and volunteerism. He remarked, “We are so blessed to have BAPS here in Canada, and of course, to have this mandir in our community of Delta,” and expressed his continued support for the mandir and its future growth within the community.
Councillor Linda Annis expressed her appreciation for the milestone occasion, noting the strong support for the growth of the local Hindu community and the important role the mandir will play in serving future generations.
Shri Ravinder Mangla stated, “This temple is far more than a place of worship. It is a centre of faith, values, learning, and selfless service that nurtures spiritual growth, fosters harmony, and strengthens communities.”
The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Vancouver will continue to serve as a centre for spiritual, cultural, and humanitarian activities for people of all ages. Through weekly assemblies, educational programs, cultural initiatives, and community service activities, the mandir will help preserve Hindu traditions and values while fostering understanding, inclusivity, and service to the wider community.
The creation of this mandir is the culmination of the dedicated efforts of volunteers, supporters, and well-wishers whose commitment and service have helped establish a lasting centre of faith and community for future generations.

/india/news/nasha-mukta-bharat-2-2.t: BAPS Youths Join Government of India’s ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ Pledge Campaign
/india/news/nasha-mukta-bharat-2-2.text:
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ Pledge Campaign
With the objective of inspiring India’s youth to lead addiction-free lives and become catalysts for positive social change, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today launched the nationwide ‘Nasha Mukta Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’ (Drug-Free Youth for a Developed India Pledge Campaign). Young people from thousands of locations across the country participated virtually in the programme, including MY Bharat volunteers, NSS volunteers, schools, colleges, educational institutions, and more than 125 spiritual organizations.
More than 30,000 young men and women from over 60 BAPS centers across India participated in the campaign. BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha organized special assemblies for youths at all its centres, during which participants took the online ‘Nasha Mukta Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ pledge, reaffirming their commitment to the campaign.
In Ahmedabad, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, International Convener of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, delivered an inspiring message to the youths, saying, “Bhagwan Swaminarayan commanded his followers to remain free from all addictions. Only one who is free from addictions can become a true satsangi.” He further added that since Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is inspiring the nation’s youth through this campaign, everyone should come forward with enthusiasm and dedication to support it.

/india/news/national-sanskrit-university.t: National Sanskrit University Launches New Academic Courses in ‘Akshar-Purushottam Darshan’, Tirupati
/india/news/national-sanskrit-university.text:
National Sanskrit University (NSU), Tirupati, a premier Central University of India, formally inaugurated its new Shastri (B.A.) and Acharya (M.A.) academic courses in ‘Akshar-Purushottam Darshan’, the Vedic doctrine propounded by Parabrahma Swaminarayan. It will now give students the opportunity to study Akshar-Purushottam Darshan with the same academic depth as other classical philosophies. The inauguration event, organized by the Faculty of Darshanas (Philosophies), took place in the Chelkani Annarao Auditorium.
The afternoon ceremony commenced with soul-stirring Vedic verses sung by university students, followed by traditional prayers by swamis and devotees of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. The program was formally inaugurated with the lighting of the lamp by the dignitaries.
Academic Inclusion of Vedic Ideology
The official inauguration of the new curriculum was performed by eminent scholar Bhadreshdas Swami, Head of the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute, and Prof. Gullapalli S.R. Krishnamurti, Vice-Chancellor of NSU.
A Global Philosophy for Peace
Welcoming the guests, Prof. K. Ganapathi Bhat, Dean of the Faculty of Darshanas, emphasized that this is no ordinary occasion. He stated, “Just as Adi Shankaracharya and Madhvacharya established centers to spread Vedic knowledge throughout India, the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha has established spiritual centers globally, from Abu Dhabi to Paris. Now, a center for Akshar-Purushottam Darshan has been established at NSU.” He further added that this philosophy is based on providing inner peace and harmony rather than intellectual conflict.
The Ocean of Vedic Sanatana Dharma
In his inauguration address, Bhadreshdas Swami described Vedic Sanatana Dharma as a vast ocean, “The same Vedic knowledge has flowed in the forms of Advaita, Vishishtadvaita, or Dvaita, and today it is flowing in the form of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan.” He quoted the definition given by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj: “The Akshar-Purushottam principle should be well known, as it is the form of Brahmavidya – divine, Vedic, and eternal.” He described NSU as a ‘rare university’ that maintains a unique balance of respect for philosophy, tradition, and devotion. He likened the start of these courses to sowing a seed that will eventually grow into a massive banyan tree of knowledge.
Confluence of Ancient Tradition and Modern Expansion
Presiding over the ceremony, Vice-Chancellor Prof. G.S.R. Krishnamurti highlighted a significant historical parallel. He mentioned that after Adi Shankaracharya, it is Bhadreshdas Swami who has accomplished the monumental task of writing Sanskrit commentaries (Bhashyas) on all three foundational texts of Vedanta (the Prasthanatrayi). He credited His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj for awakening this philosophy in the hearts of the masses and giving it a global identity. The Vice-Chancellor added, “We have established this department to ensure that this profound philosophy reaches every individual. Today we have sown a small seed; in the future, it will flourish and bloom into a grand banyan tree.”
Commemorating Spiritual Heritage
The launch of these courses coincides with the first anniversary of the creation of the ‘Akshar-Purushottam Darshan Mandap’ on the university campus. Like other Mandaps, this pavilion has been instrumental in providing philosophical knowledge to students. More than 300 devotees gathered to witness this academic and spiritual milestone.
The program concluded with a vote of thanks by Prof. Narayan from the Department of Dvaita Vedanta, who coordinated the event along with Dr. Gyanranjan Panda, Co-coordinator of the Sahitya Department.
संसद के अधिनियम द्वारा स्थापित प्रमुख केंद्रीय विश्वविद्यालय, राष्ट्रीय संस्कृत विश्वविद्यालय (NSU), तिरुपति ने आज परब्रह्म स्वामिनारायण प्रबोधित 'अक्षरपुरुषोत्तम दर्शन' में नए शास्त्री (बी.ए.) और आचार्य (एम.ए.) शैक्षणिक पाठ्यक्रमों के औपचारिक उद्घाटन के साथ एक ऐतिहासिक मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया। दर्शन संकाय के अंतर्गत आयोजित यह कार्यक्रम चेलकानि अन्नाराव सभागार में संपन्न हुआ।
समारोह की शुरुआत अपराह्न 4:00 बजे विश्वविद्यालय के छात्रों द्वारा हृदयस्पर्शी वैदिक मंगलाचरण के साथ हुई, जिसके बाद बी.ए.पी.एस. (BAPS) स्वामीनारायण संप्रदाय के संतों और भक्तों द्वारा पारंपरिक प्रार्थना की गई। कार्यक्रम का औपचारिक शुभारंभ उपस्थित गणमान्य व्यक्तियों द्वारा दीप प्रज्वलन के साथ हुआ।
वैदिक विचारधारा का शैक्षणिक समावेशन
नए पाठ्यक्रम का आधिकारिक उद्घाटन बी.ए.पी.एस. स्वामीनारायण शोध संस्थान के प्रमुख और प्रख्यात विद्वान साधु भद्रेशदास स्वामी तथा एनएसयू के कुलपति प्रो. गुल्लपल्लि एस.आर. कृष्णमूर्ति द्वारा किया गया। 'प्रस्थानत्रयी स्वामीनारायण भाष्य' के रचयिता साधु भद्रेशदास स्वामी ने अक्षरपुरुषोत्तम दर्शन को एक विशिष्ट वैदिक दर्शन के रूप में शैक्षणिक मान्यता दिलाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई है।
शांति के लिए एक वैश्विक दर्शन
अतिथियों का स्वागत करते हुए, दर्शन संकाय के अधिष्ठाता (डीन) प्रो. के. गणपति भट्ट ने जोर देकर कहा कि यह कोई साधारण अवसर नहीं है। उन्होंने कहा, "जिस तरह आदि शंकराचार्य और मध्वाचार्य ने पूरे भारत में वैदिक ज्ञान फैलाने के लिए केंद्रों की स्थापना की, उसी तरह बी.ए.पी.एस. स्वामीनारायण संस्था ने अबू धाबी से पेरिस तक विश्व स्तर पर आध्यात्मिक केंद्र स्थापित किए हैं। अब, एनएसयू में अक्षरपुरुषोत्तम दर्शन के लिए एक केंद्र स्थापित किया गया है।" उन्होंने आगे कहा कि यह दर्शन बौद्धिक संघर्ष के बजाय आंतरिक शांति और सद्भाव प्रदान करने पर आधारित है।
वैदिक सनातन धर्म का महासागर
अपने उद्घाटन भाषण में, साधु भद्रेशदास स्वामी ने वैदिक सनातन धर्म को एक विशाल महासागर बताया। उन्होंने कहा, "वही वैदिक ज्ञान अद्वैत, विशिष्टाद्वैत या द्वैत के रूप में प्रवाहित हुआ है, और आज यह अक्षरपुरुषोत्तम दर्शन के रूप में प्रवाहित हो रहा है।" उन्होंने परम पूज्य महंत स्वामी महाराज द्वारा दी गई परिभाषा को उद्धृत किया: "अक्षरपुरुषोत्तम सिद्धांत को अच्छी तरह से जानना चाहिए, जो ब्रह्मविद्या का स्वरूप, दिव्य, वैदिक और सनातन है।" उन्होंने एनएसयू को एक "दुर्लभ विश्वविद्यालय" बताया जो दर्शन, परंपरा और भक्ति के प्रति सम्मान का अनूठा संतुलन बनाए रखता है। उन्होंने इन पाठ्यक्रमों की शुरुआत की तुलना एक बीज बोने से की जो आगे चलकर ज्ञान का एक विशाल वटवृक्ष बनेगा।
प्राचीन परंपरा और आधुनिक विस्तार का संगम
समारोह की अध्यक्षता करते हुए, कुलपति प्रो. जी.एस.आर. कृष्णमूर्ति ने एक महत्वपूर्ण ऐतिहासिक समानता बताई। उन्होंने उल्लेख किया कि आदि शंकराचार्य के बाद, यह साधु भद्रेशदास स्वामी ही हैं जिन्होंने वेदान्त के तीनों आधारभूत ग्रंथों (प्रस्थानत्रयी) पर संस्कृत भाष्य लिखने का महान कार्य संपन्न किया है। उन्होंने इस दर्शन को जन-जन के हृदय में जगाने और इसे वैश्विक पहचान दिलाने का श्रेय परम पूज्य प्रमुख स्वामी महाराज को दिया। कुलपति ने आगे कहा, "हमने इस विभाग की स्थापना यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए की है कि यह गहन दर्शन प्रत्येक व्यक्ति तक पहुंचे। आज हमने एक छोटा सा बीज बोया है; भविष्य में यह एक विशाल वटवृक्ष के रूप में पुष्पित-पल्लवित होगा।"
आध्यात्मिक विरासत का स्मरण
इन पाठ्यक्रमों का शुभारंभ विश्वविद्यालय परिसर में ’अक्षरपुरुषोत्तम दर्शन मंडप’ की रचना के अवसर को एक वर्ष पूर्ण होने पर हुआ है। अन्य मंडपों की तरह यह मंडप भी विद्यार्थीओं को दार्शनिक ज्ञान होने के लिए उपकारक बना है। बी.ए.पी.एस. के वर्तमान आध्यात्मिक प्रमुख परम पूज्य महंत स्वामी महाराज की कृपा से, इस शैक्षणिक और आध्यात्मिक मील के पत्थर का साक्षी बनने के लिए 300 से अधिक श्रद्धालु एकत्रित हुए।
निष्कर्ष
शास्त्री और आचार्य कार्यक्रमों की शुरुआत यह सुनिश्चित करती है कि राष्ट्रीय संस्कृत विश्वविद्यालय के छात्रों को अब अन्य शास्त्रीय दर्शनों की तरह ही शैक्षणिक गहनता के साथ अक्षरपुरुषोत्तम दर्शन का अध्ययन करने का अवसर मिलेगा।
कार्यक्रम का समापन द्वैत वेदान्त विभाग के प्रो. नारायण द्वारा प्रस्तावित धन्यवाद ज्ञापन के साथ हुआ, जिन्होंने साहित्य विभाग के सह-संयोजक डॉ. ज्ञानरंजन पण्डा के साथ कार्यक्रम का समन्वय किया।

/india/news/hindola-festival-2026.text:
Every year, during the monsoon months of Ashadh and Shravan (July - August) the mandirs in India and abroad are awash with devotion. The arrival of the Hindola Utsav during these months usher a new breeze of bhakti and festivity in the mandirs of India. For one whole month, the chal (mobile) murti of the Lord is placed in a hindola and pulled to and fro with a string. The sadhus and devotees sing the hindola bhajans with the accompaniment of the mrudang and cymbals. The mandir ambience is charged with the sound and fragrance of bhakti.
The festival finds its origin in the streets of Vrundavan 5000 years ago where the Gopis rocked Lord Krishna on a decorated swing. Ever since, to experience the divine joy of rocking the mighty Lord in a small swing, the hindola festival became the focus of devotion.
Even Lord Swaminarayan was revered and entertained by the devotees through their devotion. Once in Vartal, a decorative hindolo was tied to a couple of mango trees, and the devotees rocked the Lord to and fro. In response to their devotion, the Lord, while standing in the hindola, appeared in twelve divine forms and blessed the devotees. History also reveals that Lord Swaminarayan often sat on a swing tied between two tamarind trees at Laxmivadi in Gadhada.
Today, in memory of the Lord's divine sports, the hindola festival is celebrated with joy and enthusiasm at all Swaminarayan mandirs. It is an aesthetic experience of devotion to the Lord, requiring meticulous preparation by sadhus and devotees to produce hindolas of a variety of colors, shapes and forms. The hindolas are made of vegetables,leaves, flowers, earthen pots, fruits, dry fruits, beans, rakhis, chocolates, steel dishes and cups, etc.
Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Shri Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj

/birmingham-al/news/inauguration-of-baps.t: Inauguration of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Birmingham, AL
/birmingham-al/news/inauguration-of-baps.text:
The Murti Pratishtha Mahotsav of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Birmingham, Alabama, was celebrated through a series of sacred ceremonies and cultural programs from July 31 to August 2, 2026.
The new mandir represents the culmination of more than four decades of devotion, perseverance, and selfless service that have defined the local BAPS community. Inspired by the vision and blessings of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the community took root in the 1980s through small weekly spiritual assemblies. As the congregation grew, these gatherings led to the establishment of a hari mandir in Roebuck in 1997.
Following the mandir’s expansion and the arrival of new murtis, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed their murti pratishtha on September 23, 2000. For the next twenty-six years, the mandir in Roebuck served as a spiritual home where generations of devotees gathered to worship, celebrate Hindu festivals, nurture their spiritual growth, and strengthen family and community bonds. Rooted in the timeless values of Hinduism, the community carried these values beyond the mandir through service, compassion, and volunteerism.
The sacred murtis for the new mandir were consecrated by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj on August 20, 2023, in Robbinsville, New Jersey. Their installation in Birmingham marked the continuation of this spiritual journey and the beginning of a new chapter for the community.
The three-day celebration brought together more than 1,000 devotees, dignitaries, community leaders, guests, and well-wishers from across Alabama and beyond, offering all who attended an opportunity to experience the mandir’s serenity, spirituality, and timeless beauty firsthand.
Kirtan Aradhana
The celebrations commenced on Friday evening, July 31, 2026, with a Kirtan Aradhana, an evening of devotional music and prayer. Devotees and swamis offered traditional compositions in praise of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Gunatit Guru Parampara, creating an atmosphere of joy, devotion, and spiritual reflection.
Vishwashanti Mahayagna
On August 1, 2026, devotees gathered for the first Vishwashanti Mahayagna to be held in Birmingham. Participants offered prayers and oblations into the sacred fire as swamis recited Vedic mantras. The yagna sanctified the mandir in preparation for the installation ceremony and concluded with prayers for peace, harmony, and the well-being of people and communities worldwide.
Women’s Cultural Program
On the afternoon of August 1, 2026, an uplifting celebration for women, by women, brought traditional music, dance, and cultural heritage to life. Through vibrant performances and meaningful presentations, the program celebrated women's pivotal role and honored the selfless sacrifice, dedication, and service through which they helped transform the vision of the new mandir into a sacred reality for generations to come.
Nagar Yatra
On August 1, 2026, the day concluded with the Shobha Yatra, a jubilant ceremonial procession welcoming the sacred murtis to their new home. Devotees dressed in radiant traditional attire filled the procession with devotional singing, cultural dances, and festive music, transforming the streets into a vibrant celebration of faith and heritage.
The procession symbolized the sacred murtis extending their divine presence and blessings to the wider community, bringing people together in a shared spirit of faith, unity, and harmony.
Murti Sthapan Vidhi
On August 2, 2026, Pujya Gnanpriyadas Swami performed the sacred Murti Sthapan Vidhi. As swamis chanted Vedic mantras and performed traditional rituals, the sacred murtis—previously consecrated by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj—were reverently installed in their respective shrines.
The murtis included Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami, Ghanshyam Maharaj, Bhagwan Shri Krishna and Shri Radhaji, Bhagwan Shri Ram and Shri Sitaji, Shri Hanumanji, Bhagwan Shri Shankar and Shri Parvatiji, Shri Ganapatiji, and the Guru Parampara.
The sacred ceremony established the new mandir as a place of devotion, tranquility, reflection, and spiritual growth for generations to come.
Dedication Assembly
The inauguration festivities culminated in the dedication assembly, a grand commemorative assembly celebrating the remarkable journey that brought the new mandir to life.
The program reflected upon the core pillars of samp (harmony), seva (selfless service), satsang (spiritual fellowship), and samarpan (sacrifice) that sustained the community throughout this journey. Swamis, dignitaries, community leaders, and devotees gathered to recognize decades of dedication and volunteerism, while reflecting upon the mandir’s future role as an enduring source of spirituality, inspiration, and service. The occasion was filled with heartfelt gratitude for the countless individuals and families whose devotion, sacrifice, and selfless efforts helped make this historic milestone possible.
The three-day celebration brought together distinguished dignitaries, community leaders, and various guests from across Alabama, whose presence reflected the strong relationships, mutual respect, and shared commitment to service cultivated by the BAPS community throughout the state. Among the distinguished guests were U.S. Representatives Gary Palmer and Mike Rogers; former Alabama Secretary of State John H. Merrill; Alabama State Representatives Mike Shaw, Ginny Shaver, Leigh Hulsey, Patrick Sellers, and Phillip Ensler; Jefferson County Tax Assessor Gaynell Hendricks and Assistant Tax Assessor Charles R. Winston, Jr.; Birmingham City Councilor Darrell O’Quinn; former Pelham City Council President Maurice Mercer; Hoover City Councilors Derrick Murphy and Steve McClinton; former Hoover City Council President John B. Lyda; Walter F. Scott III, attorney and legal counsel for the mandir project; and Ethan Vice, District Director for U.S. Representative Gary Palmer.
With its doors now open, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Birmingham begins a new chapter as a spiritual and cultural landmark for Alabama and the broader Southeast. It will provide a place for worship, spiritual learning, cultural enrichment, and community gathering, while serving people of all ages through religious, educational, youth, family, health and wellness, humanitarian, and volunteer initiatives.
Building upon more than four decades of faith and service, the mandir will continue to uplift lives, strengthen families, and contribute to the wider community—carrying forward a legacy of devotion, unity, and selfless service for generations to come.

/melbourne/news/baps-womens-leadership-s.t: BAPS Women's Leadership Seminar at the Parliament of Victoria
/melbourne/news/baps-womens-leadership-s.text:
The Parliament of Victoria
On Tuesday 28 July 2026, 85 women from BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, representing communities across metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria, attended the BAPS Women's Leadership Seminar at Parliament House, Melbourne. The seminar was hosted by the Hon. Lily D'Ambrosio MP, Minister for Energy and Resources, Minister for Climate Action and Minister for the State Electricity Commission.
Ms Sarah Connolly MP, Member for Laverton, conducted the program. The keynote address was delivered by the Deputy Premier of Victoria, the Hon. Gabrielle Williams MP, who spoke on the qualities and skills that shape effective leadership.
Members of Parliament shared the experiences that had shaped their careers, the challenges they had overcome and the values that continue to guide them in public life. Their accounts encouraged those present to embrace opportunities, remain resilient and lead with integrity, compassion and purpose.
"Leadership is about showing up, listening to your community and being prepared to serve," one Member of Parliament said. "Every one of you has the ability to make a meaningful difference, no matter where your journey begins."
The seminar also drew out the common ground between public service and the principles of BAPS. Guided by the teachings of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS encourages individuals to lead with humility, selfless service and compassion, and to make a positive difference within their communities.
Following the formal program, those present had the opportunity to speak with parliamentarians and ask questions about leadership in public life. Bringing together participants from across the state, including regional communities, the seminar formed part of the ongoing work of BAPS in encouraging women to serve society with compassion and integrity.

/chicago/news/honoring-americas-250th-an.t: Honoring America's 250th Anniversary Through Unity, Service, and Community, Chicago, IL
/chicago/news/honoring-americas-250th-an.text:
As the United States celebrates the 250th anniversary of its independence, devotees at BAPS Hindu mandirs across North America joined local communities to commemorate this historic milestone through service, reflection, and civic engagement.
As an official America250 supporting partner, BAPS is honored to participate in this nationwide commemoration, helping foster unity, service, and civic engagement across communities.
BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Chicago, participated in America 250 through a variety of events.
The American Gift
Over the same weekend, the mandir's weekly spiritual assembly featured a special program titled "The American Gift," reflecting on how the nation provides opportunity, community, and shared values. Hundreds of Hindu Americans gathered to celebrate, joining together in a flag-raising ceremony that honored their identity as devoted members of both their faith and their country.
Interfaith Dialogue
On July 15, 2026, an interfaith evening celebrating America 250 brought together friends from the Christian, Islamic, and Hindu traditions. Representatives from Baitul Ilm Academy in Streamwood, Immanuel United Church of Christ in Streamwood, and The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Schaumburg joined the gathering.
Themed “Shared Paths, United Hearts,” the evening featured a thoughtful panel discussion on how faith communities can foster understanding through shared values, bridge differences with mutual respect, and work together to contribute to America’s next chapter.
The celebrations highlighted the values that unite communities across backgrounds and beliefs. Through interfaith discussions on religious liberty and pluralism, as well as volunteer efforts supporting local causes, devotees reflected on how America's ideals have allowed generations to preserve their traditions while giving back to the communities they call home.
For more than 50 years in North America, BAPS has worked to serve society through humanitarian relief efforts, health awareness initiatives, educational programs, environmental campaigns, and community service activities. As the United States marked 250 years, BAPS devotees were honored to celebrate not only the nation's history, but also the opportunity to continue building stronger, more compassionate communities together.

/india/news/gujarat-flood-relief-work-20.text:
Gujarat Flood Relief 2026
Following heavy rainfall across Gujarat that triggered severe flooding in Dholka, Valsad, and Navsari-Dang districts, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha swamis and volunteers, under the guidance of Mahant Swami Maharaj, carried out extensive relief operations — many wading through chest/waist-deep water to reach stranded families.
Dholka:
2,000+ food packets distributed (avg. 700–800/day)
Drinking water distributed to stranded residents
Shelter provided to NDRF/Army personnel and flood-affected families
Valsad: (Tithal, Chikhli, Khaparwada, Dungri mandirs)
11,500 food packets, 1,600 water bottles, 1,500 ration kits distributed
385 volunteer instances over 3 days
Reached flood/rail-affected areas, low-lying zones, railway station, and government offices
Sankari:
200 ration kits distributed to flood/rail-affected areas
Navsari & Dang: (Bilimora, Undhach, Gandevi, Navsari city)
Hot khichdi meals served to 3,500 people over 2 days
Fresh breakfast served to 500 people
250 post-flood ration kits (grains, pulses, spices, sugar, oil, tea, biscuits, chevdo) distributed
Across all affected regions, BAPS swamis and volunteers reaffirmed their commitment to service, compassion, and humanity in times of disaster.

/nadiad/news/rathyatra-celebration-2026.text:
Rathyatra
The 149th Rathyatra was celebrated with great joy and devotion at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Nadiad, on Thursday, 16 July 2026. The Rathyatra was celebrated in a grand and divine atmosphere, with devotees participating with great enthusiasm and devotion.
Pujya Sarva Mangal Swami shared the history and importance of the Rathyatra and gave his blessings.
Swamis performed puja and offered fruits and prasad to Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Bhagwan Jagannath. Swamis and youths then took Thakorji on a divine chariot ride. Devotees, volunteers and hostel youths participated enthusiastically and helped make the event successful. The celebration concluded with everyone receiving Thakorji's prasad.

/apac/news/sanskrit-conference-2026.text:
As part of the auspicious silver jubilee celebrations of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in Australia and New Zealand, a five-day conference was organised by the BAPS Swaminarayan Research Institute (BSRI) in Adelaide, Australia. Titled “Sanskrit Conference: Apni Ekta” the conference was inspired by the 100th shloka of the Satsang Diksha, authored by Mahant Swami Maharaj.
The conference served as a powerful testament to the revival of traditional knowledge systems and the real-world applications of Sanskrit.
The conference hosted 292 select students, 64 teachers, and 10 Swamis from the Pacific region. Delegates who participated in the following courses took part in the conference: Satsang Siddhant Adhyayan, Satsang Diksha Visharad and Siddhant Sarvasvam.
The conference utilised multifaceted delivery by incorporating panel discussions, podcasts, and interactive workshops to bridge traditional academia with practical, modern-day practicality. Across the five days, learned local and senior sadhus dived deep into verse 100 from Satsang Diksha focusing on one Ishtadev, one guru and one siddhant.
Alongside content delivered by Swamis and teachers, 14 young scholars presented final exam presentations in the Sanskrit language.
Through their rigorous study of scripture and language, this emerging group of scholars is proudly utilising timeless Hindu traditions to navigate and elevate themselves. A special session at the conference focused on the daily use of Sanskrit for communication, thinking, and learning. The students vowed to develop their understanding of the language to greater heights. Looking ahead, delegates will learn to integrate Sanskrit into their daily conversations at home, lead prayers and scriptural readings during assemblies, and assist with teaching Sanskrit to younger children. These practical next steps ensure that the knowledge gained at the conference will have a real and lasting impact, both in their personal lives and throughout the community.
Senior Swamis also had given their guidance via zoom call and inspired the children to balance their studies and Sanskrit learnings, while providing practical tips for how to study. Mahant Swami Maharaj had also sent special video blessings for these young scholars which showed the path for true success in their life.

/miami/news/silver-jubilee-celebrations-.t: Silver Jubilee Celebrations of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Miami, FL
/miami/news/silver-jubilee-celebrations-.text:
A vibrant celebration of tradition, music, and community service took center stage as hundreds gathered at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Boynton Beach, Florida, to celebrate a historic milestone: the Rajat Jayanti Mahotsav. Marking 25 years of cultural preservation, unity, and growth, the Silver Jubilee brought together multiple generations for an unforgettable weekend of reflection and joy.
What began a quarter-century ago as a vision shared by a handful of dedicated families has blossomed into a cornerstone of the community. At the heart of the celebration was the theme of Rajipo—the sincere yearning to please the Guru. Every effort throughout the weekend, and indeed the very foundation of the Mandir over the past 25 years, reflected the aspiration to earn the Rajipo of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.
The true spirit of the Mahotsav was cultivated over an entire year, as members of the Miami Mandal quietly and consistently offered their bhakti in preparation: a continuous 365-day chain of upvas, kirtan bhakti on every Ekadashi, weekly balika pradakshinas, a 25-hour akhand dhun, samuh puja, and morning and evening feris around the Mandir. These acts of devotion, sacrifice, and unity laid the foundation for a truly memorable Silver Jubilee.
Satsang Diksha Homatmak Yagna
The celebrations began on Saturday, May 30, 2026 as devotees and well-wishers gathered at the Mandir for the Satsang Diksha Homatmak Path Yagna, held in the divine presence of Pujya Swamis. What made the occasion especially memorable was that the sacred yagna was conducted entirely by youths between the ages of 5 and 22, who performed the auspicious rituals with devotion while flawlessly chanting complex Sanskrit shlokas. Twenty-one yagna kunds were arranged outdoors, each accommodating 16 participants. Across two sessions, more than 550 devotees participated in the sacred yagna, marking an auspicious beginning to the Rajat Jayanti celebrations.
Kirtan Aradhana
The main weekend of festivities began on June 19, 2026 with a welcoming dinner that set a warm and festive tone as attendees arrived in traditional attire. Among the most touching moments was the return of families who had grown up or spent many years at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Miami before moving away. Their homecoming brought a special sense of joy and nostalgia, giving the evening the feeling of a grand family reunion.
The evening continued with a captivating Kirtan Aradhana performed by children, youths, and Pujya Swamis, with more than 1,500 people in attendance. A specially composed Mahotsav kirtan, which devotees had listened to in their homes throughout the preceding month, opened a two-hour medley of devotional kirtans and live music. The performances featured an array of instruments, including harmonium, keyboards, tabla, khanjari, manjira, octapad, hand kartals, cabasa, shehnai, and flute. The Kirtan Aradhana brought the community together in an atmosphere of devotion, gratitude, and reflection, setting a deeply spiritual tone for the milestone weekend.
Patotsav Mahapuja
Saturday, June 20, 2026, began with the Patotsav Mahapuja, a traditional ceremony commemorating the anniversary of a mandir’s murti consecration (pran pratishtha). The ceremony marked the sacred occasion 25 years earlier when the Mandir’s murtis were consecrated by His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
Nineteen Swamis from across the region led the elaborate rituals, including the sacred abhishek of the murtis, and offered collective prayers for peace and harmony throughout the world. The ceremonial Patotsav arti was performed by the Swamis together with more than 1,500 devotees. A magnificent annakut featuring an expansive array of sweet and savory offerings was presented to the murtis as the congregation sang devotional thals. The morning concluded with heartfelt stories and cherished memories from the Mandir’s 25-year journey.
Women's Cultural Program
At midday on Saturday, the women’s cultural program served as a powerful testament to the Mandir’s enduring legacy, bringing together women spanning nine decades, from ages 5 to 95. Curated entirely by women, for women, the program highlighted the community’s longstanding commitment to empowering women and fostering their personal, cultural, and spiritual growth. U.S. Congresswoman Lois Frankel attended the program in its entirety and was joined by State Attorney Alexcia Cox and Assistant Public Defender Schnelle Tonge.
The program featured a traditional symphony, a panel discussion, and a skit highlighting the pioneering women who played an important role in establishing the Mandir’s grassroots foundation 25 years ago. Devotional folk dances and a symbolic “passing of the torch” ceremony celebrated the continuation of this legacy from one generation to the next.
Beyond fostering lifelong friendships, the Mandir has provided generations of women and girls with opportunities to learn Sanskrit and Gujarati and develop skills in public speaking, devotional singing, culinary arts, Bharatanatyam, and cultural crafts. These traditions, values, and skills continue to be passed on to younger generations, ensuring that the Mandir’s rich cultural legacy will flourish for years to come.
Grand Finale
Saturday evening featured the Silver Jubilee Grand Celebration Program, drawing more than 1,100 guests, including devotees from across the nation, members of sister congregations in Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville, Melbourne, and beyond, as well as generations of youths who had grown up attending the Mandir before moving to other states. The three-hour program, hosted by three middle-school-aged children, took the audience on a journey through skits, video presentations, monologues, and speeches presented by youths and Swamis. A moving personal testimonial from a member of the congregation added a heartfelt dimension to the evening, which culminated in a grand finale featuring vibrant traditional dances. State Senator Lori Berman also attended the evening celebration.
Despite the intense summer heat throughout the weekend, the community’s enthusiasm and spirit never wavered—a living testament to the values of Samp (togetherness), Suhrudbhav (friendship), and Ekta (unity) that His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj continues to inspire.
On Sunday, June 21, the Rajat Jayanti celebrations culminated with the Grand Finale for the local Miami community. An encore presentation of Saturday evening’s program welcomed another 1,500 guests from across South Florida, spanning St. Lucie County to Miami-Dade County. The occasion was further honored by the presence of Palm Beach County Vice Mayor Marci Woodward and Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores. At the heart of the program was a cultural showcase that brought to life three enduring pillars of the Mandir community: Seva (selfless service), Sanskar (cultural values), and Shraddha (unwavering faith).
Nurturing the Next Generation
Throughout the weekend, the presence of revered BAPS Swamis brought an invaluable spiritual dimension to the celebrations. Despite demanding schedules and the sweltering summer heat, the Swamis devoted themselves tirelessly to the children and youths, personally guiding them through their preparations and performances while strengthening bonds of mentorship that will help nurture their faith for years to come. As the celebrations drew to a close, guests gathered for a festive mahaprasad dinner featuring authentic Gujarati cuisine, sharing fellowship, laughter, and gratitude for the remarkable journey they had experienced together.
While the Rajat Jayanti Mahotsav celebrated a historic milestone, it also looked toward the future, symbolizing the passing of a cherished legacy from one generation to the next. The foundation of Seva, Sanskar, and Shraddha, strengthened by the Miami Mandal over the past quarter-century, now serves as the foundation for the next 25 years. The Mahotsav left the community inspired and united, with renewed devotion to carry forward the values and vision that have shaped the Mandir’s journey and to begin the next chapter together.

/apac/news/kishore-kishori-shibir-2026.text:
Sakshat Prapti
Over 500 kishores and kishoris participated in the Kishore-Kishori Shibirs 2026, themed ‘Sakshat Prapti’ and held over one to two days at eight centers across Australia and New Zealand: Adelaide, Auckland, Brisbane, Canberra, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney and Wellington.
The theme conveyed that prapti is not something the youths must strive to gain: they have already been blessed with it through Bhagwan and the Satpurush. The challenge is recognising it and experiencing its joy in daily life.
Four sessions developed the theme. The first explored prapti no mahima and the challenges that stop youths from feeling it, encouraging them to turn from the small heap of everyday problems to the Himalayan scale of their attainment. The second examined the bhido the gurus have endured and the parivartan it has sparked, showing how the Satpurush, despite his limitless samarthya (divine capability), remains an ajatshatru — one who has no enemies. The third focused on vishwaas in the Satpurush, grounded in the evidence of his life rather than inherited, and the fourth on krutarthpanu, the fulfilment of realising one has already attained everything worth attaining.
Each session paired discourses by swamis with live kirtan and nirupan, a parivartan case study, a panel discussion with local devotees and a Kirtan Aradhana, followed by small-group breakouts led by volunteers.
The shibirs concluded with a practical guide to daily praptino vichar, following Mahant Swami Maharaj’s wish that devotees set aside fifteen minutes each day, and a video ashirwad from Pujya Anandswarup Swami on valuing the guru’s agna. The youths offered a collective pratigna to Swamishri, leaving not only understanding what they have attained, but equipped to live by it.

/raleigh/news/shri-swaminarayan-jayanti-.t: Shri Swaminarayan Jayanti & Ram Navami – Women’s Celebration, Raleigh, NC
/raleigh/news/shri-swaminarayan-jayanti-.text:
Women devotees at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Raleigh, NC celebrated the auspicious birth anniversaries of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram through a devotional program centered on the theme, “Preme Pragatya Re,” celebrating Bhagwan’s boundless love for His devotees.
The program presented how Bhagwan incarnates on earth out of compassion, with the ultimate purpose of granting moksha, or liberation, while also guiding devotees, through His own life and actions, to live pure, noble, and virtuous lives.
The life of Bhagwan Shri Ram was presented through the many relationships in which His love was expressed. As an ideal son, He honored and respected His parents with complete sincerity, offering a lasting example for both youth and families today. As an ideal husband, the sacred and enduring bond between Bhagwan Shri Ram and Sitaji, as well as Laxmanji and Urmilaji, reflected values of loyalty, sacrifice, and mutual respect. Across every role He fulfilled, Bhagwan Shri Ram demonstrated how to live an ideal life while guiding others with compassion and care.
Similarly, the life of Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan highlighted His profound love for devotees through the gift of true gnan, or knowledge, and a spiritual connection that transcends the material world. Through His interactions, teachings, and genuine care for each individual, Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan established a relationship rooted in eternal well-being. This same spiritual connection continues today through the guidance of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, through whom devotees continue to experience Bhagwan Shri Swaminarayan’s presence and love.
Women of all ages offered their devotion through a vibrant cultural program featuring devotional songs, traditional dances, thoughtful skits, and inspiring speeches. The performances brought forward the message of the theme in thoughtful and engaging ways, adding to the devotional atmosphere of the celebration and highlighting the spirit of divine love.
